subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin came under pressure due to conflict in West Asia triggering inflationary spikes across oil and gas, freight, foreign exchange and core raw materials including steel, aluminum and precious metals.
Improved mix driven by higher contribution from premium variants and PAM (parts, accessories and merchandise) business helped offset gross margin pressure.
Cost structures were rationalized by deferring noncritical operating expenses and accelerating cost savings under internal LEAP program.
Operating scale was leveraged to drive cost efficiencies across manufacturing and supply chain operations.
Judicious price actions were taken across select models, balancing margin protection with market momentum.
ICE EBITDA margin held up better than overall margin, cushioned by strong operating leverage, cost savings and higher profitability in parts business.

subsections.label: Consolidated results context
points: Consolidated PAT of INR1,418 crores compares to a normalized profit of around INR1,100 crores last year (excluding one-time gain).
Last year included a onetime gain of approximately INR700 crores before tax on account of dilution of company's shares of investment in associates consequent to public issue and private placement.

subsections.label: EV unit economics
points: Total P&L investment in VIDA business remained flat sequentially at around INR230 crores despite volume growth, due to continuous improvement in per unit economics.
PLI benefit of INR48 crores accrued in the quarter, covering 60% of EV portfolio; expected to cover almost all products by end of December 2026.
FY27 will be the first full year of PLI accruals, providing a structural tailwind to EV portfolio.
Some EV models have turned gross margin positive, which will further enhance overall EV profitability going forward.
EBITDA loss per unit in EV business improved from ~INR50,000 in previous quarter to ~INR40,000 in current quarter, reflecting improvement trajectory.

subsections.label: Q2 FY27 outlook and pricing
points: Marginal uptick in input cost inflation expected in Q2 FY27, to be neutralized via continued mix improvement, optimizing discretionary spends, and accelerating cost-saving programs.
Primary focus remains on driving EBITDA growth while progressing towards medium-term EBITDA margin target range of 14%-16%.
Investment behind growth to continue, both in capacity expansion and brand building supporting premium, scooters, EV and global business portfolio.

Cumulative blended ICE price increase of 4.5% taken since end of February 2026 across different models/months/geographies; marginal additional ICE price increase taken in July in anticipation of commodity cost increase.
EV price increases are in early double digits per unit, partly reflecting added functionality/differentiation rather than pure price pass-through.

Company states it has not passed on all commodity cost increases — some areas saw less pass-through, others more; in some entry-level variants/geographies a calibrated price reduction was taken to expand market.

key_figures.label: H2 FY27 industry growth outlook
key_figures.value: approaching double digit for full year

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Growth was broad-based, supported by improved affordability post GST rate cuts, healthy urban and rural demand, and continued acceleration in EV adoption.
Strong retail momentum continued into Q2, with July retail growth of 28% YoY, both ICE and EV registering similar strong momentum as in Q1.

subsections.label: Channel stock and pent-up demand
points: VIDA has pretty much nil channel inventory (2-3 days depending on region), indicating whatever is shipped is retailed immediately, pointing to pent-up demand.
ICE scooters (e.g., Xoom, some Destini variants) running channel stock at typically half of normal average levels, indicating depletion of channel stock alongside 87% YoY growth in ICE scooters.
Motorcycle channel stock is at 6 weeks, described as forward-looking and not yet where the company wants to be; expect some increase over the next couple of months to prepare for festive season.

subsections.label: Retail finance
points: Retail finance penetration jumped to close to 65% last month, supported by easing credit conditions helping the market; expected to become even more helpful moving into festive season.

subsections.label: Pricing actions and demand response
points: Weighted average price increases taken, but with tactical price cuts in select variants/geographies (e.g., one variant of HF Deluxe) to boost demand and gain share among first-time buyers.
HF Deluxe price cut in select states seeing an immediate boost in demand and increased footfalls into showrooms since implementation; Splendor portfolio growing stronger since this intervention.
Company believes there is an unaddressed/underserved market of consumers falling off mobility that such interventions can substantially grow in certain geographies.

subsections.label: Delhi EV policy proposal
points: Great momentum seen in Delhi EV market ahead of the proposed Delhi EV policy (effective FY28): inquiries and retails have nearly doubled last month.
Company preparing infrastructure — increased supplies to Delhi, activated dealerships, trained dealer service technicians, and increasing own charging network/charge points.

subsections.label: Industry growth outlook
points: H2 FY27 will have a high base effect from the GST-driven jump in H2 FY26 sales, so YoY growth will be lower on a base basis, but momentum still expected to yield positive H2 growth.
Full-year FY27 industry growth plans are approaching double digits.

key_figures.label: Parts and accessories (PAM) revenue growth YoY
ICE scooters growth YoY (alt. figure cited)

subsections.label: Growth mix and strategy
points: Strategy of growing in EV, premium, global business, and scooters all performed well, contributing to a positive mix benefit of 8% of the 13% uplift between volume growth (23%) and revenue growth (36%).
Growth in revenue going forward will increasingly come from shift to higher-value products: scooter, premium, EV and global businesses on top of volume growth.
Strategy of focusing on fast-growing segments continued to yield results, consolidating gains in the Commuter segment as well.

subsections.label: Motorcycle category dynamics
points: Within motorcycles, 100cc category is also growing but 125cc-and-above categories are growing faster; Hero has outgrown the industry in 100cc, gaining 230 bps market share to reach ~86% share.
GST-driven affordability tailwind continues to support 100cc as the first commuter purchase category for many customers.
Higher motorcycle categories are growing faster as India urbanizes and becomes richer, and Hero has gained share there too.

In 100cc specifically (Splendor, Passion), category expansion combined with market share expansion (segment grew from 32% to ~33%) attributed to interventions beyond product, including retail finance and other affordability measures.

subsections.label: PAM business growth drivers
points: PAM revenue growth of ~25%+ driven by expanded reach (deeper penetration with formats), operational efficiency initiatives, larger SKU coverage, new parts groups, and new lines of business performing well.
Growth partly comes from eating into the gray market, but also from accessories (with traction increasing as VIDA and premium range increases) and exports business.
New GPC 2.0 investment (CapEx of INR750 crores) announced to more than double capacity to handle parts business.

subsections.label: VAHAN market share commentary
points: Management noted the VAHAN market share fell 150 bps YoY in Q1 despite overall growth, in context of a question about calibrating price increases versus growth focus; management reiterated continued focus on volume growth with calibrated (not full) price pass-through of commodity costs.

key_figures.label: Flex fuel motorcycles sold since dispatch start

subsections.label: New product launches — ICE
points: Super Splendor XTEC 2.0 launched with best-in-class mileage and silent start feature.
Passion Plus Disc variant launched, expanding the 100cc portfolio.

subsections.label: New product launches — EV (VIDA)
points: Premium variant of VIDA VX2 launched with 187km IDC range and superior fast-charging capability, called VX2 Plus 4.4kWh, launched with campaign 'Hafte Mein Ek Baar' emphasizing consumers can charge just once a week; comes with twin removable battery for flexible charging.
VX2 Go 3.1kWh variant launched in August offering ~120km IDC range, targeted at consumers with easy access to home/office charging, leveraging existing favorable VX2 styling.
Both new VIDA variants expected to contribute significant volume going forward; company will share more detail as they stabilize in forthcoming quarters.
VIDA now offers a full range from 2.2kWh to 4.4kWh battery options, giving consumers complete flexibility.

subsections.label: Flex fuel powertrain
points: Flex fuel variants introduced in June for core commuter segment's highest-selling models Splendor and HF — first in the category to do so.
Comes with smart engine technology and components specifically designed to work at higher ethanol blends (20% to 85% ethanol content).
Dispatches began third week of July; strong early traction with ~5,000 units sold within 2 weeks in limited outlets; company describes itself as differentiated/only player in this category currently.

subsections.label: Electric motorcycle platforms
points: Company continuing to advance electric motorcycle range, with more updates expected soon.

Two motorcycle platforms were unveiled at EICMA 2025: Project Ubex — a neo-naked motorcycle concept for urban mobility, combining thrill/acceleration with city and road friendliness; and VXZ — a high-performance motorcycle developed in collaboration with Zero Motorcycles of USA, targeting adventure/aspirational high-performance consumers.
These are new platforms, developed with learnings from the scooter platform but tailored to motorcycle-consumer needs for performance, rideability, gradability and range.
Electric motorcycle platform products are not expected this year (FY27); timelines point to launches starting next year.

subsections.label: Leadership/technology capability
points: New CTO Sachin Agrawal joined in May, bringing multiple decades of experience across different powertrains, bolstering powertrain development capability.

Anuj Dua appointed as Chief Business Officer for Premium segment; brings over 2 decades of experience across global product strategy, brand building and market expansion across geographies (9 years at Royal Enfield, 10 years earlier at Hero).

subsections.label: Premium segment product priorities (Anuj Dua)
points: Immediate priorities: elevate consumer retail experience across all touchpoints (search journey to in-use journey); portfolio expansion with exciting products coming over next 12 months; focus on merchandise and accessories reflecting global trend towards mass customization/personalization.
Continuing partnership with Harley-Davidson to be taken to next level.

Investment in community/lifestyle engagement and MotoSports (including Dakar) paying dividends across the globe, especially India and Latin America; adventure segment cited as fastest-growing segment globally.

Upcoming premium motorcycle models referenced by analysts include XPulse 421 and XMR 250; company confirms many models in the works, with a few refreshes launching before festive season and larger full-body-change models in upcoming quarters (the two specifically named models will not launch before festive).

subsections.label: EV capacity expansion
points: EV capacity has increased from 15,000/month at end of last year to close to 30,000/month currently (first week of August), with plan to reach ~45,000/month before end of FY27 — tripling capacity within the financial year as committed.
First leg of EV capacity expansion came on stream on August 1st.
Second phase of VIDA capacity expansion (the remaining 1/3) will come in Q4 FY27.
Company confident in ramping production quickly given low channel stock indicating strong underlying demand.

subsections.label: ICE capacity expansion
points: Splendor capacity increased by 2,000/day (a little over 50,000/month increase) driven by confidence from 15% YoY growth in Splendor within the quarter — already completed to prepare for festival season.
Destini capacity doubled and Xoom scooter capacity increased by a further 50%, both driven by confidence in scooter growth (dispatches nearly doubled YoY) and 230bps of scooter market share gain.
ICE scooter front capacity addition of 1,500/day completed.
Combined ICE + EV capacity addition of ~2,500/day; total output currently ~65,000/month, expected to a little more than double by H2 FY27.
2/3 of total planned capacity expansion already completed; remaining 1/3 (second phase VIDA expansion) to complete in Q4 FY27.

subsections.label: Export expansion
points: Company entering more markets and introducing more products: opened Germany with launch of ICE vehicles; started selling VIDA in Nepal (launched earlier in July).
Company aims to sustain the high growth trajectory seen over the last 2 years of 40%+ YoY export growth going forward.
Volume expansion plans keep exports growth in view; price realization and FX gain from exports contributed benefit, including a 25bps FX/higher realization contribution to EBITDA last quarter.

subsections.label: Delhi market activity
points: Company jumped from 4th to 2nd rank with 16.7% EV market share in Delhi, driven by doubling of inquiries and near-doubling of retails last month.
Increased supplies to Delhi, activated all dealerships, trained dealer service technicians, and increasing own charging network/charge points ahead of proposed Delhi EV policy (FY28).

subsections.label: Leadership changes
points: New CTO Sachin Agrawal joined in May 2026, bringing multiple decades of powertrain development experience.

Anuj Dua appointed Chief Business Officer for Premium segment, with over 2 decades of 2-wheeler OEM experience (Royal Enfield, Hero), tasked with leading the premium business as the company's 'next big growth engine'.

subsections.label: Parts business capacity investment
points: New GPC 2.0 investment with CapEx of INR750 crores announced, more than doubling capacity to handle the parts business, supporting growth in parts, accessories and merchandise (PAM).

subsections.label: Collaboration/partnerships
points: Partnership with Zero Motorcycles of USA for high-performance electric motorcycle platform (codenamed VXZ).
Ongoing partnership with Harley-Davidson to be taken to the next level in the premium/lifestyle business.

subsections.label: EV self-sustainability strategy
points: 4-pillar strategy to achieve EV business self-sustainability: PLI benefits (targeting 100% portfolio coverage by December 2026), scale (operating leverage from capacity ramp), BOM cost reduction/LEAP savings program, and calibrated price increases in line with industry.

New non-product revenue streams being developed: Battery as a Service offering across the EV portfolio for accessibility; VIDA Edge connected services program as a paywall benefit unlocking connected features; extended warranty and other value-added services bundle.

subsections.label: Commodity and geopolitical risk
points: The conflict in West Asia triggered inflationary spikes across oil and gas, freight, foreign exchange and core raw materials including steel, aluminum and precious metals, causing transitionary commodity cost pressures in Q1 FY27.
Net commodity inflation impact of approximately 4.5% contributed to gross margin contraction of 300bps QoQ.
A marginal further uptick in input cost inflation is expected in Q2 FY27, planned to be neutralized through mix improvement, discretionary spend optimization and cost-saving programs.

subsections.label: Category/growth risk
points: Sub-125cc motorcycle category growing slower than other categories despite GST tailwinds, though Hero has gained share within it.
H2 FY27 will face a high base effect from the large jump in H2 FY26 sales post GST, resulting in lower YoY growth from a base perspective, though momentum is still expected to yield positive growth.
VAHAN market share declined 150bps YoY in Q1, flagged by an analyst amid concerns on price increases affecting entry-level demand.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: 14%-16% EBITDA margin is the medium-term guidance; short-term impact from transitory commodity inflation acknowledged, with mitigation via volume and focus on absolute EBITDA growth rather than just EBITDA percent.
Confident of returning to the 14%-16% range in the medium term, but not committing to it in the short term given current cost pressures.

Q2 FY27 to see marginal input cost uptick, to be neutralized via mix improvement, discretionary spend optimization and cost-saving program acceleration; primary focus remains driving absolute EBITDA growth while progressing towards the medium-term margin target.

subsections.label: Capacity and industry growth outlook
points: EV capacity to reach ~45,000 units/month before end of FY27 (tripling from 15,000/month at start of year), with second phase VIDA expansion completing in Q4 FY27.
2-wheeler industry (ICE + EV combined) grew ~14% in Q1 FY27; similar trajectory expected in Q2 based on July trends.
H2 FY27 industry growth expected to be positive but lower YoY due to high base effect from H2 FY26 GST-driven sales jump; full-year FY27 industry growth plans are approaching double digits.
PLI benefit expected to cover almost all EV products by end of December 2026, with FY27 being the first full year of PLI accruals as a structural tailwind.

subsections.label: Continued investment priorities
points: Investment behind growth to continue in both capacity expansion and brand building, supporting premium, scooters, EV and global business portfolio.

guidance_ledger.statement: 14% to 16% is our guidance for the midterm; confident of going back to it in the midterm, but not in the short term.

Primary focus will remain on driving EBITDA growth while progressing towards our medium-term EBITDA margin target range of 14% to 16%; plan to neutralize marginal input cost uptick via mix improvement, discretionary spend optimization and cost-saving programs.
We should see us go to close to 45,000 per month before the end of this financial year — tripling our capacity of EV within this financial year.
We expect 100% of our portfolio to be PLI compliant by December 2026.
Right now, plans are towards full year of approaching double digit as an industry growth.
H2 does have a base effect of big jump that happened in sales in H2 last year post GST, hence YoY growth will be lower, but we expect still a positive growth in H2.
Currently clocking 65,000 a month; capacity addition will more than -- a little more than double.
High growth trajectory that you saw in our exports over the last 2 years of 40% plus year-on-year — we are aiming for that kind of growth going forward.
It's not this year. We will be looking at products coming in from the next year.
We are putting all 4 levers (scale, PLI, BOM cost reduction, calibrated pricing) at the same time, and we should continue on our trajectory to look positive by the end of the year.
New investment of GPC 2.0 with CapEx of INR750 crores, which pretty much more than doubles our capacity to handle parts business.
FY27 capex commitment: ₹1,500 cr (explicitly confirmed as in FY27).
Reiterated medium-term margin guidance of 14%–16%, but avoided committing to a precise FY27 outcome due to volatility.
Near-term expansion: within ~a month, capacity to be ~50% higher than last quarter.

risk_register.risk: Commodity cost inflation (West Asia conflict driving oil/gas, freight, FX, steel, aluminum, precious metals inflation)
risk_register.note: Net commodity inflation impact of ~4.5% caused 300bps QoQ gross margin contraction in Q1 FY27; marginal further uptick expected in Q2 FY27.
This category still growing but slower than 125cc-and-above and other 2-wheeler categories, despite GST tailwinds and Hero's share gains within it.

risk_register.risk: High base effect in H2 FY27
risk_register.note: H2 FY26 saw a big sales jump post GST, creating a high base that will lower YoY growth in H2 FY27 even though momentum remains positive.

VAHAN market share dropped ~150bps YoY in Q1 FY27, raised by an analyst amid concerns that price increases could be impacting entry-level demand; management maintains focus on growth via calibrated (not full) price pass-through.

risk_register.risk: EV business currently loss-making at unit level
risk_register.note: EV EBITDA loss per unit improved from ~INR50,000 to ~INR40,000 QoQ; company working towards profitability via 4-pillar strategy (scale, PLI, BOM cost reduction, calibrated pricing) targeting positive trajectory by end of year.
Mitigation but near-term pressure.

risk_register.risk: West Asia developments impacting commodity costs, metals, gas
risk_register.note: Plus labor cost increases.

risk_register.risk: Fuel price hikes in Bangladesh/Sri Lanka
risk_register.note: Could hit demand short-term.
Have been priced and passing it on so far.
Described as evolving; operationalization and pricing still under industry discussion.
Persistent geopolitical tensions create uncertainty.
Volatility in commodity prices impacts margins.
Shifting trade policies across major economies create uncertainty.
Expected to be range-bound within 1% to 2% in Q3.
Ongoing geopolitical and supply uncertainties could impact future performance.

themes.label: Market share recovery
themes.note: Wholesale market share up 30bps in Q1 with strong gains in scooters (+230bps) and EV (+400bps in a year), yet VAHAN retail market share fell ~150bps YoY.

themes.label: EV market expansion
themes.note: EV wholesale growth of 151% YoY, VIDA quarterly volume of 57,000 units (+26% QoQ), monthly capacity tripling from 15,000 to ~45,000 by year-end, and new VX2 Plus/VX2 Go launches.

themes.label: Commodity cost management
themes.note: West Asia conflict drove ~4.5% net commodity inflation causing 300bps gross margin contraction QoQ; mitigated via mix, LEAP cost savings and calibrated pricing, with EBITDA margin decline contained to 120bps.

themes.label: Product innovation
themes.note: New launches across ICE (Super Splendor XTEC 2.0, Passion Plus Disc), flex-fuel Splendor/HF variants (first in category), and EV (VX2 Plus, VX2 Go) plus upcoming electric motorcycle platforms (Ubex, VXZ with Zero Motorcycles).

themes.label: Export tailwind
themes.note: Export/global business grew >60% in Q1, gained 110bps market share, with new market entries (Germany ICE launch, Nepal VIDA launch) and a target to sustain 40%+ YoY growth trajectory.

themes.label: EV profitability path
themes.note: EV EBITDA loss per unit improved from ~INR50,000 to ~INR40,000 QoQ; 4-pillar strategy (PLI, scale, BOM cost reduction, calibrated pricing) targeting positive EV profitability by year-end.

themes.label: Premiumization strategy
themes.note: New CBO Anuj Dua appointed for Premium business unit, described as the 'next big growth engine', with focus on retail experience, portfolio expansion, merchandise/accessories, and Harley-Davidson/MotoSports partnerships.

key_takeaways: 2-wheeler industry volumes grew 14% year-on-year in terms of VAHAN or retail sales, of which 11% was growth in ICE and 67% was in EV.
Quarter 2 also saw a strong retail growth, year-on-year retail growth in July of 28%.

Our volume grew at 23% year-on-year, and our revenue grew 36%; the extra 13% uplift came from improved price realization as well as mix, with a positive mix of 8% from EV, premium, global business and scooters.
Overall, we saw our wholesale market share increase by 30 basis points in quarter 1.
In EV, we had a wholesale growth of 151%, and this has helped us gain more than 400 basis points of market share here within 1 year.
Gross margin for the quarter came down under pressure, contracting 300 basis points quarter-on-quarter, primarily due to an approximate 4.5% net commodity inflation impact.
Our overall EBITDA margin decline was lower at 120 basis points sequentially, landing at 13.3%, thanks to disciplined cost management as reflected in a 14% sequential reduction in other expenses.
Our primary focus will remain on driving EBITDA growth while progressing towards our medium-term EBITDA margin target range of 14% to 16%.

HEROMOTOCO.about: Hero Moto Corp earlier also known as “Hero Honda” is one of India’s first motorcycle manufacturers. The company started in 1984 as a Technological collaboration with Honda, Japan. Before this collaboration, Hero was selling Cycles under the brand name, Hero Cycles. In 2011, Honda group sold its 26% stake in the company to the Munjals (promoters) and ended the JV. Post the termination of JV, the name of the company was changed to Hero Motocorp. [1] [2]

quarters.summary: Eicher Motors reported record Q1 FY27 performance across both Royal Enfield and VECV, with consolidated revenue growth of 32% YoY and highest-ever EBITDA. Management guided to continued growth momentum for FY27, backed by strong booking/inquiry funnel trends, capacity ramp-up (Cheyyar brownfield to 2 million units by FY27-28, Tada greenfield Phase 1 taking total capacity to 2.45 million units by FY29-30), and international expansion (Brazil CKD facility, Indonesia CKD under consideration). Near-term headwinds include commodity cost inflation (partially softening), tight channel inventory ahead of festive season, and macro/geopolitical uncertainty in export markets.

subsections.label: Gross Margin Drivers
points: Substantial inflation seen in input costs across key commodities: aluminum, crude oil, steel, copper, precious metals.
Additional disruption in supply chain and logistics contributed to cost pressure, though challenges have been mitigated so far.
Net impact of about 4% to 4.5% on margin from increased input cost of commodities and processes involved.
Value engineering benefits of about 0.4% achieved; company continues to advance value engineering and cost reduction programs.
Advanced purchase program conducted for critical parts and raw materials, expected to kick in further going forward.
Price increase of 1.75% on majority of 350cc motorcycles in April 2026 partly mitigated commodity impact, contributing about 1.2% benefit against overall commodity piece.
Remaining 0.2% benefit from mix and other factors.
Commodity situation remains volatile; management declined to give forward guidance on commodity impact for Q2, but noted slight softening versus Q1 headwind depending on inventory holding period.

subsections.label: Other Expenses Decline Drivers
points: Other expenses lower by about 7%, driven by multiple factors.
Q4 FY26 had marketing ad campaigns around the Cricket World Cup costing about INR20 crores, which did not recur in Q1 FY27.
INR10 crores benefit from two product launches that occurred in Q4 FY26 but not in Q1 FY27, totaling INR30 crores of non-repeat expenses.
Remaining INR22 crores benefit from controlled marketing expenditure given the current situation.

subsections.label: ASP and Non-Vehicle Revenue Drivers
points: ASP growth of 2.8% from Q4 FY26 driven by price increases (1.2%), international business mix increase (1%), currency depreciation (0.4%), and allied business revenue increase (0.6%).
International business revenue crossed INR1,000 crores for the first time, now 15.3% of revenue vs 13.7% in Q4 FY26.
Allied businesses (spare parts, service income, accessories, apparel) now about 15% of revenue.
Service job cards grew ~20% YoY, averaging about 9 lakh per month, described as a huge growth driver.
Accessories and apparel growth of more than 30%; almost all bookings through 'Make it yours' feature lead customers to add accessories.
Accessories penetration increased from initial 35-40% to current 87% of consumers buying motorcycles also buying accessories; more SKUs being added as penetration rises.
Apparel business has moved to a 'core collection' brand strategy; roadshow received overwhelmingly positive response from dealers and customers.
Extended warranties and customer retention for service are also growing, supporting non-vehicle revenue.

subsections.label: Depreciation Increase
points: Depreciation increase this quarter attributed to capitalization related to new module and Flying Flea launch (start of production and start of sale).
Average gross block increased by approximately INR346 crores.
Some tools and dies depreciation also kicking in.

subsections.label: Standalone vs Consolidated Revenue Gap
points: Gap between standalone and consolidated revenue of over INR400 crores in Q1 FY27 versus average gap of around INR200 crores in the last 4 quarters attributed to growth from subsidiaries, particularly strong performance in Brazil and other international subsidiaries, offset partly by revenues booked in India for exports and subsidiaries.

subsections.label: Capacity Ramp-up and Operational Issues
points: Faced LPG shortage issues in Q1, managed by converting back to PNG.
Faced manpower shortage issues; recruited additional manpower and extended support to contractors.
Faced issues on availability of key commodities, which were managed.
Oragadam and Vallam plants have been running three shifts since April.
First module at Cheyyar kicked in on time in the last week of July, taking build capacity to about 1.5 million motorcycles per year.
Next Cheyyar module targeted to kick in by first week of October; company is trying to prepone this.
Entire brownfield capacity expansion at Cheyyar (from the INR958 crores investment announced in February 2026) will be completed by FY27-28, taking capacity to 2 million.
Andhra Pradesh Tada greenfield Phase 1 (INR1,225 crores, Board-approved this quarter) will take overall capacity to 2.45 million by FY29-30, built in modules given continuing growth momentum.
Supplier conference held to discuss inventory situation and align vendor ecosystem; vendors also planning 24/7, 3-shift operations to support production ramp-up.

June 2026 production rate reached 4,500 motorcycles/day, totaling about 1.16 lakh motorcycles produced that month; current delivery rate has risen to 5,000+ per day post first module kick-in, ranging 5,000-5,100 after ramp-up.

subsections.label: Inventory / Channel Stock
points: Current dealer inventory stock is about 10-12 days, described as lean due to strong Q1 retail performance.
In-transit inventory adds another approximately 4-5 days on top of dealer inventory (normally max in-transit inventory is about 7 days).

Company is shifting distribution model toward direct billing to dealers to cut inefficiency in secondary transit and depot management; direct billing has grown from about 1-1.5% of volume historically to about 4.5-4.7x that level; expected to save another 4-5 days.
Plan to build inventory ahead of festive season by combining faster capacity ramp-up with logistics efficiency gains (direct billing) and vendor ecosystem readiness.

subsections.label: Key International Markets
points: International business revenue crossed INR1,000+ crores, about 15% of overall revenue in Q1 FY27, having grown 2x over the last 2 years.

Brazil is the biggest market outside India and is leading growth; retail volume grew over 3x in the last 3 years, built on years of brand-building, riding community development, and events; Royal Enfield holds the number two position in the middleweight segment in Brazil.
Every fourth Royal Enfield motorcycle exported now ships to Brazil; company is setting up its own CKD facility in Brazil due to strong growth momentum.
Rest of LatAm shows strong demand momentum led by Colombia; Royal Enfield is number two in Argentina in the middleweight segment; Mexico is also growing.
USA market has been very slow but showed some green shoots of growth in Q1 following a new trade deal cutting tariffs on motorcycles; management says it needs to wait and see.

Europe is in a market adjustment phase with business pressure on dealers/distributors; company has established its own distributorship/subsidiary performing well, and opened its Riders Club, which has exceeded 42,000 members, building blocks for future growth once market opens up.
APAC market was previously weak due to uncertainties but showed green shoots in Q1 with growth in retail and wholesale.
SAARC (especially Nepal and Bangladesh) saw robust 60% growth last year, driven by strong brand awareness.
Portfolio expanded in Nepal and Malaysia with the launch of 2026 Goan Classic 350; Guerrilla 450 APEX variant introduced in Australia and New Zealand.
Royal Enfield motorcycles (Goan Classic 350, Guerrilla 450, Super Meteor) won industry awards at major automotive shows in Thailand and Malaysia.
Royal Enfield ranked as the world's third strongest automobile brand by Brand Finance.
Company remains cautiously bullish on international markets, expecting normalization of energy situations and tariff conditions to help markets recover strongly.
Total international market size outside India is about 0.8-1 million units, with Royal Enfield holding an 8-9% share currently.

subsections.label: ASEAN Strategy - Thailand and Indonesia
points: Thailand has a CKD plant; initial expectation was that ASEAN treaty would allow shipping to Indonesia without quota restriction via the Thailand CKD plant, but Indonesia has maintained quota restriction limiting sales to about 10,000 vehicles/year.

Company is exploring setting up a CKD plant directly in Indonesia via an identified assembler/distributor partner; decision expected to be made this quarter; local content requirement for Indonesia CKD is low, allowing a faster path.
Indonesia carries a luxury tax of about 160%+ above 250cc regardless of CBU or CKD status, so a CKD plant would not remove this tax but would remove the 10,000-unit quota cap.

Thailand market has been weak for the past 2 years due to tourism dip and weak economy, but retail momentum and dealer sentiment turned positive in Q1; Royal Enfield holds number two position in the middleweight segment in Thailand.
Company is building brand collaboration in Thailand with Muay Thai and Thailand tourism development to increase consumer awareness ahead of market recovery.

subsections.label: Flying Flea Distribution Strategy
points: First Flying Flea store opened in Jayanagar, Bengaluru.
Plans to expand footprint in Bengaluru first with five additional touchpoints, followed by another five (total 10 locations) over the next 2 months.

subsections.label: Demand Funnel Indicators
points: In India, continuing strong growth momentum, with volumes tracking over about 32% growth over Q1 FY26.

Other funnel indicators such as overall booking, walk-ins, and telephonic inquiries continue to maintain very strong growth, slightly higher than volume growth, indicating unmet demand due to inventory constraints rather than demand issues.
Premiumization trend in the two-wheeler industry continuing over the last 3+ years.

Average age group of interested customers is approximately 25-30 years.
All prospective customers are looking at the motorcycles and taking test rides.

subsections.label: Customer Demographics
points: Royal Enfield's professional customer profile broadly includes business owners, agricultural workers, students, government employees and other professionals.
Company tracks government employee demand by category (central/state) and tailors marketing activation around pay commission or income tax benefit developments that put free cash in customers' hands.

About 5-6% of buyers are existing Royal Enfield owners upgrading from one Royal Enfield to another; over 70% are upgraders overall; about 25% are first-time buyers, with Hunter and new launches driving increased first-time buyer share.

subsections.label: Growth Outlook for Higher Base Period (H2 FY27)
points: Management expects to continue growth even against a higher base starting September/October, driven by continued strength across the demand funnel (bookings, walk-ins, telephonic inquiries).
Growth strategy includes continued new product launches (Hunter, Guerrilla 450 APEX, Bullet 650, GT Cup series, more CTG updates to come).
Brand awareness and marketing activation spend, which was scaled down last year in Q1 due to supply-demand situation, will be ramped up again.
New business initiatives like Re-own and Assured Buy Back are gaining traction and add to the growth playbook.

subsections.label: VECV Structure
points: Management indicated no current plans to hive off VECV as a separate listed entity; current focus at Eicher Motors level is on EV, with a lot of work still needed there.
Decision on VECV structure has not crystallized.

subsections.label: VECV Fleet Modernization MoU
points: VECV signed an MoU for the fleet modernization scheme PARIVARTAN, announced by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for the NCR.
The scheme targets over 2 lakh vehicles; implementation details are being finalized.
VECV is well positioned to address the opportunity with its comprehensive portfolio spanning CNG, LNG, electric and BS-VI diesel solutions.

subsections.label: 125 Years Celebrations
points: Marked 125 years of Royal Enfield with unveiling of World Origin Site plaque at Redditch, birthplace of the brand, with five generations of motorcycles lining Enfield Road for the unveiling.
Flagged off the biggest ever edition of the Himalayan Odyssey, bringing together riders from eight countries, as part of 125-year celebrations.
Opened registrations for the 2026 Continental GT Cup, introducing the GT-R750 for the professional category and expanding the championship to 8 cities in India.
Hosted community experiences including inaugural Himalayan Basecamp: Ladakh Edition, Himalayan Spirit in Kochi, Gymkhana in Chennai, and GRRR Nights in Bengaluru.

subsections.label: Commodity and Input Cost Inflation
points: Substantial inflation seen across key input commodities including aluminum, crude oil, steel, copper, and precious metals.
Supply chain and logistics disruption added further cost pressure, though challenges have been mitigated so far.
Situation remains volatile; management declined to provide forward-looking guidance on commodity impact for Q2, though noted slight softening depending on inventory holding period.

subsections.label: Manufacturing Operational Constraints
points: LPG shortage issues faced in Q1, managed by converting back to PNG.
Manpower shortage issues faced in Q1, managed through additional recruitment and support to contractors.
Issues on availability of key commodities managed during the quarter.

subsections.label: Channel Inventory Tightness
points: Current dealer inventory is lean at 10-12 days due to strong Q1 retail; situation described as tight ahead of the festive season, requiring capacity ramp-up and logistics efficiency (direct billing) to build adequate stock.

subsections.label: Macroeconomic and Geopolitical Uncertainty (International)
points: Dynamic macroeconomic and geopolitical environment affecting international markets.
International markets have been trading through rough patches over past few quarters due to macro uncertainties and industry-specific factors.
USA market has been very slow; Europe is going through a market adjustment phase with dealer/distributor business pressure; APAC previously affected by uncertainties.
Thailand market weak for past 2 years due to tourism dip and weak economy.

subsections.label: Indonesia Market Access Constraints
points: Indonesia maintains a quota restriction limiting sales to about 10,000 vehicles/year regardless of ASEAN treaty expectations from the Thailand CKD plant.
Indonesia luxury tax of about 160%+ above 250cc applies regardless of CBU or CKD status, representing a structural cost hurdle.

subsections.label: Capacity Roadmap

Company will ramp up marketing/brand awareness initiatives to support growth.

guidance_ledger.statement: Entire brownfield capacity expansion at Cheyyar will be completed by FY27-28, taking production capacity to 2 million motorcycles per year.

Company is on track to build inventory ahead of the festive season through capacity ramp-up and logistics efficiency (direct billing), though situation is currently tight.

Company continues to advance value engineering programs and cost reduction programs, with value engineering to kick in across all platforms over time, with current focus on the J platform (450cc/650cc).

quarters.summary: Eicher Motors Ltd anticipates continued demand growth, with strategic capacity expansions and a focus on premium motorcycle segments, while navigating commodity inflation and geopolitical uncertainties.

subsections.label: Demand and channel health
points: Management sees sustained structural demand; explicitly: 'there is no structural correction… demand… continuing.'

Premium motorcycle segment expansion: Govindarajan described premiumization as persistent: 'only the premium segment is growing,' with the premium market expanding from ~70,000/month (FY22/23) to ~1.1 lakh/month now, and RE contributing ~90,000+ of that.
April momentum: Reported April sales ~1.04 lakh, '57% growth' YoY (also referenced strong momentum/'growth of 51%' at one point).

Inventory tightness: Dealer + depot inventory '7, 8 days'; dealer inventory even lower. Short-term constraint attributed to temporary disruptions: 'manpower availability due to elections and LPG shortages' (week-to-10-day phenomenon), now 'back on track.'

key_figures.label: Eicher brand HD trucks market share

subsections.label: Royal Enfield: Demand, mix, product actions, and electric entry
points: FY26 upgrades/variants launched: Guerrilla 450 Apex, 2025 Hunter 350, Meteor 350, Goan Classic 350, Himalayan Mana Black; positioned as 'thoughtful upgrades' generating volume gains.
Milestones: Meteor 350 cumulative >6 lakh since 2020. Himalayan 450 +53% to 38,000+ retails globally.
Distribution innovation: Plan to make 350 range more accessible via Flipkart and Amazon (work in progress).

Pipeline disclosure discipline: No detailed timelines, but management confirmed projects shown at EICMA are 'on track… no delay.' Specific callouts: 'S6… will also come in' (Flying Flea S6), and 'Bullet 650… dispatch is already started.'
Segment positioning unchanged: RE reiterated focus on 'middleweight between 250cc to 750cc' and did not signal intent to go below 350cc near term, noting existing platform potential in 350/450/650.

subsections.label: Electric (Flying Flea) entry and commercialization approach
points: Entry into EVs positioned as brand expansion: Flying Flea described as a 'City Plus electric mobility brand.'
Launch: Flying Flea C6 launched in Bengaluru (first week of April 2026) with 'very exciting' response.
Go-to-market: Highly controlled ramp—'deliberate city-by-city approach', currently one store; management stressed 'we are not in a rush' and avoided volume targets.
Product/brand validation signals cited: C6 won the Red Dot Award pre-launch; media ride feedback 'journalists really, really love the motorcycle.'

subsections.label: VECV: Segment performance, market share progress, and EV traction
points: Eicher brand HD trucks: 25,155 units (+14.1%), market share improved to 9.1%.
LMD trucks: 46,195 units, management claimed leadership with emphasis that leadership must pair with 'profitable growth.'
New segment (SUV / small commercial EV platform): 2,452 Pro X delivered including 726 EVs—called out as opening 'an important new avenue for growth.'
Buses: Eicher buses 18,651; Volvo buses record 712.
Volvo trucks: 1,712.
Exports: +33.9% to 6,933 units despite 'challenging external environment.'
Aftermarket: Spare parts sales +13.9% to INR3,045.5 cr (notable scale and growth).

subsections.label: Product portfolio and pipeline (ICE)
points: FY26 upgrades/variants launched: Guerrilla 450 Apex, 2025 Hunter 350, Meteor 350, Goan Classic 350, Himalayan Mana Black; positioned as 'thoughtful upgrades' generating volume gains.
Milestones: Meteor 350 cumulative >6 lakh since 2020. Himalayan 450 +53% to 38,000+ retails globally.
Distribution innovation: Plan to make 350 range more accessible via Flipkart and Amazon (work in progress).

Pipeline disclosure discipline: No detailed timelines, but management confirmed projects shown at EICMA are 'on track… no delay.' Specific callouts: 'S6… will also come in' (Flying Flea S6), and 'Bullet 650… dispatch is already started.'
Segment positioning unchanged: RE reiterated focus on 'middleweight between 250cc to 750cc' and did not signal intent to go below 350cc near term, noting existing platform potential in 350/450/650.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield: Capacity expansion roadmap (key operational lever)
points: Near-term debottlenecking: Current declared capacity ~1.4 million; additional '500 module per day' kicking in June/July raises run-rate to '~1.6 million plus.' Clarified as per-day modular capacity across facilities; effectively brownfield debottlenecking.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion: INR958 cr capex announced; targeted to lift total annual capacity to ~2.0 million by 'Q2 of FY28.'

Greenfield land bank and timeline: Andhra Pradesh greenfield—MoU signed for 261 acres to support future growth beyond 2.0 million. Tentative execution window shared: '24 to 30 months… fully operational' after land and business case finalization.
Strategic rationale: management framed land as the longest lead-time bottleneck—'The longest lead time is always… land parcel in hand.'

subsections.label: Major strategic development: Proposed Volvo JV for captive vehicle financing
points: Eicher disclosed intent to set up a 50:50 JV with Volvo for 'financing, leasing and other financial services business.'
Capital commitment: Eicher investment 'up to INR750 crores for the 50% stake' into Volvo Financial Services India (VFS India) via fresh equity infusion.
Base business scale: VFS India operating 10+ years with AUM INR1,806 cr and net worth ~INR500 cr (as per management Q&A).

Purpose and positioning: Designed as a 'captive financing arm for VECV, EML and Volvo Group products in India.' Meant to improve conversion and customer experience: 'using financing as a lever for… superior customer experience.'
Volvo brings global product capability; Eicher brings distribution and market knowledge to capture business 'in a more aligned and efficient manner.'
Pacing / risk stance: Management emphasized controlled growth and underwriting discipline—JV will be run 'absolutely independently' with decisions based on 'risk profile.'

Capital runway / medium-term AUM aspiration (management math): With additional capital, leverage capacity (they referenced D/E up to 5:1) could support scaling to ~INR9,000–10,000 cr AUM over ~5 years, and 'we don’t think… additional money at least for the next 5 years.'

Notable change: Vinod Aggarwal stated this is the first time Eicher has 'seriously evaluated entering this business,' enabled by the maturity of the Volvo partnership and Volvo’s global financing success.

subsections.label: Margins, commodity inflation, and pricing actions (key investor debate)
points: Q4 FY26 (RE / EML commentary): CFO quantified Q4 commodity impact: ~90 bps margin headwind.
Pricing action: January price increase delivered ~70 bps; residual ~20 bps mitigated via value-driven cost reduction and mix/model price variance.

Q1/FY27 setup: 'war situation' operating environment and mitigation levers Govindarajan described current environment as 'complex because of the war situation' creating both inflation and availability constraints.
Expected commodity headwind: '~3% to 3.5% on the material cost level impact… incremental in Q1.'

Pricing: RE took ~1.75% price increase in April; management implied roughly ~50% recovery of the inflation via price, remaining to be addressed through: accelerated value engineering / cost reduction ('front ending' projects into July/August), austerity measures, and pre-buy and inventory strategies ('we also have done some prebuy'). Management also confirmed operating leverage is an additional mitigant.
VECV pricing response: VECV announced ~2% price increases effective 1 April, alongside ongoing value engineering, commodity optimization, and transaction price improvements.

subsections.label: Industry and demand outlook: Management stance, headwinds, and confidence markers
points: No formal numeric guidance provided for FY27 volumes/industry, but tone remained constructive: RE: strong inquiry/booking rates; 'working on fulfilling the demand.' VECV: 'traction… quite good,' but environment 'dynamic' with 'global uncertainties… supply chain volatility.'
Short-term disruptions: Elections-driven labor migration and LPG availability created ~2–3 weeks of disturbance; management indicated normalization over recent days with production 'back.'
Europe (RE): 'market adjustment year' with industry degrowth and OBD2B pre-registered inventory overhang slowing fresh billings; RE claims to be holding share in a declining market.
US (RE): tariff-related uncertainty acknowledged but characterized as small exposure: 'only about 3% of the total market for us.'
Brazil: explicitly elevated as strategic growth engine—'Brazil is now our largest and the fastest-growing international market, second only to India,' with ~71% growth and product awards.

VECV recorded its highest ever second quarter sales, with strong performance in light and medium-duty trucks.
Royal Enfield maintained strong growth in international markets, achieving the number 1 position in the SAARC market.
VECV announced an investment of INR544 crores for a new transmission production facility, enhancing capacity.
98% of the energy used at Royal Enfield plants comes from renewable sources, highlighting sustainability efforts.
Eicher Motors is optimistic about continued growth driven by strong demand and strategic initiatives.

EICHERMOT.about: Eicher Motors Limited, incorporated in 1982, is the listed company of the Eicher Group in India and a leading player in the Indian automobile industry and the global leader in middleweight motorcycles. Eicher has a joint venture with Sweden’s AB Volvo to create Volvo Eicher Commercial Vehicles Limited (VECV). VECV is engaged in truck and bus operations, auto components business, and technical consulting services business [1]

quarters.summary: Management guided to strong single-digit domestic industry growth for FY'27 with TVS expected to grow ahead of industry, continued EV and scooter momentum, cautious near-term outlook (Q1-Q2) due to commodity inflation (3-5% of revenue) and supply chain/labor disruptions expected to ease within 2-3 weeks, and continued capex/investment behind capacity expansion, Norton, R&D and new product launches including Hyundai-TVS 3-wheeler EV JDA.

key_figures.label: Price increase offset of commodity inflation

subsections.label: Margin trajectory
points: CFO/CEO emphasized looking at EBITDA trajectory rather than quarter-to-quarter movements; EBITDA moved from 6.5% historically to 13.1% in Q4 FY26.

Improvement driven by scale benefits, better product mix, premiumization, 3-wheeler and international business strengthening realization per vehicle, and cost leverage/amortization of fixed costs over larger base.
Management declined to give explicit margin guidance, stating pricing is only one lever alongside value, TCO, technology and connectivity, and variant strategy.

subsections.label: Investment breakdown FY26
points: Of the INR2,400 crores total investment in FY26, the predominant share was for overseas subsidiary Norton, with products readying for Q2 FY27 launch.
INR200 crores invested in TVS Credit Services.
Strategic investment in Dubai (~INR300 crores) to build infrastructure focused on international markets.

subsections.label: FY27 investment/capex outlook
points: Investments (Norton, TVS Credit, Dubai-type items) expected to be about 70% of FY26 level (i.e., INR500-600 crores lower), as many earlier investments are expected to start yielding revenues/results.
New investment opportunities beyond Norton/Dubai/TVS Credit could arise, to be disclosed closer to decision.

Total capex for TVS Motor in FY27 estimated at ~INR3,500 crores, comprising ~INR2,000 crores product development, ~INR1,000 crores+ capacity expansion (1.5 million unit addition), and additional R&D/testing investment.

key_figures.label: TVS Motor International business sales growth
Indonesia products monthly volume (last year avg)

subsections.label: TVS Credit performance
points: TVS Credit achieved record PBT of INR1,248 crores in FY26 driven by sustained growth in disbursements supported by improved consumption sentiment and traction across all retail financing segments.
2-wheeler category witnessed strong demand aided by steady recovery across urban and semi-urban markets; increasing EV adoption supported by broad affordability and good finance penetration.
Consumer durable financing remained steady driven by seasonal purchases and increased discretionary spending.

Company maintained focus on risk-calibrated growth via prudent, proactive underwriting, calibrated credit policy restrictions and sharper credit matrices; overall portfolio quality improved via reduction in total credit cost and GNPA.
TVS Credit continues to focus on leveraging technology, digital transformation, deeper customer relationships while maintaining strong risk management, with external credit rating of AA+.

subsections.label: Domestic portfolio mix outlook
points: EV, scooters, premium and super-premium categories expected to grow well in FY27; economy category expected to face greater challenge due to inflation/fuel price sensitivity among that customer base.
TVS's scooter category share (including EV, SSP) is ~38% currently and is expected to move above 40%.
Strong brands cited: Jupiter, Ntorq, 125, 150 (150 recently launched with outstanding response); Orbiter and iQube doing well in EV; Apache/Ronin doing extremely well in premium/super-premium.
New moped with alloy wheel doing extremely well, indicating customers are willing to pay for added value even amid demand challenges.

Ronin has grown steadily from 2,000 to 4,000 to 8,000+ units/month over the last 3 years domestically, with pull starting in international markets (e.g., Indonesia); management expects it to soon cross 10,000/month and become a long-standing premium brand like Apache.

subsections.label: EV 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler business
points: TVS iQube S launched with 4.7 kilowatt battery, 175 km range, new color graphics; iQube has driven electric mobility adoption in India with 900,000+ cumulative customers.
EV 3-wheeler VAHAN share continuously increasing; company confident of reaching a prominent position in EV passenger and EV cargo segments this financial year.
EV monthly production has moved from average 30,000-32,000 units/month last year to ~40,000 currently, headed toward 50,000/month.

key_figures.label: King Kargo Heavy Duty CNG top speed

subsections.label: New product launches
points: Orbiter V1 (1.8 kW) has done well and targets a different set of customers; now available in 2 ranges - V1 (1.8 kW) and V2 (3.1 kW).
Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) launched across EV portfolio, allowing customers to subscribe to battery usage instead of paying full battery cost upfront.

TVS King Kargo Heavy Duty CNG launched, built on durability and ease of operation with robust leaf spring suspension, ergonomic cabin, top speed of 62 km/h, excellent ground clearance and turning radius; initial response promising and expected to take a prominent position in the cargo category alongside the cargo EV variant.
TVS iQube S launched with 4.7 kW battery and 175 km range, positioned as a favorite EV for families, with new color graphics.

subsections.label: Norton
points: Company invested in Norton since 2021 in building new products; unveiled products at EICMA, Milan with excellent feedback.
New Norton models coming: Manx, Manx R, Atlas, and Atlas GT; more details closer to launch.
Models will be available in Europe and some in India; FY27, especially Q2, seen as a very important period for Norton launches.
Norton products are getting ready at Hosur plant and Solihull; Solihull will manufacture a high-end model while other models will be made in India (Hosur), leveraging India in a big way.
Management views Norton launches as key to redefining the super-premium class globally and a turnaround year for the next phase of growth for TVS and Norton.

subsections.label: R&D and innovation focus
points: Company continues to invest in technology, R&D, innovation and brand building even amid near-term cost pressures.
TVS's strength cited as R&D, software, digital and connected services, driving continuous product investment as a medium-to-long-term growth strategy.
No specific motorcycle category launch other than existing lineup indicated for next 12 months; management reiterated continuous investment behind technology and models that delight customers.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion plan
points: Company is increasing capacity by another 1.5 million units to reach ~8.3 million units given strong demand; this is the first time such significant capacity is being added in the next 12 months.
Work on capacity addition already started in the last quarter of FY26; reviewed quarter-by-quarter.
Company is also planning capacity additions for FY28 and FY29.
Management's stated priority: capacity will not be a constraint to growing ahead of industry.

subsections.label: Norton manufacturing footprint
points: Solihull (UK) plant will manufacture a high-end Norton model; other models will be manufactured in India, primarily leveraging the Hosur plant.

subsections.label: International business performance and outlook
points: Africa, Asia, LatAm remain key regions; Africa has done extremely well; company now focusing on growing LatAm with encouraging traction seen in many markets.
Asia doing well; Sri Lanka fully back on track; Nepal doing extremely well; Bangladesh has undergone some changes with exports expected to start soon.
Q4 exports performance reflects sustained momentum with improved product mix; 3-wheeler export segment has started showing improvement.
Demand for TVS products is strong across every international market; company closely monitoring geopolitical/war-related effects but confident of continued pull for products.
Africa is preferred market for HLX series 100/125/155; demand is so strong company is currently unable to fully meet it.

LatAm growth is ahead of industry (market share gains), but management indicated it will take 2-3 years to build good distributors, brand investment and visibility; LatAm is TVS's focus area going forward alongside strengthening Africa and Middle East (still seen as having huge headroom).
LatAm strategy will use a full portfolio (premium via Apache/Ronin plus entry-level and country-specific models), similar to how Indonesia products (Bebek & Skubek) are performing well.
Company sees opportunity to leverage EV 2-wheelers (iQube, Orbiter) internationally, especially in Asia where response has been good; Orbiter is now being introduced in Asian markets.

Domestic growth in FY26 was aided by GST rate reduction from 28% to 18%; India's large consumer base (1.4 billion) and rural/self-income customers seen as structural demand driver for 2-wheelers; government infrastructure investment (roads) also supportive.

subsections.label: Supply chain disruptions
points: Supply chain disruption emerged post geopolitical unrest (West Asia conflict), with rising gas prices and energy costs affecting commodity prices and availability.

Company keeps only 21-30 days of dealer stock domestically (cash-and-carry model), making it critical to ramp production quickly to meet strong retail demand; delays in energy/raw materials can affect production.
Labor challenges seen across India (not only South), particularly among Tier 2 suppliers; Tier 1 suppliers managing better; company supporting Tier 2 suppliers.

May production improving versus April; channel stock has started improving this month due to better production in first 10 days of May; expect normal 21-30 day range to be restored by end of month/first week of June.
Management expects to be fully out of Tier 2 disruption within 2-3 weeks.
International logistics facing ~15% increase in lead times (about 8-10 days delay) due to container availability challenges, requiring closer planning and support to distributors.
Company working closely with distributors to manage transit delays and support ordering/planning given high demand pull for products in every market.

subsections.label: Competitive/category positioning
points: TVS positioning across EV, scooter, premium/super-premium (Apache, Ronin) segments seen as strong growth drivers versus economy category which faces higher headwinds from inflation and fuel prices.
Value-added products (e.g., new moped with alloy wheel) continue to find demand despite overall category challenges, indicating customers are willing to pay for value.
Company emphasizes pricing as only one lever among multiple (TCO, technology, connectivity, variant strategy) versus pure price-based competition.

subsections.label: Hyundai-TVS Joint Development Agreement
points: TVS Motor signed a joint development agreement with Hyundai Motor Company to commercialize an electric 3-wheeler.
Hyundai Motor will lead design and co-develop the EV 3-wheeler, leveraging its R&D expertise, advanced mobility technologies and human-centric design approach.
TVS Motor will co-develop using its leading-edge electric platform, extensive 3-wheeler engineering expertise and deep local market understanding.

Management declined to give specific timeline/revenue contribution details at this stage, indicating more details will be shared closer to launch; expects the partnership to contribute positively to the company's overall EBITDA journey.

subsections.label: Dubai strategic investment
points: Company established a strategic investment/infrastructure in Dubai with significant focus on international markets, with ~INR300 crores invested cumulatively over a couple of prior quarters.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical risks
points: Ongoing West Asia conflict cited as a headwind affecting commodity prices (steel, aluminum, crude oil derivatives) and input costs, plus supply chain disruption.
Commodity/input cost inflation estimated at 3-5% of revenue for Q1 FY27, described as 'unprecedented' with significant impact concentrated in a single quarter compared to past similar situations.
Company has been able to offset about 35% of price increases needed via pricing actions; continues to monitor and pass on price increases in both domestic and international markets.
El Nino risk could moderate rainfall despite reservoir water levels currently 16% higher, which is good for Kharif season but bears watching for Q3/Q4 impact on rural demand.
Geopolitical situation (war-related) affecting international markets broadly across the industry, not just TVS; company closely monitoring.
Labor availability challenges across India, especially among Tier 2 suppliers, though expected to be resolved within 2-3 weeks.
International logistics delays (~15% increase in lead time, 8-10 days) due to container availability challenges creating distributor planning issues.
Management flagged general 'unprecedented' cost environment requiring close monitoring and countermeasures over the next two quarters (Q1, Q2 FY27).

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Company expects a good single-digit growth for the domestic industry in FY27, with potential for better growth in H2 if conditions improve; TVS expects to grow ahead of the industry.
EV, scooters, super-premium categories expected to grow well; economy category faces greater challenges from inflation/fuel prices.
International market momentum from Q4 FY26 expected to continue through FY27, with company confident of growing ahead of industry despite geopolitical challenges and logistics delays.
Company will remain cautious in Q1 and Q2 FY27 due to raw material availability timing issues and supply chain disruption, though demand itself is not a concern.
Company reiterated it does not give explicit margin guidance but expects EBITDA margin trajectory to keep improving via scale, product mix, premiumization and cost reduction.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR3,500 crores for TVS Motor (product development ~INR2,000 crores, capacity expansion INR1,000+ crores, plus R&D/testing investment).
FY27 investments in overseas subsidiaries/Norton/TVS Credit/Dubai-type items expected to be about 70% of FY26 level (~INR500-600 crores lower than INR2,400 crores).

key_takeaways: TVS Motor Company surpassed all its previous highs and achieved an all-round record performance, achieved the highest ever sales volume, revenue and profit in FY25-26.

Sales volume grew from 4.7 million units to 5.9 million units, a 24% growth. Revenue grew from INR36,251 crores to INR47,270 crores, a 30% growth and operating PBT grew from INR3,563 crores to INR4,975 crores, a 40% growth.
Company's EBITDA grew by 37% to INR6,079 crores; EBITDA margin improved by 60 basis points to 12.9% vis-a-vis last year's 12.3%.
Q4 company achieved the highest ever revenue of INR12,808 crores, a growth of 36% over last year, and achieved the highest EBITDA of 13.1%.
TVS Credit services achieved a record level of PBT of INR1,248 crores in FY25-26; book size is now INR30,631 crores.
TVS Motor International business recorded highest ever sales of 15.8 lakh units in FY26, a growth of 33% year-on-year.
TVS Motor signed a joint development agreement with Hyundai Motor Company to commercialize an electric 3-wheeler.

Company facing near-term challenges from commodity price inflation (3-5% of revenue), supply chain disruption (labor, raw materials) and geopolitical issues (West Asia conflict), but expects to overcome these within 2-3 weeks and remains confident of growing ahead of industry in FY27.
Company is expanding 2-wheeler/3-wheeler capacity by 1.5 million units to reach ~8.3 million units to meet demand; FY27 capex guided at ~INR3,500 crores.

quarters.summary: TVS Motor Company expects continued growth in Q4 FY26, driven by strong domestic and international demand, premiumization, and a focus on cost reduction and product innovation.

subsections.label: Profitability and Cost Management
points: The company's operating EBITDA margin improved by 120 basis points to 13.1% from 11.9% in Q3 of last year.
On a normalized basis, Q3 FY '25 EBITDA would have been at 12.4%, indicating a year-on-year margin improvement of 70 basis points and a quarter-on-quarter improvement of 40 basis points.
The company recognized INR41 crores as an exceptional item towards the past service cost arising from the new labor codes.

subsections.label: Demand Drivers
points: The low inflation drove demand across product categories, leading to increased sales, deeper market penetration, and enhanced market share.
The company saw a successful festive season with robust demand.
Rural grew by almost 19% and urban by about 21% in Q3 FY26.

subsections.label: Product Performance
points: Scooters have really done well, with a 40% category share of the overall 2-wheeler industry.
Premium and super-premium segments are growing faster than the industry.
The entry-level segment is not growing as much.

subsections.label: Norton and New Products
points: Norton is building the lineup unveiled in EICMA 2025, targeting the super premium category.
The new Manx and Atlas families position TVS in the premium, high-emotion luxury motorcycle segment.
TVS is gearing up for the launch of new Norton products in the Indian markets.

subsections.label: Capacity and Supply Chain
points: There were challenges in EV production due to magnet availability, but the situation is improving.
TVS is investing in capacity increases to meet demand.
The company aims to maintain dealer stock at 21 to 30 days to ensure fresh products for customers.

subsections.label: International Market Performance
points: Demand in Africa continues to grow on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
LatAm has grown over last year, and this growth momentum will continue.
Asia region is doing well, with Sri Lanka coming back in a big way.
Europe continues to face challenges and is not growing.

subsections.label: Commodity Inflation and Pricing
points: There are increases in aluminum, copper, zinc, platinum, palladium, and rhodium prices.
TVS has taken about 0.2% to 0.3% price increases to offset commodity inflation.
The company focuses on a combination of scale benefits, cost reduction, and product mix to manage inflation.

subsections.label: Market Strategy
points: TVS Credit continued to drive penetration of existing products, expand product offerings, and scale up distribution.
The company maintained its focus on risk-calibrated growth across product categories, building a diversified book.
TVS Credit disbursed loans to over 41 lakh new customers, bringing its total customer base to nearly 2.3 crores.

subsections.label: Investments and Strategic Focus
points: TVS invested INR200 crores in TVS Credit Services and INR60 crores to INR70 crores in Norton for pre-marketing activities.
The company is investing in the ION PT TVS project and the e-bike business.
TVS has strategically invested in Dubai for international market focus.

subsections.label: Commodity Price Risks
points: Commodity prices, including precious metals, have seen increases, impacting costs.
The company is managing these risks through pricing strategies and cost management.

subsections.label: Q4 Outlook
points: TVS expects Q4 to perform extremely well, driven by GST benefits and strong domestic and international demand.
The company anticipates EV penetration to improve going forward, with products like iQube and Orbiter performing well.
TVS is confident of growing ahead of the industry in both domestic and international markets.

The company's operating revenue grew by 27% to INR12,476 crores in Q3 FY26.
TVS Credit disbursed loans to over 41 lakh new customers, expanding its customer base to nearly 2.3 crores.
The company is gearing up for the launch of new Norton products in the Indian markets.
TVS expects Q4 to perform extremely well, driven by GST benefits and strong demand.
The company is confident of growing ahead of the industry in both domestic and international markets.

subsections.label: Overhead Costs
points: Other expenses include variable expenses such as packing and freight, which increased by about INR 120 crores due to the festive season.
R&D expenses increased by about INR 20-25 crores.
Marketing expenses increased by about INR 65 crores due to new product launches.

subsections.label: Festive Season Impact
points: The festive season has shown positive momentum with VAHAN industry growth of 24% and TVS growth above 32%.

subsections.label: Product Launches
points: Launched TVS Orbiter, a smart, sustainable urban EV commute with a range of 158 kilometers and priced at INR 99,900.
Launched TVS King Kargo HD EV for urban logistics with a range of 156 kilometers.
Launched TVS Ntorq 150, India's quickest Hyper Sport Scooter with a top speed of 104 km/h.
Launched Apache RTX, an adventure rally tourer.

subsections.label: Margins, Pricing, and Cost Levers
points: Material cost ratio: Q4 71.4% of revenue (+80 bps YoY); FY26 also 71.4% (+10 bps).

Pricing actions: Jan price increase ~1% supported Q4 realization.
Q1 FY27 price increase 1%–1.5%, with uncertainty on sustaining through the quarter.
Commodity pressure: Management flagged 'significant increase… predominantly steel' entering Q1; refused to quantify magnitude ('too early to give a range').
Mitigation toolkit: value engineering, e-sourcing, supplier negotiations, turnover discounts; plus broader OPEX scrutiny.
CFO: cross-functional teams reviewing 'each of the operating expense… head-wise individually' to drive reductions.

Operating leverage absence in Q4: CFO attributed to one-time provisioning for performance-related bonuses and commodity turbulence; acknowledged analyst observation that Q4 didn’t show typical leverage.
Other cost risks into FY27: potential inflation in transportation expense (fuel-linked), conversion costs, and FX (rupee weakening) impacting 'other expenditure.'
Industry pricing discipline: CEO expects discipline to strengthen; 'industry… should look at taking multiple price hikes during the year' given input inflation.

key_takeaways: Demand is being underwritten by replacement + GST-driven TCO reset, with management repeatedly emphasizing baseline resilience despite diesel noise and localized disruptions.

Near-term margin risk is real and concentrated in commodities (steel) plus fuel-linked opex; company response is measured price increases (1–1.5%) + intensified internal cost programs, but with explicit limits if commodities spike sharply.
Mix and product cycle are turning more favorable if mining/infra-led tippers and multi-axles accelerate and new high-HP products ramp—management expects visible share benefit from Q2.

EV strategy moved from 'investment' to 'execution' milestone with Switch India profitability and a tangible battery pack manufacturing timeline; cell manufacturing remains optional/phase-3 contingent on demand.
Capital deployment is flexible and need-based, with likely incremental support for financing and E-MaaS subsidiaries, while Switch India reduces funding burden due to profitability.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was a record quarter (highest-ever quarterly revenue) delivered against a genuinely tough external business environment, with revenue +17% YoY and +3% QoQ, EBITDA +26% YoY, EBITDA margin +60bps YoY, and normalized PAT +55% YoY. Growth was broad-based across Wire Harness (India + NA CV recovery), Modules & Polymers (restructuring benefits offsetting commodity shocks), Aerospace (>20% YoY growth) and Consumer Electronics (large capex build-out with faster ramp expected). Management flagged copper and polymer commodity inflation as near-term headwinds with a pass-through lag, continued Europe restructuring, aggressive but disciplined capital allocation (leverage at an all-time low of 0.8x), and continued M&A-led diversification (Auto Crews, Nexen, Utaka) with intent to eventually list emerging businesses like consumer electronics independently within the five-year plan.

subsections.label: Highest-ever quarterly revenue
points: Management reported "our highest ever quarterly revenue in Q1 FY27", notable because historically Q1 has always seen a sequential decline over Q4, but this time Q1 exceeded Q4—positioned as evidence of broad-based momentum.

subsections.label: Profitability
points: EBITDA growth outpaced revenue growth.
Management emphasized "There was no one-off items impacting PAT this quarter."
Adjusted for the normalization in the base quarter, Q1 FY27 PAT grew 102% on recorded basis.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation, Balance Sheet
points: Capex for the quarter was ₹1,614 crore, consistent with guidance of ₹6,000 crore ±10% over four years.
3 plants operationalized in the quarter; 13 facilities under development; 10 expected to go operational during this year.
Leverage improved to 0.8x, described as "all-time low," below the policy ceiling of 2.5x and internal aspiration of <1.5x.

subsections.label: Management tone / confidence
points: "These results were delivered against a genuinely tough external business environment."
Despite commodities/logistics volatility, "we were able to maintain and of course improve… margins."

subsections.label: Wire Harness: India strength + North America CV recovery; margin resilience despite copper
points: Management cited "strong momentum in India, combined with a recovery in the North American commercial vehicle business."
North American CV wire harness revenue grew 31% YoY.
Wire harness margins held up better than analysts expected.
Geographic/FX mix dampening: copper impact was "very, very high in India" (including rupee depreciation) but less severe elsewhere (euro translation effects).
Structural cost actions + operating leverage: teams have been "chipping away at the cost base" during China/US slowdowns; now benefiting as US improves.

subsections.label: Modules & Polymers / Vision Systems / Integrated Assemblies
points: Modules & Polymer described as the key driver of margin improvement via multi-quarter restructuring undertaken over the last 1.5 years to align footprint "with the market," enabling absorption of inflation and YoY margin improvement.

Restructuring rationale: post-acquisition Europe footprint plus underutilization due to EV demand not meeting expectations ("EVs did not come out as expected"); actions included consolidating sites, improving utilization, and trimming some headcount.

Polymer input shock in Germany driven by crude-linked inflation, with polymer prices up 55% YoY and 66% sequentially, impacted "IMTP and regional system divisions"; despite this, both divisions held flat to improving margins via cost optimization.

Management refused to quantify quarterly commodity headwind/offset precisely, citing complexity of many grades of engineered plastics, hundreds of SKUs, and program-level netting that often happens later: "we would really be able to talk more about that in Q4," noting Q4 typically sees nettings/true-ups and stronger performance.

subsections.label: Aerospace: scaling with improving visibility
points: Aerospace revenue grew more than 20% YoY.
Order book grew 17% since FY26-end, giving "strong visibility on future growth."
