subsections.label: Third facility
points: "Remains on track for commissioning in the third quarter of FY27" (elsewhere management aimed for later in current calendar year).
Adds "upstream integration capabilities."

subsections.label: Capex and capacity build-out
points: Total consumer electronics capex across GF1/GF2/GF3 clarified at ~₹7,500 crore over the remaining 2-3 years, versus an initial figure cited as ₹65 billion spread over 3 years.
Roughly one-third of the consumer electronics capex has already been incurred.
GF3 designed for 40 million units annually at full capacity.
Exit FY26 run-rate capacity is 16 million units, targeted to scale to ~56 million units total capacity by FY29.

subsections.label: Operating model and ramp dynamics (vs auto)
points: Ramp expected to be materially faster than automotive: "It does ramp much faster, unlike the automotive business… it takes about two years… Here you'll see a much faster launch… in the next couple of months."
Order patterns: consumer electronics "does not have such long order tails… It happens more in the same year itself," with orders "currently in negotiation."
Management asked investors for time: "request for another two quarters for you to really see the impact."

subsections.label: Ownership and funding
points: JV partner holds a 10% equity stake with an option to increase to 49%, but is currently "quite happy at that 10%" despite the option.
Company funds 90% of the equity share.
Management would not speculate on partner stepping up; will update if it changes.

subsections.label: Product scope and capacity fungibility
points: Current focus is glass products with a "17-stage process," high technical sensitivity (scrap/scratch rejection).
Existing capacities are "already completely taken by the customer that we have," suggesting early utilization is committed.
Management did not provide current utilization/capacity for GF1/GF2 beyond calling them "a fraction" and "prototypes… small batch productions."

subsections.label: China OEM mix
points: Historically started with international OEMs; now selectively adding local Chinese OEMs while staying "extremely picky" and not chasing unprofitable volume ("we do not chase top line where we cannot make the profitability margins").

subsections.label: Chinese OEMs expanding to Europe
points: Management claimed they are already engaging; "we've already been visited by them… discussing supplies," seeing advantage due to existing China relationships and global footprint.

subsections.label: Regulatory tailwinds and product content expansion: Vision Systems in India
points: On India's emerging safety/monitoring regulations (e.g., driver drowsiness/monitoring), management affirmed tailwinds and tied the Auto Crews acquisition directly to the opportunity.
Auto Crews has interior digital mirrors and driver monitoring systems for buses; requires localization/homologation but provides a "very strong platform" to scale into India as regulations expand.

subsections.label: Capital independence / value unlocking
points: Clear intent to incubate and then separate: emerging businesses should "stand on their own feet," potentially including separate listing: "Yes, absolutely."
Timing indicated within the five-year plan, "for us the faster the better," but tied to execution and market readiness; no firm FY28 commitment.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth: technology and adjacency expansion
points: Announced acquisition: Shenzhen Auto Crews (interior/exterior digital vision and monitoring systems), expanding next-gen mobility content: camera monitoring systems, "folded full display mirrors," around-view, driver monitoring, dash cams.
Completed (July): Nexen's Autoelectric and Utaka Geiken.
Nexen adds global PV/CV wiring harness and "opens up cross-selling possibilities," strengthens OEM relationships.
Utaka adds "completely new products," expected to take longer to synergize.
Nexen housed under a new emerging vertical: Vehicle Systems, spanning products such as exhaust systems, brake systems and others.

Newly acquired businesses are not yet at benchmark margins (e.g., not necessarily at ~11% EBITDA), but the objective is to "transform… over the period," citing prior playbooks (MWSI, PKC) and purchasing/synergy leverage from Motherson's larger scale.

subsections.label: New growth arenas
points: Robotics, automation, AI, semiconductors, humanoids: management said "Answer is all of them."
Confirmed existing semiconductor supplies (small currently) and potential JVs under discussion (not disclosed).
Claimed "won small orders" supporting humanoids production (niche, early).
Internal automation referenced via in-house robotics entity "Robis," using automation/AI to reinforce "source locally, produce locally, supply locally" as logistics/currency volatility rises.

subsections.label: Macro context (used to frame resilience)
points: South Asia/India called a "clear bright spot."
Global light vehicle industry declined 1.8% YoY, with China light vehicle industry down 3.1% YoY.
Commercial vehicles: CV industry grew 5.4% YoY, with North America recovery supporting growth; outlook "remains favorable through FY27."

subsections.label: Commodity volatility and pass-through lag
points: Copper prices rose 4% sequentially in Q1 FY27, following sequential increases of 13% in Q3 FY26 and 16% in Q4 FY26, and were up 40% YoY.
Copper costs are "typically passed on… with a lag of one or two quarters" (elsewhere said 3-6 months lag).
Polymers (Germany): extreme YoY/QoQ spikes tied to crude/geopolitics.
Management noted occasional extra costs incurred to ensure timely delivery in some instances.

subsections.label: Europe operational complexity
points: Restructuring is ongoing; potential for more actions this year ("opportunity perhaps to do more in this… financial year"), but detailed quantification deferred to year-end true-ups.

subsections.label: Consumer electronics disclosure constraint
points: Management repeatedly declined to give near-term detailed capacity/utilization/revenue projections; emphasized that program mix and customer negotiations determine realized economics.

quarters.summary: Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd achieved record revenues in FY26, with significant growth in emerging businesses and a strong order book providing future growth visibility. The company continues to focus on capacity expansion and strategic partnerships to drive growth.

subsections.label: FY26 headline performance and quality of earnings
points: Record scale: FY26 delivered the highest ever quarterly and annual revenues.
Profitability inflection in Q4 attributed to improving profitability in emerging businesses, particularly lighting and electronics and aerospace.
Margins held despite inflation due to operational excellence initiatives, cost optimization programs, and improving efficiencies across plants.

subsections.label: Balance sheet strengthening
points: Leverage ratio at an all-time low of 0.8x, reinforcing the stated policy of <2.5x and internal aspiration of <1.5x.

subsections.label: Order book, portfolio mix, and strategic roadmap (Vision 2030 / 3CX10 / D.E.M.A.L.)
points: All-time-high book business of USD 96 billion, providing strong visibility for future growth.
Diversified across PV, CV, off-highway, rolling stock, 2W, and geographies.
Management emphasized emerging markets rising in the mix due to growth and manufacturing ecosystems supporting exports under 'globally local'.

subsections.label: Consumer electronics (within Lighting & Electronics / emerging businesses)
points: FY26 revenues increased ~7.5x YoY; Q4 revenues +46% sequentially after the second facility went live in Q3.
Achieved Q4 production run-rate aligned to annual guidance of 14–16 million units.
Third facility (GF3) commissioning remains on track for Q3 FY27.
GF3 described as the group’s largest facility, a size of 33 football fields.

subsections.label: Aerospace (non-automotive adjacency with accelerating scale)
points: FY26 revenues +40% YoY; order book increased >20% to USD 1.6bn.
Won orders across metallic parts, subassemblies, and wire harness for business jets and rotary wing aircraft.
Two new India facilities expected to come up in Q1 FY27 to serve the existing USD 1.6bn backlog.

subsections.label: Wiring harness and broader automotive operations
points: Wiring harness division saw ~170 bps QoQ margin expansion despite copper inflation.
North America recovery optionality expected to support further improvement.

subsections.label: Capacity and ramp characteristics
points: Third facility (GF3) commissioning remains on track for Q3 FY27.
Management emphasized electronics ramps faster than auto: orders can move 'straight 0 to 100' once the season/program starts.

subsections.label: Capital allocation, capex pipeline, and shareholder returns
points: FY26 capex: INR 5,911 crore (~49% of EBITDA), allocated to growth, backward integration, and maintenance.
FY27 capex guidance: ~INR 6,000 crore ±10%, with 50% growth / 50% maintenance.
16 facilities under development globally, 13 scheduled to come on stream in FY27; all are in emerging markets.

subsections.label: Supply chain risk mitigation
points: 'Globally local manufacturing strategy' reduced dependence on long-distance supply chains.
Red Sea disruptions had minimal impact.
For customer-nominated components: 'back-to-back supply arrangements' to mitigate escalation.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth pipeline and transaction timelines
points: Atsumitec integration: FY26 was the full first year, progress pleased.
Completed acquisition of another Honda San asset.
Yutaka Giken acquisition on track to close by end of H1 FY27.
Nexans automotive harness business closing expected end of June, beginning of July.

subsections.label: Cost headwinds, pass-through mechanics, and operational resilience
points: Copper prices increased 16% sequentially in Q4, ~38% YoY.
Middle East tensions led to crude-linked inflation late in the quarter.
Polymer prices in Germany rose significantly post conflict escalation.
Raw materials have long-term pass-through arrangements with major customers; timing lag of 1–2 quarters acknowledged.
Energy/gas/freight and some overhead-type costs are a matter of negotiations, but management expressed confidence in recovery due to strong OEM relationships.

subsections.label: Vision 2030 framing
points: Target reiterated: USD 108bn gross revenues by 2030.
ROCE moderated to 16.1% due to capacity build; aspiration reiterated: 40% ROCE across businesses over time.

guidance_ledger.statement: Targeting 108 billion in gross revenues by 2030.
Aiming for a 40% ROCE for the group.
FY27 capex guidance: ~INR 6,000 crore ±10%, with 50% growth / 50% maintenance.
The majority of Greenfields are expected to come on stream by the second half of FY27 and will contribute towards growth in the FY27 year.
The third plant is expected to commence operations in the third quarter of FY27, doubling current capacity.
Expect the leverage ratio to be around 0.9 by the end of the year.

quarters.summary: Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd reported its highest ever quarterly revenues in Q3 FY '26, driven by strong growth in consumer electronics and aerospace segments, and maintained a comfortable leverage ratio of 1.1x. The company is focused on expanding its capacity with 12 Greenfield projects and aims to achieve its Vision 2030 targets.

subsections.label: Financial Discipline
points: The company maintained financial discipline with a net leverage of 1.1x, well within its financial policy.

subsections.label: PAT Normalizations
points: Normalizations to the reported PAT include a post-tax impact of approximately INR 37 crores, related to the new labour code implementation (INR 25 crores) and costs for transformative measures in Europe (INR 12 crores).

subsections.label: Industry Trends
points: The global PV production outlook remains encouraging with FY '27 production projected to grow to approximately 93 million units, up from around 91 million units expected in FY '26.

subsections.label: Consumer Electronics and Aerospace Growth
points: The consumer electronics business recorded a 75% quarter-on-quarter revenue growth, with meaningful margin improvement in Q3.
The aerospace business continues to gain traction, growing at a 41% year-on-year growth rate in the third quarter.

subsections.label: Greenfield Projects
points: The company announced two new Greenfield facilities, one in Vision Systems in India and the other in Wiring Harness in Morocco, bringing the total to 12 Greenfield projects across emerging markets.

subsections.label: Acquisitions and Partnerships
points: The company signed an agreement to acquire 100% of the wiring harness business of Nexans Autoelectric, expected to be completed by the end of H1 FY '26.
A joint venture with Egtronics Company Limited focused on manufacturing clean mobility electronics was announced.

subsections.label: Industry Conditions
points: Despite dynamic industry conditions where global PV production volumes have de-grown year-on-year, the company delivered strong financial performance.

subsections.label: Future Outlook
points: The company remains confident in its ability to deliver long-term sustainable value for all stakeholders and is focused on achieving its Vision 2030 targets.

guidance_ledger.statement: Leverage ratio expected to be around 0.9 by the end of the year.
Target of 108 billion USD in gross revenues by 2030.
Maintain a 40% ROCE target for the group by 2030.

quarters.summary: Management remains anchored in strategic resilience for the remainder of FY27, expecting continued growth aided by RBI's raised GDP forecast, strong CAFE Phase 3/CV ADAS regulatory tailwinds, sustained margin trajectory (~14%), continuing localization, and new JV ramp-ups (TACO e-axle JV and TSF/Wheels-Brakes India air systems JV), while flagging monsoon variability, El Nino risk, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, and volatile commodity/sourcing environment as key downside risks. Next quarter automotive industry growth is expected to be a resilient 8%, driven by festive demand, stronger rural cash flows and ongoing infrastructure activity.

subsections.label: Revenue drivers
points: YoY growth driven mainly by higher sales in Power Solutions and 2-wheeler Powersports segments.
QoQ growth driven by strong performance in Power Solutions and mobility aftermarket segments.

subsections.label: EBITDA drivers
points: Improvement in EBITDA margin YoY primarily driven by growth in revenue and optimization of expenses.
QoQ EBITDA increase due to revenue growth.

subsections.label: PAT drivers
points: April-June '25 quarter had an exceptional item of profit on sale of video solutions, access and intrusion and communication systems under the Building Technologies segment, which caused the reported YoY PAT decline.
Excluding this exceptional item, PAT grew 9.9% YoY.
QoQ PAT growth mainly due to revenue growth and higher mutual fund gains, which are taxed at a lesser rate.

subsections.label: Margin sustainability
points: Management attributes sustained margin improvement over the last ~2 years to continuous improvement in operational excellence, continued increase in localization content, favourable volume growth, productivity improvements, and favourable product mix.
CFO added that the company benefits from Bosch's worldwide purchasing organization, which helps navigate a volatile sourcing market and maintain margins.
Management stated no one-off items in employee costs or other expenses in the quarter.
Product mix expected to remain favourable through the rest of the year (FY27).

subsections.label: Purchase mix / localization
points: Broader purchase goods as % of sales reduced by ~200 bps over last 2-3 years from 40%+ level.
Sourcing from parent within that basket has risen to ~53%, a decadal high, versus declining proportion from local subsidiaries.
Management attributed this partly to a surge in volumes; localization plans remain on track and localization content will continue to increase, with updates to be shared in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Bosch Chassis Systems acquisition financials
points: No goodwill or amortization expense associated with the Bosch Chassis Systems acquisition.

Sale of Chassis Systems business was completed in July; consolidation is underway, and full numbers/segment breakup (2-wheeler, 4-wheeler, CV, tractor, export, aftermarket) will be shared in upcoming quarters.
Consolidated results including Chassis Systems will be published starting next quarter.

subsections.label: JV order books
points: Management stated they entered the TACO e-axle JV only after securing a healthy order book from both Bosch and TACO sides.
For the TSF/air systems JV, customer discussions are starting in September at the IAA auto show; more order book detail to be shared in a quarter.
Management declined to disclose specific order win details for the JVs at this time.

subsections.label: Power Solutions division
points: Achieved strong growth, significantly outperforming the broader automotive market, driven by robust demand across passenger cars, commercial vehicles and tractors.
Growth largely attributed to volume effect and some new product introductions over the last 2 quarters.
Focus on navigating evolving regulatory landscape including CAFE Phase 3 and ADAS implementation in commercial vehicles.

Received Delivery Excellence award from a leading commercial vehicle manufacturer; awarded Best Quality Performance, Best in Technology and Innovation, and named Business Partner of the Year by a prominent tractor and utility vehicle maker.
Upcoming CAFE Phase 3 regulation (coming April) and CV ADAS (coming October next year) seen as further growth boosts.

subsections.label: 2-wheeler and Powersports division
points: Successfully met a surge in market demand with zero production disruptions for customers despite geopolitical and supply chain complexities.
Advanced safety systems integrated into the first electric motorcycle from a leading 2-wheeler manufacturer for its commercial launch.
Showcased latest innovations across powertrain, safety and electrification at the ACMA Mobility Foundation Technology Show.
Honoured by a leading global 2-wheeler manufacturer for development speed and engineering support on a flagship scooter platform.
2-wheeler business growth YoY driven by growth in value-added EMS products, increased sales to premium motorcycle platforms and steady demand from major domestic OEMs.
QoQ growth driven by higher production volumes from 2-wheeler OEMs supported by channel inventory replenishments.
Management confirmed market share gains in premium 2-wheeler platforms via new product introductions to new OEMs, not merely a mix shift.

subsections.label: Mobility aftermarket division
points: Independent aftermarket business was a standout performer, achieving its highest ever monthly sales in June.
Original equipment segment also delivered robust growth.
Performance driven by strong contributions from lubricants, batteries, spark plugs and braking systems, and rotating machines.

Strategically accelerating workshop programs and expanding portfolio with new product launches: Tulix LED range of advanced lighting solutions, Prithvi heavy-duty commercial vehicle battery, PC clutches and suspension systems.

Management believes recent strategic corrections (product launches, workshop expansion, market approach) make current high single-digit growth momentum sustainable going forward, after a prior low-growth period.

subsections.label: Consumer goods / Power tools division
points: Consumer goods business grew YoY driven by strong demand for tools supported by marketing campaigns, but declined QoQ due to seasonal factors.
Strong sequential growth and accelerated demand in construction and automotive sectors; online sales channels continuing to expand share of total sales.
Strategic focus centered on driving cordless conversion, extending product portfolio, and expanding market reach to key customers, key users and small-to-medium enterprises.

subsections.label: Automotive industry demand trends (Q1 FY27)
points: Indian automotive industry concluded Q1 FY27 on a resilient note despite geopolitical disruptions in West Asia, supported by strong domestic demand, lower GST rates and favourable base effect vs Q1 FY26.
PV demand remained strong despite geopolitical tensions, elevated inflation within RBI's target band, and heat waves; supported by sustained SUV preference and healthy consumer sentiment.

HCV segment maintained healthy demand despite an INR7.5/litre increase in diesel price, supported by stable freight activity, steady replacement demand and sustained spending in construction/infrastructure; momentum in steel and cement provided a strong foundation for further growth.
LCV demand remained robust, driven by healthy last-mile logistics, sustained e-commerce and FMCG demand, and a low base effect.
3-wheeler sales maintained strong growth momentum, supported by steady passenger mobility demand and increasing last-mile connectivity.
EV segment continued to expand market share, driven by attractive operating economics and lower running costs.
Tractor demand remained resilient despite concerns over uneven monsoon, supported by healthy farm cash flows from a strong Rabi harvest and pre-Kharif farm activities.
2-wheeler market recorded robust growth, supported by low base effect and resilient rural demand.

Next quarter: resilient 8% growth expected, driven by festive demand, stronger rural cash flows and ongoing infrastructure activity; monsoon variability, potential El Nino effect and geopolitical tensions flagged as key downside risks.

subsections.label: Export outlook
points: Currently in a high single-digit export trend (~8%, 8.5% of revenue); aim is to continuously increase this over the next few years, on an increasing trend over the next couple of years.

subsections.label: GST/demand normalization
points: Contrary to expectations that demand would normalize a couple of quarters after the GST rate change, sustained growth has continued; GST-related effects may normalize in 1-2 more quarters, but consumption-led growth is continuing sustainably, aided further by lower GST rates already in effect.

subsections.label: Revenue growth composition
points: Company has outperformed market volume growth by a few percentage points; growth driven by a combination of underlying volume growth and content/mix, though exact volume vs content-per-vehicle split not separately quantified.

subsections.label: Fuel-agnostic technology stance
points: As a technology company, Bosch supports whatever technology the market/OEMs/regulations demand — including SDVs, electrification, CNG/alternate fuels, ADAS.
Management sees continued momentum and volume growth in combustion technologies for many years to come, including possible upgraded legislation in combustion technologies.

On OEMs increasingly wanting to own software/electronics architecture themselves, management does not see this as a negative for Bosch's content-per-vehicle and is happy to engage with OEMs on different collaboration models.

subsections.label: Bosch Chassis Systems acquisition
points: Chassis Systems business was acquired from a Bosch sister company; sale completed in July, consolidation underway.
Minimal cost synergy effects expected from the acquisition — some small improvements only, not seen as a major benefit.

Strategic rationale is portfolio addition of a powertrain-agnostic product line into Bosch Limited; the acquired company operates with very good performance characteristics and has strong secured projects for several years, described as profitable with good growth and good market share.
Consolidated results including Chassis Systems will be published starting next quarter.
An investor meet is planned at the Chassis Systems location in Chakan, Pune in November, including a site/plant visit.

subsections.label: e-Axle JV with TACO
points: JV with TACO (Tata AutoComp) will produce e-axles; will be operational out of Nashik.
JV is in final stages of merger control clearances (requiring approvals from multiple jurisdictions since both Bosch Group and Tata Group operate worldwide).
Revenue from the JV expected to start flowing by late next year.
JV entered into only after securing a healthy order book from both Bosch and TACO sides.

subsections.label: Air systems JV with TSF Group / Wheels and Brakes India
points: JV will be operational out of Chennai.
In final stages of merger control clearances.
Customer discussions to begin in September at the IAA auto show; real business discussions to follow, with order book/further details to be updated in a quarter.

key_figures.label: RBI FY26-27 real GDP growth forecast (revised)
RBI FY26-27 real GDP growth forecast (previous)

subsections.label: Macro backdrop
points: Domestic economy remained resilient in Q1 FY27, driven by robust private consumption and stable RBI monetary policy under a neutral stance.
Food and energy volatility pushed June retail inflation to 4.38%, reaching RBI's 4% medium-term target for the first time in 17 months, but remaining within the 2-6% flexible target band.
This policy flexibility is seen as critical for India's macro stability in FY27, allowing RBI to manage price stability amid external volatility while prioritizing steady growth.
RBI raised its FY26-27 real GDP growth forecast to 6.7% (from 6.6%), backed by strong capex momentum in the budget, keeping India the fastest-growing major economy.

subsections.label: Key downside risks flagged
points: Geopolitical disruptions/tensions in West Asia flagged as a risk to industry demand.
Monsoon variability and potential El Nino effect flagged as downside risks to next quarter's 8% growth expectation and to tractor/rural demand.
Elevated inflation (within target band) and heat waves across select regions cited as headwinds to PV demand during the quarter (though demand remained strong despite these).
Diesel price increase of INR7.5/litre cited as a potential headwind to HCV demand (though demand remained healthy despite it).

Volatile and dynamic commodity/sourcing environment: strong cost increases over recent quarters have leveled off somewhat, but management would not give guidance on this due to dependence on global conditions, geopolitics, supply chain and logistics issues.
Ongoing external uncertainties requiring enhanced supply chain agility through diversified sourcing and proactive management of commodity and currency risk.

subsections.label: Strategic priorities to address risks
points: Company priorities remain focused on strengthening operational resilience amid external uncertainties, enhancing supply chain agility through diversified sourcing, and managing commodity and currency risk proactively.

key_figures.label: RBI FY26-27 real GDP growth forecast (revised)

subsections.label: Company outlook
points: Outlook for remainder of FY27 anchored in strategic resilience, supported by strong capex momentum and RBI's improved GDP growth forecast.
Product mix expected to remain favourable through the rest of the year.
Margins expected to be sustained on an upward trend given continued operational excellence, localization, volume growth, productivity and mix improvements.
Localization content expected to continue increasing, with updates in coming quarters.
Export share of revenue expected to keep increasing over the next couple of years from current ~8-8.5% level.

Growth drivers for the next 3-5 years cited as: significantly increasing volume growth across the mobility portfolio (Power Solutions, 2-wheelers, mobility aftermarket, power tools, and now Chassis Systems), new product introductions, new technology introductions (e.g., commercial vehicle ADAS starting next year), and premiumization of vehicles.
CAFE Phase 3 regulation coming in April expected to be a growth boost for Power Solutions; CV ADAS regulation coming in October next year also expected to support growth.
e-Axle JV with TACO: revenue expected to start flowing by late next year.
Air systems JV: customer discussions to start in September; order book/details update expected in a quarter.

guidance_ledger.metric: Next quarter (Q2 FY27) automotive industry growth
guidance_ledger.statement: Next quarter we expect a resilient 8% growth driven by festive demand, stronger rural cash flows and ongoing infrastructure activity. However, monsoon variability, potential El Nino effect and geopolitical tensions remain key downside risks.
India's automotive industry is expected to witness steady growth in FY27, supported by stable macroeconomic conditions and continued policy support.
We are on an upward trend, and we would say that we will sustain this [~14% margin].
Product mix is quite favorable through the year [FY27].

Our localization plans are well on track and consistently increasing localization content. We will continue to go in this path and continue to increase our localization content. As you go by in the coming quarters, we will continue to share our localization updates.
Currently we see high single-digit trend (~8%, 8.5%). Over the next few years, our aim is to continuously increase this number... over the next couple of years, this is on an increasing trend.
Upcoming legislations on CAFE Phase 3, which will come up in April, should be an even better boost [for Power Solutions]. Content opportunity to be shared separately.
CV ADAS coming up in October of next year. A lot of preparation going on towards that.

guidance_ledger.metric: e-Axle JV with TACO revenue start
guidance_ledger.statement: Revenue should be coming out of the [e-axle] JV by late next year.

guidance_ledger.metric: Air systems JV with TSF Group order book/business details
guidance_ledger.statement: We are now starting to talk to customers starting September in the IAA auto show. And from then on, we should start to discuss real business. Give us a quarter, and then we will update you more on the order book and further details.

guidance_ledger.metric: Bosch Chassis Systems consolidated financial disclosure
guidance_ledger.statement: Starting next quarter, we will publish consolidated results, and you will start to see the impact of this. We will share more details in the upcoming quarter's conference call.

guidance_ledger.metric: CAFE Phase 3 content per vehicle (prior quarter carryover)
guidance_ledger.statement: Content per vehicle will increase [due to CAFE 3]; more details to be shared in upcoming calls.

We see significantly increasing volume growth in all our mobility portfolio over the next 3 to 5 years... premiumization of vehicles, the volume increase in vehicles, new technology in vehicles, all of which are growth drivers for us.
It looks a little stable [at this point]. But I wouldn't want to give you any guidance on how this is going because it's so dynamic and externally oriented.
Offhand, I won't be able to give you a good number because this cuts across different domains. But this is something we can work towards and we can share more data to you independently.
We currently maintained a flattish outlook [for volume growth across segments], but that doesn't mean we have no issues ramping up when required or going much beyond as required.
The PC segment is expected to record steady growth in FY27, supported by resilient consumer demand; geopolitical uncertainties may weigh on demand in Q1 though overall outlook remains stable.
The CV segment is projected to register stable growth, aided by sustained infrastructure spending and strong e-commerce-led logistics demand.

The tractor segment is expected to post stable growth, supported by healthy reservoir levels and stable prices, aided by deferment of emission norms in the 25 HP to 75 HP category; potential El Nino conditions could pose a downside risk.
The Three-Wheeler segment is likely to witness positive growth driven by organic growth in both passenger mobility and last mile cargo demand.

The Two-Wheeler segment is expected to register healthy growth with a below normal monsoon potentially weighing on rural demand; stable macroeconomic fundamentals are likely to provide underlying support.

guidance_ledger.metric: Air systems JV (Brakes India/Wheels India) operations start
guidance_ledger.statement: We currently see this JV commencing operations end of 2026.
The JV will offer according to customer demand samples in '27 and series readiness by 2028.
The SOP from the JV is most likely third quarter of next year [calendar year], and everything is on track for that; first shipments from the JV will happen from the third quarter of next year.
Content per vehicle will increase [due to CAFE 3]; more details to be shared in upcoming calls.
Bosch Limited's consolidated revenue from operations will increase by 22% from INR18,000 crores to INR22,000 crores on a pro forma basis for FY25.

guidance_ledger.metric: Bosch Limited pro forma EBITDA margin
guidance_ledger.statement: The FY25 EBITDA margins will improve from 12.8% to 13.9% on a pro forma basis led by higher margins of RBIC.
Passenger Cars are expected to achieve all-time high production levels.
The Tractor business is projected to hit a record, supported by strong rural sentiment and ongoing state subsidies.
The Two-Wheeler segment is set to scale a new peak, driven by improving rural sentiment and recent GST cuts.
The Commercial Vehicle segment is poised for healthy growth fueled by sustained infrastructure spending.
The tractor market is projected to reach an all-time high.

risk_register.note: Indian auto industry and PV/2-wheeler demand remained resilient despite geopolitical tensions in Q1 FY27.

risk_register.risk: Monsoon variability / potential El Nino effect
risk_register.note: Flagged as key downside risk to next quarter's 8% growth expectation and to tractor demand; tractor demand remained resilient despite uneven monsoon concerns.
June retail inflation reached 4.38%, hitting RBI's 4% medium-term target for first time in 17 months, but remains within the 2-6% flexible band; PV demand stayed strong despite this.
HCV segment maintained healthy demand despite this increase.
Cited as a headwind to PV demand during the quarter, though demand remained strong.

Strong cost increases over recent quarters have leveled off somewhat; management declined to give forward guidance given dependence on global conditions, geopolitics, supply chain and logistics issues; worldwide purchasing organization helps manage this.
Company managing commodity and currency risk proactively as part of strategic priorities.

risk_register.risk: Supply chain complexities / geopolitical disruption impact on 2-wheeler production
risk_register.note: 2-wheeler/Powersports division ensured zero production disruptions for customers despite ongoing geopolitical and supply chain complexities.
Analyst raised risk of Bosch losing Tier-1 captured value; management does not see this as a negative and expects continued engagement with OEMs on various models.
Both TACO e-axle JV and TSF air systems JV are in final stages of merger control clearances requiring approvals from multiple jurisdictions, involving procedural/admin work.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical instability in West Asia impacting energy price stability and shipping/logistics routes
risk_register.note: Heightened geopolitical instability, particularly in West Asia, poses a material risk to energy price stability and has created volatility in key shipping and logistics routes.

risk_register.risk: Strait of Hormuz situation / Ukraine war
risk_register.note: Cited as part of overall geopolitical environment causing management to be careful/conservative on FY27 outlook; also not providing a tailwind on logistics costs.
Acute semiconductor shortages have eased, but overall supply chain environment remains fragile; geopolitical friction creates new unpredictable bottlenecks.
Independent Mobility aftermarket stagnated as it continued to face significant supply chain pressures.
Significant surge in demand post GST reforms managed while dealing with ongoing supply chain pressures; 100% delivery commitment maintained with zero production disruptions.
Could pose a downside risk to the tractor segment FY27 outlook.
Could potentially weigh on rural demand for the Two-Wheeler segment in FY27.
Market described as competitive; company working on material cost via localization/negotiation/design-to-cost and plant productivity/AI.
The business is closely coupled with legislation, which can impact growth.
Projected slowdown in global growth from 3.2% in 2025 to 3.1% in 2026.
Adjustments in the global economy due to geopolitical events and trade realignments.
Influencing market sentiments worldwide.
Weaker tax inflows and elevated CAPEX spending keeping fiscal discipline in focus.

themes.label: Strategic acquisition
themes.note: Bosch Chassis Systems acquisition completed in July, adds a powertrain-agnostic, profitable, high-growth business with minimal cost synergies but strong strategic portfolio value; consolidated results to be published from next quarter.

themes.label: Regulatory-driven growth
themes.note: CAFE Phase 3 (April) and CV ADAS (October next year) regulations expected to boost Power Solutions content and growth.

themes.label: Financial accretion
themes.note: Revenue grew 22% YoY and EBITDA grew 28% YoY to INR8,180 million, with EBITDA margin sustaining at ~14% versus post-COVID 12-13% range.

themes.label: Manufacturing excellence
themes.note: Sustained margin improvement attributed to operational excellence, localization, productivity gains and favourable product mix; worldwide purchasing organization aids sourcing amid volatility.

themes.label: EV and hybrid technology
themes.note: EVs already integral to mobility offering via e-axle JV with TACO though not yet material to turnover; EV segment continues expanding market share in the broader industry.

themes.label: Geopolitical risk overhang
themes.note: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia, monsoon variability, potential El Nino and volatile commodity/sourcing conditions flagged as ongoing external risks.

themes.label: Cautious FY27 outlook
themes.note: Management anchors FY27 outlook in strategic resilience, expecting 8% industry growth next quarter, but declines to give specific commodity cost or fuel-agnostic revenue guidance given external volatility.

quarters.summary: Management struck a tone of "cautious optimism" for FY27: domestic macro (RBI's flexible inflation targeting, continued govt capex) is seen as supportive, but geopolitical risks (West Asia/Strait of Hormuz conflict, Ukraine war) and their potential impact on crude/energy prices and logistics are flagged as headwinds. FY27 volume outlook across segments is broadly flattish/steady, with company guiding for continued content-per-vehicle increases, upcoming CAFE Phase 3 and ADAS-related opportunities, and new JV-led entries (air systems JV with Brakes India/Wheels India targeting first operations end of 2026, samples in 2027, series readiness by 2028; Tata AutoComp JV SOP likely Q3 of next calendar year/Q3 FY28).

Strong productivity progress in plants; ramping up AI usage in plants to gain productivity and efficiency.
Market described as competitive; company continuing cost progress accordingly.

points: QoQ growth driven mainly by Power Solutions business on account of robust growth in overall automotive market.
Two-Wheeler business QoQ growth mainly due to higher sales of exhaust gas sensors from ramp-up of OBD2 norms implementation from 1st April 2025.
FY growth driven mainly by Power Solutions business on higher demand in overall automotive segment.

subsections.label: Consumer Goods business
points: QoQ growth driven by product range expansion through traditional trade channel and incrementally supported by e-commerce growth.
FY growth mainly on account of growth in global and blue tools and accessories and incentive schemes launched.

Closed fiscal year with momentum, delivering over INR14 billion in Q4.
Success underpinned by continued focus on preparing customers for upcoming legislation (CAFE Phase 3), actively aligning with OEMs for rollout scheduled April 30, 2027.

Spearheading adoption of ADAS in commercial vehicles; proactive approach positions partners to comply as regulation takes effect starting Jan 2027 for new commercial vehicle models, extending to all commercial vehicles by October 2027.

Bosch Limited named one of India's top 50 innovative companies by CII; Two-Wheeler division was a key contributor.

Exports delivered outstanding growth (~17%), reflecting notable improvements in Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
Sustained focus on go-to-market strategies and market coverage initiatives drove steady growth across core product portfolio.
Positive development seen across filters, lubricants, rotating machines, braking systems, wipers and auto electricals, demonstrating fundamental health of offerings.

subsections.label: Power Tools division

Cordless segment delivered another quarter of double-digit growth, driven by Cordless 3.0 initiative creating battery lock-in effect via targeted online and offline promotions across 25 key industrial clusters, accelerating adoption of battery platform.

subsections.label: Innovation recognition
points: Bosch Limited named one of India's top 50 innovative companies by CII; Two-Wheeler division was a key contributor.
New Intelligent Puncture Detection System commended this year, following last year's recognition of Sensorless Quickshift technology.

points: Actively aligning with OEMs to prepare customers for CAFE Phase 3 regulations, with rollout scheduled April 30, 2027.
Spearheading adoption of ADAS in commercial vehicles, with regulation taking effect starting Jan 2027 for new commercial vehicle models, extending to all commercial vehicles by October 2027.

subsections.label: Power Tools certification and new product
points: First Power Tool company in India to receive mandatory BIS certification for angle grinders, drills and hammers.
Launched new magnetic drill GBM30 — first locally sourced finished good, addressing a much-awaited market requirement.

points: Bosch supports all technologies including the European version of BS7 (Euro 7); technology, manufacturing and competence readiness already demonstrated with OEMs.

subsections.label: Auto industry demand drivers (Q4 FY26)
points: PV demand accelerated notably towards year-end, driven by strong SUV traction, leaner dealer inventories, robust consumer sentiment, festive and wedding season tailwinds, and GST benefits.

LCV production recorded healthy growth driven by e-commerce demand during festive season, 10% increase in infrastructure spending supporting freight activity, and budget utilization by fleet operators; stable credit conditions and cumulative 125bps repo rate cut improved affordability for small operators.

HCV growth supported by 10% increase in infrastructure spending, stronger goods movement, Q4 budget utilization by fleet operators/logistics, infrastructure-led goods movement, demand for school buses, and steady replacement demand.

Tractor segment was standout performer, supported by robust rural demand, favorable farm economics, strong rabi sowing season (area coverage up ~1.59 million hectares YoY), and policy tailwinds enhancing affordability driving first-time and replacement demand.

Three-Wheeler production rose sharply on demand for urban mobility and heightened last-mile cargo activity during festive season; OEMs scaled production anticipating sustained demand aided by supportive policies and festive tailwinds.
Two-Wheeler segment posted healthy growth supported by strong festive/wedding season demand, improved rural liquidity and stable urban consumption.

subsections.label: India cost competitiveness vs global (Bosch India role)
points: Bosch operates on an international production network model where production centers are set up in the region of consumption (Europe for Europe, India for India); some export happens based on shortfalls/extra demand.
For Bosch India to play a bigger role/export more, economics/commercial sense and landed cost parity with contracted obligations at destination need to work out.
Company is working on cost competitiveness on material via localization and overall value-add efficiency.
Current Strait of Hormuz situation and associated logistics costs are not providing a tailwind.
Company is increasing export share; example cited: NOx sensor plant in Abu Dhabi exporting back to Europe with a good export share, though this varies by product.

subsections.label: Content per vehicle
points: Content per vehicle has been on a constant increase and this trend is expected to continue in the upcoming fiscal year.
CAFE Phase 3 related content per vehicle is expected to increase; further details to be shared in upcoming calls.

subsections.label: BS7 preparedness
points: Bosch is an agnostic player supporting all technologies, including the European version of BS7 (Euro 7); has already demonstrated technologies and worked with OEMs for some time.
Technology preparedness, manufacturing capability and competence are not a challenge; company is well prepared to handle movement towards BS7 if government legislates it.

subsections.label: Air systems JV with Brakes India and Wheels India
points: Announced joint venture with Brakes India Private Limited and Wheels India Limited to expand capabilities and solidify global partnership in commercial vehicle sector.

JV to focus on engineering, manufacturing and sale of electronically controlled and software-driven modules for air compression, air processing, air suspension and air parking brakes, for commercial vehicles (trucks and buses), covering both ICE and BEVs, across LCV and MHCV segments.
Registered office in Chennai; global supply chain including India managed by entities of Bosch, Brakes India and Wheels India.
Bosch currently is not a player in electronically controlled/software-driven air compression/processing/suspension modules at all — this JV represents a new entry into the portfolio for Bosch.

Rationale: TSF Group (Brakes India/Wheels India) is a strong established player in pneumatics and hydraulics for CV suspension, braking and air systems; combining Bosch's electronic control/software capability with TSF's market position enables faster time-to-market than going alone.
Management does not see this as a change in Bosch's Tier 1 position; will continue to play the same Tier 1 role. Detailed tier/commercial terms still being worked out.
This JV will also help scale globally, since the market for air systems today is largely global; India adoption expected to grow over the coming 2 years.
JV aims to commence first operations end of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and operational readiness; samples to customers in 2027; series readiness by 2028.
Company will still need to win projects for this venture; already working on this, and will share more information as the JV setup progresses.

Market for the underlying air processed braking/suspension technology in India is described as very nascent/early stage/brand-new portfolio; interest currently largely global, with more adoption expected in Indian market in coming ~2 years.
Content-per-vehicle and market opportunity/exact scope details to be shared in a future call once finalized; management declined to speculate on numbers now.

Management noted continuous work on portfolio expansion, decluttering and enhancement generally, and will share information on any further JVs (e.g., other segments) as and when available/through regulatory approvals.

subsections.label: eAxle JV with Tata AutoComp
points: Establishment of the JV was targeted mid-2026 and is on track.
SOP (start of production) from the JV is most likely Q3 of next calendar year (i.e., Q3 FY28); everything on track for that; first shipments from the JV will happen from Q3 of next calendar year.
Company has orders from clients based on which the whole JV concept was worked on; more details on exact orders to be shared once the JV is set up in coming months.

subsections.label: Acquisition of Robert Bosch Chassis Systems (Bosch Chassis)
points: Minority shareholder approval for the acquisition has been obtained; company is still awaiting regulatory approval before proceeding further.
Valuation report has been published together with the postal ballot notice (link available; investors can contact Company Secretary for access).

Company declined to disclose FY26 revenue, margin and profitability figures for Bosch Chassis, citing that the process for the whole CV report is not yet complete and closing has not occurred; noted that what has been published in the valuation report aligns with original plans given current RBI/mobility market trends.

subsections.label: Global production role for Bosch India (potential)
points: There is an opportunity for Bosch India to become a bigger player in the Bosch Group's global supply chain / potentially a preferred low-cost supplier, but this is still work in progress on how production architecture evolves.
Preconditions include making economic/commercial sense and landed cost being competitive at destination markets.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro risks
points: Heightened geopolitical instability, particularly in West Asia, continues to pose a material risk to energy price stability and has created volatility in key shipping and logistics routes.
Geopolitical friction (including Strait of Hormuz situation, Ukraine war) creates new unpredictable bottlenecks requiring constant monitoring and proactive management.
Geopolitical uncertainties, particularly the West Asia conflict, may weigh on PC segment demand in Q1 FY27, though overall outlook remains stable.
Potential El Nino conditions could pose a downside risk to the tractor segment outlook.
Below-normal monsoon could potentially weigh on rural demand for the Two-Wheeler segment.

subsections.label: Supply chain
points: Acute semiconductor shortages of the past have eased, but the overall supply chain environment remains fragile.
Independent (Mobility) aftermarket continued to face significant supply chain pressures, causing stagnation in that channel.
Two-Wheeler/PowerSports division managed ongoing supply chain pressures while scaling production to meet GST-reform-driven demand.

subsections.label: Cost/currency risk
points: Key priorities for FY27 include enhancing supply chain agility and managing commodity and currency risks effectively.
Forex gains/losses due to INR fluctuation impact other expenses.
Strait of Hormuz situation and associated logistics costs are not providing a tailwind on landed cost competitiveness.

subsections.label: Competitive market
points: Management describes the market as competitive, requiring continuous work on material cost via localization, negotiation and design-to-cost, plus plant productivity gains including AI adoption.

subsections.label: Macro outlook FY27
points: Domestic economy expected to remain resilient, driven by robust private consumption, fiscal stimuli and stable RBI monetary policy keeping inflation within 2%-6% target range.
Government's continued focus on capital expenditure outlined in the budget expected to bolster domestic demand and create opportunities.
Overall outlook for FY27 described as one of 'cautious optimism'; key priorities are enhancing supply chain agility and managing commodity/currency risks.

subsections.label: Segment-wise FY27 industry outlook
points: India's automotive industry expected to witness steady growth in FY27, supported by stable macroeconomic conditions and continued policy support.
PC segment expected to record steady growth, supported by resilient consumer demand; West Asia conflict may weigh on Q1 demand but overall outlook remains stable.
CV segment projected to register stable growth, aided by sustained infrastructure spending and strong e-commerce-led logistics demand.

Tractor segment expected to post stable growth, supported by healthy reservoir levels and stable prices, aided by deferment of emission norms in the 25 HP to 75 HP category; potential El Nino conditions could pose downside risk.
Three-Wheeler segment likely to witness positive growth driven by organic growth in both passenger mobility and last-mile cargo demand.
Two-Wheeler segment expected to register healthy growth, with below-normal monsoon potentially weighing on rural demand, though stable macro fundamentals likely to provide underlying support.

subsections.label: Company volume/content outlook
points: Management currently maintains a flattish volume outlook for FY27 given potential headwinds (notably West Asia crisis impact on crude oil prices), but is 'cautiously optimistic' and open to ramping up beyond flattish if required, similar to the prior year.
Content per vehicle expected to continue increasing constantly, including from CAFE Phase 3 related content.

guidance_ledger.statement: We currently maintained a flattish outlook [for volume growth across segments], but that doesn't mean we have no issues ramping up when required or going much beyond as required.
Content per vehicle is a constant increase, and we expect this trend to continue also in the upcoming fiscal year.
India's automotive industry is expected to witness steady growth in FY27, supported by stable macroeconomic conditions and continued policy support.
The PC segment is expected to record steady growth in FY27, supported by resilient consumer demand; geopolitical uncertainties may weigh on demand in Q1 though overall outlook remains stable.
The CV segment is projected to register stable growth, aided by sustained infrastructure spending and strong e-commerce-led logistics demand.

The tractor segment is expected to post stable growth, supported by healthy reservoir levels and stable prices, aided by deferment of emission norms in the 25 HP to 75 HP category; potential El Nino conditions could pose a downside risk.
The Three-Wheeler segment is likely to witness positive growth driven by organic growth in both passenger mobility and last mile cargo demand.

The Two-Wheeler segment is expected to register healthy growth with a below normal monsoon potentially weighing on rural demand; stable macroeconomic fundamentals are likely to provide underlying support.

key_takeaways: Quarter-on-quarter, the Mobility business has grown by 23.3% in Jan-March '26 as compared to Jan-March '25, driven mainly from the Power Solutions business, which grew by 27.4%, mainly on account of robust growth in overall automotive market.
Revenue from operations in Jan-March '26 stood at INR55,657 million, which grew by 13.3% over Jan-March '25.
Revenue for the period April-March '26 grew by 10.8% over April-March '25 from INR180,874 million to INR200,347 million.
EBITDA for Jan-March '26 was INR7,815 million, which grew by 20.8% over the same quarter of previous year.
EBITDA for period April-March '26 was INR26,503 million as compared to INR23,097 million April-March '25, which grew by 14.7%.

Profit after tax for FY '25-'26 stood at INR27,702 million, which is a growth of 37.6% over the same period of previous year. The significant growth impact is mainly due to the profit on sale of the Video Solutions, Access and Intrusions and Communication Systems under the Building Technologies segment.
The Power Solutions division achieved a landmark results surpassing INR130 billion, total net sales for 2025 calendar year.

We are pleased to announce a joint venture with Brakes India Private Limited and Wheels India Limited... focus on engineering, manufacturing and sale of electronically controlled and software-driven modules for air compression, air processing, air suspension and air parking brakes with a registered office in Chennai.
India's automotive industry is expected to witness steady growth in FY '27, supported by stable macroeconomic conditions and continued policy support.

quarters.summary: Bosch Limited anticipates robust growth across the automotive industry, driven by strong economic fundamentals and supportive policies, with expectations for record production levels in passenger cars, tractors, and two-wheelers.

subsections.label: EBITDA and PAT growth
points: The improvement in EBITDA margin was primarily driven by a favorable product mix and optimization of expenses.
The significant growth in PAT is mainly due to the profit on sale of the Video solutions, Access and Intrusion and Communication systems business under the Building Technologies segment.

subsections.label: Automotive production and demand
points: India's automotive production remained robust in the October-December quarter, driven by broad-based strength across Passenger Vehicles, 2-wheelers, and Commercial segments.
Higher festive demand, rural market recovery, and improved supply chain conditions supported manufacturing activity across most vehicle categories.

The Heavy Commercial Vehicle production recorded steady growth, driven by robust infrastructure demand, strong freight movement, and continued momentum from GST 2.0, festive demand, government fleet orders, and ongoing road construction and mining activity.
The bus segment showed notable traction driven by school, intercity, institutional transport orders alongside steady fleet additions by state and private operators.
The LCV production remained robust, fueled by GST rationalization and a visible revival in demand following GST 2.0.
The 3-wheeler segment saw a sharp production increase driven by strong demand for both urban mobility and last-mile delivery during the festive season.
Tractor production showed strong momentum, supported by healthy rabi sowing activity and carryover liquidity from a robust kharif harvest.
The 2-Wheeler production was moderate in October as OEMs adjusted output following earlier inventory buildup, but picked up in November and December.

subsections.label: Sector-wise sales performance
points: The Mobility business has shown significant growth driven by the Power Solutions business, mainly due to growth in Passenger Cars and Off-highway segments.
The mobility aftermarket recorded growth mainly due to GST reforms and strong growth in the OE segment.
The 2-Wheeler business grew significantly due to higher sales of exhaust gas sensors for OBD-II norms implementation.

The Consumer Goods business saw marginal decline due to market challenges but grew in the April-December period due to new launches in entry-level mid-price point segment, measuring tools, and outdoor garden equipment.

subsections.label: Two-Wheeler & Powersports
points: Bosch's strategy focuses on providing advanced technology to enhance end-user experience, playing a key role in the launch of new vehicles by several well-known 2-wheeler OEMs.
The launch of new TVS Apache RTX 300 and Harley X440 T marked significant milestones, integrating Bosch powertrain and safety systems.
Bosch showcased its latest innovations at the EICMA 2025 event in Italy, demonstrating commitment to creating value for partners and end users.

subsections.label: Bidadi plant achievements
points: The Bidadi plant was awarded at the National CII SCALE Awards 2025 for digital excellence and innovation in logistics.
The plant secured the Champions Trophy and the Challengers Trophy at the CI KAIZEN Awards 2025 for developing low-cost solutions in productivity and quality improvement.

subsections.label: Localization efforts
points: Bosch is localizing NOx sensor components for common rails and plans further localization for common rail products.
The company has increased export volumes for spark plugs and components for common rail products, and relocated pumps from Japan to India.

subsections.label: Macroeconomic overview
points: The global economy is adjusting to geopolitical events and trade realignments, with a projected slowdown in global growth from 3.2% in 2025 to 3.1% in 2026.
The Indian economy shows resilience with higher growth compared to peers, supported by resilient domestic demand and easing inflation.

subsections.label: Automotive industry outlook
points: Bosch anticipates steady and robust growth for the Indian automotive industry in FY 2026, with expectations for record production levels in Passenger Cars, Tractors, and 2-Wheelers.
The Commercial Vehicle segment is poised for healthy growth fueled by sustained infrastructure spending and e-commerce logistics expansion.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw highest-ever OHT quarterly sales volume (16% YoY growth) with revenue growth of 24% YoY, though EBITDA margin was impacted by raw material inflation and higher India mix; management expects better EBITDA-to-PAT flow-through as On-Highway volumes scale up and core OHT trajectory improves. Forward guidance remains largely qualitative: On-Highway revenue vision of INR5,000 crores by 2030 reiterated, balance capex of ~INR3,000 crores (INR1,500-2,000 crores in FY27) to be spent as per schedule, and further price hikes/raw material impact expected in Q2-Q3, but management repeatedly declined to give explicit forward-looking volume/margin guidance.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin was particularly impacted on account of raw material prices due to geopolitical situation globally and its impact on supply chain.
The impact was partially offset by certain price hikes during the quarter.
India's contribution has increased to overall 40% of the volumes, which has impacted the margin slightly.
India margins are marginally lower than export margins, though not as low as it used to be earlier when India mix was sub-20%.
Company expects better flow-through from EBITDA to PAT as it steadily scales up volumes in On-Highway segment and benefits from improved trajectory of core OHT business.

Company gave increments to staff.

subsections.label: Freight cost
points: Freight rate as percentage of revenue is around 5%.

subsections.label: OHT business highlights
points: Highest ever quarterly OHT sales volume reported, led by decent uptick in end markets and segments.
Europe witnessed a stable environment; company working with channel partners across key markets to increase market share.
India performed exceptionally well in Q1 despite a high base from last year, aided by marketing efforts, superior product range, and growing infra capex in India.
In Americas, tariff rate settled at 10% level leading to better performance led by USA; sharper go-to-market strategy and stable end markets expected to sustain growth momentum.
Long runway of growth expected in Americas given BKT's brand positioning and focus on high-quality products.

subsections.label: Carbon Black business highlights
points: Decent volume growth YoY in Q1 FY27, with third-party sales at around 10% of overall business.
Commissioned Phase II of Carbon Black plant during the quarter, taking total capacity to 360,000 MTPA.
Increased captive power plant capacity to 64 MW as part of energy circularity model.
Geopolitical challenges expected to impact pricing and supply on the back of increased crude prices; some price increases expected to offset raw material inflation.
Demand continues to be robust in this segment.

New Business Head for Carbon Black, Mr. Ashish Kumar Datta, appointed effective July 3, 2026, bringing 36 years of cross-functional leadership experience across chemicals, coatings and polymer industries; previously with Lubrizol Advanced Materials (Berkshire Hathaway company).

subsections.label: On-Highway Business vertical
points: Distribution network and channel infrastructure set up in April; go-to-market strategy went live.
Started supplies in Truck Bus Radial (TBR) segment with positive trade response.
2-wheeler tire product portfolio introduced with select products targeting domestic market, with encouraging feedback from end users.
Launched 24x7 journey assistance program 'YOU FORWARD' in June for 2-wheeler riders across India, positioning company as a mobility partner beyond product offerings.
First digital campaign for the initiative featured actor Rakesh Bedi.
Entry into On-Highway is a strategic adjacency complementing existing OHT strengths.
Business seeded in Q1; gradual ramp-up expected starting Q2.
On-Highway segment currently small; company will refrain from sharing revenue or volume details at this juncture.

Brands launched include Loadxpert, Milexpert, Zenova and Thyros for trucks and 2-wheelers; Q1 was focused on setting up systems and 'seed marketing'; ramp-up of sales and production to proceed as per plan with no surprises expected.
FY27 will be a year of building the On-Highway portfolio; FY28 onwards will be 'serious business'.

Distributor approach is pan-India, not selective; country has been sliced and diced intelligently; distributors appointed across all categories including cars; dealer appointments will increase as production ramps up rather than being over-aggressive upfront.
70 distributors added per Annual Report (context from analyst question).

subsections.label: India growth drivers
points: India revenue growth of over 35% mainly from Off-Highway tire market, coming from all three sectors: agri, mining and industrial construction.
Growth is largely from replacement demand; OE mix broadly remained the same.
Mining sector is also helping aid this growth.
Directionally sustainable growth rather than a one-off, per management.

subsections.label: Capex completed
points: New Carbon Black facility line commissioned in Bhuj, taking capacity to 360,000 MTPA at a capital outlay of INR800 crores.
Power capacity at Bhuj increased from 40 MW to 64 MW at a capital outlay of INR125 crores.
All balance capex projects amounting to approximately INR3,000 crores are progressing as per schedule.

subsections.label: Regional performance and dynamics
points: Europe: stable environment; base last year was lower, and good monsoon/season aided the agricultural segment; company working with channel partners to increase market share.
India: exceptional performance despite high base from last year; India revenue mix higher than Europe revenue mix for the first time in a quarter.

Americas: better performance led by USA with tariff rate settled at 10%; sharper go-to-market strategy and stable end markets support continued growth; long runway of growth given BKT brand positioning and high-quality product focus.

End-user inventory levels described as normal — no buildup or shortage; no meaningful prebuying observed in Europe despite peer commentary on prebuying ahead of price increases (any prebuying, if it happened, would be minimal to the company's knowledge).

subsections.label: US tariff refund
points: Company, like other companies, has applied for US tariff refunds; too early to comment on timing of returns.

key_takeaways: Q1 started on a positive note; delivered highest quarterly sales volume in OHT segment despite challenges across many international geographies, end markets, and supply chain.
Delivered 16% sales volume growth in OHT on a year-on-year basis, led by decent uptick in end markets and segments.
During Q1, launched on-road products in the TBR and 2-wheeler segment in domestic market.
Stand-alone revenue for the quarter stood at INR3,409 crores, registering a growth of 24% year-on-year.

Stand-alone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR703 crores with a margin of 20.61%, impacted by raw material prices due to geopolitical situation and partially offset by price hikes; India's contribution increasing to 40% of volumes also impacted margin slightly.
Profit after tax stood for the quarter at INR432 crores.
Commissioned Phase II of Carbon Black plant during the quarter, taking total capacity to 360,000 MTPA; also increased captive power plant to 64 megawatts.
As on June 30, '26, gross debt and cash and cash equivalents were approximately INR4,690 crores and INR2,965 crores respectively, with net debt of approximately INR1,725 crores.
Board of Directors recommended a first interim dividend of INR4 per equity share.
pressing_questions: Disha Sheth repeatedly asked about sustaining the 24% sales momentum going forward based on order book, and whether margin profile would tweak as Indian business mix grows to 20%; Rajiv Poddar declined to give forward-looking statements each time, ultimately asking the analyst to refrain from continuing to ask ('I'm repeatedly saying please do not ask the forward-looking statements... third time I'm telling you, please refrain from that. We will not make comments. I'll keep on rejecting the comments.')

Yash Agrawal asked whether investors should expect stronger free cash flow generation and higher capital return from FY28 as the major capex cycle ends; Rajiv Poddar said he cannot comment as it is a Board decision.
Mumuksh Mandlesha asked for an update on the refund of US duty; Rajiv Poddar said it is too early to share details.
Yash Agrawal asked how to think about the core OHT margin profile going forward in the next few quarters; Rajiv Poddar said under current volatility, no comments can be made on future guidance.

quarters.summary: Management flagged raw material cost upticks and margin pressure expected in FY27 due to geopolitical/supply chain headwinds, with price hikes and product mix improvement being used to partially offset the impact. The company stopped giving explicit volume/revenue guidance for FY27 given geopolitical uncertainty, but reiterated its stated 2030 vision for on-highway (INR5,000 crores revenue) and maintained an intent to sustain consolidated EBITDA margins between 23%-25%; total capex plan through FY29 stands at INR6,800 crores (including ~INR3,000 crores already spent), with FY27 capex expected between INR1,500-1,800 crores.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin for the quarter was particularly impacted towards the end of the quarter on account of headwinds faced due to the geopolitical scenario and its impact on supply chain.
FY26 standalone EBITDA registered a degrowth of 10% YoY.
Company is maintaining a steady balance between superior product mix and price hikes to partially offset raw material cost impact.

subsections.label: Other expenses
points: Other expenses moved significantly in the quarter and for the full year due to increased production (highest ever quarterly and annual volumes), driving higher conversion costs; no theoretical/structural jump, purely volume-linked.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Company paid INR12 per share dividend over the previous 3 quarters in addition to the recommended final dividend of INR4 per share.
Net debt position of INR895 crores as of 31st March 2026, calculated from gross debt of INR4,049 crores against cash and cash equivalents of INR3,154 crores.
Funding source for the balance INR3,800 crores capex (through FY29) will be a mix of sources; company still working on finalizing this.
Management declined to confirm whether current debt level of ~INR4,000 crores represents peak debt, citing volatile environment and ongoing project announcements.

subsections.label: On-Highway business (TBR, 2-wheeler, PCR)

Early market response has been encouraging, reflecting acceptance of product quality and performance.

key_takeaways: We have been resilient in a challenging external environment. While macroeconomic uncertainties continue to persist, at BKT, we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable and profitable growth over the medium to long term.

We are now witnessing raw material price upticks due to supply chain disruptions and are closely monitoring the situation, while maintaining a steady balance between superior product mix and price hikes to partially offset this impact.

H2 performance was significantly better than H1, which resulted in a strong operational year for the company, where we delivered our highest ever quarterly volumes in Q4, and also the highest ever volumes annually in FY 2026.
India continues to outperform all markets and witnessed a sustained momentum. We are cautiously optimistic for this geography given the weather forecast of IMD for the upcoming monsoon season.
In December '25, we commissioned our new line for carbon black, taking the total capacity available to us at 265,000 MTPA... we have witnessed full utilization levels for the new lines.

We have entered the truck bus radial segment with the new product launches in February '26... Building on this momentum, the company plans to introduce the passenger car radial or PCR tyres by the end of the current calendar year following a phased and calibrated approach.
The Board of Directors has approved an additional capex of INR2,000 crores, which will support capacity expansion and infrastructure development across both OHT and on-Highway tyre categories.

The stand-alone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR663 crores with a margin of 22.9%. The margin was particularly impacted towards the end of the quarter on account of headwinds faced due to geopolitical scenario and its impact on supply chain.

So then in that case, like we have about INR4,000 crores of debt in the books. So can we assume that its peak debt that we have in the books today?

BALKRISIND.about: Balkrishna Industries Limited (BKT) started its Off-Highway tyre business in 1987. For over 30 years, BKT has successfully focused on specialist segments such as agricultural, construction and industrial as well as earthmoving, port and mining, ATV, and gardening applications. [1]

quarters.summary: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue grew 12.8% YoY to ₹74 bn with sequential growth described as muted, while EBITDA margin fell ~150 bps YoY to 11.7% on raw material cost pressure and macro/geopolitical cost volatility (RM/energy/logistics, especially West Asia-linked). India delivered its strongest YoY quarterly growth in 14 quarters, volume-led, while Europe posted muted reported growth due to Netherlands plant closure/transition overlap costs, with restructuring benefits expected from H2 FY27 and a long-term aspiration of high-teens EBIT for Europe. RM inflation is expected to remain elevated (~8% sequentially in India in Q2) before cooling from Q3, with further price increases planned in both India and Europe to catch up with cost inflation.

key_takeaways: CFO transition: CFO Gauro Kumar announced his decision to leave Apollo Tyres after ~22 years, post completion of the NSCD project ("Having completed the NSCD project… it was an emotional decision to leave Apollo Tires").

Netherlands plant closure executed: The Netherlands plant stopped production in June 2026 as planned; management expects restructuring benefits from H2 FY27 ("financial and operational benefits… from H2 of the current fiscal year").

European mix/footprint reconfiguration underway: Capacity and SKU transfers across Netherlands → Hungary, and lower-end Hungary → India are ongoing; timing and execution risks (transition-related revenue loss, cost overlap) remain key near-term swing factors.
Consolidated Q1 FY27: Revenue ₹74 bn, +12.8% YoY (sequential growth "muted"); EBITDA margin 11.7%, down ~150 bps YoY, primarily due to raw material (RM) cost pressure.
India operations: strongest growth in 14 quarters; volume-led with RM inflation defense. Revenue ₹54.6 bn, +15.6% YoY, +4.3% QoQ; described as "highest ever revenue" for India.
Europe operations: muted reported growth due to transition; margin impacted by overlap costs. Revenue €147m, +0.5% YoY; EBITDA €13m, margin 8.9% vs 10.8% last year.
Anti-dumping duty on Chinese tyres (Europe): expected positive, as Chinese tyres had taken share at the lower end; this could "feed into the Apollo brand volumes."

Manufacturing footprint shifts: Netherlands → Hungary/India transfer; Hungary capacity expansion from ~17,000 to ~21,000 PCR tyres/day; India expansion expected towards end of FY27 with ramp through FY28; India capacity utilization very tight, running into the 90s through FY27.

quarters.summary: Apollo Tyres delivered strong Q4 FY26 consolidated growth (revenue +14% YoY, EBITDA margin 14.6%) and expects to sustain and accelerate top-line growth in India and Europe despite a tough macro environment marked by West Asia geopolitical volatility hitting raw material, energy and logistics costs. Near-term margins face pressure from steep raw material inflation (mid-to-high teens sequentially in Q1, possibly higher in Q2), being mitigated via calibrated price hikes (6-8% announced in India for Q1, 2% in Europe) and disciplined cost control; balance sheet strength (net debt/EBITDA at 0.4x) provides cushion. Europe restructuring (Enschede plant closure by June 30, 2026) is expected to start benefiting margins from H2 FY27, with a long-term ambition to return to/surpass the earlier normalised 16%+ EBITDA margin.

subsections.label: Leverage & Balance Sheet
points: Consolidated net debt to EBITDA improved dramatically from 3.2x/3x (March 2020) to 0.4x (March 2026), driven by focus on cash flows and profitability.
India Operations net debt to EBITDA improved from 1.1x (March 2025) to 0.7x (March 2026).
Balance sheet described as very strong, providing financial strength to navigate future uncertainties and ride out near-term difficult times.

subsections.label: Tax Transition
points: Following enactment of the Finance Act 2026, the company decided to transition to the concessional tax regime effective FY27, reducing applicable tax rate from 34% to 25%.
This transition resulted in deferred tax liabilities providing a positive net impact of almost INR 570+ crores, recognised in the P&L during the year and reflected in net profit.

subsections.label: A&P Spend Trend
points: Q4 FY26 A&P spend was elevated due to Cricket Jersey sponsorship activation, exceeding usual levels by more than INR 100 crores (4% of sales vs typical ~2%).

subsections.label: Europe Other Operating Income Decline
points: Of the 3% overall Europe revenue decline, 1% was from pure sales/price-mix decline while 2% was from a drop in other operating income.

Europe had received state aid from Hungary/EU when setting up the plant, amortised over 10 years; as TBR assets move to India, that other operating income accrual moves out of Hungary, causing the YoY drop.
This decline will continue to reduce over the next few quarters as TBR assets are no longer in Hungary; it is not a cash impact since the state aid was already received in full.

subsections.label: Enschede Closure Cash Impact
