key_takeaways: We reported another strong quarter where we have continued to scale new heights, once again surpassing our previous peaks to achieve our highest ever quarterly revenue.
Consolidated revenue from operations for Q1 FY27 stood at INR 5,557 crores, representing a robust 26% year-on-year growth.
EBITDA excluding exceptional income in the previous year grew by 21% year-on-year to INR572 crores with EBITDA margins of 10.3%.

Three factors weighed on the margins this quarter: commodity and gas price inflation, mathematical margin dilution from pass-through (~40 bps), and minimum wage increases across multiple manufacturing states.
We remain confident in our annual EBITDA margin guidance of 11% plus/minus 50 basis points with a bias towards the higher end.
PAT attributable to shareholders grew 24% to INR296 crores compared to normalized PAT of INR239 crores in Q1 FY26.

The Lighting System vertical reported revenues of INR1,153 crores, up 14% year-on-year... supported by the significant new order of approximately INR450 crores of annual peak value announced last quarter.

During the quarter, we also announced entry into the 4-wheel passenger vehicle seating systems segment... to support this new product line, the company's Board of Directors had approved the setting up of state-of-the-art greenfield manufacturing facility in Chhatrapati, Sambhajinagar with a proposed investment of approximately INR320 crores.

During the quarter, we had received Press Note 3 approval for our proposed JV with Inovance. However, as was advised earlier, the joint venture will also require approval in their host country China. There have been recent regulatory changes in China, tightening the norms for such technology partnership.
Together with these orders, our total sunroof order book have crossed INR500 crores.

So, is it at a critical scale where you think it's getting closer to profitability of the corporate average? [Green mobility segment profitability]

Just on the China JV, the comment which you made, can you just elaborate on what is the current status? So are we able to import the e-Axle today? So is there a restriction over there or there are no restrictions? ... in a worst case... if they do restrict then what would be our strategy in kind of increasing our presence on the four-wheeler EV business?
Given the minimum wage hike impact, by when do you expect customers to compensate, would you be able to pass on 80%, 90% of impact to customers?

quarters.summary: Uno Minda expects the automotive industry to sustain growth momentum in FY27 and plans to execute a dual strategy of vertical growth in core businesses along with scaling new-age/emerging technology platforms. For FY27, total capex is planned at ~INR1,750 crores (INR650 crores sustaining, INR1,100 crores growth capex plus land), with 7 of 11 ongoing projects commencing production/ramp-up and commercial operations expected to begin in EV powertrain and sunroof segments. Despite start-up costs at newly commissioned plants, the company continues to expect an annual EBITDA margin of around 11% plus/minus 50 basis points, and expects commodity and labor cost inflation impacts in coming quarters which it is working to pass through to customers on shorter cycles.

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 Drivers
points: Revenue growth was broad-based, driven by volume expansion across most of the core product offerings.
EBITDA margins maintained despite volatile input cost environment, reflecting disciplined focus on operational efficiencies.

Depreciation increase followed capitalization of strategic facilities including new 4-wheel lighting plants in Khed City and Indonesia, 2-wheeler alloy wheel expansion at Supa, 4-wheeler alloy wheel Phase 1 commissioning at Kharkhoda facility, and capacity expansion at Bawal.
Finance costs rose due to planned higher borrowing to fuel capex programs and manage incremental working capital for growth.
TG Uno Minda revenue surge followed capacity expansion of site and curtain airbag business, aligning with India's intensifying focus on vehicle safety.

subsections.label: FY26 Financial Summary
points: Performance reflects sustained demand across core product portfolio, continued scale-up of new businesses, and healthy execution across platforms.
Normalized EBITDA growth underscores operating strength even while continuing to invest in new capacity and future-ready technologies.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation
points: Sustaining and growth capex have largely been funded through internal accruals; incremental debt has primarily been driven by acquisition (UMEVSPL/FRIWO).
Balance sheet remains strong with improving net debt-to-equity ratio.
ROCE calculation capital employed includes capex for land bank and CWIP currently not generating returns; ROCE would be higher excluding these non-deployed assets.

Board recommended final dividend reflecting strong financial performance and robust cash flow generation; company will continue to balance reinvestment for long-term compounding with returning cash to investors.

subsections.label: Q4 Margin Commentary
points: Certain debit/credit adjustments for the entire year get settled in Q4, reflected in the 11.3% margin; quantum difficult to share as it varies by business.
Little jump from Q3 to Q4 margins because of lag impact (Q4 gets Q3 prices, Q3 gets Q2 prices) — nothing exceptional this quarter.
Certain price settlement income was accounted for in the quarter due to customer price settlements.
Gross margin compression of ~1% in Q4, driven primarily by new businesses at lower margins and commodity price impact, not materially by the small EV trading business (~INR40-45 crores).

subsections.label: Fundraising
points: The INR2,500 crores fundraising is an enabling resolution taken every year (also done last year), covering a mix of instruments including NCDs and other borrowings, not necessarily equity, to obtain in-principle shareholder approval; no specific fundraise plan currently exists.

subsections.label: Switches
points: Largest division within Uno Minda portfolio and one of the fastest-growing verticals.
Growth during quarter primarily driven by 2-wheeler switching business, supported by sustained domestic volume growth and increase in share of business with some customers.

4-wheeler switching business (Uno Mindarika) continued to outperform industry growth, supported by increasing premiumization and rising adoption of advanced feature-rich switching systems by OEMs, resulting in higher kit value per vehicle.
Witnessed further increase in share of business with leading Indian PV OEMs, strengthening domestic market leadership.
Shifting-cum-expansion of 4-wheeler switching facility at Farrukhnagar progressing as per plan; expect to complete transition of Manesar plant to Farrukhnagar over next 6 months.

subsections.label: Lighting
points: 2-wheeler lighting portfolio continued to anchor growth, supported by sustained market share gains over past few years, increase in share of business with key customers, and rising EV penetration where Uno Minda remains a leading supplier to multiple e-2-wheeler OEMs.
Received significant new order for unserved models with SOP scheduled H2 FY28, expected to materially enhance share of business and strengthen overall market position.

4-wheeler lighting business, after threefold expansion over past 5 years, is now in phase of consolidation; with SOP of multiple new programs and bulk of capacity expansion in place, focus is now on stabilizing operations and driving steady sustainable growth.

subsections.label: Casting
points: Quarter revenue mix well diversified across 4-wheeler alloy wheel, 2-wheeler alloy wheel, and aluminum die casting.

Growth largely driven by ramp-up of recently commissioned capacities including 4-wheeler alloy wheel facilities at Bawal and Kharkhoda; reported growth also reflects impact of higher base aluminum prices.

Near-term moderation observed in alloy wheel penetration among customers, led by shift in customer vehicle mix toward entry-level models where alloy wheel adoption is relatively lower, impacting 4-wheeler penetration.
In 2-wheeler segment, demand softness observed due to shift in customer preference toward steel wheels in place of previously planned alloy wheels in specific programs.
Business continues to diversify customer base and has secured new orders in 2-wheeler alloy wheel segment including electric 2-wheeler programs.

Long-term outlook remains positive; structural growth drivers for alloy wheels remain intact, supported by industry volume expansion and expected gradual increase in alloy wheel penetration across segments.

subsections.label: Seating
points: Quarter performance driven by increased share of business with existing and new customers, along with higher domestic demand for suspended seat.
Exports gained momentum, supported by improved offtake from international customers and addition of new export accounts, diversifying revenue base.
Secured new export orders from 3 new customers from Europe and North America in the CV segment; supplies expected to commence in FY28, providing strong visibility for future growth.

points: Newly introduced reporting category consolidating sustainable technology portfolio: Uno Minda EV Systems, Uno Minda Auto Innovation (2W/3W/4W EV businesses), EV-specific business of controller business, and Uno Minda Westport (alternate fuel and CNG systems).
Reorganization intended to ensure streamlined visibility and sharper insights into high-growth EV and alternative fuel business.

points: Construction of new greenfield facility for high-voltage EV powertrain components under Uno Minda Auto Innovations Private Limited (UMAIPL) progressing on schedule, with Phase 1 commissioning planned H2 FY27.
Initiated supplies of electric drive unit in line with earlier communication and customer demand.

subsections.label: Alternate Fuel Business

subsections.label: Other Products

Contribution during quarter distributed across core and aftermarket verticals; remaining revenues driven by aftermarket segment including batteries and external sales from Uno Minda Katolec, providing additional portfolio stability.
FY26 growth reflects underlying strength of diversified adjacencies.

subsections.label: Aftermarket and International Business

subsections.label: 4-Wheeler EV Powertrain Facility Expansion (Khed + CSN)
points: Board approved establishment of state-of-art greenfield manufacturing facility under UMAIPL in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra for electric powertrain products for passenger vehicles; will assemble/manufacture EDUs and dedicated hybrid transmission systems.
Capex will be phased over next 2-3 years, with facility expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY28.
This is the second EV-powertrain plant announced by UMAIPL in quick succession, following ongoing setup of facility in Khed City, Pune, slated to begin operations H2 of current fiscal year.

Management rationale for second plant despite first still under construction: good visibility on new business for both EDU and DST via strategic partnerships with customers; a customer requested being closer to them, and there was limited scope for a DST line at the existing Khed plant since it was already earmarked for existing businesses.

Same team will be responsible for commissioning both plants, but staggered timing (one plant commissioning this year, other after 1 year) allows effective effort allocation, and experience from first plant commissioning will carry over to the second.

Multiple plants across different businesses (wheels, lighting, switches, sunroof, airbags, EV products) are managed by separate dedicated business teams with no overlap in commissioning responsibility, giving confidence in execution.

subsections.label: Financial Highlights
points: Consolidated revenue from operations stood at INR 5,018 crores, registering a robust year-on-year growth of 20%.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 554 crores, growing 21% year-on-year with EBITDA margins at 11%.
Finance costs during the quarter increased to INR 53 crores, reflecting higher borrowings for capital expenditure and working capital needs.
Depreciation increased by INR 21 crores to INR 179 crores, driven by commissioning and capitalization of multiple facilities.
PAT attributable to shareholders stood at INR 277 crores, with a 28% year-on-year growth excluding the impact of new labor code.
Revenue from operations for 9 months ending December '25 stood at INR 14,252 crores, translating into a robust year-on-year growth of 16%.
EBITDA excluding exceptionals for the period grew by 17% to INR 1,580 crores, with normalized EBITDA margins stable at 11.1%.
PAT attributable to shareholders for the 9-month period stood at INR 871 crores, with a normalized PAT of INR 841 crores, representing a strong year-on-year growth of 25%.
Net debt as of December end was at INR 2,298 crores with a net debt to equity of 0.33.
ROCE achieved was 18% based on annualized profits of 9 months FY '26.
The Board declared an interim dividend of INR 0.9 per share, 20% higher than last year's interim dividend.

subsections.label: Automotive Industry Overview
points: The Indian automobile industry recorded a strong rebound with year-on-year volume growth of close to 17% and aggregate industry production of around 9.1 million units.
Export volumes grew by approximately 24% year-on-year to about 1.7 million units, supported by a gradual recovery in international markets.
Domestic PV sales reached 1.28 million units, the highest ever for a third quarter, with PV export growth at 11%.
The 2-wheeler segment recorded a strong growth with total industry production volumes reaching approximately 6.8 million units, reflecting year-on-year growth of about 15%.
EV 2-wheeler sales grew by 7% to 3.6 lakh units, with penetration levels declining to 5.1%.
EV 4-wheeler sales grew by 60% year-on-year to 48,000 units, with penetration reducing to 3.6%.

subsections.label: Switching Systems
points: The Switching System business recorded revenues of INR 1,241 crores, delivering around 19% year-on-year growth.
Growth was primarily driven by the 2-wheeler switching business, which delivered over 30% year-on-year growth.
Exports in the 2-wheeler segment recovered, securing additional export orders including heated grip from an American 2-wheeler OEM.

subsections.label: Lighting Systems
points: The Lighting systems business reported revenues of INR 1,129 crores, registering a healthy year-on-year growth of 15%.
Growth was supported by continued momentum across both the 2-wheeler and passenger vehicle lighting portfolios.
The industry-wide transition towards LED-based lighting contributed to a meaningful increase in kit value per vehicle.

subsections.label: Casting Business
points: The casting business delivered a strong performance with revenues of INR 971 crores, registering a robust year-on-year growth of 26%.
Growth was driven by the ramp-up of recently commissioned capacities and an increase in base aluminum prices.

subsections.label: Seating Systems
points: The Seating Systems business reported revenues of INR 361 crores, recording an impressive year-on-year growth of 32%.
Growth was driven by favorable customer mix in the 2-wheeler segment and higher domestic supplies of suspended seats.

subsections.label: Acoustic Business
points: The acoustic business delivered a stable performance with revenues of INR 210 crores, driven primarily by domestic demand.
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has notified mandatory implementation of acoustic vehicle alerting systems for electric vehicles.

subsections.label: Other Products
points: The other product business reported revenues of around INR 806 crores, representing year-on-year growth of 19%.
Uno Minda EV Systems business recorded a healthy increase in revenues to INR 158 crores during the quarter.

subsections.label: Capacity Expansion
points: The Board approved the setting up of a greenfield 4-wheel alloy wheel manufacturing facility with a capacity of 1.8 million wheels per annum.
The project entails fresh capital expenditure of INR 764 crores to be deployed in a phased manner over the next 3 to 4 years.

points: International business contributed approximately 10% of total revenues during the quarter.
Exports have increased largely on account of better exports in 2-wheeler switch and seating business.

subsections.label: Labor Codes Impact
points: The company assessed the financial implications of new labor codes, resulting in an increase in liability provisions by INR 28 crores.
The company expects marginal impacts on cost on a recurring basis arising from the revision to the labor codes.

subsections.label: Trade Agreements
points: The India-U.S. trade deal and the India EU FTA are expected to improve competitiveness and create long-term opportunities for trade and investment.
The reduction in reciprocal tariffs from 50% to 18% is a positive step for export-oriented manufacturing.

Advanced economies are expected to grow about 1.8% in 2026, while emerging markets remain the primary growth drivers with growth expected to stay above 4%.

quarters.summary: Management expects the Sapphire Foods merger to complete by end of FY27, with NSE/BSE approvals received in June and regulatory filings progressing; the new leadership team is fully in place and building "DIL 2.0"; KFC targets 5-6% SSSG and 105k-110k ADS to cross 20% Brand Contribution margin (~1.5-2 years horizon); store opening guidance remains unchanged; Pizza Hut's full turnaround push is expected post-merger (around FY28); technology platform buildout (with Cognizant) is expected to be ready before merger integration; Biryani By Kilo is targeted to become a INR 1,000 crore brand over the next few years.

key_figures.label: EBITDA (highest ever, as cited by Chairman)
Seasonal factors led to higher utility costs

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: The improvement in Brand Contribution and effective management of G&A costs helped post highest ever Operating EBITDA.
Judicious use of discounting helped restore KFC Gross Margin.
Food commodity inflation, hike in minimum wages and annual increments, and significantly higher LPG prices impacted costs during the quarter.
Teams effectively managed LPG availability during the period.
Slight price increases taken in KFC and Pizza Hut to mitigate cost impact; raw material and packaging prices being monitored going forward.
Seasonal factors led to higher utility costs and higher wage costs during the quarter.

key_figures.label: KFC Brand Contribution margin YoY increase
Franchise brands (incl. Costa) revenue growth YoY

subsections.label: KFC
points: KFC continued to post double-digit sales growth building on strong H2 FY26 momentum.

Marketing spends deliberately rebalanced towards driving dine-in visits rather than deep online discounting; media investments focused on positioning the brand at the center of consumption and celebration moments, both in-store and on delivery.
Rebalancing investment towards dine-in channel is showing good results, with offline saliency improving YoY.

subsections.label: Pizza Hut
points: Pizza Hut delivered sequentially better SSSG numbers, working on a 'back-to-basics' reset.
Marketing activity remained measured and purposeful, focused this quarter on communicating improved product quality and everyday value, building the foundation for a stronger brand.
Higher costs and operating deleverage led to Brand Contribution margin eroding slightly despite Gross Margin improvement.
Ended quarter with 626 stores as the brand continues to be right-sized.

Pizza Hut remains the number 2 pizza brand nationally (Domino's is number 1); the biggest historical issue has been the 3-way decision-making structure between DIL, Sapphire and Yum!, which is expected to ease post-merger.
Fundamental problem for Pizza Hut is low ADS versus competition, which requires differentiated offering/innovation across all price points, not just entry price points.
Full push behind Pizza Hut expected once merger structure is sorted, likely around FY28.

subsections.label: Own brands (Vaango, Biryani By Kilo)
points: BBK continues to progress well on top line and bottom line; company is on track to realize the acquisition case turnaround of BBK; Brand Contribution has turned positive versus negative at time of acquisition.
Post-acquisition, company has been evaluating expanding BBK in newer formats; BBK Express is a small box, lower capex format showing initial good response in food courts.
Testing BBK in dine-in format through food courts with good response; also launched BBK at a couple of airport locations to test.
Planning to test a sattvic vegetarian portfolio for BBK during the Shravan and Navratri season.
Objective is to grow BBK into a INR 1,000 crore brand in the next few years.
Vaango continues to do well; company is bullish on the South Indian food space, described as healthy food that works across dayparts; product needs to be stabilized a little further.

Biryani category is the largest ordered online item on platforms in India, yet the biggest branded players are only around INR 300-350 crore, offering a large opportunity for consolidation and standardized product offering.

subsections.label: Franchise brands (Costa Coffee)
points: Costa Coffee leaned into peak summer season with cold beverage and frappe range, driving footfall and trials through April-June heat.
Costa continued to expand presence in high visibility travel and transit locations.
Higher input costs led to lower Gross Margin for the franchise brands portfolio, but Brand Contribution margin was higher than last year on better cost management.

subsections.label: Dine-in vs delivery strategy
points: Delivery today is eating into dine-in sales rather than adding incremental net top line, unlike the post-COVID period when delivery was purely incremental.
Company is making concerted efforts to bring consumers back to dine-in stores for best customer experience and full flavours.
Dine-in pricing proposition ensures dine-in customers get the best deal along with a better experience.
North region typically favors delivery/convenience more than other regions.
Target is to move KFC offline saliency to 59%-60%, not expected to reach 65% in the near future.
Shift towards dine-in is a broader principle across the business, not format-specific, though pizza is inherently more dine-in oriented.

key_figures.label: International Brand Contribution margin YoY improvement

subsections.label: Store network
points: Plan for opening new units remains in line with guidance given earlier.

subsections.label: Aggregator dynamics
points: Indian QSR industry continues to mature; the interplay between aggregator platforms and dine-in-led brands is an evolving dynamic being navigated thoughtfully, brand-by-brand.

subsections.label: Indian food category opportunity
points: Per capita consumption / incidence of eating out is low in India today; consumers currently associate Western brands with eating out while considering Indian food as home food.

As per capita income grows and more women join the workforce, the Indian food category outside home is expected to expand significantly; management believes in a mature market (15-20 years out) Indian food category outside home could be a far bigger category than Western food category.
South Indian food category and North Indian food category are large but under-organized, offering further expansion opportunities beyond biryani.

subsections.label: Sapphire Foods merger
points: Merger process with Sapphire continues to progress along expected timelines; approvals received from both NSE and BSE in June, bringing the company closer to the next phase of regulatory filings.
Timelines broadly on track with stated target of completion by end of FY2027.
Management thanked Yum! Brands for continued confidence in DIL and RJ Corp as long-term partners.
Merger synergies readiness is not seen as an issue; it was important for the new team to join and settle in first so integration becomes easier, which has been demonstrated.
Technology piece is the other big lever that needs to be sorted before the merger; progress being made as per plans, expected to happen before merger approvals with integration starting post that.
IT integration between Sapphire and Devyani should not be a big challenge since both were on the same technology stack (previously controlled by Yum!) and processes on both sides are very similar.

subsections.label: DIL 2.0 organizational build
points: New leadership team fully in place and settling in well in respective roles under Manish Dawar's leadership; encouraged by early cultural and operational shifts across the organization, described as building 'DIL 2.0'.
New hires include COO, CTO, and Chief Marketing Officer; joining timelines ranged from about 2-3 weeks to about 2 months.

As part of DIL 2.0, entire business development (BD) activity has been consolidated under one leader, unlike the past where individual brands handled their own BD; this led to rethinking of the store opening strategy and approach to landlords.
Promoters are very bullish on the business and have never viewed investment as an issue; promoters feel Devyani can become 'another Varun' (referencing Varun Beverages) over time.

Key priorities for the remainder of the year: 1) opening new stores per earlier guidance, 2) maintaining positive SSSG across brand portfolio, 3) improving efficiency/margin structure via technology adoption and cost control, 4) building next level of team and organization structure with right processes, and 5) getting ready for the merged entity.

subsections.label: Technology buildout
points: New Chief Technology Officer hired, with strong QSR industry background from India and overseas.
Rather than building a full in-house tech team, company decided to build a core team in-house and outsource buildout to Cognizant Technologies.
Combination of core in-house team plus Cognizant outsourcing expected to enable faster rollout, on track before the merger.
Technology adoption is a leverage point that will take a few quarters to realize benefits, with 'a few quarters' counted after the merger since platforms are currently being built.

subsections.label: Global KFC brand initiatives
points: Renewed global thrust for KFC brand around three initiatives: beverages (sub-brand 'Kwench'), sauces, and boneless snacking; all three initiatives are planned to come to India, with India part of the global pipeline.
Company already in discussions to experiment with 'Kwench' in India; product needs to be optimized for Indian conditions and taste.

Capex considerations for new rollouts are viewed differently in Western markets versus India; most homework on 'Kwench' from capex and product optimization perspective is done, with planning underway for test launch timing.
Sauces and boneless initiatives are relatively simpler and will follow once 'Kwench' is established.

subsections.label: International business / Thailand
points: International business posted another quarter of 20%+ YoY growth; Gross Margins remained stable sequentially.
Effective cost management and operating leverage helped improve Brand Contribution margin.
Company has been very happy with Thailand results; currently one of three franchisee partners there.
No formal process has been launched for expanding territory in Thailand; no one has approached the company, but management remains keen to look at opportunities if they arise.

subsections.label: Macro backdrop
points: Quarter presented a mixed macro picture; external environment became more challenging as the conflict in the Middle East pushed crude oil to elevated levels through April and May, feeding into LPG and fuel costs, while the rupee remained under pressure.
RBI, in its June policy, held the repo rate steady but moderated its FY27 growth outlook and raised its inflation projection, reflecting these pressures.
Operating environment has remained volatile, along with usual seasonal complexities.
Demand has remained stable so far, but the forecast of a below-normal season combined with El Niño risk is a reminder that consumption recovery in India rarely moves in a straight line.

LPG availability was a big constraint through the cycle, although the company managed to mitigate the impact; macro pressures are not seen as fully behind the company, with periodic news continuing to emerge.

It is too early to comment definitively on Q2 SSSG trends since the quarter is still in its early stage (month of July); Q2 also faces a different drag effect from Shravan timing versus last year, though broadly a positive trend has been seen in July.

subsections.label: KFC margin trajectory
points: Key driver for improving KFC Brand Contribution margin remains the ADS number; crossing a threshold of 105,000-110,000 ADS is expected to enable crossing 20% Brand Contribution margin, as demonstrated in the past.
Key lever for ADS is a combination of SSSG in existing stores and quality of new stores (starting new stores at a higher ADS number).
Focus on promoting dine-in channel better versus delivery channel is another lever expected to push margins up; positive results already seen from this quarter's experimentation.
As ADS goes up, operating leverage benefit follows, further helping margins.
Given macro uncertainty, margin achievement timing is contingent on stable conditions; company continues to bring efficiency into the business as a continuous process.
Technology adoption is a leverage point expected to help but will take a few quarters post-merger to realize benefits.

subsections.label: Store opening guidance
points: Plan for opening new units remains in line with the guidance given earlier.

subsections.label: Merger completion
points: Company continues to expect completion of the merger with Sapphire Foods by end of the current financial year (FY27).

subsections.label: Pizza Hut strategy timing
points: Full energy and push behind Pizza Hut expected once the merger and structural issues are resolved, referenced as around FY28.

guidance_ledger.statement: Timelines are broadly on track with our stated target of completion by the end of FY 2027; we continue to expect completion of the merger by end of the current financial year.
We are looking at a SSSG of about 5% to 6% for KFC.

guidance_ledger.metric: KFC ADS threshold for 20% Brand Contribution margin
guidance_ledger.statement: Once we cross a threshold of 105,000 ADS to 110,000 ADS, we will be able to cross 20% Brand Contribution margins in KFC.
Our target remains to get to a number of 59%-60% offline saliency; I do not think we will be able to get to 65% in the near future.
Our plan for opening new units remains in line with the guidance given earlier.
FY28 is when we will put all our energy behind Pizza Hut once the two entities come together.
Our objective is to make sure that this brand gets to INR 1,000 crore brand in the next few years.

guidance_ledger.metric: KFC global initiatives rollout (Kwench, sauces, boneless)
guidance_ledger.statement: All of those initiatives will come to India, one after the other; Kwench homework is mostly done, planning test launch timing; other pieces will follow once Kwench gets established.
We are hopeful that piece also should happen before we get the merger approvals and the integration starts post that.
We do not see an issue in terms of readiness for merger synergies; we are on track and making good progress.

For 2026 (calendar year), we are not planning to add any net new stores for Pizza Hut - the idea is to consolidate and realign the portfolio.
If you put the two companies together, we are going to be almost a USD 1 billion top line by the time we complete the merger.
I feel very confident that we will be able to largely have the new team in place by next quarter.
Having tested Tea Live in India and Thailand, we have decided to discontinue the brand, and the same will happen in the next quarter.
It will take maybe a couple of months by the time we actually launch that in the market.
Maybe we can fix an Analyst Day in the next couple of quarters, and we can take you guys through in detail on what our plans are.
We feel confident that we will be able to sustain the initiatives that you have seen... it will take another couple of quarters by the time we are firmly able to say that the worst is behind us.
If you can help me foresee the inflation in the near future, I will be able to tell you that.

key_takeaways: We begin the new financial year on a strong note. The momentum we built through the second half of FY26, anchored by KFC's strong same-store sales performance has continued into Q1 FY27.
KFC continues to post double-digit sales growth and delivered another positive SSSG of 3.3% during the quarter.
The business has improved profitability and posted its highest ever EBITDA of INR 255 crore at 16.1% of the revenues.
On a consolidated basis, we delivered a 16.5% year-on-year growth in revenues, reaching INR 1,581 crore.

The improvement in Brand Contribution and effective management of G&A costs helped us post our highest ever Operating EBITDA at INR 151 crore. Our consolidated Operating EBITDA grew nearly 38% year-on-year and represents an EBITDA margin of 9.6%.

The merger process with Sapphire continues to progress along expected timelines. We received approvals from both the NSE and the BSE in June, bringing us closer to the next phase of regulatory filings.
We ended the period with 1,855 stores in India and 2,255 stores globally, as of June 30, 2026.
The new leadership team at DIL is fully in place and is settling in well.

quarters.summary: Devyani International closed FY26 with KFC posting its strongest SSSG (4.9%) in 14 quarters and consolidated revenue growth of 18.5% YoY in Q4; the proposed merger with Sapphire Foods remains on track for completion by end of the current fiscal year, and management guided to 200-225 net new stores in FY27 (100-110 from KFC) while discontinuing the Tea Live brand and continuing to reset the Pizza Hut portfolio with no net store additions planned for CY2026.

key_figures.value: small (approx. 1.5%-2% referenced by analyst, not confirmed by management)

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Consolidated revenue growth of 18.5% YoY in Q4 driven by strong KFC and international business performance.
Full year revenue crossed the INR 5,500 crore milestone, reaching INR 5,611 crore.
Both gross margin (68.8%) and brand contribution (14.1%) improved YoY on a consolidated basis.
Operating EBITDA grew 13.8% YoY to INR 123 crore, representing 8.6% of sales.

subsections.label: Balance sheet movements
points: Increase in debt during FY26 was temporary, raised for an equity infusion required in Thailand; the debt was squared off by the second week of April.
Increase in intangible assets predominantly reflects the Biryani By Kilo consolidation, with the acquisition consideration sitting largely on the intangible/goodwill side along with brands.

subsections.label: Pricing actions
points: A very small menu price correction was taken in KFC, less than 0.5 percentage point on a portfolio basis, only to tweak bits of mismatches; described as a continuous process.
Management could not foresee future inflation trends to comment on further near-term price increases.

subsections.label: KFC
points: KFC delivered its strongest performance in the last 14 quarters, posting 4.9% positive SSSG, driven by stable demand environment and tailored, sustained customer engagement.
KFC continues to anchor overall growth momentum and network expansion.

Growth was aided by shifting promotional focus from online to offline/dine-in channels; online promotions were reduced while offline deals/pricing were tailored to attract dine-in customers, with offline gains exceeding online losses.

SSSG improvement is a combination of higher average order value (AOV) and higher incremental transactions; historically, negative SSSG was driven more by weak dine-in versus resilient online, and the strategy reversed this by focusing on the dine-in channel.
Company is also working on recovering lapsed consumers while continuing to recruit new consumers.

Approximately 45 days into the current quarter, KFC has been able to maintain SSSG trends in line with the previous quarter, though management said it would take a couple more quarters to confirm sustainability.

Gross margin expansion in KFC was driven by a combination of favourable raw material and packing material costs, and tweaking the mix of promotions/discounting/deal timing in favour of dine-in customers.

subsections.label: Pizza Hut
points: Focus remains on portfolio consolidation and operational discipline.
SSSG improved sequentially despite remaining negative at -3.7%; ADS remained stable at ~INR 30,000 per store per day.
Brand contribution for the quarter was slightly negative, primarily due to operating deleverage arising from lower same-store sales.

No net store additions during the quarter; negative store count this quarter is due to a strategy reset from a business development (BD) perspective focused on better-quality stores and a stronger pipeline, involving closure of loss-making stores.
No net new Pizza Hut store additions planned for calendar year 2026; focus is on consolidating and realigning the portfolio.

New Chief Marketing Officer Sandeep Anand has joined and will oversee Pizza Hut operations; going back to basics by identifying product gaps, missing pricing layers, and reassessing quality (dough, cheese, toppings) on a de novo basis.

Store staff being retrained on both product quality and customer experience (CX); a complete revival strategy is expected to launch in the market in a couple of months, with a possible Analyst Day in coming quarters to detail brand-by-brand plans.

subsections.label: Own Brands (Vaango and Biryani By Kilo)
points: Both Vaango and Biryani By Kilo reported mid-single-digit positive SSSG.

Biryani By Kilo has achieved positive brand contribution, turning around from a loss-making brand; company has started measured expansion into offline channels via test launch of smaller Express formats in food courts.

Wherever new Express outlets have opened, they have been profitable; management is bullish on Biryani By Kilo's potential once performance is further stabilized, seeing scope for further profitability growth beyond breakeven.

subsections.label: Franchise Brands (including Costa Coffee)
points: Revenue growth remained steady at nearly 3% YoY.
Elevated coffee and cocoa prices impacted input costs, leading to a 1.2% YoY decline in gross margins.
Portfolio delivered a healthy brand contribution margin of 16.1%.

subsections.label: International Business
points: International business continues to deliver strong and consistent growth, with Nepal (still a relatively small contributor) posting an impressive 46% YoY sales increase and Thailand growing revenues 19%.
International business crossed INR 500 crore in quarterly revenues for the first time.
Improved gross margins and operating leverage drove brand contribution margins to 17.7%.

subsections.label: Store network and brand discontinuation
points: Ended FY26 with a system store count of 2,256 stores, representing a net addition of 217 stores over the last 12 months.
Having tested the Tea Live brand in India and Thailand, the company has decided to discontinue the brand, effective next quarter.

key_figures.label: Digital kiosk penetration across KFC network

subsections.label: Digital and technology initiatives
points: Achieved more than 80% digital kiosk penetration across the KFC store network, enhancing customer experience, convenience and engagement across physical formats.

Making strong progress on DIL Commerce, a unified technology platform designed to strengthen operational execution, deepen customer engagement and create a scalable digital backbone for future growth.
Technology, automation and data-led decision-making remain central to the DIL 2.0 transformation journey, playing a key role in enhancing efficiency, scalability and customer experience.

Company will manage all tech-related changes within existing budgets, including Yum! charges, and plans to leverage current infrastructure better with overlaying AI technology rather than materially changing store size or capex per store.

Company continues to explore equipment that can work on both gas and electricity, and has begun evaluating a shift to electrical equipment across the portfolio in response to the gas crisis (e.g., successfully switched Biryani By Kilo equipment to electrical).

subsections.label: Demand environment and consumer engagement
points: Demand sentiment during the quarter remained broadly stable, helped by favourable policy stimulus and GST rate rationalization.
Volume-leading growth in adjacent consumption categories like FMCG points to stable-to-improving demand trends.
Owned and franchise brands maintained positive SSSG trends.
Value-led initiatives and accessibility-focused campaigns at KFC are resonating well with customers, resulting in improved average daily sales trends and sequential recovery in SSSG performance.
Company believes business is well positioned for stronger performance during the year, though external and seasonal factors remain fluid.

Dine-in footfalls have improved industry-wide post Q4 per broader QSR commentary; company has treated online and offline as two different businesses with distinct pricing/incentive strategies to give consumers a reason to visit stores.
Management notes geopolitical/macro uncertainties (e.g., COVID and subsequent events) tend to put more pressure on small-scale players, which helps larger players like DIL consolidate further.
Strategic priorities remain unchanged: disciplined expansion, stronger profitability and deeper consumer relevance through innovation and digital engagement.
Company sees significant momentum on the travel segment, driving focus on opening multiple brands' food courts at highways, malls and food courts.

subsections.label: Proposed merger with Sapphire Foods
points: The proposed merger is a strategic combination of two scaled-up and complementary platforms, united by a shared vision for long-term growth.

Upon completion, the merged entity will emerge as one of the largest QSR platforms globally and as one of the largest partners for Yum!, with a diversified portfolio of leading brands, expanded geography reach and enhanced operational capabilities.
The merger is expected to unlock meaningful synergies, strengthen execution and create a more agile and efficient organization capable of accelerating growth across markets.
Process is progressing as per plan; company remains on track to complete the merger by the end of the current fiscal year.
Filings with stock exchanges have been completed; company expects to receive necessary approval shortly, following which it will proceed with the CCI application.
Combined entity, post-merger, is expected to be almost a USD 1 billion top line business.
FY27 store addition guidance of 200-225 stores is on a standalone DIL basis (including all brands: KFC, Costa, Vaango, Biryani By Kilo), not factoring in the merger scenario.
Mumbai territory operations are managed by Sapphire, not DIL, so Mumbai-specific questions must be addressed by Sapphire.

subsections.label: Management team transformation / DIL 2.0
points: Steps taken to transform the management team under new CEO Manish Dawar; largely new team expected to be in place by next quarter.
Focus is on bringing in experienced, forward-looking professionals with deep operational and strategic expertise as the company prepares for the next phase of growth and integration.

DIL 2.0 is a transformation journey led by new leadership and enabled by digital technology, automation and AI, aiming to build a common, scaled-up 'ONE DIL' view and a frictionless organization across employees, brands and technology.
Core pillars of DIL 2.0: reimagining how the company works, expanding brand reach, making the organization more efficient, and focusing on digital transformation.

Opportunities identified in driving greater collaboration across brands: sharing capabilities, common infrastructure, strategic thinking at middle management level, consumer insights and best practices across the portfolio, aiming for a leaner, more agile, more productive growth-oriented organization.

New leadership hires: Neeraj Tiwari as CTO (technology leadership gap identified); Sandeep Anand as CMO (also overseeing Pizza Hut operations, background combines QSR and technology); Robinder to lead Costa and smaller brands (New York Fries, Sanook Kitchen); a new COO (background from FMCG and technology, companies like Unilever and Amazon) also announced, expected to join in the next couple of weeks.
Rationale for leadership hires tied to skill-gap analysis conducted ahead of the impending merger with Sapphire Foods, given the combined entity's scale (~USD 1 billion top line).

Company had previously tied up with a leading IT company as a technology partner to develop its own apps and technology stack in-house, requiring in-house capability to manage the technology going forward.
Possible Analyst Day planned in the next couple of quarters to detail brand-by-brand strategy once the full new leadership team is in place.

subsections.label: Gas crisis
points: A significant gas crisis occurred in the country due to the Middle East war; teams managed it effectively with minimal impact on the business.
The gas crisis continues to be an issue in some parts of the country; company is not yet fully out of it and continues to monitor the situation closely.
Gas cost described as a small cost as a percentage of sales, though management did not disclose an exact figure.
In response, company is evaluating a shift to electrical equipment across the portfolio (e.g., Biryani By Kilo) and exploring dual gas/electric-capable equipment to mitigate future impact.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Elevated coffee and cocoa prices impacted input costs for the Franchise Brands portfolio, leading to a 1.2% YoY decline in gross margins for that segment.
Management stated it cannot foresee future inflation trends and therefore cannot comment on the likelihood of further near-term price increases.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical uncertainty
points: Macro-level factors are not controllable; multiple macro issues have recurred over the last 3-4 years starting from COVID.
Company accepts this as a reality and continues to focus on what is within its control, noting such situations put more pressure on small-scale players, aiding consolidation for larger players.

subsections.label: Store expansion outlook
points: Company expects to add approximately 200 to 225 net new stores in FY27 as DIL, with KFC expected to contribute 100 to 110 (also referenced as up to 120) stores of these additions.
The balance of additions will be driven by Costa Coffee, Biryani By Kilo and international businesses.
No net new Pizza Hut store additions planned for calendar year 2026 as the brand focuses on consolidation and realignment.
Guidance for 200-225 stores is on a standalone DIL basis (not factoring the Sapphire merger), covering KFC, Costa, Vaango, and Biryani By Kilo.

subsections.label: Merger completion timeline
points: Company remains on track to complete the merger with Sapphire Foods by the end of the current fiscal year.
Filings with stock exchanges completed; approval expected shortly, after which the CCI application will be filed.

subsections.label: SSSG sustainability outlook
points: Management expressed confidence in sustaining KFC's improved SSSG trends, noting it will take a couple more quarters to confirm the worst is behind, and remains uncertain about the macro environment going forward.

pressing_questions: Just wanted to understand the gross margin expansion on KFC, it is a pretty big number. What has really driven that?

quarters.summary: Devyani International is focusing on strategic initiatives, including a merger with Sapphire Foods, to strengthen its market position and improve operational efficiency. The company is also working on turning around its Pizza Hut business while continuing to expand its KFC outlets.

key_figures.label: Consolidated operating revenue for Q3 FY26

subsections.label: Financial Highlights
points: Consolidated operating revenue for Q3 FY26 was INR 1,441 crore, up 11.3% YoY.
Consolidated gross profit was INR 993 crore with margins at 68.9%, reflecting a 20 basis points improvement YoY.
Consolidated brand contribution was INR 200 crore, with a margin improvement to 13.9% from 11.7% in the previous quarter.
Operating EBITDA pre-Ind AS was INR 124 crore with margins at 8.6%, up from 6.8% in the previous quarter.
Reported EBITDA was INR 227 crore with margins at 15.7%.
Indian operations grew 12.1% YoY to reach INR 978 crore in revenues with a gross margin of 71%.
International business revenues reached INR 473 crore, up 10.1% YoY with improved gross margins at 64.9%.

points: KFC in India added 54 net new stores in Q3 FY26, reaching a total of 788 stores.
Average daily sales for KFC in Q3 FY26 was stable at INR 90,000.
KFC India revenue was INR 603 crore, up 5.9% YoY with a gross margin of 69.8%.
Brand contribution margin for KFC was 16.8%, 40 basis points lower than the previous year.

subsections.label: Pizza Hut Performance
points: Pizza Hut India opened 18 net new stores in Q3 FY26, ending with 639 stores.
Pizza Hut India revenue for the quarter was INR 178 crore with ADS at INR 31,000.
Gross margin for Pizza Hut was 76%, an improvement of 1.2% from the preceding quarter.
Pizza Hut delivered a positive brand contribution of INR 1.4 crore with margins at 0.8%.

subsections.label: Franchise and Own Brands Performance
points: Franchise brands, including Costa Coffee, posted revenues of INR 56 crore with stable gross margins at 75.7%.
Own brands, including Vaango and Biryani by Kilo, recorded revenues of INR 94 crore with gross margins at 64.2%.
Vaango crossed 100 stores with revenues of INR 20 crore for the quarter.

quarters.summary: Management reported the highest-ever Q1 performance across volumes, revenues, EBITDA and profit, driven by double-digit volume growth and strong demand pipeline across infrastructure, housing and urban real estate. Q2 FY27 is expected to be optically softer due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and full-quarter West Asia cost impact (INR130-140/ton), but management expects double-digit volume growth for FY27, prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter, net debt/EBITDA to stay below 1x, India Cements EBITDA/ton to reach INR1,000 by Q4 FY28, capacity to reach 212.7 million tons (grey, domestic) by end FY27 and beyond 242 million tons consolidated in 2-2.5 years, and Cables & Wires to launch in Q3 FY27.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 highlights
points: Q1 was the highest ever first quarter performance for UltraTech across volumes, revenues, EBITDA and profit.

Operating EBITDA per ton has been steady above INR1,200 this quarter, reflecting cost discipline and operating leverage while absorbing the sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory on a volume base enlarged by acquired assets still ramping up to system profitability.
The acquired assets' improvement capex-led cash flows through the P&L over fiscal '27 and '28 will result in the per-ton EBITDA trajectory moving upwards sustainably.

subsections.label: Cost pressures - Q1
points: The biggest one-off cost inflation in Q1 was fuel cost and packing bags, with packing bags having the larger cost impact.
Fuel cost went from INR874 to INR915 per ton, a 5% increase; INR25 to INR40 per ton increase in fuel cost alone.

Packing bags went from an average of about INR9/bag to peaks of INR14-15/bag before settling around INR10/bag, averaging about INR12/bag for the quarter (about INR20/ton impact); fuel contributed about INR40/ton and bags about INR20/ton.

Limestone raising cost rose 13-14% QoQ to the highest level in 2 years, driven largely by industrial diesel prices, which rose from INR78-80/litre pre-war to INR150s/litre during the war (about 50% increase, cited also as INR100 to INR157/litre).

subsections.label: Cost outlook - Q2 FY27
points: Q2 FY27 (July-September) will see the full impact of the war since costs will come to a head from July 1, plus monsoon-related maintenance costs (kilns undergoing maintenance) and negative operating leverage from lower seasonal volumes.

Management expects costs to rise by INR130 to INR140 per ton in aggregate, covering fuel, maintenance and operating deleverage combined - cannot attribute one line item specifically to the war versus normal seasonal effects.
The prior INR250 industry-wide cost impact estimate cited previously was described as 'not a very thorough number'; for UltraTech specifically, the increase is expected at INR130-140/ton.
There is a positive offset within the negative operating leverage as UltraTech's size (volumes) has continuously grown, giving some advantage versus smaller peers.

H2 FY27 variable costs (packaging, energy) are expected to be lower on a per-ton basis versus H1 if the war ends and oil, coal and pet coke prices subside; ocean freight insurance premiums have risen to 4-5% from below 1% due to the war.

subsections.label: India Cements turnaround
points: The printed revenue number of INR1,013 crores (vs INR1,021 crores same period last year) reflects an accounting adjustment - since Q1 FY27 the company reports ex-factory sales, net of freight cost; on a like-for-like basis (ex-freight), revenue was INR993 crores vs INR821 crores, a 21% growth backed by 19% volume growth.
India Cements' EBITDA per ton has climbed sequentially and unbroken: from roughly INR386/ton in Q2 FY26 to INR400 (Q3 FY26), INR509 (Q4 FY26) and INR603 (Q1 FY27).

Every lever behind the improvement is owned by the company: brand migration to UltraTech is 100% complete; premium and trade volumes are rising; cost improvement capex of about INR2,000 crores is being deployed into waste heat recovery, preheater upgradation, cooler upgradation etc.
Green power trajectory for India Cements is planned to step up from around 3% of power requirements to about 86% by end of FY28.
India Cements' conversion ratio has improved rapidly to already 1.5x for production.

Q2 FY27 may look optically softer for India Cements due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and West Asia cost effects, but management maintains that the INR1,000/ton EBITDA target remains in sight with full benefit of the capex program flowing through from Q4 FY28.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: As of now, the company is fully booked in terms of cash flows: all operating cash flows will be ploughed back into growth, and beyond that, into dividends for shareholders.
No foreseeable requirement for further investment in cables and wires beyond current plan; that business will first mature and milk the investment already made.
Capital allocation remains committed to cement and shareholders.

Dividend is viewed by the Board as a percentage of profits; management is 'expecting good dividends' going forward, without confirming whether last year's payout (which had a one-off/special component) is repeatable.

subsections.label: Historical outperformance vs industry (volume & EBITDA)
points: June 2022 quarter: UltraTech grew 17.7% in volume vs industry's ~15.5%; UltraTech EBITDA/ton of 1,230 vs industry's ~800.
June 2023 quarter: UltraTech grew 20% in volume vs industry's 15.4%; UltraTech EBITDA was 25% higher than industry.
June 2024 quarter: UltraTech grew 6.5% in volume while rest of industry degrew; UltraTech EBITDA was 26% higher.
June 2025 and September 2025 quarters saw a volume shock/degrowth for UltraTech, but the company recovered.
December 2025 quarter: UltraTech grew 15% vs industry growing about half that rate.
March 2026 quarter: UltraTech grew 9% vs industry growing less than half that rate.
June 2026 (Q1 FY27) quarter: UltraTech grew 13%; industry results awaited to assess market share gains.

subsections.label: Demand drivers - infrastructure
points: Maharashtra planning INR20,000 crores greenfield shipbuilding cluster anchored around Mazagaon Dock.
Odisha announced a deep seaport at Ganjam and shipbuilding cluster at Paradip with investment of over INR50,000 crores.
Tamil Nadu signed ~INR18,000 crores MoU for data centres and shipbuilding projects.
Ports, shipyards, data centres are among the most cement-intensive asset classes in the economy.
Cabinet approved ~INR20,000 crores plus Ahmedabad-Dholera semi high-speed rail corridor.
Metro programs continue to expand across Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune and Uttar Pradesh.
Additional ~INR30,000 crores infusion into NIIF with private capital across roads, ports and urban infrastructure.
India's capex revival is also being propelled by power and data centres, both concrete-hungry sectors.
Vadhavan port - multiple packages have already been awarded, meaning that work will commence, adding to positivity.
River linking (e.g., Ken-Betwa project) expected to be cement-intensive: river banks have to be built (concrete), with silting work and concrete structures on either side.

subsections.label: Demand drivers - housing & urban real estate
points: Housing and urban real estate has had a very strong start to calendar '26.

Across India's top 8 cities, Q1FY26 saw a very big growth in number of units sold per registry records; prices have remained strong, indicating a structurally mature end-user-driven market where absorption keeps pace with supply.
Bangalore stood out on the strength of GCC and technology sector employment.

Redevelopment is significant: Mumbai's Slum Rehabilitation Authority set to redevelop about 850 acres of land; developers continue land banking aggressively; private real estate companies continue to acquire land parcels across cities.
India's grade A office market opened Q1 with a very strong start - premium housing, redevelopment, office towers, hotels are building upwards and outwards simultaneously, all built on cement.

subsections.label: Macro backdrop
points: India's macroeconomic engines demonstrate resilience even as global energy markets endured a disruptive supply cycle.
Benchmark lending rates remain attractive, improving housing affordability and lowering cost of capital for infrastructure developers.
Near-term watch points: coal sector growth slowing in May, lower coal and refinery output, and modest 2% YoY state capex growth in April-May - viewed as timing effects, not a change in trend.

subsections.label: Monsoon/weather impact on demand
points: Part of Q1 demand was helped by drier weather, particularly in June; Rajasthan is going through a very dry patch and may face a water crisis next year impacting demand.
July onwards, wet spells have started across various parts of the country; barring 1-2 states, every state has experienced rains.
Still early in monsoon season - August and September data needed to assess weather progression and impact of dry/wet spells.

subsections.label: East region demand outlook
points: East was the slowest region in April-June, partly due to elections and labor availability.

Multiple Eastern states have gone through elections; land reforms about to come into place in one Eastern state; structural change will be visible over next 2-3-4 years, not next quarter - East expected to witness a good demand upcycle.

subsections.label: Pricing
points: Cement prices were constructive during the quarter; all-India exit prices improved through June even as monsoon sets in.
East and South led price improvements; Central and West were steady; North was a consistent performer.
Industry expects prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter due to cost increases - viewed as a constructive outcome for this time of year.
Cost escalations of the past 2 quarters are still to be fully passed through, and with demand momentum, a supportive price environment is expected as the busy season approaches.
Premiumization and blended cement mix continue to support blended realizations regardless of headline price movements.
Management said prices move with demand: if demand is strong on an all-India basis, prices can go up; if the cost curve comes down, prices are not necessarily forced to reduce.
On pricing outlook for the monsoon quarter, management said 'expecting higher is everybody's desire, we will attempt it, we'll see where we land.'

subsections.label: Brand transition - Kesoram and India Cements
points: Management converted the Kesoram and India Cements brands to 100% UltraTech; these brands were operating in B or C category space and the company did not vacate that space.

Post brand conversion, the true performance of UltraTech is visible; the team successfully converted customers who were buying B/C category cement into A category brand buyers willing to pay a price premium.
This conversion of B/C category markets to UltraTech at higher price points is cited as a key driver of the company's ability to outperform on both volumes and pricing versus peers.

subsections.label: Retail vs institutional market strategy
points: India is fundamentally a retail market for cement given low urbanization and low RMC penetration; management believes cement will remain a branded product play as long as India remains a retail, individual-homebuilder market.

Similar branded dynamics exist in other Indian commodities like steel (TMT rebar) and paints, because these are retail markets too - contrasted with markets like UAE where RMC is the biggest customer and there's no brand play.
For UltraTech specifically, despite having the largest number of RMC plants in the country (477), RMC is only 3.5% of total sales, underscoring the branded retail nature of the business.
The brand play will persist as long as India remains in nascent stages of RMC adoption and urbanization.

subsections.label: Network and reach
points: UltraTech has almost 76 operating facilities spread across the country.
Network of nearly 2,000 plus/minus warehouses.
150,000 channel partners across the country.
Dedicated transporters, with more than 50% of transport service providers dedicated to UltraTech.
16,000-plus employees across the country.
5,000-plus UBS stores (dedicated dealers/outlets for UltraTech Cement).

subsections.label: Capacity expansion
points: Projects under execution for capacity growth are backed by capex of about INR17,000 crores in the next 2 to 2.5 years.
Consolidated capacity to go beyond 242 million tons, with grey cement capacity reaching 212.7 million tons by end of fiscal '27 and the balance completed the following year.
Every ton of committed expansion is fully backed by secured limestone; there is no raw material constraint on the growth trajectory.
March 2028 exit target of 235 million tons domestic, implying 22-25 million tons added in FY28 beyond the 212 million tons expected by March 2027, and 37 million tons total added across FY27-28.

Team has already started working on growth plans beyond 240 million tons; industry capacity addition estimates for FY27-28 could not be firmly quantified as some industry players are reportedly revisiting their expansion plans.
Inorganic growth opportunities will be examined if they arise, alongside the organic capacity plan.
12 million tons of new capacity commissioned across the country in April-June, of which UltraTech commissioned 8.7 million tons at Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam and Patratu.
Current capacity stands at 200.1 million tons domestic and 205.5 million tons including international operations.

subsections.label: Green energy transition
points: Green power capacity stands at 1,897 MW, meeting 47% of total power requirement at end of quarter (lower average during the quarter itself).
71 MW of renewables and 19 MW of WHRS commissioned this quarter.
Expect to reach 2.5 to 3 gigawatts of green power very shortly.
Green power is a structural buffer that helped absorb the West Asia fuel cost shock and is cheaper than conventional power.
India Cements green power trajectory planned to step up from around 3% currently to about 86% of power requirements by end of FY28.

subsections.label: Cost efficiency levers
points: Cement lead distance has come down further from 367 km to 360 km, a 7 km reduction; annualized at INR2.5-3 per ton per kilometre, this represents a visible upfront saving.
Clinker conversion has improved to 1.5x, a small improvement.
Power consumption has gone down and power rate has gone down because of power mix changes.
Management prefers to present a comprehensive annual cost-saving number at year-end rather than quarter-by-quarter, since Q2 will show a negative (cost increase) performance.

subsections.label: Regional performance
points: East region was the slowest growing in April-June quarter, partly due to elections and labor availability.
South and North grew a shade below 15%.
West and Central grew above 15%.
East and South led price improvements during the quarter; Central and West were steady; North was a consistent performer.

subsections.label: Fuel sourcing strategy
points: Pet coke has become more expensive in energy terms than coal, making domestic coal more attractive to buy.
Company is fully inventory loaded on coal, which is expected to cap fuel cost per kcal from rising further beyond around INR2/Kcal.

subsections.label: Cables and Wires supply chain
points: Sourcing raw material from Hindalco, with a lead distance of only four hours, providing tangible working capital and logistics benefits.

Working capital will initially be higher due to inventory ramp-up; structurally, the company is working on financing suppliers to release working capital, targeting stabilization to around 30 days plus/minus after about six months (around April-June FY28).

subsections.label: Competitive positioning drivers
points: Decades of consistent delivery, bag after bag, site after site, has made UltraTech synonymous with reliability; quality standards apply to every ton, with product complaints resolved ASAP.
Complete network of plants (integrated plants, grinding units, bulk terminals) is focused on meeting customer requirements.
Legacy of governance and ethical conduct at Aditya Birla Group/UltraTech is at its highest pecking order, giving dealers and institutional buyers assurance that commands a premium.
Combination of network reach, brand trust, and quality is described as unique to UltraTech and not replicable by competitors.

subsections.label: Brand vs commodity dynamics
points: India's cement industry will remain a brand-driven, retail play as long as India remains an individual-homebuilder, low-urbanization market; similar to other Indian retail commodities like steel and paints which are also branded despite being commodities elsewhere in the world.
As RMC penetration remains low (industry ~20%, UltraTech 3.5%), brand power in the trade/retail market will remain central to the business for the foreseeable future.

subsections.label: India Cements merger considerations
points: Most targets set at the time of the India Cements acquisition are nearing completion; before contemplating merger into a stand-alone entity, remaining steps include completing the ongoing capex program and disposing of certain non-core assets (land).
Expected completion of the turnaround journey by Q4 FY28 or possibly a quarter earlier.
Certain operating parameters for India Cements still need to be brought in line with UltraTech's stand-alone performance.

Entire India Cements volume is now reported as part of UltraTech's consolidated (stand-alone) volume; the company has stopped reporting India Cements stand-alone volumes separately in the presentation/press release.

subsections.label: Cables and Wires new business launch
points: Project is on schedule and on budget, within the approved INR1,800 crores investment program (INR888 crores spent/committed to date).
Channel partners onboarding is moving at a frantic pace; facility setup is complete; trial runs have commenced; key regulatory approvals are in place; leadership team is on board.
SAP/ERP systems are in place; CRM is under testing and will be live before launch.
Reaffirmed commissioning and product launch in Q3 FY27 (October-December 2026), precisely as previously committed.
Management does not intend to scale up further capex in cables and wires for now; the business will first mature and 'milk' the current investment before any further expansion.
No formal guidance given for the Cables and Wires business other than the aim to be 'profitable, grounded and grow with the market.'

subsections.label: Track record of delivery
points: Company crossed 200 million tons of capacity a year early versus prior commitment.
Brand migration of India Cements and Kesoram was completed a quarter early versus prior commitment.
Cables and Wires launch commitment for Q3 FY27 is being reaffirmed and delivered as promised.

subsections.label: West Asia crisis / geopolitical risk
points: Q1 FY27 opened with the most disruptive situation - the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, crude crossed $100, and coal costs spiked; situation later de-escalated but remains fluid and uncertain.
Management cannot fully separate cost impacts attributable to the war versus normal seasonal/maintenance effects.
Ocean freight insurance premiums have risen to 4-5% from below 1% due to the war, reflecting broader disruption.
Structural buffers (green power, AFR substitution, reduced lead distance) helped the company absorb the shock better than peers.

subsections.label: Cost inflation risk
points: Sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory absorbed during the quarter.
Industrial diesel prices spiked sharply (from INR78-80/litre pre-war to INR150s/litre during war), driving up limestone raising costs by 13-14% QoQ to a 2-year high.
Cost pressure of INR130-140 per ton expected in Q2 FY27 from fuel, monsoon-related kiln maintenance, and negative operating leverage.
Cost escalations of the past two quarters are still to be fully passed through to prices.

subsections.label: Weather/monsoon risk
points: Dry spell in certain states (e.g., Rajasthan) could lead to water crisis and demand impact next year.
Still early in monsoon season; effects on demand to be clearer only in August-September.

subsections.label: Demand-side structural risk (long-term)
points: Management flagged that a slowdown in structural demand growth (e.g., people not buying houses, industrialization stalling, data centers shifting to other countries like Pakistan) would be the biggest challenge for the industry and the company over a 5-year horizon, though this is not currently foreseen.

subsections.label: Capacity constraint risk
points: If demand remains strong, the challenge for the company will be insufficient capacity, necessitating continued expansion.

subsections.label: Volume and demand outlook
points: Management is targeting double-digit volume growth for the full year FY27.
Industry volume growth for Q2 FY27 expected at around 7-8% based on marketing intelligence, though it is still early.
Q2 FY27 may look optically softer due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and West Asia cost effects, but the direction of travel and destination remain unchanged.

subsections.label: Cost and margin outlook
points: Cost increase of INR130-140 per ton expected in Q2 FY27, covering fuel, monsoon maintenance and operating deleverage combined.
H2 FY27 variable costs expected to be lower per ton than H1 if the war ends and oil/coal/pet coke prices stabilize.
Comprehensive annual cost-saving numbers (previously flagged around INR200+/ton for FY28) will be given at year-end rather than quarter by quarter, since sequential figures can look mixed.
The 'magical' INR1,400 per ton EBITDA figure previously discussed is reiterated for the January-March 2028 quarter, contingent on there being no war.

subsections.label: Capacity and capex outlook
points: Grey cement domestic capacity to reach 212.7 million tons by end of FY27, with consolidated capacity to go beyond 242 million tons in the next 2-2.5 years, backed by capex of about INR17,000 crores.

March 2028 domestic capacity exit target of 235 million tons, implying 37 million tons of capacity addition across FY27-28; industry-wide capacity addition estimates remain unclear as some players are reportedly revisiting expansion plans.
Team has begun work on growth plans beyond 240 million tons; more details to be shared once finalized.
Inorganic growth opportunities will be examined if they arise, alongside organic expansion.

subsections.label: India Cements outlook
points: India Cements EBITDA per ton target of INR1,000 remains in sight, with full capex benefit flowing through the P&L from Q4 FY28.

Merger of India Cements into a stand-alone entity is contemplated only after completion of the capex program and disposal of certain non-core (land) assets, expected around Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier.
Green power mix for India Cements targeted to reach about 86% of power requirements by end of FY28, up from about 3% currently.

subsections.label: Cables and Wires outlook
points: Commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Q3 FY27 (October-December 2026), within the approved INR1,800 crores capex program.
No further capex scale-up planned for now; business will first mature and 'milk' the current investment.
No formal financial guidance given; management's stated aim is to be profitable, grounded and grow with the market ('sky is the limit' but no specific numbers).

subsections.label: Balance sheet and capital allocation outlook
points: Net debt to EBITDA expected to remain below 1x for the year, continuing the trend of prudent leverage management.

Capital allocation remains focused on growth capex (fully funded via internal accruals) and shareholder dividends; dividend framed as a percentage of profits, with management expecting 'good dividends' though not confirming repeatability of the prior year's special/one-off component.

We are confident that this year also, we'll end the net debt to EBITDA below 1x.

A step change in the green power trajectory from around 3% of their power requirements to about 86% of their power requirements by the end of fiscal '28.

themes.note: Double-digit volume growth (13.1%) driven by strong demand pipeline across infrastructure, housing and urban real estate; management targets double-digit volume growth for FY27.

themes.label: Cost pressures
themes.note: Fuel, packing bag and industrial diesel/limestone cost inflation from the West Asia crisis; further INR130-140/ton cost increase expected in Q2 FY27.

themes.label: Brand transition

themes.label: M&A integration (India Cements/Kesoram)

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: Domestic capacity reached 200.1 million tons with consolidated capacity targeted beyond 242 million tons in 2-2.5 years, backed by INR17,000 crores capex.

themes.label: Green energy transition

key_takeaways: Q1 was the highest ever first quarter performance for UltraTech across volumes, revenues, EBITDA and profit.
Domestic grey cement volumes grew 13.1%, capacity utilization improved to 81% from 76%, EBITDA of INR5,146 crores and PAT of INR2,604 crores, up 17.2% YoY.
Kesoram and India Cements brands have been converted to 100% UltraTech; the converted brand grew 21.3% YoY as B/C category customers migrated to the A category UltraTech brand at a price premium.
Operating EBITDA per ton held steady above INR1,200 despite the sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory, reflecting cost discipline and operating leverage.

India Cements delivered a clear turnaround: like-for-like revenue grew 21% and volumes grew 19%, with EBITDA per ton climbing sequentially from INR386 (Q2FY26) to INR400, INR509 and INR603 (Q1FY27); India Cements EBITDA per ton of INR1,000 remains targeted by Q4 FY28.

Domestic capacity reached 200.1 million tons and total capacity 205.5 million tons after commissioning of Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam and Patratu; consolidated capacity to go beyond 242 million tons in 2-2.5 years backed by ~INR17,000 crores capex.
Cables and Wires project remains on schedule and on budget, reaffirming commissioning and product launch in Q3 FY27.
Net debt to EBITDA improved to 0.87x from 0.94x at start of year, and company remains confident of ending FY27 below 1x.
Q2 FY27 expected to be optically softer due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and full quarter impact of West Asia cost disruption, with an expected INR130-140 per ton cost increase.
pressing_questions: What is the sort of working capital days for the Cables and Wires business, particularly on inventory days given the low lead distance from suppliers like Hindalco?
What steps remain before India Cements could be merged into a stand-alone entity, given most acquisition targets are nearing completion?
Given industry players revisiting expansion plans, what is UltraTech's estimate of industry-wide capacity addition for FY27-28?
Is there a structural shift toward prioritizing profitability/pricing over market share, or vice versa, if input costs decline later in the year?
How cement-intensive are river-linking projects like Ken-Betwa compared to something like a hydropower plant?

quarters.summary: UltraTech expects sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum in FY27 and beyond, targets double-digit volume growth for UltraTech itself in FY27, plans capex of INR8,000-10,000 crores every year for the foreseeable future to grow beyond 240 million tons capacity (37 million tons already committed to take capacity to 242.5 million tons by FY28), and expects cost-efficiency programs (India Cements/Kesoram) to push India Cements EBITDA/ton beyond INR1,000 by FY28, with near-term cost headwinds from the West Asia conflict (fuel, bags, forex) being managed via pricing and sourcing measures; leverage to be maintained below 1x.

subsections.label: Margin and cost drivers
points: EBITDA per ton improvement driven by improving trade mix and premiumization along with realization gains.
