key_takeaways: Total income was INR788.7 crores, up 134.9% versus INR335.8 crores in the same period last year. Commercial CMS projects drove the growth with CMS contributing over two thirds of revenue this quarter.

Gross margin was 62.1% versus 56.3% in Q4FY25, driven largely by the business mix. Higher freight cost was managed towards the end of the quarter due to the conflict while ensuring continuity of supply to customers.

EBITDA stood at INR319.4 crores and a margin of 40.5%. This exceptional operating margin reflects the record high revenue this quarter, and it is also partly because of a function of the uneven nature of revenue flows and should not be seen as an indicator of future performance.

For the FY, revenue was INR2053.1 crores versus INR1,497.3 crores, a growth of 37.1%. EBITDA was INR603.4 crores versus INR342.8 crores in FY25 with FY26 EBITDA margin at 29.4% compared to 22.9% last year.

For the FY26, the free cash flow was negative at INR49.4 crores, driven primarily by higher working capital during the year, along with increased capital cash outflows. Working capital days stood at 137 days in Q4FY26 versus 107 days in Q4FY25, mainly driven by higher inventories and receivables, and we believe that this should normalize in FY27.

While we have not given formal guidance in the past that we do not intend to do so going forward, we did indicate earlier that FY26 would be a year of strong growth when viewed against FY24... this outlook was accurate.

A key element of this is our investment in large-scale peptide commercial facilities. This will help us move into a more differentiated space, focused not only on peptide fragments, but also on peptide APIs.

As we experienced in FY26, growth over the next 2 to 3 years is also expected to remain lumpy... if performance is assessed over a longer horizon, say, 10 to 12 quarters, a clear trend line should emerge consistent with the growth outlook that we have always outlined.

The role change between Sucheth and me effective April 1 was part of a preplanned transition... the Board felt it would be more effective for one of us to focus more on the day-to-day business and the other promoter to focus more in terms of the long-term.
pressing_questions: Sir, in Q3 con call, an individual investor has asked a question about inventory manipulation. But in the transcript, some words are changed, which has changed the essence of the question, whereas the audio on your website is crystal clear and SEBI guidelines also don't allow these changes. This looks like actual manipulation somewhere. Can you please justify this? (Management response deferred: 'I'll have to check back on what you have mentioned and then revert back to you.')

quarters.summary: Q3FY26 total income grew 11.4% YoY but gross margin and EBITDA margin declined QoQ due to product mix (absence of a high-margin CMS product and paliperidone shipment delay), plus a one-time labor code impact. Management maintains that the medium-term/2-3 year growth trajectory remains largely preordained by existing CMS/GDS products ramping up, with peptide and big-pharma engagement seen as key drivers of growth beyond 3 years; no specific numeric guidance was given for Q4/FY26.

key_figures.label: EBITDA margin excluding labor code impact
Profit before tax (prior year, before extraordinary items)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin was a function of the product mix within the business this quarter; includes manufacturing expenses and other costs attributed to the product.
Lower gross margins combined with increase in overheads led to lower EBITDA margin of 19% this quarter.
Overheads include an impact of INR10 crores towards labor codes in Q3FY26; without this impact EBITDA would be INR95 crores at 21% margin.

One high-margin CMS product did not ship this quarter, and paliperidone (a high-margin GDS specialty product) also did not ship due to operational issues at customer end — these two products were the major factors impacting gross margin.
CMS product margins are significantly higher than prime API/GDS product margins; rest of products were pretty consistent.

Management states this quarter's gross margin is an outlier/aberration due to product mix and a few smaller factors, not a steady representation of future margins; last two-three quarters gross margins seen as better representation.
Business believed capable of 30%+ EBITDA margin if everything favorable, sustainable at higher gross margins; FY24 ~30% EBITDA margin cited as fair representation of business capability.

subsections.label: Working capital and cash flow
points: Deterioration in working capital over last few quarters due to higher inventories and uneven order flow leading to higher receivables at quarter end.
Optimal utilization of cash remains top priority; focus on inventory optimization, accelerated customer collections, and even delivery flow.

Inventory is being ramped up ahead of expected revenue ramp-up from expanded capacities; inventory holding period expected to normalize from ~124 days (4 months) to ~90 days (3 months) over next 2-3 quarters.

Increase in PAT should be correlated with increase in inventory only insofar as inventory is being built for future sales, not as a direct profit-from-inventory-gain relationship (management pushback on analyst's inventory-gain hypothesis).
Free cash flow was restricted to negative INR9.2 crores for the year having secured substantial advances from customers.
Capex investments moving in line with plan, adjusted to deal with evolving nature of the business.

subsections.label: Overall summary
points: Q3FY26 financials in line with expectations even as it was a dip quarter-to-quarter.
Company expects FY26 to be a year of growth and remains optimistic about the future given business potential.
Remain committed to balancing growth and profitability by continuously optimizing costs and processes for long-term sustainability.

subsections.label: Order flow and lumpiness
points: Ramp-up of new production and molecules happening in a lumpy manner, with individual shipments potentially around INR100 crores or INR50 crores.
New business coming in with deliveries expected to happen over 12 to 24 months.
Larger value of individual CMS shipments as business is prospering means small changes in operational/logistical details can have big impact on a quarter's performance, affecting operating leverage.

subsections.label: Pipeline dynamics
points: Development pipeline (preclinical to Phase III) actively maintained; number of commercial molecules (9) has stagnated but value per molecule has increased significantly — first commercial CMS molecule was ~INR30 crores, now several multi-hundred crore molecules exist in CMS pipeline.
Some projects that were previously worked on became unviable, offsetting new project additions; company aims to keep the pipeline list active rather than inflate numbers.

Business development team's goals are aligned around quality of projects and customers rather than sheer count; threshold for engagement with marketplace has risen over the years (now seeking well-funded programs with reasonable chance of reaching clinic).

Company cannot foresee whether a Phase II/III drug becomes a multi-hundred-crore molecule or remains a smaller ~INR50 crores molecule; pipeline table is described as a dispassionate, lagging representation of reality, not predictive of scale.

subsections.label: Prime GDS portfolio
points: Ezetimibe and Mirtazapine continue to be key contributors for the prime GDS portfolio.

On the specialty side, Apixaban and Donepezil contributed, but there was significant impact from Paliperidone due to operational issues at the customer end causing delay in shipments — a reminder of inherent business risk.

subsections.label: CMS/CDMO business
points: Commercial CMS projects contributed to over 50% of the revenue this quarter, along with other priority sustains.
CMS business seeing good traction with a range of customers across geographies; existing portfolio doing well in terms of customer relationships.

Commercialization of a new CMS molecule occurred, with shipments in the tail end of the quarter, though a lot remains to be shipped; expected to be a continuous, growing business into Q4 and next year, though revenue contribution this quarter was small.

Additional volume capacity expansion for a CMS product (in Unit 3) has been successfully completed and ramp-up has started, with volumes shipped in Q3; ramp-up still very early and expected to take another one or two quarters to pick up.

subsections.label: Peptide capability and R&D investment
points: Traction on the peptide side of the business, with customers keen to work with Neuland across the life cycle of products from process design to commercial manufacturing.
At least 5 or 6 innovators have come into Neuland this year with peptide projects underway in development, though still very early stage without revenue certainty.
It would be ideal for Neuland in FY27 to secure at least one commercial manufacturing arrangement for a peptide NCE; considered very much possible and something the company is working towards.
Large peptide facility being set up will be ready for commissioning in July.
Big pharma engaging with Neuland on peptides at an early, conversation stage; peptides seen as a likely entry point to new big pharma relationships not previously familiar with Neuland.
Board approved shifting the R&D facility to a new campus in Genome Valley to build a state-of-the-art R&D center, including a modern process development/scale-up facility for peptides.
Combination of new modern peptide R&D setup with newly created large-scale peptide manufacturing capacity would create a configuration likely unmatched by many Indian CDMOs.

subsections.label: Unit 3 capacity ramp-up
points: Additional volume capacity expansion for a CMS product completed in Unit 3; ramp-up started with volumes shipped in Q3, but still very early — expected to take another one or two quarters to pick up.

Company has not yet reached the capacities it has built; ramp-up timeline and path to full capacity utilization still being uncovered, involving supply chain complexity, inventory management, product manufacturing/modification, and regulatory filings across different markets.

No fundamental problems facing the ramp-up; it is simply a matter of time to reach full production, both for the Unit 3 new facility and other CDMO molecules; CMS business expected to ramp up fairly rapidly.

subsections.label: Peptide facility
points: Large-scale peptide manufacturing capacity is being created and will be ready for commissioning in July.
New R&D campus in Genome Valley will include modern process development/scale-up facility for peptides, complementing the large-scale manufacturing capacity.

subsections.label: Trade deals impact
points: India-EU and India-U.S. trade deals discussed: EU deal reduces tariffs/fees for API import, which is traditionally borne by customers (formulators), making Indian API procurement slightly cheaper for European pharma companies and making Neuland marginally more attractive; no material change expected.

U.S. deal has no direct benefit since pharma has been exempt from tariffs all along; deal removes a bit of an overhang for the industry, but does not alleviate the potential concern about continued U.S. intent to secure domestic API manufacturing, which the company will monitor and strategize around.

subsections.label: Inventory and supply chain complexity
points: Ramp-up of new production facility involves complexity not just in supply chain (inventories and inventory management) but also product manufacturing, modification, and regulatory filings across different markets.
Even the drug product manufacturer (customer) sometimes fails to fully comprehend all these domains that need to be addressed for ramp-up.

subsections.label: Innovator engagement strategy
points: Innovators increasingly viewing Neuland as an integral partner in the innovation journey; increasing interest from a wider range of customers in Neuland's capabilities as a proven commercial NCE drug substance manufacturer and developer of robust processes for complex molecules.
Track record as an agile partner opening more possibilities and increasing share of existing business.
CDMO industry is competitive, but Neuland has carved out a space with focused strategy, building adjacencies and working with customers on cutting edge of innovation.

Engaging with innovators and biotech/big pharma to identify 'white spaces' where they need a partner like Neuland — process led to the peptide manufacturing investment identified 2-3 years ago after recognizing capacity saturation in the West amid emergence of GLP-1/amylin analogues.

Next 2-3 years focus: aggressively find partnerships in peptides to monetize the built assets; beyond that, could pursue other white spaces such as new modalities (e.g., oligonucleotide) or geographic expansion (building capabilities in the U.S. or Europe).
On generic side, customers remain keen to work with Neuland given track record and portfolio of products.

Organizational scaling needed: a team suited to handle an INR1,500-2,000 crore business may not be suited for an INR5,000-10,000 crore business; company working on upskilling and expanding teams to think from a growth perspective and deploy capital appropriately while balancing growth-capital risk.

subsections.label: Business transformation journey
points: Neuland began as a quality-focused API manufacturer over 4 decades ago; evolved over the last 15 years working with venture-backed biotech companies on NCE molecules; business now transitioned such that majority of revenues derive from human-health focused CDMO business, and company has started working with big pharma.

Historic transition (started ~2005-2006) from low-margin APIs to complex APIs/CDMO services involved two major challenges: (1) capital allocation for facility modification to accommodate Phase II/III CDMO molecules with no guaranteed return to underwrite investment, and (2) organizational/internal challenge of discontinuing low-margin, high-volume legacy products (e.g., Ranitidine, once one of the largest products) despite resistance from customers (even with 2-year notice periods) and internal teams.

GDS business mindset shift: operations team's mindspace historically dominated by GDS products even though more value comes from CMS projects; transition in planning team's outlook has been underway over the last 2 years.
Long-term strategic plan takes a longer-term view (2-3 year horizon) given natural unevenness and long gestation periods of CDMO and specialty GDS businesses.

Company aspires to decadal growth; potential for the business to grow at 20%+ CAGR from 2026 to 2036, contingent on a sequence of right plans falling into place; currently viewed as being in the early phase of the growth cycle since ramp-ups are yet to begin.

subsections.label: Flagged risk factors
points: High-risk nature of customers' attempts to bring novel therapies for unmet medical needs impacts Neuland's projections time and again.
Changing regulations and developments in underlying industries are changing business dynamics.
Performance of individual products can significantly influence overall business performance (e.g., paliperidone shipment delay due to customer-end operational issues).
Foreign exchange fluctuations, raw material cost volatility, and unforeseen geopolitical risks flagged as factors that could significantly influence business performance.
Continued U.S. intent to secure domestic API manufacturing remains a potential overhang/concern not alleviated by the India-U.S. trade deal.

Business inherently uneven and lumpy on a quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year basis, making quarterly performance difficult to predict or model; product-mix-related developments are very difficult to call out ahead of time.

subsections.label: Forward outlook
points: Company expects FY26 to be a year of growth and remains optimistic about future potential, though Q3 was a dip quarter-to-quarter.

Management declines to give specific guidance for Q4 or FY26, citing lumpy ramp-up (potential shipments of INR100 crores or INR50 crores) and preferring to be guarded rather than directional; suggests looking at medium-term horizon rather than quarter-on-quarter.
Growth for the next 2-3 years viewed as largely 'preordained' since products are already in place and just need to be executed, notwithstanding occasional quarterly hiccups.
Growth beyond the 3-year period will depend on newer investments such as peptide capacity, expanded wallet share with big pharma relationships, and other uncertain factors.
Company aspires to a 20%+ CAGR over the 2026-2036 decade, contingent on execution of a sequence of strategic plans.
EBITDA margins of ~25-30% (with FY24 ~30% cited) viewed as representative of business's margin capability going forward, with potential for 30%+ if conditions are favorable.

Gross margin trajectory: this quarter's dip viewed as an aberration; last 2-3 quarters seen as better representation of sustainable gross margins going forward; management declines to give a specific gross margin number/guidance.
Paliperidone-related shipment delay expected to resolve in next financial year (FY27).

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect FY '26 to be a year when we see growth and we continue to be optimistic about the future, given the potential that our business holds.
Management declined to give any specific guidance for Q4 or the remainder of FY26, citing lumpy ramp-up and requesting focus on medium-term horizon instead.
Growth for the next 2 to 3 years is kind of preordained by the fact that these products are already there, and we just need to execute.
There is a potential for a business like this to grow at 20-plus CAGR, but that requires a sequence of right plans to fall in place.

EBITDA margins that we've had in FY '24, which is around 30%, is a fair representation of the kind of margins that this business is capable of; we believe this business is capable of 30% EBITDA margin and higher if everything is in favor.

The gross margin that you've seen in this quarter is more of an outlier or an aberration; what we have seen in the last two, three quarters is perhaps a better representation of the gross margins going forward.
The ramp-up has started and volumes were shipped in Q3, but it is going to take maybe another one or two quarters to really pick up.

A lot of the additional CMS molecule remains to be shipped; going forward in Q4 and into the next year, we believe it will be a continuous business going forward, though revenue contribution this quarter is a very small component.

It would be ideal for Neuland in FY27 if we were able to secure at least 1 commercial manufacturing arrangement for a peptide NCE. That's something that is very much possible and that we are working towards.
Large peptide facility will be ready for commissioning in July.
The paliperidone shipment issue is expected to resolve next financial year.
You will see inventory days coming back to something like 90 days from the current 124 days over the next two or three quarters.

risk_register.risk: High-risk nature of customers' drug development for unmet medical needs impacting projections
risk_register.note: Constantly reminded of this risk impacting Neuland's projections time and again.
Number of developments in underlying industries changing the dynamics for Neuland.
Paliperidone shipment delay due to customer-end operational issues, and absence of a high-margin CMS product, significantly impacted quarter's margins.
Flagged as a factor that could significantly influence business performance.
Flagged as a factor that could significantly influence business performance.
Unforeseen geopolitical risks flagged as an influencing factor.

India-U.S. trade deal removes some overhang from tariff exemption uncertainty, but does not alleviate the potential concern of continued U.S. intent to secure API manufacturing domestically; company will monitor and strategize.

Inherent uneven nature of overall business on quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year basis; large individual CMS shipment values mean small operational/logistical changes can materially affect a quarter.
Higher inventories and uneven order flow led to higher receivables at quarter end; working capital at 145 days of sales.
Some projects previously worked on became unviable even as new projects (6-8) were added last quarter; company actively manages list rather than inflating numbers.

themes.label: Gross margin volatility / product mix
themes.note: Gross margin fell to 52.1% from 53.2% YoY due to absence of a high-margin CMS product and paliperidone shipment delay; management calls this quarter an aberration.

themes.label: CMS/CDMO ramp-up
themes.note: Unit 3 capacity expansion and new CMS molecule commercialization are ramping up, expected to pick up further over the next 1-2 quarters.

themes.label: Peptide capex and innovator traction
themes.note: 5-6 innovators engaged on peptide projects; large peptide facility to be commissioned in July; FY27 target to secure a commercial peptide NCE arrangement.

themes.label: Working capital and inventory build
themes.note: Inventory days rose to 124 from 94 (FY25) ahead of expected revenue ramp-up; expected to normalize to ~90 days over next 2-3 quarters.

themes.label: Long-term growth aspiration
themes.note: Management reiterates 2-3 year growth is largely preordained by existing products, with a decadal aspiration of 20%+ CAGR (2026-2036) contingent on execution.

themes.label: Trade policy / tariff overhang
themes.note: India-EU and India-U.S. trade deals seen as marginally positive/neutral; U.S. reshoring intent for API manufacturing remains an unresolved overhang.

themes.label: Business unevenness / lumpiness
themes.note: Management repeatedly emphasizes inherent lumpiness of CDMO/GDS business, cautioning against quarter-on-quarter interpretation of results.

key_takeaways: Total income was INR447.8 crores, which is 11.4% YoY as compared to INR401.9 crores in the same period last year. The commercial CMS projects contributed to over 50% of the revenue and other priority sustains for this quarter.
The gross margin for the quarter was 52.1% as compared to 53.2% in Q3FY25 and was a function of the product mix within the business this quarter.

The EBITDA stood at INR85 crores at a margin of 19%. The lower gross margins this quarter, combined with the increase in overheads led to a lower EBITDA margin of 19% this quarter. The overheads include an impact of INR10 crores towards labor codes in Q3FY26. Without this impact, our EBITDA would stand at INR95 crores with a margin of 21%.
The profit before tax was INR54.3 crores as compared to INR71.8 crores in Q3FY25 before extraordinary items, which is the sale of property and the quarterly EPS stands at INR31.5 per share.
The 9-month performance shows that we have been able to maintain a 56% margin versus the same period of 55% last year.

The working capital for the quarter stood at 145 days of sales... there was a cash outflow of INR254 crores towards capex for the 9MFY26... we have been able to restrict free cash flows to negative INR9.2 crores for the year having secured substantial advances from our customers. Our net debt stood at negative INR202.6 crores.

Ezetimibe and Mirtazapine continue to be key contributors for the prime GDS portfolio. On the specialty side, we saw Apixaban, Donepezil contribute, but there was a significant impact from Paliperidone where we had some operational issues at the customer end, which has caused some sort of a delay in terms of shipments.
During the last quarter, we were able to take that significant step as our Board had approved shifting of our R&D facility to a new campus where we can build a state-of-the-art R&D center.
pressing_questions: Sir, my question was a bit different. I'm looking at last 4-year data. So either are we transitioning to a much bigger size molecule and hence, looking at the number, number of commercials is not relevant or has there been far more dropouts and that trend is not going to be there anymore at this for next 2 years. Only then we can achieve this 20% curve that you are indicating either of the two has to play out?

And last suggestion, because you indicated Q3 was on expected lines. And if you were aware that there is going to be a significant product mix, a qualitative callout would help given that our quarterly are very volatile, a qualitative callout will help us then outsiders. If it was on expected lines as you indicated in the beginning?
So, prima facie, it looks like whatever profits we do are due to inventory gain. So, can you please provide some clarity on these points? Or will we be seeing any write-off?

NEULANDLAB.about: Neuland Laboratories is engaged in manufacturing and selling of bulk drugs and caters to both domestic and international markets.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was soft with flat YoY volumes amid extreme PVC resin price volatility and inventory write-downs hurting consolidated EBITDA margins (7% normalized). Management expects Q2 FY27 to show double-digit YoY volume growth, second half FY27 stronger than first half post-monsoon, and continues to guide for high double-digit volume growth in FY27 and coming years, with EBITDA margins sustained at 7-8% over the next 12-15 months before inching up with operating leverage from Varanasi and Window profile plant ramp-ups.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Consol EBITDA was hurt due to inventory write-downs, aggressive pricing and fixed expenses for new business verticals.
One-offs included upfront costs linked to Varanasi plant ramp-up and additional salary costs to build a ground-level team for the Window profile (D2C) business.
Majority of the shortfall from the 7% consol EBITDA margin was attributable to inventory losses, per management's simple math explanation.

At Kisan, business-level EBITDA margin is actually 5-6% (6-7% excluding inventory losses), but P&L optics were hurt by inventory losses amid PVC price volatility; margin improvement expected once volumes pick up.

subsections.label: Working capital initiatives
points: Inventory at 80 days reflects softer sales volume in the last six months; scope to rationalize as sales momentum picks up in coming quarters and by FY27-end, releasing funds at both raw material and finished goods levels.

Debtor days stable at 30, supported by cash-and-carry schemes working well in stronger markets (South and West India experience improving, cash-and-carry being gradually introduced there too); target to bring debtor days down to 25 by FY27-end or H1 FY28.
Credit terms with suppliers expected to improve as raw material buying scale increases from Q2/Q3 onwards (following flattish volumes in FY26 and Q1 FY27), aiding further working capital release.

Company working on all three working capital levers - inventory, debtors, and creditors - to bring net working capital days down from current 45 to target of 30, with potential to eventually release 10-15 days of working capital by next year.

subsections.label: Funding strategy
points: Company is almost net cash; past CAPEX of Rs.500-600 crores over last 2-3 years was funded via internal cash flow and fundraise from promoters and a foreign fund.

Total CAPEX planned for FY27 and FY28 is Rs.200 crores (Rs.100 crores each year), 100% expected to be funded from internal cash flow with no requirement for debt or equity raise; only if incremental funding is needed beyond internal generation would debt or equity be considered.
Next leg of CAPEX requirement over next 5 years pegged at Rs.600-700 crores, with 70-80% expected to be funded from internal cash flows.

Return ratio math (25% ROC on Rs.5,000 crore revenue target) remains unchanged from previous call; based on projected gross block of ~Rs.1,500 crores, working capital of Rs.300-400 crores (at 25-30 days), total gross capital employed of Rs.1,800-1,900 crores, and EBITDA of Rs.500-600 crores at 10-12% margin.
There is room for near-term margin improvement of 50-100 bps, with a further 50-100 bps improvement expected post plant stabilization.
Cost synergies from Kisan merger expected at ~1% at overall company level post-merger.

key_figures.label: Kisan sales volume Q4 FY26 (most recent)
Q2 FY27 YoY volume growth expectation

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Both primary and secondary demand in April were worst hit due to extreme PVC price drop of 30% in first 20 days; recovery started from May onwards.
Construction segment forms 60% of sales and is expected to be the main driver of sales momentum as monsoon recedes.

Agri demand normally strong in March/April but April suffered due to PVC price crash; some pent-up demand seen in May/June; monsoon currently slowing agri demand, with construction expected to take over as main contributor.
July trends are in line with the decent momentum seen in May and June.
Over next 15-20 days, overall demand expected to be slightly soft due to peak monsoon, before construction activity picks up strongly post-monsoon.

Distributors have been very cautious on restocking given PVC price volatility; if price stability sustains for the next 10-15 days, restocking is expected to begin, boosting overall industry sales in Q2.

Despite industry-wide volume contraction, Apollo maintained flattish volume YoY (total sales volume growth flat YoY in Q1 FY27), suggesting market share gains as smaller players with weaker balance sheets struggled to absorb inventory write-downs.

Kisan sales volume has run at ~5,500 tons/quarter over the last 4 quarters, versus current plant capacity of 8,000-8,500 tons/quarter, though Q4 FY26 volume ticked up to ~7,000 tons (vs ~6,500 tons in Q4 FY25).
Q2 FY27 YoY volume growth is expected to be double-digit.

subsections.label: Pricing environment
points: Minimum Import Price (MIP) applied ~12 days back at $766 per MT (~Rs.82/Kg on export basis); current Reliance price is slightly above this, and market price is 1-2% above MIP level, creating a premium.

Premium sustained despite monsoon due to low channel-partner inventories and steady demand; prices expected to remain stable to slightly downward in the coming weeks but cannot fall below the Rs.82/Kg MIP floor set by the Indian government.

PVC resin availability issue in past few days attributed mainly to extensive rains disrupting port de-stuffing, not to customs duty or MIP-related supply constraints; global availability is not a problem (material available within +/-10 days of schedule).

Following the extreme Q1 price drop, importers had been discouraged from importing resin; with market stabilization and MIP providing a price floor, importing activity is resuming, and no supply disruption is expected in the near future.

subsections.label: Product-wise performance commentary
points: CPVC grew YoY in Q1 despite flattish company-level growth; Lubrizol tie-up is showing results already, and co-branding/co-marketing activities are expected to create more visibility for both brands and house of APL Apollo; CPVC portfolio growth is expected to be a major contributor to targeted high double-digit company volume growth.

Window profile is ramping up as a direct D2C product offering, requiring additional salary/team-building costs at the ground level; targeted to contribute 7-8% of revenue in FY27, settling at ~10% at current capacity utilization, with long-term potential to reach 15% of overall Apollo Pipes portfolio.
New products carry a margin profile of 10-15% and a ROC focus target of 25%, in line with ongoing strategy.
Bath fittings are kind of flattish.
Water tank is growing in double-digit.
Government infrastructure business (O-PVC or HDPE) is almost zero, one of the major drags on overall volume remaining flat.
Fittings is doing fine with single-digit growth despite tough last five quarters, a period during which the segment faced difficult conditions.
Kisan business EBITDA margin has run at 5-6% at business level in recent quarters, reflecting 12 months of weak macro/industry support.
Company has stopped sharing segmental data; segment-wise growth across agri, plumbing and infra not separately disclosed given flattish overall performance.

Each large plant target EBITDA margin

subsections.label: Plant ramp-up and expansion
points: Varanasi plant is newly commissioned and ramping up; Q1 industry scenario is not the right barometer for its performance, but traction is being seen from Q2 onwards; total revenue capacity at full utilization is Rs.300 crores, with utilization targeted at 30% in FY27, 50-70% in FY28, and the balance (implying full utilization) in FY29.
Maharashtra plant (under Kisan) continues to ramp up.
Long-term target by FY31: four large plants across India, each contributing Rs.800-1,000 crores revenue with 10%+ EBITDA margin from the PVC pipes business (piping, UPVC, CPVC, fittings).

Other products (window profiles, water tank, solvents, bath fittings) plus new additions are targeted to generate a combined Rs.1,000 crores revenue portfolio within the next four years - the long-term five-year goal for Apollo Pipes in plumbing and bath fitting.
Kisan-side rationalization: team rationalization undertaken, a few plants within Kisan shut down, focus placed on Tarapur plant to feed all of Maharashtra and neighbouring states.
Kisan brand being launched at some Apollo Pipes distributors in South and North India.

South India plant: land identification underway with some pockets already identified; land acquisition expected to be completed in FY27, with plant construction starting from Q2 of the following year; two milestones (Varanasi ramp-up and Maharashtra/Kisan plant ramp-up) are prerequisites before starting South India plant, but timeline can be fast-tracked if these plants perform better than expected.

Plant geographic positioning strategy: Secunderabad mother plant covers North; Kisan plant covers West (Maharashtra, Gujarat, partly Madhya Pradesh); Varanasi plant covers Uttar Pradesh and Bihar belt till Odisha; missing piece is a larger South India plant (small existing Bangalore plant has very limited capacity); once all four plants ramp up fully, additional satellite plants could be added if required.

subsections.label: Regional demand and distribution notes
points: South and West India distributor experience with cash-and-carry schemes is improving, with gradual introduction of such schemes in these regions.
South India identified as an attractive growth region with plans for a larger plant to cover the whole country once operational.

subsections.label: Kisan Mouldings merger
points: Company has already filed the scheme for merging Kisan Mouldings into Apollo Pipes at some point.

Synergies already achieved include one source of raw material and one source of managing finance and technology; however, Kisan will retain its own sales team and admin cost at the plant level as a separate brand.
Once fully integrated, cost synergies of approximately 1% at the overall company level are expected.
Plan for South India plant, including land acquisition, expected to be finalized within the next six months.

key_figures.label: Time frame expected for government fund disbursement pickup (Nal Se Jal)
Months into new financial year (Nal Se Jal disbursement)

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Geopolitical situation continues to disrupt global supply chain, contributing to a soft start to FY27.
High volatility in PVC resin prices in Q1 FY27, with prices falling by Rs.32/Kg in April, slightly in May, and by Rs.5/Kg again in June.
Extreme 30% price drop in first 20 days of April hurt both primary and secondary demand.
Monsoon impacting construction industry performance in near term (next 15-20 days of peak monsoon expected to soften demand further before recovery).
Recent PVC resin availability issues attributed to extensive rains at ports delaying de-stuffing of ships, not to structural supply shortage.

Government CAPEX/Nal Se Jal fund disbursement has seen some budget encouragement but no actual pickup yet; new budget allocations, disbursement of funds, new tenders and contractors is a long-driven process expected to take time - four months into FY27 with nothing concrete yet, though pickup hoped for in next 3-4 months.

Competitive intensity remains high, with smaller players facing disruption from PVC price volatility due to weaker balance sheets and margin spread, unable to absorb inventory write-downs as well as Apollo.

Kisan Mouldings historically had operating losses over the last three quarters, reflecting a weak plant, weak brand and lack of macro industry support over the last 12 months; P&L optics distorted by inventory losses despite reasonable business-level EBITDA margin.
MIP was applied ~12 days back at $766/MT (~Rs.82/Kg), acting as a price floor for PVC resin.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Second half of FY27 expected to be much better than first half as monsoon impact eases and construction industry performs better.
Q2 FY27 to be better than Q1 FY27 on a QoQ basis, and will show double-digit growth on a YoY basis.

Company continues to maintain high double-digit volume growth guidance for FY27 and coming years, supported by Varanasi plant ramp-up, continuous ramp-up of Maharashtra plant (Kisan), and new products like Window profile starting to contribute to top line, fueling growth into FY28 and FY29.
Margins guided at 7-8% EBITDA at business level for next 12-15 months; once plants stabilize and operating leverage benefits kick in, margins expected to inch up.
PVC prices expected to remain stable in the near future given the MIP price floor of Rs.82/Kg.
Long-term revenue target of Rs.800-1,000 crores per plant across 4 plants by FY31, plus an allied products portfolio revenue target of Rs.1,000 crores within the next 4 years.

guidance_ledger.statement: Apollo Pipes Q1 FY27 total sales volume was flat YoY.
It will be double-digit growth on YoY basis in Q2.
We are confident of high double-digit volume growth for next coming years, including FY27... we continue to maintain our high double-digit volume growth in the coming years.

At the business level, we believe that 7% to 8% EBITDA margin for the next 12 to 15-months is what we are going to achieve. Once the plants stabilize and we start getting the operating leverage benefits, then margins will start inching up.
There is always a room to improve our margins by 50 bps to 100 bps... as Varanasi plant and Window profile plant stabilize, margins will further inch up by 50-to-100 bps.
We expect that business to contribute 7% to 8% to our revenue in FY27, and gradually, it will keep on improving and maybe it will settle at around 10% as per the current capacity.
Once the current capacity gets consumed, then we will expand more capacity and the business has potential to be like 15% to the overall Apollo Pipes portfolio.
Our long-term target by FY31 is to have four large plants across India, each plant contributing Rs.800 crores to Rs.1,000 crore of revenue with 10% plus EBITDA margin from the PVC pipes business.
That portfolio in the next four years should be generating Rs.1,000 crores revenue... that is our long-term five-year goal for Apollo Pipes as a business in the plumbing and bath fitting segment.

Next leg of CAPEX requires Rs.600-700 crores put together in five years... I think 70%-80% will be met from our internal cash flows... we are 100% sure that the ongoing CAPEX will be funded from internal cash flow.
The margin profile is 10%-15%... whatever new product addition takes place, it should be like double-digit margin, and more than that, the focus is that it should generate 25% ROC.

CPVC has grown in Quarter 1 on a YoY basis despite the flattish growth for the company at a consolidated level... the CPVC portfolio growth is going to be the one major contributor [to high double-digit growth].
In both the years, the total CAPEX will be near about Rs.200 crores divided by like Rs.100 crores in each year. This will be funded from operating cash flow.

We will have a net working capital day target of 30, which right now is 45, but we are confident that there is scope of release of working capital by 10-to-15 days eventually, if not this year, but definitely by next year.
Idea is to bring debtor days to maybe 25-days, maybe by FY27-end or maybe in first half of FY28, but there is a clear visibility.

key_takeaways: Apollo Pipes Q1 FY27 total sales volume was flat YoY.

quarters.summary: Apollo Pipes reported a challenging FY26 with consol EBITDA down 30% due to inventory write-downs, aggressive pricing and new-vertical fixed costs, but management is bullish on FY27 and beyond, targeting INR400 crore+ revenue in Q1 FY27, gradual margin recovery, and a 5-year plan for 35% revenue CAGR to reach INR5,000 crores revenue by FY31, backed by capacity expansion (existing 3 plants to INR1,000 crore each, new South India plant, allied products vertical) and Group Chairman Sanjay Gupta joining the Board.

subsections.label: PVC price volatility
points: FY26 was a roller coaster year for PVC prices: dropped 15% in first 8 months, rallied 75% in next 4 months, then fell 25% in 2 months to settle at INR84/kg current price.

subsections.label: EBITDA decline drivers
points: Consol EBITDA declined 30% for the full year due to inventory write-downs, aggressive pricing strategy, and fixed expenses for new business verticals.

subsections.label: Gross margin deterioration reasons (Q4)
points: Despite 13-14% increase in realization, gross margin deteriorated QoQ and YoY due to: (1) continued aggressive pricing strategy despite NSR/PVC price increases to maintain dealer confidence and catch up on volume growth momentum, promising benefit in Q1; (2) costs associated with building up the window profile business including sampling at showrooms; (3) write-downs from selling off unsold/dead finished goods inventory to clear space for volume ramp-up.
Inventory gains on raw material were minuscule this quarter since company was clearing inventory rather than building it.

subsections.label: Other expenses increase (standalone)
points: Increase in other expenses in Q4 standalone was mainly related to start-up expenses for the window profile business.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory by entity
points: Apollo standalone EBITDA has been in range of INR8,000-10,000/ton regularly; volume increase will bring operating leverage benefits, gradually improving spreads to INR8,500-9,000/ton.

Kisan is currently barely breaking even due to highly underutilized plants; sales initially coming at lower MSRs; expected to take 1-2 quarters to show significant margin improvement, pulling out of the -1% to -2% EBITDA margin seen in last 4 quarters.

Kisan margin disappointment in Q4 attributed to weak Jan-Feb demand recovering only towards end of Feb/March, leading to push/aggressive sales in first two months that hurt margins; operating leverage benefits expected from Q1 as plant ramp-up continues.

subsections.label: Working capital
points: FY26 working capital cycle increased by ~10 days to 45 days from 35 days in FY25, mainly driven by inventory days rising from 70 to 80 days.
As plants ramp up and PVC price settles, inventory days expected to fall by 5-10 days during FY27.
Channel financing program is progressing smoothly.
FY27 exit target is below 35 days (internal target 30 days as of March 2027), at minimum touching the FY25 level.

subsections.label: Capex plans
points: FY26 capex was INR150 crores.
FY27 capex guidance of ~INR100 crores includes ensuring Kisan plant capacity to reach INR1,000 crore revenue potential plus brownfield expansions at existing plants.

Kisan Mouldings: ~INR30-40 crores capex already incurred to take revenue to ~INR500 crore; additional INR50-60 crores planned for brownfield expansion to build capacity toward INR1,000 crore revenue with 10-12% EBITDA margin target.

key_figures.value: some impact from heavy March-end inventory

subsections.label: Demand scenario
points: Demand trends viewed as encouraging; industry sitting at a low base after 2 slow years in construction/government infra demand, giving strong headroom for sales growth.
Company has been very aggressive in last 4-5 months, reflected in Q4 FY26 volume and revenue results; wants to carry this momentum into Q1 FY27, a normally strong quarter.
Amitabh Bachchan renewed as brand ambassador to help push brand with dealer network, channel partners, plumbers and consumers.

subsections.label: Channel inventory dynamics
points: Channel inventory got heavy towards end of March due to price movements, impacting April volumes to some extent; INR400 crore Q1 revenue target already factors in April weakness.
Expectation that after strong March, April would be light but May-June would pick up; company already seeing inventory filling up in channel.
Channel running at very low stock currently; not a big challenge as channel remains cautious on prices; some slight inventory build seen with price increases but not significantly higher.
Post-March destocking, channel inventory considered normal or below normal.

subsections.label: Demand by segment
points: Demand from agri is good, being the main season for water pipes.
Construction plumbing demand in both rural and urban regions is good; rural has been outperforming urban in the last 2-3 months.
Projects that spilled over into Q4 are seeing contractors rushing to close them, supporting demand.
Government infra demand remains low despite promises of payment releases and capex kickstart; nothing significant seen on ground yet.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 volume/revenue guidance basis
points: Q4 revenue was ~INR350 crores; targeting INR400 crores for Q1 FY27, roughly 15% QoQ jump.
Q4 NSR was INR110/kg with expectation of minimal change (INR2-4 here and there), implying double-digit volume growth for Q1.

Confidence in volume growth stems from core existing products, dealer network, addition of new dealers from group, and aggressive pricing adopted 4-5 months ago now playing out — not from any infra pickup.

subsections.label: Import dynamics ahead of duty change
points: High imports from China expected in the next 15-30 days ahead of duty exemption ending, but channel likely cautious given past losses from higher imports/inventories.
Monsoon season post July 1/August expected to pressure demand in Q2, limiting scale of import stocking.

subsections.label: Product/segment mix
points: Sales split: plumbing construction ~60-65% of total pie; agri and government infra ~35%.

Within construction plumbing: CPVC growing 10-12%, water tank growing 20-30%, window profile business ramping up (small Q4 contribution but expected 4-5% contribution to construction plumbing revenue this year), and base UPVC pipes and fittings demand uptick also expected to drive FY27 volume growth.

subsections.label: Kisan Mouldings strategy
points: Kisan plant currently capable of generating INR400-500 crore revenue; closed FY26 at ~INR200-250 crore.

Strategy: first take Kisan to ~INR500 crore (INR30-40 crore capex already incurred), then build capacity to INR1,000 crore via brownfield expansion (additional INR50-60 crore capex) targeting minimum 10-12% EBITDA margin.
Management intends to eventually merge Kisan Mouldings into Apollo Pipes Limited; already working on the process, with timelines to be shared in future investor calls.

subsections.label: CPVC / Lubrizol tie-up
points: CPVC grew 10% in FY26; with Lubrizol tie-up and support, expecting more than 20% growth in FY27 within the CPVC segment.

subsections.label: Window/door profile business
points: Window profiles sold on a per-length basis, not per-kg basis.
Volume from window profile business is included in overall segment volume; contributing ~1.5% to total sales currently.
Currently present in North India and South India geographies.

subsections.label: Market share strategy
points: Current market share ~2-2.5% on an industry size of ~INR55,000 crore (also cited as INR50,000-60,000 crore); targeting 3-3.5% market share in next 3-4 years assuming 7-8% industry growth.
Market share gains expected to come at the expense of smaller/weaker unorganized players amid ongoing sector formalization and rising brand/channel awareness among consumers.

subsections.label: SKU expansion
points: Company references its SKU range within the piping segment (including new products) as part of the strategy to sustain growth alongside distribution network, brand support and dealer network.

subsections.label: Existing plant network
points: 3 plants currently: main North India plant, West India plant, and new Varanasi plant. All three targeted to reach INR1,000 crores revenue each in the next 5 years.
Varanasi plant is now fully operational; this year's focus is to ramp it up and gain confidence/conviction before starting work on the South India plant.

subsections.label: South India plant plan
points: Company already has a plant in the Bangalore region (Tumkur); new base likely to be set up near that area (Malur, Tumkur, Bangalore belt).

Land acquisition work expected to start after 1 year; based on past project execution experience, plant can go live ~18 months after land is finalized, implying South India plant likely towards FY28 end.

subsections.label: Allied products vertical
points: Plan to build a fourth INR1,000 crore revenue stream from allied products such as windows and bath fittings, alongside the piping business plants.

subsections.label: Distributor strategy
points: Net-net distributor addition will be modest (4-5%) as company seeks a strong set of distributors who can match its 35% annual growth commitment.
Plan involves clean-up of smaller/weaker dealers, attaching them to larger ones, mirroring the strategy used in Apollo Steel Pipes; some additions expected from group network.
More relevant distributor addition numbers to be shared after ~2 quarters.

subsections.label: Regional demand
points: Rural markets are all agri-driven, doing well due to main water-pipe season; urban and rural construction plumbing demand both good, with rural outperforming urban in last 2-3 months.

subsections.label: Window profile geography
points: Window and door profile business currently present in North India and South India.

subsections.label: Channel financing
points: Channel financing program is undergoing smoothly, supporting working capital management.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Competitive intensity has increased significantly in last 3-4 years; top players reduced pricing and entered a price war fighting for share, pressuring industry margins.

At the same time, clean-up at the bottom level of unorganized/high-cost, zero-brand-value players is occurring as they cannot sustain against aggressive organized-player pricing, leading to capacity shutdowns.
Ashirvad Pipes' promoter reportedly planning a large new pipe plant in FY27, expected to keep competitive intensity elevated over the medium term.
After 2-3 years of flattish industry volume growth, low base could enable growth of 7-8%, creating INR4,000-5,000 crore of new market for every incremental growth step.

subsections.label: Group synergies
points: Leveraging group network under new Chairman Sanjay Gupta's guidance; large dealers within the group have already started taking up PVC pipe dealerships.
Group synergies identified over the last 4-5 years are now being worked on closely for business benefit.

subsections.label: Board changes
points: Group Chairman Mr. Sanjay Gupta has joined the Board to support the company's 5-year growth vision.

subsections.label: Kisan Mouldings merger plan
points: Management confirmed intent to ultimately merge Kisan Mouldings into Apollo Pipes Limited; already working on execution approach, with timeline details expected in future investor calls.

subsections.label: 5-year growth plan
points: Drawn a 5-year growth plan to achieve 35% revenue CAGR and hit INR5,000 crores revenue by FY31.
Plan involves 3 existing plants each capable of INR1,000 crore revenue, a new South India plant for another INR1,000 crore, and INR1,000 crore from allied products such as windows and bath fittings.

subsections.label: Demand slowdown
points: Demand remained impacted throughout FY26 due to slowdown in both the private real estate sector and government infrastructure spending.

subsections.label: PVC price uncertainty
points: Impact of crude price rise (due to geopolitical conflict) on PVC prices is uncertain; management cannot give clear guidance on pricing but expects prices to remain under pressure for the next few months and is not bullish on prices.
Prices expected to remain stable within a plus/minus 5% range in the near term, with limited scope for large moves either way.

subsections.label: Import duty risk
points: Import duty exemption ends 30th June 2026, after which 8.25% duty will hit import costs again; high imports expected in the 15-30 days before the exemption ends.
Post duty reinstatement and monsoon season (post July 1/August), demand pressure is expected in Q2, limiting import stocking impact.

subsections.label: Government infra demand weakness
points: Government infra demand remains low despite promises of payment releases and capex kickstart; nothing significant observed on ground yet.

subsections.label: Kisan Mouldings underutilization
points: Kisan plants are highly underutilized, contributing to weak margins (-1% to -2% EBITDA margin over last 4 quarters); ramp-up needed to reach breakeven and beyond.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Management is bullish on FY27 and beyond, aiming to carry current momentum over the next 4-5 years.
5-year plan targets 35% revenue CAGR to reach INR5,000 crores revenue by FY31, supported by ramp-up of existing plants, a new South India plant, and allied products vertical.
Apollo standalone margins expected to gradually improve from INR8,000/ton towards INR8,500-9,000/ton with volume-driven operating leverage.
Kisan margins expected to improve from near-breakeven, taking 1-2 quarters to show significant improvement, moving toward INR5,000-6,000/ton and eventually INR10,000/ton as scale increases.
Consol EBITDA per ton expected to progress from INR6,000-8,000/ton currently towards INR10,000-12,000/ton over the next 2-3 years.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 43% YoY / 25% QoQ to INR1,671mn with EBITDA up 86% YoY / 15% QoQ to INR323mn, led by broad-based growth across PTC, PASC, and SDA segments. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 25-30% and EBITDA margin guidance of 20-22%, approved a new INR200 crore greenfield multipurpose facility (groundbreaking 20 July 2026) targeting ~INR300 crore peak revenue, and flagged Electrolyte Salts guidance of INR40-60 crore for FY27 despite a Middle East crisis-driven raw material shortage that delayed production in Q1.

subsections.label: Margin commentary
points: Management noted the company has lost one quarter with a little lesser margin but still sticks to 20-22% EBITDA margin guidance for the year.

Price pass-through of raw material cost increases had not been thorough previously, which visibly impacted margins; price increase acceptance from customers has begun in the last 40-50 days as global raw material prices rose.

subsections.label: ROIC framework
points: As the company shifted from high asset-turn chemistries (PTC, SDA, Electrolyte Salts, asset turn ~1:3) into multistage chemistries (pharma/agro intermediates), asset turn ratio has moderated to around 1.5.
Management targets ROIC of about 20-22% as a decent achievement despite the changing asset turn profile.
New greenfield facility investment of INR200 crores is expected to generate an asset turnover of 1.2x-1.5x.

key_figures.label: Pharma & Agro Intermediates and Specialty Chemicals (PASC) revenue
Electrolyte Salts revenue this quarter (as referenced in Q&A)
Expected pharma molecules revenue (3 new molecules, FY27)

subsections.label: Phase Transfer Catalysts (PTC)
points: PTC continues to be one of the strongest pillars of the portfolio; acceptability of PTC chemistry is expanding across the chemical value chain as industries focus on process efficiency, product selectivity, and sustainable manufacturing.
PTC is increasingly viewed as a process-enabling technology improving manufacturing economics and supporting greener chemistry, not merely as a catalyst.

Company has forward-integrated PTC into SDA and Electrolyte Salts & Solutions; as SDA/Electrolyte demand rises, more PTC will be internally consumed and less sold externally, though the company will continue producing/selling PTC to loyal, long-term customers to its best capability.

subsections.label: Pharma, Agro and Specialty Chemicals (PASC)
points: PASC delivered one of its most encouraging quarters strategically; molecules commercialized in recent quarters are seeing increasing customer acceptance, resulting in repeat orders and demand improvement.
Transition from initial commercialization to recurring procurement validates product quality and customer confidence.

Commercial production of one pharma intermediate commenced in Q1 itself; demand expected to strengthen progressively through the year, with additional pharma molecules expected to move towards commercialization in H2.
Several R&D-ready molecules within this segment are entering pilot-scale manufacturing, while development activities for others are underway.
Glymes (e.g., MONOGLYME) are sold mainly into the pharma industry, not lithium-ion batteries; company has very limited exposure to battery manufacturers via glymes.

subsections.label: Structure Directing Agents (SDA)
points: SDA outlook continues to strengthen; Euro 7 standards implementation has begun translating into revenue with visible customer demand validating the anticipated opportunity.
Gradual geographical implementation of Euro 7 expected to position the segment for strong demand.
China SDA demand has shifted toward EVs for passenger vehicles, but real SDA demand comes from large diesel engines; Chinese demand for diesel trucks/engines is yet to pick up meaningfully.

Rest of world (outside China) demand is growing rapidly; as Euro 7 shifts geographically (eventually to US, Japan, China, India over next 3-5 years), it removes the geographical limitations that existed under Euro 6, expected to translate into stronger demand and growing market share for Tatva.

subsections.label: Electrolyte Salts
points: Business continues to make steady progress toward larger commercial scale; demand for electrolytes in energy storage devices is rapidly increasing, broadly in line with expectations.

Severe short supply of certain key raw materials due to the Middle East crisis led to significant production delays, impacting revenue recognition for the quarter; the situation is now gradually streamlining in terms of availability.

Progress with hybrid battery customer is advancing well, steadily moving towards commercial supply; hybrid battery customer's commercialization is expected to begin around October/November calendar 2026, with full-scale commercialization expected in late 2027 as the customer stabilizes their new battery manufacturing plant.
Company does not sell into lithium-ion batteries; its electrolyte solutions are for zinc battery and supercapacitor battery applications, and other types of batteries (not lithium).
Major part of current Electrolyte Salts demand is coming from a couple of customers using electrolytes in stationary energy storage systems.

No formal order book held for this segment; it operates on a quarter-on-quarter basis; a couple of months of productivity were lost due to war-related raw material unavailability, though infrastructure and customer demand visibility remain clear otherwise.

subsections.label: Semiconductor chemicals
points: First batch produced on commercial plant scale was delivered to the customer this quarter and successfully qualified by the customer — considered one of the company's biggest achievements of the past decade.

Achievement validates research capabilities, manufacturing excellence, quality systems, and ability to meet global semiconductor industry standards; opens door to potentially significant larger opportunities as additional products progress through customer qualification.

Product qualified is used as a key starting raw material for semiconductor manufacture — the most stringent of 3 possible specifications (the other two being an etching agent for PCBs and a cleaning agent for circuits).
End customer for qualification is an MNC intermediary supplier, not the semiconductor/fab manufacturer directly.

At least 3-4 more plant-scale trials expected over the next 2 years as the customer tests consistency of quality and other parameters before commercialization talks begin; commercialization process in semiconductor industry is rigorous and will take patience.
Currently 5 products in the semiconductor pipeline: one produced at plant scale (delivered/qualified), one produced at pilot scale (under customer evaluation), and 3 others in development phase.
Major commercialization not foreseen before Q4 2028 given the lengthy qualification process.

subsections.label: Product pipeline (mature, excluding semiconductor)
points: About 8-9 different mature products (excluding semiconductor products, which are long-term) are expected to commercialize before 2028.
About 7-8 products are seen moving into commercial or piloting phase in the near future, most involving electrochemistry or continuous flow chemistry.
2 commercial molecules currently use continuous flow chemistry.

subsections.label: MONOGLYME/flame retardant product updates
points: Company installed equipment to produce MONOGLYME via continuous flow chemistry, targeting ~2,000 tons capacity, but converted this equipment to produce raw material for a different product (electrolyte for supercapacitor batteries) after a sharp China-driven price drop (from $4.6-4.8 to $2.1 within 30 days); prices have since recovered to $3-3.5 but company remains cautious on scaling MONOGLYME, producing only a few hundred tons via conventional chemistry.
Flame retardant product (linked to the polymer industry) remains uncommercialized; economics have not improved, and no commercialization is expected in the near future.

subsections.label: Continuous flow / batch chemistry transition
points: Transitioning products from conventional/batch to continuous flow chemistry improves productivity, reduces cost, and can reduce number of chemistry stages (e.g., a 2-stage product done in a single stage), freeing reactor capacity for larger revenue from existing infrastructure.

New reactor capacity (from debottlenecking and new facility) will be consumed by both existing products (converted from conventional to continuous flow) and new products; no current plans for contract manufacturing given sufficient organic growth opportunity, though informal customer commitments exist for new capacity.

subsections.label: New greenfield facility (Jolva)
points: Board of Directors approved establishment of a new greenfield manufacturing facility involving an investment of approximately INR200 crores; groundbreaking ceremony scheduled for 20 July 2026.

Facility is designed as a future-ready, multipurpose, multiproduct platform fungible across sectors (not dedicated to Pharma & Agrochem Intermediates, Electrolyte, or SDA specifically) — will support commercialization of new products, provide operational flexibility, and create capacity for the next growth phase.
Facility built to scale up R&D-ready products developed over recent years and to meet growing domestic demand as the Indian economy develops.

Rationale: new pharma and agro product introductions over the last 2-3 years are causing capacity constraints at existing sites; new molecules in the pipeline will need this infrastructure by the time Dahej facilities near saturation.
Company philosophy is to build capabilities ahead of demand; this project reflects that philosophy.
Peak revenue potential from new facility estimated at INR300 crores; theoretical commercialization timeline is 21 months, with internal push targeting 18 months.

subsections.label: Dahej facility saturation
points: Dahej facility has consumed nearly all available land parcels and is nearing space saturation; only a very small production block (4-6 reactors) is feasible via debottlenecking, insufficient to address incoming growth.

Beyond INR800-850 crore revenue, the company expects to get stagnated without new infrastructure; management foresees this constraint arising from next year itself, driving urgency on the new greenfield project.
Current capacity peak revenue potential is INR900 crores.
Major future growth must come from the new site (Jolva), not Dahej.

subsections.label: Semiconductor business capex
points: No capex currently being undertaken specifically for the semiconductor business, as major commercialization is not foreseen before Q4 2028; the semiconductor opportunity is treated as over-and-above current capacity plans.

subsections.label: China anti-involution / subsidy policy
points: Reports (not yet law) suggest China may remove VAT/subsidies for specialty chemicals, agro intermediates, and pharma intermediates industries, potentially effective from January of next year; heard from both customers and suppliers.
If implemented, companies like Tatva Chintan could see some benefit within the chemical space, but it is too early to predict, and management is not speculating on the outcome.

subsections.label: Competitive moat on continuous flow chemistry
points: Management does not view continuous flow chemistry capability as an unreplicable moat; competitors could develop similar capability with dedication, focus, and sustained investment, though it takes time versus the faster/easier conventional chemistry route.
Company positions itself as among the smallest players within its chemical segment relative to peers.

subsections.label: Raw material availability
points: Severe short supply of certain key raw materials for Electrolyte Salts due to the Middle East crisis (war situation) led to significant production delays, impacting Q1 revenue recognition; a couple of months of productivity were lost; situation is gradually streamlining in terms of raw material availability.

subsections.label: Pricing pass-through lag
points: Price increases from raw material suppliers were rampant and came at short notice, and the company had not been thorough in passing these costs on to customers, which affected margins; price pass-through to customers has only begun in the last 40-50 days as customers start accepting higher prices given no alternative globally.

subsections.label: China pricing volatility
points: A sharp China-driven price crash in MONOGLYME (from $4.6-4.8 to $2.1 within 30 days) caused the company to withhold planned capacity investment in glymes; prices have partially recovered to $3-3.5 but company remains cautious.

subsections.label: Flame retardant economics
points: Flame retardant product economics remain unfavorable, tied to the polymer industry, with no near-term reversal expected; commercialization not planned in the near future.

subsections.label: Semiconductor qualification timeline risk
points: Semiconductor industry qualification and validation processes are rigorous and slow; management does not expect major commercialization before Q4 2028, and cautions it will not be an easy or overnight process to acquire business in this sector.

subsections.label: China SDA demand
points: China SDA/diesel truck demand has been slow to pick up as passenger vehicle demand shifts to EVs, though the real SDA demand driver (large diesel engines) is seeing a slow uptick.

subsections.label: Analyst-raised execution risk (addressed)
points: When asked about the biggest execution risk to achieving FY27 guidance (customer demand, raw material volatility, or new product commercialization), management stated it foresees no obstacles to this year's guidance, as demand from customers and segments is quite visible.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin outlook
points: Management reiterated 25-30% growth forecast for FY27 and confirmed intention to maintain Q1's run rate for the rest of the year.
EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20-22% despite the lower-margin quarter caused by lost Electrolyte Salts volume.

subsections.label: Electrolyte Salts trajectory
points: Guidance of INR40-60 crores annual revenue (down from a prior implied higher range in commentary) reiterated; sufficient capacity already in place to meet this demand without additional investment; demand visibility from customers is described as crystal clear.
No formal order book exists for this business; it is managed on a quarter-to-quarter basis.

subsections.label: Pharma molecule ramp-up
points: 3 new pharma molecules expected to contribute INR70-80 crores revenue in FY27, gradually ticking up in the following financial year, with a full-utilization potential of around INR200 crores.

subsections.label: Long-term growth CAGR
points: Over the next 3-4 years (factoring in Jolva's commercialization), management envisages at least 20-25% compounded revenue growth year-on-year.

subsections.label: ROIC target
points: Company targets a post-tax ROIC of around 20-22% as a decent achievement, acknowledging a shift in asset turnover profile as the product mix moves toward multistage pharma/agro intermediate chemistries.

key_takeaways: For Q1 FY27, Tatva Chintan reported operating revenue of INR1,671 million, reflecting a 43% year-on-year growth and 25% sequential increase. EBITDA stood at INR323 million, representing a 86% growth Y-on-Y and 15% improvement over the previous quarter.
Phase Transfer Catalysts contributed INR428 million in revenue, a 38% growth quarter-on-quarter and 47% increase year-on-year.
Electrolyte Salts achieved INR63 million in revenue, recording a down 52% sequentially and a growth of 76% Y-o-Y.
Pharma & Agro Intermediates and Specialty Chemicals delivered INR584 million in revenue, 63% growth quarter-on-quarter and a growth of 25% Y-o-Y.
Structure Directing Agents reported INR578 million in revenue, reflecting a 10% growth quarter-on-quarter and a 47% increase year-on-year.

In line with the growing opportunities across our business, I'm pleased to share that our Board of Directors has today approved the establishment of a new greenfield manufacturing facility involving an investment of approximately INR200 crores. We have scheduled the groundbreaking ceremony for this on 20th July 2026.

Coming to Semiconductor. I'm extremely proud to share that our first batch produced on commercial plant scale was delivered to the customer during this quarter, and this batch has been successfully qualified by the customer. We consider this to be one of the Tatva Chintan's glaring achievements of the past decade.
This year marks 30 years of Tatva Chintan, and this milestone belongs to every stakeholder who has been a part of our journey.

Can you also let us know what is the total addressable market for market opportunity for us in this particular sale [semiconductor]?
