quarters.summary: Management guided to ~25% revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin for FY27, citing convergence of multiple growth initiatives (Electrolyte Salts ramp-up, PASC/Pharma commercialization, SDA Euro 7 tailwind, semiconductor chemicals validation) despite geopolitical/raw-material cost headwinds; the Dahej new production block is fully operational and Jolva greenfield project groundbreaking is expected within this quarter, with commercial production targeted for early CY2028.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Q4 FY26 EBITDA growth was primarily supported by better product mix and improved operating leverage.

Improved efficiency of plant output and rising occupancy is absorbing some raw-material cost variables, helping maintain EBITDA margin guidance of 20-22% despite Iran-related raw material price increases and higher fuel costs.

subsections.label: Tax rate explanation
points: Quarterly tax rate was exceptionally high at 38% due to unavailability of 10AA benefits this year on account of carryforward losses on an income-tax basis, combined with heavy capex (~INR100 crores) increasing deferred tax.
Annual effective tax rate for FY26 was ~26%.
Going forward, as depreciation between books and income tax synchronizes more with continued asset use, effective tax rates are expected to come down.
Company continues to enjoy tax holiday benefits at the Dahej facility.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / Dividend
points: Company retains ~90% of net profit earnings, distributing ~10% of profit as dividend.
Management views the dividend payout as fair to stakeholders who have kept faith in the company, while plowing back the majority of earnings into the business.

An investor questioned the rationale of paying dividends while short-term borrowings/loans have increased, noting an equitability concern regarding interest cost hitting the P&L; management maintained its retention/payout policy as a management decision.

subsections.label: Overall demand environment
points: Over the last couple of quarters, gradual pickup in momentum in business activity across segments.
Order flows are becoming relatively more stable with a consistent gradual uptick in demand.
Customer interactions are increasingly moving beyond short-term procurement towards broader business discussions and future requirements.

Overall environment across key end-use segments has improved significantly compared to the last couple of years, helping better planning, improved continuity in business discussions, and more structured commercial engagement across all segments.

key_figures.label: Pharma, Agro Intermediates and Specialty Chemicals (PASC) revenue

subsections.label: Phase Transfer Catalysts (PTC)
points: PTC continues to deliver steady organic growth in line with historical trends.
Industries across the chemical sector are increasingly recognizing the process and efficiency advantages offered by PTC chemistry in various applications, supporting long-term organic growth.

subsections.label: Structure Directing Agents (SDA)
points: Demand is consistently growing as the industry approaches the 2027 implementation of stricter emission norms via Euro 7.
First implementation of Euro 7 norms begins with Europe, followed gradually by other geographies.
Improved customer engagement across key geographies with business discussions becoming more structured.
Management expects to grow SDA revenue by at least 20% in FY27, targeting INR250-300 crores.
Orders for Euro 7 applications are gradually increasing month-on-month; uptick in numbers expected around July-August as the switch from Euro 6 to Euro 7 occurs.

SDA is a duopoly market (Tatva vs. Sarchem/US manufacturer); it is not price-sensitive — once a product is approved for a specific vehicle variant, there is no scope for replacement during that variant's life.
Tatva was a late entrant in Euro 6 timing but is well-positioned early for Euro 7, expecting market share to gradually rise given a pricing advantage versus the US manufacturer.
Customers deliberately maintain a balance between the two suppliers to keep both engaged — maximum volume share to any one customer is capped around 70%.
With Euro 7, Tatva expects to match Sarchem's share pattern in most (85-90%) of new opportunity cases.

SDA business risk is not around price fluctuation risk (raw material cost pass-through mechanisms exist based on precise annual forecasts) but around demand volatility, as seen in the post-COVID inventory pile-up and subsequent demand crash over the past two years; demand has now normalized with regular orders being placed.

subsections.label: Electrolyte Salts and Solutions (ESS)
points: ESS segment continued to scale gradually, supported by increasing consumption in energy storage applications.
The customer utilizing electrolytes for energy storage devices has shown a steady ramp-up in volumes, expected to strongly strengthen during the current year.
Work with a customer engaged in hybrid battery application is progressing well; commercial business for this application is expected to begin in Q3 of the current year.
Segment is steadily strengthening its strategic relevance within the overall portfolio and will be a relevant contributor to overall revenue this year (8-10% of FY27 revenue).
Q4 FY26 growth is currently from only one application; second application (hybrid battery) will go online around November-December of the current calendar year.
On a yearly basis, ESS revenue is projected to be about 4x the current quarter's revenue.
Hybrid battery ramp-up will be gradual, reaching full scale by 2028 when the actual vehicle launch occurs (mid-2028); ramp-up acceleration expected late CY27 or early CY28.

subsections.label: Pharma, Agro and Specialty Chemicals (PASC)
points: Commercial traction has improved meaningfully; Agro intermediates commercialized earlier are witnessing sustained demand and are expected to see healthy offtake during the year.

On the pharma side, all product validations are successfully completed; commercialization begins from the current year — one product commercializing in Q1, and two others from Q3, produced/delivered on a campaign basis.

Q4 FY26 sequential decline was not due to lack of orders but due to production streamlining challenges after starting trial production from the new facility in January and commercializing in February; issues have now been overcome and production is moving smoothly.
Good order visibility till end of the current calendar year, expected to continue into the next year as well.

Both agrochemical products (photochlorination and the larger product) are seeing production ramp-up; challenges with photochlorination product have also been gradually resolved and dispatch has become consistent.

Pharma segment revenue estimate of INR70-75 crores in FY27, a completely new add-on to existing business (previous pharma revenue was negligible, coming only from validation trials); dispatches for the first product have already begun.

Management does not see agrochemical volume demand concerns (reported industry-wide) impacting Tatva's specific products, given insignificant volume relative to total demand; confident in demand visibility for both current year (CY26) and next year (CY27), including for Pharma products.
PASC has definitive chances of becoming much larger than SDA once the Jolva plant becomes operational.

subsections.label: Semiconductor Chemicals
points: Plant-scale trials for the first product have been completed successfully; dispatch to happen in the current quarter — a significant milestone and confidence booster for the team.
Marks an important step in the company's long-term semiconductor roadmap; scale-up will remain gradual.
Complex chemistry requiring multiple validation cycles; final commercialization expected around 2028-2029.

Supply chain: intermediaries (large MNC integrator companies supplying fab companies) are involved — Tatva's chemicals undergo qualification first at the integrator level, then at the end customer level; supply likely routed through Japanese/South Korean MNCs before reaching Taiwan-based fabs.

Entry barrier considered even more difficult than SDA; company has been working in this segment for ~8-9 years and is now seeing first-line commercialization (validation stage, not full commercialization).
Purity levels achieved: 99.99%; impurity profiles below 1 part per billion (1,000 parts per trillion range).
Chemicals to be used in bleaching or cleaning processes in chip manufacturing.

subsections.label: Dahej new production block
points: The new production block at Dahej site is now fully operational on commercial scale.
Continued work on process optimization and strengthening manufacturing readiness for upcoming opportunities.
Facility can scale up to revenue of INR850-900 crores from existing facility, made possible only due to the new plant becoming operational.
Certain specific bottlenecks remain to be removed via minor capex infusion of INR10-12 crores per year.
Full potential revenue ramp-up expected not in the current financial year but in the next financial year (FY28).
Target margin of 25% (previously achieved historically) becomes realistic and achievable once the plant is fully operationalized.

subsections.label: Jolva Greenfield Project
points: Preparatory work has progressed further; groundbreaking expected to commence during the current quarter (within next 60 days from mid-May, i.e., mid-July).

During detailed engineering, design-stage feedback led to further trials that helped optimize the process and engineering requirements, reducing the number of reactors required at the plant — this caused a ~4-6 week delay but strengthens long-term scalability and operational efficiency.
Now in final designing stage; bids will be called from construction companies for civil construction.
Timeline: from groundbreaking (mid-July 2026), 18-20 months to commercial production, targeting January-March 2028.

This facility will be a key enabler for products with strong domestic demand and will significantly enhance manufacturing flexibility as the company moves towards commercialization over the next 18 months.
The Jolva project will go in multiple phases; Phase 1 revenue potential estimated at INR400-500 crores.

Will include a dedicated facility for a large new agro product (produced via an in-house developed, novel technology route with no known prior patent or process filed) plus a multi-purpose plant (MPP) with capacity for existing products.
Total capex for Jolva project (combined FY27+FY28): INR100 crores in FY27 and INR175 crores in FY28.

Jolva facility, once operational, is expected to bring the next phase of growth from FY28-29, including launch of 2 new Agro intermediates with significant revenue potential, successfully piloted using proprietary technology.

subsections.label: 30-year milestone and inflection point
points: FY26 marks the company completing 30 years of operation, a journey defined by committed innovations.
Company achieved revenue in excess of INR500 crores in the recently concluded financial year.
Management believes the company is at an inflection point where multiple initiatives across business segments are beginning to converge, reflecting early stages of a more structured growth cycle.

Foundation built on consistent investment in technical capability, innovative technology, customer-centric approach and disciplined execution; sustained efforts are gradually coming together across the business, setting the stage for a more integrated and scalable growth platform.
Continued emphasis planned on operational excellence, technology-led differentiation and long-term value creation for stakeholders.

subsections.label: Geopolitical conflict impact
points: Current ongoing geopolitical conflicts pose challenges, leading to rising cost of fuel and packing material.
Biggest challenge is the steep increase in prices of key raw materials of crude origin and related to ammonia.
Freight rates are also increasing.
Availability of raw materials has continued almost smoothly, except for some delays in certain cases.

Company worked closely with customers, and most major customers have shared the impact of rising costs; increased prices have been gradually implemented on new orders; all open orders for existing customers have been honored at existing rates.

Amines were nearly unavailable for 2-3 weeks immediately after the Iran issue started (around March), causing loss of production days; availability has since become smooth again, but prices have risen by ~30-40%.

Most customers have accepted the price pass-through; in certain cases customers are adamant about not allowing the raw material price change, which may have some adverse but limited impact on EBITDA — expected to be compensated by increased volumes/plant efficiency and occupancy gains.
Overall geopolitical uncertainty may not directly hit Tatva but could hit its customers, per management, prompting a conservative growth guidance stance of 20-25% rather than higher.

subsections.label: Agrochemical industry demand concerns
points: There is broader industry concern on agrochemical volumes; however, management does not see this concern reflected for Tatva's own products given the insignificant volume relative to total market demand.

subsections.label: SDA demand volatility (historical)
points: Past 2 years saw demand vanish due to massive post-COVID uptake followed by inventory pile-up and subsequent demand crash; this demand volatility (not price fluctuation) is characterized as the inherent risk in SDA business; demand is now normalizing with regular orders being placed.

subsections.label: FY27 guidance reiteration
points: Guidance already given in previous calls maintained: revenue growth of ~25% and EBITDA margin in the range of 20-22% on a realistic basis.
Despite geopolitical issues raising costs, management does not intend to change guidance, as price increases are gradually being absorbed by customers.

Even though ESS, PASC, and SDA individually could suggest stronger growth than 20-25%, management stays conservative at 20-25% given geopolitical uncertainties that could affect customers even if not directly impacting Tatva.
With multiple developments getting into commercial phase, momentum of growth is foreseen to continue for the next 2 years.
Once the Jolva greenfield project goes online, it will bring the next phase of growth from FY2028-29.

key_takeaways: Congratulate all the stakeholders on achieving revenue in excess of INR500 crores in recently concluded financial year.
This year also marks an important milestone as your company completed 30 years of operation, a journey defined by committed innovations.
Tatva Chintan is at an inflection point where multiple initiatives across our business segments are beginning to converge, reflecting the early stages of a more structured growth cycle.
Order flows are becoming relatively more stable. There is a consistent gradual uptick in demand.
The new production block at Dahej site is now fully operational on commercial scale.
With respect to the new greenfield project at Jolva, the preparatory work has progressed further, and we expect to commence the groundbreaking during this quarter.
The current ongoing geopolitical conflicts definitely pose challenges...the biggest challenge is the steep increase in the prices of key raw materials, which are crude origin and related to ammonia.
With multiple developments getting into commercial phase, we foresee the momentum of growth to continue for next 2 years.
We have already maintained that we will be growing the revenue by around 25% and EBITDA should be in the range of somewhere around 20% to 22% on a very realistic basis.

subsections.label: Adjustment basis for YoY comparisons
points: All YoY growth comparisons are based on Q1 FY26 adjusted performance, excluding INR25 crores arbitration award and INR10 crores arbitration claim settlement (recorded under other income, both pre-tax), and a one-time exceptional post-tax income of INR80 crores from unrealized mark-to-market gain on reclassification of investment (recorded below PBT).

subsections.label: Margin resilience despite input cost pressure
points: Consolidated EBITDA grew despite a spike in input cost due to geopolitical tensions; EBITDA margin remained stable at 21% reflecting disciplined cost management and operational efficiency focus.

Gear division margin did not grow despite revenue growth because gains were dragged by raw material price increases; EBIT margin was roughly flat versus last year's corresponding quarter (17.9% vs 18.8% full-year FY26).

subsections.label: MHE margin decline drivers
points: Three factors contributed to MHE margin decline: shift in sales mix, input cost increase, and overall revenue degrowth (lower throughput volume) — each contributing roughly 2.5-3 percentage points of the decline.

MHE Q1 FY26 was flagged previously as an exceptional margin quarter due to a couple of favorable orders; against full-year FY26 EBIT margin of 24.7%, current quarter EBIT margin of 25.6% is broadly in line with expectations.

subsections.label: Goodwill impairment (Benzler Radicon Europe, 2010-11 acquisition)
points: Goodwill of approximately INR102 crores in FY25 was impaired to nil in FY26 in the consolidated financial statements only; the impairment was purely a non-cash accounting charge with no tax impact.

A tax deduction of GBP1 million remains over 5 years in the UK entity via amortization of goodwill recorded as an asset in local books; a marginal goodwill book value remains in the UK entity to be amortized over the balance 3-4 years.

subsections.label: Working capital - defense orders
points: Defense orders with 2-3 year execution timelines carry higher working capital days versus standard gear orders (historically working capital increased by 15-20% compared to overall gear division for similar long-execution orders); higher margins on such orders are expected to absorb the cost of working capital interest.

subsections.label: Price pass-through strategy
points: Most orders accepted in Q1 include price increases; company has back-to-back strategic tie-ups with key raw material suppliers to lock raw material prices upon order acceptance.

Catalogue products (54% of gear revenue) are priced on a monthly-refreshed price list, diluting input cost impact; engineered products also benefit from raw material price locking, reducing impact versus MHE.
Blended BOM cost increase averages 5%, with specific steel grades up 5-7%, bearings up 6-7%, fabricated gear cases (outsourced) up 7%, and tooling up 6-10%.

subsections.label: Revenue recognition timing (Gear)
points: Gear finished goods worth INR70 crores were dispatched in Q1 FY27 but not revenue-recognized due to Ind AS cut-off/title transfer timing, while INR77 crores of Gear revenue was carried over from Q4 FY26 into Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Company maintains a strong balance sheet with net cash of approximately INR700 crores.
Capex program of ~INR400 crores over FY26-FY28 remains on track; further capex evaluation to seek board approval in the near future.

subsections.label: Order book quality and timing
points: Demand shown across key user industries; major contributors to order intake were power, steel, cement, and MHE.
Power sector contributed ~27% of total gear order intake via a large single order previously mentioned in the Q4 FY26 con-call.

Enquiry activity healthy; order inflows improving steadily across domestic and international markets; demand across key user industries continues to strengthen.
MHE division received an overseas order of ~INR21 crores from the port industry in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Revenue-to-order-book conversion mismatch
points: Significant raw material price increases have lengthened the time taken to convert enquiries into orders, causing high order book levels but slower revenue conversion in Q1 and expected in Q2.

Market currently in a 'correction' phase (Q1) transitioning to an 'acceptance' phase (Q2) regarding price increases; Q3 and Q4 expected to show more significant improvement as market accepts stabilized prices.

subsections.label: Gear division performance drivers
points: Growth underpinned by steady execution of order book and gradual improvement in international market.

Revenue growth partly reflects carry-over of INR77 crores from Q4 FY26 into Q1 FY27, plus a further INR70 crores of finished goods dispatched before June 30 but not revenue-recognized due to Ind AS cut-off/title transfer timing.
Bulk of orders received in the second half of May and in June, limiting conversion into quarter revenue despite a healthy order book.

India standalone gear business growth has been low single digits over recent quarters even as order book builds, driven by legacy events: US tariff actions from Q2 last year and the US-Iran event in Q4 impacted order pipeline; catalogue product (monthly price list) volumes also declined.
Gear order intake mix was 27% catalogue products and 73% engineered products in Q1 FY27, versus a revenue mix of 54% catalogue and 46% engineered.

subsections.label: MHE division performance drivers
points: Revenue moderation primarily due to project execution delays, specifically in two large power-sector orders where design engineering clearance from the end customer (via EPC main contractor) took longer than expected (originally expected in April).
Progress expected in Q2 with good revenue contribution from these delayed orders.
Underlying business momentum, healthy order book and improving order inflow provide strong visibility for coming quarters.

subsections.label: Naval/defense order margin context
points: A prior naval gearbox order carried a 1-2% margin impact due to learning curve and engineering effort (first-of-kind order); that order has been fully executed and cost is behind the company.
Future similar large defense orders are expected to carry better margins given existing learning curve and completed detailed engineering.

subsections.label: FY30 segment mix outlook
points: By FY30, Gear division (including marine business) is expected to contribute ~70-75% of total revenue, and MHE ~25-30%.

subsections.label: Growth geographies
points: Bulk of international revenue growth this quarter came from Middle East and US, driven by resumption of dispatches for orders that were on hold in Q4 last year due to improving macro conditions, now eased.
Both Middle East and US regions also show stronger traction in open order book and enquiry quantum/nature.
Middle East demand weakness/strength noted specifically in cement and mining & minerals end markets.
European market traction still awaited; based on early feelers, European market bounce-back expected in a minimum of two quarters.
International share of consolidated Gear division revenue was ~36% in Q1 FY27, with international Gear revenue growth of 37.6% YoY.
Overseas order intake grew 63% YoY to INR194 crores, with MHE contributing INR21 crores of that overseas intake; overseas open order book grew 73% YoY to INR256 crores as of June 30, 2026.
FY26 export revenue by geography: Middle East INR66 crores, Radicon USA INR102 crores, UK (Benzler Europe group) INR102/171 crores, Singapore INR22 crores.
Company serves customers in 95+ countries.

subsections.label: Assembly centers and India exports
points: Company measures total exports at the organization level (not exports-from-India alone) due to multiple overseas assembly centers set up for customer connect and proximity.
Assembly centers include local outsourcing of certain parts (value addition), while main manufacturing remains based in Anand, India.

Exports from India (standalone) declined ~35% to sub-INR30 crores in the current quarter, but overall (organization-level) exports are still expected to register double-digit higher percentage growth for the year despite this India-origin export decline.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity and pricing
points: Whenever there is a stiff/abnormal price increase, the market moves through a 'correction' phase (competitors sitting on higher inventory at historical lower prices squeeze pricing) followed by an 'acceptance' phase as inventory levels normalize across players; Q1 was correction phase, Q2 expected to be acceptance phase.

Manufacturing cycle for catalogue products is 2-3 months and for engineered products 4-5 months; existing orders on hand have price protection, but new projects will face price pressure from MNC competition.

Company positions itself as preferred supplier based on quality and faster production infrastructure versus competitors, enabling it to compete with MNCs even where MNCs offer more competitive pricing.
MNCs setting up local manufacturing plants create competitive pressure, particularly on new project pricing.

subsections.label: Export OEM relationships
points: Relationships with export OEMs have increased in number; monetization timing tied to regional recovery — near-term opportunities seen in Middle East and US based on early enquiry/order book signs, while European market (amid rising defense spending and industrial cycle uptick) still awaits traction, expected in a minimum of two quarters.

subsections.label: Sugar sector outlook
points: Sugar sector demand currently muted due to poor/prolonged monsoon impacting sugarcane crop and sugar season expectations.
Ethanol blending traction, if sustained, could support future sugar plant expansion and better sector traction, but near-term outlook remains muted.

subsections.label: Aerospace certification
points: Company is not currently working deeply on aerospace-related certifications; no near-term plans disclosed.

subsections.label: Mid-term revenue target
points: Reiterated mid-term target of reaching INR5,000 crores in topline by FY30; management calls this challenging but still achievable.

Achievability of the FY30 target is contingent on: securing a couple of large enquiries from the marine segment, expansion in export territories, continuation of the committed capex plan, and further capex under evaluation pending board approval.
By FY30, Gear division (including marine business) expected to contribute ~70-75% of total revenue, and MHE ~25-30%.

subsections.label: Acquisition strategy
points: Company is not actively looking for acquisition opportunities in the European region, especially where the opportunity demands significant investment in a manufacturing setup.

subsections.label: Patents
points: Company has filed for certain patents but declined to disclose the commercial markets/segments being targeted for competitive reasons.

subsections.label: Company background
points: Company has an operating history of 75+ years.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro risk
points: Spike in input costs attributed to geopolitical tensions during the quarter.
US-Iran tensions have picked up again in the last 48 hours (as of the call), adding to macro uncertainty and limiting confidence for full-year guidance.
Last year's US tariff actions (from Q2) and the Q4 US-Iran event both significantly impacted the gear division's order pipeline.

Large part of gear business is routed through PSUs, which are dependent on fiscal budgets, government fund allocation, and macroeconomic conditions — disturbances at this level delay capex plans of customers in thermal power, cement, and steel sectors.

subsections.label: Input cost / commodity risk
points: Significant (not minor) raw material price increases have lengthened the enquiry-to-order conversion time, contributing to the mismatch between strong order book growth and lower revenue growth guidance.

MHE division more exposed to price increase impact than gear due to its highly customized, project-based nature involving non-raw-material cost components (delivery/fuel cost, packing material cost) that are harder to lock in versus gear's catalogue/price-list and raw-material-locking mechanisms.

subsections.label: Execution / project delay risk
points: MHE division experienced delays in design engineering clearance from end customers routed through EPC main contractors, particularly in two large power-sector orders, extending hierarchy and approval timelines.

subsections.label: Weather/agri risk (sugar)
points: Prolonged, below-expectation monsoon rainfall this year is negatively impacting the sugarcane crop and expected sugar season traction.

subsections.label: Competitive risk
points: MNCs setting up local manufacturing facilities and expanding presence create pricing pressure risk, particularly for new (not-yet-quoted) projects.
Some competitors sitting on higher, lower-cost historical inventory create near-term pricing pressure until market-wide price correction completes.

subsections.label: Defense/Naval order visibility risk
points: No significant update in the last 90 days on defense/shipbuilding orders versus prior guidance; naval gearbox project margin impact of 1-2% previously noted due to learning and manufacturing cost on a first-of-kind order.

subsections.label: FY27 guidance rationale
points: Given ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty and limited near-term visibility, targeting low double-digit consolidated revenue growth while maintaining last year's EBITDA margin, supported by healthy order book, strong enquiry pipeline, and disciplined execution.

Guidance is deliberately conservative; Q1 and Q2 FY27 already show improved but not significantly improved traction; too many variables (e.g., renewed US-Iran tension) remain, limiting comfort for a higher full-year number.
Management may revisit guidance in a future quarterly call as conditions improve.

subsections.label: Segment margin targets
points: Gear division EBITDA margin targeted at 24% going forward, with EBIT margin target of 19-20% for the current/next year.
MHE division sustainable EBITDA margin targeted at 22-24% for FY27.
Overall exports growth expected at a double-digit higher percentage in FY27.

subsections.label: Defense/Naval order timeline
points: No significant update in the last 90 days versus the guidance provided in the April call; enquiry for large defense orders (anticipated order book of ~INR1000 crores) still expected to be released in Q4 of the financial year, consistent with prior communication.

guidance_ledger.statement: Given the ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty and limited near-term visibility, we are targeting to have a low double-digit consolidated revenue growth while maintaining the EBITDA margin as we had it in the last year.
Maintaining the EBITDA margin as we had it in the last year.
Loosely speaking we should be able to maintain 24% margin EBITDA margin for gear division.
1% above the current level about 18.8% is what we had in the last year, we should be able to somewhere around 19% to 20%, 20% on an average is what we are meeting at EBIT level margin for gear.
We are seeing a 22% to 24% EBITDA margin for MHE business for the year as a sustainable margin.
We had set the target of reaching to 5000 crores in a top line by FY30. That target looks challenging but still achievable for us.
We expect Gear to be almost 70% - 75% of the total revenue in FY30 and almost 25% to 30% for MHE for the overall revenue in FY'30. Gear will also include the marine business.
In terms of the overall growth we will see a double-digit higher percentage growth at least for this year when it comes to exports.
Based on the early feelers, it looks like two quarters minimum that we see for the European market to bounce back.
The enquiry of these orders are likely to be released in Q4 of this year. As on today, we maintain the same communication.
In Q2 also we are seeing that we will pick up, the market will pick up, but it will still gradually pick up... not that a stiff percentage improvement.
Q3 and Q4 is what we are expecting to improve significantly when it comes to market's acceptance of the stabilized prices.
We are not expecting any degrowth to happen compared to FY26. We are expecting growth. The amount of growth is currently what is under question.
From FY26 we will be able to definitely maintain or grow it. We are expecting growth, but the geopolitical situation will control it a little bit.
Whatever growth trajectory we have shown in the last two, three years, we can definitely continue with the same pace and growth percentage.
Considering the revenue mix, the sustainable margin is around 20% to 22% in between.
We had lowered our guidance and communicated that we are reducing the revenue in the quarter ending March by at least 5%, released in the month of January.
Anytime in Q1, they are going to release the RFP. And then we are expecting orders to come by Q4 of the financial year.
P-17 Alpha also they have deferred, but it may come in the financial year of '28, around Q3.
As we had planned, we would be ramping our exports up to 50% in the next 3 to 4 years... going forward we expect it will still improve.
We have a capex plan of INR400 crores between FY26 to FY28; roughly INR95 crores spent so far.

themes.label: MHE growth momentum
themes.note: MHE revenue declined 2.9% YoY on project execution delays even as order intake grew 38.1% YoY and open order book rose 18.8% YoY.

themes.label: Order book visibility
themes.note: Consolidated open order book rose 36.8% YoY to INR1,518 crores, with Gear open order book up 46.9% YoY to INR1,043 crores.

themes.label: Product mix (engineered vs catalogue)
themes.note: Gear order intake mix shifted to 73% engineered/27% catalogue, while quarter revenue mix was 54% catalogue/46% engineered, affecting price pass-through ability.

themes.label: FY27 guidance withheld
themes.note: Company issued conservative low double-digit revenue growth guidance for FY27 with flat EBITDA margin, citing macro uncertainty and limited visibility, with possible revision in future quarters.

themes.label: International/export expansion
themes.note: Overseas revenue grew 21.9% YoY to INR151 crores (~29% of consolidated revenue), with overseas order intake up 63% YoY and overseas order book up 73% YoY, driven by Middle East and US.

themes.label: Defense order pipeline delays
themes.note: No significant update in the last 90 days on defense/naval enquiries; enquiry release still expected in Q4 FY27 per prior communication.

key_takeaways: The Gear division which contributed nearly 80% of our consolidated revenue to INR416 crores during the quarter delivered a strong performance with revenue growing by 16.3% year-on-year.
The consolidated order intake increased 18.8% year-on-year to INR570 crores during the quarter.
Our open order book currently stands at INR1,043 crores, is up 46.9% year-on-year, providing strong revenue visibility and giving us confidence in our growth trajectory over the coming quarters.
The MHE division reported a marginal decline in revenue during the quarter with revenue moderating by 2.9% year-on-year. This was primarily on account of project execution delays.
During the quarter, order intake witnessed a significant growth of 38.1% year-on-year reaching INR185 crores.

For the quarter ended June 2026, Elecon reported consolidated revenue from operation of INR521 crores. This represents a healthy year-on-year growth of 11.9% over adjusted revenue of INR465 crores in Q1 FY '26.

Despite a spike in input cost due to geopolitical tensions, our consolidated EBITDA remained resilient and grew by 3.9% year-on-year to INR109 crores. EBITDA margins remain stable and sustainable at 21%.

Given the ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty and limited near-term visibility, we are targeting to have a low double-digit consolidated revenue growth while maintaining the EBITDA margin as it we had it in the last year.
We had set the target of reaching to 5000 crores in a top line by FY30. That target looks challenging but still achievable for us.
pressing_questions: Sir, on the international revenue side, it's grown nearly 22% this quarter. Could you please talk about which are the geographies majorly contributed for this growth? Also, you can talk about Middle East impact on the international revenue side. Is there any specific end markets within Middle East regions like oil and gas and infra driving this weakness? And when we can expect the recovery in the Middle East side?
If our order book is up by 37%, our order inflows are up by 23%, I think we are running on record order books now, then why are we guiding only for low double-digit revenue growth?

Considering all these things and also the order book that we are getting, why are we thinking about this lower double-digit that again is not making sense from our perspective because demand environment is good... why we are not able to reap the fruit from this?
We might not be able to give exact guidance in terms of number, but what are our aspirations for the same given the fact that we are doing significant capex around INR400 crores till FY28?
In the last year we said that Q3 onwards, we are expecting some order from Naval or defense probably... is that timeline attached to that or are we seeing some difficulty going forward?

quarters.summary: Elecon reported moderate consolidated revenue growth of 6% in FY26, with Q4 revenue declining due to delayed order inflows, extended dispatch timelines and customer-led deferment amid geopolitical/macro uncertainty; management held FY27 guidance in abeyance pending greater clarity, while MHE division continued strong growth momentum and the Gear Division carries a strong open order book supporting expected normalization and recovery in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Q4 Performance Drivers
points: Slower conversion of the order pipeline into revenue, in line with a broader industry trend of uneven execution cycles across all capital-intensive sectors.

Several customers across key end-user industries recalibrated their capex schedules, leading to a shift in business direction across the value chain; underlying demand environment remains constructive.
Profitability impacted by operating deleverage due to lower revenue conversion, marginally higher employee costs, along with a change in product mix.
Margins expected to improve gradually as execution accelerates and volumes pick up.

subsections.label: Goodwill Impairment Explanation
points: Goodwill represented the amount acquired in 2010-11 when Elecon acquired Benzlers and Radicon Group in Europe.

Over the last 15 years Elecon integrated these businesses into the Radicon group of products/geographies; there is no separate structure — single sales/marketing/operations team handles the combined product mix.

Management concluded the goodwill as a standalone carrying amount did not have much value in financials, though the business as a whole retains good cash flow/profitability that need not be discounted.
Goodwill was never part of standalone financials — always part of consolidated financial statements; tax deduction (if any) will accrue in the books of the UK entity holding the goodwill.
A tax deduction is being claimed annually in the UK entity; about 5 years remain with only 1 million GBP left to be claimed gradually as deduction.

subsections.label: Capex Program & ROCE Discussion
points: Capex plan of INR400 crores spread between FY26 to FY28; roughly INR95 crores spent so far across different categories.
Capex split: Gear Division ~80% of spend, MHE Division the remaining ~20%.

ROCE decline from FY24 to FY26 attributed to growing equity/capital employed base — nearly INR800 crores of balance is parked in conservative investments yielding ~8%, rather than deployed into installed capacity expansion.

Cash generation has outpaced capex deployment in recent years; company plans to build capability and increase installed capacity over the next two years, expecting resultant revenue and EBITDA/margin improvement.

Management views the large investment cushion as 'a good problem to have,' providing flexibility for strategic investments/expansion while closely monitoring macro conditions before committing to major expansion.

subsections.label: Receivables Movement
points: Receivables increase of about INR90 crores versus last year's balance sheet — of this, INR70-75 crores is attributable to February and March sales not yet due as of March 31, and about INR15 crores relates to an overdue bucket compared to same period last year, expected to be effected in April.

subsections.label: Demand & Deferment Drivers
points: Delayed order inflows, extended dispatch timelines and customer-led deferment of delivery amid ongoing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties impacted Gear Division near-term performance.
During the year, healthy inflow of orders secured across key sectors including power, steel, cement and material handling equipment.
Strong open order book for next year supported by strengthening demand environment and healthy project pipeline.

Steel sector customers specifically asked for deferment of delivery; order booking was also later than expected as customers deferred capex investment due to geopolitical scenario, preventing execution within the year; deferment was broad-based, not tied to any specific large order.

Geopolitical risk intensified starting last week of February, intensified further in first week of March, with the largest impact felt in March; approx. INR77 crores of orders were affected across three buckets (on-hold ready-to-dispatch, scheduled-but-deferred delivery, and production halted).
Company had already flagged in the December quarter call that March quarter revenue could be reduced by at least 5%.

MHE order inflow for the quarter was a 10-quarter low due to timing difference — expected opportunities deferred to Q1; more than INR15 crores in orders already received in April, expected to help mitigate the Q4 gap.
MHE inquiry pipeline is strong at more than INR1,000 crores across various sectors.

Gear Division has a large single order (LOI already received) from the power sector, described as the single largest order ever in the industrial gear business market — expected to convert to an order within 1-2 days; further details to be published once finalized.
Sector-wise order book sensibility: power, steel and cement are the three main sectors seeing good demand.
Cement sector is relatively stagnant, more skewed to brownfield than greenfield projects, moving at their own pace, though orders coming from 2-3 major contractors.
Sugar industry demand anticipated to rise due to potential gas/petroleum supply constraints from the war situation, driving ethanol demand — this is anticipatory, not yet realized.

Steel sector deferment: gearboxes were ready but could not be delivered/invoiced due to customer-requested deferment; expected to clear in Q1; described as a usual phenomenon exacerbated by the geopolitical situation.

subsections.label: Raw Material / Input Cost Pass-through
points: Raw material prices/logistic costs were secured/locked in as soon as orders were received, anticipating cost increases, to safeguard margins.
Execution cycle is not long, so pending orders are largely already covered by locked-in input costs; suppliers are not in a position to claim additional costs on pending orders.

subsections.label: Gear Division Performance
points: Gear Division continues to be the largest contributor, accounting for ~63% of consolidated revenue in Q4.
Revenue decline reflects a temporary gap between order booking and deferment of delivery driven by phasing of execution in large industrial projects.
Demand fundamentals remain strong, supported by sustained customer engagement and healthy inquiry pipeline across domestic and overseas markets.
EBIT margin impacted by lower throughputs and changes in product mix — considered transitional factors expected to normalize as execution improves.

Strong order intake and open order book of INR894 crores provide good visibility for coming quarters; expected to return to steady growth trajectory as execution timelines normalize and macro conditions stabilize.

subsections.label: MHE Division Performance
points: MHE continued strong growth momentum in Q4 FY26, reinforcing its role as key growth driver.
Growth driven by sustained demand across power, cement and ports, supported by both replacement demand and ongoing industrial infrastructure investments.
EBIT reflects stable profitability despite dynamic revenue mix; margins remained healthy, supported by balanced contribution from equipment sales and aftermarket services.

Order book provides strong foundation for continued growth; MHE seen as structurally high-growth segment supported by long-term trends in industrial automation and increasing focus on material handling efficiency.
MHE delivered revenues ahead of the guidance set for the year, supported by robust demand and strong execution pipeline (per closing remarks).

subsections.label: Product Mix & Margin Dynamics
points: Engineered products carry better margins than catalogue products; company continues to prioritize higher-margin engineered products.

Despite engineered mix improving YoY (40%→45%), margins have not improved because engineered orders on hand could not be executed/dispatched/invoiced this year due to customer deferment; margin embedded in this unbilled inventory (valued at cost) is not yet reflected in financials.

At the start of the year, margin projections assumed a 50-50 EP/CP split; however, catalogue product orders came in more than engineered product orders during the year due to customer-side project delays, while engineered orders on hand as of March 31 may be executed in the next year.

Management is not providing explicit guidance that margins will revert upward due to ongoing geopolitical uncertainty, but if domestic orders proceed smoothly and expected demand materializes, EBITDA levels could return to the previously suggested range of 22%-24%.

Gear margin decline versus FY22-24 peak attributed to: (1) engineered orders not reflected in invoicing this year (unlike FY22-23 growth period), and (2) R&D cost investment in developing new products/upgrading existing ones (4 patents taken, 3 more being applied for, per investor presentation).

Navy/defense development order carried a slightly lower margin (1-2 percentage points lower, as communicated in a previous call) due to developmental initiatives/activities involved in executing the first order; a repeat order of the same grade would carry better margins.
Sustainable MHE margin expected in the 20-22% range considering the revenue mix, given equipment contribution is expected to increase while spare parts/aftermarket may not grow at the same pace.
Management stated the Gear-to-MHE mix may shift further as MHE continues to grow alongside Gear growth, but long-term consolidated margin is not expected to vary due to mix shift.
Capacity utilization with capex addition currently stands at 56-60%.

subsections.label: R&D and IP
points: Continued focus on research and development ensures innovation, product customization and end-to-end life cycle support remain central to offerings.
Company is developing new products and upgrading existing products; investor presentation shows 4 patents taken and 3 more being applied for, contributing to R&D cost incurred during the year.

subsections.label: Capex and Capacity Plans
points: Capacity utilization currently at 56-60% following capex addition.

Company plans to build capability and increase installed capacity over the next two years as part of the INR400 crore FY26-28 capex program; results expected in terms of revenue increase and EBITDA/margin improvement.
No capex yet incurred for the newly established Mexico step-down subsidiary; management to update at a later date.

subsections.label: Mexico Subsidiary / Export Strategy
points: Established a step-down subsidiary in Mexico, strengthening presence in Latin American region as part of international expansion strategy.
Currently a 50% tariff (Section 232) applies to exports from India to the company's US subsidiaries/customers; Mexico establishment aims to supply Latin America where this tariff is not applicable.
No significant capex committed yet for the Mexico entity; management will update later.

Export mix expected to improve going forward despite the geopolitical scenario; company has managed to maintain at least last year's export performance; some improvement seen in order booking in a few entities, while the Middle East has suffered significantly.
Company cannot currently comment specifically on sustainable margins tied to export/domestic mix due to the ever-changing scenario.
UAE overseas entity is exposed to Middle East-related disruption risk (e.g., Strait of Hormuz closure); domestic operations and other entities are not seen as affected.

subsections.label: Input Cost and Supply Chain Management
points: Raw material and logistics cost increases are being pre-empted by securing prices/placing orders as soon as customer orders are received, to safeguard margins.
Execution cycle is short, so most pending orders' input costs are already locked in; suppliers cannot claim additional costs on orders already placed.

No supply chain issues currently observed for domestic orders due to Strait of Hormuz closure or Middle East tensions; only the UAE overseas entity is expected to be affected, not domestic operations or other entities.

subsections.label: End-Market Demand by Sector
points: Power, steel and cement are the three main sectors showing good demand in the current order book.
Steel sector is now expanding its executions; power sector customers are demanding fast project closure — no delays anticipated in deliveries for power, cement, and steel going forward.
Cement demand is relatively stagnant, more brownfield-oriented, moving at its own pace, though orders are coming from 2-3 major contractors.
Sugar industry demand anticipated to rise due to potential ethanol demand driven by concerns over gas/petroleum supply amid the war situation (anticipatory, not confirmed).
No current order visibility from the nuclear sector.
Engineered/customized products have better margins than catalogue products, so company prioritizes pursuing engineered product orders where possible.
Possibility of significant uptick in Middle East orders for infrastructure redevelopment once the regional conflict situation clears, but direction/timing remains uncertain.

subsections.label: Defense/Navy Order Pipeline
points: Expecting a very good/large order from the Indian Navy in Q4 (current) — described as a big order at this moment.
Corvette RFP now expected to be released anytime in Q1 FY27 (deferred), with orders expected by Q4 FY27 — earlier expectation was Q2 FY27, indicating a delay.
P-17 Alpha order also deferred, may come in Q3 FY28; shipyard has not yet even received the RFQ for this.
Project orders of this scale are typically executed over two to three years.

For large project orders, margins are described as good; smaller orders see a margin gap; first Navy order had 1-2 percentage points lower margin due to developmental activities, but repeat orders of the same grade are expected to have better margins.

subsections.label: International Expansion
points: Establishment of a step-down subsidiary in Mexico to strengthen presence in the Latin American region, as part of strategy to expand into new sectors and geographies.
Strategy focuses on portfolio diversification, expansion into new sectors and geographies and continuous strengthening of engineering and execution capabilities.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation Philosophy
points: Strong net cash position of ~INR700 crores provides significant strategic flexibility to pursue growth opportunities while maintaining financial discipline.

~INR800 crores parked in conservative investment instruments yielding ~8%, kept for flexibility for strategic investments and expansion; company closely monitoring macro conditions before committing to major capex/expansion decisions.
Board recommended a final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share (face value INR1), subject to shareholder approval.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and Macro Risks
points: Ongoing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties led to delayed order inflows, extended dispatch timelines, and customer-led deferment of delivery, primarily impacting the Gear Division.
Geopolitical event intensified from last week of February through first week of March, causing ~INR77 crores of order/dispatch impact in March across on-hold, deferred and halted-production orders.
Customers across key end-user industries recalibrated capex schedules due to macro/geopolitical uncertainty.

Middle East region has suffered significantly in terms of order booking due to ongoing tensions; UAE overseas entity is exposed to related risk (e.g., Strait of Hormuz closure impact), though domestic operations are not expected to be affected.
Management describes current challenges as transient and does not believe they alter the company's long-term growth trajectory.
Conflicting news/information on the geopolitical situation as of the call date creates ongoing uncertainty, prompting a cautious 'wait and watch' approach before providing forward guidance.

subsections.label: Product Mix & Margin Risk
points: Unfavourable product mix (more catalogue vs. engineered product execution this year) contributed to margin compression versus historical levels.
Change in product mix and lower throughput cited as factors impacting Gear Division EBIT margin.

subsections.label: Input Cost / Raw Material Risk
points: Anticipated increase in raw material and logistics costs; company states this is being pre-emptively addressed by locking in prices at order receipt and passing costs into new orders.

subsections.label: Defense Order Timing Risk
points: Corvette and P-17 Alpha defense RFP/order timelines have been pushed out/deferred relative to earlier expectations.

subsections.label: FY27 Guidance Stance
points: Given continued macroeconomic uncertainty and limited near-term visibility, management believes it is prudent to adopt a cautious approach and is holding guidance for FY27 at this stage, to revisit once there is greater clarity and stability in the operating environment.
Management explicitly stated they will not be providing forward-looking guidance for FY27, as previously communicated.

Despite lack of specific guidance, management does not expect degrowth compared to FY26 — they expect growth, though the magnitude is currently uncertain and will be influenced by the geopolitical situation.

Management expects to at least maintain or grow margins from FY26 levels; anticipated raw material/logistics cost increases are already being factored into new orders so should not adversely affect margins.

If domestic orders proceed smoothly and expected demand materializes, EBITDA could return to previously suggested levels of 22%-24% for the Gear Division, though this is not being given as firm guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty.
MHE Division growth expected to continue at the same pace/percentage as shown in the last two-three years, supported by strong inquiry flow, particularly from the power sector.
Strategic priorities remain unchanged: disciplined execution, operational efficiency, prudent capital allocation, and strengthening presence in high-growth markets.
MHE division delivered revenues ahead of the guidance set for the year in FY26.

guidance_ledger.statement: Given the continued macroeconomic uncertainty and limited near-term visibility, we believe it is prudent to adopt a cautious approach. Accordingly, we are holding our guidance for FY27 at this stage and will revisit our outlook once there is greater clarity and stability in the operating environment.
We are not expecting any degrowth to happen compared to FY26. We are expecting growth. The amount of growth is currently what is under question.
From FY26 we will be able to definitely maintain or grow it. We are expecting growth, but the geopolitical situation will control it a little bit.
If all the domestic orders go smoothly and what demand we are expecting comes in, we will be able to go back to the EBITDA levels that we had suggested even earlier, which is close to 22% to 24%.
Whatever growth trajectory we have shown in the last two, three years, we can definitely continue with the same pace and growth percentage.
Considering the revenue mix, the sustainable margin is around 20% to 22% in between.

guidance_ledger.metric: Consolidated EBITDA margin impact from Gear-MHE mix shift
guidance_ledger.statement: The mix might change further, but we do not expect the long-term margin to vary.
We had lowered our guidance and communicated that we are reducing the revenue in the quarter ending March by at least 5%, released in the month of January.
Anytime in Q1, they are going to release the RFP. And then we are expecting orders to come by Q4 of the financial year.
P-17 Alpha also they have deferred, but it may come in the financial year of '28, around Q3.
As we had planned, we would be ramping our exports up to 50% in the next 3 to 4 years... going forward we expect it will still improve.
We have a capex plan of INR400 crores between FY26 to FY28; roughly INR95 crores spent so far.

themes.label: Order book visibility

key_takeaways: The Gear Division, which accounted for approximately 63% of consolidated revenue in Q4, reported revenue of INR472 crores, reflecting a decline of 21% year-on-year, primarily due to delayed order inflows, extended dispatch timelines and customer-led deferment of delivery amid ongoing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties.
The MHE Division, which contributed approximately 37% of the consolidated revenue in Q4, continued its strong growth trajectory, posting a 37% year-on-year increase in revenue during the quarter.
Despite the challenging environment, we delivered moderate consolidated revenue growth of 6% in FY26.

Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR158 crores, with a margin of 21.2%; Net profit for the quarter came in at INR108 crores, translating into a PAT margin of 14.5%, excluding the one-time impairment of goodwill of INR102 crores.
For the full year FY26, adjusted consolidated revenue stood at INR2,341 crores compared to INR2,227 crores in FY25; Adjusted EBITDA for FY26 stood at INR498 crores, with margins of 21.3%.

As part of our strategy to expand into international markets, we are pleased to announce the recent establishment of a step-down subsidiary in Mexico, further strengthening our presence in the Latin American region.

Given the continued macroeconomic uncertainty and limited near-term visibility, we believe it is prudent to adopt a cautious approach. Accordingly, we are holding our guidance for FY '27 at this stage and will revisit our outlook once there is greater clarity and stability in the operating environment.

On the balance sheet front, we continue to maintain a strong financial position, with a net cash balance of approximately INR700 crores; The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share.
pressing_questions: Do we expect the Gear-to-MHE ratio of 63:37 (vs historical 75:25) to continue going forward and what effect on EBITDA margin?
What issues is MHE facing since order inflow for the quarter was a 10-quarter low?

Capex program of INR400 crores — how much was spent in FY26 and what is the split between Gear and MHE? Also, ROCE has fallen from 29% in FY24 to 20.4% in FY26 — when can it bounce back to 25% by FY28?

On defense side, Navy order impacted margins — will future RFPs (Corvette by Q3 FY27, IAC in Q1 FY27) lead to winning at least one or two Navy orders by FY27, and are we qualified for upcoming Navy orders?
What is current capacity utilization in Q4, and how would you rank end markets (power, steel, cement, mining, defense, sugar, plastic and rubber) by pricing power?
Within domestic gears, where exactly are we seeing delays in dispatches where customers are not ready to take delivery — is it specific to a large order or broad-based?
On Mexico: do we still attract 50% tariff, and what capex is planned for Mexico?
Given visibility improving in domestic steel/power markets, why is there no real guidance on growth or margins for FY27?
Given the March goodwill note 8B, can you explain the goodwill write-off comment and whether any tax benefit was received?
Could the geopolitical risk starting only on the night of 27th-28th February make such a large one-month difference in revenue?
Receivables increased from INR610 crores to INR720 crores — what is the reason?
What is the current update on the aircraft carrier defense order expected by FY27, and on the P-17 Alpha order?
What is the sustainable margin for MHE going forward given the changing revenue mix (equipment vs. spare parts)?

ELECON.about: Elecon Engineering Company Ltd., incorporated in 1960. Company manufactures and sells power transmission and material handling equipment in India and internationally. In addition, it engages in the steel and non-ferrous foundry business. [1]

quarters.summary: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27 delivered sequential profitability improvement (EBITDA margin up 331bps to 16.7%, cost per tonne down INR206 sequentially to INR4,241) despite a Y-o-Y decline in total volumes (trade -2%, non-trade -21%) driven by a deliberate value-over-volume strategy, geopolitical/West Asia cost pressures (~INR110/tonne absorbed), and diesel/logistics disruptions. Management reiterated full-year guidance of ~8% trade volume growth, cost of INR4,250/tonne for FY27, capacity expansion to 119 million tonnes, and cost leadership initiatives worth INR130-150/tonne, while flagging continued near-term cost pressure in Q2 from geopolitical tensions.

subsections.label: Cost bridge / drivers of INR206/tonne sequential savings
points: Savings driven by efficient sourcing of fly ash (raw material), lower RE power price per unit, and clinker factor reduction of ~2%
Logistics contributed marginally, ~INR10/tonne from lead distance reduction
Fixed cost optimization also contributed despite lower capacity utilization
INR206 improvement is after absorbing INR110/tonne hit from West Asia geopolitical escalation; gross underlying improvement was INR316/tonne
Cost journey breakdown: efficiency factor ~INR30-50/tonne, input material and logistics ~INR50/tonne, clinker factor ~INR50/tonne, fixed cost optimization ~INR80/tonne

subsections.label: NSP / realization commentary
points: ASP/NSP sequential increase was one of the lowest in industry; management attributes this partly to accounting treatment differences (Incoterms, netting off certain expenditures against NSP unlike some peers)
Q1 saw disruption from multiple beyond-control factors causing an aberration in NSP performance vs UltraTech (down ~INR100 vs UltraTech this quarter vs ~INR50 better in preceding 8 quarters)
Company investing into channel growth this period, which impacts reported NSP under its accounting approach
Price is a market force; company is focusing controllable cost improvements as differentiator going forward

subsections.label: Depreciation
points: Depreciation number lower in the quarter due to true-up entries taken on account of merger of Sanghi and Penna, which had made Q4 depreciation higher Q-on-Q; run rate to stay similar going forward

subsections.label: RMC segment margin decline
points: No specific reason cited for margin fall from 14-15% to 7%; attributed to raw material pricing and certain financial/lease accounting factors; segment still relatively small

subsections.label: Fly ash and power sales accounting
points: Fly ash and power sales revenue booked under other operating income
Fly ash consumption is ~30% of long-term contracted volume, with surplus sold in market at a profit versus long-term purchase price, reducing effective cost of supply

subsections.label: Other expenses / acquired asset stabilization
points: Sharp Y-o-Y jump in stores & spares, advertising & sales promotion, and repairs & maintenance costs attributed to intensity of investment requirements in acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi, and others)
Company expects stabilization as one unified cement platform this financial year, reducing surprises associated with acquired assets

key_takeaways: Ambuja Cements delivered stronger profitability, improved operating efficiency and continued strategic execution in Q1 FY27 despite a challenging operating environment characterized by stable cement demand but industry-wide pressure from higher imported fuel prices, elevated freight costs and geopolitical developments in West Asia.
Trade sales share improved from 74% to 78% of overall sales, with premium products comprising 34% of trade sales.

Net operating cost reduced to INR4,241 per metric ton, a reduction of INR206 PMT from the previous quarter, keeping the company firmly on track for its guidance to achieve INR4,250 per ton for this financial year.
RE power capacity is now at 973 megawatts, up almost 500 megawatts over the past year; WHRS capacity stands at 228 megawatts, helping reduce unit power cost from INR5.9 per kWh to almost INR4.9.

Cost transformation initiatives are expected to deliver savings of almost INR130 to INR150 per ton, providing strong visibility toward the cost leadership target and mitigating pressures from geopolitical tensions.
Ambuja has evolved into a 109 million ton capacity integrated cement platform, with expansion projects expected to increase installed capacity to 119 million tons by end of this financial year.

Revenue of INR9,500 crores, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crores, EBITDA margin improved 331 basis points to 16.7%, EBITDA per ton of INR931, PAT of INR660 crores and net worth of almost INR72,000 crores.

Total trade volumes declined 2% Y-o-Y and non-trade declined 21% Y-o-Y in Q1, but management highlighted an 8% Y-o-Y improvement in trade volumes seen in July, supporting continued confidence in the 8% full-year trade volume growth guidance.

quarters.summary: Note: This transcript is actually of the Ambuja Cements (with ACC and Orient Cement) Q4 FY'26 earnings call, not an Orient Cement-specific call. subsections.label: SLA partnerships

Breakdowns and reliability issues at acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi) due to deferred maintenance
Lower government incentives due to reduced GST rates and exhaustion of incentive periods at some plants
Industry unable to fully pass on cost inflation to customers amid softening demand, pressuring margins
Past capex execution delays due to wrong contractor selection, team-building lag post-acquisition, and incomplete engineering before project starts

quarters.summary: FY26 revenue grew 21.2% YoY to INR1,632 crores with EBITDA margin at 23.8%, in line with or better than guidance despite US tariff and logistics headwinds. Higher LNG segment sales this year contributed to total company sales growth.

subsections.label: Working capital / contract assets
points: Working capital increased meaningfully from INR731 crores (FY25) to INR990 crores (FY26), primarily driven by contract assets.

Project orders now exceed INR1,000 crores in the order book; under percentage-of-completion method (POCM/ICICI guidelines), revenue is booked as per project completion percentage while collections follow payment terms (e.g., 30%, 50%, 60% milestones), causing contract assets to rise.
Advances from customers have also increased to around INR500 crores, partially offsetting the contract asset build-up.
Management expects contract assets/working capital to remain elevated as big project orders continue to grow, though inventory and vendor payments remain well controlled.

subsections.label: Operating cash flow discussion
points: Despite 18% revenue CAGR over the last 3 years, operating cash flow has not grown correspondingly — INR177 crores on INR966 crores sales in FY23 versus INR116 crores on INR1,587 crores sales more recently.

CFO explained that in project orders, investment (WIP) can run ahead of collections because payment terms are staged (e.g., 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%, 100%) and are only collected once each completion milestone is met, even if production has progressed further.

Product mix shift — from ~30% project orders earlier to more than 60% project orders now — with standard tank orders reducing and non-standard/project orders increasing, is a structural driver of this pattern.

Management indicated that if the project-heavy mix continues, similar constrained operating cash flow growth (relative to sales growth) can be expected going forward; vendor payments remain timely and inventory is under control.

subsections.label: Order pipeline commentary
points: Company expects more high-value aerospace orders of similar nature (~INR200 crores) in Q1 or Q2 FY27, which would improve order booking for FY27.
Order inflow run-rate expected at INR450-500 crores per quarter going forward, aided by the aerospace order pipeline.

2 additional small Mini LNG Terminal orders received recently from The Bahamas, currently under construction; company is targeting similar island-nation energy projects (following prior success in Scotland, Caribbean, and Bahamas).

Highview Power: management has bid for all planned projects; Highview is awaiting commissioning results of the first (Manchester/Carrington) project before proceeding; next project (Scotland, ~8x bigger) order value expected to be around 8x-10x of the present order booking, though timing depends on Highview's own investment decisions (favorably expected in 6-8 months).
ITER repair work is expected to continue for the next 7-8 years, with average annual order flow of INR50-60 crores expected for at least the next 5 years.
Third ISRO launchpad tender expected by end of current quarter, bidding expected in Q2, with order outcome possibly by end of the year.

LNG business is described as lumpy/project-based — orders can be large (e.g., INR200 crores) or absent in a given period; yearly targets are expected to be maintained or improved despite quarter-to-quarter variability.

subsections.label: Industrial Gas Solutions
points: Largest revenue contributor; delivered strong quarter and record year marked by high-value order wins, important volume milestones, and growing global recognition.

Significant aerospace order (~INR200 crores) received from a leading US-based private space company during Q4; company expects more high-value orders in Q1 FY27, reflecting proven execution capabilities and growing confidence from global aerospace players.

Transport tanks achieved milestone of >300 transport tanks and semi-trailers sold in FY26, surpassing earlier benchmarks; strong order inflows continue across transport tanks, IMO tanks, and standard industrial gas products.
Disposable cylinders crossed 2 million units dispatched in FY26 despite challenging US tariff environment, reflecting sustained international demand.
Liquid cylinders and Cryoseal brand continue to gain strong market acceptance with record order intake during the year; demand robust across domestic and export markets.

subsections.label: LNG Solutions
points: Breakthrough quarter and defining year; landmark order from Cochin Shipyard for LNG fuel tanks for LNG-powered ships marks entry into the marine LNG ecosystem, a market undergoing structural transition to cleaner fuels.
Cochin Shipyard order involves 6 LNG tanks of 800 cubic meters with stringent execution timeline; deliveries expected at ~2 tanks per year over 2-3 years.
LCNG stations order received from Gujarat Gas; continued dispatches of LNG fuel tanks to OEMs.
LNG truck segment adoption has seen near-term challenges, but long-term opportunities remain robust supported by favorable economics and regulatory tailwinds.
LNG semi-trailer business in India maintains market leadership with >250 trailers operating and dominant market share.
First batch of 5x1,500 cubic meter tanks dispatched for the Bahamas Mini LNG Terminal, reaffirming capability to execute large complex LNG storage infrastructure projects.
46 kl trailer is the most optimized/standard transport size; smaller-capacity LNG trailers exist but are not standard/hot-selling.
Storage demand expected to rise as customers now prefer at least 2 tanks (main + standby) versus earlier single-tank setups, to avoid stock-outs at fueling stations.
Qatar supply disruption (war-related damage) is expected to sustain higher demand for storage and transportation equipment for several years until Qatar's facility is repaired.
LNG products' India market share estimated at 60-65% on average across different products; global market share estimated at single digits (6-8%).
LNG division expected to grow faster than standard products, aided by LNG's ~15-20% cost advantage versus diesel/petrol even as fuel prices generally rise.

China-origin LNG tank imports considered limited risk due to PESO regulatory approval requirements (no Chinese facility currently PESO-approved) and India's need for localized design/servicing (per-truck dimension customization, ongoing maintenance support) that Chinese suppliers cannot easily match.

subsections.label: Cryo-Scientific Division
points: Continues to strengthen position as trusted partner for complex global scientific infrastructure projects.
Repeat order received from ITER, France for modifications related to cryostat panels, validating deep execution expertise in the world's most ambitious fusion energy project.
Completed production of a highly complex LOX tank for submarine-related application, highlighting capabilities in mission-critical cryogenic engineering and advanced defense applications.

ITER work expected to continue for 7-8 years; current repair work ongoing for 1.5 years at the shop, followed by site installation work; ITER also approaches INOX directly for ad hoc/short-notice equipment due to quality and delivery track record.
Very few global players operate in this space (2-3 suppliers); INOX believes the division will grow substantially in coming years due to strong engineering execution and competitive offers.
Third ISRO launchpad tender expected by end of quarter; bidding expected in Q2; order outcome possibly by year-end.

subsections.label: Beverage Keg business
points: Delivered exceptional year and strong close to FY26; recorded 31% increase in keg dispatch volumes over previous year, reflecting market expansion and demand momentum.

Secured approvals and active orders from 3 of the world's leading global breweries — Heineken, AB InBev, and Molson Coors — collectively representing >40% of global beer market volumes, positioning the company for the next growth phase.
Supplied kegs to Heineken breweries in Bulgaria, Croatia, and Reunion Island in FY26; secured first order from Molson Coors USA; secured repeat orders for non-standard kegs from Orban, Germany.
Distribution partnerships in Germany, Poland, and United Kingdom now operational, providing direct commercial access to the European market.
Increasing focus on specialized non-standard keg variants for niche applications, which yield higher margins and differentiate from commodity players.

Revenue was roughly flat YoY (INR26.13 crores FY26 vs INR27.15 crores FY25) despite 31% volume growth, because product mix shifted toward smaller 20-liter kegs (vs larger 30/50-liter kegs) and because kegs were dispatched without the 'sphere' component (7-8/10 components that customers now fix on-site themselves).
Installed capacity is ~300,000 kegs/year, presently utilized at about one-third; building infrastructure allows scaling up to 1 million kegs without major issues.
Global kegs market size is ~120 million kegs with 4-5% annual replacement demand (4-5 million kegs/year); only 2-3 manufacturers in Europe and 1 in China, with INOX being the second player in Asia.
Starbucks coffee keg samples supplied successfully; trial orders expected this quarter.

MSRTC bus conversion equipment supplied is running successfully, but customer relationship not being pursued aggressively due to difficult payment terms; understood the customer is now working with other suppliers.

subsections.label: Disposable / Industrial refrigerant cylinders
points: Refrigerant gas manufacturers operate under a quota system limiting production and sales, constraining overall market growth to marginal levels; company aims to grow market share by targeting new/under-served US customers in FY27.
RFQ process is underway for the next cycle; RFQ expected within about a month, with ordering expected at the start of next year.

subsections.label: Data center cooling initiative
points: MoU signed with a European company to jointly develop liquid nitrogen-based cooling solutions for data centers; this is an early-stage R&D-led initiative with meaningful development expected over the next 6-12 months.
Cryogenic cooling technology viewed as a compelling and scalable opportunity given growing energy efficiency requirements in modern data centers.

Partner company is a pioneer in IT infrastructure manufacturing (racks, cooling systems); INOX will provide the cooling solution while partner manufactures racks/systems, offering a joint solution to customers.
Attended a European exhibition and received significant feedback; project is in trial/initial development stage and may take 6 months to 1 year to develop a product for the application.

Rationale: liquid nitrogen cooling can bring chip/microprocessor temperature down to 77K (-196°C) in fractions of seconds/minutes versus slower air-conditioning or water-chilling methods; company is studying potential energy and time savings.

No other company currently pursuing this exact approach, but major companies like Intel and Microsoft have expressed strong interest during discussions at the European exhibition; INOX plans to develop and test prototypes, including at its R&D facility at IIT Mumbai, and share data with interested parties.
R&D spend as a percentage of turnover — management deferred providing a specific figure ('wait for some time').

subsections.label: Engineering capability / learning curve
points: Cryogenic systems integration and engineering have deep learning curves; replicating INOX's capabilities would require highly skilled people, a modern plant, and prototype development across many product types.
Company holds more than 30-40 types of approvals and certifications, which must be regularly renewed/reviewed — a cumbersome, ongoing task.
Estimated 10-15 years for a well-resourced competitor with skilled people and a modern plant to replicate INOX's facility and capabilities.

Product development methodology is demand/application-led — the company listens to customers and marketing before developing products, rather than developing products first and searching for applications; example given is Cryoseal, developed ~25 years ago for artificial insemination applications, now used in ~95% of India's insemination programs.
Overall, ~95% of products developed by the company get commercialized, reflecting a disciplined, need-based R&D and development approach.
