subsections.label: FY28 EBITDA guidance rationale
points: Company issued new guidance of minimum reported EBITDA of INR3,000 crores in FY28, nearly 2.3-2.4x the FY26 EBITDA of about INR1,290 crores, in response to investor feedback requesting a forward view beyond the current year.
Guidance is based on the assumption of a minimum 4.6 GW opex sales capacity by 1 April 2027 (3,100 MW at start of FY27 plus 1,500 MW of new capacity added during the year).
Corporate-level EBITDA guidance includes both RE Power Sales and RE Services segments.

Steady-state net debt corresponding to the INR3,000 crores EBITDA guidance is expected to be about INR16,000 crores for the assets generating that EBITDA (actual debt could be higher due to under-construction assets).

subsections.label: FY27 capacity addition guidance reaffirmed
points: Company reaffirms guidance of minimum 1.5 GW new opex capacity addition in FY27, having already added ~500 MW (400 MW RE power sales + ~100-127 MW RE services) in Q1.
Confidence in meeting or exceeding the 1.5 GW target is detailed further in Q&A #3 of the shareholder's letter.
543 MW of the 1.5 GW target is linked to the CTU project at Koppal, with two BESS bays commissioning by October '26 and March '27, and fungibility between bays expected to help mitigate any slippage.

subsections.label: Longer-term capacity growth view
points: Management believes it can add ~4,000 MW or more of new contracted capacity over the next 2-3 years (similar to the last 2 years), but does not expect to triple contracted capacity in 2 years, as that would risk signing more than can be executed.

guidance_ledger.metric: New RE Power Sales/opex capacity addition
guidance_ledger.statement: We had given a guidance and stick to it, that we will add over 1.5 gigawatt in the current fiscal in terms of opex capacity, and we've added 400 megawatt in the first quarter of the year, and we have plenty of unbuild capacity.
We are comfortable providing a new guidance, that we will have a minimum EBITDA of INR3,000 crores in FY28, which is nearly 2.4x the EBITDA in FY26.

guidance_ledger.metric: Minimum opex sales capacity by 1 April 2027
guidance_ledger.statement: 4.6 gigawatt will be the minimum opex sales capacity on 1st April 2027, which was 3,100 megawatt at the start of the year plus about 1,500 megawatt of new capacity we're adding this year.

guidance_ledger.metric: Steady-state net debt corresponding to FY28 EBITDA guidance
guidance_ledger.statement: We have provided that the steady-state net debt corresponding to this INR3,000 crores EBITDA will be INR16,000 crores.

guidance_ledger.metric: New capacity signing over next 2-3 years
guidance_ledger.statement: Could we meet or exceed 4,000 megawatt over the next couple of years? The answer is yes... we certainly think that megawatt-wise, we can do as much or more in the next 2 years to 3 years.
We think we should all be prudent and assume that there is heavy curtailment for the rest of the financial year.

guidance_ledger.metric: RE Power Sales EBITDA margin (3-4 year target)
guidance_ledger.statement: Prior guidance stated EBITDA margin would go from ~83% to nearly 86% over 3-4 years; this quarter's call did not explicitly restate the 86% target but reported continued margin expansion.

Prior quarter guidance said a proper announcement on storage/DSM/curtailment impact would come in 3-4 months; this quarter management discussed BESS strategy in detail (first BESS investment greenlit, 3 MOUs signed) but did not reference a formal standalone announcement.
Prior quarter: potential upside from lowering interest rates due to company-specific factors, but hesitant to make bold bets. This quarter, actual reduction achieved from 9.4% to 8.4%.

subsections.label: EBITDA margin drivers
points: RE Power Sales EBITDA margin improved from ~82% to 83.5% predominantly due to operating leverage as capacity grows while operating expenses/SG&A do not grow at the same pace; gross margin remains similar.
RE Services EBITDA margin improved from 14.4% to 19.6% on a good growth year.

RE Power Sales EBITDA margin expansion is driven by SG&A compressing as a % of total income from 18% to 9%; management believes the business is reaching critical mass so the pace of SG&A reduction will slow.

Company believes RE Power Sales EBITDA margin can rise from ~83% today to nearly 86% in 3-4 years, but may remain a couple of percentage points below very large pure utility players due to scale and genuinely higher operating costs of selling/building at 13 MW PPA sizes (large business development organization, multiple offices, projects across multiple states).

subsections.label: Run-rate EBITDA methodology
points: Run-rate EBITDA reflects the run-rate of plants already commissioned as if they operated for the full year; historically reported EBITDA has been about 1.1x the run-rate EBITDA at the start of the fiscal.
Run-rate EBITDA is NOT adjusted for active curtailment; it only factors in standard grid downtime/maintenance of up to ~1-1.5%.

Risks to full realization of run-rate EBITDA into reported EBITDA: (1) post-COD revenue stabilization takes 3-6 months due to technical stabilization, documentation, regulatory approvals, ramp-up; (2) Rajasthan 525 MW CTU project (~13% of run-rate EBITDA) facing grid backdown - a 40% backdown for 6 months implies ~2.5% EBITDA risk, a 50% backdown for the full year implies ~6.5% EBITDA risk; (3) upside from continued asset additions.

subsections.label: Leverage & cost of financing
points: Cost of financing reduced from 9.2% to 8.5% over the year (9.4% to 8.5% over three years), mainly due to refinancing of matured portfolios and a strategy of moving debt to fixed-rate.
40% of portfolio is on fixed-rate financing as of March 2026, insulating from interest-rate risk.
DSCR of 1.3x for FY26 for stabilized projects (operating >12 months).
Weighted average loan tenor (19 years) kept shorter than PPA tenor (23 years) for asset-liability management; net debt-to-EBITDA and credit rating are tracked consistently.

subsections.label: Cash flow hedge / accounting explanation
points: The INR414 crore cash flow hedge pre-tax gain is an accounting entry against VPPA/I-REC contracts (contract-for-difference), based on power curve analysis and price projections over 25 years; it sits as a financial asset on one side and a hedge reserve on the liability side, offsetting with zero P&L impact since tariffs are fixed and guaranteed over the 25-year contract.

subsections.label: Minority interest explanation
points: Minority interest is negative at the SPV/asset-co level because average asset age is under two years and profit after tax at asset-co level only turns positive after year four or five (interest and depreciation dominate in early years); this reflects the young age of the fleet, not an operational issue.

subsections.label: Balance sheet notes
points: Gross block and capital work-in-progress reflect ongoing and completed capacity additions.
Net debt of ~INR9,600 crore is broadly in line with capacity addition and net debt/EBITDA metrics tracked by the company.
Total equity reflects IPO proceeds.

subsections.label: ROIC / ROE clarification
points: Cash ROIC is about 13-14% (3-year average 13.75% in prior fiscal, ~13% in FY26), not single digits; cash ROE rose from 16.81% in FY25 to 17.42% in FY26 (as per shareholder letter Page 11).

subsections.label: Repeat vs new business
points: Continue to have nearly three-fourths (74%) of new volumes contracted in the past year with existing clients, consistently around the 75% mark for many years, indicating strong client satisfaction, with Data and AI a big part of growth.

FY26 saw 1,400 MW commissioned and 1,400 MW newly contracted, fully replenishing the pipeline.

subsections.label: Client diversification / credit quality
points: 82% of volumes are with clients credit rated AA, AAA or multinationals; another 14% is A-rated; hence 96% is A-rated and above.
The correlation between serving the biggest/best customers and getting repeat capacity growth opportunities with them is highlighted as a virtuous cycle.

subsections.label: CFD / VPPA structure
points: Contract for Difference (CFD) means the customer (often global big tech) buys the green attribute, not the physical power; customer pays the difference between an assured contracted tariff and the realized tariff on the energy exchange.

Example: if contracted value is INR3.4/unit and exchange realization is INR2, company receives INR1.4 as CFD payment; if exchange realization is INR5, company pays back INR1.6 - net revenue remains fixed at INR3.4, so there is no merchant price exposure.
CFD is a common global contracting structure; SECI has recently indicated plans for CFD-type structures for other purposes as well.

subsections.label: BESS in current contracts
points: Of the 2,600 MW under execution, BESS quantum is very small (5-7 MW), so tariff for BESS is not meaningfully broken out separately from the overall portfolio tariff.

subsections.label: Two business segments
points: RE Power Sales: long-term PPA power sales; operational capacity ~3,100 MW, contracted yet-to-be-executed 2,600 MW; total contracted 5.7 GW.

RE Services: builds plants for customers who own the assets, with lifetime revenue from maintenance/servicing and shared infrastructure/power transmission; operational capacity 555 MW with 215 MW under construction.
Combined total portfolio across both segments is ~6.5 GW.

subsections.label: Data & AI segment growth
points: 42% of total contracted 5,700 MW is Data & AI, up from 14% two years ago; in MW terms grown ~10x from 260 MW to 2,400 MW.
New account wins in Data & AI include Princeton Digital Group and Iron Mountain; repeat deals with existing clients like STT Data.
AI chip deployment drives disproportionate power consumption growth - buildings housing AI chips consume ~10x the power of comparable buildings without them, driving strong future demand.

Data centre demand is concentrated in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu (cable landing points Mumbai, Chennai); Karnataka is a second-order state, with Andhra Pradesh expected to emerge in a couple of years.
Partnerships structured as strategic JVs (e.g., data centre operators taking 26% equity) rather than vendor relationships, reflecting CEO-level strategic decisions on both sides.
Data & AI customers also include global big tech - publicly known relationships include Apple, Meta, Google, and Amazon.

subsections.label: Conventional industries
points: Beyond Data & AI, contracted volumes span industries including cement, auto components, tire manufacturing, and chemicals.

subsections.label: Geographic/segment diversification of growth engines
points: Growth engines are diversified across STU-connected plants (state-specific), CTU-connected projects (17% of capacity, ~12-13% of run-rate EBITDA) supplying big tech with IREC-type solutions, and onsite solar (13% of capacity, similarly meaningful EBITDA share).

Pie chart of capacity mix has shifted materially over time: Karnataka fell from 60% (Apr 2023) via 43% to now form part of a more diversified base; Gujarat rose to 36% before further diversification; 'other states' now form 14% of the portfolio and are expected to keep growing as more capacity comes up there.
Within Karnataka (33% of run-rate EBITDA) diversification exists across 6 sites, 55 customers, 71% solar/29% wind - illustrating both site and technology diversification to avoid unitary risk.

subsections.label: Wind vs solar resource performance
points: FY26 was a strong year for wind generation (PLF rose from 32% to 35%) but solar PLF was slightly lower due to marginally lower radiation; technical uptime and performance for both wind and solar remained strong, with the PLF variance attributed to resource availability, not technical performance.
El Nino weather effect typically corresponds with lower wind output but less rainfall/more solar output, reinforcing the value of wind-solar diversification.

subsections.label: Segment revenue and margin (via CFO)
points: Both RE Power Sales and RE Services segments grew 28-30% and saw margin expansion.
RE Power Sales gross margin profile remains consistent at ~92-93%, with EBITDA margin expansion driven by operating leverage.
RE Services had a very healthy year versus the previous year, with both gross margin and EBITDA margin expanding.

subsections.label: Execution discipline / commissioning ramp-up
points: Company added 1,471 MW of new capacity across both RE Power Sales and RE Services segments in FY26, versus less than 500 MW in the prior year - a 3x jump in the IPO year.

This ramp-up followed a deliberate 2-year investment plan (starting Jan/Feb 2024) in organizational capability (team) and project development (land, evacuation infrastructure) to capture growth, with a lead time before commissioning could scale.

Company executed plants within budgeted cost consistently over the last four years, reflecting robust project development (land/permitting), project management, supply chain management, financial discipline, and right-of-way/transmission management - described as a multi-year, not one-time, achievement.

subsections.label: Grid uptime / curtailment
points: Grid uptime of 99.24% (only 0.76% attributable to expected maintenance downtime, not curtailment) reflects predominantly STU-connected portfolio, which saw no curtailment last year.
Curtailment issues are concentrated in CTU projects, particularly in Rajasthan and Gujarat, not in STU projects.

Bikaner 2 substation (housing the 525 MW CTU project) is currently experiencing ~30% curtailment of power injected; grid has forecasted end of backdown by September 2026, but management cautions this is the grid's own (externally controlled) estimate and urges conservatism given historical delays in large transmission network builds.

subsections.label: FY27 capacity build plan
points: Guidance of minimum 1,500 MW addition in FY26-27; one ~500 MW CTU project (Koppal, Karnataka - 450 MW wind, 80 MW solar) planned, with the remainder (~1 GW or more) in STU where curtailment risk is seen as low.

Company plans light solar commissioning in the July-September quarter (rainy season) with some wind commissioning, and will resume solar module deliveries from September/October given ALMM module transition uncertainty.

subsections.label: Organizational capability for scaling commissioning
points: Management describes the scale-up from ~500 MW/year to 1,500 MW/year as originally feeling like 'a real stretch' but achieved through the 2-year capability investment; hopeful the run-rate can grow further over time, though not explicitly projecting or forecasting beyond current guidance.

Capacity mix diversification over time: Karnataka (60% in Apr 2023) and Gujarat's shares have diluted as 'other states' have grown to 14% of the portfolio as of April 2026, and this share is expected to keep growing with more capacity coming up in these states.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / FX / commodity risk (Iran war)
points: Management has not yet seen any material adverse movement in equipment availability or capital costs attributable to the Iran war; situation described as volatile with that caveat.

subsections.label: CTU grid backdown / curtailment risk (Rajasthan)
points: 525 MW CTU project in Rajasthan (~13% of run-rate EBITDA) facing grid backdown; risk quantified as ~2.5% of EBITDA if 40% backdown continues for 6 months, or ~6.5% of EBITDA if 50% backdown continues for the full year.

Bikaner 2 substation currently experiencing ~30% curtailment of power injected; grid has forecast backdown ending by September 2026, but management flags this as an externality beyond company control and urges conservative expectations given delays typical in large transmission builds.
PPAs do not provide protection for curtailment - corporate customers do not have pay-for-performance contracts and are not liable to pay if power is not generated for any reason.

subsections.label: Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) regulatory risk
points: New DSM rules introduced a few weeks prior to the call are seen as onerous on power producers industry-wide; rules have been challenged in court (sub-judice) and MNRE/Ministry of Power are in active discussions to find a resolution.
Impact assessment is immature given the recency of the announcement; industry-wide forecasting systems will need improvement to mitigate DSM impact.

Mitigation being explored: energy storage (BESS) to limit downside from curtailment/DSM and capture upside value (storing daytime power for higher night-time tariffs), to be blended into customer contracts.
Company expects to make a proper announcement on storage strategy and DSM/curtailment/revenue impact within three to four months.

subsections.label: ALMM (Approved List of Models and Manufacturers) / module cost risk
points: Domestic module prices expected to be elevated with ALMM potentially effective from June 2026; tariffs historically adjust reasonably quickly (up or down) to reflect module price changes given competitive industry dynamics, preserving target IRRs.

If module costs rise due to India cell manufacturing requirements, this is passed to customers via higher tariffs; customer savings on power bills may fall from 30-35% to 22-25% (range varies by state and wind/solar mix), but customers remain enthusiastic buyers of green power - no impact expected on margins or volumes.

Historical pattern across similar transitions (0% import duty to import duty, to Make-in-India cells) shows accelerated buying ahead of the deadline as customers rush decisions to lock in current tariffs; company has not yet started procuring modules for post-June-2026 commissioning as the effective transition date/extension remains uncertain.

Company has deliberately planned light solar commissioning in July-September quarter (rainy season) and will resume module deliveries from September/October, based on experience from prior similar transitions.

subsections.label: Interest rate / macro risk
points: Potential for further reduction in interest cost via refinancing of new project sets is offset by macro uncertainty (potential rising interest rates, FX rate movements); management hesitant to commit to any specific improvement given this uncertainty.

subsections.label: Client/contract dispute risk
points: Despite more than 1,100 contracts, company reports zero ongoing client disputes; diversity of clients and small average contract size (13 MW per plant across 3,100 MW portfolio) is viewed as an inherent risk mitigant.

points: Company does not give financial guidance for next fiscal but guides at least 1,500 MW (1.5 GW) of new RE Power Sales capacity addition in FY26-27, expressing confidence in achieving this.
100% of capacity expected to be commissioned in FY26-27 is already contracted at start of fiscal (part of 2,600 MW under execution); remainder will come in the following fiscal.
Management does not treat 1,500 MW as a ceiling - 'we would try to do more' - and hopes the annual run-rate can grow further over time, though not formally forecasting beyond current guidance.

Consolidated profit after tax, PAT has grown from about INR19 crores in fiscal 24-25 to INR86 crores in fiscal 25-26.
42% of our contracted capacity is with Data and AI, up from about 14% two years ago; in MW terms this has grown nearly 10 times from about 260 MW to 2,400 MW.
We continue to have nearly three-fourths or 74% of new volumes that we contracted this past year was with existing clients.
Our guidance on new capacity addition is that we would have at least 1,500 MW or 1.5 GW of RE Power Sales capacity addition in financial year 26-27.
Reported PAT has seen a massive leap of about 4.4x from slightly below INR20 crores for fiscal 25 to slightly in excess of INR85 crores in fiscal 26.
pressing_questions: What impact do you see on your business due to ongoing Iran war and supply constraints? Any impact on rate of interest or increase in project capex module cost due to FX movement?

How much of your under-construction capacity, which is roughly around 2.6 GW I believe, is under CTU connection, and how do you think about the curtailment for the new capacities and does your PPA provide for any protection?

How you think about the impact of the new deviation settlement mechanism (DSM). Of course, I think it's most likely to impact the CTU connected projects, but how can it impact your revenues if it goes through in current form and what are the mitigation which is available to us?

With domestic module prices going to be elevated with ALMM now could be coming in from June 26, how are you seeing the project IRRs evolve in the C&I segment, sir? Is the margin pricing pressure going to be absorbed by you guys or the customers or the module maker through higher tariffs, sir?

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw total income and EBITDA growth with margin expansion, aided by a strong garmenting recovery on US-India tariff rationalization and UK/EU FTA-driven demand; management guided to calibrated price hikes from Q2 (apparel 5-7%, fabric 7-8%) to offset RM inflation, expects H2 to be stronger on festive/wedding season recovery, targets doubling revenue with EBITDA growing faster than topline over 3-5 years (directional, pending Kearney strat-plan), and reiterated garmenting order book full till December with double-digit EBITDA margin as an endeavour (not guidance) given global trade unpredictability.

subsections.label: Topline & Profitability drivers
points: Total income growth of 6% YoY driven by strategic focus on premiumization, casualization, and geographical diversification.
EBITDA margin expansion of 40 bps YoY despite gross margin drop, aided by improved operational efficiencies.

Gross margin drop of 35 bps attributed to business mix shift — suiting (highest gross margin, domestic dominance) had a smaller quarter versus last year, while garmenting (export, lower gross margin than domestic suiting) grew, changing the overall mix; despite this, EBITDA still grew 40 bps.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & Cash
points: Company sustained debt-free status; net cash surplus improved by INR209 crores YoY (from net debt of INR55 crores in June'25 to net cash surplus of INR154 crores in June'26).
Net working capital days improved by 15 days YoY (from 90 to 75 days), aided by working capital management initiatives.

subsections.label: Depreciation
points: Depreciation increase of 25% YoY includes a one-time INR11 crores impact from a lease accounting error (store depreciation) in the prior year period; this one-off will not recur in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Raw material cost inflation quantum
points: Wool prices increased almost 100% over the same quarter last year.
Cotton and flax prices increased by about 20% over last year.
Chemicals costs increased by about 30% over last year.
Despite this cost inflation, the company delivered the same amount of gross margin without taking much price increase in the quarter.

subsections.label: Garmenting order book status
points: Company closed taking orders for December on 31st July; from 1st August started booking for Q4 (January onwards), meaning garmenting capacity is full from now till December.
Order book is described as looking 'very good' and serves as forward guidance for the segment.

Orders are taken on a cost-plus costing module basis, so margins should not be affected unless something dramatic happens in the near-term (2-3 months) before order fulfillment; long-term export customers understand and adjustments can be made for minor cost swings.
No capacity available till December across five factories (three in Karnataka, one new in Andhra, one in Ethiopia); currently booking for January.

CEO met CEOs of major global brands (Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Brooks Brothers, Charles Tyrwhitt, Taylor brands, Men's Wearhouse) in UK/US in July; all bullish about the business with good off-take growth and okay consumer sentiment at the premium end across territories, including India.

subsections.label: Consumer trend observation
points: Suit usage appears to be returning in the Western world, though product mix is shifting slightly from 100% pure wool suits to some poly-wool blends to manage costs; this is only a consumer trend observation and has not yet resulted in actual orders.

key_figures.label: High Value Cotton Shirting EBITDA margin
High Value Cotton Shirting EBITDA margin
Park Avenue & Raymond Ready-to-Wear casual mix growth

subsections.label: Segment reclassification
points: Company officially instituted a segment reclassification to provide transparency on core operations vs growth bets, as promised in the previous call.
Emerging businesses — Ethnix by Raymond, Raymond Home, innerwear, sexual wellness, and newly launched Chairman's Collection — carved out into a standalone reporting segment.
Portfolio now split into five segments: Branded Textile, Branded Apparel (only four core brands), Garmenting, High Value Shirting, and Emerging Business.

subsections.label: Garmenting Business
points: Stellar 50% YoY growth driven by strong order book execution following US-India tariff rationalization and onboarding of new global clients from Europe and UK.
EBITDA margin swing of 1100 bps YoY (from -4.1% to 7.3%) driven by capacity utilization improvement as plants run full.

subsections.label: Branded Apparel
points: Revenue grew 4% YoY, supported by high double-digit growth in LFS and online channels, with casual brands witnessing double-digit growth.
EBITDA margin impacted by adverse channel mix (shift toward margin-dilutive e-commerce/LFS channels), though partially mitigated by reduced markdowns and store rationalization.
Growth muted partly due to EBO closures losing some sales during transformational journey.

First quarter impacted by Adhik Maas (inauspicious month in India with no celebration dates), delaying wedding/festive dates by 20-25 days into H2, hurting suits/blazers off-take since Raymond is largely a formal brand.
Management expects H2 to be very strong as wedding dates return in winter and festive period (Onam to Ganpati to Puja to Diwali) spans a longer period than last year.

subsections.label: Branded Textiles
points: Revenue decline primarily due to base effect from previous year, where Q4 FY26 IT issues pushed a large amount of fabric business invoicing into Q1 FY26, making that a large quarter for comparison.
EBITDA margin decline due to scale deleverage from this base effect.
Despite inflationary pressures on raw material prices, overall product mix remained resilient.

subsections.label: High Value Cotton Shirting
points: Revenue decline due to base effect of last year (same IT-issue-driven invoicing shift as fabric business).
EBITDA margin improvement due to favourable product mix despite high raw material costs.

subsections.label: Emerging Business
points: Comprises Ethnix by Raymond, Raymond Home, Park Avenue Innerwear, Chairman's Collection, and Sexual Wellness.
Company continues to execute tactical investments in this segment to drive long-term growth.
Revenue grew 9% YoY to INR79 crores.

subsections.label: Brand-wise / channel performance
points: Large growth coming from casual brands; e-commerce and LFS are key growth channels though margin-dilutive, with e-commerce growing high double-digit and LFS growing upwards of 25%.

ColorPlus and Parx (casual brands) growing at double digit; casual portion within Park Avenue and Raymond Ready-to-Wear grew 200 bps YoY, moving casualization mix from 15-16% to 18% within those brands.
TRS (The Raymond Store format) growing plus 5-6% like-to-like; EBOs growing plus 3% like-to-like despite active store closures.

subsections.label: Loyalty ecosystem
points: Loyalty ecosystem reached 12.4 million members, providing a data-led consumer insight engine to drive repeat visits and lower marketing acquisition costs.

subsections.label: Garmenting geographic mix shift
points: US-India tariff rationalization and proactive expansion into UK and EU markets (helped by free trade agreements) created robust demand recovery in garmenting segment.
During Trump tariffs, US share fell from 65% to 55% and business also declined since seasonal shift of 10% of business cannot happen suddenly (requires sampling etc).
US tariffs got rationalized, some old clients returned but some have not, having placed orders with Vietnam, Cambodia, Turkey and other factories — those orders will take time to come back.
US share currently 59-60%; UK share moved from 10% to 12%; Europe moved from 5-6% to 7-8%.
Europe orders are yet to fully materialize — FTA has just been announced and will take about 6-9 months to come into force; currently largely inquiries and sample orders, bulk orders expected later.
UK bulk orders have started coming through as FTA has been live from 15th July; orders came in Q1 but most are getting made in Q2/Q3.
New UK clients: Next, T.M. Lewin (shirting client, benefiting from UK-India FTA duty rationalization making Indian shirting competitive against historically competitive neighboring countries).
New Europe clients already being processed: El Corte Ingles (Spain, biggest departmental store), OVS (Italy), Carl Gross (Germany).

Endeavour is to restrict US dependence to around 55% of exports while still running factories full and being ready to add new lines/capacity, with rest-of-world growing faster than US in export portfolio.
Order book is spread across Europe, US, Japan, Korea, Asia — all regions.
India-Australia/New Zealand FTA on wool has no material impact since wool import from Australia already had zero tariff.

subsections.label: ESG / Renewable energy geography-agnostic goals
points: Renewable energy share increased from 8-9% to ~12% this year; company intends to reach 25% by 2030, expects to reach that target sooner than planned.
Company remains fully on track for target-driven 2030 ESG goals.

Ethnix net reduction since last June
Net EBO reduction as % of network

subsections.label: Store footprint optimization
points: Continuing to optimize store footprint to enhance store productivity and margins; active network stands at 1627 stores across 600 cities.
133 stores exited and 85 new high-yielding stores opened since June 2025; Q1 FY27 saw 8 branded EBO stores opened and 24 closed (net -16), TRS format net +6, Ethnix opened 1 and closed 18 (net -17).
Overall net EBO reduction of 34 stores cumulatively, about 9% of the network, with Ethnix accounting for a net reduction of 29-30 stores since last June.
High double-digit growth in more modern channels like e-com and LFS for branded apparel.

Store closure process is not over; will take another 2-3 quarters due to FOFO partner commitments, notice periods with landlords, and negotiations — hence this year designated as 'year of consolidation'.
Net openings in branded EBO stores will be negative this year; company will do calibrated opening.
Once EBO rationalization is stabilized (3-4 more quarters), company will look at next phase of EBO growth, which is when margin recovery and sales recovery via the main EBO channel are expected.

subsections.label: Ethnix business model change
points: Ethnix will close a few more underperforming stores.

Big project is changing the business model: top-end structured products like sherwanis/bandhgalas (priced INR50,000-INR1.5 lakh+) moving from Made-to-Stock to Made-to-Measure model, since customers spending this much want customization (embroidery, color, fabric, collar) and are willing to wait 14-21 days.

Basic products (kurtas, kurta sets, bundis) will move to other channels: 50-100 TRS stores in wedding-heavy market areas at no extra cost to the company, and e-commerce/D2C — D2C already live in Q1 and starting to see traction, with marketplace agreements in final stages going live this quarter.

Full range/groom collection will be retained in high-impact flagship stores in high-impact wedding-shopping territories (e.g., Linking Road, Santa Cruz, Borivali in Mumbai), combining high-value EBO sales with higher-ROCE sales from other channels to steadily bring the brand toward profitability.

subsections.label: Marketing initiatives
points: Launched 2026 Garment Exchange Program (GEP) themed 'Refresh Your Style with Perfect Tailoring' — offers value-added tailoring services in exchange for pre-owned garments, incentivizing engagement, promoting circular fashion, and strengthening brand connection.
Premiumization should work on both ASP growth and margin growth; ASP growth without margin growth via premiumization may not be worth it.

subsections.label: Vertical integration advantage
points: Vertical integration (own fabric mill, in-house design, own garmenting, own brand understanding) helps win orders from top-end brands like Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Brooks Brothers.
Company also does B2B fabric/garmenting business for other Indian brands — could supply fabric only, garment-making only, or both, in various combinations.
Anyone with garmenting capability stands a better chance in textile/B2B fabric business, since integrated fabric+garment solution strengthens sales pitch domestically and abroad.
Garmenting tailwind does not create incremental uptrend for standalone textile business beyond this integrated-pitch advantage.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro headwinds
points: Collapse of peace talks between US and Iran pushed Brent crude back to USD100/barrel within the quarter, now settling at USD80, exerting pressure on energy costs and freight.
Anticipated Federal Reserve rate hikes contributing to significant currency volatility.
International headwinds arise without warning — a 'Truth Social message' can change the situation suddenly, making forward guidance for garmenting/export business very difficult to predict.

subsections.label: Domestic climatic and inflationary pressures
points: Persistent El Nino conditions leading to record-breaking heat waves and a potentially subpar monsoon, being monitored as a factor in discretionary spending.
RBI adjusted FY27 growth outlook down to 6.6% from 6.9% amid headwinds; CPI projections revised up to 5.1%.
Steady upward pressure on key commodities including wool and cotton, driven by supply constraints and high demand.

subsections.label: Business mix and calendar effects
points: Adhik Maas (inauspicious month) in Q1 delayed celebration/wedding dates by 20-25 days, hurting suit/blazer off-take for the formal-brand-driven Branded Apparel business in summer months.
US tariff volatility caused some old garmenting clients to shift orders to Vietnam, Cambodia, Turkey and other factories, which will take time to return.

subsections.label: Pricing guidance
points: Q1 saw largely no individual ASP hikes due to honored forward bookings; Q2 onwards company will take some price increases, calibrated based on how Q3/Q4 situation evolves.

Guidance range: apparel price hikes of 5-7%, fabric price hikes of 7-8% (fabric needs more due to higher raw-material proportion of COGS, 7-9% depending on quality; apparel 5-6% should suffice), while watching volumes since company runs its own 11 factories and needs volume for capacity utilization.

subsections.label: Garmenting margin outlook
points: No explicit guidance on EBITDA margin trajectory given international unpredictability, but endeavour is to reach double-digit EBITDA margin in garmenting, potentially faster than the previously discussed 2-year horizon if conditions stabilize.

FY24 was peak garmenting EBITDA margin at 10%; margin depends on maintaining the right product mix (suit vs shirt vs trouser) — shirts are more competitive/lower margin (casualization impact), so higher suit mix supports margin.

subsections.label: Long-term revenue/EBITDA aspiration
points: Directionally, aim (without yet having completed the Kearney India transformation/strat-plan) is to at least double the turnover in five years and grow EBITDA faster than topline, with medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin target of mid-to-high teens; potential drop-outs, mergers/acquisitions not factored into this directional statement.
Cannot give segment-wise 3-5 year revenue guidance at this stage.

subsections.label: ROCE outlook
points: Mid-teens ROCE considered a good outcome for a manufacturing-driven business as an endeavour, but explicitly not a target being chased — ROCE viewed as an output metric, not a metric to chase; near-term ROCE improvement will take time as the company remains in investment mode (new stores, new garmenting lines/factories).

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Company is ahead of its budget phasing for the year and ahead of last year; doing decent in Q2; management expects to end up having a very good year overall with H2 particularly strong on premiumization and casualization.
Garmenting order book fully booked till December provides visibility for the full year, contingent on no dramatic shifts in US-India relations or Middle East conflict.

subsections.label: ESG targets (reiterated)
points: Renewable energy target of 25% of total energy requirement by 2030, expected to be reached ahead of schedule.
Company remains fully on track to achieve target-driven 2030 ESG goals.

guidance_ledger.statement: Total income of INR1,560 crores in Q1 FY27 versus INR1,475 crores in Q1 FY26, representing a 6% year-on-year growth.
EBITDA for the quarter rose to INR135 crores, an 11% year-on-year growth, with EBITDA margin of 8.6%, a 40 bps expansion.
Prior quarter guided double-digit top-line growth for FY27 even in year of consolidation; Q1 delivered only 6% YoY total income growth.
Bottom-line should grow faster than top-line this year; Q1 EBITDA grew 11% vs 6% topline growth, consistent with this guidance.

Garmenting revenue grew 50% YoY in Q1 with EBITDA margin at 7.3% (vs -4.1% last year); order book full till December, consistent with prior guidance of high double-digit growth with EBITDA growing much faster.
Endeavour to reach double-digit EBITDA margin in garmenting (FY24 peak was 10%); may not take two years if conditions stabilize, but no formal guidance given due to international unpredictability.
Branded Apparel grew only 4% YoY in Q1 due to Adhik Maas calendar effect and EBO closures, versus prior guidance of double-digit growth outpacing GDP; management expects H2 to be very strong.

Company is ahead of its budget phasing and ahead of last year, doing decent in Q2; expects a very good year overall, contingent on no dramatic US-India or Middle East developments.

Plan to add a gross of about 100 EBO stores in FY27.
Reduced Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions 4-5% this year from FY25 baseline, on track to reduce by 15% by 2030.
CEO declined to commit to specific 3/5/10-year revenue numbers, citing early tenure (88 days); long-term strategy being built with a consultant, expected around November 2026.

key_takeaways: Total income of INR1,560 crores in Q1 FY27 versus INR1,475 crores in Q1 FY26, representing a 6% year-on-year growth.
EBITDA for the quarter rose to INR135 crores, a 11% year-on-year growth, resulting in an improved EBITDA margin of 8.6%, a 40 basis point expansion over the same period last year.

We sustained our debt-free status with a net cash surplus of INR154 crores in June '26, a marked improvement from a net debt position of INR55 crores in June '25, which is a INR209 crores swing within the year.
Net working capital days improved by 15 days, stood at 75 days in Q1 FY27 versus 90 days in Q1 FY26.
Since June 2025, we exited 133 underperforming stores and strategically opened 85 new high-yielding locations, bringing our active network to 1627 stores across 600 cities.

We have officially instituted a segment reclassification to provide complete transparency on our core operations versus growth bets... This now breaks up our portfolio into five segments: Branded Textile, Branded Apparel, Garmenting, High Value Shirting, and Emerging Business.

Garmenting Business: revenue of INR296 crores versus INR197 crores in the same quarter last year, reflecting a robust growth of 50% year-on-year... The segment achieved an EBITDA of INR22 crores versus negative INR8 crores last year same quarter, with an improved EBITDA margin of 7.3% versus minus 4.1% last year, which is a 1100 bps jump.

We have closed taking orders for December on 31st July. From 1st August, we've started booking for fourth quarter, that is January onwards, which means my garmenting capacity is full from now till December.

quarters.summary: FY26 was a "year of recovery" with highest-ever total income of INR7,034 crores (11% YoY growth) and EBITDA of INR804 crores (23% YoY growth, 11.4% margin); Q4 FY26 also delivered highest-ever quarterly total income of INR1,810 crores (15% YoY) with EBITDA up 53% YoY to INR152 crores. Management has termed FY27 the "Year of Consolidation," targeting double-digit top-line and double-digit (faster) bottom-line growth without providing formal numeric guidance, while focusing on premiumization, casualization, store rationalization (net 30-40 EBO additions), working capital improvement (<70 days NWC), and a new long-term strategy being built with an external consultant expected to conclude around November 2026.

subsections.label: Gross margin explanation
points: Decline in reported gross margin (from 54-55% range to 51-52%) attributed to a one-time INR53 crores government subsidy on the Amravati plant included in the Q4 FY25 base; excluding this, Q4 gross margin would be in the 44-45% range and FY26 gross margin at 44% shows no real drop.
EBITDA still grew because Q4 income grew 15% versus opex growth of only 1.2%; for the full year income grew 11% versus opex growth of 5%, with the gap flowing into EBITDA.

subsections.label: Opex and employee cost decline drivers
points: Factory utilizations rose from a traditional 80-85% range to above 90%, with some factories above 95%, giving scale advantages that reduced opex as a percentage of sales.

Employee cost as % of sales fell from ~15% (Q4 FY25) to ~12-13% (Q4 FY26) due to: (1) higher factory throughput reducing employee cost per unit; (2) lower garmenting utilization and variable labour costs in the prior-year base when US orders were down; (3) closure of loss-making stores reducing both employee cost and losses, creating a positive delta on both fronts.
Management stated opex reduction should be sustainable if turnover this year is higher than last year, since factories should continue running at the elevated pace.

subsections.label: Working capital and cash generation
points: NWC improved from 87 days to 77 days (10-day improvement) versus last March, reflecting efficiency gains.
CFO plans to target under 70 days of working capital in the next financial year, with levers including reviews to clamp down on overdue debtor outstandings and further inventory management work.
Management targets an additional 8-9 days reduction in working capital next year.

subsections.label: Capex breakdown
points: Of the INR180 crores FY26 capex, INR50 crores was for SAP (S/4HANA) implementation, INR60 crores for the new garmenting factory in Hyderabad, and the balance for new stores and plant maintenance capex.
Capex for next year (FY27) expected to remain broadly similar to FY26.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / shareholding
points: Raymond Limited has bought around 4.85% of Raymond Lifestyle's stock; rationale and future intentions were deferred to Group CFO Rakesh Tiwary to address in a subsequent call.

subsections.label: Branded Textile segment
points: Revenue growth driven by robust volume growth and premiumization.
EBITDA growth driven by improved product mix, strong volume, ASP growth, and scale leverage.

Business is India's core cash cow; expected to grow in low-to-medium single digit range in volume terms, with value growth targeted higher than volume via premiumization; casualization (suits to jackets, corduroy, blended materials) is also a lever.

Growth strategy includes moving from Tier-1 cities to next layer of cities, servicing top-end boutique/bespoke tailoring demand (designer shops proliferating in cities like Bombay and Delhi), ramping up an ecosystem supporting tailors (akin to salon-industry support models), and building a profitable fabric export business (leveraging garmenting expertise) alongside domestic growth.

subsections.label: Branded Apparel segment
points: Current reported Branded Apparel segment numbers include emerging/new businesses; management to begin separately reporting core four marquee brands (Park Avenue, ColorPlus, Raymond Ready-to-Wear, Parx) versus emerging businesses starting next quarter.
Core four brands EBITDA margin of 7.8% targeted to reach double digits over the next two years.
Witnessed double-digit like-for-like growth in retail channels of the segment.

Emerging/new businesses currently in a strategic investment phase, contributing INR140 crores of revenue but INR30 crores of losses in FY26; excluding this turnover/losses, the four core brands' margin would look better (7.5-8%).

Growth strategy: premiumization and casualization; ColorPlus positioned as primary casual brand leading casualization drive, with Park Avenue, Raymond Ready-to-Wear and Parx providing secondary casual support; product mix shifting to smart casuals, polos, chinos, t-shirts, corduroy, denim.

Casual portfolio currently ~15% of Park Avenue and Raymond Ready-to-Wear revenue (up from 10% a year ago), targeted to reach 20-25% and eventually ~45% over time without abandoning the formal segment.
Special formal products like non-iron shirts being developed to benefit from K-shaped recovery.
Design system being digitized with AI-driven design capabilities to shorten supply chain and turnaround time and improve design quality via web crawling of global best practices.
Distribution to become more calibrated: stores concentrated in higher town classes, closing underperforming stores.

subsections.label: Garmenting segment
points: Demand recovery seen post US-India trade deal, leading to highest-ever monthly revenue in March.
Implemented duty-paid terms for US clients, which helped retain clients through the year, expected to benefit going into next year.
Business expected to accelerate next year aided by UK and Euro FTAs and the US-India trade deal.

Reduced US dependency from 65-67% level; expanding geographic base to Europe/UK given improved FTA access and better relative freight economics versus US (freight from Indian ports to European ports reportedly declined last month while freight to American ports rose amid West Asia conflict).
US orders are returning even as Europe orders grow incrementally, improving the overall margin mix; top-line expected to grow high double digits with bottom-line growing faster.
Order books described as solid: Q1 FY27 order books fully booked, and booking underway for latter half of Q2 FY27.

US customer inventory pipelines described as decent since importers held onto stock amid tariff-driven price increases; Europe market not great overall but premium segment (where company operates) unaffected, consistent with a K-shaped recovery pattern seen since COVID.
Company noted it is among the best organizations globally for suit-making, supplying to major global brands (unnamed) and stated it will double down on Europe and UK for garmenting business growth.

subsections.label: High value cotton shirting (B2B)
points: Q4 FY25 EBITDA of INR61 crores included a one-time government subsidy of INR53 crores for the Amravati plant, inflating the prior-year base; excluding that, the segment performed better than last year's same quarter.

subsections.label: Sleepwear business discontinuation
points: Company is stopping the sleepwear segment; annual EBITDA drag from this segment was about INR20 crores, expected to be recovered going forward, though provisions were taken this year reflected in the reported numbers.

subsections.label: Home business and innerwear
points: Home business turned EBITDA neutral last year and is expected to generate some profit this year.

Innerwear business (Park Avenue) has strong products management believes are competitive with the market leader; this year will focus on consolidation and system cleanup, with profitability targeted as an add-on to the apparel business within the next two years.

subsections.label: Raymond Ethnix (ethnic wear)
points: Competitive intensity has increased sharply post the success of Manyavar, with many regional/local players emerging especially in markets like UP and Bihar; growth for larger organized brands may have slowed as a result.

Category requires regional customization (Bengali, Punjabi, Tamil, Maharashtrian wedding styles differ significantly), making it difficult for a national brand to replicate a single design nationally.

Strategic recalibration this year: rather than targeting the bridegroom's main outfit, Ethnix will focus on products for people around the bridegroom (kurtas, bandis/Modi jackets) which have lighter structure but higher volume potential, distributed through both Ethnix stores and The Raymond Shop (TRS) network.
Plans to also enter Indo-Western wear (e.g., bandhgala jackets), leveraging the company's strong suit-making design/production capabilities.
AI-based design tools are planned as a future tool to attack the bridegroom segment directly, likely after the year of consolidation.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization gains
points: Factory utilizations rose from a traditional 80-85% range to above 90%, with some factories operating above 95%, driving scale advantages and opex reduction flowing into EBITDA.
New garmenting factory being set up in Hyderabad as part of FY26 capex plan.

key_figures.label: Revised GDP growth estimates (post recent volatility)

subsections.label: Garmenting geographic diversification
points: Historically ~65-67% of garmenting business was US-dependent, creating vulnerability to tariff-related disruptions; company scouted diversification into strong Asian markets as well as European and UK markets.
UK-India FTA announced and Euro-India FTA also announced (though not yet implemented), driving increased interest from these regions.

Freight costs from Indian ports (e.g., Nhava Sheva) to European ports have reportedly declined recently even as freight to American ports rose amid West Asia conflict, making Europe attractive from both a freight and margin perspective.
US orders are returning, and management expects the geographic mix to shift with incremental orders from Europe, improving overall margin structure in garmenting.

subsections.label: Domestic macro environment
points: India remains a relative bright spot with GDP estimates around 6.8-7.2%, though global headwinds (US-Iran conflict, elevated Brent crude prices above $100, rising energy/raw material/freight costs) persist.
Domestically, extreme heat waves affecting multiple states and a below-average monsoon forecast (92% of normal) may impact discretionary spending.

Stock market volatility linked to West Asia conflict is causing affluent consumers to feel a 'paper money' wealth effect, tempering conspicuous consumption; GDP growth projections have been revised down from high-7% levels toward 6.6-6.8%.

subsections.label: Marketing strategy revamp
points: New CMO Kalpana Singh joined in March from HUL; to be introduced to investors next quarter.

Strategy is to move from fragmented marketing to a connected omnichannel system across the full consumer journey, with each brand (Park Avenue, Raymond Ready-to-Wear, Raymond MTM, ColorPlus) to be positioned and recognized distinctly.
Increased presence in high-impact media like cricket and cinema, including a cinema campaign tie-up with Dhurandhar 2; building digital and influencer ecosystem.
Raymond Linen has been advertised heavily this year and is performing well.
FY27 plans include holistic marketing campaigns: sharper brand positioning per brand, differentiated communication, prudent media selection, and last-mile activities to drive footfall in EBOs.

subsections.label: Channel economics
points: EBO is the most profitable channel (D2C), followed by MBO (distributor-led), then LFS (large format stores, akin to modern trade, where retailers negotiate but provide brand visibility/scale, e.g., large in-store displays at Shoppers Stop/Lifestyle/Reliance stores).
No formal revenue split targets provided across channels, but EBO is expected to remain the largest channel, followed by MBO, then LFS; e-commerce also forms part of the channel mix.

GTM expansion planned in MBOs and large format stores (LFS), particularly for casual products; apparel already performing well in LFS with SSPD comparable to top category brands, and company is the top brand in some LFS.

subsections.label: Branded Apparel growth sustainability
points: Management expects Branded Apparel growth to remain directionally strong despite near-term consumer sentiment softness linked to West Asia conflict and stock market volatility denting affluent-class discretionary spending; smaller discretionary price points historically bounce back well in downturns.

India's urbanization and forward economic movement support continued category growth; company (not a market leader in Branded Apparel) aims to grow faster than GDP growth, targeting double-digit growth.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Raymond viewed by management as a top-10 recognizable Indian brand.
In Ethnix/ethnic wear, competitive intensity has risen due to entrants inspired by Manyavar's success, especially regional players in markets like UP and Bihar.

subsections.label: Leadership transition
points: New leadership team appointed during the quarter: Satyaki Ghosh as CEO (joined with ~30 years FMCG experience across GE, PepsiCo, L'Oreal, Spencer's Retail/RPG, Aditya Birla Group), Rakesh Tiwary as Group CFO, E.C. Prasad as Lifestyle CFO (joined ~3 months back, prior CFO at Bajaj Electricals, also worked at Voltas and Emami), and Kalpana Singh as new CMO (joined March from HUL).
Company is also on the lookout for a new CIO, expected to be announced next quarter.
New leadership expected to bring renewed focus on expanding Branded Apparel, scaling newer categories, and driving operational efficiencies across the value chain.

subsections.label: FY27 - 'Year of Consolidation'
points: Company designates FY27 as the 'Year of Consolidation,' shifting focus to restoring sustainable profitability through a lean, high-performing network, rather than aggressive expansion.

Store network plan: gross addition of ~100 EBO stores in FY27, with continued exit of underperforming stores; net increase expected to be 30-40 stores (some commentary also cites gross open >100, closures of 50-60, net addition ~40, ending FY27 network around 1,700 stores from ~1,650-1,653 currently).
Aggressive store expansion decision to be reconsidered next year depending on this year's consolidation results.

Company has engaged a large consultancy firm to build a three-year strategy; the engagement has been awarded, with strategy work to start once cost negotiation is finalized (expected start ~20-25 May or by 1 June), a ~12-14 week strategy project plus ~2 weeks presentation (~16 weeks total), targeting a plan by around November 2026 with execution starting around Q3 FY27.
Digital transformation: S/4HANA (SAP) implementation completed in the textile and home part of the business, intended to modernize supply chain and enhance operational agility.

subsections.label: Raymond Limited stake purchase
points: Raymond Limited has purchased ~4.85% of Raymond Lifestyle's stock; rationale and future plans to be addressed by Group CFO Rakesh Tiwary in a future call.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical risks
points: US-Iran conflict keeping Brent crude prices above $100, leading to increased energy, raw material, and freight costs.
Extreme heat waves affecting multiple Indian states and a below-average monsoon forecast (92%) may impact discretionary spending domestically.

West Asia conflict and stock market volatility are causing affluent consumers to pull back on conspicuous consumption due to a wealth-effect perception, even though management does not believe they are losing actual money.
Downward revisions in India GDP growth estimates (from high-7% range toward 6.6-6.8%) linked to this volatility.
Risk that US could reimpose tariffs (e.g., another 30-40% tariff 'under some other pretext') which could disrupt garmenting order book strength.

subsections.label: Raw material cost risks
points: Merino wool prices are rising sharply; flax (linen raw material, sourced mainly from Europe) prices are also increasing, creating a headwind to gross margin gains from premiumization even as premium mix should directionally support margins.
Flax is a once-a-year crop, currently in the fields (harvested in September); this year's crop currently looks good, but pricing remains elevated.

subsections.label: Supply chain / logistics observations
points: No major disruption yet seen in raw material sourcing (wool from Australia, minimal disturbance; freight largely stable) or export shipping timelines due to the US-Israel-Iran conflict, as of the call date.
Freight between India and Europe (for flax/linen) reported slightly better in April versus March.
Reports of steps toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz noted as a positive development being watched.

subsections.label: Competitive risk in Ethnix
points: Rising competitive intensity in ethnic wear from regional/local players (especially in UP, Bihar) following Manyavar's success, potentially slowing growth for organized/national brands in that category.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: FY27 designated the 'Year of Consolidation,' shifting focus from recovery to restoring sustainable, profitable growth via a lean, high-performing network.
Management targets double-digit top-line growth and double-digit bottom-line growth for FY27, with bottom-line expected to grow faster than top-line; explicit numeric EBITDA guidance not provided.

Net store additions targeted at 30-40 for FY27 (gross additions >100, closures ~50-60), taking the network to around 1,700 stores by year-end from ~1,650-1,653 currently; network not expected to dip below current level.
Aggressive store expansion strategy to be considered in the following year depending on FY27 consolidation results.
Working capital target of under 70 days for FY27, an incremental improvement of about 8-9 days versus FY26's 77 days.

Garmenting business expected to perform much better next year, supported by returning US orders and growing Europe/UK business under FTAs; Q1 FY27 order books already fully booked and H2 Q2 booking underway.
Branded Apparel segment expected to sustain double-digit growth, expected to outpace GDP growth given the company is not the market leader in that segment.
Core four apparel brands' EBITDA margin (7.8%) targeted to reach double digits over the next two years.

Long-term (3-year) strategy being developed with a newly appointed consultancy; plan expected around November 2026 with execution starting around Q3 FY27; no specific 3/5/10-year revenue targets given yet as CEO stated it is too early in his tenure (88 days) to commit to such numbers.

ESG targets: renewable energy share to rise 5-6% this year from FY25 baseline, on track for 25% of total energy requirement by 2030; Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions reduced 4-5% this year from FY25 baseline, on track for 15% reduction by 2030; 40% female representation target by 2030.
Innerwear business expected to become a profitable add-on to the apparel business within the next two years.
Home business expected to generate some profit this year, having turned EBITDA neutral last year.

key_takeaways: For the first time in our history, we crossed the INR7,000 crores mark, recording our highest-ever total income of INR7,034 crores and 11% year-on-year growth.
EBITDA for the year rose to INR804 crores with a 23% year-on-year growth, with an EBITDA margin of 11.4%.
We remain debt-free with a net cash surplus of INR179 crores. Net working capital improved significantly over last March and has come down by 10 days from 87 days to 77 days.
We recorded our highest-ever Q4 total income of INR1,810 crores, a 15% year-on-year growth. EBITDA for the quarter rose by 53% to INR152 crores.
Our EBITDA margin improved by 210 basis points Q-o-Q to 8.4%, and we created robust cash flows and we generated close to INR200 crores of net cash during this quarter.

In our Branded Textile segment, revenue grew 14% to INR831 crores in Q4, driven by robust volume growth and premiumization. EBITDA for the segment grew by 126% to INR115 crores on account of improved product mix, strong volume, ASP growth, and scale leverage.

As we enter FY '27, we would like to call this the Year of Consolidation. We plan to add a gross of about 100 EBO stores in FY '27; however, we will continue to exit underperforming stores during the year and we think the net increase would be 30 to 40 this year.
We are not giving a guidance at this stage; however, our idea is even in the year of consolidation to keep a double-digit top-line growth and a double-digit bottom-line growth.

So, my question is regarding the Branded Textile segment, which is the cash cow for the company. So, if I look at the numbers from FY '23 to '26 over the last four years, revenue has barely gone up and profitability has declined... how should we look at this segment going forward?

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) marks SBI Funds Management's first earnings call post-listing. Management flagged a silent period post-result-declaration and declined to give specific forward guidance on QAAUM growth, opex, or ESOP costs, but highlighted continued momentum in SIP flows, AUM growth, alternate business scale-up, cost discipline, and product pipeline expansion (SIF, PMS, AIF, hybrid, passive) as drivers of future outlook.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margins across equity, debt, liquid, and passive strategies remained stable during the quarter, while net margins improved at overall level despite the regulatory change around transition to base expense ratio and removal of exit load structure.
Margin improvement is not linked to TER reduction; the reduction impact has been passed on to distributors in a calibrated manner, keeping the company net neutral to slightly positive.

Margin increase is attributed to asset mix — concentration on low-yielding passive assets has come down by default, replaced by high-yielding equity and hybrid funds, increasing yield by two basis points on total stock basis.
Movement of assets from liquid (low yield) into arbitrage funds (higher yield) is a similar mix-driven margin lever.
Significant growth in gold and silver ETF, a high-margin product within the ETF category despite being classified as ETF.

subsections.label: Cost management
points: Company has demonstrated strong cost management on both Q-o-Q and Y-o-Y basis, attributed to ability to scale business while managing cost of operations and optimizing distribution and other models, resulting in a tight operating ratio.
Major cost reduction driver is the digital transaction model — 94% of transactions are processed digitally, reducing costs through digitization of processes.

Opex will remain focused on technology and human resources — quality of manpower, fund managers, and people, along with technology upgradation in AI and digital areas; no specific guidance given due to silent period.
Employee expense YoY drop of 1% in Q1 attributed to new labour code implementation adjustments; no changes to employee benefits; training expenses expected to come in Q2/Q3.

subsections.label: Other income
points: Dip in other income compared to last year attributed to mark-to-market impact on the company's investment portfolio, which impacted last quarter's book, making other income a little muted; last year also had some mark-to-market impact on the portfolio.

subsections.label: Dividend policy
points: Company paid a special dividend last year; a new dividend policy has now been created and uploaded publicly; future payments will depend on final board and AGM approvals.

subsections.label: ESOP
points: Company has a board-approved ESOP policy followed every year, internal to the organization, in line with industry and SEBI guidelines; details on FY27 ESOP cost not disclosed in this forum.

SBI channel contribution to active equity AUM

subsections.label: AUM leadership and growth drivers
points: Active QAAUM growth of 10% YoY and 21% three-year CAGR supported by consistent performance and healthy flows.
Passive QAAUM growth of 12% YoY reinforcing leadership in the segment.

Alternate business (PMS, advisory, offshore, AIF) continues to scale; AIF grown from ₹5,300 crores to ₹6,800 crores in the last one year — early days of the alternates journey, ambition to grow significantly; company has started hiring resources and will launch one more product this quarter in this category.

subsections.label: Distribution mix (SBI vs Direct/Other)
points: On active equity AUM, SBI contributes about 35% (retail part adjusted for passives and institutional money); on overall AUM basis, SBI's distribution contribution is about 20%.

On SIP flows, the split mirrors the equity AUM split: roughly one-third (33%, ~₹1,300 crores) from SBI channel and two-thirds (~₹2,700 crores) from other channels and direct business; management's endeavour is to maintain this ~35%/65% ratio going forward by leveraging digital tools and delivery.

subsections.label: Revenue mix between mutual fund and alternates
points: Almost 90-92% of operating revenue comes from mutual fund business; PMS, advisory and international contribute remaining ~8%; endeavour is to increase both sides, with mutual fund topline high but low remunerative, and alternates (AIF/PMS) offering higher revenue potential going forward.
AIF and PMS business is more margin accretive than equity — more selective, regulations comparatively easier, done in partnership spirit, considered more attractive than equity margins.

subsections.label: SIP trend commentary
points: SIP flow slightly flattish quarter-on-quarter because of market volatility and geopolitical conditions, but flow maintained; fresh SIP additions of 1.7 million and live SIPs at 16 million viewed as very strong numbers giving confidence in the SIP growth story.

Flow share continues to be in double digits, benefiting from the company's positioning as 'house of hybrids' — in volatile times hybrid funds get higher share; flow market share and AUM market share described as aligned, around 11-12% for equity and hybrid, varying by category.

subsections.label: AI and digital initiatives
points: AI and technology initiatives have continued to improve customer experience, productivity, strengthen distributor enablement, and enhance investment management capabilities.
For investors, AI-driven tools offer personalized nudges, easier on-boarding, and intuitive digital journeys.
After the success of AI in the InvesTap Nxt mobile app, about 50,000 distributors now use the partner app and portal for advanced analytics, real-time reporting, and customer insights.
Around 94% of investor transactions are processed digitally through the company's secure hybrid cloud infrastructure.
Company is enhancing its in-house research platform, Neo, by integrating AI capabilities to strengthen investment management and performance workflows.

subsections.label: New product launches
points: Robust product pipelines across Mutual Fund, SIF, PMS, and AIF with strong focus on differentiated investor-centric solutions.
Strengthening SIF offering — second strategy to launch this quarter, positioned in the Ex-Top 100 long-short category.
Last quarter, company introduced six new strategies; currently has an NFO underway — SBI Nifty Midcap 150 Momentum 50 ETF FOF.
Launching the SBI Balanced Hybrid Fund to complete the hybrid suite.

Continued enhancement of product platform across active, passive, and alternate strategies with meaningful progress in AIF, PMS, and SIF capabilities, alongside steady expansion of international business through Gift City and offshore mandates.

subsections.label: Distribution franchise depth
points: Distribution franchise continues to be deepened, supported by over 23,000+ SBI branches, over 124,000 independent financial advisors, nearly 10,000 national distributors, and over 90 banking partners including State Bank of India, enabling reach at over 98% pin codes across the country.

Company remains market leader in B30 locations with MAAUM market share of 19% (later cited as 25%+ market share by MD); strong presence in Tier-2/Tier-3 markets reflected in robust B30 market share, with nearly 65% of SIP contribution originating from these markets despite contributing 44% of AUM by amount, underscoring deepening penetration.
New customer addition is also majorly from B30 markets.

subsections.label: SBI/YONO channel penetration
points: SBI is the largest distribution franchise; via YONO, reach extends to around 12 crore customers who regularly engage with the platform.

NISM certified bank employees have gone up to 15,700; company available at 98.2% pin codes through SBI's franchise; SBI has been supporting distribution network reach, especially in Tier-2/Tier-3 cities where market share is strong.

Company has been involved with YONO since the YONO 2.0 launch around December-January 2026; mutual fund folios, transactions, and SIP creation are now directly accessible/creatable via YONO with two-way compatibility; around 2.5 lakh YONO users applied through the platform directly during the recent IPO in addition to other channels; YONO is expected to be enlarged further with the upcoming KYC 2.0.

subsections.label: B30 strategy
points: Leadership in B30 attributed to SBI's distribution network which is predominantly present in B30 locations; company has also enlarged its mutual fund distributor network to B30 cities and is engaging with other agencies for investor awareness as part of a long-term strategy around SIPs, mutual funds, and investments in these locations.

subsections.label: Macro and industry backdrop
points: Quarter characterized by steady domestic economic momentum, healthy corporate earnings, and constructive equity market conditions, even as global markets witnessed intermittent volatility in interest rates, liquidity, and commodities.
Indian household savings continued their structural shift towards financial assets, supporting stable participation across investment categories.
Industry mutual fund QAAUM grew around 15% YoY and remained broadly stable sequentially, driven by market strength and sustained retail flows.
Equity-oriented assets saw strong YoY expansion with notable outperformance in small and mid-cap segments, while large-cap delivered more moderate gains.
Monthly SIP inflows industry-wide remained resilient at over ₹31,000 crores, signalling durable investor behaviour through market cycles.

Debt assets moderated due to institutional redemption patterns and tight short-term liquidity, while passive products (ETFs and index funds) continued to expand meaningfully among institutional and retail investors.
Overall industry flows remained constructive despite short-term volatility across categories.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: B30 market remains underpenetrated and competition has been chasing market share in these locations; company maintains leadership via SBI's distribution network, expanded mutual fund distributor network in B30, and investor awareness initiatives.

SEBI's proposed entry of PMS through mutual fund route (for INR 25 lakh ticket size) viewed very positively by management — expected to increase number of players; company expects to be one of the leaders in this category and wants to scale it up significantly, citing dual benefit of launching PMS products with mutual funds embedded and expecting PMS products from others to include the company's mutual funds in their portfolios.

subsections.label: Strategic pillars
points: Strategy guided by four core pillars: democratizing wealth creation, accelerating digital delivery, strengthening investor performance, and building new growth engines.
Company remains committed to delivering consistent outcomes for investors, deepening industry leadership, and building a resilient, technology-led, future-ready asset management franchise.

subsections.label: IPO and listing
points: This is the company's first earnings call following its listing, described as a significant moment; management thanked investors for participation in the IPO and for trust placed in the organization.
Company committed to continued transparency, disciplined execution, and regular engagement with stakeholders following listing.

subsections.label: Alternates business build-out
points: Alternate business is a very large focus area; company has huge ambition plans to grow this business, has started hiring resources, and will launch one more product in this category this quarter.

subsections.label: Regulatory changes
points: Regulatory change around transition to base expense ratio and removal of exit load structure required prudent management to preserve long-term margin resilience; company navigated this TER reduction efficiently — majority of the reduction was passed on to distributors in a calibrated manner from April itself, resulting in a net neutral to slightly positive impact rather than a negative one; confident this will continue as majority (70-80%) of business involves distribution channels getting a percentage of TER that moves dynamically with any increase or decrease.

subsections.label: Market volatility
points: Global markets witnessed intermittent volatility in interest rates, liquidity, and commodities during the quarter.
SIP flow was slightly flattish quarter-on-quarter due to market volatility and geopolitical conditions, though flow was still maintained.
Debt assets moderated industry-wide due to institutional redemption patterns and tight short-term liquidity.

subsections.label: Other income volatility
points: Dip in other income compared to last year attributed to mark-to-market impact on the company's investment portfolio, which impacted the last quarter's book.

subsections.label: Silent period constraints
points: Management repeatedly declined to give specific forward guidance (on QAAUM growth for the year, opex, ESOP costs for FY27) citing that results were declared today and the company is in a silent period.
Management pointed to historical trends (e.g., 17% YoY growth in operating profit) as reference points rather than providing explicit guidance.
Opex is expected to remain focused on technology and human resources — quality of manpower, fund managers, people, and technology upgradation in AI/digital areas, without specific numerical guidance.
Distribution mix endeavour is to maintain roughly one-third from SBI channel and two-thirds from other/direct channels going forward, using digital tools and delivery.
Endeavour to increase the revenue contribution from PMS/AIF/international business by focusing on high-revenue AIF and PMS products going forward.
Company is very bullish on SEBI's proposed PMS-via-mutual-fund framework and wants to scale that opportunity up in a big way.
Dividend payments will continue as per the newly created and published dividend policy, subject to board and AGM approvals.

guidance_ledger.statement: Management declined to project QAAUM growth for the year, citing silent period post-results.

Opex will be mostly focused on technology and human resources — quality of manpower, fund managers, people, along with technology upgradation in AI, digital and other areas; no numerical guidance given due to silent period.
Management declined to disclose ESOP cost details for FY27, citing board-approved policy followed internally; offered to discuss one-to-one but not in this forum.
Endeavour is to maintain the equivalent split of ~35% from SBI channel and ~65% from direct and other channel by using digital tools and digital delivery going forward.
Endeavour is to increase the revenue contribution from PMS, advisory and international business by getting into high-revenue AIF and PMS products going forward, from current ~8% share.
Company has huge ambition plans to grow the alternate business significantly, has started hiring resources, and will launch one more product in this category this quarter.
Company is very bullish about SEBI's proposed PMS through mutual fund route for INR 25 lakh ticket size and wants to scale it up in a big way, expecting to be one of the leaders in this category.
Company will continue to pay dividends as per its newly created and published dividend policy, depending on final board and AGM approvals.
Company will continue to improve its cost-to-income ratio.
Company is confident it will continue to remain net neutral or positive on TER reduction impact even as it grows further, as majority (70-80%) of distribution channel business shares TER dynamically.
