MSUMI.about: Motherson Sumi Wiring India, a JV between Sumitomo Wiring System and Motherson Group, is a market leader in the Indian wiring harness industry with a market share of over 40%.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 6.3% YoY to Rs.358 crores, below Aurionpro's normal growth/profitability trajectory due to continuing MEA disruption, project go-live timing shifts, data center milestone timing, supply chain pressures and capacity deployed to AI-native stack build-out. Management expects improving execution and acceleration through the year, especially H2, driven by data center ramp-up, transit wins and banking product build-outs, but declined to give formal FY27 revenue or margin guidance citing ongoing uncertainty, particularly around the Middle East.

key_figures.label: Q1 revenue vs historical company size
Sequential growth from Q1 to Q1
Data center as share of TIG business

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margin drop is purely a function of revenue, business mix, and the amount of capacity going into converting the order book to revenue.
A chunk of actual product R&D goes in as expenses, temporarily showing a lower EBITDA number than if capacity were purely used on delivering revenue.
Banking margins expected to remain fairly strong in the longer run despite the temporary drag from build-outs.

As the software business becomes larger and more global over the next 3-5 years, operating leverage will kick in and incremental investment needed to enter new markets will come down, making banking margins healthier over time.

Data center business remains four or five points below enterprise margin levels and will stay so for some time, but will more than make up for it with volume; this is a multi-year play rather than a change over a few quarters.
As more IP and products are introduced into the data center business (like was done in transit), margins will slowly improve.
R&D expense would more or less remain at a similar number for FY27 (10.5-11%), with some R&D projects reaching natural end-of-life which may reduce this a little after half of the year.

Cost was taken upfront in Q1 for the data center business to build capacity in advance of demand, since visibility into the pipeline supports it; this cost has already been reflected in the cost structure but is expected to pay for itself.
Employee costs have almost doubled over the past 5-6 quarters.

subsections.label: Cash conversion focus
points: Extreme focus this year on both conversion of order book to revenue and conversion of revenue/EBITDA to cash, targeting 60-70% EBITDA-to-cash conversion for FY27.
A big historical deployment of cash was acquisitions; company does not plan any meaningful acquisition for the next few quarters, freeing up cash demand.
No meaningful increase planned in R&D expense, which should also reduce pressure on cash as business gets larger.

Typically at the end of H1, company has negative OCF purely due to payment cycles; management would not commit to a positive OCF at end of H1 this year but expects to be in good shape in H1 and accelerate through H2.

Project cycles typically convert to cash over a roughly 12-month cycle; management declined to set a specific expectation on H1 OCF turning positive or achieving the 60-70% EBITDA-to-cash conversion target.

subsections.label: Historical growth trajectory context
points: Management disputes the framing that top-line has been 'stuck' in a range; cites organization has progressively grown from a Rs.400-500 crore company to current size over successive years, not stuck in any particular quarter or year.
Q1 size this year (Rs.358 crores) equates to what the size of Aurionpro used to be four to five years back (FY21 full-year revenue was Rs.375 crores), reflecting the scale of growth over that period.
Sequential growth from Q1 to Q1 this year is stronger than in most previous years.
Company acknowledges being below its longer-term trend line (historically ~20% margin range) currently and will find a path back to it.
Data center business targeted to grow higher than 40-50%, potentially 50-100%, in FY27, and expected to become higher than a third of TIG business.
Transit growth targeted north of 30% for FY27; banking growth has been 20-25% over the last couple of years.

subsections.label: Order book and pipeline strength
points: Not a demand issue — order book is strong, pipeline is healthy, engagement is improving.
Priority is converting demand into go-lives and revenue.
Conversion improved from Q4 and sequential growth was stronger than in the last few Q1s.
Order book is a necessary but not sufficient condition for revenue — projects must be executed to convert order book into revenue.

Very large deals have longer conversion cycles versus typical 12-month projects; larger data center deal sizes (now much larger than three-four quarters back) require capacity buildup that is not instantaneous.
Capacity buildup expected to normalize by end of Q2 or early Q3 for data center-related conversion.
Banking order book conversion slowdown is more temporary and tied to capacity diverted to product build-outs, expected to normalize over the next quarter or two.
Pipeline described as the busiest management has ever seen, though no specific deals to be named before closing.
Deal activity improving, execution gathering pace; order book gives confidence that momentum will build with meaningful acceleration in H2.

key_figures.label: Data center as share of TIG business
key_figures.value: roughly a third currently, expected to reach ~40%

key_figures.label: TIG as share of enterprise business
Data center deal size referenced by analyst
Product win rates in transaction banking / transit

subsections.label: Banking & FinTech
points: Banking and FinTech revenue grew about 5% YoY to Rs.200+ crores in Q1 FY27.
Won a large transaction banking mandate, rare for Q1.

$33 million fintech deal already contributing to revenue but ramp-up is gradual, not a sudden jump; management clarified there is no pass-through revenue in this deal — all of it is company capacity delivering.

Significant capacity currently diverted to build out AI-native banking product stack (banking software 2.0) across trade finance and other products, temporarily reducing capacity available for revenue-generating delivery.

Banking software 2.0 must do everything software 1.0 did, plus provide agents/rails/tools for AI agents to be first-class operators on banking workflow, and provide banks/human operators tools to govern these agents.
Product build-outs are expected to normalize over the next quarter or two, freeing capacity back to revenue conversion.
Multiple product launches already announced; more expected in coming quarters, some receiving exceptional feedback even in newer markets like Europe; analyst recognitions expected to be announced.
Transaction banking stack win rates north of 50% in markets where present, sustained over the last two-three years.
Transaction banking has significant headroom in Southeast Asia and MEA; traction building in Southeast Asia and Europe.
Arya.AI seeing strong demand across banking and insurance as customers move from experimentation to production.
Current banking/TIG revenue mix is roughly 55-45 or 56-44; expected FY27 mix is a few points above 50% for banking and a few points below 50% for TIG.

subsections.label: TIG (Transit & Infrastructure Group) / Data Center
points: TIG revenue was Rs.157 crores in Q1 FY27, up 8.4% YoY, but saw sequential decline attributed to the large data center deal not yet translating to revenue given various non-immediate-revenue components; ramp-up expected over next few months.
Q2 will see a pickup in TIG/data center, with a much more significant pickup in Q3 and Q4.

Data center business at an inflection point; as capacity comes online and secured mandates convert into revenue, conversion should accelerate through the year, moving growth above the recent 40-50% trajectory into a higher band (potentially 50-100% for FY27).
Data center pipeline described as very, very large; it's a question of choosing the right mix of deals to execute.
Company quickly established itself as a strong full-stack partner in the data center space to serious hyperscale players with very large investment plans.
Capacity built in advance for data center execution, reflecting in current cost structure but expected to pay for itself.
Data center could become ~40% of TIG business (from roughly a third currently) by year end.
TIG represents about 45% of enterprise business currently.

Analyst noted growth this year appears largely dependent on a data center deal referenced at approximately Rs.350 crores; management disputed this, stating data center will contribute from more than just that deal, and transit, banking, and AI businesses will also grow, though multi-year execution means only part of the large deal converts this year.
New customer logos added: 23 in Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Transit
points: Transit demonstrates strength of full-stack model; secured mandates from Mumbai Metro and Delhi Metro, and other successes across the transit portfolio.
These wins deepen India leadership as well as global play as international pipeline expands.
Transit business took five to six years to build IP across every point of the value chain, now making it a powerful competitor.
Transit product win rates north of 50% over the last 2-3 years.

subsections.label: AI-native technology strategy
points: Enterprise software entering its most consequential architectural shift since the cloud; next generation will reason over context, coordinate work through agents, and act in real time.
In mission-critical industries served by Aurionpro, software must evolve around trusted data, domain intelligence, security and accountability.
AI will make domain depth more valuable as systems of record become systems of intelligence and action.
Winning requires production-grade software, proprietary intelligence, implementation capability and trust — the stack being built through AurionAI, Arya.AI, and Lexi Labs.
Completing key build-outs across AI-native banking portfolio, beginning with trade finance already announced; this absorbs capacity today but creates a reusable platform over time.
As build-outs mature, capacity will shift towards implementation, accelerating revenue conversion for the banking business.
AI is creating a new infrastructure super cycle in India; company intends to be foundational to it.

AI-driven tool sets are boosting productivity of consultants/developers; this productivity uptick is expected to make up for not adding proportional staff, though a temporary effect may be seen over a few quarters as the organization adjusts.

Company's point of view: banking software 2.0 must extend software 1.0's functions to include providing agents/rails/tools for AI agents to act as first-class operators, plus governance tools for banks/human operators to oversee these agents.

key_figures.label: Middle East contribution to revenue (last year)

subsections.label: Geographic diversification
points: Expanded demand generation in the United States, Southeast Asia, and Europe, as previously indicated at the end of Q4.
Secured largest ever order in the United States.
Escalated sales push into newer markets for both transit and banking.
Refocusing banking segment away from MEA into Southeast Asia and Europe; expects to see wins in these regions this year.
Southeast Asia is a strong base for the lending solution set, being expanded to include the transaction banking stack.
Expanding into Europe in a meaningful way.
Some new product feedback received from newer markets not previously present, such as Europe.
Last year, company got double-digit percentage of revenue from Middle East and expected significant contribution to growth, which came down to zero this year.

MEA deals are progressing more than in Q4, but have not been able to close deals to the same extent; management expects to potentially announce Middle East wins in the next quarter or two but cannot predict timing confidently.
No year-on-year comparison impact of Middle East expected after Q3 since the comp base goes away, irrespective of whether the situation itself normalizes.
Stronger geographic balance versus last year; differentiated IP and a healthy pipeline.

subsections.label: Strategic focus and portfolio approach
points: Company organized as a fairly decentralized group of probably 13-14 P&Ls, most product P&Ls, some services P&Ls, each aiming to become a top-three global player in its focus area.
Strategic bets selected at intersection of three factors: long demand runway, contested (not winner-take-all) global leadership space, and Aurionpro's unique advantage to build tier-one IP/assets.
Ambition (stated five years back and unchanged) is to become a top-three global player in data center, transit, banking software, and AI segments.

Directional 2030 value potential disclosed as a wide range (~$560 million to $1.7 billion), derived from named-account/dollar/geography-specific SAM (serviceable addressable market) rather than a broad TAM, with an obtainable market share estimate of 5-15% of SAM.

In practice, once products are built and competing, actual market share won tends to be higher than conservative estimates, with win rates upwards of 50% on many products (e.g., transaction banking, transit).
No significant M&A planned for the next few quarters (previously a major cash use over the last two-three years via multiple acquisitions).
Management to consider internally whether to begin disclosing data center revenue at a sub-segment level in investor materials, given growing investor interest.

subsections.label: Key headwinds
points: Continuing MEA (Middle East) disruption remains the primary question mark; deals that failed to close in Q4 due to West Asia crisis have still not closed, though progressing better than in Q4.
Timing shifts in project go-lives and data center milestones contributed to below-trend Q1 performance.
Supply chain pressures cited as a factor affecting Q1 execution.
Capacity deployed to AI-native stack build-out reduces near-term delivery capacity, affecting revenue conversion and margins temporarily.
Large/complex project execution risk: minor slippage (e.g., from Q4 to Q1) can be very material to revenue given exceptionally large project sizes.
Management has made a 'second-half acceleration' statement for several years; it proved true four of the last five years but not last year, so caution is warranted on execution risk repeating.
No fundamental capacity issue to service order book, but capacity ramp-up in complex product/project businesses takes time, unlike simple services staffing.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Management declined to give a formal full-year revenue growth guidance, citing too many uncertain factors, especially Middle East, to do a good job of providing guidance.
Expects business to accelerate through the year, especially into H2, driven by execution across data center, transit, and banking geographic pivot.
Sequential growth from Q1 to Q1 this year is stronger than most previous years.

No specific FY27 margin guidance given; declined to answer directly whether prior 20-22% margin guidance needs recalibration due to data center mix, though implied data center margins remain a few points below enterprise average.
R&D expense expected to remain around 10.5-11% of revenue for FY27, potentially declining slightly after H1 as some R&D projects reach natural end-of-life.

Cash conversion is an extreme focus area for FY27; expects to show progress through the year on both order-book-to-revenue and revenue/EBITDA-to-cash conversion (targeting 60-70%), with more detail to be shared at H1.
Company will not declare specific numbers on data center's expected share of TIG or absolute growth beyond directional ranges (e.g., 50-100% growth, ~40% of TIG).
Directional 2030 value potential of ~$560 million to $1.7 billion disclosed based on named-account SAM analysis with 5-15% obtainable market share.

guidance_ledger.statement: No formal full-year guidance given; management expects acceleration through the year especially in H2, but declined to declare a specific growth number due to uncertainties, particularly Middle East.
Declined to answer directly whether prior 20-22% margin guidance needs recalibration given data center-heavy mix; no explicit new number given.
R&D would more or less remain at a similar number, probably between 10.5% and 11%, potentially coming down a little after H1 as some R&D projects reach natural end-of-life.
Growth number for the data center business would probably be anywhere between 50-100%, moving above the recent 40-50% trajectory into a higher band.

guidance_ledger.metric: Data center share of TIG business
guidance_ledger.statement: Data center roughly a third of TIG business currently; expected to become bigger than a third, maybe about 40% of TIG by the time the year finishes.

Banking a few points above 50% and TIG a few points below 50%, largely similar to current 55-45/56-44 mix; may not dramatically change within the year but could shift more into next year as data center growth accelerates.
Q2 will certainly see a pickup and then a much more significant one in Q3 and Q4 for TIG/data center.

Cannot fully expect Middle East situation to normalize by Q2; can expect the year-on-year comparison impact to go away by Q3 purely because the comp base goes away, irrespective of whether the geopolitical situation itself resolves.

Focused sharply on cash conversion this year; typically H1 OCF is negative or close to zero due to payment cycles, management would not commit to a positive H1 OCF but expects to be in good shape in H1 and accelerate through H2; will provide more detail at H1.
Not going to make any meaningful acquisition for the next few quarters/times, freeing up cash demand.

Data center margins will remain a few points below enterprise margin for some time; will improve over a multi-year period as more IP/products are introduced, similar to the transit business trajectory over five-six years.
As the software business becomes larger and more global, operating leverage will kick in, reducing incremental investment needed per new market and making banking margins healthier over time.
Management will consider internally whether to start disclosing at a sub-segment level (e.g., data center) in investor materials.
PAT margin was 15.02%, within the guided ranges of 15% to 16% but towards the lower end of our planned ranges.

We will not throw a half-baked number out because there are uncertainties we don't know, especially around the Middle East; we will continue to grow ahead of the industry growth rate by a meaningful number.
How much of INR 1800 crore order book is executable over the next 12 months? Something in the range of 68%-72%.
My best guess is we are talking of a number somewhere between 150 and 200 crores... over the next four quarters, but we are working very hard to drive productivity improvements and try to shrink it.
I feel the INR 200 crores–INR 250 crore sort of number is the right number for working capital/balance sheet pressure due to larger contracts.

guidance_ledger.metric: Data center hyperscaler deal revenue recognition
guidance_ledger.statement: We faced some delays in terms of project execution, but I would say a fairly large chunk of it within the year.
As we get to a steady state, we probably should be able to grow 10%-12%, even if we don't sell a single new logo in the Banking space.
I feel it will grow very strongly into FY27... I feel like next year would be a good one for Europe.
The business is becoming meaningfully more global and that will accelerate in the new year.

Over the next couple of years as the business matures, I feel strongly that the margins will get even better... you should see the contribution margins meaningfully go up, steadily go up, but you will see the actual final end state only when the growth rates come down.
It's now becoming a meaningful driver of revenue... it will become much more sizable going into next year.

risk_register.note: Continuing disruption from West Asia crisis; deals that failed to close in Q4 still have not closed as of Q1, though progressing better than Q4; expected to remain a question mark with no reliable timeline for normalization, though YoY comp impact should disappear after Q3.
Timing shifts in project go-lives and data center milestones contributed to below-trend Q1 performance.
Cited alongside other factors as contributing to Q1 execution shortfall.

risk_register.risk: Capacity diversion to AI-native product build-outs
risk_register.note: Significant capacity diverted to build out AI-native banking stack and data center capacity, temporarily reducing delivery capacity and masking underlying EBITDA; expected to normalize over the next quarter or two.
Very large projects have longer conversion cycles than typical 12-month projects; minor schedule slippage can be very material to revenue given project sizes.
Management has made the same H2 acceleration statement for several years; proven true four of the last five years but not last year, so remains watchful.
Typically negative or near-zero OCF at H1 due to payment cycles in large complex projects; focus this year on improving both order-book-to-revenue and EBITDA-to-cash conversion.
Biggest impact on Q4 and likely Q1 FY27, causing missed Banking deal closures and slowed project execution/go-lives; spend appetite considered intact once situation clears.
Large hyperscaler win required execution/investment start, but revenue slipped from Q4 into Q1 due to unanticipated planning delays; a INR 350-crore deal.
One-time impact absorbed from labor code implementation.
Five years of rapid growth (business quadrupled) has left the company stretched in places, exposing vulnerabilities amid revenue miss and pace of AI-led disruption.
Investing ahead of confident revenue expectations that did not materialize (Q4 miss of >INR100 crores); management committed to more conservative front-ending of costs going forward.
Emerging cybersecurity risks (referenced news around 'Mythos' and a '5.5 security layer') requiring urgent investment to strengthen technology stacks for both Aurionpro and clients.

risk_register.risk: Decision-making slowdown due to AI/cybersecurity prioritization by banks
risk_register.note: Banks and other serious organizations are prioritizing separate AI and cybersecurity investment decisions, potentially delaying other buying decisions.
Referenced as a genuine factor constraining execution alongside MEA war issues, affecting order book executability estimate (68-72%).

risk_register.risk: Working capital / balance sheet pressure from large contracts
risk_register.note: Larger projects bring higher working capital needs as they scale; management estimates INR 200-250 crores of pressure, but does not expect increased debt.

themes.label: MEA Geopolitical Disruption
themes.note: Continuing MEA disruption impacted Q1 execution; deals expected to close in Q4 still have not closed, though progressing better than Q4; contribution to growth fell to zero from double digits last year.

themes.label: AI-Native Product Transformation
themes.note: Building AI-native banking stack (software 2.0) through AurionAI, Arya.AI, Lexi Labs absorbs capacity today but creates a reusable platform, temporarily affecting revenue conversion and margins.

themes.label: Data Center Inflection
themes.note: Data center business at an inflection point; growth expected to move from 40-50% trajectory to a higher band (50-100%), with capacity built in advance and acceleration concentrated in H2.

themes.label: Investment-led Margin Pressure
themes.note: Margin drop this quarter linked to capacity diverted to R&D/product build-outs and data center mix, which runs a few points below enterprise margin; expected to normalize over a quarter or two.

themes.label: Geographic Diversification
themes.note: Expanded demand generation in US, Southeast Asia and Europe; refocusing banking away from MEA; secured largest-ever US order.

themes.label: Order Book Strength
themes.note: Order book strong and pipeline healthy, described as busiest pipeline ever seen; conversion, not demand, is the constraint.

themes.label: Cash Conversion Focus
themes.note: Extreme focus on cash conversion for FY27, aided by no major M&A and no R&D expense increase, but H1 OCF typically negative due to payment cycles.

key_takeaways: Revenue was Rs. 358 crores, up 6.3% year-on-year. Banking and FinTech grew about 5% to Rs.200 crores plus. TIG grew 8.4% to Rs. 157 crores. EBITDA was Rs. 61 crores at 17% and profit after tax was Rs. 45 crores.

We added 23 new customer logos, which is a record for Q1. In the United States, we secured our largest ever order. We also won a large transaction banking mandate, which is rare for Q1. Started execution on one of our largest projects in the data center space and escalated our sales push into newer markets for both transit as well as banking.
This is not really a demand issue. Our order book is strong. The pipeline is healthy. Engagement is improving. Our priority is converting demand into go lives and revenue.
We expect growth to move above the recent 40-50% trajectory that we have had for the data center business into a higher band than that.

The first half performance is obviously starting with Q1 is relatively modest, but deal activity is improving, execution is gathering pace and our order book gives us confidence that momentum will build with meaningful acceleration in the second half.

We've made or rather I have made the same statement about accelerating in second half for the last several years but last year it wasn't true, so we need to remain watchful on MEA and on large project timelines.
We enter the remainder of FY27 with landmark wins as you have seen, a much stronger geographic balance than we had last year, a differentiated IP and a healthy pipeline.
We are cautiously optimistic about the year ahead and confident in Aurionpro's long-term trajectory.
pressing_questions: So also, I think in one slide, we have mentioned, you know, our directional path for 2030. So, we just wanted to know the value potential that you have given is a very huge range. So, you know, just could you maybe help us like, what are other parts of your focus in that? Like, what's the reason? I think it's 560 million dollars to 1.7 billion dollars, right? That's a decently big change. So, could you narrow it down for us and our pathway to reach that potential? And just one more suggestion, sir, the data center is going to become like more than 20% of our business, can we disclose it separately in PPT?

So, three questions. Specifically, you indicated that in Q1, it was impacted by the seasonality, project timing shifts, as well as higher input cost. So, can you quantify or throw some color on the impact of all these factors? And are we expecting to normalize entirely by Q2? Or are we seeing some pass-throughs in H2 as well?... A question about order book... what specifically needs to happen with the next two quarters for the conversion to return?... a follow-up question on the previous participants. So, we see that FY27 margins are impacted due to data center heavy mix. So, should we expect any recalibration in the earlier margin guidance of 20% to 22% in the near term?

Instead of focusing much more on revenue and EBITDA for FY27, I would like to ask you about the cash conversion which we are seeing in Q1 and in the running quarter as well. And as our cash conversion was not that great in FY26, how do you see FY27 panning out when it comes to cash conversion, cash to EBITDA conversion as such?
So, like H1 last year, we saw extremely negative OCF. So, going into H1 this year, can we see a positive OCF and then probably build on that in H2 and show a conversion of 60-70% EBITDA?

quarters.summary: FY26 revenue grew 20.2% YoY to INR 1,411 crores against a planned ~30% growth target, with EBITDA margin of 20.02% and PAT margin of 15.02% — within guided ranges (20-21% EBITDA, 15-16% PAT) but at the lower end. Q4 was impacted by the MEA geopolitical war, hyperscaler data-center project delays, and one-time labor code costs, with management expecting continued MEA impact into Q1 FY27. The company enters FY27 with an order book exceeding INR 1800 crores, healthy pipeline across segments, and plans for higher upfront investment (R&D/capex of INR 150-200 crores over next four quarters) and transient working-capital/balance-sheet pressure (~INR 200-250 crores) as it scales large contracts and builds AI-native product stacks; management expects a strong FY27 with growth ahead of industry rates, though declined to give a specific number given MEA uncertainty.

subsections.label: FY26 Performance vs Plan
points: FY26 was a year of strong execution against a complex backdrop; by the company's own standards the final result was below par.
Entered the year planning revenue growth close to 30%; plan was intact right up till entering H2, but actual growth came in at 20.2%.
EBITDA margin (20.02%) and PAT margin (15.02%) were within guided ranges but towards the lower end of planned ranges.

subsections.label: Q4 Drivers of Miss
points: War in MEA was the biggest impact on Q4 and likely Q1 FY27, particularly affecting Banking deal closures and project completions.
Data center business affected in Q4 as a large hyperscaler win required execution/investment start, but revenue slipped from Q4 into Q1 due to unanticipated planning delays.
One-time impact absorbed from labor code implementation.
Company significantly stepped up expensed and capitalized investments to address AI and data center opportunities; timing of these investments would have been better had H2 revenue plan been met.
Five years of rapid growth (business has quadrupled) has left the company stretched in places; current revenue miss and speed of AI-led disruption exposed vulnerabilities.

subsections.label: Margin Trajectory / Investment Impact
points: Management does not plan for significant margin dip as scale of orders increases; large orders are not necessarily low margin, just mistimed on execution.

Contribution margins on hardware/software stack (owning the whole value chain, e.g., transit) are improving structurally, but current margins are masked by high growth-related costs; margins expected to improve further as business matures and growth normalizes to single digit/low-teens.

Software stack rebuild (reinventing entire stack, which was not originally anticipated) will temporarily pressure margins due to expensing of investments, though the same long-run margin-improvement logic applies.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation / Balance Sheet
points: CAPEX increased significantly in H2, driven by material transactions on the TIG side (transit and data center) and heavy investment in building the Banking and AI software stacks.
Increase in intangibles reflects accelerated development cycle to build 'software 2.0' versions of every Aurionpro product and enter new spaces (e.g., trade finance).
A large chunk of investment is expected to be routed to the P&L when backed by client projects; some investment will be front-ended ahead of client projects to get ahead of the market.

Transit stack investment (back-office software, CCHS) is largely a one-off nearing completion; AI research investment (Tabular Foundation models, explainability) will continue as these are less mature spaces requiring time to commercialize.
Management does not anticipate increased debt; expects to remain comfortable on overall cash position while focusing on shoring up the balance sheet.
Transient pressure will be on the growth-oriented side of the balance sheet (working capital from large contracts, product build-out investment), not the debt side.
Company working on efficiency measures: tighter controls on relationships/contracts, efficient contracting and payment terms to minimize working capital needs.

key_figures.label: Large hyperscaler data center deal size

subsections.label: Demand Picture
points: Management does not see any material change in the demand picture for the business, aside from transitionary events such as supply chain disruptions and the Middle East war.

Data center demand in India is accelerating; Transit business is extremely strong in India, executing against large orders while now competing aggressively globally; Banking remains a significant player with exceptional win rates.
Long-term demand view, if anything, would have changed to the upside rather than downside.

Some decision-making slowdown seen as banks prioritize AI and cybersecurity investments alongside core spend, but overall RFP/buying process volumes in India, South Asia and Southeast Asia remain broadly unchanged; MEA is slow currently but expected to normalize once the situation stabilizes; US and Europe are small and not materially impactful currently.
Slight question mark on order book executability (68-72%) due to genuine supply chain disruptions and Middle East war-related execution constraints, expected to ease but not guaranteed.

subsections.label: Revenue Mix by Vertical
points: Banking probably ends up being slightly more than 50% of revenue with TIG slightly less, varying quarter to quarter.
TIG could grow a bit faster into next year due to picking up larger orders, but over the longer run relative growth rates between Banking and TIG are expected to be a wash.

subsections.label: Banking and AI Software
points: Continued wins with multiple strategic go-lives in FY26, creating strong references across public sector banks and international markets.

Rebuilding the Banking stack with 'Aurion AI', starting with a fully AI-native trade finance platform on agentic architecture announced a few weeks back, with agents handling workflows and foundation models reasoning over bank data for real-time decisions.
A series of AI-native applications will follow across the entire Aurionpro stack over the next couple of quarters.
Investing in proprietary research through Arya and Lexsi Labs, including foundation models tuned for Banking.
Believes there is opportunity to displace legacy vendors at large scale globally with the new AI-native product line.

subsections.label: Transit
points: Secured large strategic wins across India; pipeline extremely strong; business becoming meaningfully more global, expected to accelerate in the new year.
Investing across the full stack (software, systems, hardware) to compete at scale; owning the full stack differentiates a category leader from an average vendor.
Strengthening software stack with back-office software and CCHS builds (e.g., MMRDA project), traditionally not done before; this investment is largely a one-off nearing completion.

subsections.label: Data Center
points: Business reached a clear inflection point in FY26; secured one of India's largest AI-focused data center mandates from a leading hyperscaler along with several other wins.
Becoming a partner of choice for hyperscalers in the AI era; engagements carry elevated investment cycles being funded with urgency.

Business model is capital-light services: design, integrated engineering, and program management of the data center build; company will continue to selectively pick specialized high-margin design deals as well as full-spectrum engagements.
Large hyperscaler deal (INR 350 crores) is in execution with revenue recognition expected largely within the year, delayed from planning issues.
Also announced a Brownfield data center facility deal in Mumbai.

subsections.label: Payments
points: Payments becoming a meaningful driver of revenue with growing scale in terms of merchants; expected to become much more sizable going into next year, requiring further build-out investment.

subsections.label: Cross-sell / Upsell Strategy
points: Two key product principles: 'Product Superiority' (being better than alternatives in 2-3-4 specific ways) and 'Never Fail a Customer'.
Expansion strategy: add modules (regulation-driven) and add adjacent products (cash → liquidity management → virtual accounts → trade → supply chain finance) to existing bank relationships.
Acquisitions (InfraRisk, OmniFin, Fintra, Arya) have expanded the product surface area to support cross-sell/upsell rather than only selling to new logos.

Account management program exists but management acknowledges there is room to push more aggressively on wallet-share capture from existing clients; still relatively small in scale with many single-product relationships.

subsections.label: NBFC Platform
points: North of 30 clients including fairly large NBFCs; company is competitive in the space.

Company has a policy around deal-size threshold for announcements, so NBFC wins are not always announced individually given typically smaller deal values; may announce a batch of wins together for more visibility.

key_figures.label: Orion MSP publication timeline for next version

subsections.label: AI-Native Product Build-out
points: Every product group is building a brand-new AI-native version of its product from zero; spans trade finance, transaction banking, lending (corporate and retail), and will extend into a couple of new product lines not yet disclosed.

Building one of the leading research labs on Tabular Foundation models, personally led by a named technical leader (Vinay); published Orion MSP a couple of months back, with a stronger version expected in the next 4-8 weeks aimed at doing well on global benchmarks.
Investing heavily in an AI engineering framework covering explainability and enterprise AI adoption capabilities.

Over the last six months invested heavily in an AI development stack including AI-based code generation and a modern development stack, which management says is beginning to deliver material productivity improvements that could reduce future capitalized development spend.
Emerging cybersecurity risk (referenced 'Mythos' and '5.5 security layer') noted as requiring urgent investment to strengthen technology stacks.

subsections.label: Software Buying Behavior / Contract Tenure
points: Management sees no material change in software buying behavior or contract tenure in Banking or Transit; core business-process software purchases remain long-term decisions (10-15 year horizon), not short-term.
Clients increasingly buy based on 'AI readiness' of the vendor's stack, which is driving disproportionate win rates for Aurionpro when competing on this angle.

Management does not see core banking business-process software being displaced by frontier AI model providers (e.g., Anthropic, OpenAI); views an 'agent' as roughly 70-80% software plus an intelligence/model layer, reinforcing the continued need for software.

subsections.label: Middle East (MEA)
points: MEA had become an increasingly important growth engine over the last couple of years, particularly for Banking, but war in the region caused the company to fall short on Q4 committed deal closures and planned project completions.

Impact was a 'double whammy': lost/delayed license revenue from deal closures plus slowed execution/go-live of previously announced wins (including with Saudi Arabian banks) due to inability to put teams on the ground.

Management sees some deal activity restarting in the Middle East (POCs restarting) but buying processes have not resumed full steam; full stabilization tied to resolution of the geopolitical situation, timing uncertain.
Spend appetite in the region considered intact once the geopolitical picture clears.

subsections.label: Europe
points: Business has matured; Fenixys is doing very well and continuing to grow strongly.
Acquired more clients, expanding the business, and also taking it outside Europe into Middle East, South Africa, and US.
Being considered for more buying processes/RFPs in Europe; wins logged but not yet at the scale seen in Middle East or Southeast Asia; expected to be a good year for Europe in FY27.

subsections.label: Southeast Asia
points: Now investing heavily in Southeast Asia as part of diversification strategy to reduce reliance on the Middle East.

subsections.label: US
points: US remains a very small market for the company currently, not materially impactful.

subsections.label: Diversification Strategy
points: Pivoting to diversify geographically after heavy MEA reliance in recent years; expects to be much more diversified over the next couple of quarters.
Doubling down on customer/prospect relationships in Middle East (getting 'closer' to customers) while also pushing Southeast Asia, Europe, and India to balance demand across territories.

subsections.label: Competitive Positioning vs AI Platforms
points: No immediate signs of frontier model firms (e.g., Anthropic) competing on core banking business-process software; such firms may offer skills like financial analysis but not full business-process execution.

Company launched first fully AI-native, built-from-scratch (software 2.0 plus agents) trade finance platform, viewed as the most advanced trade finance platform in the market today; believes rolling out more such products will increase competitiveness and market share.
Believes it holds a disproportionate win rate due to being perceived as ready for AI-driven change in banking software.

subsections.label: Global Transit Competition
points: Company is extremely strong in India transit currently, executing against very large orders, and is now competing aggressively in the global transit market, aiming to be a meaningful global player over the next few years.

subsections.label: AI-Native Transformation Strategy
points: Stepping up investments now with urgency and scale, organized around an AI-native way of working personally led by the Group CEO.
Vision 2030 conviction only strengthened despite near-term roadblocks; medium-to-long-term growth drivers across each business considered intact.
Approaching inflection points across several businesses simultaneously, prompting a significant, coordinated investment response.

subsections.label: Past Acquisitions Supporting Product Expansion
points: Acquired InfraRisk, OmniFin, Fintra, and Arya to add net-new products and expand surface area for cross-sell/upsell with existing bank relationships.
Management indicated more acquisitions may still be pursued to expand product surface area and relevance to banking clients.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / MEA War
points: War in MEA was the biggest driver of Q4 shortfall and is expected to continue impacting Q1 FY27; considered a temporary factor though acknowledged it could also be read as a sign of a longer-term shift.

If the geopolitical situation persists for another quarter, order inflows, deal conversions, and execution timelines could be further affected; company is responding by doubling down on customer proximity in the region and diversifying to Southeast Asia, Europe and India.

subsections.label: Execution/Planning Risk
points: Company mistimed investment against a large hyperscaler data-center contract, leading to revenue slipping from Q4 into Q1 due to unanticipated project planning delays.

Management flagged a broader lesson: as the company has grown four times in four years (from ~INR 375 crores to INR 1,400-1,500 crores), even small increases in front-ended investment can now translate into hundreds of crores of impact if matching revenue does not materialize as planned; plans to be more conservative in front-ending costs going forward.

subsections.label: Labor Code Implementation
points: One-time cost impact absorbed from labor code implementation in the period.

subsections.label: Organizational Stretch
points: Five years of rapid growth (business quadrupled) has left the company stretched in places, exposing vulnerabilities highlighted by the current revenue miss and pace of AI-led disruption; management committed to addressing these gaps and improving resilience against extraneous shocks.

subsections.label: Cybersecurity
points: Emerging cybersecurity risks referenced (including news around 'Mythos' and a '5.5 security layer') requiring urgent action and investment to strengthen technology stacks; considered a risk applicable to Aurionpro itself and to client organizations such as banks.

subsections.label: Decision-Making Slowdown
points: Banks and other serious organizations are prioritizing AI and cybersecurity investment decisions, which could cause some slowdown in decision-making/buying cycles even outside MEA.

subsections.label: FY27 Outlook
points: Company declined to give a specific FY27 revenue growth number, citing uncertainty especially around the Middle East; committed to growing ahead of industry growth rates by a meaningful margin.
Management stated there is a possibility of returning to prior years' growth rates but wants to revisit the specific number in a quarter or two as things settle.
Confident in delivering a strong FY27 despite near-term roadblocks; each business considered built for the current AI-driven inflection moment.

Expects higher upfront investment than a typical year in FY27, with larger projects bringing higher working capital needs as they scale; management would rather absorb temporary balance sheet pressure than underinvest.
Does not anticipate significant margin dip as order scale increases; expects to get better at planning execution of large orders.

Transit business expected to become meaningfully more global with acceleration in the new year; Europe expected to be a good year in FY27; Banking mix expected to be slightly more than 50% of revenue with TIG slightly less, though TIG could grow faster in FY27.

R&D/software development capitalized spend guided at INR 150-200 crores over the next four quarters, with efforts underway to shrink this via productivity improvements (AI-based code generation, modern development stack).
Payments business expected to become much more sizable going into next year.

guidance_ledger.statement: When we entered the year, we planned for the revenue to grow close to 30%.
Revenue actually grew 20.2% to INR 1,411 crores.
EBITDA margin was 20.02%, well within the guided ranges of 20% to 21% but towards the lower end of our planned ranges.
PAT margin was 15.02%, within the guided ranges of 15% to 16% but towards the lower end of our planned ranges.

We will not throw a half-baked number out because there are uncertainties we don't know, especially around the Middle East; we will continue to grow ahead of the industry growth rate by a meaningful number.
How much of INR 1800 crore order book is executable over the next 12 months? Something in the range of 68%-72%.
My best guess is we are talking of a number somewhere between 150 and 200 crores... over the next four quarters, but we are working very hard to drive productivity improvements and try to shrink it.
I feel the INR 200 crores–INR 250 crore sort of number is the right number for working capital/balance sheet pressure due to larger contracts.
We are not planning on any significant margin dip because the scale of the orders increases.

guidance_ledger.statement: We faced some delays in terms of project execution, but I would say a fairly large chunk of it within the year.

Banking probably ends up being slightly more than 50 and TIG ends up being slightly less or thereabouts... there is a possibility TIG grows a bit faster going into next year, but longer run I think it's a wash.
As we get to a steady state, we probably should be able to grow 10%-12%, even if we don't sell a single new logo in the Banking space.
I feel it will grow very strongly into FY27... I feel like next year would be a good one for Europe.
The business is becoming meaningfully more global and that will accelerate in the new year.

Over the next couple of years as the business matures, I feel strongly that the margins will get even better... you should see the contribution margins meaningfully go up, steadily go up, but you will see the actual final end state only when the growth rates come down.
It's now becoming a meaningful driver of revenue... it will become much more sizable going into next year.

themes.label: AI-Native Product Transformation

themes.label: Data Center Inflection

themes.label: Investment-led Margin Pressure

key_takeaways: FY26 revenue grew 20.2% to INR 1,411 crores against a planned ~30% growth, with EBITDA margin at 20.02% and PAT margin at 15.02%, within guided ranges but at the lower end.
The biggest impact on Q4 and likely Q1 was the war in MEA, affecting both Banking deal closures and planned project completions; management believes this is temporary.
Data center business performance was also affected in Q4 as revenue from a large hyperscaler win slipped from Q4 into Q1 due to unanticipated planning delays.
Company has significantly stepped up both expensed and capitalized investments to meet what it feels are generational opportunities in AI and data centers.
Company enters FY27 with an order book exceeding 1800 crores and a healthy pipeline across all segments.
Management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number due to uncertainty, particularly around the Middle East, but expects to continue growing ahead of industry growth rates.
Order book executable over the next 12 months is estimated at 68-72%.
Estimated R&D/capitalized development spend of INR 150-200 crores over the next four quarters, and transient working capital/balance sheet pressure of INR 200-250 crores in FY27.

AURIONPRO.about: Established in 1997, Aurionpro Solutions Limited works in providing business solutions in the fields of Transaction Banking Platform, Customer Experience (ACE Platform), Smart city and Smart Transportation experience and Cybersecurity solution. The company primarily offers software products and consulting services to banking industry in India and abroad.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was framed as a "reset" quarter after an operating-model overhaul: management streamlined the organization, tightened execution and materially optimized cost structure, enabling faster-than-market growth on a leaner cost base with intent to convert incremental gross profit into operating leverage and sustainable profitability. Commercial volumes and market share rebounded sharply QoQ, gross margin was defended above 30% despite commodity pressure with expected upside as inputs ease, OpEx fell sharply even as volumes doubled, a ₹780 cr QIP was completed strengthening the balance sheet while capex is set to fall sharply post cell commissioning, distribution is pivoting to a multi-channel dealer model, service issues (mostly parts-supply driven) are described as largely behind, and the battery/cell vertical is moving from capability to commercialization with 4680 NMC cells deployed, LFP certification achieved, and capacity expansion path to 20 GWh funded outside parent equity. Energy storage (Shakti/Mahashakti) is being reset to LFP chemistry with a large new MOU signaling a demand pipeline, targeted to start contributing revenue from Q3/Q4 FY27.

subsections.label: Margin profile
points: Automotive gross margin defended at 30.5% despite commodity cost pressure; management reiterated it as 'industry leading above 30% despite the commodities.'
Forward view: margins expected to stay in-range near-term with potential improvement as 'over the next quarter or two commodities come down, and margins will further improve again.'
Target band reiterated at ~30–32%.

subsections.label: Cost structure and operating leverage
points: Consolidated OpEx fell 22% QoQ to ₹333 cr even as volumes roughly doubled.
A one-time OpEx benefit came from reversal of previously accrued ACC PLI penalties (~₹55 cr); excluding this, OpEx would have been ~₹380 cr, still down vs Q4's ₹428 cr (which included leases).
Adjusted operating EBITDA improved from -₹326 cr in Q4 to -₹195 cr in Q1.
OpEx outlook: expected to come down into the ₹300–325 cr range over the next couple of quarters, while keeping margins steady and volumes 'steady to slightly growing.'

subsections.label: Balance sheet and capital allocation
points: ₹780 cr QIP completed; management said this strengthened the balance sheet and adds flexibility.
Auto capex: 'hardly any capex now'; factory already at ~1M units/year capacity.
Cell capex cycle finishing with 6 GWh commissioning; no further capex foreseen after that, and this capex is funded through debt.
Explicit annual capex run-rate after cell completion: ~₹50 cr ('maybe 30 to 50 crores. 50 crores you can take a target number').
Depreciation decline QoQ attributed to a policy change: depreciation policy evolved 'in sync with the industry standards' (₹10–20 cr impact cited).

subsections.label: ASP dynamics
points: ASP decline QoQ attributed '90%...to product mix.'
Management expects mix to improve from Q1 levels, with ASP broadly in a 'plus minus 5%' band around current levels, aided by premium recovery and motorcycles.

subsections.label: Commercial performance: volumes rebound and share recovers
points: Deliveries nearly doubled QoQ to ~39,200 units; orders at ~44,000.
Broader e-2W market grew ~17% QoQ while 'Ola registrations grew 97%'.
Market share improved from 5.1% to 8.4% QoQ.
Growth described as 'broad-based with sequential improvement across every region of the country,' implying less dependence on any single region.

subsections.label: Roadster motorcycles
points: Currently 'a small minority' of contribution.
Demand strongest for the 9.1 kWh variant, but deliveries constrained by 4680 cell supply during factory installation pause.
Order-to-delivery gap in Q1 partly attributed to this constraint.

subsections.label: Energy storage (Shakti/Mahashakti) revenue contribution
points: Revenue contribution in Q1 minimal—delivered 'a few hundred' Shakti Gen 1 units and then paused scaling.
Management expects 'numbers from battery business' starting Q3, with early revenues from Mahashakti possibly beginning 'either Q4 or Q3' (worded as an aspiration).

subsections.label: 4680 cell status and ramp
points: 4680 NMC cells 'already commercially deployed'; 'few thousand...on the roads already.'
Production paused in Q1 to expand installation from 2.5 to 6 GWh; restart expected 'sometime this month...in a week, 10 days.'
Portfolio penetration: 'about three of our vehicle products...have the 4680 cell in them,' to scale with the 6 GWh ramp.
Yield at pause was 'high 70s or 80 percent,' with a roadmap to '90 plus percent within a quarter of restarting.'

subsections.label: Chemistry roadmap
points: LFP: 46100 LFP cell BIS certified and vehicle ready; 'almost all of Ola Electric's auto business will move to LFP soon enough.'
NMC retained for top-end performance: 'about 20% of our portfolio will be NMC based.'
Energy storage (Shakti/Mahashakti): 'All of Shakti and Mahashakti...will be LFP based.'
NMC also positioned for niches like drones, with 'encouraging responses from global OEMs' and Indian companies; many are 'testing our cell.'

subsections.label: 15 Aug product event
points: Flagged as a major update point; management teased 'very exciting stuff,' including Shakti Gen 2 / Mahashakti details and additional formats for C&I (data centers, etc.).

subsections.label: Capacity expansion to 20 GWh (structure and funding)

Prismatic R&D to complete 'by end of this year.'
Funding: expansion will be via separate equity at the cell company level: 'We will not need use any parent entity equity to go from six to twenty.'
Timing: equity raise targeted in FY27 (management corrected expectation away from FY28/29).

subsections.label: Geographic quality
points: Growth described as 'broad-based with sequential improvement across every region of the country,' implying less dependence on any single region.

subsections.label: Strategic pivot: distribution shifts to multi-channel dealer model
points: Ola moved from 'single-channel company-owned' to multi-channel distribution.
Rationale: dealer economics + execution at scale; 'local nuances of auto retail...customer engagement, the servicing...a dealer can do much better at scale.'
Future role split: company stores become 'more like experience centers' (higher quality, fewer over time); dealers become the 'backbone in terms of volume and transaction and service.'
Rollout timing: first dealer shops go live by Janmashtami (~4 Sep); management expects 'meaningful scale before the Diwali season.'
Dealer interest: 'almost a thousand people interested,' but Ola emphasizes selecting 'high-quality' partners.
Route-to-market for Shakti: multi-channel—company stores, auto dealers, plus 'traditional channel also' for inverter/battery-style distribution.

subsections.label: Service: parts supply-driven issues largely resolved
points: Management stated 'most of the service challenges are now behind us.'
Root cause emphasized as parts availability (not high service incidence), including vendor issues and 'macro geopolitical situation.'
No 'material' ongoing supply chain issues claimed, but some critical parts are closely monitored.
Under the dealer model, parts become 'cash and carry,' expected to reduce parts-availability friction.

subsections.label: Energy storage (Shakti/Mahashakti): product reset to LFP; new MOU signals demand pipeline
points: Mahashakti (utility-scale energy storage): first MOU signed; described as 'very meaningful growth driver.'
MOU size: 20 GWh over the next 5–6 years.
Pipeline building with 'high quality renewable platforms, utilities...everybody is now engaging with us.'
Shakti Gen 1 used NMC chemistry; Ola intentionally did not scale it due to economics: 'NMC is costier...gross margins...were not to the target level.'
Shakti Gen 2 (LFP) to be announced 15 Aug; claimed margin profile: 'gross margins are going to be actually even healthier than our auto segment.'

subsections.label: Capital discipline message
points: Capex dropping to ~₹50 cr post cell commissioning.
Expansion beyond 6 GWh designed to be financed at cell-company level rather than via parent equity.

key_takeaways: Execution proof-point post-reset: strong QoQ rebound in deliveries/revenue and market share, while OpEx falls materially—suggesting operating leverage potential if growth sustains.
Near-term margin stability with input-driven upside: management repeatedly anchored gross margin at ~30–32% with potential improvement as commodities soften.
Major GTM shift is underway: multi-channel dealer rollout is positioned as a near-term growth accelerator and a structural fix for service/retail execution at scale.

Battery/energy storage is moving from capability to commercialization: LFP certification + 6 GWh commissioning + Shakti Gen 2 economics are presented as the next leg, with explicit intent to monetize beyond vehicles and into grid/C&I storage.
Capital discipline message is strong: capex dropping to ~₹50 cr post cell commissioning; expansion beyond 6 GWh designed to be financed at cell-company level rather than parent equity.

quarters.summary: Management framed Q4/FY26 as an inflection point: industry-leading gross margins (38.5% in Q4), first-ever operating cash flow positive quarter, and a Gigafactory entering scale-up, even though volumes/revenue remained depressed due to internal service/execution issues. For Q1 FY27, the company guided to 40,000-45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of Rs 500-550 crores (nearly double Q4 level), with adjusted operating EBITDA/cash flow breakeven at the Auto level targeted through FY27 as volumes recover toward 20,000-25,000 units/month.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin improvement reflects vertical integration, Gen 3 maturity, rising architecture, downstream control, and increasing integration of own cells.
Excluding PLI, gross margins are still high (33.5%), countering the perception that margin strength is incentive-driven.

Management expects short-term commodity pressures and recent aggressive growth investment to weigh marginally, but margins to remain healthy in the short term and incrementally improve in the long term.
EV competitors would need heavy investment in technology and manufacturing to close the margin gap; Ola's gross margins now exceed ICE industry margins.

subsections.label: Cash flow milestone
points: Q4 FY26 was the first operating cash flow positive quarter, supported by strong gross margins, PLI inflows, lower OpEx, and tighter working capital discipline.
Auto business is close to free cash flow generation; as volumes rise in the rebound, meaningful sustained free cash flow is expected.
Cell business remains in the investment phase but expected to move into sustained revenue growth this financial year and cash flow generation over time.
No more CapEx needed for Auto business scale-up, implying high CFO-to-free-cash-flow conversion.

subsections.label: OpEx reset
points: OpEx reduction reflects network rationalization, tighter sales and service costs, lower fixed overheads and stronger operating governance.
Benefits of '26 actions' (cost actions discussed in prior Shareholders' Letter) expected to flow through over the next couple of quarters.

subsections.label: Breakeven math
points: Consolidated financials basis used for breakeven communication to avoid confusion caused by segment-level financials previously.

With ~35-38% gross margin, ~Rs 1.4 lakh ASP (~Rs 50,000 gross profit/vehicle) and ~Rs 300-350 crore consolidated OpEx, adjusted EBITDA breakeven works out to 20,000-25,000 units/month, subject to pricing mix and commodity conditions.

subsections.label: Revenue recognition change
points: One-time change in revenue recognition policy for extended warranty/care packages: previously recognized upfront, now recognized over the product life (3-year/5-year), causing a ₹20-30 crore hit in ASP/revenue this quarter.
Impact already baked into published numbers; no further one-time restatement expected in future quarters; this revenue will now be recognized every quarter as it is earned.

subsections.label: CapEx and cash outlook
points: Auto CapEx cycle largely behind, with only ~₹50 crore/year maintenance CapEx expected going forward given large existing capacity.
Cell business CapEx for 6 GWh mostly complete; payouts happening in Q1 and a bit in Q2 of FY27; no further CapEx until capital is raised at the cell subsidiary level.
R&D capitalization (20-30% of overall R&D) will continue; PPE CapEx expected to stay below ₹50 crore/year.
Net debt of ~₹950 crore as of 31 March, with gross cash of ₹1,550-1,600 crore and debt of ~₹2,500 crore.
Expect ₹300-500 crore of operating cash flow burn over FY27 as volumes ramp, potentially lower if volumes rise faster; operating cash flow to turn positive after crossing 20,000-25,000 orders/month.
₹400+ crore of debt repayments due this year; company may choose to accelerate repayments given relatively higher cost of debt.

subsections.label: Demand backdrop
points: Demand for EVs has gone up meaningfully in the last few weeks per management; customers are buying whatever is available in the network, leading to very low free inventory days (3-4 days) and an auto backlog.
Company is focused on ramping up supply chain quickly to fulfill orders/backlog; delivery timeline improvements expected to lift volumes another 10-20% in the near term.
Orders are growing ahead of registrations because of a production backlog; some of this backlog is expected to convert into registrations this quarter.
Q1 FY27 order guidance of 40,000-45,000 represents healthy pull-in in demand; registrations may be a little up or down but expected in a similar range.

subsections.label: Breakeven bridge / volume ramp
points: Q4 volumes were not steady-state; they were impacted by internal operations issues, and recovery is now in its third month, with continuing month-on-month growth on top of rebound.
Rebound itself (independent of new demand) should get volumes to ~17,000-18,000 units/month, a mix of scooter and bike (bike ~15% of volumes).

Beyond the rebound, production backlog exists; as suppliers scale production back up, better stability on service and improved inventory availability should push volumes closer to 20,000-22,000 units/month over the next quarter.

subsections.label: Roadster (motorcycle) growth engine
points: Roadster is becoming Ola's second Auto growth engine; motorcycles are India's largest two-wheeler category with very low EV penetration.
Ola has 50%+ market share in electric motorcycles; bikes require higher range than scooters, and Ola's Bharat Cell (4680 cell) enables an almost 500 km certified range top-end product.

Significant uptick seen in Roadster demand in the northern belt of India, the heartland of the bike market; management sees the bike EV movement continuing over the next couple of quarters, aided by petrol price macro.
Company is supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained in bikes.

subsections.label: Cell/own-battery transition into vehicles
points: Around 15% of orders are already on products using Bharat Cells (own 4680 cells), with very good customer feedback.
Plan is to transition the full vehicle portfolio to Ola's own cells by September 2026, described as a meaningful ramp-up of the Gigafactory.

subsections.label: Recovery pattern
points: Sales recovery has been broad-based: Ola is strong in the north and east (a growing EV market) and is regaining position in the south and west.
Service backlog reduction has driven a V-shaped recovery in sales; weekly registration numbers are ramping up.

subsections.label: Product quality & execution improvement
points: Product quality improving with Gen 3; warranty cost is 70% lower than Gen 2.
Service metrics improved sharply: service stats down 88%, same-day closures at ~87%, part dependency down 69%.
Warranty costs came down from 500+ crores in FY25 to only 59 crores in FY26, validating Gen 3 platform leadership.
Service challenges were largely linked to service network operations, which have also meaningfully improved per KPI tracking.

subsections.label: Technology roadmap
points: Cell technology roadmap ladders towards solid-state (performance) and sodium-ion (cost) chemistries; these technologies already exist at lab scale and are working.
Company is not currently focused on spending capital to make solid-state/sodium manufacturing-ready; focus remains on ramping up the 46-series NMC cell.
An LFP cell has also been brought in and will start ramping up in the factory over the next quarter.
As the industry matures for solid state and sodium, Ola plans to bring those products to market.
A prismatic cell is under development, to be released soon; details not yet disclosed.

subsections.label: Product roadmap discipline
points: Company deliberately paused new product launches (including delays like the 'Gig' product) until volumes recovered, to be more disciplined on new capital allocation.
As frontend operations stabilize and volumes ramp up again, new product launches will resume over the course of this year.

subsections.label: Battery service parts execution
points: Historic service part unavailability stemmed from a direct-to-service-center parts distribution model (vs. traditional dealer-stocked model), initially causing 10-day waits for even basic replacements and 20-30 day fulfillment times.

Parts are now stocked in service centers and procurement is done based on forecasts, improving fulfillment, though some parts shared between production and service still see production being prioritized while supply chain ramps up.

subsections.label: Gigafactory scale-up
points: Gigafactory is entering the scale phase; Phase 1 infrastructure in place for 6 GWh scale-up.

Installation up to 6 GWh is largely complete, with commercialization expected by end of this quarter; delay (from planned a month earlier) attributed to Iran war disrupting container shipments, now expected in June.
Own domestic IP built for the battery business enabled productionizing and scaling the Gigafactory with commercially viable yields and prices.
Company plans to expand from 6 to 20 GWh by next year, but only by raising capital separately at the cell entity; strong inbound interest from private equity players given asset leadership.
Commissioning process is sequential: install equipment, commission it, then ramp up yields; the already-commissioned 3 GWh is in a ramp-up phase with good yields.
Supply chain for cathode powder, anode powder, and electrolyte (domestic) is also ramping up in parallel to increase Gigafactory productivity and output.
By end of Q2 FY27 (September), Gigafactory expected to be producing 2+ GWh; capacity allocation for the year: ~2 GWh in-house, ~1+ GWh external auto sales, remainder for Shakti and Mahashakti.

subsections.label: Capital allocation for capacity expansion
points: Company will not ramp up beyond 6 GWh right now from a capital allocation perspective; will first grow into existing 6 GWh capacity.
Expansion of prismatic cell capacity (beyond cylindrical, which is current capacity) planned only after capital is raised at the subsidiary level, targeted within this financial year.

Combined Auto (up to 1 million units annual capacity) and Gigafactory (6 GWh) asset base can support approximately Rs 15,000-20,000 crore of annual revenue scale without needing meaningful incremental CapEx.

subsections.label: Cell cost advantage
points: Even at current low production volumes, building own cells is cheaper than importing on a pure BOM cost basis, an advantage that has improved amid a lithium industry upcycle.
As Gigafactory scales toward 6 GWh, a 10-15% cost advantage (including Gigafactory operational overheads) is expected versus buying cells externally.

subsections.label: Regional recovery pattern
points: Recovery in market share is broad-based: Ola is strong in north and east (a growing EV market) and gaining back position in south and west.

subsections.label: Bike geography
points: Significant uptick in the Roadster product seen in the northern belt of India, described as the heartland of India's bike market.

subsections.label: Supply chain ramp-up
points: Company is focused on ramping up the supply chain quickly to fulfill increased orders and backlog, as demand has outpaced current inventory availability.
Suppliers are scaling production back up in tandem with demand recovery.

subsections.label: Parts distribution model fix
points: Historic parts shortage stemmed from a direct-to-service-center distribution model (vs traditional dealer-stocked model) leading to long wait times; parts are now stocked at service centers and procured based on forecast rather than reactive requirement.

subsections.label: Brand strength
points: Despite service challenges during the period, brand has held well due to fundamental product quality, performance, and price-value proposition, per a third-party brand strength survey.
Brand recall is industry leading; NPS is above industry averages, and specifically strong where there are no service delays.
Ola is by far the highest-searched brand in the EV space in India per Google brand dashboard data.

Business model involves no marketing/advertising spend (no print, TV, IPL sponsorships, no billboards), relying on product-driven word of mouth; management may consider some advertising in coming months to educate a larger customer base on EV benefits and on the brand's turnaround from past service challenges.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: April registrations for Ola were up 20% month-on-month, while the broader E-two-wheeler industry declined by more than 22%.

Management views the current EV demand upswing as an opportunity where competitors will need more CapEx and new product rollouts, while Ola's capacity (Auto and Gigafactory) is already built out, enabling it to scale to a million units a year without incremental capital.

subsections.label: Store/customer experience
points: Company does not plan to introduce dealerships in the Auto business, believing its direct model strategy is correct despite past execution slip-ups.

Store/service experience has improved over the last 1-2 quarters but not yet back to the level seen roughly 2 years ago; company expects to be ahead of industry standards on key metrics (service turnaround time, staff quality, sales process) within the next 1-2 quarters.
Backend process improvements are being built to support better frontend customer experience as volumes ramp up in parallel.

subsections.label: Macro/energy security positioning
points: Management frames Ola as uniquely positioned across two structural shifts: mobility moving from ICE to EV, and energy moving from imported fuels to locally made batteries.

Government and consumer sentiment increasingly favor EV encouragement (e.g., media reports of incentives for buses); policy stakeholders are expected to accelerate domestication of the battery supply chain.
Grid/solar rollout is seen as having maxed out without paired battery deployment, prompting announcements like floating solar with batteries.

Management expects policy developments akin to ALMM in solar (e.g., ALBM, ALCM for batteries/cells), possible ACC PLI extension, and domestic procurement mandates for BESS deployments; company's battery business positioned to benefit.

subsections.label: Cell business capital raise / monetization
points: Company plans to expand Gigafactory capacity beyond 6 GWh only by raising capital separately at the cell entity; significant inbound interest from private equity players given the asset's leadership position.

Management confirmed continued interest from external parties regarding cell business monetization (media reports cited ~Rs 2,000 crore) but declined to share further detail ahead of a public disclosure; ambition is to be the largest cell business in the country by capacity and revenue, expanding beyond 6 GWh once subsidiary-level capital is raised.
Expansion into prismatic cell capacity (beyond current cylindrical cell capacity) planned only after capital raise at subsidiary level, targeted within this financial year.

subsections.label: Three revenue engines for Gigafactory
points: Mobility (EVs): captive demand expected to consume 1.5-2 GWh by end of this financial year; also in conversations with external Indian and global companies interested in buying Ola's cells given world-class specs.

Shakti: launched last quarter, already delivered to some customers; currently supply-constrained as Auto business is prioritized; strong demand from retail and B2B customers (telecom towers, petrol stations, dark stores, organized retail chains) looking to replace diesel generators/lead acid batteries with lithium.

Mahashakti (grid storage): to be built on Prismatic LFP platform, currently in product development; conversations underway with multiple platforms, specs shared, more details to follow in coming quarters.

subsections.label: FY27 priorities
points: Recover volumes, hold margin leadership, reduce OpEx, ramp up the Gigafactory, improve auto cash generation and scale Shakti and Mahashakti.

subsections.label: Investor communication plans
points: Management plans an Analyst and Investor Day at the Gigafactory in the coming month or two, in response to feedback that the company's technical/engineering work is not well understood by the market/analyst community.

subsections.label: Commodity/input cost risk
points: Short-term commodity pressures flagged as a factor that could weigh on gross margins, alongside recent investment into aggressive growth.

subsections.label: Supply chain disruption
points: Remaining 3.5 GWh of Gigafactory commissioning was delayed by about a month due to the Iran war causing container shipment delays; now expected to complete in June.

subsections.label: Execution/service risk
points: Company faced parts supply chain and service network execution challenges (long wait times for parts, slow fulfillment) which have been substantially but not completely resolved; some work still remains as supply chain continues to ramp.
Store/customer experience has improved but has not yet returned to levels seen roughly two years ago.

subsections.label: Debt cost risk
points: Cost of debt currently is relatively higher, prompting consideration of accelerating some debt repayments.
