Power & fuel increase from tariff/rate hike
Power & fuel increase from higher consumption/quantity

subsections.label: Other expenses spike (key explanation)
points: Increase largely from power & fuel: 'the increase is 58 crores… in power and fuel.'

Split between rate vs volume: ~₹28–29 cr from tariff/rate increase; ~₹28 cr from higher consumption/quantity (notably higher casting activity at Rajpura and no Jejuri shutdown like last year): 'casting production and sales in Rajpura has increased… last year we had long shutdown of Jujeri plant, and this time we are running normal full month.'

subsections.label: Structural regulatory hit to power optimization (Maharashtra)
points: Power trading benefit lost: 'We used to get about 10 crores per annum of benefit by power trading… that has stopped.'
Green power usage window curtailed: 'Earlier we were allowed to use the green power for 17 hours, now it is only allowed for eight hours.'
Direct implication: renewable projects still pay back but less: 'instead of getting 100 crore benefit in a year, we may get 80 crores… payback… from three years may go to 3.6 or 3.7 years.'
Management's mitigation path is explicit: battery storage is the workaround—'all that will become possible if we have battery storage.'

sections.title: Q1 FY27 Operating Snapshot (Volumes, Mix, Realizations) by Product

key_figures.label: Pig iron external sales growth YoY

subsections.label: Pig iron ('Pigaran')
points: Management attributed lower external sales to higher internal consumption, noting last year's Q1 had 'stoppage of JG plant for a few days', depressing internal consumption then.

Management stated it 'improved sales realization on Pigaran' and later highlighted the downcycle has likely turned: 'continuously falling commodity prices have taken a break… Pigaran prices have gone up.'
Export parity support noted: 'we are also exporting 30,000 metric tons of Pigarin… realization is likely better than domestic prices.'

subsections.label: Castings
points: Realizations held despite broader commodity weakness: 'we could hold the sales realization on castings.'
Management emphasized resilience in prior periods: 'though the commodity prices went down, our casting realization did not go down, rather, we maintained or slightly improved.'

subsections.label: Tubes
points: Realizations were pressured by adverse mix: 'we had to sell more of line types in the absence of high realizing export orders as well as… oil and gas tubes.'
Tubes remain the most explicitly volatile segment, with headwinds from dumping and weaker oil & gas order flow.

key_figures.label: Tube size coverage (current, up to 10 inches)
Tube size coverage (with 18 inch expansion, additional)

subsections.label: Renewable power (near-term commissioning; but regulatory headwind)
points: 35 MW solar plant: 'in the stage of commissioning'; expected commissioned Jun–Sep quarter.
12 windmills (2.1 MW each): also targeted for Jun–Sep commissioning.
Management is evaluating MW-scale battery storage to restore/expand benefits under new regulations.

subsections.label: Foundry/castings expansion and forward integration
points: Solapur 'two-part / no-bake' foundry (large castings): capacity 15,000 TPA (management clarified phase structure: 'phase one, phase two, we have plugged together to make it to 15,000… There will be no more on that.').
Commissioning targeted by October.
Ramp expectation: within 1–1.5 years reach 500–600 T/month (vs 1,250 T/month nameplate); full utilization about one more year after that.
Demand visibility: 'One of the customers wants the full capacity.' Management already exploring another large casting foundry.
Rajpura foundry expansion (two phases): Existing ~25k TPA; Phase 1 to 40–50k TPA in ~8 months; Phase 2 to 6,000 T/month (~70k TPA).
Current situation: 'Rajpura Foundry is totally sold out.'
Group casting capacity (post expansions): stated 'realizable' capacity across foundries: ~270,000 TPA.
To reach 300,000 TPA castings: 'in three to four years' (with a potential 7th foundry).

subsections.label: Pig iron upgrades and cost efficiency
points: Blast furnace upgrade to 300 m³; pig iron capacity up to 360,000 TPA.
Efficiency projects: pulverized coal injection (PCI) and other features already in BF1/BF2; further expansion underway.
Oxygen plant + enhanced PCI at blast furnaces: completion expected Feb–Mar (next year implied).

subsections.label: Steel and rolling expansion
points: Rolling capacity at Jejuri ('JD') to 25,000 T/month from 15,000; implies ~300,000 TPA rolling, with ~240,000 TPA saleable external alloy steel.
Koppal steel plant: early-stage; MD stated they are ready and intend to proceed; execution horizon ~2 years.
Converting one BF to steelmaking: 'all the government clearances in place… press the button… commissioned within two years' (land clearance within existing premises still needed).

subsections.label: Tubes: product capability upgrades + premiumization
points: Premium couplings project (Baramati): ordering expected 'in next few weeks' time.'
Expander mill (to make larger seamless tubes up to 18"): build time ~2 years; management expects reaching ~350k TPA tubes 3–4 years out.

Strategic rationale (internal actions to raise oil & gas mix): expand processing capacity to execute project 'windows'; bring premium couplings in-house; expand size range: 'only up to 10 inches… covers only around 60%… if we go up to 18 inches… another 40%.'

subsections.label: Total capex envelope
points: FY27 capex indicated ₹600–700 cr, but expected to rise as large projects trigger.
Medium-term: 'around three to three and a half thousand crores in next four years.'

subsections.label: Strong demand
points: Castings demand broad-based—'very strong from all the sectors, tractors, automobile as well as… earthmoving equipment, stationary engines.'

subsections.label: Weaker/volatile demand
points: Oil & gas tubes—'oil and gas related activity is subdued because of which the volumes are less. Export volumes… got affected.'
No major substitution concern acknowledged: When asked about seamless losing share to welded, management replied: 'This volatility is nothing to do with that.'

Legal status: High Court decision favored industry; state appealed.
Current: pending in Supreme Court; 'judgment has not come… still Supreme Court judgment has not come.'
Company continues to provide and disclose as contingent.

Export opportunities supporting domestic pig iron: 'many… are exporting… and we are getting support for the domestic Pigarin prices.'
Some relief vs coke dumping: 'there is some break to the dumping of coke into India.'

points: Castings: pass-through largely working: 'We have been able to pass on the cost increase to customers in case of castings.'
Alloy steel: still negotiating: 'still under discussions… with delay… should be able to pass it all.'
Tubes: less contractual pass-through; more market-driven: 'in case of tube, it is a market dynamics… we have to really get the increase from the market.'

Company-level improvement expected sequentially as (a) pig iron recovers and (b) price resets conclude: 'we are still in the process of concluding price increases… I expect that we will get these benefits in quarter two and three and thereafter.'

Tubes: targeting ~10% volume growth YoY, with recovery in remaining quarters: 'optimistic that we will catch up with the loss… in the remaining three quarters.'

risk_register.risk: Operational stoppages (Hiriyur blast furnace, steel plant)
risk_register.note: Hiriyur blast furnace was stopped for ~3.5 months in FY26 due to unfavorable market conditions causing a 68,000 ton shortfall; one blast furnace also had a 5-day stoppage in Q4; steel plant took two fortnight stoppages for fume extraction system erection.

risk_register.note: Management cited tariff period, Middle East war, Hormuz blockage, high fuel costs, and disruptions in many areas as headwinds, though demand and growth have been sustained despite them.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory changes affecting green power utilization
risk_register.note: New government regulations in Maharashtra could restrict prime slot solar utilization; some utilization-period regulation changes are currently sub judice, affecting FY26 power benefit realization; company exploring battery storage to mitigate.
Solapur ramp-up is described as 'ticklish' due to core productivity and complexity of casting (complicated blocks and heads), not customer-related, requiring time to stabilize process and output.
ONGC order for seamless tubes has seen a delay; management does not have exact pending order figures currently.

themes.label: Commodity price recovery
themes.note: Management believes the commodity downtrend has reversed: 'continuously falling commodity prices have taken a break,' with pig iron prices up and steel price hikes announced.

themes.label: Input cost inflation

themes.label: Casting volume growth & capacity expansion

themes.label: Backward integration & green power

themes.label: Realization mix shift (value-added castings/exports)

themes.label: Operational disruptions (Hiriyur, steel plant)

key_takeaways: Near-term earnings swing factors are (1) power/fuel inflation + regulatory changes in Maharashtra, (2) timing of price pass-through (castings largely done; steel pending), and (3) tubes mix recovery (oil & gas/export normalization).

Management confidence is anchored in: Commodity stabilization + pig iron export support; Strong casting demand and sold-out Rajpura capacity; A clearly staged capex plan (renewables commissioning, large castings, rolling expansion, steelmaking at Koppal, expander mill for tubes).

Most explicit headwind remains tubes: dumping and subdued oil & gas are restraining high-margin mix; management response is capability expansion (premium couplings + expander mill) rather than short-term pricing levers.
pressing_questions: When asked about seamless losing share to welded, management replied: 'This volatility is nothing to do with that.'

quarters.summary: Management expects commodity price recovery (pig iron, steel, tube) to support realizations in FY27, targets ~15% volume growth in casting (production ~1,85,000-1,90,000 MT incl. Oliver), 10-11% volumetric growth in tubes, continued capex of INR600-700 crores/year across pig iron, foundry, steel and tube expansion, and progress on backward integration (mines, beneficiation, pellet plant, green power) while flagging commodity price volatility, cost inflation (coal, dollar) and Hiriyur blast furnace stoppage as key headwinds.

subsections.label: Sales realization pressure
points: Overall top-line growth of 3% (standalone) / 5.1% (including Oliver) was achieved after accounting for drop in sales realizations due to low commodity prices.
Quarter 4 saw pig iron prices and steel prices pick up, partially offsetting the annual realization drop.
Tube realization dropped ~10% for the year; management expects at least half of this drop to be recovered in FY27 as pig iron, steel, power and fuel costs rise.

subsections.label: EBITDA margin trajectory
points: Compared to October, pig iron prices are up INR5,000/ton; compared to December, up INR4,000/ton.
Cost pressures include dollar at INR95 and coal prices up by about $25 per ton, which will factor into costs even as value addition improves.
Management stated current EBITDA is just above 12.5%, and is comfortable only at 15% EBITDA; effort continues across all products for volume growth.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Cash generation is better than the company's ability to invest; borrowings have been reduced substantially.
Company plans to continue investing at INR600-700 crores/year across pig iron, foundry, steel and tube, and hopes to generate cash better than that.
Obligation areas for investment include making mines operational, beneficiation plant, and pellet plant.

subsections.label: Merger update
points: Company is working on merger of Oliver into Kirloskar Ferrous Industries, expecting to close in the next couple of months to get merger benefit for FY25-26 itself.

subsections.label: Casting business growth journey
points: Management considers 20-25% growth targets not realistic; targets volumetric growth of ~15% as reasonably good.
Casting production grew from 1,39,000 to 1,62,000 tons, about 23,000 tons more produced and sold.
Company expects to march forward to about 1,90,000 tons due to large number of castings under development moving into serial production.
Demand for casting remains robust from auto sector and tractor sector.
Sixth foundry (large casting foundry) to be commissioned; expected to get good loading given growth in large castings.
Large capacity underutilization exists at Solapur; effort is to take Solapur to 60,000 tons.
Company has started working on creating a seventh foundry to avoid manufacturing capacity shortfall over next 2-3 years.
Feasibility exists for future aspirational volume growth up to 3 lakh metric tons per annum, requiring more foundries with output increasing 10-15% every year.

subsections.label: New customer acquisition in casting
points: 3 new customers added to casting after 6 years of steady 26 customers.
One new customer is a diesel engine manufacturer with facility in India, manufacturing for India (Indian supply for KFIL) and export.

Other 2 customers use engines for stationary application, tractors (TREM V next level); direct export orders booked, starting with small direct exports in earthmoving equipment, with visibility for more exports in earthmoving equipment and tractor industry.
Clear volume growth plan and SOP timelines exist for these customers; visibility for next 3-4 years is volume going up to 3 lakh metric tons per annum.

subsections.label: Realization mix shift
points: Customers increasingly look to KFIL for intricate/difficult castings, blocks and heads rather than conventional tractor housings/crankcases; portfolio of tractor housings has not grown much.
New order bookings are at better pricing than conventional tractor housings/crankcases.
Sales realization remained flattish after giving commodity price reduction to customers (INR10-12/kg reductions).
Machine shops progressing well across all 3 locations; 22 HMCs purchased and absorbed into operation, with more to follow; expected machining value of about INR100 crores within a year.

Combination of better-priced castings, machining value addition, and export casting pricing is sustaining/improving realization; expect realization to exceed INR130/kg within 2 years partly as commodity price increases flow back.

subsections.label: Solapur foundry utilization
points: Minimum expectation from both Solapur lines is at least 6,000 tons/month; actual could be ~5% more.
Actual last quarter was 4,200 tons/month against 6,000 tons target, i.e., about 70% utilization; another 30% capacity utilization improvement expected over next 3-4 quarters.

Solapur ramp is 'ticklish' due to core productivity and complexity of casting (complicated blocks and heads) — not a customer-related issue but a foundry process/complexity issue that takes time to stabilize.

subsections.label: Oliver Engineering ramp-up
points: Oliver produced 13,500 tons last year, but by Jan-Mar reached run rate of 1,700 tons/month.
Effort is to take Oliver production to at least 2,000 tons/month to reach 24,000 tons for the year.

Oliver run rate expected to move from 1,700-1,800 in April to 2,200-2,300 by year-end, averaging ~2,000/month, yielding 24,000-25,000 tons for the year; order bookings and machining setup already in place.
After merger, sourcing that had shifted to Oliver (about 2,000 tons vs earlier 1,700) will appear in Kirloskar Ferrous books.

subsections.label: Combined foundry run-rate (Solapur + Koppal)
points: Company targeting to reach 15,500 tons/month per line, totaling 45,000-46,000 tons/quarter (with Oliver) within a couple of quarters.
Shift of some sourcing to Oliver and effort to produce more blocks and heads at Koppal affects the timeline to reach the 45,000/quarter run rate.

subsections.label: Seamless tube order book / oil & gas
points: Pending orders exist from last tenders; new tender expected this year, and company expects to pick up those orders.
Exports growing; fuel prices high and reconstruction requirement rising support expectation of robust domestic and export orders in oil & gas segment.
Management does not currently have exact figure for pending tube orders.
Debottlenecking and capacity utilization improvement expected to give 10-11% volumetric improvement in tube business.
ONGC order and other high-margin joint orders are pending; ONGC order has seen delay.

subsections.label: Pig iron pricing dynamics
points: Hiriyur did not get full volume in Q4 (start-up spillover from Oct-Dec into January).
One blast furnace took a 5-day stoppage during the quarter causing some production loss.

Pig iron typically runs 15-day order book with 1-2 days stock; committed pricing to regular customers for a month means price increases from January had spillover effect and full benefit did not come into Q4; further fine correction in price increase happened even in April.
Company expects steel and tube prices to also rise given rising international pig iron price ($475) and coal cost pressure.

subsections.label: Blast furnace / pig iron capacity plan
points: Long-term plan is to set up one blast furnace in Koppal for steel, which will result in pig iron sales going down to 5 lakh tons instead of 6-7 lakh tons; blast furnace 2 will go for alloy steel production.
Plan to expand seamless tube plant in Baramati so entire steel blooms go to Baramati.
Opportunity exists at Hiriyur to upgrade the blast furnace to produce close to 3,00,000 tons of pig iron, either continuing as pig iron or moving into spun pipe or steel.
Phase 2 plan is to take both MBFs into steel.

subsections.label: Green power expansion
points: 35 MW solar plant to be commissioned by July-August and 25 MW wind plant by September, equivalent to about 90 MW of combined solar/wind (55+35).
Existing 70 MW plant in Jalna already up and running; will reduce CO2 emissions, positioning Jejuri as a green steel producer.
Preliminary work started on bringing in megawatt-level battery storage system to increase utilization of green power despite new regulations coming in Maharashtra.
Wind generation is stronger in monsoon while solar generation is weaker in monsoon — complementary generation profile.

subsections.label: Rolling mill and steel debottlenecking
points: Plan to debottleneck rolling mill to roll the entire 3 lakh tons; of that, 50,000-60,000 tons to go to Ahilyanagar and remaining 2,40,000 tons (20,000/month) for external (non-KFIL) sales.
Currently at 85,000 tons of external sales last year; effort is to expand external sales and internal consumption ahead of the new steel plant coming online.

subsections.label: Oxygen and PCI improvements
points: 150 TPD oxygen plant to be commissioned towards end of year, enhancing oxygen enrichment from 2.5% to 5%.
PCI level to increase from 130 kg to 160-170 kg, resulting in pig iron output increase and coal consumption reduction — productivity and cost benefit.

subsections.label: Tube mill capacity expansion
points: Capacity expansion in Baramati targets bigger size tubes; immediate next-year focus is capacity utilization improvement.
Basic study, design and source study completed for the biggest tube mill; project expected to complete within next 1.5 years.
Investment for the tube mill project could be 500+ crores, part of overall capex plan of INR600-700 crores per year covering pig iron, foundry, steel and tube projects.

subsections.label: Backward integration
points: Coke requirement fully met from own Coke Oven; 52 MW of waste heat recovery power running from blast furnace and Coke Oven.
Progressing on operationalizing Jambunath Gudda iron ore mines with very good quality iron ore, expected to help produce better quality prime pig iron.
Plans to bring in beneficiation and pellet plant once mines are operationalized, to use all kinds of iron ore and sell some pellet quantity in the market.
Backward integration strategy described as 'mine to machine castings' and 'mine to seamless tubes', with energy management as key to monetizing energy cost into future savings.

subsections.label: Cost inputs
points: Company always holds 3 months of coal; fourth month price will change with market.
Team is working on coal purchase commitments, coke price, production cost and margin impact for Q1 FY27 clarity.
Rising dollar (INR95) and coal price increase (~$25/ton) add cost pressure even as value addition and commodity price increases provide some offset.

subsections.label: Oliver merger
points: Company is working on merging Oliver into Kirloskar Ferrous Industries and looks forward to closing it in the next couple of months, so as to get merger benefit for FY25-26 itself.

subsections.label: Backward integration roadmap
points: Roadmap includes bridging the gap from pig iron to blast furnace steel to seamless tube (Baramati) and value-added Jejuri steel sold in market.
Own Coke Oven fully meets coke requirement; 52 MW waste heat recovery power running.

Investment of INR125-150 crores planned in Hiriyur to upgrade blast furnace capacity and bring manufacturing cost in line with Koppal via efficiency improvement/cost reduction, with payback period of less than 2 years.
Operationalizing Jambunath Gudda iron ore mines for better quality prime pig iron, followed by beneficiation and pellet plant investment.
Strategy described as 'mine to machine castings' and 'mine to seamless tubes' with energy management central to monetizing energy costs into future savings.

subsections.label: Alloy steel strategy
points: Long-term plan to convert one blast furnace in Koppal to steel, reducing pig iron sales to 5 lakh tons (from 6-7 lakh tons), with blast furnace 2 dedicated to alloy steel production.
Plan to expand seamless tube plant in Baramati so entire steel blooms go there.

Jejuri alloy steel currently uses ~30% green power; pushing to commission additional 35 MW solar (Jul-Aug) and 25 MW wind (Sep) power, equivalent to ~90 MW combined with existing 70 MW at Jalna, to reduce CO2 emissions and position as green steel producer.
Plans for debottlenecking rolling mill to roll entire 3 lakh tons capacity, splitting between Ahilyanagar (50,000-60,000 tons) and external/non-KFIL sales (2,40,000 tons).

subsections.label: External macro disruptions
points: Tariff period, war in the Middle East, Hormuz blockage, fuel cost increases and disruptions in many areas/places have affected demand and cost conditions.
In spite of these conditions, management remains optimistic about better demand position and continued growth.

subsections.label: Commodity price volatility
points: Pig iron commodity market has been terrible for the last 3 years (not just 1 year), with continuous price falls without a substantial fall in raw material prices.
Management expects that pain is over and prices should improve, though this needs to be watched closely.
International pig iron price at $475 is encouraging, but whether it converts to Indian pig iron price increases needs to be seen and how much of it is realizable is uncertain.

subsections.label: Cost inflation
points: Dollar has risen to INR95 and coal prices have risen by about $25 per ton on average, adding cost pressure even as some value addition offsets it.
Coking coal has further risen, affecting Q1 FY27 spread outlook; management is analyzing coal purchase commitments, coke price, production cost and margin impact.

subsections.label: Operational disruptions
points: Hiriyur blast furnace was stopped for almost 3.5 months during FY26 due to market conditions not being conducive, causing a ~68,000 ton production shortfall for the year.
One blast furnace took a 5-day stoppage during Q4, causing production loss.
Steel plant took two fortnight-long stoppages during the year for erection of primary and secondary fume extraction systems to improve environmental aspects.
Hiriyur did not get full quarter-4 volume due to start-up spillover from Oct-Dec into January.

subsections.label: Regulatory risk
points: New government regulations in Maharashtra could limit prime slot utilization of solar energy, prompting company to explore battery storage systems to improve wind/solar utilization.
Some regulation changes regarding utilization period are currently sub judice (in court), affecting realized power cost benefit calculations for FY26.

Management reaffirmed commitment to 1,80,000-1,85,000-1,90,000 MT target for FY26-27: Solapur to reach 60,000 tons, Koppal already over 1,05,000 tons, and Oliver contributing 25,000 tons.
Numbers referenced are production numbers, not exact sales numbers; small difference of 2-3% expected due to foundry stage rejection.
Management highlighted that last year casting production and sales increased by 23,000 tons, and this year the effort is for another ~25,000 ton increase.

subsections.label: FY27 overall growth outlook
points: Reversal of commodity price fall should help sales realization; efforts to increase volume in pig iron, casting, steel and tube continue.
Management looks forward to at least 15% growth once again in FY27, provided commodities do not fall again.

subsections.label: Tube guidance
points: Tube volume was 1,88,700 tons in FY26 vs 1,68,800 tons in FY25; company targets 10-11% volumetric growth from here.
On sales realization, expects to recover 5-6% of the ~10% value decline seen last year in tubes, aligned with NSR of ~1,13,000/ton, as pig iron, steel, power and fuel costs rise.

subsections.label: Pig iron production recovery
points: With a little improvement/positive contribution from Hiriyur, company expects to quickly return to ~7 lakh metric tons or at least 680,000-690,000 tons with current productivity levels.

key_takeaways: Quarter 4 pig iron production quantity was 1,58,152 metric ton compared to quarter 4 last year, 1,62,286 metric ton — lower by 3% compared to the last year.
Casting production is 36,596 metric ton against 32,474 ton, which is 13% higher than the last year.

Total year production last year '25-'26 was 6,23,939 metric tons against last year's 6,31,103 metric tons; major drop to the extent of 68,000 was because of stoppage of Hiriyur blast furnace for almost 3.5 months because of the market conditions not being conducive.
Total sales value for the quarter is INR 1,781 crores; year-end sales were INR6,861 crores against INR6,628 crores last year.
Profit before tax is INR514.43 crores against INR532 crores before exceptional item against INR432 crores, an improvement of about INR100 crores on the PBT.
Overall growth on the top line achieved was 3%, including Oliver about 5.1%, after accounting for the drop in sales realizations because of commodity prices being low.
Company is working for merger of Oliver into Kirloskar Ferrous Industries and looks forward to close it in the next couple of months so as to have the benefit of merger for the year '25-'26 itself.
Casting business demand remains robust from auto sector as well as the tractor sector; company expects to march forward to about 1,90,000 tons and is commissioning a sixth foundry.
3 new customers added to casting after 6 years of steady 26 customers, including a diesel engine manufacturer and 2 customers for tractor/earthmoving applications with export visibility.
Company is comfortable only when EBITDA is at 15%; currently just above 12.5%.

KIRLFER.about: KFIL, incorporated in 1991, is a part of the Pune-based Kirloskar Group. KFIL manufactures pig iron and ferrous castings such as cylinder blocks, cylinder heads, and transmission parts and different types of housings required by automobile, tractor and diesel engine industries. It is one of the leading players in foundry-grade pig iron manufacturing and ferrous castings in the domestic market.[1]

quarters.summary: Management flagged a stellar Q1 FY'27 performance with revenue and profitability improving sharply (~4x QoQ and ~12x YoY) driven by civil engineering strength, cost control, and automation-led productivity, even as Beryl remained roughly break-even and MES continued its restructuring. Management guided civil/core (ex-Beryl) revenue run-rate of Rs.240-250 crore for FY27 (already reiterated as achievable), EBITDA margin of at least 20-23% for FY27, PAT margin target of 15-16% (potentially higher once Beryl contributes), Beryl expected to break even in Q2 and turn EBITDA-positive from Q3, and a longer-term FY28 revenue target of Rs.300-350 crore aided by a planned structural-design acquisition; power/T&D (poles, towers, substations) business is seen scaling 3-5x over 2-3 years to $5-10 million with high margins, and management's 5-year aspiration is to become a full-service civil engineering (and eventually architectural) solutions provider via further acquisitions.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Almost 4x jump in profitability over Q4 and 12x over Q1 last year attributed to revenue increase, operational efficiency improvements and cost control, without Beryl contributing to the bottom line.

Two sustainable drivers cited for margin improvement: (1) reduction in non-performing automobile engineering (MES) division headcount and associated expensive software/other costs, and (2) high automation brought into operations along with an incentive system driving higher productivity, visible over the last 3-5 months — both described as long-term in nature, not one-time.
MTM (mark-to-market) losses that hit the prior quarter did not recur this quarter; instead there was an FX gain of about Rs.1-1.2 crore as the rupee strengthened slightly against a stable dollar.
Other expenses declined due to reduced employee cost from MES automobile downsizing, lower software costs, and no MTM loss this quarter (versus prior quarter).

subsections.label: PAT margin trajectory
points: Management targets maintaining 15-16% PAT margin, with potential to move up once Beryl starts contributing meaningfully to the bottom line.
Beryl's own PAT margin is expected to remain lower (at most ~10%) versus the standalone Indian business which can be higher; consolidated PAT margin trajectory depends on Beryl's contribution mix.

subsections.label: Work-on-hand as demand indicator
points: Management treats 'work on hand' at end of quarter as the key demand/workflow indicator for the technologies business (analogous to EBITDA per kg in packaging), rather than seasonality, because project flow determines utilization of the team.
Civil work on hand at $4.4-4.5 million (vs $2.7-3.7 million/$3.5 million last year) gives confidence for continued positive performance in the next quarter.

Beryl's work on hand is described as immaterial/not tracked because its projects are small (each $5,000-$20,000) and completed within a week or 10 days, unlike Mold-Tek Inc.'s structural steel projects ($20,000-$500,000 each, lasting 3 months to 1 year).
MES work on hand accumulated at any time used to be less than a quarter million during the EV downturn — cited as a negative indicator that led to the restructuring.

subsections.label: MES/BIW restructuring
points: MES division has bled for the last couple of years; last financial year overall MES loss was ~Rs.7-8 crore due to holding people and software in anticipation of an EV market revival that has not materialized.
Team downsized from 125-130 people a year ago to 50-60 now; expensive EV-specific software costs and resources let go; some staff shifted into poles/towers/substation design.

Company intends to keep a thin team of 50-60 in EV/automobile design to retain knowledge for whenever the EV market recovers (expected in 2-3 years), while this team is now reasonably occupied versus previously idling.

MES was profitable only in FY22 and FY23 (and partly FY23-24); for the remaining ~5-6 years, uneven workflow (projects for 3 months, none for next 3 months) caused unprofitability, prompting the restructuring to a leaner, more consistently-loaded team.

subsections.label: Power distribution / T&D (MES) growth
points: New contract signed with the number one power distribution company in the USA amid data-center-driven demand for power transmission/distribution work; team started with ~10 people, growing to 20-30.

This MSA-based work is expected to generate about $1 million per annum with very good margins over the next 12 months (from August), with potential to expand into other lines of activity with the same client in future years.

Overall sector opportunity for substation/pole/tower design outsourcing from the US is estimated at $200-300 million (with the broader in-house market at $0.5-1 billion, of which ~$100 million is outsourced); Mold-Tek's addressable share is estimated at $5-10 million per annum, not $100 million.

Current run-rate for this vertical (poles/towers + substations) is about $2 million; management expects 3x-5x growth over the next 2-3 years given robust demand from data-center-linked infrastructure buildout.

Engineers are being trained (content and videos created) in American electrical line distribution design conventions to ramp capacity faster; some automobile-design staff are being shifted into this line.

subsections.label: Beryl acquisition integration
points: Beryl remains near break-even and did not contribute to bottom line this quarter; expected to reach break-even in Q2 and turn EBITDA-positive from Q3 as the India-based design team becomes operational.
Beryl's design team creation has been in process for 6-7 months; team now executing projects for Florida clients, expected to become margin-positive from Q3 onward.

Beryl historically limited operations to Florida; now expanding into Georgia (Atlanta), having been newly listed as an approved engineering service provider there — expected to widen its addressable client base (residential permitting, insurance claims, inspections) and roughly double the number of contracts over time, benefits accruing from Q3/Q4.

Beryl received a $1 million Master Purchase Order from Hillsborough County (received last month), providing a steadier flow of work over the next 12 months from July; this is apart from regular day-to-day residential orders.

Beryl's revenue growth has been constrained partly by internal disruption (loss of 2 of 38 staff, both in the design function) and partly by external demand impact from a 4-5 month US government funding shutdown earlier in the year affecting government-funded projects (Jan-May); workflow expected to improve now that funding has reopened.

Beryl's business today is dominated by permits, inspections and approvals (design revenue insignificant); once the India-based design team is in place, clients seeking permits/inspections could also be sold design services, potentially lifting monthly design revenue from $20,000-$30,000 to $200,000-$500,000 and lifting the ~10% EBITDA margin ceiling upward over time — this shift may take about another year.

Original Beryl promoters were expected (per acquisition MoU) to subscribe to warrants within 6 months (lapsed in April); they declined as the 6-month average price ($165) was well above the current market price (~$130), and management stated it will not press them to invest their own money; no incremental inclusion plan from their end currently expected.

Beryl's BD/sales team (3-person engineer team in Atlanta) is being trained to also market Mold-Tek's core structural design/detailing services in the US, leveraging local American presence and credibility with contractors/fabricators; contribution expected from Q3 onward after a couple of months of presentation/training.

One PE is planned to relocate from India to Florida from October/November (pending L1 visa) to join the existing 4-member Beryl design team for front-ending work; back-end India team (currently 6-8) to scale to 15-20 as growth materializes.
Florida residential permits declined ~10% YoY, an industry headwind noted alongside the government-shutdown impact.

subsections.label: M&A strategy for structural design capability
points: Company is in talks to acquire a US structural engineering design firm (with both structural steel and residential design background, ~7-8 PEs, ~15 engineers total) to complement Beryl's strength in permits/residential work and Mold-Tek's strength in detailing/connection design, aiming to become a complete civil engineering service provider.
Deal size/valuation details not yet disclosed as discussions are at an early stage; management noted no unusual inflation in PE valuation multiples despite rising capex-driven demand.

Rationale: building an in-house US PE team from scratch is 'next to impossible' given difficulty finding experienced PEs willing to work for an Indian-owned company; acquiring an established ~15-20 person firm with 15-20+ years of existence provides deep-rooted general-contractor relationships and a proven project track record that would otherwise take 10 years (5-10 years by another reference) to build organically.

Target profile: team of 10-20 employees, about half PEs/SEs, since very small 2-3 person PE practices (e.g., 2 PEs and 5-6 engineers in a small town) lack capacity for big projects while very large construction companies are not suitable acquisition targets.

Timeline: CEO Prasad returning to the US on 16th August to engage target company; Chairman traveling to meet them in late September; potential decision (deal or drop) expected around October, with possibility of closing within this calendar year — management cautioned against firm date commitments given past delays.

Once a structural design acquisition is completed, the combined entity (design + detailing + connection design + permits) could charge fees as a percentage of project cost (2-3%, versus 3-5% industry benchmark for combined structural+architecture) rather than hourly rates — a materially different, higher-margin commercial model versus Mold-Tek's current outsourced/piecemeal engagement with erectors and fabricators.

5-year aspiration: become a complete total-solution civil engineering provider (commercial, residential, government-funded projects) and eventually add architectural services (also via acquisition) to cover projects from inception to completion, billed on a percentage-of-project-cost basis.

Company has already executed a couple of data-center structural design projects over the last 1-1.5 years and is actively marketing further data-center structural work using this track record; the planned acquisition is expected to further strengthen the value proposition for data-center and other large projects.

Beryl lost 2 staff at the end of November as part of the integration disruption; Beryl's design support team currently stands at 6 people, with 4 currently front-ending in the US and a 5-6 person Atlanta office team assisting execution; the Atlanta BD team numbers three.

subsections.label: Key risks flagged
points: EV/automobile design market has shown no real turnaround as of today, prompting continued downsizing of that team (kept at a thin 50-60 headcount to retain domain knowledge for an eventual EV recovery expected in 2-3 years).

Beryl's growth was affected by a US government funding shutdown lasting 4-5 months (Jan-May) impacting government-funded residential permitting/inspection projects, a demand-side headwind now easing as funding has reopened.

Beryl lost 2 of 38 staff (both in design) during acquisition integration, creating a setback in building design capability; replaced partly via local outsourced hires, which do not generate cost arbitrage until the India-based team is fully ramped.
Finding and acquiring the right US structural design firm has proven difficult and time-consuming in the past, with risk of continued delay if a suitable target/fit is not identified.

Beryl's original promoters declined to subscribe to warrants under the acquisition MoU as the required subscription price ($165, based on 6-month average) was well above the current market price (~$130), reflecting share price volatility risk; management stated it will not compel further investment.

Historical MES workflow volatility (projects for 3 months, none for the next 3 months) caused significant uncertainty and losses over 5-6 of the last 7-8 years, which the current restructuring aims to address.

subsections.label: Forward outlook
points: Management reiterated confidence that Rs.240-250 crore ex-Beryl revenue for FY27 is achievable, having already delivered Rs.61 crore in Q1 with similar momentum expected in Q2.

EBITDA margin guided to reach at least 20%, potentially 23%, up from 11% in FY26 (last year; alternatively cited as 16% in one reference), driven by cost control, automation and Beryl's eventual contribution.
PAT margin target maintained at 15-16%, with potential upside once Beryl scales; Beryl itself is capped at around a 10% PAT margin, while the standalone Indian business can exceed that level.

FY28 (next year) directional target of Rs.300-350 crore, contingent on completing a planned structural-design acquisition; management declined to give a precise number given inherent business dynamism.
Beryl expected to break even in Q2 FY27 and turn EBITDA-positive from Q3, with a longer-term (next year, if not this year) potential to add $0.5-0.75 million to the bottom line.
Power/T&D vertical (poles, towers, substations) guided to grow 3x-5x over the next 2-3 years toward a $5-10 million annual revenue ceiling for Mold-Tek, with high margins.
New power-distribution client MSA expected to generate about $1 million per annum over the next 12 months, with potential to expand into other activity lines with the same client in future years.
Structural design firm acquisition targeted to potentially close within this calendar year (decision expected around October), which would support the FY28 growth target.

points: Main contributors for Q4 growth are Beryl numbers added in top line for the last five months, plus improvement in civil work-on-hand and execution of quantum of work in the Civil Structural Division.

subsections.label: FX / Hedging policy
points: Depreciation impact stems from forward contracts done in the past at various levels (85, 89, 92) being marked-to-market; this is an accounting-standard-mandated notional loss, not an actual cash loss.
Rupee moved from ~INR 83.42 at start of FY (Q1 2024-25) to INR 95 by year end, ~INR 10 depreciation over the year, with premium of only about INR 3.
Company decided to stop 100% forward hedging and limit forwards to 25%-50% of turnover going forward, since previously some years produced INR 2-3 crore profits but this year fully went adverse.
In response to analyst feedback, company plans to separate operational EBITDA from MTM gains/losses reporting starting this financial year to give clearer picture of operational margins.
As of mid-Q1 FY27, rupee is at 95.5 vs 95.15 at March 31 close; management expects only a few lakh of MTM loss in Q1 FY27, not like the INR 4 crore hit in Q4.

subsections.label: Receivables / Debtors
points: Debtors increased in line with 81% Q4 YoY revenue jump (INR 32.6 crore to INR 59 crore).
September receivables (INR 30 crore) did not include Beryl; only December numbers included two months of Beryl (November-December), as November 1 was effective acquisition date.
March receivables (INR 41 crore) include acquisition-related costs recognized in Q4.

subsections.label: Preferential allotment cancellation

This was an independent transaction (investor showed interest to invest separately) not directly tied to Beryl purchase consideration.
Regulatory deadline for fund transfer was May 31 (BSE/NSE), and allotment was cancelled on April 30 as funds were not transferred.
Separately, about 30% of Beryl acquisition monies were kept in lock-in as a standby guarantee, contingent on a minimum working/continued-service period of 3 years for Richard Lyon and team.

Employee cost stood at 73% of revenue for FY26, inclusive of Beryl's five-month numbers.

Acquisition due diligence and legal/auditor fees for Beryl were required (per Companies Act) to be expensed upfront rather than capitalized, causing a one-time hit to consolidated numbers; this contribution effect will normalize/turn positive in coming quarters.

Construction ('raking the ground') expected to start in June, building expected ready by end of financial year.
Expected cost savings of approximately INR 2 to 2.5 crore per annum accruing in FY 2027-2028.

subsections.label: Business evolution / history
points: Until 2010, company mainly provided Engineering Services for Pre-Engineering Metal Buildings (PEMB) - industrial and commercial sheds - a lower end of the engineering services spectrum.

After acquiring RMM (2008) and Crossroads (2011), company entered structural steel detailing for high-rise commercial/residential buildings and industrial plants, which remains the main revenue contributor today.
PEMB has shrunk to about 5% of revenue from being a larger share historically.

MES (Mechanical Engineering Services) started about 10 years ago with poles and towers/electrical structures, later diversified into automotive BIW (Body in White) work for companies including Tesla, BMW, Mercedes, Skoda via Tier-1 vendors, providing robotic manufacturing simulation support in 2D/3D.
BIW automobile projects grew rapidly until 2023 but have seen a tremendous demand drop over the last two years as EVs have not taken off as expected and new model introductions slowed.

Company has moved into structural designing (connection design, and some member design) beyond pure detailing, adding higher value-added services; recent Beryl acquisition (Tampa, November 2025) added residential building design, inspections, and expert services with a 40-member team.

subsections.label: Detailing vs. Design distinction
points: Structural design involves designing building members (columns, beams, purlins) for safety against wind, earth, and soil loads based on architect's building size/dimensions; must be certified by a Professional Engineer (PE) licensed per US state.
Company has PEs certified to stamp drawings in more than 20 US states.
Detailing means providing complete fabrication/erection drawings (dimensions of columns, beams, connection plates, gusset plates) coded for shop floor manufacture and site erection sequence.
Design services command far higher billing rates ($70-80/hour even outsourced to India) versus detailing ($25-30/hour).

Sales approach differs: fabricators are primary contacts for detailing (they are responsible for erection); for design services, builders and architects become primary contacts; Engineer on Record (EOR, appointed by builder) is consulted in both cases.

subsections.label: MES restructuring rationale
points: BIW auto team bled profitability for ~1.5-2 years due to reduced automobile workflow amid EV transition and delayed new model launches, causing more than INR 7 crore of losses in the last financial year.
Team downsized from 160 to 60 people gradually starting January, completed by end of March; downsizing does not apply to poles/towers/electrical substation work which is ramping up rapidly in the US.
MES automobile team fully closed from April 1 (last operational date March 31); this loss-making segment is no longer contributing losses going forward.
MES Europe exposure: more than 50% of mechanical projects were from Europe (automobile companies); now with focus shifting to poles/towers/substations, 80-90% of that work comes from the US.

subsections.label: Civil / structural design growth ambitions
points: Management aims for structural design to reach 30-40% of revenue within 3-4 years, given design's higher value-add versus detailing.
Company is at the verge of breaking into full project design work with better hourly rates, aided by references from partial design contributions on various buildings.

Considering both organic (internal design team build-up) and inorganic (acquisition) growth paths; in talks with a company near Atlanta office for a high-rise structural design acquisition, though nothing concluded yet.

Portfolio gap: current design capability (via Beryl) does not cover high-rise buildings, only up to 3-storied residential/small commercial buildings; company still seeking to acquire a high-rise design capability.

subsections.label: Beryl integration and outsourcing
points: 5 months into Beryl integration (effective November 2025), not a single person from the 40-member team has resigned, attributed to company's HR practices and prior acquisition experience.

Two Mold-Tek engineers currently in Tampa; four people trained in India; combined 6-member team joined Beryl's design function (originally only 6 of 40 people were in design, now growing toward 12) to enhance design services which are more revenue-generative than inspection.

Beryl's sales team (4 members, 10-15 years experience in US structural design/drafting/inspection) is expected to be leveraged to cross-sell/support core Mold-Tek steel detailing and design services, seen as a near-term synergy alongside longer-term residential design synergy.
Beryl team members visiting India and Mold-Tek's Atlanta office to understand operations and pitch for projects.
Beryl revenue potential: management targeting growth from ~$5.6 million to $7 million driven by deploying additional India-based design resources (not just existing order backlog).
About 50% of Beryl's work (excluding inspection, which is ~50% and not outsourceable) can gradually be outsourced to India; design portion is fully outsourceable.

Beryl inspection revenue linked partly to Florida regulatory mandates (FEMA, FDEM government projects, and analyst-raised SB 4-D condominium inspection mandate); first phase of inspections largely completed with payments received recently; second phase increasingly converting into design work as defects are found in inspected buildings, though a government shutdown delayed progress for several months before recently restarting.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Ovation (a competitor) started later but scaled via acquisition of a small Atlanta-area detailing company (8-10 members) then building an India team; despite being 8-9 years old, Ovation's revenue is about half of Mold-Tek's, with higher percentage growth attributable to smaller base.

Compared to Beryl's productivity monitoring practices (e.g., 'Internal Eye Support' tool), Mold-Tek is adopting weekly (vs monthly) productivity monitoring and stricter shift vigilance, yielding 10-15% productivity improvement in April; an incentive-based mechanism is also being designed.

Company distinguishes itself from Pinnacle Infotech, which focuses on BIM (Building Information Modeling - electrical, plumbing, mechanical, auxiliary equipment services) rather than structural detailing/design; Mold-Tek has a small 5-10 person BIM team but views BIM as a crowded, low-value 'CAD-like' market and not a strategic standalone focus.

subsections.label: Talent / attrition management
points: Attrition rate in India is in double digits but not very high, managed through in-house training/recruitment team and a portal ('almanac') for final-year engineering students.

Company recruits 60-75 engineers annually from colleges (8-10% of employee strength) to build a trained pipeline against attrition, since staff need training in American standards (95% of civil projects are American; 50%+ of mechanical projects historically European, shifting to 80-90% US via poles/towers work).

subsections.label: Interarch/Affordable Robotic Partnership
points: US-India trade talks remain in limbo, creating uncertainty on duties/tariffs that would apply to buildings made by Interarch (with Mold-Tek providing other services); this uncertainty is preventing US customers keen to use Indian Interarch buildings (to save costs) from proceeding, so nothing much is happening on this revenue opportunity.

subsections.label: AI threat assessment
points: Management views AI as having limited disruptive role in structural design/detailing for at least 5-10 years, as no one will risk constructing a building based on AI-generated data; buildings must be engineer-designed, detailer-checked, and plant-fabricated.

Company is a service provider using third-party software (SDS, Tekla, Pro-E, SOLIDWORKS) rather than a software developer; any AI-based tools adopted by these vendors would be leveraged by Mold-Tek given its 20 years of field experience.

Potential AI impact estimated at reducing headcount by 5-10% (e.g., from ~1,000 to 800-900) rather than a software-company-style disruption, mainly in checking/QA functions (checker, modeler, QA - three levels of checking).
Company currently has zero back-charges, cited as evidence of near-100% quality, implying limited need for/impact from AI-driven quality improvement.

subsections.label: Beryl acquisition rationale
points: Beryl acquisition (completed November 2025) is described as strategic, not a sign of desperation, given the company has zero debt and INR 25-30 crore of deposits.

Beryl adds residential-side design/inspection capability with PEs and qualified staff, expanding portfolio beyond industrial and high-rise to individual residential buildings, small (1+1, 1+2, up to 3-storied) offices, shops, and schools.

Under recent Companies Act provisions, acquisition due diligence costs (auditor fees, legal fees) had to be expensed in Q1 of consolidation (Q3 for this deal), which made consolidated numbers appear more negative than the underlying business performance.
About 30% of Beryl acquisition consideration was held in lock-in as a standby guarantee, contingent on the seller/promoter (Richard Lyon) and team continuing service for a minimum of 3 years.

subsections.label: Further M&A pipeline
points: Company is in talks with a company located near its Atlanta office for a possible high-rise structural design acquisition, though nothing concluded.

Management is pursuing both organic (in-house design team build-up) and inorganic (acquisition) growth paths to expand structural design capability, since current portfolio (via Beryl) does not cover high-rise design.

subsections.label: Flagged risks
points: BIW automotive segment demand has structurally declined for ~2 years due to slow EV adoption and delayed new model launches, causing recurring annual losses of INR 7-8 crore before the recent team downsizing.

Rupee depreciation risk: forward contracts taken in the past at various rate levels caused a large MTM loss (~INR 4 crore in Q4, ~INR 7 crore for the full year) when rupee depreciated from ~83.42 to ~95 over the year; premiums received (~INR 3) did not offset the depreciation.
US-India trade talks uncertainty is stalling the Interarch/Affordable Robotic Partnership revenue opportunity, as customers are unwilling to commit given unknown future duties/tariffs.

Preferential allotment to Beryl promoter Richard Lyon was cancelled after he declined to invest due to price differential (issue price INR 164 vs market price ~INR 130 at time of BSE approval) and market conditions.
Government shutdown in the US caused a multi-month (five-six months) slowdown in Beryl's second-phase design-related project inflow (post-inspection), though work is now restarting.
AI is a longer-term watch item, though management does not view it as a near-term disruptive threat to detailing/design given regulatory/liability constraints on AI-based construction.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Management projects FY27 revenue of ~INR 250 crore, derived from Beryl contribution of ~INR 25 crore plus 10-15% organic growth on core business, and cross-checked via Q4 FY26 run-rate of INR 59 crore x 4 = ~INR 240 crore.
EBITDA margin projected to move from 11% (FY26) to at least 15% in FY27, aided by removal of MES/BIW losses (INR 7-8 crore annual drag) and improved Civil Engineering Services (CES) work flow.
Standalone/core India business (MES + Civil) expected to grow 15-20% with EBITDA margin in the region of 15-16%, following curtailment of excess MES staff.
Beryl margins expected to remain around 8-10% next year, as it will take a couple more quarters to add real design value from India and take on substantial India-executed design work.

Productivity improvement of 10-15% already achieved in April (from weekly monitoring, stricter shift vigilance, incentive-based mechanisms borrowed from Beryl practices); target is at least 20% productivity improvement for FY27.
Nashik office expected to generate INR 2-2.5 crore annual cost savings starting FY2027-28.
Q1 FY27 MTM loss expected to be minimal (a few lakh) versus the INR 4 crore hit in Q4 FY26, given rupee has been relatively stable (95.5 vs 95.15 at March 31).

guidance_ledger.statement: Do you think INR 250 crore top line is a realistic number? ... hitting INR 250 crores I think is certainly possible.
EBITDA margin should move from 11% to at least 15% is our projection.

Our engineering services from India, now that we have curtailed the excess staff in MES, both the MES and civil from India, that's our core business, standalone business, will certainly go up by at least 15%-20% and EBITDA in the region of 15%-16%.
This year I would conservatively take it at around 8%-10% margin for Baryl [next year].
Our target is to improve productivity by at least 20% in this financial year.
This year, it should cross $1.5 million to $2 million.
Right now, in terms of Baryl, you are expecting from $5 million to $7 million mark ... yes [driven by scaling up Indian team to enhance design services].
It can reach a level of about $0.5 million in the next one year's time per annum.
Probably the cost savings of around INR 2 crores - INR 2.5 crores per annum can accrue in the next financial year, 2027-2028.
That is now stopped. The team has been closed from April 1st ... which itself can add about INR 7 crores to INR 8 crores back to the profitability.
There will be a little bit, a few lakhs of MTM losses, but not like INR 4 crores which we suffered in Q4.

themes.label: Beryl acquisition integration
themes.note: Beryl added revenue and zero attrition in 5 months, but one-time acquisition costs and low seasonal quarter weighed on Q4 profitability; targeted to scale from $5.6M to $7M via India design support.

themes.label: Design mix upgrade
themes.note: Structural design (currently 8-10% of civil revenue vs 100% detailing 3-4 years ago) targeted to reach 30-40% of revenue in 3-4 years given higher billing rates ($70-80/hr vs $25-30/hr for detailing).

themes.label: Civil order book growth
themes.note: CES work-on-hand grew ~60-70% YoY from $2.5-2.84 million to $5 million, driving improved execution and capacity needs.

themes.label: M&A strategy for structural design capability

key_takeaways: I am very glad to inform you that there is a good turnaround in Q4. While last year, Q4, we made a loss of about INR 1.6 crores, this year we ended up with a profit of INR 2.28 crores, in spite of a huge MTM loss of INR 4 crores on rupee depreciation.
The overall year ended up at INR 10 crores total profitability, PAT as against INR 12.16 crores last year, a drop of 17%.

Main contributors for growth are Beryl numbers in the top line for the last five months have been added. And apart from that, there is a wonderful improvement in civil work on hand and the execution of quantum of work, which has been done in the Civil Structural Division.

We have taken a call on reduction of MES mainly in BIW auto sector ... the team has been downsized from 160 to 60. Whereas the good news in MES is poles and towers and electrical substation work is ramping up rapidly in the United States, and the team from 45 to 50 people last year are currently around 80 people and growing.

The line of BIW automobile has been curtailed considerably starting from end of March ... which in fact caused more than a INR 7 crore loss during the last financial year. So, that will not be there going forward in future.

Coming to the next positive development is the work on hand for civil work has increased substantially over the last quarter. While the last year's beginning of the month, it was about 4 million, it has gone up to 5 million at the end of this quarter.

The EBITDA is INR 20 crores now, down from INR 23 crores last year ... PBT for the full year is INR 13.5 and PAT is INR 10.57 crores. Consolidated also EBITDA is INR 19.64 crores and PAT is INR 10.09 crores.
This quarter itself we have done INR 59 crores. So, multiplying by 4, you will see INR 240 crores is easily feasible ... hitting INR 250 crores I think is certainly possible.
I think EBITDA margin should move from 11% to at least 15% is our projection.
pressing_questions: This year our EBITDA fell to the level last seen 11 years back in 2015, which is INR 10 crores ... I hope in FY27 it will not become INR 5 crore EBITDA.
Now, sir, also now 2.9 lakh preferential share that were issued at INR 164 that has also been cancelled. So, that also is a huge vote of no confidence in the company.

So, now our receivables also have jumped a lot on a year-on-year basis. They have basically doubled whereas our revenues have hardly increased by 40%. So, I hope this is a temporary answer. I hope it is not out of desperation that we are just going out and doing acquisitions because the standalone business is going nowhere.

Is there any way to figure out where we are in that timeline because if we are still in the middle or beginning of this tailwind of revenues, that would be great. But if we are sort of at the end of it, then maybe Baryl revenues would decline going forward.
Sir, what is the threat that you see from AI now? You see the IT index itself is at 3-year lows and all the big giants are at multi-year lows. So, where does it leave a small company like ours?

MOLDTECH.about: Incorporated in 1985, Moldtek Technologies Ltd provides Civil and Mechanical Engineering Design Services[1]

quarters.summary: Apollo Micro Systems reported its highest-ever standalone June-quarter revenue and margins, announced a landmark ~INR1,550 crore acquisition of a 41.33% promoter stake in Premier Explosives to build an integrated missile/weapon value chain, and flagged large near-term order inflows expected from QRSAM, MIGM, Pinaka, and Akash-NG during FY27, with execution/production for QRSAM and MIGM starting from the next financial year. Management reiterated a 40-45% topline growth guidance (standalone and consolidated) and guided consolidated order book to reach INR3,500-4,000 crore by year end, while flagging Ideal Explosives losses, promoter pledge reduction (targeted by Q1FY28), and continued reliance on defense procurement cycles as key watch items.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 Highlights
points: Closed the best June quarter in company history, delivering highest standalone revenue, EBITDA and PAT margins.

At consolidated level, growth is described as strong given long procurement cycles; management emphasizes year-on-year over quarter-on-quarter comparisons due to milestone-based execution of defence contracts causing uneven quarterly revenue recognition.
PAT growth outpaced topline growth at the standalone level, delivering the highest-ever PAT for a June quarter.

subsections.label: Fund Utilization
points: Of total funds raised (~INR3,300 crore), approximately INR2,500 crore is earmarked for the Premier Explosives acquisition, ~INR500 crore for working capital debt, and the remainder for general corporate purposes.

subsections.label: R&D Spend Clarification
points: Management initially misquoted R&D as 4% of revenue during the call, then corrected at closing: last financial year (FY26) R&D investment was INR72.53 crore against revenue of INR764 crore, translating to ~9.5% of revenue.
Average R&D spend has traditionally been 6% to 8% of revenue over the last 3-4 years.
