MIGM expected Apollo share of order

subsections.label: Order Book Composition
points: Consolidated order book of INR1,704 crores includes Ideal Explosives order book of INR480 crores, reflecting healthy and robust orders across the group.
Premier Explosives is in CCI (Competition Commission of India) approval mode; management cannot comment on its futuristic order book.

subsections.label: QRSAM Order Pipeline
points: Bidding and negotiation for QRSAM has completed; Bharat Electronics (BEL) expected to take the order anytime, after which the missile portion order flows to BDL.
Apollo is supplying complete guidance system, onboard computer, and front-end/rear actuation system — almost 5 sub-systems for QRSAM.

subsections.label: MIGM Order Pipeline
points: DAC approval has been received; Indian Navy expected to initiate discussions with Apollo and BDL before floating inquiry, expected next month end.
20% advance payment provision viewed as a strong encouragement for the company.

subsections.label: Other Large Programs
points: Akash-NG: 1,000 numbers already cleared by MoD, expected this financial year.
Pinaka: 2,000 numbers being negotiated by Indian Army with 2-3 vendors, negotiation already completed; orders expected anytime.
QRSAM and MIGM orders expected this financial year, with partial Pinaka orders also expected this financial year.
Execution for QRSAM and MIGM will start only from the next financial year.

subsections.label: Order Execution Commentary
points: Current order book is spread across this financial year with partial spillover into next financial year.
Management declined to disclose which specific orders are currently under execution.

subsections.label: Ideal Explosives (Bulk Explosives / Coal India)
points: Q4 FY26 was EBITDA positive for Ideal; Q1 FY27 is PAT positive but profitability remains low.

After the Coal India ban was lifted, Ideal participated only in select circles of Coal India where margins could be justified in the shrinking-margin bulk explosives business, resulting in lower volumes this time as it is primarily a volumetric business.

Manufacturing of various accessories previously made by erstwhile parent GOCL will start in Ideal within the next couple of quarters, expected to add benefit to bulk explosives supply and improve margins.
Cost and overhead measures related to post-acquisition integration of Ideal have already been taken up, significantly reducing multiple overheads; further measures planned.
Restructuring process ongoing; management reiterates it will take at least 3-4 quarters to bring Ideal to full profitability, expected to be fully positive from the next financial year.

New components will be manufactured under already-obtained licenses; infrastructure augmentation is in process post-Apollo takeover; as new plants start, revenue mix is expected to change and improve overall numbers.

subsections.label: Premier Explosives Synergy on Product Profile
points: Prior to Premier acquisition, Apollo depended on third parties (e.g., MIL) for explosive requirements for programs like MIGM; post-acquisition, Apollo will have its own explosive facility, speeding up production activity.
Current consumption of explosives and propellants in existing business is minuscule but expected to increase from next financial year as MIGM and other rocket-class orders ramp up.
In-house production (post-Premier) expected to improve margins versus outsourced/arm's-length basis, though comparative margin levels cannot yet be quantified due to low current consumption.
Acquisition does not change the product profile itself, but changes the scope of the product (i.e., in-house explosive/propellant capability).

subsections.label: Smart Bomb / Precision Guided Munitions
points: Working with Pinaka (surface-to-surface) and a program called TARA (air-to-surface/air-to-air) to make smart bombs with guidance and range extension.
Air Force holds thousands of dumb bomb inventory under modernization scheme seeking conversion to smart bombs — described as a big requirement.
500 kg smart bomb Air Force Make-II program has nothing to do with Premier Explosives directly; only the guidance/range-extension portion may leverage Premier support.

subsections.label: Autonomous Systems / Underwater Vehicles
points: SAVIOR semi-submersible autonomous vessel (ASW) is a next-generation ISR requirement from Indian Navy; multiple building blocks already developed and proven on other programs.
Company plans to build a swarm of autonomous USVs under a new program that has already commenced activity.
This financial year and next, company will heavily invest in autonomy across land, air, and sea segments.
Autonomous systems program (PSO, SAVIOR) is currently 'pure Apollo' and not integrated with Premier or Ideal.
Aerial bombs (1kg to 25kg range, 9 variants) already established with testing completed and acceptance recently received; drones and other platforms to be pursued via tie-ups with other companies.

subsections.label: Naval Mines
points: Moored mine: combat trials already completed; handover to Indian Navy expected anytime this month; technical trials yet to complete, hence orders expected only next financial year (not this year).
Limpet mine: already completed; orders expected from Q4 onwards this financial year.
Company expects to sign DCP (Development-cum-Production) partnership contract for moored mine within next 2 weeks.

subsections.label: Safety and Detonation Device (SDD)
points: Indigenously designed and developed SDD successfully handed over to Indian Navy with 100% indigenous content.
SDD strengthens potential across MRO and future weapon/missile programs, offering cost savings and reduced import dependence.

subsections.label: SAVIOR ASW Program
points: Received Make-II prototype sanction order from Indian Navy for SAVIOR Anti-Submarine Warfare system, a semi-submersible autonomous vessel for intelligence operations and reconnaissance.
Program strengthens position in autonomous maritime systems, opening doors to next-generation underwater surveillance, intelligence, and ASW capabilities.

subsections.label: IPREC / IPREK Program
points: Indian Air Force has recognized Apollo as prime development agency for IPREC program under Make-II category of DPP 2020.
System converts a 'dumb bomb' into a precision range-extension and precision-guided bomb.
IPREC is primarily a conversion system; no explosive or propulsion requirement (unlike SDD, which has minuscule explosive requirement).

subsections.label: Make-II Program Timelines
points: Customer expectation is to complete the two PSOs (Pilot/Program Sanction Orders) under Make-II within a span of 18 months, potentially with some spillover.
Post-completion, an order can be expected within a year's time from there.
Indian Navy expects delivery/timelines next financial year.

subsections.label: Anti-Drone Make-II Program
points: Anti-drone Make-II order (from July 2024) yet to go for trials; company is preparing for trials.
No pre-commitment for orders exists; after successful trials, opportunity and requirement flow follows.
TAM for this opportunity is dynamically changing; management expects to give updated guidance around the December-ending quarter once trial clarity improves.

subsections.label: Kusha Program
points: 150 km range version recently tested successfully; company expects an appreciation letter from the Prime Minister's Office very soon.
Apollo's contribution includes 7 very critical sub-systems, including critical actuation systems (front-end, rear-end) and other onboard systems.
Conversion into firm order may take 2-3 years; program is on a fast track.
Two more range versions (250 km and 500 km) expected to undergo DRDO trials in the next few months.

subsections.label: R&D and IP Strategy
points: Company builds further capability in areas where it already has strength by investing in R&D, and partners/allies with industry or academia where it lacks capability.
Significant advisors include retired DRDO scientists; partnerships with academia for deep research requirements.
Existing proven IP building blocks in both hardware and software underpin the strategy.

subsections.label: Unit III Facility
points: Building a huge new facility (Unit III); first phase production has already started.
Complete/final production activity expected to start before March 2027.
Once total capacity is operational and fully utilized, future plans will be finalized; company also looking at export opportunities via this facility.

Unit 3 expected to be fully commissioned and ready to occupy export opportunities in the next couple of quarters; once ready, export orders will be accepted and company will get more aggressive on exports.

subsections.label: Ideal / Premier Integration Plans
points: Company planning number of new production plants at Ideal and additional integration facilities at Premier.
Future integration plan to be announced in the next 2-3 months, noting the plan has changed following the Premier acquisition.

At present, Apollo, Ideal, and Premier explosives businesses will operate separately; no merger decision has been made — management will comment further once the Premier acquisition is complete over a few quarters.

subsections.label: TNT/Propellant / Explosive Capacity
points: Post-Premier acquisition, Apollo will have its own explosive facility rather than depending on third-party suppliers such as MIL for programs like MIGM.

subsections.label: Export Strategy and Process
points: Export revenue currently nil; hence no margin comparison possible versus domestic orders.
Exports are expected to be direct orders from various friendly countries, subject to approval from the ministry for each specific item and country combination.
Company has already started submitting offers for various mature product lines to different customers.
Company has been going slow on export opportunities requiring mass production until Unit 3 is fully commissioned (expected in next couple of quarters).
Meaningful breakthrough export orders possible this financial year, but no firm commitment; sizable export orders expected for sure next financial year.
Export opportunities, once realized, will be excluded/additional to the overall revenue growth guidance already given.

subsections.label: Autonomous Systems Market Size
points: Management declines to give firm order-size commentary but notes that even if 2-3 players enter the fray and prove capability, everyone could still enjoy a few thousand crores worth of orders in the autonomy space.

subsections.label: HAL / Tejas Related Orders
points: HAL orders currently around INR100-150 crores; Apollo participates in Tejas Mark 1 with only a couple of systems; expecting an additional ~INR150 crores order from HAL.

subsections.label: Premier Explosives Acquisition
points: Entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 41.33% promoter stake in Premier Explosives Limited for approximately INR1,550 crores through an all-cash transaction.
Marks a significant step in strengthening presence across the defence manufacturing ecosystem; with this acquisition, Apollo has presence across the entire missile and guided weapon value chain.
Acquisition serves as backward and forward integration; Premier is strong in propulsion systems for both space and weapon applications.
Partnership aims to enable Apollo's journey toward making a complete weapon independently without interdependency on other companies, and to become a prime OEM for in-house developed weapons.
Not limited to missile programs — extends to various ammunition programs where Apollo is strong in fuzes and engineering.
Open offer completion timeline is in regulator's hands; management unable to provide a firm date (e.g., not confirmed for 15th September).
Premier is in CCI approval mode; no comments possible on Premier's futuristic order book until acquisition formalities complete.

subsections.label: Artillery Shells / 155mm (Premier)
points: Premier has already conducted testing on 155mm artillery shells and provided complete filled shell samples to the Indian Army for testing.
Continuous orders expected for Premier on this front; going forward, Apollo will handle fuze and other electronic components while ammunition portion will be handled by Premier.

subsections.label: Further M&A Plans
points: Management indicated 2-3 additional companies are being planned for acquisition; formal announcement will follow once MOUs are signed with these companies.
No further clarity given on capability gaps beyond stating there are 'a lot' and urging investors to watch for updates in the coming months.

subsections.label: Fundraise / Capital Plans
points: No further fundraise currently planned for this or next financial year; company is focused on consolidating the current preferential round pending exchange approval.
Management indicated it will keep investors updated as the company becomes more agile and dynamic with disclosures over time.

subsections.label: Defence Procurement Cycle Risk
points: Year-on-year performance is viewed as more meaningful than quarter-on-quarter, given long procurement cycles and milestone-based execution causing uneven revenue recognition across quarters.

subsections.label: Ideal Explosives Losses
points: Ideal remains a loss-making acquisition undergoing restructuring; profitability remains thin due to lower bulk-explosive volumes and shrinking margins in that segment post the Coal India ban being lifted (only select circles participated in).

subsections.label: Regulatory / Open Offer Uncertainty
points: Timeline for open offer completion related to Premier acquisition is fully in the regulator's hands; management cannot provide guidance on timing.

subsections.label: Promoter Pledge
points: Promoter pledge has come down in the June quarter but is expected to take another full year to be reduced to zero, targeted by around Q1 FY28.

subsections.label: TAM/Order Visibility Uncertainty
points: TAM for anti-drone Make-II opportunity is continuously and dynamically changing; firmer guidance only expected once trials are completed.

subsections.label: Growth Guidance
points: Management continues to stand by prior guidance: growth of 40% to 45% expected to continue this financial year onwards, on both consolidated and standalone basis.
Separate guidance for the next financial year will be given at the end of this financial year.
Company does not give explicit EBITDA margin guidance, but states EBITDA momentum will continue to be similar / better than the present level.

subsections.label: Unit III and Future Plans
points: New future plans will only be articulated once Unit III facility is fully operational, likely after December, given the facility is also targeted for export opportunities.

subsections.label: Ideal Explosives Outlook
points: Ideal expected to become fully positive from the next financial year, following 3-4 quarters of ongoing restructuring.

subsections.label: Export Guidance
points: Meaningful export order breakthroughs possible this financial year (not firmly committed); sizable export orders confidently guided for next financial year.
Export revenue will be excluded from/additional to the current overall revenue growth guidance.

subsections.label: Promoter Pledge Guidance
points: Promoter pledge expected to be fully eliminated within about a year, targeted around Q1 FY28.

guidance_ledger.statement: We continue to stand by the same guidance as far as the growth is concerned. Somewhere in between 40% to 45% is the continued growth that we will continue to demonstrate, in this financial year onwards.
We are not giving EBITDA guidance anytime, sir. But the momentum will continue to be same... definitely better than the present this thing.

By end of this financial year, we are expecting a single order more than INR2,500 crores, INR3,000 crores, which could bring our order book to INR3,500 crores to INR4,000-odd crores on a consolidated basis.
BDL order value is something around I'm expecting INR11,000 to INR12,000 crores kind of thing... first phase actually, they are releasing for only 1,000 numbers QRSAM.

guidance_ledger.metric: MIGM program budget and order timing
guidance_ledger.statement: Like order, we are expecting by December or January, we are expecting the purchase order. The total budget is INR3,500 crores kind of thing... we are expecting MIGM 70% order from this INR3,500 crores deal.
MIGM, even QRSAM also, the execution starts from next financial year only.
We are expecting another INR150 crores order we are expecting from HAL.
It's something which is going to be positive, fully positive from the next financial year.
I will be able to give you a guidance around December ending quarter on the opportunity size that it could culminate into.
Converting into the order, now it may take 2-3 years time I think, definitely.
This financial year, we are likely to get some meaningfully good breakthrough orders is what I can broadly say, but I'll not be able to give a firm commitment and guidance.
For next financial year for sure, there will be a sizable orders, which will be pulled in terms of the export opportunities, is what the current guidance I can confidently give.
I think next 1 year I think we'll reduce. I think, it is going to take another 1 year to close all the pledge part.
Moored mine orders, we are expecting next financial year only, not this year. We are yet to complete the technical trials.
Limpet mine, we maybe start getting orders, maybe 4th quarter onwards, maybe we are expecting orders.
Maybe the final production as a complete production activity, I think before March '27, we are going to start.

guidance_ledger.metric: Future strategic plan disclosure (post Unit III / Premier)
guidance_ledger.statement: I think we'll come out only once that total facility is operational... anything December, after December only, we are able to come out with a new this thing.
I think next 2-3 months' time, we'll be coming out with our plan, actually.
For the next financial year, we'll give you a separate guidance at the end of this financial year.
During the last call, we had indicated an internal target of achieving a 15% PAT margin at the standalone level. We commit; we deliver. We close the year with the full year PAT margin of 16%.
We will continue to grow at a similar rate, in this particular financial year and the subsequent financial year backed by the size of the order book that we are going to have.
The order book size will increase significantly as we have been telling, and that something, which is going to happen in this financial year.

Prior guidance was 45%-50% CAGR organic growth; actual standalone growth for the year came in around 36%, described as an 8-9% miss versus guidance due to pending customer approvals; management commits to bounce back and maintain similar momentum going forward.
As of now I'm not able to give any guidance on IDL... I think we will be quite vocal about IDL's revenue guidance and other things from Q3 onwards.

guidance_ledger.horizon: before end of this financial year

Before end of this quarter, you'll start getting to hear more significant news which we have been vocal during the last quarter con-call as well.

We are currently charting our Vision 2036 document, which will be unveiled soon and will outline our detailed strategy, key growth areas, and strategic direction for Apollo's growth over the coming decade.
We are expecting the DAC approval any moment... this is something which is going to happen very shortly.

guidance_ledger.horizon: this financial year and next-next financial year

guidance_ledger.metric: Five-year revenue visibility on new licenses

In the years ahead, we will be having some meaningfully good decent amount of share in the export size which is being recorded as an export from the country.

For higher capacities for the defense explosive requirements... we would be doing a very large expansion. The DPRs are getting ready and as and when we feel it necessary... we will keep disclosing to the investors from time to time.

risk_register.note: Management emphasizes YoY over QoQ comparisons should be used to judge underlying business momentum.
Q1 FY27 PAT positive but profitability very low; volumetric bulk explosives business faces shrinking margins; restructuring ongoing, expected to take 3-4 more quarters.

risk_register.note: Timeline for open offer completion is fully in regulator's hands; management unable to comment on timing.
Pledge has come down in June quarter but will take another year to fully close, expected around Q1 FY28.
TAM is continuously dynamically changing; firmer guidance possible only after trials complete.

themes.label: Revenue/margin growth momentum
themes.note: Best-ever June quarter with 88% consolidated revenue YoY growth, 31% EBITDA margin and 18% PAT margin standalone; 40-45% growth guidance reiterated.

themes.label: Order book & large-ticket order visibility
themes.note: Consolidated order book at INR1,704 crores expected to reach INR3,500-4,000 crores by year end on large QRSAM, MIGM, Pinaka and Akash-NG orders.

themes.label: Land systems entry / diversification
themes.note: Continued diversification into autonomous underwater vehicles (SAVIOR), precision guided munitions (IPREC), naval mines and smart bombs across land, air and sea.

themes.label: IDL Explosives transformation
themes.note: Ideal turned PAT positive in Q1 FY27 but profitability remains thin amid lower Coal India volumes; restructuring expected to yield full positivity from next financial year.

themes.label: Licensing and IP moat expansion

themes.label: Export order ramp-up
themes.note: Export revenue currently nil, but direct export opportunities being pursued pending ministry approval; sizable export orders confidently guided for next financial year, excluded from current revenue guidance.

themes.note: Premier Explosives stake acquisition (~INR1,550 crores) aims to build backward/forward integration across the missile value chain; 2-3 further acquisitions under consideration.

key_takeaways: Best-ever June quarter: highest standalone revenue of INR156 crores, EBITDA and PAT margins of 31% and 18% respectively.

Entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 41.33% promoter stake in Premier Explosives Limited for approximately INR1,550 crores through an all-cash transaction, marking a significant step in strengthening presence across the defence manufacturing ecosystem.
With this acquisition, we have a presence across the entire missile and guided weapon value chain.
Successful handover of indigenously designed and developed Safety and Detonation Device to the Indian Navy, with 100% indigenous content.
Received a Make-II prototype sanction order from Indian Navy for development of SAVIOR Anti-Submarine Warfare system.
Recognized by Indian Air Force as prime development agency for IPREC program under Make-II category of DPP 2020.
Consolidated topline for Q1 FY27 stood at INR251 crores, registering YoY growth of 88% compared to INR134 crores in Q1 FY26.
Standalone order book stood at INR1,224 crores, while consolidated order book stood at INR1,704 crores, which includes an order book of INR480 crores at Ideal Explosives Limited.
pressing_questions: Deepak Sharma asked for forward-looking guidance in terms of revenue and EBITDA margin on consolidated and standalone basis for the next 2 or 3 years, and to quantify the order book size expected from QRSAM and MIGM and the time frame for conversion into revenue.
Amit Kumar asked management to highlight the order book trajectory for the next 3 years, including Premier, given the current INR1,700 crores consolidated order book.
Meet Gada asked whether further acquisitions can be expected considering current funds, and what the missing links in the overall capability chain are.
Ashit Kothi asked whether Apollo plans to merge its explosives business with Premier Explosives or keep them as separate entities.
Jayakanth Kasthuri asked about Project Kusha capabilities and addressable size possibility, as well as plans for aerial drone/UAV platforms given the sub-surface and swarm vessel developments.

quarters.summary: Apollo Micro Systems delivered its highest-ever quarterly and full-year revenue, EBITDA and PAT in Q4/FY26 on strong order book execution; management expects continued growth at a similar or accelerated pace in FY27 driven by large ticket orders expected to hit this financial year, an expanding order book, new licenses (UAVs, INS, radars, torpedoes, mines, ATGM, decoys/chaffs/flares, aerial bombs, rockets, missiles, loitering munition), and export order ramp-up, while IDL Explosives remains in a loss-making transformation phase with formal revenue/margin guidance to be given from Q3 onwards; an additional acquisition by subsidiary Apollo Defence Industries is expected to close before end of this financial year and a detailed Vision 2036 strategy document will be unveiled subsequently.

subsections.label: Five-year performance (FY21-FY26)
points: Revenue grew from operations at a CAGR of 30% while EBITDA grew at a CAGR of 41% over FY21-FY26.
Bottom line significantly outpaced top-line growth, registering a PAT CAGR of 64% over the same period.
EBITDA margin improved from 19% in FY21 to 24% in FY26, an expansion of 500 basis points.
PAT margin expanded by 700 basis points, increasing from 5% in FY21 to 12% in FY26.
ROCE improved substantially from 10% in FY21 to 18% in FY26, demonstrating enhanced operational efficiency and capital productivity.
Working capital cycle improved significantly, reducing from 626 days in FY21 to 359 days in FY26.

subsections.label: FY26 full-year performance
points: Company had indicated an internal target of achieving 15% PAT margin at the standalone level during the previous call; closed the year with full-year standalone PAT margin of 16%, exceeding the target ('We commit; we deliver').
Consolidated top-line for FY26 stood at INR904 crores, a 61% YoY growth compared to INR562 crores in FY25.
EBITDA (excluding other income) grew 69% to INR218 crores in FY26 versus INR129 crores in FY25.
PAT growth outpaced revenue growth, increasing 91% to INR107 crores in FY26 compared to INR56 crores in FY25.
FY26 described as a breakthrough year marked by strong financial discipline and operational execution.
ROCE and ROE stood at 18.23% and 11.21% respectively in FY26.
EBITDA margin expanded by 114 basis points to 24% in FY26; PAT margin expanded by 185 basis points to 12% in FY26.

Made the highest investment in R&D within the industry during FY26, with R&D expenditure at 8% of revenue (around INR72 crores absolute), and recorded zero attrition within the R&D team, reflecting strength and stability of the talent base.

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 quarterly performance
points: On a consolidated basis, Q4 FY26 marked the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT performance.
Revenue surged 81% YoY to INR293 crores compared to INR162 crores in Q4 FY25, driven by robust execution of the order book and successful transition of multiple products into the production phase.
EBITDA increased 88% to INR68 crores in Q4 FY26.
PAT recorded exceptional growth of 164% YoY, rising to INR37 crores versus INR14 crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

subsections.label: Promoter pledge
points: Promoter pledge currently stands at around 39%; management earlier stated an intent to bring it down to zero in FY2026 but reiterated commitment to exit this in the current financial year.

subsections.label: Standalone organic growth vs prior guidance
points: Standalone organic revenue growth for the year was around 36% versus an earlier guidance of 45%-50% CAGR.

Shortfall attributed to certain projects expected to be executed in the last quarter of the previous financial year that could not happen because of pending approvals from the customer, which is also reflected in inventory holding; management expects to bounce back and continue similar momentum.

subsections.label: Order book visibility
points: Order book as of 31st March stood at INR1,432 crores on a consolidated basis, providing strong visibility for future growth.

Management expects large ticket projects (which they have been vocal about for the past year) to be received during this financial year, which will cumulatively increase the order book size on both standalone and consolidated basis.
Management expects to continue growing at a similar rate in this financial year and the subsequent financial year, backed by the anticipated order book size.

On execution timeline of current order book: some orders will be executed in this financial year, some will spill over to next financial year; a few more orders are expected in this financial year which will support the demonstrated momentum growth.
Management declined to disclose the composition of the order book, stating they would take the question offline.

subsections.label: Mine and munitions market opportunity
points: All variants of mine (shallow water, deep water, limpet mines, diver-carried mines) together represent an immediate market opportunity of approximately INR4,000-4,500 crores, out of which some orders are expected this financial year and some in subsequent years on a continual basis.
Some overseas opportunities exist for mines; company has started submitting offers for export opportunities.
Aerial bombs / dumb bombs represent a sizable market; company is working with DRDO to reduce production costs, with trials already successful.
Company expects a large naval order (DAC approval) for mines/torpedo related program 'any moment'.

subsections.label: Ammunition and artillery demand
points: State-owned defense PSUs recorded a 42% surge in exports reaching INR8,389 crore, with a large part from explosives as part of ammunition, particularly for artillery, driven by demand in Europe.

Company is expanding heavily into ammunition and artillery, has already started getting orders, and expects an ammunition order shortly; explosive portion supported by IDL Explosives subsidiary while hardware/intelligence-related work is done by parent Apollo.
Confirmed that this pertains to filled artillery shells, not only empty shells.

subsections.label: IDL Explosives subsidiary performance
points: IDL last year's performance stood at around INR380 crores, little less than INR380 crores; expected to continue maintaining a similar level of performance.
There has been a huge shift of management at IDL, which had been in place for decades; outlook towards IDL is now totally different.

Management is unable to give guidance on IDL currently as it is undergoing a transformation phase; more initiatives will be taken over the next couple of quarters and management will be vocal about IDL's revenue guidance from Q3 onwards.

IDL was loss-making for the last few years, but operational loss has been reduced significantly at EBITDA level and at different levels of the balance sheet due to transformation initiatives; going forward, a huge improvement is expected.
On a consolidated basis there will be a dent owing to presently negative EBITDA of IDL, described as purely temporary; bounce-back expected in the next few quarters.

subsections.label: Land systems entry
points: Company's heritage strength has been in air and underwater domains including missiles, electronic warfare, avionics, torpedoes, sonars, and underwater mines; presence in land systems has historically been limited but is now changing in a deliberate and well-resourced manner.

FY26-27 will mark serious entry into key defense domains including armament electronics, fire control systems, battle tanks, infantry combat vehicles, artillery platforms, and vehicle-mounted counter-drone systems, with trials scheduled in upcoming quarters.

subsections.label: Rocket and guidance programs
points: Remarkable progress in development of futuristic rocket programs like the BM-21 Grad rocket.
Trusted partner and supplier for various guidance and navigation system programs, including the Pinaka program and others.

Continuing role as approved production partner for DRDO; already approved production partner for multi-influence ground mine; expecting to become a DCPP partner for other mine variants including India's first indigenous naval mine of its class, designated Vighna, developed under DCPP with DRDO.

subsections.label: Air domain focus
points: In the Air domain, focus areas include unmanned systems, loitering munition, rail platforms, and counter-drones.

subsections.label: Program stage breadth
points: Company has participated in around 150+ indigenous programs and around 700+ onboarded technologies (per management commentary responding to an analyst reference), spanning missile programs, naval programs, air defense programs, land systems programs, at various stages — development phase, serial production phase, and trials phase.
Revenue contribution is expected from these programs as they move into production; company claims presence across every indigenous missile program of the country.

subsections.label: Presence in QRSAM, Kusha and BrahMos programs
points: Company has a good and decent presence in both the Kusha program and QRSAM program, including systems like SAMs and actuation systems.
RF seeker development for BrahMos-related and other internal R&D programs has started; company is setting up a specialized RF seeker testing facility at the upcoming Hardware Park unit.

subsections.label: FY26 R&D product development
points: Focused and rigorous R&D efforts culminated in successful development of products such as Mini Torpedo, sensor suits for underwater autonomous vehicles, fiber optic gyro-based INS systems, and several other advanced solutions.
Actively working on multiple critical and next-generation technologies and solutions to strengthen future capabilities and growth trajectory.
Good progress made in FY26 in developing inertial navigation systems based on fiber optic gyros; products to be unveiled soon with updates to investors from time to time.

subsections.label: Technology focus areas
points: Commitment to emerging technologies spans three core areas: RF systems, artificial intelligence, and inertial navigation systems.
In RF: developing RF sensors such as RF tracking and direction-finding systems, electronic warfare sensors, and advanced communication suites.
In AI: building embedded AI for sensor fusion for autonomous vehicles and underwater autonomous systems, and for battlefield and direction-finding applications.

subsections.label: Licenses and technology transfers received in FY26
points: Received industrial license for TNT and RDX through subsidiary IDL Explosives.

Received a DPIIT license covering UAVs, INS systems, radars, torpedoes, underwater mines, ATGM, decoys, chaffs and flares, aerial bombs, rockets, missiles, and loitering munition — described as a lifetime license paving the way for penetrating into full-fledged platforms for Indian and global markets.
Received transfer of technology for directed energy weapons, including laser-based DEW and electro-optical tracking systems.

subsections.label: Evolution to full weapon system manufacturer
points: Company has evolved from a subsystem and systems manufacturer to establishing itself as a full-fledged weapon system manufacturer.
Built on 41 years of technological excellence; positioning to evolve into a multi-disciplinary defense system powerhouse driving next-generation innovation.

Company holds a unique standing point with the ability to re-engineer and develop advanced systems and technologies by virtue of holding the IP, described as a key differentiator versus peers who may be limited to system integration or production-partner roles.

subsections.label: Greenfield expansion / Unit 3 status
points: Greenfield expansion in Telangana was one of the key FY26 highlights.
Unit 3 civil work is complete for phase one; phase two civil work is still ongoing.
Some ordered machinery has already been received and installation is in process; MEP, electrical, and facade works are ongoing in phase one.
Company will take possession of the premises phase-wise and subsequently shift machinery presently in Unit 1 to Unit 3 on a stage-by-stage basis.

subsections.label: IDL Explosives capacity expansion (TNT/HMX)
points: TNT and HMX licenses obtained (500 tons TNT, 50 tons HMX) are for industrial explosive requirements; capacities are not limited to that level.

For higher capacities to meet defense explosive requirements, a very large expansion is planned; DPRs are being prepared and details will be disclosed to investors over time given the sensitivity of the area.
Rationale for starting with smaller capacity relates to obtaining industrial explosive licenses first, with larger defense-oriented expansion to follow as DPRs mature.

subsections.label: RF seeker testing facility
points: Company is setting up a specialized RF seeker testing facility at its upcoming unit in Hardware Park to support internal R&D on RF seeker programs.

subsections.label: In-house test facility build-out
points: Company is setting up all test facilities that had previously been outsourced for several years, which is expected to contribute to improvement in overall inventory/working-capital holding periods, with visibility expected in a few quarters.

subsections.label: Export strategy
points: One of the four pillars of Vision 2036 is deepening presence in Indian defense procurement while meaningfully expanding in global markets, converting the first export order into a sustained international revenue stream.
Company expects exports to start inching up and subsequently escalate to higher scales, with requisite initiatives already underway.
Audits by customers of interest who wish to place export orders have already started; new facility completion awaited to firmly take up export opportunities given commitment to on-time delivery.
Company has already started submitting offers for various export opportunities and expects to secure a meaningfully good/decent share of the country's recorded export size in the years ahead.
Currently in the Middle East as of the call, noting operations there are normal with no supply chain issues observed.

subsections.label: Sector export context
points: State-owned defense PSUs recorded a 42% surge in exports reaching INR8,389 crore, with a large part attributable to explosives/ammunition, particularly for artillery, driven by demand in Europe.

subsections.label: Inventory and receivables
points: Improvement in inventory holding days seen this financial year, expected to continue in subsequent years.

Predominant business currently comprises development orders; company expects decently good production orders in this financial year and the subsequent financial year as programs mature and larger players have started receiving orders.

As company has predominantly been a subsystem supplier to platform integrators, it is likely to receive large production orders; as production orders hit and revenue recognizes, inventory levels are expected to slowly come down.

As business grows and number of programs increases, inventory will also grow in parallel because gestation cycles of raw material procurement, production and testing cycles in defense systems are highly elongated — a factor common across the industry.
As scale of operations increases, a decent improvement in holding periods is expected, partly aided by the in-house build-out of test facilities previously outsourced.

Inventory holding (and related shortfall vs prior growth guidance) also tied to timing of customer approvals on certain projects that were expected to execute in the last quarter of the previous financial year but were delayed pending approvals.

subsections.label: Global supply chain environment
points: Geopolitical issues affecting supply chains are not new and have existed for a long time; management does not contemplate a significant dent to overall performance in the years ahead, though timing of revenue recognition could shift by a quarter due to various operational conditions globally.

During the Covid-19 period there was supply chain disruption which led to a reset in how the company gives guidance to OEMs and semiconductor suppliers (primary raw material) regarding what material is needed at what point in time; a similar reset would occur again as and when global events happen.
As of the call, management sees nothing very significant currently impacting operations; speaking from the Middle East, conditions there are normal.

subsections.label: Defense explosive market opportunity for IDL
points: Company is already part of the defense explosive market via systems it supplies, currently outsourcing explosive content, which will continue with captive systems going forward.
Company has been part of the defense ecosystem/DRDO technology ecosystem, so management does not see a major challenge penetrating deeper into the defense explosive market.

Market size for defense explosives is described as pretty large while the number of industry players currently supplying it is pretty small, presenting a large opportunity for both captive requirement and country-level requirements.

subsections.label: Global TNT/HMX demand-supply
points: Global conflicts have been at their highest peak level in the last six years, causing huge depletion of stocks across various countries.
ESG and other issues have kept many explosive plants unoperational for decades in many countries, creating opportunity for explosive companies both in India and globally.

Rationale for entering explosives is to access full-fledged platform opportunities, leveraging experience and qualifications already achieved, including as a DRDO production partner, indigenous R&D-based development, and direct orders from Army and Navy.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning / differentiation
points: Company avoided the term 'monopoly' but noted uniqueness in certain products where it is the only company qualified, including full-fledged development with all-round IP (including explosives).

In certain areas competitors exist but are limited to system integration or production-partner roles, whereas Apollo differentiates through its ability to re-engineer/develop advanced systems by holding the underlying IP.

subsections.label: Private sector in ballistic missile production
points: In response to a question about the Defence Secretary's comment on potential private sector involvement in ballistic missile production, management stated it would be a fantastic opportunity where the company could be a key contributor given existing building blocks, but the company is not presently pursuing this on its own; interest from a few players eyeing large programs exists, and management is open to collaborative/consortium-based opportunities.

subsections.label: Vision 2036
points: Company is charting a Vision 2036 document to be unveiled soon, outlining detailed strategy, key growth areas, and strategic direction for the coming decade; a glimpse has already been shared via the shareholder letter and tear sheet.
Vision is to grow as a global OEM over the next 10 years with recognizable revenue streams across land, air and sea domains, expanding presence in Indian markets while scaling in global markets.

Four pillars of the vision: (1) becoming a global OEM 'Made in India', transitioning from a tier-1 supplier of critical electronics to a recognizable global OEM in defense platforms; (2) building recognizable and diversified revenue streams across land, air and sea so no single platform, program or customer defines the company; (3) deepening presence in Indian defense procurement while expanding meaningfully in global markets, converting the first export order into a sustained international revenue stream; (4) driving conviction-led innovation backed by futuristic R&D in RF technologies, AI, autonomous systems, and inertial navigation technologies.
More detailed financial parameters/nitty-gritties of the FY36 Vision will be communicated to investors over time as numbers culminate; at this point only a directional glimpse is being given.

subsections.label: Additional acquisition via Apollo Defence Industries
points: An additional acquisition by subsidiary Apollo Defence Industries Private Limited is expected to be completed before the end of this financial year, which will complement organic growth and strengthen the overall business.

On the specific RF-related acquisition previously flagged: management is bound by an NDA and cannot divulge details currently; more significant news expected before end of this quarter; the process had been delayed owing to global conflicts and internal process considerations, but management will become more vocal as things progress.

subsections.label: FY26 key milestones
points: Key highlights of FY26 include a successful fundraise, greenfield expansion in Telangana, 100% acquisition of IDL Explosives, receipt of the first export order, a tripartite alliance with Indian Navy, IIT Chennai and AMS, and an MoU with GRSE.

subsections.label: Order timing and approval risk
points: Certain projects expected to be executed in the last quarter of the previous financial year could not happen because of pending approvals from the customer, contributing to the shortfall versus prior organic growth guidance of 45-50% CAGR (actual standalone growth ~36%) and to elevated inventory holding.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / supply chain risk
points: Geopolitical issues affecting global supply chains have existed for a long time and are not new; management does not currently contemplate a significant dent to performance but acknowledges revenue recognition timing could shift by a quarter due to global operational conditions.
Covid-19 period caused a supply chain disruption previously, requiring a reset in procurement guidance to OEMs/semiconductor suppliers; a similar reset would occur again with future global events.

subsections.label: Promoter pledge
points: Promoter pledge remains at around 39%, versus a prior stated intent to bring it to zero in FY2026; management reiterated commitment to resolve this in the current financial year but could not give an immediate roadmap.

subsections.label: IDL Explosives consolidation drag
points: IDL Explosives currently has negative EBITDA, which creates a dent when consolidated at the group level; management describes this as purely temporary during an ongoing transformation phase.

subsections.label: Growth and order book outlook
points: Management expects to continue growing at a similar pace, or an accelerated pace, in the years coming ahead including the current financial year, backed by anticipated large ticket order inflows and order book growth expected in this financial year.

Order book of INR1,432 crores will see some orders executed this financial year and some spilling to next financial year, with a few more expected orders in this financial year supporting continued momentum growth.
Guidance on FY36 Vision financial parameters/nitty-gritties to be shared with investors progressively as the plan culminates.

subsections.label: IDL Explosives guidance timing
points: Management stated they cannot currently give guidance on IDL Explosives revenue or margins as it is undergoing a transformation phase, but will start giving guidance on IDL revenue and margins from Q3 onwards.

subsections.label: Promoter pledge resolution
points: Management stands by its commitment to bring down promoter pledge (currently ~39%) in the current financial year, though no immediate detailed roadmap was given.

subsections.label: Acquisition and RF seeker facility timing
points: Additional acquisition via Apollo Defence Industries expected to close before the end of this financial year.
More significant news on the previously flagged RF-related acquisition expected before the end of this quarter.
DAC approval for a naval order (mines/torpedo related) expected 'any moment'.

key_takeaways: We are pleased to share that we have delivered our highest ever quarterly and 12 months revenue marked by consistent execution, operational discipline, and a strong commitment to indigenization and the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative.

An additional acquisition by our subsidiary Apollo Defence Industries Private Limited is expected to be completed before end of this financial year, which will significantly complement our organic growth and overall strengthen our business.

Between FY21 and FY26, our revenue grew from operations at CAGR of 30%, while EBITDA grew at a CAGR of 41% over the same period. Our bottom line significantly outpaced top-line growth registering a CAGR of 64%.
We commit; we deliver. We close the year with the full year PAT margin of 16%.
At consolidated level, our top-line of FY26 stood at INR904 crores, registering a strong year-on-year growth of 61%, compared to INR562 crores in FY25.
Our order book as of 31st March stood at INR1,432 crores on a consolidated basis providing strong visibility for future growth.

FY26-'27 will mark our serious entry into key defense domains including armament electronics, fire control systems, and battle tanks, infantry combat vehicles, and artillery platforms, vehicle-mounted counter-drone systems with trials scheduled in the upcoming quarters.

We have received a DPIIT license covering UAVs, INS systems, radars, torpedoes, underwater mines, ATGM, decoys, chaffs and flares, aerial bombs, rockets, missiles, and loitering munition. This is a remarkable achievement, which are a lifetime license for the company.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: 86% of Q1 revenue from AI-led engineering, data and integration, and cloud services gives leeway to focus simultaneously on margin expansion alongside growth.

Combined entity delivered 16.0% reported EBIT in Q1 itself, ahead of the FY27 guided 15.5%, reflecting rapid execution of the Encora integration playbook and realization of SG&A/operational synergies.
Encora G&A reduced by 40% versus its level at announcement, and combined G&A expected to improve further in Q2 due to full-quarter impact of actions taken in Q1.

Rest-of-world margin appeared flattish because reduction in India government business and exit from the higher-margin data center business (both sitting in RoW) offset gains, plus Encora consolidation; management expects RoW margins to expand from here on.

subsections.label: Hedging and one-offs
points: Hedge losses of $10 million incurred in Q1 plus an outstanding $14 million MTM loss on hedges to be realized over the next two quarters.
No open hedge book beyond Q3, so a positive ~$10 million earnings impact is anticipated from Q4 onwards as hedge losses are eliminated.

Exceptional/acquisition-related expenses of $6.5 million in Q1 (vs $5.4 million in Q4) remain well within the guided $15 million budget for acquisition and integration costs; marginal integration costs expected in Q2 and none from Q3 onwards.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / financing
points: Acquisition accounting based on fair value of shares on closing date (INR 1220) vs signing date (INR 1815), resulting in lower goodwill of approximately $600 million.

$550 million term loan for Encora acquisition fully drawn as of June 30; 3-year tenure at fixed 4.6% rate (2.99% post-tax due to 35% India tax benefit); no restrictive covenants and no cash restricted.
Loan is denominated in India, providing a natural hedge; company does not intend to add incremental forex hedges given this natural hedge.
Net working capital absolute increase driven by Encora consolidation, but number of days of working capital has actually come down.

Customer relationship intangibles of $480 million recorded on acquisition, amortized over 12 years, generating an annual D&A charge of $40 million (clarified impact of $4 million per annum on a per-item basis).
Loan repayment schedule: ~$59 million in FY27, ~$209 million in FY28, ~$258 million in FY29, and ~$75 million final tranche in Q1 FY30.

subsections.label: Cash flow
points: FCF-to-PAT conversion improved sharply YoY (95.3% vs -56.5% in Q1 FY26), reflecting strength of the operating model and disciplined working capital management.

Historically Q1 (and H1) had been near-zero/negative for free cash flow; structural improvement over the past two-to-three years has now made Q1 strong, and management expects to build on this going forward.

subsections.label: EPS
points: EPS excl. exceptional costs broadly stable at ₹13.3 vs ₹13.8 last quarter, notable given ~25% expansion in equity base from the Encora transaction and incremental interest cost on acquisition financing; company remains on track for EPS accretion in FY27 as previously guided.

subsections.label: Long-term track record
points: Over the current management's 9-year tenure, revenue CAGR of 21.7%, EBIT CAGR of 24.6%, and PAT CAGR of 24.1%.

subsections.label: Nuuron - AI Operationalization Platform
points: Nuuron is described as an 'operating system,' not a platform; it is further layered by 8 AI platforms and 22 AI assets, with 100+ (130-odd) reusable AI agents and accelerators, bringing together enterprise knowledge, decisions, workflows, governance, agents and execution to help enterprises move from AI pilots to AI operations.
Nuuron is explicitly positioned as not another model, copilot, or agent marketplace, but the operating layer moving enterprises from experimentation to production.
Combined with Forward Deployed Engineers, Mod Squads, and reusable AI assets; the delivery model is shifting from an effort-based model to an outcomes-based model.

Coforge's differentiation is framed as applying AI inside complex industries (domain knowledge, execution discipline, governance, measurable outcomes) rather than competing on model ownership or AI infrastructure.
Company has 11,000+ data and AI practitioners and invested $58 million in AI innovation in FY26; ~30% of active engagements currently leverage AI in delivery workflows.

subsections.label: Enterprise Autonomy thesis
points: AI conversation has shifted from 'how do we deploy AI' to 'how do we operationalize/govern/scale it and turn it into measurable business outcomes' - termed 'Enterprise Autonomy' by Coforge.
Every enterprise will have models, cloud, and agents; the differentiator will be 'Applied AI' - AI grounded in business context, process, policy and risk.

subsections.label: AI adoption trends / model strategy
points: Most enterprises are avoiding tying themselves to a specific model, hyperscaler, or cloud, given rapid change and model providers now offering services on proprietary clouds.
Coforge has built quick-turn service offerings around token economics/token ops given fast-changing dynamics.
Partnership with Zscaler has produced monetized service offerings around the Guardian AI platform and managed-services constructs for Mythos-related security vulnerability assessments.
Enterprises are increasingly focused on 'enterprise sovereign AI' / 'enterprise open intelligence,' seeking to bring data processing in-house with associated security/governance controls.

Coforge is not working with Chinese LLMs; management has not seen North American enterprise clients actively leveraging China-based models; John Speight echoed the same for UK/Europe clients, though this could change with new LLM releases and token cost issues.

subsections.label: Client engagement highlights

Latin American bank: AI-enabled Mod Squads spanning engineering, testing, modernization and business analysis targeting 30-50% delivery throughput increase.
Fintech: modernized AI Vibe Coding Developer Portal using reverse/forward engineering agents on GitHub Copilot and Claude Opus, contributing to a new modernization engagement.
Wealth management firm: AI-led framework accelerated API transformation by three months.
Wealth and Asset Management platform: AI-native Advisor Experience Desktop powered by 20+ specialized AI agents delivering 30%+ advisor productivity gains.
Investment services institution: AI-led operating model transformation with 40% of portfolios transitioned in year one and delivery cycle times reduced by 80%.

Global travel technology leader: Mod Squad model delivered 30% productivity gains and 22% reduction in manual effort; cargo platform COSYS+ went live for one of India's largest aviation hubs, extending footprint to 20 airports globally.
Australian medical indemnity insurer: large-scale core platform transformation serving ~40,000 healthcare professionals.
Large specialty insurance provider: CodeInsightAI used to migrate to Azure, reducing technical debt by 92%, delivering 99.93% field-level accuracy and 65% productivity improvement.
Life Sciences (biopharma): agentic audit platform identified $4 million in savings opportunities at 95% accuracy.
Manufacturing (global automotive manufacturer): CodeInsightAI modernized legacy landscape, reducing documentation effort by 70%, modernization cycles by 50%, and operating costs by 35%.
Leading European client: secured 5-year, $230 million+ AI-led transformation programme using Low-Code/No-Code platforms, AI-powered automation, and AI-infused SDLC.

subsections.label: Encora integration playbook
points: Coforge's proven integration playbook: immediately and fully integrate acquired organization, ask acquired-firm leaders to leave on Day 1 for immediate/complete effective control, with all Encora operations overseen by Coforge leaders who led due diligence.
Ahead of plan even before one full quarter has elapsed post-acquisition, consistent with prior value creation from Cigniti, SLK Global and Incessant acquisitions.

All 45 legal entities migrated onto SAP S/4HANA effective May 1, creating a unified operating and reporting environment from day one; revenue recognition, planning systems, and performance management processes aligned across the organization.
Management remains confident of not only delivering but surpassing the 15.5% consolidated EBIT margin guidance for FY27 based on integration progress to date.

Effectively operationally run Encora for three months already ('in the weeds'), not passive post-acquisition oversight; cost synergies (40% G&A reduction) already exceptional; Encora added 9,256 employees in Q1 FY27.

Encora case for acquisition rested on three pillars: (1) AI-led engineering capability strengthening the combined engineering-data-cloud core; (2) adding a new Hi-Tech vertical and nearly doubling the healthcare business, both now showing sequential growth; (3) cross-selling opportunity to scale up acquired clients, with one ex-Encora client already a top-10 account and a path to $50 million+ over 12-18 months, plus two more accounts in the 11-20 bracket (including a Travel account) targeted for scale-up.

Encora expected to reach Coforge's order intake intensity within two quarters (not four); margins between the organizations already indistinguishable; revenue growth expected to be indistinguishable from Quarter Three onwards.
Coforge has been recognized as the 3rd consecutive year fastest growing material tech services firm globally.

subsections.label: Industry deflation vs tailwinds
points: Industry has deflationary trends linked to efficiency gains from AI, but also significant tailwinds around legacy modernization, AI-ready data foundations, cloud infrastructure scalable for AI/compute/model hosting/MLOps, and security.
For Coforge specifically, deflation is not seen as a dominant headwind; tailwinds are described as very strong, with growth strong right now.

Medium-term opportunities include custom agentic solutions, agent harnesses, managing the agentic ecosystem, and model development/deployment support - requiring a 'hard pivot' by the industry to realize.

subsections.label: Currency / hedging risk

Whether deflationary trends versus AI-led opportunity tailwinds will shift in the industry's favor over time.

quarters.summary: Coforge closed FY26 with 29.2% USD revenue growth and a structural margin reset in Q4 (EBIT margin 16.6%), and management guided FY27 to industry-leading revenue growth with EBITDA margin of 20.5%-21% (consolidated) and EBIT margin 16.5%-17% standalone / 15.5% consolidated, alongside FCF/PAT of 100%+, driven by AI-led automation, G&A leverage, Encora synergies, and closure of a low-margin India portfolio.

subsections.label: Accounting changes
points: Effective FY26, realized gains/losses on cash flow hedges are reported under other income/expense within forex gain/loss instead of being adjusted to revenue, aligning presentation with peer practice and isolating revenue/EBIT margin from currency fluctuation; PBT and PAT unchanged; comparatives restated.

Deferred tax liability reversal of ~INR 181 crores related to Cigniti merger amalgamation scheme effective in FY26, credited to provision for tax in Q4 FY26; this is a non-cash one-time benefit; cash taxes paid in Q4 remain unchanged.

Hedge reclassification was undertaken working with auditors, timed to year-end so reporting aligns with market practice; if hedge losses were added back to revenue as before, Q4 EBIT margin would have been 15.2% vs guidance of 15%, indicating underlying operational improvement.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Q4 EBIT margin record of 16.6%, up 231 bps QoQ, driven by SG&A leverage, favorable FX, direct cost reduction from lower third-party costs, lower marketing spend, and lower ESOP cost, partially offset by a provision for doubtful debts.
Margin improvement in Q4 is described as operational, giving confidence in sustaining and further improving margins in FY27.
150 bps margin gap between FY27 standalone and consolidated EBIT margin guidance attributed to amortization (~$40 million annually) related to Encora.

subsections.label: Cash flow and capital allocation
points: Q4 FCF of $73.7 million was the highest quarterly FCF on record.
Net cash improved despite a $36 million reduction in the working capital line and $61 million in dividends paid.

FCF/PAT guidance raised from earlier 70-80% to 100% from FY27 onwards, driven by improved rigor in collections, payables management, and contract structuring; management expects this could move toward 110-120% in a couple of years.
Positive capex inflow in cash flow statement due to sale/buy-back of AI-led data center assets built in Q1 to the client.

subsections.label: Tax and minority interest
points: Steady state effective tax rate guidance for FY27 is 23-24%.

Minority interest expected to decline sharply from Q1 FY27 onwards as the Cigniti share allotment record date (16 May) passes, with corresponding increase in Coforge share count but net EPS upside expected.

subsections.label: Hedging policy
points: Company has taken a $550 million dollar loan in India providing a natural hedge, aligning cash flows and balance sheet with dollar liabilities, shifting toward balance sheet hedges and reducing cash flow hedge volumes.
Natural hedge arises because receivables are in dollars in India offsetting dollar payables.
Mark-to-market hedge losses expected to continue for one or two more quarters before tapering off from Q3.

subsections.label: Order intake and pipeline
points: Q4 was a very strong quarter for both order intake and large deal closure.
Executable order book of $1.75 billion reflects total value of locked orders over the next 12 months and is a record high, 16.4% higher YoY.

This executable order book figure excludes the impact of framework agreements already signed, which are described as nearly assured revenue streams for FY27 and beyond, with material additional revenue expected from these framework agreements not accounted for in the order book.

Confidence in revenue growth stems not just from the order executable but from the balanced nature of the portfolio across travel, healthcare, banking, and insurance verticals — management describes the portfolio as 'not hitching our wagon to one star.'

Analyst noted that applying a conservative conversion multiple to the 12-month forward executable order book implies ~18-19% FY27 growth; management did not confirm whether the previous 1.3x-1.4x conversion multiple still holds, citing macro and AI deflation uncertainty.

subsections.label: Vertical performance and drivers
points: Growth was broad-based with all key industry units performing strongly, led by top 10 and top 20 client relationships.
Top 10 clients span industries: five BFS clients, three travel clients, one insurance client, one public sector client.

BFS growth of 12% was constrained by one top-three banking client not growing this year; the account has been transferred to President John Speight's personal stewardship with a completely refactored engagement team and new AI-led transformation approach; management expects better BFS numbers in FY27.

Travel vertical continues to perform well even amid Gulf War/crude concerns; press reports on Spirit Airlines impact on Coforge are said to be negligible, with budgeted revenue from that airline at about 10 bps of FY27 revenue; secular tailwinds cited include 'One Order' initiatives and airport reconstruction/retail mall expansion.
High-tech business (from Encora) is under new leadership based in a newly established office and is expected to start growing from Q1 FY27 and grow handsomely through the year.

Cigniti acquisition (testing services) two years ago faced concerns about low (12%) EBITDA dragging Coforge's growth story; portfolio now operates at 19% EBITDA with cross-sell driving major growth in constituent clients.

subsections.label: UK public sector framework agreements
points: John Speight described the $150 million+ five-year deal as sole-awarded to Coforge and typical of how UK public sector business works, with multiple TSRs/SOWs issued against the award.
Expected run rate base of around $4-5 million per quarter from this framework deal, with revenue starting to flow from Q1 FY27.
Coforge has other UK public sector opportunities in the $10-100 million size range considered 'locked and loaded' for future award, in addition to the signed $150 million deal.
Framework deals in Coforge's business are restricted to UK public sector only, not other sectors or geographies.
Prior successes cited include the Scotland 111 services rollout.

subsections.label: Six moats for AI opportunity capture
points: Moat 1: Deep domain expertise — Applied AI (vs commoditizing Generative AI) is the differentiator, backed by 150+ scaled AI engagements across BFS, insurance, travel, healthcare.
Moat 2: Strong client intimacy — trust, context, and proximity to decision makers shape demand; relationships do not commoditize.
Moat 3: Reinvented delivery models — hybrid AI 'ModSquads' combine AI agents and senior AI specialists, driving 40-50% faster time to market.
Moat 4: Agility at scale — being built for agility with AI-first offerings, requiring internal adoption of agentic AI and a lean talent pool.
Moat 5: Scalable AI platform — OneAI platform is composable, enterprise-grade, agentic, with 100+ domain-specific solutions and 75+ horizontal capabilities.

Moat 6: AI-enabled workforce — specialized engineers, forward-deployed engineers (FDEs), agile management, with 30,000+ AI-enabled trained workforce, 11,000+ data/AI practitioners, 600+ advanced AI practitioners built via upskilling investment.

subsections.label: Five growth vectors / value pools
points: Opportunity 1: ModSquad Monetization — hybrid delivery pods priced on outcomes, not hours.
Opportunity 2: Multimodal AI strategy planning across LLM providers/tools without vendor lock-in.
Opportunity 3: Brownfield Modernization — accelerated legacy modernization via proprietary platforms like CodeInsight.AI, delivering $40M+ in client savings.
Opportunity 4: AI-led engineering transformation — improving productivity/quality while lowering costs, backed by multi-layered knowledge graphs, pre-built agents, enterprise governance.
Opportunity 5: Agentic AI platform opportunity — deploying engineers from routine work to agentic AI orchestration, described as the highest margin and most strategically valuable work.

subsections.label: Internal AI adoption ('client zero')
points: AI embedded across SDLC driving 25-35% productivity uplift in development, 40-60% in code generation, and up to 10x faster modernization timelines.
Internal operations use AI to drive 40-60% lower effort on financial analysis and 30-40% lower recruitment screening cost.

subsections.label: Reference architecture and delivery model (CTO commentary)
points: Most enterprise AI pilots never reach production because of surrounding architecture and delivery gaps, not just the model; pilots run in controlled conditions masking structural issues exposed in production.

Reference architecture has three layers: (1) Business architecture layer — business goals, high-impact use cases, OCM-led operating model redesign; (2) Decisioning engine/'decisioning atlas' — proprietary asset enforcing domain-specific reasoning chains, ontologies, knowledge graph mapping cross-system compliance hierarchies, and temporal context for state coherence across multi-step agentic workflows; (3) Composable AI backbone — swappable with hyperscaler compute, sovereign AI cloud, or any model provider, including AI gateway for model routing, MCP gateway, token ops, and canary release capability.
Reference architecture enforces deterministic guardrails around probabilistic LLM outputs, solving two failure modes: hallucinated domain logic and lost agent coherence in long-running processes.

Operationalized via proprietary AI ModSquads and forward-deployed engineers (FDEs); ModSquads implement agent harnesses for long-running durable agents with a RAG loop (planner, generator, evaluator agents) tied together with guardrails/contracts and anti-leniency/adversarial patterns; governance protocol for human-in-the-loop checkpoints implemented via templates, registration, versioning, and lifecycle management of 110 agent archetypes.

subsections.label: Case studies
points: Tier-one bank: AI-led COBOL to Java 21/Quarkus modernization of an 11,000-line mainframe module with Copybooks, VSAM, and Assembler dependencies, completed in half the client-given time, using decomposition agents plus one senior FDE and two junior consultants generating production-grade code with hexagonal architecture, non-blocking reactive IO, JWT authentication, open telemetry, distributed tracing, and container-native deployment.

Large group insurance benefits provider: architecture deployed on Azure with Trust AI enforcing responsible AI guardrails at inference time, model garden for multi-LLM routing, enterprise RAG orchestrating retrieval across multiple vector databases (EM25 algorithm + semantic search), governance-as-code, automated security policies, token-level FinOps, and operational kill switches; resulted in 40% productivity benefit and 50% velocity gains.

subsections.label: Workforce metrics
points: Total headcount stood at 35,777 with net addition of 436 during the quarter.
Utilization during the quarter was 82.5%.
LTM attrition remains one of the lowest in the industry at 10.8%, reiterated as a consistent strength.

subsections.label: Client wallet share and cross-sell
points: Growth driven by ability to increase wallet share, particularly across key accounts, via an industry solutioning and AI specialist cadre focused on crafting business solution-led proactive deals.
Encora integration completion is expected to expand the addressable wallet across the combined client set.
Cross-sell from Cigniti acquisition scaled top two Cigniti clients from $25-30 million per year collectively to $75 million per year.

subsections.label: AI market recognition
points: Received over 25 AI recognitions from leading analyst firms including seven leader positions from Everest, HFS, Constellation Research, ISG, and Avasant.

subsections.label: Industry expansion debate
points: Analyst question on whether the AI opportunity will expand the overall IT industry (referenced at ~$250 billion) beyond current size over 2-4 years, and whether mid-tier players (vs Tier 1) could be greater beneficiaries in this AI cycle versus the prior cloud/digital cycle.

Management (Vic Gupta) noted significant application entanglement and integration problems across Fortune 1000 clients, creating opportunity in brownfield migration, modernization, and agentic systems; responsible AI/governance is described as non-negotiable for regulated industries.
Management believes Coforge's speed of execution, nimbleness, and client intimacy are moat advantages in this AI cycle.

subsections.label: Turnaround and acquisition track record
points: Company started at $400 million revenue nine years back and has grown almost seven times over the 10-year turnaround period led by Sudhir Singh, John Speight, Saurabh Goel, Madan, and Vic since inception of the turnaround.
Cigniti acquisition (2 years back) initially raised concerns given 12% EBITDA of a publicly listed testing services firm, but has scaled to 19% EBITDA with strong cross-sell driving client growth.
Encora integration is now complete, expanding the addressable client wallet; Encora described as 'the defining example' of value creation through acquisitions, following SLK and Cigniti.

Cigniti amalgamation scheme became effective in FY26, remeasuring deferred tax balances; share allotment to Cigniti shareholders has a record date of 16 May, after which minority interest will decline substantially in the P&L from Q1 FY27, with an effective merger entry from Q1.

subsections.label: Four key FY27 priorities
points: Priority 1: Build pipeline momentum in AI transformations across top verticals.
Priority 2: Expand the AI client base rapidly through hunting and farming.
Priority 3: Scale vertical agent workflows in banking, insurance, and airlines.
Priority 4: Continue investing in talent, growing the specialized FDE pool while upskilling 100% of the workforce in AI.

subsections.label: Portfolio rationalization
points: Planned closure of a $20 million low-margin India business portfolio to structurally reset margins; expected to reduce Q1 FY27 revenue by roughly $15-20 million (pass-through revenue), though other signed deals and the order book are expected to largely offset this impact, resulting in an expected flattish Q1 FY27 on a QoQ reported basis.
This discontinued India business generated $40-45 million last year, with $40 million of that coming over the last two quarters at that quarterly run rate.
Management stated confidence in the revenue pipeline and materiality of the opportunity enabled the decision to discontinue this low-margin business.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Provision for doubtful debts created a 60 bps headwind to Q4 EBIT margin.
Discontinuation of the $20 million low-margin India business portfolio will reduce Q1 FY27 revenue by $15-20 million.
Press reports on Spirit Airlines impact to Coforge characterized as negligible to none, with budgeted revenue from that airline about 10 bps of FY27 revenue.

Analyst raised concern about potential near-term headwinds in product engineering (more with Encora than Coforge legacy portfolio) as smaller SaaS companies could face pressure from AI; management responded that the answer is no and expects the high-tech business to grow from Q1 FY27.

One top-three banking client did not grow in FY26, constraining BFS vertical growth to 12%; account has been transferred to new stewardship with a refactored engagement approach; management does not attribute this to GCC (captive) movement.
Ongoing mark-to-market hedge losses expected to continue for one to two more quarters before tapering off from the third quarter.
General macro/AI deflation uncertainty flagged as a factor affecting whether historical order-book-to-revenue conversion multiples (1.3x-1.4x) will hold for FY27.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: FY27 is expected to be an exceptional year despite significant AI-driven flux; revenue growth is expected to be robust and industry-leading, though management declined to give a specific number, citing a challenging environment.
Margin guidance reflects a structural reset from automation and AI-led interventions plus holding G&A costs constant in absolute terms via AI-based interventions.
Management expects FY28 EBIT margin to improve incrementally over FY27, with the FY27 guided threshold expected to be the minimum baseline from FY28 onwards.
FCF to PAT guidance raised to 100% minimum for FY27 (from prior 70-80%), with potential to move to 110-120% in a couple of years.
Q1 FY27 expected to be flattish on a QoQ reported basis due to the India portfolio discontinuation, with fast growth trajectory expected from Q2 onwards.
Travel, healthcare, banking, insurance, public sector, and the new high-tech vertical are all expected to perform extremely well in FY27.
BFS performance expected to improve in FY27 over FY26 following resolution of a client-specific issue.
High-tech (Encora) business expected to start growing from Q1 FY27 and grow handsomely through the year.

guidance_ledger.statement: We believe revenue growth will be robust... we should be able to deliver industry-leading growth, but the intent is not to classify that or offer hard numbers around it.
Confident of achieving EBITDA margins of 20.5% to 21% in FY27 on a consolidated basis, which is including Encora.
EBIT margins of 16.5% to 17% on a standalone basis, that is, excluding Encora.
15.5% on a consolidated basis, which includes Encora.
We anticipate free cash flow to PAT to be maintained at 100% from FY27 onwards in contrast to our earlier guidance of 70 to 80%.
Steady state effective tax rate guidance for FY27 is between 23% and 24%.

We should be able to improve FY28 over FY27, obviously not by this quantum. But at least incrementally, the threshold that we have shared for FY27 will be the minimum that should be expected from us starting FY28 onwards.
In another couple of years, this can move towards 110% to 120%.
We expect to be flattish in Q1 and to be on a very fast growth trajectory from Q2 onwards; net-net, expecting a flattish quarter next quarter on a QoQ reported basis.
We expect performance around BFS to improve in FY27 over FY26.
We expect the high-tech business to start growing from Q1 itself and grow handsomely through FY27.
Around 0.8% to 0.9%... it will stay around 0.7% to 0.8%.
The expected run rate as a base is around $4 million to $5 million per quarter.

themes.note: Q4 EBIT margin hit a record 16.6% via AI-led automation, SG&A leverage, and G&A discipline, with FY27 guidance of 20.5-21% EBITDA margin and 15.5-17% EBIT margin.

themes.label: AI-led transformation and moats
themes.note: Company built six moats (domain expertise, client intimacy, delivery model, agility, OneAI platform, AI-enabled workforce) to capture AI value pools via ModSquads and reference architecture.
