key_takeaways: The firm grew 29.2% in U.S. dollar terms in FY26, with growth led by top 10 and top 20 client relationships and broad-based performance across all key industry units.
Signed 21 large deals through the year, with 11 of them coming through in the second half of the year.
Reported EBIT of the firm grew by 370 bps in FY26 over FY25.
Q4 FY26 EBIT of the firm is 16.6%, while it was 12.3% in the same quarter a year back.
Free cash flow to PAT for the quarter came in at 110%, significantly ahead of guidance of around 70% FCF on a sustained basis.
The executable order book stands at a record 1.75 billion USD, 16.4% higher than at the same time last year.

Confident of achieving EBITDA margins of 20.5% to 21% in FY27 on a consolidated basis (including Encora), EBIT margins of 16.5% to 17% on a standalone basis and 15.5% on a consolidated basis; FCF to PAT metrics going forward expected to be 100% plus.

A planned closure of a $20 million low-margin portfolio of the India business will impact Q1 FY27 revenue by $15-20 million, but management expects a flattish Q1 FY27 on a QoQ reported basis due to offsetting order book/deals.
pressing_questions: Does the previous 1.3x to 1.4x conversion multiple to the 12-month order book still hold given a punchy implied FY27 growth number, or should a higher/lower conversion rate be assumed depending on global macros or AI deflation?
How much of the margin upgrade is down to internal AI usage versus pricing/getting into more identified solutions that can lead to better pricing?
What prompted the hedge book reclassification, and what guidance is available on that change?

Given AI code is cheaper to write but more expensive to maintain/integrate, will the AI opportunity lead to an overall expansion of the ~$250 billion IT industry, and could mid-tier players be bigger beneficiaries in this cycle versus Tier 1 players who captured more value in the prior digital/cloud cycle?

Could there be near-term revenue headwinds in product engineering, particularly with Encora more than the Coforge portfolio, as smaller SaaS companies face pressure, even if longer-term share gains occur from early AI coding adoption?

COFORGE.about: Coforge is an IT services company providing end-to-end software solutions and services. . It is among the top-20 Indian software exporters. Prominent global customers include British Airways, the ING group, SEI Investments, Sabre, and SITA. Over the years, Coforge has set up subsidiaries in the US, Singapore, Australia, UK, Germany and Thailand, mainly to market and mobilise projects for the software division. The company has business partnerships with large IT companies across the world.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw one of the highest-ever EBITDA margins (13.6%) despite a ~30% sequential market dip; management expects industry M&HCV volumes to be 5%-10% lower than FY26 (best case: flat with last year), with Q2 reasonable, Q3 increasing, and Q4 peaking, subject to monsoon and geopolitical headwinds. Capacity expansion (Phase-1/1A, ~40% complete) continues to prepare for a stronger Q4 and future opportunities, with PAT margin guided in a 7.5%-8.5% band for coming quarters and margins expected to improve further toward 2030 aspirations.

key_figures.label: Revenue from operations (prior quarter, INR crores)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin of 13.6% is one of the highest ever reported, aided by a one-off benefit to a small extent and favorable product mix in the quarter.

Employee benefit expenses came down sequentially due to workforce pull-back after high deployment in the prior quarter (Q4) for higher volumes, and moderation of long-term settlement impact that had been taken in Q4.
Other expenses remained fairly in line with revenue.
Cost headwinds noted from post-war LPG cost increases and increases in tooling and consumables; company has been absorbing these costs and is in negotiation to offset them.
EPS of ~Rs. 30 is the highest quarterly EPS reported in the last four years.

subsections.label: Revenue movement
points: Top line varies along with market; revenue dipped from Rs. 669 crores in the prior quarter to Rs. 527 crores this quarter as the market came off its peak.

subsections.label: Commodity pass-through
points: All commodity costs (steel, casting, forging) are settled back-to-back with customers as a complete passthrough, so the company has no direct impact from commodity price increases.
Conversion cost increases (e.g., from steel/gas price rises) were absorbed this quarter, with the company working with customers in parallel to offset the impact in the future.
Electrification of one furnace was completed just in time, helping manage production despite lower LPG availability.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: For the next few quarters, PAT margin band is expected to be 7.5%-8.5%, a target range the company will work within.
For 2030, given market growth and capacity increases, margins are expected to move up as economies of scale kick in.
Return on assets/return on capital employed has always been strong and management will continue to focus on maintaining/improving this metric.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: FY26 was at peak, going back to FY2019 levels; usual Q1 dip occurred (~30%) but Q1 FY27 was still one of the highest in past several years at ~110,000 vehicles in M&HCV segment.
OEMs did a good job maintaining production and sales in both retail and dealers; momentum carried forward from Q4 of last year.
Product mix and new product launches helped keep the momentum from Q4.
Replacement cycle demand is a major driver: vehicles sold in 2017-2018 (with a COVID-related gap) are now entering their 7-9 year service replenishment period, causing a significant shift in volume.
Customers now have the option to upgrade to higher tonnage GVW vehicles (e.g., 10x2 or 4x2 tractor trailer instead of two 6x2s), which did not exist as an option in 2017-2018.
Delayed monsoon is currently helping the industry via continued freight movement and replacement demand; without it, a dip in the current quarter would have been seen.
Q4 expected to be another peak quarter, barring headwinds like geopolitical tension and monsoon effect.

Best-case scenario for the year is matching last year's volumes if industry navigates geopolitical cost escalations and monsoon plays out well, followed by a strong comeback from September/October and the festive season.
Qualitative year outlook: reasonable Q2, increasing demand in Q3 (barring monsoon risk), Q4 ending at a peak.
GDP growth rate of manufacturing per MPC noted at ~7% for Q1 FY27, supporting overall demand backdrop.

subsections.label: Revised outlook context
points: At the start of the year, projection was for a market 15%-20% lower than last year; revised forecast is now 5%-10% lower.

The initial lower estimate was based on how last year ended and headwinds emerging in Q4 of last year and Q1 of this year (geopolitical tension); delayed monsoon is now helping better sales than otherwise expected.
Industry volume last year was 480,000 vehicles; revised FY27 projection implies more than 450,000 vehicles.

subsections.label: Product mix impact
points: Product mix impact is pure end-market demand driven; there are seasonal demands, e.g., school buses get ordered just before school starts for replenishment.
When there are more buses in the mix, the company sees a slight dip, which is not a loss of share of business but reflects market behavior.

Sales growth lower than CV production growth in Q1 attributed to product mix and conversion of increased market share versus prior comparisons; performance from prior year's comparable quarter was actually better than 5% despite a 30% lower market.

subsections.label: Defense segment
points: Defense requires a different mindset — low volume, application-demanding, high-intensity products.
Timeline from RFQ to SOP (start of production) can range from 3 to 10 years.
Company wants diversified revenue and does not want too much dependency on defense.
Defense revenue contribution is currently 5%-10% of overall revenue depending on how tenders are awarded; can be lower or higher depending on tender timing.

subsections.label: Mining segment
points: Company is not actively pursuing deep/large mining equipment segment in India due to low volumes and different product requirements versus on-highway products.
Had a few mining products in the past, but those OEMs could not deliver them into the market.
Mining is viewed as a niche market; decision not to pursue is based on opportunity size and bandwidth/focus needed for core M&HCV business.

subsections.label: Ashok Leyland relationship
points: Company continues to aim for single-source status on new products it launches, though each OEM (not just Ashok Leyland) follows a dual-sourcing strategy based on timing.

Broadly maintained market share with Ashok Leyland; market share fluctuates month-over-month/quarter-over-quarter due to product mix, segmental and seasonal shifts, but minimum agreed share of business with the customer is ensured.
Ashok Leyland sole-supplier share previously referenced in the 30-50% range.

subsections.label: New product launches
points: Launching a new 160 tandem axle, already in pilot batch and moving into production mode, with one of the large customers.
Bus axle product launch is still in the pipeline; validation is ongoing.

Company does not want to do another design iteration for bus axles, given upcoming pass-by noise regulation; wants to ensure the launched product covers both current regulation and market need in one iteration.

subsections.label: Regulatory technology roadmap
points: Historically, regulations included emission norms (BS-III, BS-IV), axle load rating increases, and fuel economy norms — company products are already protected and performing well against these.
In the last four years, BS-VI, OBD-I, OBD-II norms have had minimal impact on product lines.
Going forward (next four years, post-2030), anticipated AEBS norms, Type-II Endurance Braking, and BS-VII are not expected to have significant impact.

More stringent pass-by noise norms and HPFE Phase-1B are anticipated to require products to be more noise-sensitive, with noise levels lower than current industry levels — this requires design iteration for gear and other components.

Industry trend of increasing horsepower: historically 60%-80% of market was within 120-180 hp; shifting toward 300+ hp for most heavy-duty applications; current product strategy and pipeline are well-matched to this shift.
Clear trend toward higher HP and shift toward 4x2 tractor-trailers, for which the company already has products in the pipeline and market.

subsections.label: Bus axle regulation clarity
points: The low-floor bus regulation change, which had caused the company to review its product spec, is now behind them — OEMs are managing floor height differently, often without needing a completely different product.
Company is now focused on ensuring the bus axle product also covers upcoming pass-by noise regulations before launch, to avoid a second iteration.

subsections.label: Reliability/product life trend
points: As technology progresses and reliability improves, parts that used to be replenished within 1 year to 18 months may extend to 3-6 years, starting roughly five years from now.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion progress
points: Nearly 40% of Phase-1 and Phase-1(a) CAPEX investment is already done, with some level of production already started.
Company is preparing for expected stronger demand in Q4.

Company is also focused on continuously improving automation, bringing in more automated lines, with focus on both safety and quality as well as improving productivity to improve top line while adding to bottom line.

subsections.label: CAPEX breakup (Rs. 120 crore program)
points: Difficult to split CAPEX cleanly between growth capacity vs. equipment replacement; new CAPEX is generally either to upgrade existing lines/equipment or completely replace with fully-automated equipment.

Capacity being added is intended to cover the next two to three years of market growth, keep the company ready for peak volumes in a particular month/quarter, and address potential export opportunities.
Capacity depends on product mix; overall capacity improvement estimated at roughly 25%-30%.

key_figures.label: Expected export share range for the year

subsections.label: Export performance
points: Exports traditionally range 8%-12% of revenue; this quarter came in slightly better at 13%.

The 13% figure represents only a marginal shift (roughly 3 percentage points upward from a 10% average) and is not expected to be a sustained new range; 8%-12% will remain the broad range for the year overall.
If opportunities arise, the company may fare better than this range in the future.
Exports are directed mainly to other CDBS (Cummins Drivetrain and Braking Systems) global entities/plants, not to the general market.

subsections.label: Export logistics
points: Logistics remain a persistent challenge; sea freight rates change randomly and sometimes ad hoc.
Company is trying to plan well ahead, especially for imports.
Many export cases are Ex-Works, providing support from customers regarding freight.
Sea freight has not been a major hurdle for the company so far despite being challenging and unpredictable.

key_figures.label: Anticipated future horsepower range for heavy duty applications
Vehicle age reference for demand shift

subsections.label: Competitive landscape - American Axle / Bharat Forge
points: American Axle and Automotive Axles are competitors; company does not have much information about American Axle's strategy/plans and cannot comment on it.
Company focus remains on existing customers, increasing share of business, and acquiring new customers.
Company's heavy presence is in the heavy-duty segment (40-ton and above), which is also its strong global foothold; new product launches are focused on this segment.
Overlap with American Axle's product profile is currently minimal since the two companies' focus areas are largely different; independent market reports are available for competition data.
Company has 30-40 years of experience following market trends and ensuring the right product is ready when trends change.

subsections.label: Meritor / Cummins Drivetrain Systems collaboration
points: Long-standing collaboration model since formation of both companies, covering domestic demand shaping, product changes impacting capacity/investment decisions.
Looking at global supply chain role for Cummins Drivetrain Systems, assessing how India can contribute more, with new investments prompting more deliberate strategy on India's strengths.
Considering defense and aftermarket as additional growth avenues alongside commercial vehicle and export business.
Aftermarket business is being grown through MHVSIL's distribution of captive Meritor products, alongside growing the overall product mix range with the market.

Meritor provides new product licensing, testing for India-specific applications (endurance testing for different local truck configurations), application analysis, customer go-to-market strategy formulation, and works with customers on application - support expected to continue for the foreseeable future.
Meritor agreement extended till 2027.

subsections.label: Long-term volume outlook
points: MHCV volume guidance is roughly flat at around 5 lakh vehicles through FY2030.

subsections.label: Execution priorities
points: Top priority is readiness with capacity investment (Phase-1/Phase-1(a) CAPEX).
Continuous automation improvement, focusing on safety, quality and productivity to improve both top line and bottom line.
Continuously looking at adjacencies including defense segment, and increasing share of business with existing customers, contingent on having required internal and supply-chain capacity.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Geopolitical tension flagged as a headwind affecting Q4 outlook and overall industry projection.
Monsoon effect flagged as a key headwind/uncertainty; delayed monsoon is currently helping demand, but future course is unknown.
Post-war LPG cost increases and increases in tooling/consumables have created cost headwinds, which the company is absorbing while negotiating offsets.
Sea freight rate volatility and unpredictability remain a logistics risk for exports, though not a major hurdle so far.

Regulatory changes (AEBS norms, Type-II Endurance Braking, BS-VII, pass-by noise norms, HPFE Phase-1B) require design iteration, particularly for noise-sensitive products, though not expected to have major impact on product lines over next 4-5 years.
Defense segment RFQ-to-SOP gestation period (3-10 years) and tender-based nature pose planning risk; company deliberately avoids over-dependence on this segment.
Mining segment risk: past products for mining OEMs were not successfully delivered to market, reinforcing decision not to actively pursue this niche.

subsections.label: Year outlook
points: Market may be 5%-10% lower compared to last year, or at best case match last year's volumes.
Q1 and Q2 expected to help bring volumes that would otherwise have been considered lower than last year.
Company's share of business has been steady, with continuous focus on increasing shares of business.
Both headwinds (monsoon, unknown outcome) and tailwinds (potential opportunity to keep exports steady and stronger) are present.
Management declined to give explicit quantitative future guidance on volume growth, citing potential addressable business opportunities tied to capacity readiness rather than committed numbers.
2030 aspirations: margins expected to move up as market grows and capacity increases bring economies of scale; return on assets/capital employed focus to continue.

guidance_ledger.statement: PAT margin range of 7.5%-8.5% is the target band the company will be working in for coming quarters.
Revised forecast suggests industry volumes could be 5%-10% lower than last year, best case matching last year's volumes (vs. earlier estimate of 15%-20% lower).
Roughly 25%-30% capacity improvement expected from the current CAPEX program.
Export share expected to remain in the broad 8%-12% range for the year overall, despite a one-quarter uptick to 13%.
Margins expected to move up the ladder as market grows and capacity expansion brings economies of scale, keeping 2030 aspirations in mind.
Management declined to give explicit quantitative future guidance on volume growth beyond qualitative commentary on capacity readiness and market opportunity.
Company will continue to focus on maintaining and improving return on assets/return on capital employed.
Q4 expected to be another peak quarter, barring headwinds like geopolitical tension and monsoon effect.
Qualitative outlook: reasonable Q2, increasing demand in Q3 (barring monsoon risk), Q4 ending at a peak.
Defense contributes roughly 5%-10% of revenue depending on tender award timing; company wants diversified revenue without over-dependence on defense.
Bus axle product launch is still in the pipeline with validation ongoing, ensuring it covers upcoming pass-by noise regulation before launch.
Meritor collaboration agreement extended till 2027, continuing support for product licensing, testing, and go-to-market strategy.
Aspirational target of INR4,500-5,000 crores top line over the next 4-5 years, reiterated in this call as INR4,000-5,000 crores with exports contributing more than current levels.
Industry expected to remain 400,000-plus in FY27, with most OEMs expecting a good year, though exact number (420k/450k/480k) too early to call.
Industry TIV expected to be 500,000-plus by 2029-2030.
Phase 1 and Phase 1A capacity expansion committed to be completed by end of December 2026.
Company will finalize the next phase of capex investment in the next 6 to 12/18 months based on domestic and export market outlook; quantum not yet disclosed.
Similar range of capex spend as FY26 (INR70+ crores) expected in the upcoming year to complete already-committed phases.
Management declined explicit forward guidance on EBITDA margin range but reiterated that efficiency initiatives will offset inflation/adverse mix and margins are expected to improve going forward.
Q1 and Q2 of FY27 expected to be a typical softer market historically, consistent with past patterns.
Company will continue to pursue off-highway and slipper suspension businesses and improve ICV products, while core focus remains heavy-duty market; no major expansion planned.

risk_register.note: Flagged as a headwind that could affect Q4 outlook and the overall industry volume projection for FY27.
Currently helping demand via freight movement and replacement cycle, but future course is unknown and flagged as the primary watch-item headwind for the rest of the year.
Post-war LPG cost increases and tooling/consumable cost increases created headwinds this quarter; company absorbed the cost and is negotiating with customers to offset in future.
Sea freight rates change randomly/ad hoc, a persistent logistics challenge for exports, though not a major hurdle so far.

risk_register.risk: Upcoming regulatory changes (pass-by noise, HPFE Phase-1B, AEBS, Type-II Endurance Braking, BS-VII)
risk_register.note: Expected to require product design iteration for noise sensitivity but not seen as having significant impact on product lines over the next 4-5 years.

risk_register.risk: Defense segment gestation and tender dependency
risk_register.note: RFQ-to-SOP period can be 3-10 years and tender-based awards create revenue variability; company avoids over-dependence on this segment.
Past mining OEM products failed to reach market; company continues to avoid active pursuit of this niche segment.

risk_register.risk: Competitive entry (American Axle via Bharat Forge)
risk_register.note: Viewed as an existing competitor with currently minimal product overlap; not seen as a new threat to market share.
Steel and metal prices have increased over the last 1-2 months; company relies on back-to-back customer agreements and provisioning to protect financials, with possible lag in adjustment.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical situation and interest rate cuts
risk_register.note: Lowered investment/other income in Q4 due to geopolitical situations and interest rate cuts; most investment income is in recovery stage.
Temporary tariff-related situation in the US viewed as near-term headwind to export order accumulation, though long-run visibility remains positive excluding this factor.
Q1 and Q2 of the financial year are typically softer historically for the CV industry, expected to continue in FY27; April-May FY27 utilization already softened to 70-80% from over 90% in Q4 FY26.
Shift from multi-axle rigid to 4x2 tractor trailer could reduce pure axle numbers produced per vehicle, though offset by product coverage across configurations, not considered a loss of business.

risk_register.risk: Uncertainty on India market readiness for e-axle/smart axle adoption
risk_register.note: India market not yet ready for e-axle; smart axle penetration limited even in developed markets, and definition of 'smart' varies by region, making timing of adoption uncertain.

themes.label: CV Demand Upcycle
themes.note: FY26 peaked at 2019-levels; Q1 FY27 saw a normal ~30% sequential dip but was still one of the highest Q1 volumes historically; FY27 industry volume outlook revised upward from 15-20% lower to 5-10% lower vs last year, with best case matching last year.

themes.label: Capacity Expansion
themes.note: Phase-1/1A CAPEX ~40% complete, production already started; expected to deliver 25-30% capacity improvement and readiness for Q4 peak demand and export opportunities.

themes.label: Export Growth Lever
themes.note: Exports rose to 13% of revenue this quarter (vs typical 8-12% range), directed to CDBS global entities; expected to stay in 8-12% broad range for the year with upside potential.

themes.label: Technical Fee / New Sales Agreement with Meritor HVS
themes.note: Meritor continues providing product licensing, India-specific testing/application analysis, and go-to-market support under an agreement extended till 2027.

themes.label: Input Cost Inflation & Margin Protection
themes.note: Post-war LPG and tooling/consumable cost increases absorbed this quarter; commodity costs remain a complete passthrough to customers; conversion cost offsets being negotiated.

themes.label: Product Mix Shift (Tractor Trailer vs Rigid Axle)
themes.note: Replacement cycle and upgrade to higher-tonnage GVW vehicles (e.g., 10x2/4x2 tractor trailers) driving volume shift; bus mix causes slight share dips that are attributed to market behavior, not share loss.

themes.label: New Technology Readiness (E-axle/Smart Axle/ADAS)
themes.note: New 160 tandem axle entering production; bus axle launch pending validation to also meet upcoming pass-by noise regulation in a single design iteration; long-term regulatory roadmap (AEBS, BS-VII, noise norms) seen as manageable.

key_takeaways: Overall, our cost of raw materials, like overall our metal cost, was about 65% for the quarter. This is kind of helped by some one-off that we had to a small extent, also some favorable mix from the products that we had sold in the quarter.
Overall, the EBITDA stood at Rs. 702 million, which is at about 13.6%. In the last quarter, we reported 12.4% EBITDA. The same time last year, we had reported 9.7% EBITDA.

Moving on, the profit for the year stood at Rs. 455 million. Obviously, net of the OCI, it is Rs. 452 million at about 8.7%. Again, this is with an EPS of about Rs. 30. I think in Q1, in the last four years, I think this is the highest quarterly EPS that we have reported.
Even though we did see a dip, almost like 30%, but that quarter, Q1 ended up to be one of the highest in the past several years at almost 110,000 vehicles in the M&HCV segment.

Beginning of this year, we had a projection, which was 15%-20% lower than last year. Now, the revised forecast, which is also what the industry is speaking about, is it could be less than 5%-10% dip compared to last year. Just for reference, last year, the industry volume was 480,000. If you do the math, we should be north of 450,000. Best case, same as last year.
So, roughly again, the capacity depends on the product mix. Roughly, I would say that we are looking at anywhere between 25%-30% capacity improvement.

So, Shikha, our exports are traditionally in the range of 8%-12%. I think that’s been what we have seen in the last year. This time we were slightly better off in terms of exports. So, we were at about 13% for the quarter, on the overall pie.

We are launching a new tandem axles, which is already in pilot batch, and it’s getting into production mode as we speak. This is a 160 tandem, so we are launching this with one of the large customers.
pressing_questions: Sir, the small point which I am trying to make understand, given the current business environment, what are the likelihoods of our company performing in comparison to the previous financial year in terms of volume growth? Secondly, sir, I think so with some notification from the State Government Bus Department in terms of some floor height and all were pending when you addressed your investors in the last call so any further clarification on the same and the introduction of those axles into the buses, what's the roadmap?
Sir, did we lose some market share from our main OEM, Ashok Leyland, for this quarter in terms of the income total pie, sir?

Sir, our overall sales growth has been lower than the CV production in the country for Quarter 1. Have we lost any market share to our leading customer? Going forward, as even American Axle enters the larger truck axles, do you see any potential loss of market share after two, three years?

quarters.summary: Automotive Axles Ltd closed FY26 on a high note riding a strong CV industry upcycle (480,000 vehicles, +16% YoY), with Q4 revenue up 18% YoY/QoQ and full-year EBITDA margin improving ~40-50bps YoY to 10.6% (net of exceptional item). Management expects the industry to remain in a "400,000-plus" stable zone in FY27, with capacity expansion (Phase 1/1A by December 2026), new product ramp-up (185 tandem/HR axles), and export growth as the key levers toward an aspirational topline of INR4,000-5,000 crores over the next 4-5 years, while Q1/Q2 FY27 are expected to see the typical seasonal softness.

key_figures.label: One-off portion of employee benefit expense (leave encashment settlement)
One-off portion of employee benefit expense (leave encashment settlement)

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 P&L drivers
points: Other income was lower than last quarter given geopolitical situations and interest rate cuts affecting investment income; most investment income is in recovery stage as of the call.
Material cost slightly improved YoY at ~68% of revenue, in line with the new business model.
Employee benefit expenses at 7% of revenue were mostly flat vs sequential quarter.
Depreciation slightly up because some investments got capitalized in the last quarter.
Other expenses at INR880 million were slightly up due to a variable portion linked to revenue.
No exceptional item in Q4, unlike the previous quarter which had reported some exceptional item.
PAT margin of 8% in Q4 FY26 was sustained at the same level as Q4 FY25, despite a significantly varied cost structure between the two years.

subsections.label: FY26 full-year P&L drivers
points: Metal cost stable and improving YoY at close to 68%.
Employee cost rose from 6.7% to 7.3% of revenue YoY due to a onetime workmen settlement in the last quarter that is applicable for the next 4 years.
Total other expenses at 14.26% of revenue are in line with revenue given the variable portion in the new business model.
EBITDA margin net of exceptional item improved 40-50 bps YoY to 10.6% from 10.1% in the previous year.

subsections.label: Cash flow and capital allocation
points: Capex spend of more than INR70 crores in FY26, representing about 60-70% of committed investment spend.
Net of investments, the company generated INR30 crores of cash in FY26.
Similar range of capex spend is expected in the upcoming year (FY27) to complete already-announced phases.

subsections.label: Technical fee structure (post new sales agreement with Meritor HVS)
points: Technical fee paid to Meritor HVS is in the range of 4% to 4.5% of sales, depending on revenue mix.
All quarterly results, including Q4, are reported after considering the technical fee.
The exact split of technical fee by domestic vs export was not disclosed due to agreement confidentiality.

key_figures.label: CV industry stable range since FY23
Variation in industry volumes between FY23-FY25
Industry total tonnage carrying capacity (previous peak)

subsections.label: Demand drivers in FY26
points: GST cuts in the later part of the year and fleets (large and small) trying to capture the benefit drove demand.
Replacement cycle kicked in a little earlier than earlier predictions, leading fleets to replace vehicles.
Very positive sentiment showed up all the way to the last date of March, with Q4 a phenomenal number for the industry and each OEM crossing individual records.
Company converted a good amount of new products launched during the year at a high success rate.

subsections.label: Cyclicality and outlook commentary
points: Industry cyclicality has narrowed (peaks and valleys) over the last 3-4 years compared to historical patterns; variation was within 5% from FY23 to FY25 before the 16% growth in FY26.
FY27 is expected to also be a good year (400,000+) per most OEM partners, but exact number (420k/450k/480k) is too early to call, as nobody forecasted the actual 480,000 achieved in FY26.

Q1 and Q2 of FY27 are typically a softer market historically, and this pattern is expected to continue; how the company comes out of monsoon and ends Q4 FY27 will define whether growth is +20% or +5%.
As of the call, current OEM demand schedules have not changed despite rising diesel prices; too early to comment on that dynamic's effect on demand.
Industry tonnage growth (8.7 million tonnes in FY19 to 9.4 million tonnes in FY26 at similar vehicle production levels) reflects increasing share of heavy-duty/higher tonnage vehicles.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization / demand fulfilment
points: Company operated at over 90% capacity utilization in Q4 FY26 (peak capacity).
In April-May FY27, the market softened; company generally operates between 70% to 80% of capacity in this period.
Unless the market goes beyond volumes seen in the last Q4, the company does not see capacity constraints at this point.

key_figures.label: Realization uplift from single to tandem axle

subsections.label: Product mix shift: tractor trailers vs rigid multi-axle
points: Clear trend over the last couple of years of increasing proportion of tractor trailers, specifically 4x2, driven by anticipated market shift; company had product ready in advance (185 axle launched a couple of years ago, now ramping up significantly) to cater to heavy-duty tractor trailer market.

This represents cannibalization of some products in the rigid/multi-axle rigid vehicle platform as it shifts to 4x2 tractor trailer, but not a loss of business since the company's product portfolio covers every segment.
The 185 axle product, initially launched with one customer 3-4 years ago, has now been launched with all major customers.

Pure axle numbers produced may decline due to configuration change from multi-axle to single axle, but this is a continuation of business, not loss of business, given company's coverage across configurations.

subsections.label: LCV/ICV/off-highway/slipper suspension segments
points: Off-highway business sustained over several years with existing customer; company closely monitoring the off-highway industry given unique regional product portfolios; current supply continues without major expansion.

Slipper suspension continues to be supplied to the largest customer under a different arrangement where supply chain has been handed over to make it easier to manage given close association with chassis/assembly line.
ICV is not a strong hold for the company globally; products continue to be improved and supplied to the same customers, but the core focus remains heavy-duty market.
LCV/ICV segment strategy deliberately limited; company does not want to go beyond a certain GVW/GAW level as required investment may not yield adequate return versus core heavy-duty business.

subsections.label: Customer relationships (Ashok Leyland, Tata Motors)
points: Ashok Leyland axle market share maintained on average for the whole year per existing agreement; difficult to speak to a single day/week/month given product mix volatility, so company aims for a healthy average balancing top line and profitability.
Primary supply to Tata Motors currently is brakes only; occasional/non-regular business for export market or buses products as needed by Tata.
For brakes, company maintains a multi-OEM strategy (not single OEM) to balance capacity utilization.
On the axle side with Tata Motors, there are continuous discussions at different levels, but no confirmed strategy disclosed to increase wallet share.

subsections.label: New product value capture / pricing strategy
points: New products aligned with changing OEM strategies; company captures value pricing based on features and benefits, even where some legacy product cannibalization occurs.
New products are marginally better in profitability compared to legacy products due to value-based pricing strategy, a longstanding policy.

subsections.label: Gears for buses and coaches
points: Company is developing and testing gears required for buses and coaches, an area viewed as a potential opportunity to increase share of business in segments where currently present but not very strong.

subsections.label: Bus code / low-floor regulation product
points: There is more clarity now on the low-floor bus code regulation; current product portfolio can meet most requirements, though some OEMs have different, still-evolving strategies; products for this regulation are protected/covered.

subsections.label: E-axle technology readiness
points: E-axle technology/architecture is an add-on to the traditional mechanical axle (adds electric motor and power electronics on top of existing mechanical gear content).
India market is not yet ready for e-axle adoption; industry remains in the traditional central drive plus mechanical axle world, which the company's current product portfolio already protects.
Content-per-vehicle uplift for e-axle depends on pricing strategy for India, which is too early to comment on.

subsections.label: Smart axle / digitalization (ADAS, electronic braking)
points: ADAS and electronic braking systems will happen but have no influence on the company's mechanical axles or brakes currently.

Company has a couple of axles qualified as 'smart axle' in the global portfolio, but these are not applicable to Indian markets as of now; if the market moves in that direction, products are available and would require licensing and industrializing.
Smart axle penetration is very limited even in developed countries; definition of 'smart' is unique to each region, making timing difficult to predict.
Products are available for whenever demand for smart axles emerges in India; company states 'when it happens, we will be there.'

subsections.label: Regulatory impact on brake/axle technology
points: Foundation brake product line is not expected to change much from upcoming safety regulations in the next 3-5 years, unless a very stringent stopping-distance norm emerges, which is not currently seen in regulatory discussions.

Western world's shift from drum to disc brakes is expected to remain a niche market (buses, hazardous goods) under current Indian regulatory landscape, meaning current drum brake capacity and demand can continue.

No major regulation changes seen on the axle side; one regulation on overload has been partially regularized but reflects typical overload already seen on Indian roads and has not changed the product portfolio.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion plans
points: Phase 1 and Phase 1A capacity expansion to be completed by end of December 2026.

Next phase of capex investment (beyond Phase 1/1A) will be finalized in the next 6-9/6-12/6-18 months based on both domestic and export market outlook; management could not yet forecast the quantum of this investment.
Capex is not only for adding capacity but also to bring in latest technology and efficient equipment to offset inflationary pressure on fixed costs and improve productivity.
Similar range of capex spend (as FY26's INR70+ crores) is expected in FY27 to complete already-committed phases.

subsections.label: Capacity vs demand management
points: Company initiated capacity expansion about 12 months ago in anticipation that product mix shift would limit its ability to serve peak market demand.
Unless market volumes exceed the levels seen in Q4 FY26, company does not see capacity constraints currently.
Capacity being created is targeted at meeting peak domestic demand (expected TIV of 500,000+ by 2029-2030) plus export opportunity, with uncertainty on exact product mix.

subsections.label: Export strategy
points: Exports are expected to be a key lever toward the aspirational topline target of INR4,000-5,000 crores over the next 4-5 years, with export contribution expected to be better than the current level.
Long-run visibility for accumulating export orders remains positive, ignoring temporary U.S. tariff-related situations; this is part of the company's global supply chain strategy.
Investments in capacity/process robustness are aligned with both export and domestic market demand.

Product line differences in Europe and North America (different axle configurations) mean exports will largely be limited to assemblies, subassemblies, and child parts rather than fully dressed/assembled axles, due to regional customization requirements.
Export growth also serves as a hedge/flexibility if the domestic market sees a downside, since global products are already plugged into the manufacturing strategy.
After the new technical fee/sales agreement, the company now directly supplies to OEs/Tier 1s in both exports and domestic markets.

subsections.label: Addressable market strategy (LCV/ICV/SUV)
points: Company's core global strength lies in medium and heavy-duty axles (Class 8 in the US, heavy-duty in Europe, and same focus in India), which differentiates it from competition.

Company already has products in ICV/LCV where it strategically wants to play but does not intend to go beyond a certain GVW/GAW level given investment-return tradeoffs versus the core heavy-duty business.
No plan disclosed to specifically expand into SUV segment.

subsections.label: FY27 priorities
points: Priority 1: complete all capex investments on time (targeted by December 2026) and realize associated benefits.

Priority 2: develop technology/products such as gears for buses and coaches (under development/testing) to realize additional share of business in segments where the company is present but not very strong.
Priority 3: remain sensitive to market demand changes, continuously focus on protecting and growing bottom line, and stay ready for potential export market opportunities.

subsections.label: New sales/technical agreement with Meritor HVS
points: Company has changed the sales agreement; under the new arrangement, it pays a technical fee to Meritor HVS in the range of 4% to 4.5% of sales depending on revenue mix.
Under the new agreement, the company now supplies directly to OEs/Tier 1s, in both export and domestic markets.
Management declined to disclose the exact percentage of sales attributable to exports to Meritor Global or the domestic/export split of the technical fee due to agreement terms.

subsections.label: Commodity price inflation
points: Steel and other metal prices have increased over the last 1-2 months.
Company has back-to-back agreements with most customers for commodity cost pass-through, a standard industry practice, though there may be a lag in adjustment.
Financial results are already trued up to the last cost increase; provisions are taken and settlement may happen later, protecting the financials.
Company aims to offset any inflationary pressure through operational efficiency and productivity improvements, both internally and via supply chain, as demonstrated historically.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/interest rate environment
points: Other/investment income in Q4 was lower given geopolitical situations and interest rate cuts in the market; most investment income is in the recovery stage.

subsections.label: US tariff situation
points: Temporary tariff-related situation in the US is viewed as a near-term headwind to export order accumulation, though long-run export visibility remains positive when this is set aside.

subsections.label: Seasonal demand softness
points: Q1 and Q2 of the financial year are typically a softer market historically for the CV industry, and this pattern is expected to continue into FY27.

subsections.label: Product mix/configuration risk
points: Shift from multi-axle rigid vehicles to 4x2 tractor trailer configurations could reduce the pure number of axles produced per vehicle, though this is expected to be offset by continuation of business given the company's product coverage across configurations.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Management declined to give a specific forward-looking EBITDA margin target for the next 5 years but reiterated confidence that efficiency initiatives will offset inflationary pressure and adverse product mix, and margins are expected to improve going forward.
FY27 industry demand expected to remain 400,000+ per most OEM partners, though the exact figure (420k/450k/480k) is uncertain given last year's outcome (480k) was not forecasted in advance.
Q1/Q2 FY27 expected to see typical seasonal softness consistent with historical patterns; how the company performs post-monsoon through Q4 will determine whether growth is closer to +20% or +5%.
Similar range of capex spend expected in FY27 as in FY26 (INR70+ crores) to complete already-committed capacity phases.
Next phase of capex beyond Phase 1/1A to be finalized in the next 6-12 months based on domestic and export market outlook; quantum not yet disclosed.

themes.label: Capacity Expansion
themes.note: Phase 1/1A capacity expansion to complete by December 2026; next phase capex to be finalized in 6-12 months based on demand outlook; utilization was over 90% in Q4 FY26 before softening to 70-80% in Apr-May.

themes.label: Export Growth Lever
themes.note: Exports positioned as key lever toward INR4,000-5,000 crore aspirational topline target, limited to assemblies/subassemblies/child parts due to regional product differences, tempered by temporary US tariff situation.

themes.label: Technical Fee / New Sales Agreement with Meritor HVS
themes.note: Under new sales agreement, company pays Meritor HVS a technical fee of 4-4.5% of sales and now supplies directly to OEs/Tier 1s in both domestic and export markets.

themes.label: Input Cost Inflation & Margin Protection
themes.note: Steel/metal prices rising, but back-to-back customer agreements and productivity/efficiency improvements protect margins; FY26 EBITDA margin improved 40-50bps YoY to 10.6%.

themes.label: Product Mix Shift (Tractor Trailer vs Rigid Axle)
themes.note: Rising tractor trailer (4x2) proportion cannibalizes rigid multi-axle demand but is covered by company's 185 axle product across all major customers, not seen as a net loss of business.

themes.label: New Technology Readiness (E-axle/Smart Axle/ADAS)
themes.note: India market not yet ready for e-axle or smart axle adoption; global portfolio has smart axle products ready but timing of Indian adoption remains uncertain.

key_takeaways: We were able to convert the demand and improve both the top and bottom lines.

The industry...has been on a tremendous ride for the last 3, 4 years. We have been seeing consistently 400-plus market since FY '23...FY '26 full year with the market closing at around 480,000 vehicles it is 16% above FY '25.
Q4 is a phenomenal number for the industry, each OEM crossing their own individual records and so did we, with our delivery and production during this quarter.
We also converted a good amount of the new products that we launched during the year and the ramp-up was pretty good done, and we were able to convert that as well at a very high success rate.

EBITDA for the full year is at INR2,692 million at 12.4%. And then we had the exceptional item...Netting of that, our EBITDA stood at 10.6% for the year. When you compare to previous year, we had 10.1%. So we are about 40 to 50 basis points above there.
The technical fee is anywhere in the range between 4% to 4.5% depending on the mix of revenue that we have.
The top line should grow in the order of rough order of INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores with export being a large -- better than the current contribution what we have today.
The last quarter, when I look at it, it was over 90%...April and May, again, the market has softened a little bit. We are still...between 70% to 80% of the capacity.
The Phase 1 and I would say, Phase 1 and 1A, that's what we call is that capacity will be completed by end of December '26.

quarters.summary: Management reiterated FY27 sales volume guidance of 10.5-11 million tonnes and expects to recover the ~300,000-tonne Q1 hot-metal shortfall from the BOF vessel shutdown in subsequent quarters; net debt/EBITDA is expected to fall below the 1.5x threshold in Q2FY27, aided by slurry pipeline commissioning (targeted first half of August, ~INR 700/ton saving from Q2), blast furnace ramp-up to 13,000 tpd by December, and an internal target of ~INR 1,000/ton controllable cost reduction, even as coking coal costs are expected to rise a further $12-15/ton in Q2.

subsections.label: Revenue and realization drivers
points: Consolidated revenue sequentially was around 8% down, largely due to sales volume decline resulting from the plant maintenance shutdown.
Revenue decline was partly offset by around INR 7,500 per ton improvement in average ASP, supported by stronger steel prices and a richer product mix.

subsections.label: EBITDA drivers
points: Despite 15% sequential decline in sales volume, EBITDA remained resilient, reflecting strength of product mix, higher realization, and disciplined cost management.

EBITDA per ton improvement was driven by increase in ASP, partly offset by $23/ton increase in coking coal consumption cost (in line with prior guidance of $20-25/ton) and lower fixed cost absorption due to lower sequential volumes.

subsections.label: Finance cost and depreciation
points: Finance cost increased to INR 548 crores primarily due to capitalization of major expansion assets during Q4FY26 (1,050 MW Captive Power Plant, BOF-III, CRM, and other associated facilities); interest costs on these assets are now recognized through the P&L for the first full quarter.
Depreciation expenses also increased during the quarter following capitalization of these newly commissioned assets.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and leverage
points: Balance sheet remains a key strength; net debt to EBITDA ratio at 1.71x, with confidence of falling below stated threshold of 1.5x during Q2FY27 supported by ramp-up of new facilities and continued focus on cash generation.
Company aims to sustain sub-1.5x leverage through the commodity cycle, reinforcing balance sheet strength.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Capital allocation remains disciplined; against FY27 capex plan of ~INR 8,500 crores, ~INR 2,000 crores invested in Q1.
Cumulative spending under expansion program stands at INR 37,457 crores out of INR 47,043 crores total announced capex.

Financial priorities going forward: driving profitable growth, maximizing returns on expanded asset base, maintaining disciplined capital allocation, generating stronger free cash flow, and preserving balance sheet strength.
Company's capital allocation framework targets 18-20% ROCE from new projects; adding back nominal depreciation gives implied desired EBITDA run-rate from these projects.

subsections.label: Cost breakdown (Q1 QoQ increase)
points: Cost increase breakdown: iron-bearing cost increase ~INR 500/ton, Middle East conflict impact of $12-13/ton, coking coal cost increase of $23/ton, and operating leverage impact from plant maintenance shutdown of ~INR 2,000/ton.

For Q2, coking coal cost increase of $12-15/ton expected, but operating leverage drag (~INR 2,000/ton in Q1) should not recur given higher production and no shutdown; Middle East conflict impact remains a watch item.

Additional cost savings expected from slurry pipeline (~INR 700/ton from Q2), higher captive coal/iron ore mix, and Jindal port loading facility (two vessels already unloaded, one loading in progress) — quantification of port savings not yet provided.

subsections.label: New leadership priorities (CFO)
points: CFO priorities: maintaining capital discipline, improving return on capital employed, strengthening cash generation, preserving balance sheet strength, and creating sustainable long-term value.

Company noted for strong integrated business model, world-class assets, captive raw material resources, disciplined capital allocation, deep adoption of theory of constraints, and growing use of AI/digital tools.

key_figures.label: Price change range across products
key_figures.value: 1,000-4,000 reduction in some products; up to 5,000/ton range overall

subsections.label: Demand environment
points: Domestically, steel industry witnessed seasonal softness typical of the monsoon season.
India continues to be fastest-growing major economy, supported by strong domestic demand, sustained capex, and stable macro environment.
Post-monsoon (from end-August), construction activity expected to recover, supported by Government of India and banking sector lending for infrastructure and construction.

subsections.label: Global steel market
points: China announced policy reset focused on capacity swap reforms to strengthen supply discipline, viewed as a positive development that could accelerate supply-side reforms.
Current mismatch between China capacity reduction (50-60 million tons) and demand decline (100 million tons) has created surplus in the international market.

Resolution of geopolitical conflicts (Ukraine-Russia, Israel-Iran) expected to open opportunities for Indian steel exports as China potentially redirects focus back to exporting machinery/equipment rather than steel.

subsections.label: Pricing trends
points: HRC prices increased sequentially and remained firm through the quarter.
TMT (rebar) prices opened strong but declined as construction slowed during monsoon.
Price-input cost relationship typically has a 4-6 week lag/band, whether prices are rising or falling.

Price cuts of INR 1,000-4,000/ton seen in some products, but prices maintained/retained in rail, rounds, specialty angles/channels, beams, structures, prefabricated structures, and specialty (quench & tempered) plates.
Company sees itself insulated from commodity HRC import pressure via advance licenses since it focuses on value-engineered, not commodity, products.

subsections.label: Seasonal dynamics and recovery potential
points: Company sees itself partially insulated from monsoon weakness given multiple product segments (9 different products); weak demand in one product can be offset via others.
Flood/waterlogging events, while undesirable, could drive future government infrastructure spending (steel/cement demand) to prevent recurrence.

subsections.label: Product mix and value-added strategy
points: Company produces long products, flat products, and specialty flat products (plates, quenched & tempered plates) - considered one of the best product mixes in the world.

Company is only private-sector producer of rails in India; 18-19 of 22 metro rail systems in the country already buy head-hardened rails from Jindal Steel, effectively making it a 100% supplier to Indian metro rail services for these specialty rails.

Company produces round billets (used for rail wheel forging) - only one other company in India produces these; strategic given Government of India's push for self-reliance (Atmanirbhar) in railway wheels.
Company is sole domestic producer of sheet piles and certain specialty heavy-section angle irons.
As newly commissioned downstream facilities ramp up, value-added product share is expected to increase further, enhancing profitability and resilience across commodity cycles.
Value-added product share rose to 66% of sales in Q1FY27 from 61% in Q4FY26.

subsections.label: Defence and specialty steel
points: Government of India's focus on defence has led company to produce specialty plates tailored for submarines, warships, and oxygen/nitrogen/hydrogen storage.
Government has restricted imports of heat-treated (quench & tempered) plates that were previously imported into India, benefiting domestic producers like Jindal Steel.

subsections.label: Unit profitability disconnect
points: Analyst noted value-added and flat product share has risen consistently but EBITDA per ton has not shown commensurate improvement.

Management explained overall EBITDA per ton is a blended figure; product-wise EBITDA (e.g., for quench & tempered plates, heavy-duty plates, head-hardened rails) is not separately published and varies widely - some products earn as high as INR 25,000/ton EBITDA, others only ~INR 7,000/ton.

Currently about 50% of products are high-EBITDA/high-NSR and 50% are low-EBITDA; goal is to convert ~30% of the low-EBITDA volume (about 1.5-2 million tons out of 4-5 million tons) into high-EBITDA value-added products over time.
Target is to produce at least 4 million tons out of 6 million tons of mill capacity as true value-added steel, generating greater value than cost incurred.

subsections.label: Rebar vs rounds substitution
points: Rebar currently not a preferred product in weak demand periods; company shifting toward rounds, which provide additional value addition of INR 5,000-6,000 versus rebar.

subsections.label: Capacity utilization roadmap
points: First and foremost focus is reaching 100% capacity utilization on the installed 15.6 million ton crude steel capacity.

Company will not reach 15.6 million tons in FY27; expects to end around 11-11.5 million tons this year, with a step-ladder path via metallics (HBI, DRI, scrap) to bridge the gap toward 12.5 million tons and beyond.
Additional metallics sourcing (HBI, DRI, scrap) required to fully utilize installed capacity given internal metallics shortfall.

subsections.label: Blast furnace ramp-up
points: New (BF-2) blast furnace at Angul is state-of-the-art, imported equipment, commissioned in 28-30 months versus ~5 years taken by a comparable Tata Steel furnace.
Monsoon-related disruptions (heavy rain >100mm in 1-2 hours) affected water management and electrical grid, slowing ramp-up; expected to resume ramp from September as monsoon recedes.
BF-1 already operating above nameplate capacity (11,000 tpd vs 10,000 tpd capacity).

subsections.label: Cost control team and levers
points: Three operational specialists (Rajiv Kumar, Biju Nair, Debojyoti Roy) tasked with cost control; controllable levers include electricity, oil, coal, coke, oxygen consumption, wastage reduction, and yield improvement.
Uncontrollable input costs include crude oil, coal prices, and iron ore prices (set predominantly by NMDC and OMC).

subsections.label: Slurry pipeline capacity math
points: 18-million-ton slurry pipeline capacity math: one existing 6 million ton pellet plant plus a new 6 million ton pellet plant = 12 million tons pellet capacity, consuming ~12.2-12.3 million tons of iron ore fines via pipeline; plus a new 5 million ton sinter plant, totaling ~17-18 million tons of iron ore fines consumption.
Pipeline designed at 60% Fe / 35-40% water; if water content reduced to 30-32%, capacity could rise to 20 million tons depending on iron ore specific gravity/density.

Company will transport about 1.5 million tons of slurry per month (~18 million tons/year), but full capacity not needed in current year as pipeline is designed for both current and future rounds of expansion.

subsections.label: Refractory/shutdown management
points: Q1 shutdown was driven by BOF vessel reaching heat-life limit (9,000-10,000 heats) requiring refractory change to avoid vessel puncture/safety risk; newer BOF-2 and BOF-3 pots will not require shutdown for longer given later commissioning dates.

subsections.label: Inventory management
points: Inventory maintained at less than 10-11 days of total production, described as lean and best-in-industry.

subsections.label: Slurry pipeline status
points: End-to-end pipeline laid; pump house and receiving station complete; communication systems in place; equipment/pump trials underway.
Pigging trial (passing a metal pig through the pipeline) to be conducted with German equipment collaborators, followed by water trial then slurry trial.
Expected commissioning in first half of August 2026; could slip to end of August due to monsoon rains (an uncontrollable factor).
This is described as the longest pipeline with the largest capacity in the country.

subsections.label: Backward integration and captive sourcing
points: Iron ore backward integration rising sharply from ~16% in prior quarter to ~28% in Q1FY27, targeted to reach ~40% by FY27 exit, providing strategic cost benefit.
Captive coal mix currently ~50%, expected to increase further as Utkal B1 ramps up and Utkal B2 mine comes online.
Jindal port has started its first loading operations; two vessels already unloaded and one vessel currently loading, expected to contribute unquantified cost savings.

subsections.label: Coking coal sourcing flexibility
points: Indian steel mills, including peers, have been importing more coke (not just coal) from Indonesia and other countries over the last 3-4 months.
Blast furnaces are flexible in using different coal blends; company aims to blend coal to avoid being outpriced in the market.

subsections.label: Earn and Invest (E&I) capital discipline mantra
points: Management reaffirmed strict 'Earn and Invest' (E&I) philosophy: expansion funded from earnings, not incremental borrowing.
Company will not add commodity capacity; expansion will be focused only on value-added/value-engineered products.

Spend management approach: annual capex budget of INR 7,000-8,000 crores (potentially up to INR 10,000 crores), tied to earnings rather than a fixed tonnage target; capex will be curtailed if earnings are tight.
Company stated it is 'not in a race' to announce large capacity additions (30/40/50 million tons) every quarter, prioritizing disciplined spend over scale.

subsections.label: Jharkhand (Patratu) MoU
points: MoU signed with Government of Jharkhand; company has been present in Jharkhand since 2006, having taken over the Patratu plant from Birla Group, scrapped old rolling mills, and commissioned two new state-of-the-art rolling mills in 2010 (wire rod mill and rebar/rounds mill).

Proposal is to add a blast furnace (2.5-2.7 million tons) behind the existing mills using the 300+ acres of available land, water, and electricity infrastructure at Patratu, effectively a 'half project' since finishing facilities already exist.

Condition of the MoU is government support/allocation of iron ore from the Jeraldaburu block (previously blocked by the Environment Ministry from 2010-2014); no investment has been committed until this iron ore access requirement is met.
Once iron ore access is secured, company will do a thorough calculation, discuss with the board, and determine funding while adhering to the Earn & Invest mantra without burdening the balance sheet.

subsections.label: Leadership transition and organizational stability
points: New senior leadership introduced: MD V.R. Sharma (returning after 2019-2022 tenure), COO Rajiv Kumar (ex-Tata Steel, ex-Vedanta Aluminium CEO), CFO Sandeep Modi (ex-Hindustan Zinc CFO, 20+ years with Vedanta Group), plus recently hired CHRO Sukhjit S Pasricha (ex-IndiGo, ex-Airtel).
Board has brought in at least eight new faces overall; six are new senior hires (CFO, CHRO, VP HR, COO, plant heads) and two are returning/existing (Sharma and Roopali Mehra).

Additional senior hires include Debojyoti Roy (Raigarh plant head, ex-Tata Steel, ~30 years experience) and Biju Nair (Angul plant head, ex-ArcelorMittal, 30+ years experience), plus personnel brought in from group companies in Oman and Czech Republic.

Management noted stability at the upper-middle management level (1,800-2,000 people from manager to VP level), describing this cohort as the stable driving force of the organization despite senior-level changes.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro risks
points: Ukraine-Russia war (ongoing four years) and Israel-Iran conflict (ongoing one year) have shattered global economy, raised fuel prices, and contributed to a stable-with-slight-downward-trend steel consumption environment.
Resolution of these conflicts is seen as a potential positive catalyst for steel demand recovery and export opportunities.

subsections.label: China oversupply risk
points: China's capacity reduction (50-60 million tons) has not kept pace with its demand decline (100 million tons), creating international market surplus; China's capacity swap reform policy could help but has not yet resolved the imbalance.

subsections.label: Cost inflation risks
points: Coking coal cost increased $23/ton in Q1 (within guided range) with further $12-15/ton increase expected in Q2.
Middle East conflict contributed $12-13/ton cost impact in Q1 and remains an ongoing risk to watch.
Iron ore, coal, coke, and oil input costs are largely uncontrollable, being set by external market dynamics (NMDC/OMC for iron ore) and geopolitical factors.

subsections.label: Operational/monsoon risk
points: Heavy rains disrupted water management and caused electrical grid/system failures, slowing blast furnace ramp-up during the monsoon season.
Slurry pipeline commissioning timeline could slip from first half of August to end of August due to continued rains.

subsections.label: Leadership continuity risk
points: Analyst flagged concern about frequent changes in senior management potentially affecting strategic continuity; management acknowledged this is an area of concern but pointed to stability at the upper-middle management level as mitigant.

subsections.label: Q2FY27 outlook
points: Management expects to make 'a perfect balance' between price and cost movements, with input costs typically catching up/down within a 4-6 week lag, except during the monsoon exception period (mid-July to end-August).
Cost reductions and better operations (post-shutdown) expected to largely offset realization losses from the price correction, keeping margins from deteriorating significantly.
Q2 cost structure expected to improve given economies of scale, higher production, absence of plant shutdown, and reduced operating leverage drag versus Q1.

subsections.label: Full-year outlook
points: FY27 sales volume guidance of 10.5-11 million tons maintained; company will aim to increase run rate to compensate for Q1 shutdown-related volume loss.
Company reiterated it will not chase tonnage growth but rather spend-based growth (INR 7,000-10,000 crores/year) targeted at value-added capacity only.
Value-added product share expected to increase further as newly commissioned downstream facilities ramp up, enhancing profitability and resilience across commodity cycles.

themes.label: Leadership transition
themes.note: New MD, COO and CFO brought in along with several other senior hires; analysts flagged concern over frequent leadership changes, management cited stability at upper-middle management level as mitigant.

key_takeaways: Consolidated revenue sequentially was around 8% down, largely due to the sales volume resulting from the plant maintenance shutdown, partly offset by around INR 7,500 per ton improvement in average ASP supported by stronger steel prices and a richer product mix.
The share of value-added product has increased from 61% in Q4FY26 to 66% in Q1FY27.

Despite a 15% sequential decline in sales volume, EBITDA remains resilient; Consolidated adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 2,667 crores; Consolidated adjusted EBITDA per ton increased by INR 1,843 per ton, taking it to INR 11,937 per ton.

Finance cost charged to the P&L increased to INR 548 crores, primarily due to capitalization of major expansion assets (1,050 MW Captive Power Plant, BOF-III, CRM, and other associated facilities) during Q4FY26, now recognized through the P&L for the first full quarter.
Consolidated profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR 844 crores.
Net debt stood at INR 15,927 crores, translating into a net debt to EBITDA ratio of 1.71x; company remains confident of achieving the ratio below stated threshold of 1.5x during Q2FY27.

Against FY27 capex plan of approximately INR 8,500 crores, the company invested roughly INR 2,000 crores during Q1; cumulative spending under the expansion program now stands at INR 37,457 crores out of announced capex of INR 47,043 crores.

Full-year sales volume guidance for FY27 maintained at 10.5 to 11 million tons; management intends to recover the ~300,000 tonnes hot metal loss from the Q1 BOF vessel shutdown in subsequent quarters.

New leadership team introduced: Mr. V.R. Sharma (MD, returning), Mr. Rajiv Kumar (COO, ex-Tata Steel/Vedanta), Mr. Sandeep Modi (CFO, ex-Hindustan Zinc/Vedanta), alongside existing WTDs and plant heads.
pressing_questions: Given that the industry typically benefits from stable leadership and long-term management tenures, should investors be concerned about the impact of these transitions on strategic continuity and long-term value creation? How do you ensure that execution against long-term objectives remains unaffected?

What kind of cost savings can we expect from the management over the next couple of years with all the initiatives that may play out — coal mines commissioning, DRI plant, slurry pipeline, conveyor belt? What kind of interest cost savings can we expect from renewed relationship with financial institutions?
Our share of value-added products and flats has been going up very consistently — the only disconnect is how come our unit profitability (EBITDA per ton) is not showing that improvement?

quarters.summary: Jindal Steel expects continued ramp-up of new Angul capacities to drive volume growth in FY27, with FY27 production guided at 11-11.5 million tonnes and sales at 10.5-11 million tonnes. Indian steel demand is expected to remain reasonably strong on infra and construction, steel prices are expected to remain supportive near-term though coking coal costs may stay volatile (guided up $20-25/tonne QoQ in Q1FY27), and leverage metrics are expected to normalize by Q2FY27 with capex now shifting from expansion to asset-sweating (sustenance capex of INR 7,500-10,000 crores planned).

key_figures.label: Net debt increase FY22 to FY26
Total capex invested in current program (FY22-FY26)

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: In addition to expansion ramp-up volumes, HRC and TMT rebar prices recovered strongly during Q4FY26, although benefits were partially offset by an increase in coking coal prices.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA per tonne declined YoY (INR 10,482 in FY26 vs INR 11,712 in FY25).

subsections.label: Australian asset impairment
points: Until the previous quarter, the Australian assets were under care and maintenance; this quarter the shaft was closed and reserves are no longer accessible, although the license is still held.
Management does not expect any further write-offs on Australian assets; this is represented by an independent valuation done by a reputed agency.
The INR 1,433 crores India-level write-off is subject to income-tax benefit; the INR 834 crores figure is on the Australia balance sheet (consolidated) and is a gross number.

subsections.label: Capital allocation and leverage
points: With ramp-up of new capacities and corresponding improvement in operating cash flows, leverage metrics are expected to normalize by Q2FY27.
Company remains committed to a disciplined capital structure while funding sustenance and future growth initiatives.

From FY22 to FY26, net debt increased by INR 7,143 crores while INR 35,498 crores was invested in the capex program, reflecting strong internal accrual allocation through the capital allocation framework.
Capex program is more or less finished; focus now shifts to asset sweating and getting returns, with future capital allocation of INR 7,500-10,000 crores towards expansion/sustenance capex.

subsections.label: Contract vs spot mix and pricing lag
points: Order book has a mix of spot selling and contractual selling; typically in a rising or falling market there is a lag in the system, which is why ASP increased significantly last quarter.
Market is seeing a slight dip but is still holding firm; existing contracts on earlier (lower) prices will continue to support the company as it moves ahead this quarter.
Current ASPs are holding strong and are higher than what was delivered in Q4, with price increases seen sequentially every month; management does not see anything otherwise at the moment.

subsections.label: Product mix shift
points: Flat sales share (led by HRC) is increasing and is expected to move towards 70% over time from around current 50:50 level; downstream facilities will add more niche/value-added products supporting realization.

Value-added product share fell QoQ (management referenced levels around 61% from 66%) as focus during ramp-up is first on capacity utilization before optimizing value-added mix; expected to normalize and improve in H2 of the year.
Additional capacities in flats/plate segment, including heat-treated plates, are doing well and growing, which will add to the value-added mix.

subsections.label: Volume performance drivers
points: Performance reflects a strong ramp-up at Angul and improved capacity utilization across operations, including Raigarh.
Dispatches have improved in line with the stronger demand environment.
Company achieved a balanced sales mix across product categories with focus on optimizing realizations by moving product mix towards higher value-added products.

subsections.label: AI and digital transformation
points: Company making strong progress on AI and digital transformation journey, from upskilling workforce to deploying AI-powered digital agents and building smarter, increasingly autonomous plants.
JARVIS (Jindal AI for real-time visibility, intelligence and systems) platform unifies production, sales, and business data into one thinking layer.
Investments in robotics and end-to-end digital integrated systems aimed at ensuring business processes are safe, connected and future-ready.

subsections.label: ESG roadmap
points: ESG journey runs in four clear phases: through FY30 building site-level control systems and credible reporting foundations; by 2030 targeting 30% CO2 intensity reduction, 50% renewable energy and full biodiversity coverage across all sites; 2030-2040 decade to scale hydrogen circularity and CCS infrastructure; by 2047 goal is net zero emissions, zero waste and net positive biodiversity.
S&P Global raised the company's ESG score from 37/100 to 74/100, and CSA score improved from 30 to 72 during the year.

subsections.label: Product development/approvals
points: HSM has performed well in terms of getting customer approvals, and the company has developed all grades needed for niche products; ramping these up in this quarter and going forward.

subsections.label: Angul expansion progress
points: Significant progress made on Angul expansion during FY26 including BF2 (4.6 mtpa, operational), DRI2 (2 mtpa, under construction), BOF2 and BOF3 (3 mtpa each), and a cold rolling complex of 1.2 mtpa enhancing product portfolio and supporting margin improvement via higher value-added products.
Commissioned the 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi Power Plant (two 525 MW modules).
Coal pipe conveyor belt between the thermal coal mine in Utkal C and Angul is operational.
Slurry pipeline from Barbil to Angul is close to completion and expected to be commissioned in Q1FY27; this is described as a challenging project.

subsections.label: Capex/project pipeline and timelines
points: Capex program is more or less finished; remaining key projects are DRI2 and PP2, with DRI2 expected towards the end of FY27.
Slurry pipeline will be commissioned this quarter (Q1FY27); ports already indicated to be commissioned.

Full utilization of slurry pipeline savings will not happen this year as utilization will increase further as other facilities (namely PP2) come online in future; savings are based on material input per tonne, not dependent on utilization level.

subsections.label: Rail rakes and power ramp-up
points: Rail rakes program of 79 rakes: 72 already acquired, remaining expected to be delivered in the next 2-3 months.

Thermal captive power plant ramp-up expected to complete within H1 of this year; excess power intended to be sold in merchant market but described as not material to overall financials, providing power stability and redundancy for facilities.
With ramp-up in steel capacities, no further excess sale of byproducts is expected going forward.

subsections.label: Metallics/backward integration
points: Currently have 15 million tonnes iron-making and 15.6 million tonnes crude steelmaking capacity while DRI plant is yet to be commissioned; FY27 production/sales guidance factors in current metallics availability.
As DRI comes online (under construction), more metallics will be available and volumes will continue to ramp up in subsequent years.
