India crude steel production growth QoQ
Safeguard duty on flat steel imports

subsections.label: Global steel industry outlook
points: Global steel industry entering a phase of measured recovery; China's demand contraction gradually decelerating while India and other developing Asia remain growth drivers.
Developed economies including EU, US and Japan expected to return to positive growth in 2027.
Middle East conflict has tempered near-term regional demand, though broader global outlook remains largely resilient.

China production remains resilient despite weak demand, signalling persistent oversupply; growing gap between production and demand contraction; record exports in CY25 compensating for demand weakness primarily in real estate construction.

subsections.label: India steel market outlook
points: India continues to assert itself as the world's fastest-growing major steel market.

Outlook underpinned by broad-based strength across all key steel-consuming sectors: infrastructure-led construction activity, automotive sector, broader industry capex cycle, and nationwide rail network expansion plan.
India has become a net exporter of steel in FY26.

No delays observed in capex execution across public and private companies despite inflationary trends in commodities; demand is expected to remain fairly healthy given the infrastructure program being rolled out.

subsections.label: Market/customer strategic focus for incremental volume
points: Company continues to focus on strategic markets where it has strong presence, closer to its facilities, and markets that tend to be larger in size, rather than necessarily entering brand-new markets for incremental volumes.
Wide product portfolio and rich value-added mix allow cross-selling to existing customers, positioning the company as a 'one-stop shop' for large portions of customer portfolios.

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing mix
points: Iron ore pricing was more or less stable during the quarter; captive vs outside buying mix is roughly 60% outside / 40% captive.

key_figures.label: Iron ore mix - captive vs outside sourcing (mine level)

subsections.label: Raw material integrated strategy
points: Company continued to progress its integrated raw material strategy during the year.
Declared preferred bidder for Thakurani-A1 iron ore block in Odisha.
For thermal coal, awarded the Saradhapur Jalatap East coal block at the end of last year.

Coal pipe conveyor belt between the thermal coal mine in Utkal C and Angul is operational, and the slurry pipeline from Barbil to Angul (a challenging project) is close to completion, expected to be commissioned in Q1FY27.

subsections.label: Overseas mining assets
points: Australian (WCL) mine has been closed (shaft closed, reserves no longer accessible, though license retained); minimal cash outflow expected going forward since a lot of people were retained.
Mozambique mine is operating at EBITDA-positive level, supplying mined coal for captive use.
South Africa mine is operating but not EBITDA positive currently due to local issues.
Excluding Australia (where the large write-down was taken), rest of the overseas mines are functioning on a net EBITDA-positive basis.

subsections.label: Cost trends
points: Coking coal cost increased by about $20/tonne during the quarter and is guided to increase a further $20-25/tonne sequentially in Q1FY27.
Iron ore price movements are difficult to predict on an index basis but are currently moving plus/minus INR100-150.
One-time start-up costs mostly covered in Q3FY26; residual INR 125 crores incurred in Q4FY26, which will not recur going forward.

key_figures.label: Incremental volumes planned this year vs last year

subsections.label: End-market focus for flat steel
points: Company maintains it is an infrastructure-led organization while ramping up facilities; focus is largely on infrastructure sector, followed by building and construction, then downstream facilities, and then automobile sector.
Rising flat steel exposure is being directed with a focus on infra, B&C, downstream and auto end-markets in that order of priority.

subsections.label: Customer approvals
points: Existing HSM approvals and developed grades are considered sufficient for now, and are not expected to hold back execution plans; company is well positioned to execute going forward.

subsections.label: Capex strategy shift
points: Management confirmed that the capex program is more or less finished and the company's focus now shifts to asset sweating and generating returns from existing assets rather than further large capacity expansion in the near term.

subsections.label: Environmental clearances
points: Company is looking to increase Environmental Clearance (EC) capacities for some mines; this process is underway and working fairly well, though a specific date is difficult to pin down; current capacities are considered fairly comfortable in the meantime.

subsections.label: Raw material cost volatility
points: Coking coal prices may remain volatile even as steel prices show recovery and remain supportive in the near term.
Coking coal prices guided to increase $20-25/tonne sequentially in Q1FY27.
Iron ore prices are difficult to predict without an index and move on a monthly basis (currently plus/minus INR100-150).

subsections.label: Global oversupply/China
points: China's crude steel production remains resilient despite weak demand, with domestic demand contracting 7% YoY in CY25, creating a growing gap that signals persistent oversupply.
China's record steel exports of 119 million tonnes in CY25 represent surplus steel entering global markets to compensate for continuing demand weakness, primarily in real estate construction.

subsections.label: Middle East conflict
points: The Middle East conflict has tempered near-term regional demand, though the broader global outlook remains largely resilient.

subsections.label: Australian asset closure
points: Australian mine shaft has been closed and reserves are no longer accessible, resulting in an impairment; while no further write-offs are expected (per independent valuation), this reflects a resolved overseas asset risk.

subsections.label: South Africa local issues
points: South Africa mining operation is running but not EBITDA positive currently due to unspecified local issues.

key_figures.label: Q1FY27 coking coal price increase guidance

subsections.label: Volume and demand outlook
points: Continued ramp-up of new capacities at Angul expected to drive volume growth.
Steel demand in India expected to remain reasonably strong, supported by infrastructure development and construction activity.
Steel prices have shown recovery in recent months and are expected to remain supportive in the near term, although raw material cost, particularly coking coal, may remain volatile.

subsections.label: Specific guidance declined/limited
points: Management declined to give explicit revenue growth guidance for FY27, noting revenue is a function of several factors beyond production/sales volumes.

Management declined to give explicit EBITDA margin guidance for FY27, citing raw material and pricing factors outside its control, but pointed to historically robust and consistent EBITDA performance as an indicator.

subsections.label: Value-added mix and capex outlook
points: Value-added product mix expected to see some movement in the first two quarters of FY27 before stabilizing in H2 as focus shifts from capacity utilization to mix optimization.
Capex program viewed as largely complete; going forward, INR 7,500-10,000 crores will be allocated to capital expansion/sustenance capex programs.
DRI2 and PP2 remain the two key projects left for this financial year, with DRI2 expected towards the end of the year.

themes.label: Capacity expansion ramp-up
themes.note: Angul expansion took total steelmaking capacity from 9.6 to 15.6 mtpa; ramp-up continuing with BOF2/BOF3, cold rolling complex and power plant commissioned.

themes.label: Capex shift to asset sweating
themes.note: Capex program largely complete; focus now shifts to sweating assets with INR 7,500-10,000 crores allocated to ongoing sustenance capex rather than new expansion.

themes.label: Value-added product mix
themes.note: Value-added mix fell QoQ during ramp-up as focus was first on capacity utilization; expected to stabilize and improve in H2FY27.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation (coking coal)
themes.note: Coking coal prices rose ~$20/tonne in Q4FY26 and guided up a further $20-25/tonne sequentially in Q1FY27, partially offsetting steel price gains.

themes.label: Pricing recovery/realization
themes.note: HRC and TMT rebar prices recovered strongly in Q4FY26, with blended ASP up INR 4,743/tonne QoQ; market holding firm despite a slight recent dip.

themes.label: Australian asset impairment
themes.note: Australian mine shaft closed and reserves inaccessible, leading to impairments of INR 1,433 crores (standalone) and INR 834 crores (consolidated); no further write-offs expected.

themes.label: India steel demand tailwind
themes.note: India projected as fastest-growing major steel market with demand growth of 7.4% in 2026 and 9.2% in 2027, driven by infrastructure, auto, capex cycle and rail expansion.

key_takeaways: FY26 has been a defining year for Jindal Steel, marked by significant progress across expansion projects, which have taken steelmaking capacity from 9.6 million tonnes per annum to 15.6 million tonnes per annum.
Consolidated gross revenue for FY26 was INR 62,412 crores, an increase of 8% compared to FY25; PAT was INR 3,361 crores, a growth of 18% over last year.

For Q4FY26, consolidated gross revenue was INR 19,399 crores, a growth of 28% QoQ, driven by expansion ramp-up volumes and strong recovery in HRC and TMT rebar prices, partially offset by higher coking coal prices.

An impairment of INR 1,433 crores (standalone, USD 159 million) and INR 834 crores (consolidated, USD 93 million) was recognized on the Australian assets after the shaft was closed and reserves became inaccessible; no further write-offs are expected.
As of 31 March 2026, consolidated net debt was INR 16,019 crores with net debt to EBITDA of 1.66x and debt to equity of 0.43x; leverage metrics are expected to normalize by Q2FY27.

FY27 production guidance is 11 million to 11.5 million tonnes and sales guidance is 10.5 million to 11 million tonnes; capex program is largely complete with focus shifting to asset sweating, with INR 7,500-10,000 crores planned for ongoing sustenance/expansion capex.
Q1FY27 coking coal prices are expected to increase by $20 to $25 per tonne sequentially.

India continues to assert itself as the world's fastest-growing major steel market, with domestic demand projected to expand by 7.4% in 2026 and 9.2% in 2027; India became a net exporter of steel in FY26.
pressing_questions: Have contracts been reset on the higher realization, and what will be the impact on realization in Q1FY27, given the recent dip in steel prices?
What will be Jindal Steel's capex outlay for FY27 and FY28, and which key projects are left — will the focus now be more on asset sweating than further capacity expansion?

We had earlier indicated a shift to high throughput and lower-margin products in Q3, but even in Q4 the share of value-added products has fallen QoQ — what is the timeline to recalibrate towards higher value-added products, and what is the target value-added mix for FY27?
Any guidance on revenue growth for FY27, and what EBITDA margin can be expected for FY27?
What were the write-downs specifically in JPML and in Wollongong, and is it fair to say there will be no additional write-downs now?
What is the current position on the rail rakes program — how many have been acquired and how many remain?
On the thermal captive power plants — when is ramp-up expected, and what is the strategy on selling excess power versus captive consumption?
On raw material security (backward integration) — where does the company see itself in the next 2 years on thermal coal and iron ore?

JINDALSTEL.about: Jindal Steel & Power Ltd is one of the India's leading steel producers with significant presence in sectors like steel and mining. The group has global presence through subsidiaries, mainly in Australia, Botswana, Indonesia, Mauritius, Mozambique, Madagascar, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania and Zambia.[1]

quarters.summary: Management raised FY27 revenue growth aspiration from ~20% to 40%+ and EBITDA margin aspiration from >20% to sustaining the Q1FY27 level of >23.25%, supported by an all-time-high order book of ~₹26,665 crore (5x FY26 revenue), strong order inflows across Optical Connectivity, Defence & Aerospace and Digital Infrastructure, capacity expansions in fibre/cable/data-centre connectivity, and continued momentum expected for at least the next 5 years driven by AI/hyperscale data centre and telecom network demand.

subsections.label: Q1FY27 consolidated performance drivers
points: Delivered highest-ever quarterly revenue, profitability and order book.
Higher contribution from technology-led products, increasing exports, improved product mix, operating leverage and continued focus on innovation collectively driving stronger profitability.
Segment revenue from telecom products stood at 85% of total revenue in Q1FY27 vs 62% in Q1FY26 and 85% in Q4FY26.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / capex breakdown (FY27 & FY28)
points: FY27 total capex ₹640 crore includes: 3 towers for fibre capacity expansion (28mn to 34mn fkm), IBR lines (₹60 crore, already ordered/under delivery), data centre connectivity subsidiary (₹65 crore), defence sector (₹100 crore), and ₹100 crore of the newly announced ₹215 crore data centre connectivity investment.
FY28 total capex ₹615 crore includes ₹325 crore for preform, ₹175 crore for defence, and ₹115 crore (balance of ₹215 crore) for data centre connectivity solutions.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / debt
points: Debt-equity ratio at a comfortable 0.3x and expected to remain in this range despite high capex, supported by internal cash generation.

subsections.label: Segmental asset movement
points: Apparent ₹1,000 crore rise in telecom segment assets (Q4FY26 to Q1FY27) was clarified as a net increase of only ₹400 crore once the ₹600 crore rise in telecom segment liabilities is netted; the movement reflects a mix of fixed assets, receivables and inventory build aligned with incremental revenue/capex.

subsections.label: Unbilled revenue
points: Unbilled revenue outstanding at end of Q4FY26 has now been billed, with the major amount of ₹300 crore billed in Q1FY27.

key_figures.label: Data centre connectivity orders in hand

subsections.label: Order book composition & tenor
points: Order book strengthened to ~₹26,665 crore - an all-time high and 5x FY26 revenue, providing healthy revenue visibility.

Orders comprise different tenors: fibre optic cable orders are 5-year contracts, BharatNet-type contracts are 3-year contracts, O&M contracts are 7-year contracts; optical fibre cable order (₹16,000 crore) varies from 3 months to 4 years.
Of the total ₹26,000 crore order book, roughly ₹22,000 crore would be executed within a 5-year period; more orders continue to be added as execution proceeds.
Order book strengthened by several strategically important orders across core businesses reinforcing HFCL's position as trusted technology partner in Optical Connectivity and Digital Infrastructure.
Defence order book ~₹300 crore excluding pending acquisition, rising to ~₹2,300 crore including it; defence export order book ~₹2,200 crore.
Data centre connectivity orders in hand ~₹850 crore-plus, including a recent connectivity solutions contract of ₹500 crore.

subsections.label: Demand pipeline / visibility
points: Based on orders received and regular customer interactions, demand pipeline and market growth visible for at least the next 5 years.
Demand driven by AI, hyperscale data centres, cloud computing, high-performance computing requiring massive high-speed data movement, plus telecom network expansion as an additional driver.
Governments globally investing heavily in secure communication networks, strategic infrastructure and offensive capabilities, adding demand from defence and public infrastructure sectors.
Company receiving a large number of inquiries; management stated they 'really do not know whom to say yes or whom to say no' given demand levels, and may need to further raise capacity.

subsections.label: Telecom products / Optical Connectivity
points: Telecom products contributed 85% of total revenue in Q1FY27, same as Q4FY26, up from 62% in Q1FY26.
Telecom product margins around 30% maintained for last 3 quarters considered sustainable given known raw material and long-term sales contract prices.
No high-margin one-time order executed in the quarter; margins reflect average contract pricing expected to continue through the year.

subsections.label: Data centre connectivity business
points: First year of dedicated data centre connectivity business; Q1FY27 revenue ~₹100 crore; full year expected ~₹800 crore (initial guidance was ₹700+ crore).
Capacity for interconnect products (including subsidiary HTL Limited) being expanded 5x; in the first year of production expected revenue >₹700 crore with visibility to multiply in subsequent years.

Board approved additional ₹215 crore investment for expansion of manufacturing base for advanced data centre connectivity products, including miniature multi-fibre and super high-density multi-fibre termination assemblies.
Data centre connectivity business is margin accretive though not at very high margins; EBITDA margin band 12-15%.
Order book for data centre connectivity already ~₹850 crore-plus, with more orders being received.
Delivery of data centre optical fibre cable has effectively commenced; connectivity (MMC) deliveries expected to start about a month later.

subsections.label: Defence & Aerospace
points: Defence portfolio spans surveillance radars (multiple variants), electronic fuzes, thermal imaging solutions, ammunitions, tactical cables, aerospace structures (via proposed acquisition), and several next-generation technologies under development.
Company remains on track to achieve ~₹500 crore defence sector revenue aspiration for FY27, based on execution pipeline, customer engagements and order visibility.
Long-term aspiration to build Defence & Aerospace business nearly comparable in scale to HFCL's current overall business.
By FY28-29, defence & aerospace expected to cross ₹3,000 crore (including pending acquisition); target of ₹5,000 crore the year after.

Defence export order book currently ~₹2,200 crore; shortlisted for major BMP-2 modernization contract; Army trials started 20th (of the relevant month), expected completion in ~1.5 months, followed by winter trials.
Indigenously designed radars/sensors integrated into a C2 (command and control) system; demonstration planned to Army Northern Command in September.
Engagement with Home Ministry's Border Protection System initiative (securing borders with Pakistan and Bangladesh) via Proof of Concept with BSF.

subsections.label: Other telecom products
points: Beyond cable and fibre, other telecom product revenue (unlicensed band radio, routers, Wi-Fi systems) expected at ₹500-600 crore for the full year, contributing ~10% or less of total revenue.
This category is margin accretive but not very high margin, with EBITDA margin of about 12-15%.

subsections.label: Revenue mix outlook
points: Export revenue expected to remain around 60% and domestic around 40% on an overall basis for FY27, since defence revenue is mostly domestic while telecom/data centre export contribution remains high.

key_figures.label: MMC and SNMT facility assembly target

subsections.label: Technology leadership / hollow-core & multi-core fibre
points: Only 2 of 20 Indian fibre optic cable suppliers can manufacture very high fibre-count cables (e.g., 7,000 fibre count) demanded by data centre operators; HFCL is one of them.

Technology evolving toward multi-core and hollow-core fibre; HFCL developing hollow-core fibre in collaboration with IIT Delhi and a government organization in Kolkata that has a tower for manufacturing hollow-core fibre.

Corning has done more work on hollow-core fibre than others, but by the time hollow-core becomes commercially viable (currently thousands of dollars per kilometre), HFCL expects to be ready with its own hollow-core fibre.
7,000-fibre cables already developed and being sold (approval under process for US market, sales started in some other markets); 14,000-fibre cable under development, expected in another 2-3 months.

Passive connectivity solutions developed in-house: plastic boxes, cassettes, jointing boxes, positioning HFCL as a one-stop shop for all data centre connectivity solutions (cable, cable routes, connectors, trays, cassettes).
Company received a large ($1 billion-plus scale) contract for cable/connectivity solutions, reflecting technology leadership at the forefront.

subsections.label: New demand vector: fibre optic drones
points: Emerging defence demand for fibre optic drones (using A2-type fibre) as countries move away from radio-controlled drones vulnerable to jamming; current global demand estimated at 70-100 million fibre kilometres, expected to grow as more countries adopt fibre optic drone technology.

points: Optical Fibre manufacturing capacity expansion from 28 mn fkm to 34 mn fkm progressing well, to be completed by December 2026.

Optical Fibre Cable manufacturing capacity expansion from 34 mn fkm to 43 mn fkm (management also referenced reaching 45 mn) progressing as planned, along with data centre connectivity infrastructure expansions, expected to be commissioned within targeted timelines.

Capacity has been continuously increased every month over the last 2-3 years; company constantly reviewing further increases based on order inflows, demand and customer inquiries - additional capacity hikes not ruled out.
IBR fibre capacity currently >14 million fkm across 12 machines, being expanded every month.
MMC and SNMT facility assembly target of 2.7 lakh assemblies per annum.

subsections.label: Preform backward integration
points: Board approved greenfield preform manufacturing facility of 300 MT per annum with capital outlay of ₹580 crore as high-level backward integration to strengthen supply chain alongside incremental fibre capacity.
Location decision pending among 2-3 sites under consideration; decision expected within the month (as of call date).

Make-versus-buy: manufacturing preform in-house is at least ~30% cheaper than buying, which given preform's 65-70% share of fibre cost translates to an 18-20% reduction in fibre costs, and roughly 10-12% overall raw material cost saving at the cable level (preform ~45% of total cable cost).

subsections.label: Data centre connectivity capacity expansion
points: Company expanding manufacturing capacity for data centre interconnect products (including subsidiary HTL Limited) by 5x, progressively over about a year.

Newly approved ₹215 crore investment for advanced data centre connectivity products including miniature multi-fibre and super high-density multi-fibre termination assemblies, driven by global enquiries.

subsections.label: US vs global market dynamics
points: Most current data centre expansion taking place in North America; US capacity of ~150 GW expected to double to ~300 GW in 3 years, vs India's 1.5 GW expected to double to 3 GW, and Europe/Southeast Asia/Middle East showing lower growth currently but expected to pick up.
US administration reportedly advises against buying Chinese fibre; combined with a 35% duty on Chinese imports (up from 10%), competitiveness of Chinese fibre in the US market is reduced.

China expected to dominate Southeast Asia; HFCL has historically competed with China in telecom and will continue to do so in the Middle East/Europe data centre markets given its world-class capacity and economies of scale.

Fibre realization pricing is highly variable depending on fibre type (A1 for telcos vs A2 for data centres), fibre count and contract length/duration; recent months have seen significant price increases; spot prices (4-6 month delivery) command 5-20% premium over 5-year contract pricing depending on buyer.
International fibre pricing generally ranges $18-$28 per fibre km, with data centre fibre specifically priced at $22-$28 per fibre km.

subsections.label: Raw material / pricing pass-through mechanism
points: Most long-term contracts (raw material purchase and sales) have an annual variation/reset clause; large in-between variations can also trigger renegotiation, though this has not yet occurred as most contracts are less than a year old.
Precedent: when the US imposed a 50% duty at one point, customers absorbed a large part of that duty; the duty has since been refunded and HFCL has paid customers back accordingly.

If raw material prices rise significantly, sales prices are renegotiated upward with customers; if they fall significantly, customers seek price reductions - small (~5%) moves do not trigger renegotiation.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning vs global peers
points: Global optical fibre cable market projected to reach ~$21 billion by 2033 driven by hyperscale data centre and AI bandwidth demand; international players (Prysmian, Corning, and Italian/Japanese peers) expanding capacity, e.g., Prysmian spending ~$1.5 billion to double capacity.

Management maintains HFCL is a world-class player with growing capacity (8 mn fkm fibre historically to ~34 mn fkm now; cable to ~45 mn fkm) and continues to review further capacity increases in response to strong inquiry levels.

Only a handful of suppliers globally (2 of 20 in India) can manufacture very high fibre-count cables required by hyperscalers, limiting the risk of oversupply despite capacity additions by global peers.
Long-term 5-year supply relationships/contracts already signed with hyperscalers create switching-cost advantage; even if demand temporarily eases, customers unlikely to change suppliers.
Demand for data centre fibre expected to continue outstripping capacity additions for at least the next 5 years.

subsections.label: Hyperscaler contracts
points: Company has separate orders (not combined) from different hyperscalers for optical fibre cable and for data centre connectivity solutions, including a hyperscaler order valued at ~$1.1 billion; more orders under negotiation with multiple hyperscalers, expected within a month or less.
Delivery under cable orders has effectively started; connectivity solution deliveries (miniature multi-fibre) expected to start about a month later.

subsections.label: Aerospace/defence order book economics
points: Order book of Defsys/aerospace acquisitions transferred to HASPL stands at ₹1,900 crore; the acquired aerospace business carried an order book of ₹2,000+ crore at time of acquisition, with expectations of a few thousand crore more in additional orders.
Export revenue mix was 50% this quarter; expected export/local revenue mix range for FY27 outlook is 65-35%.

subsections.label: Group restructuring
points: Board's Restructuring Committee is evaluating strategic alternatives to simplify the Group structure, enhance operational efficiency and unlock long-term shareholder value; Ernst & Young appointed as strategic advisor.

Management declined to comment on specific outcomes but committed to three guiding principles: creating long-term shareholder value, strengthening operational effectiveness, and preserving financial discipline.

Not the entire defence business has been transferred; ammunition business and Electronic Fuzes remain within HFCL; restructuring under active consideration with E&Y's advice to optimize revenue/profitability across each business sector.

subsections.label: Aerospace/defence acquisition
points: Proposed acquisition of an aerostructure business will expand HFCL's participation in the global aerospace value chain, expected to generate meaningful order inflows.
Acquisition process is in an advanced stage and expected to complete within the current calendar year, with consolidation expected from Q4 (of the relevant fiscal reference).

Acquired aerospace business already carries an order book of more than ₹2,000 crore, with expectations of a few thousand crore more in orders; management characterizes this as an addition of business (via dilution to fund the acquisition), not a pure dilution of the existing business.
HASPL (subsidiary of HFCL, in which HFCL holds 51% stake) structure used for the defence/aerospace consolidation; it is a transfer into a subsidiary, not a transfer/sale of business out of the group.

subsections.label: Ammunition Manufacturing Complex
points: Groundbreaking ceremony for the upcoming Ammunition Manufacturing Complex in Andhra Pradesh held on 15th May 2026, attended by the Union Defence Minister and Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister.
Complex to manufacture advanced ammunition systems including electronic fuzes, Multi-Mode Hand Grenades and other specialised products for Indian Armed Forces and global customers.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / external risk to margins
points: Management flagged that the only risk to margin sustainability is an uncontrollable geopolitical event (e.g., Suez Canal closure causing delivery delays) or similar external disruption; absent such events, margins are expected to hold.

Preform price increases are a potential headwind but management expects to offset them via better customer pricing realization and higher-margin value-added products (e.g., data centre connectivity solutions), with net margin impact seen as immaterial (a couple of percentage points at most, fully offset).

subsections.label: EPC/Army network drag
points: EPC business has been a drag due to the Army warranty period during which HFCL supported the Army network without compensation; this is expected to be resolved once the AMC contract is signed (expected mid-Q2), after which EPC revenue should increase and losses should significantly reduce, though management stopped short of guaranteeing full breakeven/profitability this year.

subsections.label: Revised FY27 targets
points: Previously outlined aspiration of ~20% revenue growth for FY27 raised to 40%+ based on Q1 progress, healthy order inflows, favourable industry dynamics, expanding global opportunities and improving execution capabilities; confidence not based on any single order but on multiple growth platforms gaining simultaneous momentum.

Previously indicated EBITDA margin aspiration of >20% for FY27; company already achieved 23.25% in Q1 itself and expects this level to be sustained (minimum) for subsequent quarters absent uncontrollable geopolitical disruption; no seasonality in margins expected.

Quarterly revenue run-rate of ~₹1,900 crore expected to be broadly maintained (not decline sequentially), with 5-10% variance possible; profitability also expected to be maintained or better, not inferior to Q1 levels.
Q2 monsoon impact considered non-material since most revenue comes from fibre optic cable exports (largely to US, which has no monsoon).
Previously communicated profitability improvement guidance was 2-3% (from an initial ~20% profitability increase target base of 16-17% margin in FY26).

subsections.label: EPC/Army AMC timeline
points: Army AMC contract expected to be signed around mid-Q2 FY27 (in final stage as of call date); once signed, EPC losses expected to reduce significantly (though some loss may remain) and roughly ₹170 crore of annual AMC revenue expected.

subsections.label: Longer-term Defence & Aerospace scale-up
points: Aspiration to build a Defence & Aerospace business that over coming years becomes nearly comparable in scale to HFCL's current overall business, with a target to cross ₹3,000 crore by FY28-29 and ₹5,000 crore three years out.
Order book highlighted in closing remarks stood at ~₹26,000 crore.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical disruption (e.g., Suez Canal closure or similar uncontrollable event) causing delivery delays and margin impact
risk_register.note: Management flagged this as the only scenario that could impact margins/growth guidance, outside its control.

risk_register.risk: Preform price increases when long-term contracts reset
risk_register.note: Some preform contracts extend beyond this fiscal year; price increases expected to be largely offset by better customer pricing and higher-margin value-added products (connectivity solutions), with net margin impact seen as immaterial.

EPC losses stemmed from supporting Army network without compensation during warranty period; expected to reduce significantly once AMC contract is signed (targeted mid-Q2 FY27), though some loss may persist.

risk_register.risk: Chinese fibre supply competition / potential oversupply from global capacity additions (Prysmian, Corning etc.)
risk_register.note: Management downplayed the risk citing US administrative preference against Chinese fibre, 35% import duty on Chinese fibre, and limited number of suppliers capable of very high fibre-count cables; expects demand to continue to outstrip capacity for at least 5 years.

risk_register.risk: Raw material cost inflation pass-through timing
risk_register.note: Long-term contracts have annual reset/variation clauses; small (~5%) input cost moves do not trigger repricing, but significant moves are renegotiated with customers (as with the prior 50% US duty episode, later refunded).

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical disruptions (broad, out of company control)
risk_register.note: Management says HFCL has remained largely insulated so far; supply chain operating seamlessly without material impact on production/dispatches, but flagged as the main uncontrollable risk factor for the next 3-5 years.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation - helium, polymer, preform prices
risk_register.note: Helium and polymer prices increased sharply in the last ~1 month; preform prices may rise once long-term contracts expire; contracts signed before recent hikes could see 1-2% margin compression.

risk_register.risk: Capacity constraints limiting large new order intake
risk_register.note: Company at 100% utilization; hesitant to accept large new orders until capacity expansion completes; some pipeline orders being turned away.
Warranty-period costs on Army network construction dragging EPC profitability, expected to be resolved once AMC contract is signed, likely Q2 FY27.

risk_register.risk: War-related drone demand diverting fibre supply/pricing (Russia-Ukraine)
risk_register.note: Additional 50-100 million km demand from military/drone applications noted; HFCL and its preform suppliers deliberately avoid supplying into this segment.

Electronic fuzes require upgrades post-Balasore trials before resubmission; BMP upgrade sample to be submitted for Army evaluation by 26th June, HFCL one of 5 shortlisted parties with uncertain outcome.

Receivables >₹2,000 crore and unbilled revenue increased from ~₹300 crore to ~₹600 crore YoY, partly due to invoicing/compliance timing issues at year-end; expected to convert to formal revenue in April-May.

key_takeaways: HFCL delivered highest ever Quarterly Revenue, Profitability and Order book in Q1 FY27.
Raised FY27 revenue growth aspiration from ~20% to 40% and above.
Achieved EBITDA margin of more than 23.25% in the very first quarter itself, against a prior aspiration of over 20% for FY27.
Order book strengthened to approximately ₹26,665 crore, an all-time high and 5 times FY26 revenue.

Optical Fibre manufacturing capacity expansion from 28 million to 34 million fibre kilometres progressing well, to be completed by December 2026; Optical Fibre Cable capacity expansion from 34 million to 43 million fibre kilometres also progressing as planned.
Board approved greenfield preform manufacturing facility of 300 MT per annum with capital outlay of Rs.580 crores for backward integration.

Data centre interconnectivity manufacturing capacity (including subsidiary HTL Limited) being expanded 5 times; expects revenue of more than Rs.700 crores in the first year of production, with visibility to increase multiple folds in subsequent years.

Board approved an additional investment of Rs.215 crores for expansion of manufacturing base for advanced data centre connectivity products, including miniature multi fibre and super high density multi fibre termination assemblies.
Defence & Aerospace revenue aspiration for FY27 remains ~₹500 crore, on track; long-term aspiration for this business to become nearly comparable in scale to HFCL's current overall business.
Groundbreaking ceremony of the Ammunition Manufacturing Complex in Andhra Pradesh held on 15th May 2026, graced by the Defence Minister and Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister.

Board's Restructuring Committee, advised by Ernst & Young, is actively evaluating strategic alternatives to simplify the Group structure, enhance operational efficiency and unlock long-term shareholder value.
pressing_questions: Why is management being conservative with 40% growth guidance when annualizing telecom product sequential revenue implies a much larger number (~INR9,300 crores)?

What is the current global pricing trend for higher fibre-count/specialized cables versus standard 288/432 fibre count cables, and how much of the 40% growth guidance is driven by realization versus volume?
How will the company sustain current margin levels once preform costs reset to newer market prices starting next calendar year, given older long-term contracts were priced lower?

What is the breakup of the order book between defence and optical fibre cable, and how much of the INR26,000 crore order book is attributable to the pending aerospace acquisition versus organic defence orders?
Is the recent INR1,000 crore increase in telecom segmental assets related to capex coming online, or is it a working capital/receivables movement?

Regarding the group restructuring, has HFCL diluted its stake in the defence business by transferring it into a subsidiary (HASPL) at 51% ownership, and how does this affect minority shareholders in HFCL Limited?

What is the total addressable market and expected market share for the new MMC and SNMT facility (2.7 lakh assemblies per annum), and what is the timeline for executing the full INR26,000 crore order book?

quarters.summary: HFCL delivered record Q4 and FY26 performance with 20% revenue growth and margin expansion, backed by an all-time high order book of Rs.21,200 crore (58% export). Management expects 20-25% revenue growth and 3-4% EBITDA margin expansion in FY27, driven by data center interconnect solutions (~Rs.400 crore FY27, ~Rs.800 crore FY28), defense scale-up (aerospace acquisition + ammunition facility), preform backward integration, and improving OFC realizations, while turnkey/EPC losses (Army NFS contract) are expected to normalize as AMC contracts convert.

points: HFCL remained largely insulated from current geopolitical disruptions; supply chain has continued to operate seamlessly without material impact on production or dispatches.
Germanium tetrachloride (raw material for preform, not directly for fibre) not flagged as an issue by preform suppliers; supply received as per commitment.
Preform not typically sold in open market in large quantity as producers largely consume in-house; company relies on long-term contracted prices (~6 months contract cycle, commercially confidential).

subsections.label: Pricing pass-through and cost inflation
points: Helium and polymer prices have risen sharply recently (~last 1 month); total cost of helium+polymer in final cable product ~20%.
Prices of cable have also risen in tandem with input cost increases; company expects to pass through preform price increases in full via cable pricing.
Contracts signed before recent price hikes may see margin compression of 1-2%, offset by newer/spot contracts with higher margins; long 5-year contracts allow prices to normalize over time.

OFC realization difficult to average due to wide variety of cable constructions (fibre count from 1 to 7,000+ per cable, different densities/technologies) — company declined to give a single blended number multiple times.

subsections.label: Demand-supply dynamics
points: Global optical fibre market undergoing structural transformation driven by hyperscale data centres, AI workloads, and cloud infrastructure expansion, adding incremental demand over and above traditional telecom requirements.
Demand concentrated in high fibre count, low-latency, high-performance solutions where supply remains constrained, driving realization improvement.

Military/drone-related demand (Russia-Ukraine linked) adds ~50-100 million km demand but company does not supply into this segment at all (not even a meter), including at the request of its preform suppliers.

Management's personal opinion is that fibre/cable prices have reached near their final level, with limited further upside; industry reports of prices reaching $30 (from $23-24) for high-fibre/high-frequency cables in Apr-Jun quarter noted by an analyst.

subsections.label: Customer mix and spot vs long-term strategy
points: Company deliberately retains spare capacity to capture more profitable spot market deals rather than pre-selling 100% of capacity, while also serving small-batch regular long-standing customers (10-15 year relationships).
Company has executed a couple of favorable spot deals recently.
IBR/AIDC-linked cable constitutes more than 50% of optical fibre cable segment revenue and is expected to remain the majority contributor going forward, depending on customer mix.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning in ammunition
points: Only 3 licensees currently exist for hand grenade-type ammunition products: 2 private companies (including HFCL) and 1 government company (Munition India Limited).

subsections.label: Defence & aerospace consolidation (HFCL Advance Systems)
points: Board approved (meeting held March 25, 2026) major strategic initiative to expand and strengthen defence business and enable participation in defence aerospace segment.
Core objective: create a focused, scalable, future-ready defence and aerospace platform by consolidating complementary defence capabilities under subsidiary HFCL Advance Systems Private Limited.
Aerospace business being acquired operates in high-entry-barrier segment with stringent qualification requirements, high precision, long approval cycles, limited global supplier ecosystem.

Acquired business comes with established capability base, certifications, long-standing customer relationships, and confirmed export-oriented order book of ~₹1,930 crore providing immediate revenue visibility.
Rationale: greenfield entry into aerostructure would have taken 5-7 years to get approvals; acquisition provides existing approvals, certifications and order book from large international companies.
Definitive agreements expected to be executed on or before May 31, 2026; closing expected within the current calendar year.
Proposed structure expected to sharpen execution focus, improve capital efficiency, and drive sustainable growth from defence vertical.

subsections.label: Strategic Restructuring Committee
points: Committee constituted to evaluate merger/demerger decisions across businesses given that defence, EPC, and fibre/telecom each require significantly different capabilities and execution skill sets.
Rationale also includes inbound interest from strategic partners who cannot partner into a mixed conglomerate structure spanning defence, EPC, cable and telecom.
No decision yet on demerger of project/EPC business or defence business; committee to study and recommend; company will communicate once decisions are taken.
No plans for an equity partnership at this stage precisely because of the current mixed business structure — this is part of the reason the restructuring committee was formed.

subsections.label: ESG
points: HFCL received ESG ratings from multiple independent agencies during the period.
Company published its first Sustainability Report, reinforcing commitment to responsible and sustainable growth.

subsections.label: Geopolitical risk
points: Management flagged geopolitical disruptions as the main external risk factor, largely outside company control (e.g., Suez/Panama Canal closure or other extreme events), though HFCL has so far remained insulated with no material supply chain impact.
War-related drone/military demand for fibre (Russia-Ukraine) is being deliberately avoided by HFCL and its preform suppliers.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Helium and polymer prices have risen sharply in the last month; preform prices may also rise once current long-term contracts expire.
Contracts signed before recent price hikes could see margin compression of 1-2%, though this is expected to be offset by newer contracts and pass-through pricing.

subsections.label: Capacity constraints
points: Company is hesitant to accept very large new orders until capacity expansion is completed, due to being already at 100% utilization.
Some large potential orders in the pipeline are being turned away/considered cautiously due to capacity constraints.

subsections.label: EPC/Army NFS contract drag
points: Army network (NFS) construction warranty period causing ongoing costs without corresponding revenue, dragging EPC profitability; expected to resolve once AMC contract with Army is signed (expected Q2 FY27).

subsections.label: Defence product qualification risk
points: Electronic fuzes required upgrades post DRDO/Army trials at Balasore before resubmission for evaluation.
BMP upgrade requires submission for Army evaluation by 26th June 2026; company is only one of 5 shortlisted parties, outcome uncertain.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin outlook
points: Management explicitly declined to give formal guidance, framing statements as 'expectations' based on current order book, raw material prices, and known customer prices.

20-25% revenue growth expectation is on a year-to-year basis (not quarter-to-quarter), off FY26 base of ~₹5,000 crore, implying FY27 revenue of roughly ₹6,000-6,250 crore; management said this is a deliberately conservative estimate and there is a 'good possibility' of over-performance.
3-4% margin expansion driven by: better realization from products, and reduction/elimination of turnkey (EPC/NFS) losses as the Army NFS contract converts to AMC.
Margin improvement expected to start from Q1 FY27 itself, based on known customer sale prices and raw material costs, absent any catastrophic global event.
Telecom product margin improvement not committed at a fixed percentage every year — 3-4% increase specific to current year context; not sustainable as an annual repeatable rate.
Management does not currently provide an 'optimum margin' target (e.g., declined to confirm a 25% aspiration over 5 years).

subsections.label: Segment-specific outlook
points: Data centre interconnect revenue of ~₹400 crore in FY27 is a conservative minimum estimate — could be materially higher.
Defence revenue of ₹500-600 crore in FY27 expected to constitute 10-12% of total revenue, largely from aerospace and land systems.
IBR/AIDC-linked revenue expected to remain more than 50% of optical fibre cable segment revenue mix going forward.
EPC business expected to turn profitable starting FY27 as AMC contract with Army is signed (~₹170 crore/year) and BharatNet execution ramps.

guidance_ledger.statement: Over and above FY26 revenue, we should definitely be able to scale up by 20% to 25% at least, based on current run rate.
3% to 4% increase in margin on a blended, overall basis is quite expected.
Our aspiration is to reach to INR10,000 crores in revenue over the next 3-5 years.
Data centre interconnect solutions expected to contribute about Rs.400 crore additional revenue in FY26-27.
Data centre interconnect solutions expected to contribute about Rs.800 crore in FY27-28.
Defence revenue expected at INR500-600 crore for FY27, contributing about 10%-12% of total revenue.
Defence margin could be a couple of percentage points higher than current/expected blended rate, something like 20-25%.
Blended margin profile of data centre interconnect business is about 20%, possibly higher than others.
Investor presentation indicates expecting ~25% improvement in realisation for FY27, due to product mix and high-density cable and recent price rises.
Total capex for FY27 expected to be roughly about INR600 crore, including fiber, OFC, defense, and part of preform business.
Capex for FY28 expected to be INR350 crore.
Preform facility currently 300 tons; possibility to scale up to 500 tons in stage 2 after 300 tons is successful (not immediate).
Preform backward integration facility will take at least 2 years to come on stream.
Make-versus-buy analysis shows backward integration reduces preform cost roughly 15% to 20%.
Optical Fibre capacity of 28 mn fkm expected to increase to 33.9 mn fkm by December 2026.
Optical Fibre Cable capacity currently 34 mn fkm expected to reach 39 mn fkm by July 2026.
Optical Fibre Cable capacity expected to reach 42.36 mn fkm by December 2026.
EPC business expected to become profitable this current financial year, as AMC contract with Army is signed (expected Q2) and BharatNet EPC contracts execute profitably.
Once AMC with Army starts, about INR170 crores or so AMC being received every year.
Definitive agreements for the aerospace/defence acquisition transaction expected to be executed on or before May 31, 2026, with closing expected within the current calendar year.
Budgeted about INR125 crore for AP ammunition facility (land & building) this year, and another INR250 crore over next 2 years.

guidance_ledger.metric: IBR/AIDC share of OFC segment revenue
guidance_ledger.statement: IBR/AIDC-linked revenue expected to continue to constitute more than 50% of overall optical fibre cable revenue mix.
31.75% consolidated telecom product margin in Q4FY26 expected to generally hold good for the current quarter also, depending on product mix.
Management declined to commit to a 25% margin aspiration over 5 years; said 3-4% increase is specific to current year and cannot be repeated every year.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical disruptions (broad, out of company control)
risk_register.note: Management says HFCL has remained largely insulated so far; supply chain operating seamlessly without material impact on production/dispatches, but flagged as the main uncontrollable risk factor for the next 3-5 years.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation - helium, polymer, preform prices
risk_register.note: Helium and polymer prices increased sharply in the last ~1 month; preform prices may rise once long-term contracts expire; contracts signed before recent hikes could see 1-2% margin compression.

risk_register.risk: Capacity constraints limiting large new order intake
risk_register.note: Company at 100% utilization; hesitant to accept large new orders until capacity expansion completes; some pipeline orders being turned away.

risk_register.risk: War-related drone demand diverting fibre supply/pricing (Russia-Ukraine)
risk_register.note: Additional 50-100 million km demand from military/drone applications noted; HFCL and its preform suppliers deliberately avoid supplying into this segment.

Electronic fuzes require upgrades post-Balasore trials before resubmission; BMP upgrade sample to be submitted for Army evaluation by 26th June, HFCL one of 5 shortlisted parties with uncertain outcome.

Receivables >₹2,000 crore and unbilled revenue increased from ~₹300 crore to ~₹600 crore YoY, partly due to invoicing/compliance timing issues at year-end; expected to convert to formal revenue in April-May.

themes.label: Data center / AI-led fibre demand
themes.note: Hyperscaler-driven demand adding 100-150 million fibre km incrementally; $1.1bn contract secured; DCI solutions to add ₹400cr (FY27) and ₹800cr (FY28) revenue.

themes.label: Realization / pricing power in high-fibre-count cable
themes.note: Realizations improved significantly on constrained supply of high fibre count/low-latency cables; ~25% realization improvement expected in FY27; management believes prices near peak.

themes.label: Defence & aerospace expansion
themes.note: Aerospace acquisition under HFCL Advance Systems adds ~₹1,930cr export order book; ammunition facility in Andhra Pradesh to commence construction; multiple products (fuzes, BMP upgrade, hand grenade) progressing through qualification.

themes.label: Backward integration into preform
themes.note: ₹580cr preform facility (300 tons, scalable to 500 tons) to reduce cost 15-20% and secure raw material availability; commissioning in at least 2 years.

themes.label: EPC/turnkey business drag and recovery
themes.note: Army NFS warranty-period losses dragging EPC margins; expected to reverse via AMC conversion (~₹170cr/year) and profitable BharatNet execution from FY27.

themes.label: Business restructuring / portfolio rationalization
themes.note: Strategic Restructuring Committee formed to evaluate merger/demerger given divergent capability needs across defence, EPC, and fibre/telecom; no decision yet.

themes.label: Input cost inflation pass-through
themes.note: Helium, polymer and preform prices rising; company expects to pass through increases fully via cable pricing, though pre-hike contracts may see 1-2% margin compression.

key_takeaways: This quarter and financial year mark a defining milestone for HFCL, as we delivered a never-before quarterly as well as annual performance, reflecting the strength of our strategy, improved business mix, and consistent execution across our core segments.
We have successfully achieved the commitment of 20% revenue growth along with expansion in margins, underscoring the structural transformation we have undertaken over the past few years.

Backed by a robust all time high order book of Rs.21,200 crore, favourable industry tailwinds, and our continued focus on high-value products and global markets, we remain confident of sustaining this growth momentum and delivering a similar trajectory in the coming periods.

We have taken strategic step towards further strengthening our manufacturing resilience with backward integration by establishment of Preform manufacturing facility, involving an estimated capital outlay of around ₹580 crore.

During the period, we secured a landmark long-term global optical fiber cable supply contract valued at approximately USD 1.1 billion, equivalent to Rs. 10159 crore providing strong multi-year revenue visibility. This is probably the highest ever single contract secured by any Indian telecom company.

The Board of Directors, at its meeting held on March 25, 2026, approved a major strategic initiative to expand and further strengthen our defence business, while also enabling HFCL to meaningfully participate in opportunities emerging in the defence aerospace segment, consolidating complementary defence capabilities under HFCL Advance Systems Private Limited.

Our export revenues increased from 4.54% in FY21 to 41.36% in FY26, reflecting a meaningful expansion of our global footprint; the share of product revenues in our mix rose from 27% in FY21 to 62% in FY26.

For the twelve months ended 31st March 2026, the Company reported consolidated revenue of ₹4949.27 Crores as against ₹4064.52 Crores in FY 2025, EBIDTA of ₹826.75 Crores as against ₹506.75 Crores in FY 2025, Profit before Tax of ₹427.68 Crores as against ₹216.59 Crores in FY 2025 and Profit after tax of ₹329.44 Crores as against ₹173.26 Crores in FY 2025.

HFCL.about: HFCL Ltd (Himachal Futuristic Communications Limited) is a diverse telecom infrastructure enabler with active interest spanning telecom infrastructure development, system integration, and manufacture and supply of high end telecom equipment, Optical Fiber and Optic Fiber Cable (OFC).[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was a weak quarter for KPIT with revenue decline both YoY and QoQ, driven by SDV program cancellations/completions in Europe and Japan and broader European OEM stress from Chinese competition, tariffs and geopolitical/input-cost pressures. Management guided that H2 FY27 will be better than H1, with a return to meaningful growth by Q4 FY27, and profitability recovery will largely track revenue recovery, aided incrementally by cost optimization, fixed-price/solutions mix and AI-led delivery efficiency. Deal wins remained strong (USD 257mn TCV) across connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous, and broad-basing strategy (new OEMs, off-highway/trucks, products & solutions, China, deep tech, micro-mobility) continues, though timing of revenue realization from wins remains uncertain.

subsections.label: PAT impact factors
points: PAT was impacted on two additional accounts: forex loss, and share of loss from Qorix.
The Qorix loss was, in some way, an impact of the postponement of certain revenues, specifically in the Europe region.
Qorix-related loss is expected to continue for at least the next quarter or two.

subsections.label: Other expenses increase
points: Other expenses were up significantly in the quarter; part of the impact was due to foreign exchange rate movement in consolidated accounts.
There were provisions related to acquisitions done by the company, and subcontracting costs incurred in the European region for clients.
Management characterized these as operational and 'nothing out of the way', i.e., no unusual one-timers beyond these factors.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory outlook
points: Margins will improve going forward, but only incrementally until revenue returns to growth; revenue will be the major driver of margin recovery.
Cost optimization can only happen incrementally, not significantly, until revenue growth resumes.
European cost-out actions take much longer than in other geographies, which will extend the time as well as cost required for margin recovery.
Margin uplift is expected to be tracked quarter-on-quarter rather than year-on-year; management does not have a precise number yet but expects it to be roughly flattish before improving.

subsections.label: Wage hikes
points: This is the first time the company has delayed wage increments (following several years across the industry where increments were soft but not stopped).
Increments will be given in stages — younger grades will receive increments soon, while senior employees' increments will be spread over the period.

subsections.label: Strategic clients revenue clarification
points: CFO clarified that 87% and 84% are percentages of the respective quarter's revenue (current vs prior quarter), not directly comparable in absolute terms; the reported 1.3% QoQ decline pertains specifically to strategic clients.

Management attributed the bulk of degrowth to the top 2 clients (viewed as strategic clients), with the associated impact not yet fully factored into the base — further impact expected in the next quarter.
Part of the prior quarter's higher revenue base included one-time license revenues that are not repeated this quarter.

subsections.label: Deal win drivers
points: USD 257 million worth of wins during the quarter, across the world, mainly driven through connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous.

subsections.label: Pipeline conversion timing
points: Pipeline remains strong across engaged OEMs; company is not worried about winning its share of business, only about the timing of realization.
Management has discounted near-term revenue contribution from this pipeline for a few quarters given uncertainty on timing.
In certain accounts, pipeline-to-revenue conversion is occurring; the drop has been concentrated in two specific accounts, but overall revenue drop was cushioned by wins in other markets.
European wins, once started, would likely be executed with more work done out of India than Europe.
Two distinct uncertainties flagged: (1) timing of revenue from Europe pipeline and recent wins, and (2) how much time it will take to cut costs in Europe.

Vendor consolidation exercises are occurring at the OEM level; KPIT believes it is faring well in these, though it expects client engagement models to evolve toward best-of-solution selection (not just traditional vendor consolidation) with a focus on solutions, products and AI.

subsections.label: Commercial Vehicle (CV) segment
points: CV segment revenue fell more than the passenger vehicle (PV) segment in the quarter because a one-time large license deal recognized last quarter was not repeated this quarter, creating an outsized YoY/QoQ impact on a smaller CV revenue base.
Management expects CV segment growth to resume next quarter (Q2 FY27), with broad-based growth continuing into subsequent quarters.
Both the Japan program (cancelled) and the Europe program (winding down as planned) are expected to fully play out in Q2 FY27, with both accounts expected to stabilize by Q3 FY27.

subsections.label: Passenger Vehicle (PV) segment
points: PV segment revenue declined modestly (USD 3.5 million QoQ) despite expectations of growth, due to a last-minute setback (Japan program cancellation) toward the end of the previous quarter.
Company was 'getting ready for growth' in PV, but that anticipated growth did not materialize this quarter.

subsections.label: SDV programs ramp-down
points: One program in Europe is winding down naturally as planned, heading to start of production.
One program in Japan was cancelled at the last minute (the vehicle program itself, not just the KPIT engagement, was cancelled).
Both programs are viewed as reaching a natural end; a pipeline still exists from these clients, but timing of further revenue is uncertain.

subsections.label: Geography-level segment view (SIMA)
points: SIMA (Southeast Asia, India, Middle East, Africa) region revenue appeared to have dropped this quarter due to its smaller revenue base, but the company is seeing significant growth in SIMA.
Growth in SIMA together with growth in the U.S. is expected to offset the Europe-specific impact at a company level, even though the impact will show up at a regional level.

subsections.label: Europe
points: Europe revenues did not fall off as much as expected optically this quarter, but this was because certain expected revenues did not come through; the resulting impact will be seen more clearly next quarter (Q2 FY27) at a regional level.
European OEMs face three structural forces: declining share in China, Chinese OEMs gaining share in Europe's home turf, and reduced competitiveness in the U.S. due to tariffs.
European OEMs are under tremendous pressure and are rethinking their strategies given these are viewed as structural, not transient, changes.
Conversation with European OEMs has shifted toward how KPIT can help reduce product cost by 30-40% and reduce cost of production, in order to restore competitiveness against Chinese entrants.

More than 50% of KPIT's current business comes from Europe; the company has been working over the last six quarters to build broader-based growth across Europe, Americas, SIMA and JKC (Japan/Korea/China).

subsections.label: United States
points: U.S. geography has done well this quarter, with growth fairly well balanced across the entire portfolio, including good growth on the commercial vehicle side and long-established relationships on the passenger car side.
Management has fairly good visibility for the momentum to continue into upcoming quarters.
Growth in the U.S., along with SIMA, is expected to help offset the Europe-specific revenue impact expected in Q2 FY27 at the company level.

subsections.label: China
points: Company will be 'very patient' with China but continues to grow and invest there.
KPIT has engaged with two Chinese OEMs, with at least one nearing a meaningful engagement.
Reasonable traction found for products and solutions in China.

Chinese OEM volumes have declined as an industry, but many aim to grow meaningfully outside China profitably, positioning KPIT as a partner given its China presence plus strong client relationships and ecosystem outside China.
Many global OEMs are forming partnerships in China, which KPIT believes it can leverage going forward.

subsections.label: Japan/Korea
points: New engagements with previously-unaddressed but stable and successful OEMs in Japan, Korea and Europe are underway, with acceleration opportunities being explored.
One OEM each engaged newly in Korea, Europe, U.S. and Japan as part of broad-basing existing passenger car OEM relationships.

subsections.label: Fixed-price/contract model shift
points: Fixed price contracting model is increasing (600-700 bps versus last year per an analyst's observation), enabling multiple levers: greater AI usage, higher-margin solutions embedded within fixed-price delivery, and product-based revenue (e.g., Beacon as subscription/platform or as a delivery tool).
Company continues to hold a premium versus competition on signed contracts and can move toward better margins over time even in competitive geographies.

subsections.label: OEM cost reduction conversations
points: Conversations with European OEMs have shifted to how KPIT can help reduce the cost of the OEM's product by 30-40% (e.g., taking a vehicle costing 100 down to 60-70) and reduce cost of production (e.g., taking a cost of 50 down to 30-35).

These types of conversations are also expected to extend to competitors' clients in Japan, Korea and eventually the U.S., as Chinese OEMs have created vehicles at attractive price points with strong features.

Beyond cost, speed-to-market is also a key focus — European OEMs are seen as taking too long to bring new models, hurting feature competitiveness by the time vehicles reach the road; KPIT is focusing on reducing time-to-market for OEMs.

subsections.label: Broad-basing strategy
points: Strategy to broad-base revenues across: (a) existing OEMs via wallet share expansion and larger program responsibility, (b) new passenger car OEMs in Japan, Korea and Europe not previously engaged with, (c) off-highway and trucks segment, (d) products and solutions, (e) new adjacencies like micro-mobility and Deep Tech.
Company has opened engagement with seven different OEMs in the off-highway segment and started working with four different OEMs in the trucks and bus business.
Leveraging the Caresoft acquisition for cost reduction programs for OEMs, an area viewed as absolutely essential for OEMs currently.
Aftersales Transformation (branded I-Dart) is another growth area.

subsections.label: Products & Solutions integration
points: Multiple products/solutions being integrated across the software development cycle and vehicle development life cycle, powered by the Beacon automotive intelligence platform.
Partnership with Microsoft for global go-to-market in the automotive area, forming a base for the products/solutions strategy.

Technica becomes infrastructure in the validation space powered by Beacon; I-Dart becomes Aftersales Transformation powered by Beacon; autonomous product development leverages a World Foundation Model built by KPIT.
Products and solutions area is expected to be margin accretive over time and is seeing good traction.
N-Dream in-vehicle gaming platform launched with Tata Motors — the first such platform launched in any vehicle in India; business model is a per-vehicle license fee.
Cymotive (cybersecurity) and Technica are among the product/solution entities being integrated into the overall offering.

subsections.label: Deep Tech / adjacencies
points: Continuing work on hydrogen technology, though meaningful revenues will take time; government is currently pushing hydrogen amid multiple controversies around alternatives, and the company will be careful about factoring this into growth.

Exploring adjacent mobility areas such as drones, humanoids, and production-floor applications — early-stage efforts not yet factored into growth, but viewed as having big opportunity; overall plan still being put together.
Data center opportunity being pursued, with clients like Cummins engaged meaningfully; company aims to extend these offerings to more clients in that sector.

Sodium-ion battery technology: NRE revenue was booked some time back; battery technology requires ~2-3 years to reach pilot production, an investment of more than $100 million, and after production, certain milestones must be met before royalty entitlement — so revenue impact is not immediate.
Micro-mobility: already seeing good traction with wins in the last-mile connectivity area.

subsections.label: Tata Motors business model
points: KPIT contract with Tata Motors coexists with Tata's own in-house ER&D and other external partners, similar to other OEMs; this is not a new or unusual model.
KPIT's business with JLR (also a Tata company) is significant, and KPIT has worked with Tata Motors for many years across passenger and commercial vehicle sides.

subsections.label: Macro/industry headwinds
points: Automotive industry has faced global challenges for some time, especially extreme competition from China.
Geopolitical situations (tariffs and others) across different regions have accentuated the pressure.
A war had a significant, largely unexpected impact on supply chain and input costs for many companies.

European players have been most impacted — facing China market impact, Chinese competition entering their home European market, and a restricted U.S. market due to tariffs/uncertainty, plus input cost pressure from the war.
Japanese players were also impacted, though less significantly than European players.
Industry-wide fallout includes job cuts, profit warnings, pay cuts, ongoing restructuring, and significant write-offs among OEMs.

subsections.label: Program cancellations/timing risk
points: SDV program cancellation in Japan (at the last minute) and planned wind-down of a European SDV program directly impacted revenue.
Timing uncertainty remains around when pipeline/deal wins will convert to revenue, particularly in Europe and Japan.

subsections.label: H2 recovery outlook
points: H2 FY27 will be better than H1 FY27, with a return to growth by Q4 FY27.
Profitability will return largely when revenues come back, though other margin levers will be used before that.
Growth turnaround by Q4 is being referenced on a quarter-on-quarter basis rather than year-on-year; management does not have full clarity yet but expects it to be roughly flattish before improving.
Medium-term and next-year-onward growth strategy is expected to deliver meaningful growth from currently impacted accounts by end of this year and into next year.

subsections.label: Margin aspiration (FY29)
points: 22-24% EBITDA margin aspiration by FY29 (stated at Analyst Day) still holds per management, supported by expected exponential growth in products and solutions revenue, some outcome-based business models, and reasonable success already seen in some solution areas.

guidance_ledger.metric: Revenue growth (H2 vs H1, return to growth)
guidance_ledger.statement: H2 will be better than H1, and we will return to growth in H2 by Q4, driven by the Q4 performance.
Our profitability will return largely when the revenues come; there are other levers we will use before that.
During the Analyst Day, aspiration of achieving 22% to 24% by FY29 — that aspiration still holds; medium-term outlook remains good.
Margins will improve going forward, but it will improve incrementally, not significantly until our revenues go back to growing ways; revenue will be the major driver.
The Qorix loss will continue for at least next quarter or two.
On the commercial vehicle, we will be on for growth next quarter... you will see a growth next quarter.
You will see the Europe impact in the next quarter... but this will be made up by growth in U.S. as well as in SIMA at a company level.

guidance_ledger.metric: SDV program stabilization (Japan and Europe accounts)
guidance_ledger.statement: The complete thing will happen in Q2; we believe that both accounts will start to stabilize in Q3.
During the quarter update in June, 2Q revenues will be flattish and 4Q will be significant growth — management confirmed this still holds.
4Q will be significant growth; when we say normal levels of margins by 4Q, largely depends on growth.

Battery technology takes about two to three years to really put the pilot production plant... after getting into production, there are certain milestones after which we may get entitled to royalty; not immediate from a revenue perspective.
We continue to work on hydrogen tech, but meaningful revenues will take some time; we will be careful in terms of factoring into our growth.

guidance_ledger.metric: Deep Tech / adjacent opportunities (drones, humanoid, data centers)
guidance_ledger.statement: We are not factoring any significant growth right now, but we believe these are good opportunities which we should be in a position to capture and we are in the process of putting together the overall plan.

guidance_ledger.metric: European OEM cost reduction impact / conversion to KPIT revenue
guidance_ledger.statement: Once we get over this hump over the next couple of quarters, some of these cost reduction initiatives will yield revenues to KPIT.
We will do it in stages. We will give it to some of the younger grades soon. The senior people will get over the period.
We expect 30% year-on-year revenue growth in solution and products, and we hope it will increase over the period.
India, we will be almost doubling, it's a small base, but doubling the revenue.
Continuation of [the two largest SDV] program would have resulted in 4 to 5 sequential growth for the year.
The goal for this year is whether we can push that up to more than 15 to 20%.
We'll be converting four of our largest clients in that model in this quarter, and we'll take the next four in the next quarter. And that will pretty much take us north of 75% overall.
We have opportunity for annualized sustainable double-digit growth... we believe that the opportunity is big, and if little bit of a help from environment, we can significantly grow in years to come.
The revenue part, which is in FY26, which is 85% of our [services], this 15% is solution and product, which will move to 60% in 3 years.

guidance_ledger.metric: Solutions & products share of revenue (medium term target)
guidance_ledger.statement: 50% revenue share to be achieved from solutions and product.
We are committed to being a net-zero organization by 2050... our internal goal, obviously, is to achieve it before 2040.
There is an important milestone that we will hit in 2030, which is reducing our own carbon footprint by more than 40%.

There will be a pre-buying that will happen in the second half of 2026 And we believe that the truck business will pick up a little bit. The European market as well as North America market is likely to pick up in the second half of 2026.

risk_register.risk: Extreme competition from China impacting global automotive OEMs
risk_register.note: Chinese OEMs gaining share in Europe and other home markets, exacerbated by geopolitical situations and tariffs.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical tariffs/uncertainty restricting U.S. market access for European OEMs
risk_register.note: Restricted U.S. market due to tariffs or related uncertainties is impacting European players specifically.

risk_register.risk: War-driven supply chain and input cost impact
risk_register.note: War had a significant, largely unexpected impact on supply chain and input costs for many companies globally.

risk_register.risk: European OEM profitability pressure and restructuring
risk_register.note: European players significantly impacted, leading to job cuts, profit warnings, pay cuts, ongoing restructuring, and significant write-offs.
Japan SDV program cancelled at the last minute; Europe SDV program winding down as planned — both directly hit revenue this quarter and prior guidance.

risk_register.risk: Timing uncertainty of pipeline conversion to revenue
risk_register.note: Company confident in winning share of business but uncertain about timing of revenue realization from wins, especially in Europe and Japan.

risk_register.risk: Qorix share of loss / associate performance
risk_register.note: Loss from Qorix linked to postponement of certain revenues in Europe; expected to continue for at least next quarter or two.
PAT impacted by forex loss; other expenses also affected by foreign exchange rate movement in consolidated accounts.
European cost to take out takes much longer time than other geographies, delaying margin recovery.

risk_register.risk: Concentration risk in top 2 strategic clients
risk_register.note: Bulk of degrowth attributed to top 2 (strategic) clients, with impact not yet fully factored into the base.
