themes.label: Vehicle Program Delays
themes.note: Japan SDV program cancelled at the last minute and Europe SDV program winding down as planned drove much of the quarter's revenue decline.

themes.label: China Strategy & Market Share Battle
themes.note: European OEMs losing share to Chinese competitors in China and at home; KPIT engaging two Chinese OEMs and finding traction for products/solutions in China.

themes.label: Diversification into Off-Highway/Trucks/Micromobility
themes.note: Seven new off-highway OEM engagements and four new trucks/bus OEMs opened; micro-mobility wins in last-mile connectivity; CV growth expected to resume next quarter.

themes.label: Solutions & Products Pivot
themes.note: Beacon-powered product/solution integration (Technica, I-Dart, N-Dream, Cymotive, World Foundation Model) with Microsoft GTM partnership seen as margin accretive growth driver.

themes.label: Wallet Share & Contract Model Shift
themes.note: Fixed price contracting share rising 600-700 bps YoY, enabling AI-led delivery efficiency and higher-margin solutions/products embedded in delivery.

themes.label: Margin Expansion Roadmap
themes.note: 22-24% EBITDA margin aspiration by FY29 reiterated, but near-term margin recovery will be only incremental until revenue growth returns, with European cost-out taking longer.

themes.label: AI-led Transformation
themes.note: AI usage in delivery, combined with fixed-price shift and solutions/products, seen as key lever for margin improvement over time.

pressing_questions: By when do we think commercial vehicles will really come back to growth? Could you give some color on why we saw the weakness during this quarter given reasonable deal wins and client additions in off-highway and commercial vehicles?
From a Europe perspective, despite the weakness, there is a reasonable number of deal wins and OEM model launches/updates by end of next year — do you believe this weakness can be temporary?
During the Analyst Day, you spoke about an aspiration of achieving 22% to 24% EBITDA margin by FY'29 — does that aspiration still hold, or would you worry about it at the moment?
Can you unpack U.S. growth between OEMs and off-highway, and do you expect this momentum to sustain for the next few quarters?
Europe revenues didn't fall off as much as expected — can we expect the impact in Q2? Can you quantify the revenue impact for the European geography?

There were two SDV programs that were going to be ramped down — are they in the base now, or do you expect the impact to continue? If in the base, should we expect Japan, Korea and China geography to bottom out?
Other expenses were up significantly this quarter — are there any one-timers, and how should we expect the margin trajectory for the next three quarters?

When we say Q4 will be stronger in terms of growth, how are you seeing European OEMs in that quarter onward — are they starting to use KPIT solutions to compete against Chinese competition, or will growth come from other geographies?
Is there a similar cost-reduction discussion happening around product development to compete with Chinese OEMs while maintaining product differentiation?

In terms of the segmental revenue, why has the CV segment fallen more than PV segment despite PV being expected to take the brunt of the SDV ramp-down — is the base not incorporating a large part of the SDV ramp-down?
Are you seeing any vendor consolidation exercise being played out at the OEM level, and how is KPIT faring in those exercises — winning share?
Are you thinking of wage hikes anytime soon, or would this be deferred to 2H depending on growth recovery?

Overall revenues in USD terms are down ~4.5% sequentially, while strategic clients (87% of revenue) are down only 1.3% — this suggests the bulk of decline is from nonstrategic clients, which doesn't reconcile given the situation — can you clarify?

quarters.summary: Q4 saw 1.8% CC / 1.9% QoQ USD growth (12% YoY / 5.8% QoQ in INR) with $349mn of new deal wins closed and pipeline satisfactory; management sees FY27 as a positive environment despite near-term headwinds from delayed vehicle programs, Honda platform cancellations and China market-share loss, with FY27 EBITDA guided at 20.5-21.2% and solutions & products revenue growth of 30% YoY, moving toward a medium-term target of 22-24% EBITDA margin and 50% of revenue from solutions & products within a few years.

key_figures.label: New deal wins (TCV) closed in quarter

subsections.label: Cash & Capital Allocation
points: Cash generation has been very good over many years, with dividend payout after dividend payout continuing
₹9.6 billion cash at quarter end with final dividend of ₹5.25 per share and dividend payout of about 33%

subsections.label: Investment Philosophy
points: Never compromised on technology investments as this is seen as core to KPIT's future
Most companies invest less than 1% of revenue in technology; KPIT has invested more than 3% for many years and has now upped this to more than 5%
Despite high investment, KPIT continues to post one of the best EBITDA numbers in the industry
$400 million strategic external investment in M&As is separate from and beyond the 5% technology investment figure

subsections.label: Efficiency Levers
points: Per-person revenue and per-person contribution has consistently risen over the last three years and is expected to continue rising, seen as a major future cost-leverage/efficiency lever

key_figures.label: Wallet share among T25 clients (prior year)
Overall market share across mobility spend
Fixed price share of new contracts
Large clients being converted to fixed price this quarter
Large clients being converted next quarter

subsections.label: Deal Wins & Pipeline
points: $349 million worth of new deal wins closed during the quarter, reflecting the number of engagements/deals signed
Pipeline continues to be satisfactory
21% of total pipeline already in products and solutions, seen as an encouraging sign

subsections.label: Key Strategic Engagements
points: Long-term partnership in excess of $50 million focused on large-scale software-defined transformation for next-generation machine platform (software-defined machines/SDM), shifting from legacy architecture to modular electronics/software architecture
Engagement with leading Japanese Tier 1 to deliver next-generation digital cockpit via KPIT's own platform, currently engaged for 3 OEMs, expanding to 5 OEMs
Two OEM programs moving toward SOP (start of production) shortly, leveraging years of production program experience in digital cockpit and AI-accelerated development

subsections.label: T25 Wallet Share Strategy
points: T25 strategy: 25 clients account for bulk of KPIT's growth over last 4 years, historically concentrated among 8 OEMs mostly in vehicle software
Wallet share among T25 clients grew 10% to 12% YoY; goal this year is to push it to 15-20%

Four levers to grow wallet share: cross-practice offerings, solutions/products for nonlinearity, working with alliances (chip makers like Qualcomm, tier 1s, cloud players), and increasing outcome-based contracting

subsections.label: Contract Model Shift
points: Substantial shift from time-and-material to fixed price contracts observed quarter-on-quarter over last couple of years
More than 80% of new contracts are fixed price

Converting existing time-and-material contracts to outcome-based is harder than winning new outcome-based programs; converting 4 largest clients this quarter, next 4 next quarter, targeting >75% overall outcome-based/fixed price

subsections.label: New Client Additions
points: Added 13 new clients this year across three segments (passenger car, truck, off-highway) — a big shift for a company historically diligent about not adding clients
4 truck OEMs added as initial engagements

6 off-highway OEMs added across 4 countries; one North America OEM awarded both current-generation and next-generation software-defined machine programs after a consulting assignment, creating a playbook for others
3 passenger car OEM breakthroughs — large, well-known OEMs previously not clients, covering almost all major passenger car OEMs outside China once fully onboarded

subsections.label: T25 to T40 Evolution
points: Composition of T25 changing to become more like T40, now balanced across passenger car, truck, and off-highway segments (previously concentrated in passenger cars), which have different industry cycles and should reduce revenue variability

key_figures.label: Current solutions & products share of revenue
Target solutions & products share of revenue

subsections.label: Growth Drivers by Segment
points: Growth driven by all four segments: connected vehicle, powertrain, vehicle engineering, and after-sales
Connected vehicles: one of the highest growth areas in the industry
Powertrain: growth continues but not highest; includes conventional, hybrid, and hydrogen-based pilot systems, broader than pure electrification

Vehicle engineering: boosted by Caresoft acquisition, addressing OEM cost-reduction pain points beyond software, bringing software benchmarking (performance, security) as a new differentiator versus industry's traditional hardware benchmarking
After-sales: fast-growing area as OEMs seek revenue throughout vehicle life, not just point-of-sale; KPIT has built strong solutions here, supported by investment in Helm (California) last year

subsections.label: Geographic/OEM Mix Nuances
points: 9% YoY growth with OEM clients per strategy
Drop in Tier 1 revenues, which was never a strategic focus
Strengthened China presence with two new engagements with Chinese OEMs; small revenue contribution but strategically important given China's market size and Chinese OEMs' expansion into other markets

subsections.label: Headwinds Impacting Segments
points: AI-led transformation caused near-term cannibalization in some areas, though seen as larger opportunity over time as KPIT moves toward full-solution ownership
Lower-than-expected growth in middleware and autonomous driving due to delayed new architecture programs (affecting players like Qorix)
Autonomous driving landscape shifting: OEMs previously wanted to build own stacks but largely failed; now focus is on integration and training on existing stacks
Program cancellations and delays in a few accounts challenged near-term growth but expanded foundation for future expansion

subsections.label: Solutions & Products Pivot
points: Solutions and products are the company's next strategic pivot, expected to grow 30%+ (up from initial 20-25% expectation)
Current 15% of FY26 revenue from solutions & products expected to move to 60% in 3 years, targeting 40% growth contribution
Medium-term target: 50% of revenue from solutions and products

subsections.label: Off-Highway/SDM Business Understanding
points: Learning off-highway business deeply (mining, agriculture, construction) rather than just porting passenger car technology, understanding business KPIs and altering software-defined machine templates accordingly

key_figures.label: Number of critical roles identified for leadership program

subsections.label: Software Integration Complexity (Anup Sable)
points: Automotive described as one of most complex machines with 100-120 computers and 5-6 network types requiring real-time handshaking for safety-critical functions like braking and steering

Cars are highly cost-constrained environments — illustrative example: a $300bn revenue OEM with 2.5-4% margins ($7.5bn net margin); saving $10/car across 10 million vehicles yields $100 million bottom-line impact, hence intense per-car cost negotiation
Integration problems arise because software components (each built by different teams/'drivers') must handshake in real time; this is the core 'traffic jam' problem KPIT solves
Complexity multiplies for OEMs with many vehicle models — same components must scale across 10-15+ models annually for large OEMs

subsections.label: AI Impact on Software Development
points: AI improves software productivity 10x to 100x, enabling generation of far more code (e.g., 10mn to 100mn lines), which multiplies (non-linearly) the downstream integration/testing/validation problem rather than solving it
AI is used both as a service-delivery accelerant (AI-infused solutions) and as a licensable product since client's own employees would also use it

subsections.label: Software V-Cycle & Coverage Areas
points: Vehicle development follows a nested 'V' cycle: requirements V, feature development V (software developers), integration & regression, lab validation (domain system HIL, then multi-domain), mule vehicles, start of production, and after-sales
KPIT's portfolio (platforms, Beacon AI-accelerated work packages, virtual validation, real validation) covers the V-cycle end-to-end, built over roughly the last 4 years

subsections.label: Beacon AI Platform
points: Beacon is KPIT's automotive mobility/mobility intelligence product for AI-first development and integration validation, used both as an AI-infused solution and a licensable product

Beacon addresses organizing 13,000+ engineers' AI usage at enterprise scale, addressing safety concerns (e.g., ISO 26262 functional safety), code confidentiality/traceability, using concepts of 'agents' (organizing an LLM model for a task) and 'harness' (extracting a specific outcome from agent-model combination at engineering scale)
Partnership with Microsoft announced at CES, among a few others, supporting Beacon

subsections.label: Technology Ecosystem / Chip-to-Cloud Stack
points: Proactive investment across the chip-to-cloud stack: chip layer via Pathpartner, E/E architecture via Technica, middleware via Qorix, application layer via Helm.ai, cloud via Dream and Summit solutions, horizontals via Caresoft (technical validation) and Cymotive (cybersecurity)
Validation is viewed as a large and continuous part of industry spend, and a key reason China can deliver programs in under two years versus four years elsewhere

Cymotive investment reflects belief in importance of cybersecurity across millions of vehicles; Volkswagen Group (via Cariad) is an investor in Cymotive, with its solution deployed across millions of VW Group vehicles

subsections.label: People & Leadership Development for Disruption
points: Identified ~60 critical/broadband roles to drive the organization amid continuous disruption (geopolitical, technical)

First batch of 40 people went through an exceptional, company-designed program with partners including McKinsey and INSEAD, involving visits to China (OEMs, government interactions, driving vehicles), California (NVIDIA, universities, AI startups), and France (INSEAD)
Building M.Tech/PhD combined programs with premier institutes for research, upskilling AI engineers and champions

key_figures.label: Chinese OEMs that have gone bankrupt
Off-highway OEM new clients spread across countries

subsections.label: India
points: India business has historically been very low despite being headquartered there; expected to change starting this financial year

Reasons: India OEMs becoming globally competitive; global OEMs taking India seriously and building 'India for India' products, partly due to China market share losses; Indian conglomerates seeking to enter passenger car business, some via buying platforms from China (KPIT involved in about 3 such conversations) and can help with production, software/system integration, and validation
India seen as potentially the #3 global market currently, with belief it could become #2 in next 10 years
Trucks and off-highway to become more relevant in India as economy and infrastructure grow
India growth will be driven by solutions and products rather than traditional services model used in Germany, North America, Japan

subsections.label: China
points: Presence in China for more than 15 years; revamped and refreshed strategy 2 years ago with four objectives
Objective 1: learn from China and bring learnings to global OEMs (Omkar and Anup spend significant time with China team)
Objective 2: help global OEMs with China presence salvage market share (e.g., GM, Volkswagen Group launching China-for-China vehicles)
Objective 3: help Chinese OEMs expand outside China amid brutal competition (30 million vehicle market, ~99 OEMs remaining after ~50 bankruptcies)
Two new engagements with Chinese OEMs added in the year; small revenue but strategically important
European OEMs (luxury) lost Chinese market share drastically in recent quarters but showing recovery, albeit with lower margins

subsections.label: Southeast Asia
points: Positioned as 'Horizon 3 for tomorrow' — building on India learnings for micromobility and other solutions
Few OEMs present (couple in Malaysia, one Chinese-owned; one in Vietnam); China also using Vietnam/Thailand as gateway to rest of world, increasing Chinese OEM presence there

subsections.label: Middle East and Africa
points: Identified as the next horizon ('day after tomorrow') beyond India/China/Southeast Asia; offerings for Africa will be built on the back of India offerings, differentiated from developed-market offerings

key_figures.label: R&D spend growth projection (McKinsey, automotive ex-China)
Number of India OEM conversations for China platform sourcing

subsections.label: Market Spend Trends (McKinsey data, Jan'26, automotive ex-China)
points: Data covers only automotive part outside China; excludes off-highway, commercial vehicles, and micromobility, but still gives good representation of automotive spend
Overall automotive R&D spend expected to roughly double by 2030

AD/ADAS spend to become 3x by 2030, the largest growth area, though not entirely addressable by KPIT because platform sourcing is concentrated among few large platform builders (requiring billions of dollars); validation/simulation remains the addressable portion for KPIT
Infotainment and digital services also a high-spend/high-growth area
E-architecture is a relatively small part of spend today but growing significantly, important for both passenger car and off-highway/commercial vehicle segments

Electrification is not the highest-spend area; multiple powertrain sheds (electrification, hybrid, hydrogen) are being invested in, and KPIT's highest growth area was infotainment, connected and security

subsections.label: T25 Client Strategy & Wallet Share
points: KPIT's marketing and account management functions (~150 people) focused on translating technology capabilities into purchasing organization value at large OEMs
T25 strategy: bulk of KPIT's phenomenal growth over the last 4 years came mostly from 8 OEMs, largely in vehicle software; now expanding focus to all T25 OEMs for wallet share depth and breadth
Cross-practice offerings, nonlinear solutions/products, and alliances with chip makers (e.g., Qualcomm), tier 1s, and cloud players identified as three key levers to grow wallet share

subsections.label: Adjacencies (Micromobility, Deep Tech)
points: Micromobility (two/three-wheelers, last-mile connectivity) revived after being parked for six years; starting from India with propulsion/vehicle engineering plus after-sales products and solutions; partnership signed with Hero Motors

Deep tech (robotics, aerospace, space tech) is being scanned as Horizon 3 — evaluating which KPIT core competencies are relevant and what would compel OEMs in these areas to work with KPIT; further clarity expected during this year and next

subsections.label: Passenger Car / Truck / Off-Highway Portfolio Mix
points: >75% of business currently from passenger car
Off-highway picking up quickly and management remains bullish

Trucking industry (mainly North America and Europe) has been in a slump for about 9 months due to seasonality and political uncertainty; pre-buying expected in H2 2026 in both Europe and North America, driving truck OEMs to open wallets for software-defined truck journeys

key_figures.label: Number of OEMs KPIT growth historically based on
People involved in creating company vision
Off-highway OEM clients in pipeline for future engagement
Number of objectives for China presence revamp

subsections.label: Full-Stack Chip-to-Cloud Investment Strategy
points: Strategic acquisitions (Pathpartner, Technica, Qorix, Helm.ai, Caresoft, Cymotive, Dream/Summit) build a complementary ecosystem across chip, E/E architecture, middleware, application, cloud, and horizontal (validation, cybersecurity) layers
Caresoft acquisition doubled down beyond software to address OEM cost reduction via software benchmarking (in addition to traditional hardware benchmarking)

Helm.ai investment (California, made last year) builds after-sales expertise to support integration/implementation work and off-highway/commercial solution building, without exclusivity to any single stack provider

Cymotive (cybersecurity) investment reflects strategic focus on protecting millions of vehicles; Volkswagen Group (via Cariad) is an investor, with Cymotive solution deployed across millions of VW Group vehicles
Ecosystem strategy explicitly modeled on how China's ecosystem approach drives faster innovation and full-stack solution delivery versus competitors

subsections.label: Partnerships
points: Partnership with Hero Motors signed to gain firsthand experience in micromobility (two/three-wheelers) ahead of scaling to other markets
Partnership with Microsoft announced at CES supporting Beacon AI platform, among a few other tech company tie-ups

subsections.label: Sustainability / ESG (EcoVoyage)
points: EcoVoyage sustainability program launched two years ago with specific ESG-related goals
Signed up to Science Based Targets initiative; committed to net-zero by 2050, with an internal aspiration to achieve it before 2040
Milestone: reduce own carbon footprint by more than 40% by 2030; company states tremendous progress already made
Social pillar anchored on three E's — Environment, Education, Energy — with employee engagement as the CSR tagline, including education initiatives from school-going children to PhD programs
Governance: commitments backed by stringent governance framework to track progress on ESG goals

subsections.label: Vision & Culture
points: Company vision 'reimagining mobility with you' for a cleaner, safer, and smarter world was developed over 9 months in early 2019 involving about 300 people
All 13,000+ employees globally work to help OEMs make vehicles cleaner, safer, or smarter, per management

subsections.label: Macro / Geopolitical Headwinds
points: Tariff and geopolitical conflicts
EV policy changes in US and Europe
Supply chain disruption
Rapid maturity of AI technology impacting OEMs, leading to multi-billion dollar write-offs
Reduced visibility versus earlier periods on where growth will come from next year

subsections.label: Client-Specific Program Disruption
points: Honda cancelled all its new platform programs (public news); impact occurred recently in April, took time for KPIT to assess full impact
This prompted KPIT to pursue a more broad-based strategy (already underway for the last two years) to reduce client concentration risk

subsections.label: China Market Share Loss for Western OEMs
points: European (especially luxury) OEMs lost Chinese market share drastically over recent quarters, though partial recovery seen in last few quarters, albeit at lower margins

subsections.label: R&D Budget/AI Budget Nuance
points: AI itself is generally not counted as a separate line in R&D budgets; AI applied within specific domains is counted, but AI budget by itself typically is not

subsections.label: Delay in Vehicle Programs
points: Most vehicle programs are delayed, primarily in passenger car segment; this postpones architecture-related revenue in near term but should benefit KPIT later at vehicle launch/integration stage
Off-highway and commercial vehicle segments are now looking to adopt SDV/AI-based software development (AIDV), partially offsetting passenger car delays

subsections.label: AI-Led Cannibalization
points: AI-led transformation is causing near-term cannibalization of revenue in some specific areas, though management believes this creates a larger opportunity over time as KPIT takes end-to-end solution ownership

subsections.label: Middleware & Autonomous Driving Slowdown
points: Lower-than-expected growth in middleware and autonomous driving due to delays in new architecture programs (impacting Qorix and similar players)

subsections.label: Program Cancellations/Delays in Few Accounts
points: Program cancellations and delays occurred in a few accounts, challenging near-term growth even as it expanded the foundation for future expansion

Continuation of these programs would have resulted in 4-5% sequential growth for the year; this outcome will now be somewhat compromised

~99 OEMs remain in a 30 million vehicle market after ~50 have gone bankrupt, pushing Chinese OEMs to look outside China.

themes.label: Solutions & Products Pivot
themes.note: Shift toward solutions and products (30%+ growth target, moving from 15% to 60% of revenue in 3 years, 50% medium-term goal) seen as core to margin expansion and future growth.

themes.label: AI-led Transformation
themes.note: AI boosts software productivity 10x-100x and drives the Beacon platform, but also causes near-term cannibalization in some revenue areas and multiplies downstream integration/validation complexity.

themes.label: Vehicle Program Delays
themes.note: Honda cancelled new platform programs and broader industry delays in new architecture programs pushed out middleware/autonomous driving revenue, though integration revenue is expected to rise later.

themes.label: Diversification into Off-Highway/Trucks/Micromobility
themes.note: 18% YoY growth in trucks & off-highway, 4 new truck and 6 new off-highway OEM wins, and revived micromobility push (Hero Motors partnership) diversify beyond passenger cars.

themes.label: China Strategy & Market Share Battle
themes.note: KPIT added two new Chinese OEM engagements and helps global OEMs salvage China market share, even as Chinese competition intensifies (~99 OEMs, 30mn vehicle market) and Western OEMs recover only partially with lower margins.

themes.label: Wallet Share & Contract Model Shift
themes.note: Wallet share among T25 clients targeted to rise from 10-12% to 15-20%, alongside a shift to fixed-price/outcome-based contracts (>80% of new deals, targeting >75% overall).

themes.label: Margin Expansion Roadmap
themes.note: FY27 EBITDA guided at 20.5-21.2%, with medium-term target of 22-24% driven by solutions/products mix, outcome-based contracting, and rising per-person productivity.

key_takeaways: Q4 growth of 1.8% in constant currency, 1.9% quarter-on-quarter growth in terms of dollar; in rupee terms, 12% YoY growth and 5.8% quarter-on-quarter growth
$349 million worth increments closed during the quarter
21% of the total pipeline is already into products and solutions
Cash generation has been very good; ₹9.6 billion cash at quarter end, final dividend of ₹5.25 per share, dividend payout about 33%, DSO stood at 47 days
18% year-on-year growth in trucks and off-highway; Q4 growth also led by trucks and off-highway (11.6%) and cloud-based connected services
EBITDA growth margin is for the year 20.8%, and for this quarter, 20.6%
Growth driven by connected vehicle, powertrain, vehicle engineering, and after sales — all four segments

Headwinds: AI-led transformation led to near-term cannibalization in some areas; lower than expected growth in middleware and autonomous driving; program cancellations and delays in few accounts challenged near-term growth but expanded foundation for substantial future expansion
Honda basically cancelled all their new platform programs, impacting KPIT, discovered recently in April

FY27 guidance: EBITDA 20.5% to 21.2%; expect 30% year-on-year revenue growth in solution and products; two of the largest SDV programs coming to an end but revenue will be largely compensated by growth in newly acquired accounts
Medium-term targets: EBITDA between 22% to 24%; 50% revenue share to be achieved from solutions and products; solutions and product revenue to move from 15% to 60% in 3 years
pressing_questions: I have three questions. The first one is just on this pivot on your sort of slide on the industry that mostly incremental spend over the next few years might be in the AD/ADAS space... at this stage, it looks like most of the spend on AD/ADAS, the big spend is happening with the new age OEMs... So just want to understand amongst the legacy players, which is your key focus, how AD/ADAS will progress in that context.

The second one is just to understand the 4 to 5% sequential growth opportunity through FY27 if there was no ramp down in the two large programs you spoke about... just want to understand on an annual basis, what is the gap in revenue that has to be covered with these newly acquired accounts to do the growth aspiration that you might have for the year in FY27.

The third bit is just on the 22 to 24% EBITDA margin range. What are the drivers of that transition from the current sort of mid-20%, 20.5% kind of range to a 22% to 24% range? Is that more to do with products and solutions being a larger share? What's the difference between products and solutions versus what the legacy business is in terms of margin opportunity set and what role does AI play in that sort of transition?

quarters.summary: Management expects same-store/total revenue growth to remain in the long-term guided range of 9%-11% for the rest of FY27, with H1 growth occupancy-led and rate growth expected to build through H2 as international/domestic mix rebalances; net debt-to-EBITDA is targeted at ~2.5x by FY28 (not FY27) driven by stable net debt and EBITDA growth; cumulative free cash flow guidance of >Rs. 3,000 crores over FY27-FY31 is reiterated; capex-heavy new hotels (W Hyderabad, Courtyard Pune, Jaipur renovation) are being pushed to H2 FY28 openings; RARE India platform is targeted to generate Rs. 100-120 crore revenue and Rs. 35-40 crore EBITDA in 1.5-2 years with 50-55% ROCE; Navi Mumbai project construction is expected to start ~1st April 2027 with a 3-4 year build timeline and capital investment backloaded to FY29-FY30.

subsections.label: Reported vs Comparable Bridge
points: Total income growth of 7.3% reported vs 10.8% on comparable basis after excluding a Rs. 9.3 crore one-time other income in Q1 FY26 base related to a subsidiary capital restructuring as part of the GIC transaction.
Same-store growth of approximately 9.1% within the comparable revenue growth, with the balance coming from new openings last year.
Q1 FY26 base also included Rs. 2.1 crores one-time expense related to the GIC transaction, which had reduced reported EBITDA for that quarter.
Q1 FY27 opex includes a Rs. 9.2 crore impact from the GST regime change (from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without input tax credit); this is a current-year impact, not a base-period adjustment.
Reported EBITDA was lower by 4% YoY, but comparable EBITDA growth was healthy at about 12.1% after adjusting for the one-time items and GST impact.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet & Capital Raise
points: Finance costs declined 25.5% YoY to Rs. 37.7 crores, contributing to a 26.4% YoY increase in PBT to Rs. 32.7 crores.
Net debt-to-EBITDA at ~3.2x trailing 12-month, and ~2.4x for operating assets excluding capital deployed towards growth.
Effective interest rate at 7.8%, approximately 300 bps lower than at time of IPO.
Credit rating remains A+ (stable) by both ICRA and CARE, unchanged since last upgrade during FY2026.

Company reiterated its forecast to generate cumulative cash flow of more than Rs. 3,000 crores over FY2027-FY2031 (Rajat incorrectly mentioned Rs. 2,000 crores on the call), enabling funding of committed growth CAPEX while maintaining a strong balance sheet.
Company cited two uncertainties: the external environment and growth opportunities that may arise; balance sheet needs to remain strong regardless of either or both playing out.
Board is enabling resolution for a capital raise of Rs. 750 crore during this meeting to have flexibility to act in time, although business stands well capitalized currently.
Management stated this enabling resolution practice will likely be taken every year going forward, not just this year, to keep the Board prepared with financial flexibility.
Numbers shown to investors (Rs. 1,200 crore to Rs. 3,000 crore path) are sum of parts, not forecast padding; no new acquisitions assumed in that path.

Management noted precedents of capital-intensive businesses keeping such enabling provisions/flexibility available to Boards, especially ahead of a massive CAPEX cycle and in sectors that respond quickly to global uncertainties.
Cannot yet comment on equity/debt mix of any raise since this is only an enabling resolution; no work done yet with investors on structure.

subsections.label: F&B Revenue Slowdown
points: F&B revenue growth slowed to ~3.7%-4% YoY (versus room revenue growth of 14%), pulling down the blended average.

International travelers tend to be higher spenders on food & beverage, especially in the upscale segment; business mix moved from ~78%-79% domestic to 80%-83% domestic, more stark in upper upscale segment.
A key restaurant renovation in Bangalore reduced F&B contribution temporarily but has now reopened.
Event cancellations due to the West Asia crisis affected F&B; some events (e.g., at Hyatt Regency Pune in June) moved to July and August.
Management expects F&B growth to recover as events pick pace.

subsections.label: Macro Demand Environment
points: Company is built around India's urbanization thesis with portfolio concentrated in dense office markets, which held up in Q1.
GCC (global capability center) leasing momentum remains strong, led by Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Pune.

Aviation passenger traffic dipped early in the quarter due to geopolitical escalation and Gulf carrier limitations, but recovered in the latter half, ending essentially flat YoY for the quarter as a whole — illustrating how quickly underlying travel demand reasserts itself once disruption passes.

subsections.label: Occupancy & Rate Dynamics
points: Domestic travelers now 82% of room nights sold (up from 78% a year ago); this more resilient domestic cohort insulated top line from disruptions to international arrivals.
36% of days in the quarter saw occupancy above 90%, indicating underlying demand compression is intact even with softer international business.
H1 revenue growth is occupancy-led; occupancy remains extremely robust — management noted that underwriting 79% occupancy for a business-hotel portfolio would have seemed unlikely five years ago.

Domestic share increase (78%→82%) comes at a cost since international business carried a rate premium of 10-20% depending on segment; as domestic/international mix rebalances into H2, rate growth is expected to return.

Rate growth was slightly soft this quarter primarily due to the West Asia crisis disrupting international inbound/business travel; raw ADR growth was in the 3.5%-4% zip code across all segments with no major disparity between segments.

July trends are described as strong, trending ahead of where the previous quarter ended, with growth now seen in rate (not just occupancy) — split roughly half rate/half occupancy — though management cautioned one month is not representative of the full year.
Same-store total revenue growth for the quarter was around 9%-9.5%, squarely within the long-term guided 9%-11% range despite headwinds.

GST impact this quarter was slightly above 2%, driven by mix (lower upper-upscale mix, higher mid-scale mix meaning more rooms sold below the Rs. 7.5k threshold); GST impact typically larger in Q1/Q2 (volume-driven growth quarters) and equalizes on a YoY basis from Q3 onward, though margin depression continues but will be lesser in H2 than H1.

subsections.label: Segment-wise Performance (Upscale vs Midscale)
points: Mid-scale portfolio outperformed broader upscale with RevPAR growth of 13.7%, driven by healthy occupancy of 81.3% vs upper-upscale occupancy of 78.4%.
Last year same quarter, occupancy for upscale was ~74% and mid-scale ~73.8% — so mid-scale has shown a much stronger YoY improvement.

Management had previously flagged two portfolio opportunities for FY27 independent of market: (1) broader mid-scale segment expected to perform better — delivered as expected in Q1; (2) part of portfolio that underperformed in FY2026 is now showing early signs of strong performance, with Q2 and beyond trends said to be far ahead of Q1.

subsections.label: Portfolio Mix Shift (Upscale vs Midscale)
points: Upper upscale and upscale hotels earned almost 4x the revenue of midscale hotels on a per-key basis in FY2026 (same-store basis), underscoring why portfolio mix matters.
Most of the 1,660 rooms across 7 new hotels in the committed pipeline sit in the upper upscale/upscale segment; an additional ~450 rooms are being rebranded from upper midscale to upscale.
Upscale share of revenue expected to move from ~40-41% today to ~60% by FY2030.

Recent GST changes make the upscale shift more valuable since GST impacts midscale rooms far more than upscale ones — every new upscale key is expected to bring more revenue per key and better margin than the midscale it often replaces or sits alongside, generating asymmetric growth (bigger jump in revenue and profit than room count alone would suggest).
Midscale remains valuable for cyclical resilience, evident from its strong RevPAR growth in Q1.

subsections.label: RARE India (Leisure/Asset-light Platform)
points: RARE portfolio now stands at 75 hotels with 1,046 rooms across 15 states — a curated collection of heritage palaces, wildlife lodges, and boutique resorts, up from 66-67 hotels at the time of the March transaction/term sheet.

RARE is asset-light: RARE owns the platform, not the underlying hotels; economics come from (1) fee income from business generated for hotel partners, (2) additional incentive fee in select hotels, and (3) selective opportunistic investments (e.g., the Itmenaan Estate acquisition).

Itmenaan Estate (8-acre estate in Uttarakhand, ~Rs. 12 crore) — owner wanted to dispose of it as they were leaving the country; entry capital is low relative to asset potential, and much of value creation will come from the RARE model itself.

Itmenaan's near-term ordinary performance was because owners moved to Canada and the hotel operated without active marketing and was delisted from RARE for a period; it will now be relisted, and management expects the Kumaon region's experience-led rate positioning (Rs. 20,000-40,000) plus RARE and potential Marriott Outdoor Collection affiliation to help it reclaim pricing.
Total capital investment in RARE stands at ~Rs. 47 crores cumulative to date, rising to ~Rs. 60 crores including the Itmenaan add-on.

RARE will remain a relatively small portion of capital allocation (expected ~10-12% zip code over 4-5 years), but management expects it to create disproportionate shareholder value because these hotels' capital requirements are disconnected from the room rates they can produce (unlike core business hotels where cost per sq ft correlates with room rates) — rate is realized through experiences and distribution.

Two revenue recognition models within RARE: (1) majority is booking/commission revenue that RARE earns on bookings it channelizes through distribution; (2) select hotels may sign more extended agreements resembling a franchise model, where RARE's revenue share is higher than just booking commission — seen as a new upside not originally underwritten. Underlying hotel revenues stay with the hotel owner; only fee income is recognized by RARE India.

~40 of 75 RARE hotels have signed up for the Marriott Outdoor Collection program — ahead of original expectations in terms of pace; 10-12 hotels are on other existing platforms (e.g., Mr & Mrs Smith) and will make their own decisions given existing contracts; RARE hotels can be on OTAs regardless (no restriction), only overlapping subscription-style platforms are the consideration.

RARE revenue potential (once stabilized) previously disclosed at Rs. 100-120 crore top line, ~35% margin (due to cost of Marriott distribution), with EBITDA contribution of Rs. 35-40 crore expected in the next 1.5-2 years — matching the investment made in the portfolio; expected to deliver 100% NOI yield in ~2 years before generating returns thereafter.

Management does not disclose blended RARE RevPAR given wide dispersion (rates from Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 55,000-70,000; occupancy 25%-75%) — considers a blended average mathematically dishonest; will continue reporting RevPAR/rate/occupancy only from the core owned Tier-1 business hotel portfolio to avoid conflicting investor signals; RARE's commission/fee income will be reported as fee income.

RARE steady-state ROCE expected to be ~5x that of consolidated SAMHI ROCE (~10%) — i.e., 50-55% ROCE — due to minimal depreciation (internally funded via accruals) and no finance cost, with EBITDA-to-PBT flow-through of ~95%; compares to mature owned portfolio ROCE of ~18-19%.

subsections.label: Hyatt Regency Pune Re-positioning
points: Very early discussion about repositioning Hyatt Regency Pune as Grand Hyatt is not being pursued right now, as the hotel has already seen significant performance improvement without that incremental CAPEX (consistent for last several quarters, referenced on Slide #27 of the presentation).

subsections.label: W Hyderabad Opening Timeline
points: W Hyderabad targeted to be fully operational in H2 FY2028 (or Calendar Year 2027); project progress had been on schedule to open around June, but management is being cautious about regulatory approvals and licenses potentially causing surprises.

subsections.label: Courtyard Pune Renovation
points: Back-office and MEP renovation has started at Courtyard Pune; Pune market was not significantly impacted by the West Asia crisis, so management strategically deferred public area and guest room renovations (to avoid taking inventory offline in a resilient market), now planned to start around April 2027, typically taking about five to six months.
Courtyard Pune renovation is spread across all 12 months of revenue, requiring renovation to be done in parts to avoid significantly impacting revenue, unlike Jaipur.

subsections.label: Jaipur (Tribute Portfolio) Renovation
points: Jaipur renovation is easier to execute because the April-onward period does not contribute meaningfully to revenue/EBITDA, allowing a bolder approach of taking inventory offline for faster renovation; most drawings and development have been received; both Courtyard Pune and Jaipur (along with W Hyderabad) are geared for H2 opening.

subsections.label: Navi Mumbai Project
points: All previously reported issues (from ~2 years back) are fully resolved; no current concerns with approvals or authorities.

Project moving on three fronts: (1) statutory approvals progressing well, with first set expected in the next few months; (2) design development, with a substantial part to be presented next quarter; (3) discussions with construction firms on construction technology given the scale of the project.
Expected to break ground around 1st April 2027 (originally targeted end of this fiscal year); expected build timeline of three to four years given size and scale.
Development approach for this large project will be more scientific with longer prep time but shorter on-site time (where majority of capital is deployed).

Capital investment through FY2028 will remain relatively small (largely RCC structure); the main capital investment phase will start in FY2029-FY2030 during finishing and engineering installations — matching current cash flow projections.

key_figures.label: GIC participation right in new upscale opportunities

subsections.label: GIC Joint Venture
points: No partnership with GIC being evaluated for existing assets at this point; per the GIC agreement, GIC has the right to participate up to 35% in new upscale opportunities after the JV agreement is signed.
The only opportunity signed since the GIC JV is the IKEA/Ingka opportunity in Noida; it is not yet known whether GIC will participate in that opportunity.
Future acquisition opportunities will continue to follow the 65:35 (SAMHI:GIC) sharing construct; the JV is described as extremely well-capitalized with firepower to grow if opportunities arise.
Navi Mumbai dual-branded development and W Hyderabad are NOT included in the GIC JV — both were seeded prior to the GIC JV and are currently, and proposed to remain, 100% owned by SAMHI.

subsections.label: Capital Raise Enabling Resolution
points: Board is taking an enabling resolution for a Rs. 750 crore capital raise to provide flexibility to act in time given two uncertainties: the external environment and potential growth opportunities.
Management does not currently see any specific opportunity on the horizon but wants the Board to have readiness.

Management indicated this will likely become an annual practice, not limited to this year, citing precedent among capital-intensive businesses and the need for flexibility ahead of a large CAPEX cycle.
No decision yet on equity/debt mix for any eventual raise, as this is purely an enabling resolution with no investor deliberation done yet.

On acquisition return profile: management is not worried about finding operationally distressed hotel opportunities even at cycle peaks, citing recent examples in Bangalore Whitefield, Hyderabad City, and Heart of Noida, where renovation/rebranding/asset management created operational turnaround and shareholder value.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and Aviation Disruption
points: Passenger traffic dipped early in the quarter due to geopolitical escalation and limitations of Gulf carriers, though it recovered by the latter half of the quarter to end flat YoY.
West Asia crisis disrupted international business/inbound travel, leading to softer rate growth and event cancellations (e.g., at Hyatt Regency Pune) that were pushed to July/August.

Management noted every quarter since Operation Sindhoor, the IndiGo crisis, and Middle East crisis has brought something unexpected, but the hotel industry and SAMHI have weathered these reasonably well due to strong domestic demand.
Crisis stabilization (not necessarily resolution — the Russia-Ukraine war example is cited as a precedent of non-resolution) is expected to allow rate growth to return in H2.

subsections.label: GST Regime Change Impact
points: GST regime change (12% with input tax credit to 5% without) created a Rs. 9.2 crore impact on Q1 FY27 opex, and this is expected to continue affecting margin depression, though impact will be lesser in H2 than H1, and impact equalizes YoY from Q3 onward.
Impact is amplified in quarters with a higher mix of rooms sold below the Rs. 7.5k GST threshold (i.e., more midscale-weighted quarters like Q1/Q2).

subsections.label: Regulatory/Approval Risk (Navi Mumbai, W Hyderabad)
points: Management flagged that regulatory approvals and licenses have historically brought surprises for hotel openings (e.g., W Hyderabad), prompting cautious guidance on opening timelines.
Navi Mumbai's earlier-reported issues are stated as fully resolved with no current concerns on approvals/authorities.

subsections.label: Revenue Growth Outlook
points: Same-store RevPAR growth and total revenue growth for same-store assets have remained within the expected long-term revenue growth forecast of 9%-11%, even with repeated headwinds.
FY27 growth expected to be occupancy-led in H1, with rate growth expected to emerge in H2 as domestic/international mix rebalances; early July trends show rate growth returning.
Management is bullish that Q2 and beyond trends (for previously underperforming portfolio segments) are running ahead of Q1 performance.

subsections.label: Leverage & Cash Flow Outlook
points: Net debt-to-EBITDA target of ~2.4-2.5x is expected to be reached by FY2028 (not FY2027 as one analyst had modeled), driven by stable net debt and EBITDA growth.

Company reiterated its cumulative free cash flow forecast of more than Rs. 3,000 crore over FY2027-FY2031 (Rajat misspoke as Rs. 2,000 crore on the call), funding committed growth CAPEX while maintaining balance sheet strength.
Board intends to take annual enabling resolutions for capital raises to remain prepared for both external problems and growth opportunities without diluting financial discipline.

subsections.label: Growth Pipeline & Portfolio Mix Outlook
points: Strong growth pipeline secured across Hyderabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Noida, and Navi Mumbai with marquee brands (The W, Westin, Marriott), deepening presence in key office/aviation markets.
Upscale share of revenue expected to rise from ~40-41% today to ~60% by FY2030, driven by new pipeline hotels weighted to upper upscale/upscale and rebranding of ~450 rooms.
Company reiterated destiny to multiply revenue by 2.5x, following the path from Rs. 1,200 crore to Rs. 3,000 crore.

subsections.label: RARE / Leisure Outlook
points: RARE and broader Leisure thesis will use a very small part of capital (~10-12% zip code over 4-5 years) but has potential to create relatively larger shareholder value, though it will take time.
RARE targeted to reach Rs. 100-120 crore stabilized top line and Rs. 35-40 crore EBITDA within 1.5-2 years, at ~35% margin, with 100% NOI yield in ~2 years and steady-state ROCE of 50-55%.

guidance_ledger.statement: Same-store RevPAR and total revenue growth for same-store assets has remained within the expected long-term revenue growth forecast of 9%-11%, even with repeated headwinds; total revenue growth remains healthy in that range.
Company clarified it did not guide to 2.5x by end of FY2027; expects to reach that level by FY2028, largely on account of stable net debt and growth in EBITDA.

Firm on the trajectory outlined last year with the forecast to generate a cumulative cash flow of more than Rs. 3,000 crores over FY2027-FY2031 (Rajat incorrectly mentioned Rs. 2,000 crores on the call), enabling funding of committed growth CAPEX while maintaining a strong balance sheet.
Upscale share of revenue moves from approximately 40%-41% today to approximately 60% by Financial Year 2030.
Revenue potential once stabilized will be about Rs. 100 crore-Rs. 120 crore of top line (as given in March presentation).
EBITDA contribution from RARE should be about Rs. 35 crore-Rs. 40 crore in the next year and a half to two years, matching the investment made in the portfolio.
This portfolio should do a 100% NOI yield in about a two-year period, after which it will start producing returns.
RARE Group could do roughly 5x the ROCE of consolidated SAMHI (~10%), i.e., the portfolio is expected to deliver 50%-55% return on capital employed.
RARE and the broader Leisure thesis will remain a relatively small portion of capital allocation, in the zip code of 10%-12%.
W Hyderabad is being targeted to be fully operational for the second half of FY2028 (Calendar Year 2027), with caution around regulatory approvals/licenses.
Public area and guest room renovations at Courtyard Pune have been strategically deferred and now planned to start around April 2027, taking about five to six months.
Jaipur renovation is geared for the second half, similar to Courtyard Pune and W Hyderabad.
Originally planning to be on-site by end of this fiscal year; now assuming, to be safe, 1st April 2027 as ground-breaking date, with three to four years to deliver the hotel.

Through FY2028, investment in the Navi Mumbai project will remain rather small (largely RCC structure); the main part of capital investment will start in FY2029-FY2030 during finishing and engineering installations, matching current cash flow statements.
SAMHI is destined to at least multiply its revenue by 2.5x, following the path of going from Rs. 1,200 crores to Rs. 3,000 crores.
As the crisis stabilizes and the world moves into H2, rate growth is expected to come through to the portfolio; already starting to play out in July, split roughly half rate/half occupancy.
Company remains absolutely confident of maintaining a 9% to 11% total revenue growth from same-store hotels in the long term — guidance held since IPO.
Margins expected to be around 38% or so, factoring in the permanent GST impact; group level margin should be maintained at 38%-plus.
Cash interest expense computed at about INR 127 crore, but guiding towards INR 135-140 crore factoring in a 15-20 bps rate increase.

Allocated about INR 250 crore to INR 270 crore of capital capex for FY27, largely towards W Hyderabad (~INR 150 crore), Westin Bangalore work, maintenance, and minor renovations at Four Points Pune and Jaipur (~INR 15-20 crore).
Expect to maintain a similar zip code of capex (~INR 250-270 crore per year run rate), majority directed towards Westin Bangalore.
Commitment to fully fund the INR 2,200 crore of capex across the existing pipeline, including Navi Mumbai.

Base free cash flow held flat over 5 years produces ~INR 1,550 crore; layering same-store revenue growth (9-11% lower end) adds ~INR 1,000 crore more; with new openings, cumulative free cash post interest exceeds INR 3,000 crore over FY27-31.
Same-store hotels expected to comfortably grow 9% to 10% year-on-year for FY27 given the reset base.
W Hyderabad expected to bring, on current revenue run-rate basis, almost 6% to 7% growth for FY28.
NCR expected to come back to mid-teens revenue growth in the current fiscal year following Hyatt Place Gurgaon renovation completion.
Current pool of assets is well geared to get to the targeted 14% to 15% ROCE with very little risk.
Group ROCE profile expected to be maintained in the mid-teens zip code even with a lot of new hotel openings, aided by variable leases and land value pre-accounted for.
Asset recycling target is more than the residual INR 100 crore, estimated at about INR 200 crore to INR 250 crore, largely through sale of single non-core assets.
Balance GIC investment of INR 150 crore expected to come over the next 2-year period, in line with capex spending on Westin - Tribute Bangalore development.

As free cash flow compounds beyond committed growth requirements, the Board intends to evaluate a disciplined mechanism to return capital directly to shareholders in a manner consistent with long-term value creation.
Company expects to structurally secure its place at 40%-plus reported margins over time, given incremental investments/openings are predominantly upscale in strong markets.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory approvals/licenses uncertainty for new hotel openings
risk_register.note: Management flagged historical surprises in approvals/licenses affecting timelines (e.g., W Hyderabad); cautious H2 FY28 target given as a result.

risk_register.risk: Severe monsoons and flooding in core markets - August
risk_register.note: One of the sequence of one-time disruptions bracketing FY26, contributing to the INR 45-52 crore revenue compression.
Part of the sequence of quarterly disruptions impacting FY26 revenue.

risk_register.risk: Middle East / Gulf conflict - March onwards
risk_register.note: Continues to impact revenue; reduced March revenue growth to sub-minus 1%; residual impact continued through April with recovery signs starting in May; inbound FIT cancellations, near land cruise and MENA impact cited; expected to continue impacting absolute Q1 FY27 numbers.

risk_register.risk: GST regulatory change (12% with input credit to 5% without)
risk_register.note: Viewed as a permanent margin impact; impacted H2 FY26 consolidated EBITDA by ~INR 14 crore; GST drag expanded from ~INR 7.5 crore in Q3 to ~INR 10 crore in Q4.

risk_register.risk: Interest rate hardening due to currency weakness
risk_register.note: Market signals suggest possible upward revision to interest rate cycle; company has factored a 15-25 bps increase into FY27 interest cost guidance.

risk_register.risk: Construction / spillover delay risk in pipeline projects
risk_register.note: Analyst flagged risk given multiple major hotel development announcements during the year; management cited strong guardrails (discount-to-replacement cost discipline, mid-teens ROCE underwriting, avoidance of long-lead greenfield assets) and separated operating/growth teams to mitigate.

New competitor announcements (e.g., a Westin in Bangalore) noted; management maintains current supply growth is concentrated in specific micro-markets (airport-Hebbal corridor in Bangalore) where SAMHI has zero presence, and that demand/supply should be evaluated at micro-market rather than city level.

Management repeatedly cautioned that 'the world is volatile' and 'bombs are flying around the world,' requiring continued vigilant monitoring even though double-digit growth is not currently seen as an alarming threat.
A dilutive low-margin corporate/outdoor catering contract at one large asset (~INR 13-14 crore revenue) will disappear starting May, removing the FY26 margin drag going into FY27.

themes.label: Revenue growth resilience amid disruptions
themes.note: Same-store total revenue growth held at ~9%-9.5%, within the guided 9%-11% long-term range, despite West Asia crisis and aviation disruption.

themes.label: GST margin impact
themes.note: GST regime change caused a Rs. 9.2 crore opex impact in Q1 FY27, with impact slightly above 2% this quarter due to midscale-weighted mix; expected to ease in H2 and equalize YoY from Q3.

themes.label: Deleveraging and balance sheet strength
themes.note: Net debt-to-EBITDA target of ~2.4-2.5x pushed out to FY2028 (from earlier FY2027 expectation) despite finance costs declining 25.5% YoY and effective interest rate down to 7.8%.

themes.label: Free cash flow compounding / capital allocation discipline
themes.note: Company reiterated cumulative free cash flow guidance of >Rs. 3,000 crore over FY2027-FY2031 and is taking an annual enabling resolution (Rs. 750 crore) to preserve Board flexibility while protecting balance sheet strength.

themes.label: Capital-efficient growth via variable leases and GIC platform
themes.note: GIC JV (65:35 split) retains right to participate up to 35% in new upscale opportunities (e.g., IKEA/Ingka Noida); Navi Mumbai and W Hyderabad remain 100% SAMHI-owned as they were seeded prior to the JV.

themes.label: Portfolio mix shift to upscale
themes.note: Upscale share of revenue targeted to rise from ~40-41% to ~60% by FY2030, aided by pipeline weighting and GST dynamics favoring upscale over midscale.

themes.label: RARE India asset-light leisure platform scale-up
themes.note: RARE portfolio grew to 75 hotels/1,046 rooms with ~40 hotels signed to Marriott Outdoor Collection; targeted Rs. 100-120 crore revenue, Rs. 35-40 crore EBITDA, and 50-55% ROCE at steady state on modest ~10-12% capital allocation.

key_takeaways: Same-store RevPAR grew 9.6% year-on-year to approximately Rs. 5,220, with portfolio occupancy at 79.3%, up from 74.2% in the year-ago quarter.
Domestic travelers now make up 82% of the room nights sold, up from 78% a year ago.
36% of the days in the quarter saw occupancy in excess of 90%, indicating underlying demand compression is intact even with softer international business.
Total income for Q1 FY2027 was Rs. 308.3 crores, up 7.3% year-on-year on a reported basis and up 10.8% on a comparable basis, which included same-store growth of approximately 9.1%.
Reported EBITDA was lower by 4% on a year-on-year basis, but on a comparable basis was healthy at about 12.1%.
Finance costs for the quarter declined by 25.5% year-on-year to Rs. 37.7 crores, resulting in a PBT of Rs. 32.7 crores, up by 26.4% over the same period last year.

Net debt as on June 30th, 2026, was approximately Rs. 1,490 crores; net debt-to-EBITDA stood at approximately 3.2x on a trailing 12-month basis and approximately 2.4x for operating assets excluding capital deployed towards growth.

Company remains firm on the trajectory to generate cumulative cash flow of more than Rs. 3,000 crores over FY2027-FY2031, and is enabling a resolution for a capital raise during this meeting, although the business stands well capitalized as of now.
The RARE portfolio now stands at 75 hotels with 1,046 rooms across 15 states, an asset-light model where RARE owns the platform, not the underlying hotels.
pressing_questions: Given that the promoter holding is slightly lower and majority of inventory addition is back-ended, and given the free cash generation being seen (implying limited near-term funding need), what is the specific reason to go ahead and take this Rs. 750 crore enabling resolution?

If we are targeting a 2.4x-2.5x net debt-to-EBITDA by year-end, based on the math it appears roughly Rs. 550 crore of EBITDA is needed versus Rs. 100 crore done in Q1 — does that outcome sound achievable and reasonable?

Considering the enabling resolution overhang on equity dilution and stock price, and given the company already has a GIC platform for upscale hotel opportunities, does taking an enabling resolution every year send a comforting signal to investors? What would be the tentative equity/debt proportion if the resolution were utilized for growth, and how is management thinking about return on capital employed given that acquisitions have become costlier as hotel owners demand more money?

quarters.summary: SAMHI closed FY26 with 12.3% revenue growth (diluted from a potential 16-17% by ~INR 45-52 crore of one-time disruptions) and PBT nearly doubling to ~INR 165 crore; management reiterated 9-11% long-term same-store revenue growth guidance for FY27, a medium-term net debt-to-EBITDA target of ~2.5x, and margin guidance of ~38% (permanently impacted by GST slab change), while laying out a FY27-FY31 free cash flow compounding plan (~INR 300-315 crore FY26 run-rate, growing to >INR 3,000 crore cumulative over 5 years) funding a fully committed INR 2,200 crore capex pipeline (W Hyderabad, Tribute/Westin Bangalore Whitefield, Ingka Noida, Marriott Sriperumbudur) without incremental leverage or equity dilution, with optionality for shareholder returns once growth needs are met.

subsections.label: FY26 commitments delivered
points: At the start of FY26 two specific commitments were set: (a) deliver revenue growth in the range of 9% to 11% and (b) bring the balance sheet to a net debt-to-EBITDA of approximately 3x — both were delivered despite disruptions.
Revenue growth came in at 12.3% for the year, anchored to commercial demand in core markets.

subsections.label: One-time disruptions bracketing the year
points: FY26 absorbed a sequence of disruptions in nearly every quarter: the India-Pakistan conflict in May, unusually severe monsoons/flooding in core markets in August, airline disruption in December, and the Middle East conflict in March which continues.
These one-time events compressed full-year revenue by approximately INR 45-52 crore, diluting revenue growth from a potential 16-17% to the actual reported 12.3%.

subsections.label: Q4 EBITDA drivers
points: Q4 consolidated EBITDA was ~6% below the same quarter last year, largely on account of expanded GST impact (more rooms sold below INR 7,500), some FF&E expense routed through the P&L, pre-opening expenses for new inventory, and the added impact of the Gulf crisis.

subsections.label: Key FY26 P&L developments
points: GST regulatory change moved the hotel slab from 12% with input credit to 5% without input tax credit, impacting H2 FY26 consolidated EBITDA by ~INR 14 crore.
~INR 5 crore was funded for FF&E product upgrade; year-end reconciliation and actuarial valuation adjustments were routed through the P&L.
The four one-time disturbances (India-Pakistan conflict through Middle East conflict) also weighed on the year.

Adjusted for these items, FY26 EBITDA growth would have been 19-20% with margins of 38%+; Q4 adjusted EBITDA would have been ~INR149 crore, a YoY growth of ~16.8%, in line with the pre-disruption trajectory.

subsections.label: Below EBITDA items
points: Finance costs fell sharply to INR 171 crore from INR 225 crore in FY25, reflecting the GIC capital infusion starting June 2025, consequent deleveraging, and reduction in cost of borrowing.
PBT before exceptional items almost doubled to INR 165 crore from ~INR 87 crore in FY25.

A deferred tax income of ~INR 330 crore was booked in Q4 on formal recognition of brought-forward losses and unabsorbed depreciation, reflecting management's confidence in continuous utilization of this tax shield — a non-cash accounting-driven income line.

FY26 reported PAT of ~INR 567 crore included the Q4 deferred tax recognition, the Navi Mumbai and other impairment reversal (~INR 83 crore), and a gain on sale of discontinued operations in Caspia Delhi.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & deleveraging
points: Net debt reduced by ~INR 516 crore to INR 1,450 crore as of 31 March 2026 from INR 1,967 crore a year earlier, reflecting GIC infusion deployed for deleveraging.
Net debt-to-EBITDA at year-end was ~3x.
Total Equity rose to ~INR 2,286 crore from INR 1,142 crore at FY25 end.
Effective interest rate for the group is now 7.9% as of 21 May 2026, with annualized interest cost run rate down to ~INR 130-135 crore.
Credit rating upgraded to A+ Stable by both CARE and ICRA during the year.

subsections.label: Free cash flow compounding thesis (FY27-31)
points: Combination of consistent same-store revenue growth, margin levers, declining finance costs, and fully capitalized growth pipeline generated free cash flow of ~INR 300 crore in FY26 (post interest and Lease MG payments) — the base number underwritten for the next phase.
FY26 free cash flow of ~INR 300 crore becomes ~INR 315 crore on a run-rate basis once additional secured interest savings are factored in.
Over a 5-year horizon (FY27-FY31), that base held flat produces ~INR 1,550 crore of free cash; layering same-store revenue growth at the lower end of 9-11% adds ~INR 1,000 crore more.

A fully committed pipeline of new openings (HITEC City Hyderabad end-FY27, Tribute Bangalore Whitefield end-FY28, Westin Bangalore Whitefield, Ingka Noida upscale hotel, new Marriott Sriperumbudur Chennai in FY29-FY30) takes the cumulative free cash post interest over FY27-31 to more than INR 3,000 crore.

subsections.label: Capital recycling track record
points: Over the past 3 years SAMHI recycled ~INR 960 crore of capital: ~INR 210 crore from monetizing 4 non-core hotels at an average 20x EV-to-EBITDA, and ~INR 750 crore from the GIC capital infusion into the subsidiary platform.
Of this, ~INR 650 crore was deployed to reduce debt and the balance funded accretive new acquisitions.

Capital recycling is described as an established, not opportunistic, part of the playbook; further candidates within the portfolio have been identified for selective execution to maximize return from capital employed, accelerate deleveraging and fund growth.
Target for asset recycling over the next 2 years is ~INR 200-250 crore, largely through sale of non-core single assets (residual target already exceeds the earlier INR 100 crore residual).

subsections.label: Capital allocation framework (framework against INR 3,000+ crore cumulative free cash)
points: First: continue deleveraging towards a medium to long-term net debt-to-EBITDA target of approximately 2.5x.
Second: commitment to fully fund the INR 2,200 crore capex across the existing pipeline, including Navi Mumbai.
Third: retain investable surplus for tactical M&A and long-term variable leases where returns are accretive.

Fourth: as free cash flow compounds beyond committed growth requirements, the Board intends to evaluate a disciplined mechanism to return capital directly to shareholders consistent with long-term value creation.

subsections.label: GST mechanics clarified (Jinesh Q&A)
points: The GST rule applies per room sold below INR 7,500, irrespective of segment or the hotel's average rate — even a hotel with average rate of INR 9,000 loses input tax credit on any room sold below the threshold.

This is not visible from segment-level occupancy data; even the best-performing hotels can sell some rooms below INR 7,500 during periods of crisis when revenue management prioritizes securing market share/volume over price.
GST impact expanded from ~INR 7.5 crore in Q3 to ~INR 10 crore in Q4, disproportionate to revenue growth, indicating more rooms sold below the threshold.

subsections.label: Margin bridge and outdoor catering drag (Q4 same-store)
points: Adjusting reported EBITDA (~INR 149 crore) for other income (~INR 8-9 crore) and adding back ~INR 22 crore of March revenue loss gives an EBITDA margin of ~38.4% versus 38.7% in the base quarter — a flattish decline.

One larger asset picked up ~INR 13-14 crore of low-margin corporate/outdoor catering business, diluting what would have been a slight margin increase; this dilutive contract will disappear starting May, removing the drag in FY27.

Same-store EBITDA bridge (Slide 28) negative impact (ex-GST) driven by FF&E expense through P&L, year-end reconciliation/actuarial costs, and the outdoor/corporate catering business at Hyatt Regency Pune.

Historically Q3-to-Q4 sees a significant revenue jump (mostly after 20 January), and hotels are geared for that; when hit by a sudden crisis in a quarter prepared for a revenue jump, cost control cannot respond immediately, making flow-through harder to maintain (visible improvement expected in April once costs like outsourced labor/fixed contracts are adjusted).

subsections.label: Depreciation increase driver
points: Depreciation increase sequentially is due to a one-time revaluation of balance life of assets, done via periodic (every 3 years) reassessment; assets deemed to have largely lived their life were adjusted with a one-time hit; no material change expected in depreciation going forward.

subsections.label: Lease accounting treatment (variable leases)
points: Lease payments made during hotel development are capitalized until the hotel opens; thereafter the variable lease portion is expensed to the P&L as revenue generation begins.

All leases have a 3- to 5-year minimum guarantee; a separate Right-of-Use (ROU) asset and lease liability is created with distinct accounting treatment, while the variable lease portion is a direct P&L cost.
Today, ~1.5-2% of revenue is attributable to variable lease payments on existing leasehold assets; on a like-to-like basis EBITDA margin would be ~150-170 bps higher excluding this lease treatment.

subsections.label: Capex allocation FY27-FY28
points: FY27 capex allocation of ~INR 250-270 crore: ~INR 150 crore for W Hyderabad (opening towards year-end), balance for ongoing work at Westin Bangalore, some maintenance capex, minor renovations at Four Points Pune and Jaipur (~INR 15-20 crore), and some investment in leisure.
FY28 capex expected to maintain a similar INR 250-270 crore run rate, with majority directed to Westin Bangalore as W Hyderabad would be largely fully invested by then.

subsections.label: Interest cost outlook FY27
points: Pure cash interest expense for FY27 computed at ~INR 127 crore, but guided to INR 135-140 crore incorporating a 15-25 bps factored increase in interest rates due to anticipated market-wide interest rate hardening from currency weakness.

subsections.label: ROCE targets by asset type
points: Current pool of assets is well-positioned to sustain a targeted 14-15% ROCE with little risk.
New openings will be a mixed bag: variable-lease assets (Ingka, W Hyderabad) tend to deliver very good ROCEs early on since building depreciation isn't carried on SAMHI's books.
Ingka Center hotel investment is largely in FF&E and hard finishes in a strong market, expected not to be dilutive.

Marriott Sriperumbudur addition requires zero incremental real estate investment; the existing Fairfield by Marriott on that land already delivers ~30% ROCE (28-32% range), so the new hotel is expected to have extremely high ROCE given no underlying real estate expense.
Overall group ROCE profile is expected to remain in the mid-teens zip code despite new openings, aided by variable leases and land value already accounted for.

subsections.label: Underwriting basis for capex funding
points: FY26 free cash flow production (EBITDA minus interest expense and lease MG) of ~INR 300 crore is considered largely secured, tested even in a tough disruption-heavy year, and viewed as available for the next 4-5 years.

Underwriting assumes no operating leverage — the same revenue growth rate is applied to EBITDA growth (conservative), yielding ~9-10% EBITDA growth and an incremental ~INR 700 crore of free cash from the existing asset pool over 5 years.

From FY28 (W Hyderabad opening) and subsequent hotel openings, incremental EBITDA contribution of ~INR 400-500 crore is expected from FY28 to FY31, flowing through to free cash without incremental debt.

Navi Mumbai and One Financial District Hyderabad are excluded (assumed zero contribution) from revenue/EBITDA underwriting since they are quasi-greenfield projects, though their full capex is still included in the INR 2,200 crore capex figure — built in as a margin of error.

subsections.label: April-May trends and Q1 FY27 outlook
points: QTD (quarter-to-date) is tracking double-digit revenue growth; April was flattish, May is strong.
May of last year was a weak base due to Operation Sindoor (started around 1st-9th May), aiding relative comparison.
Gulf crisis will continue to impact absolute numbers through Q1, but YoY growth is expected to easily be maintained in double digits.

subsections.label: Demand rebalancing and pricing
points: Long-haul international travel has resumed, including customers from the U.S., despite flying time increasing to ~20 hours, which impacts the number of people attending small meetings.
Encouraging resumption of business seen from all core markets; occupancies are not a problem, with strong capacity utilization across the group.
As business rebalances, management expects conviction to restart repricing.

subsections.label: Renovation and inventory additions during FY26
points: Added ~20% inventory to Sheraton Hyderabad.
Added inventory to Hyatt Regency, Pune.
Added inventory to one of the Holiday Inn Express hotels; opened two more Holiday Inn Express hotels during the year.
Significant renovation at Hyatt Place, Gurgaon — inventory was shut for renovation and has now reopened with new ballrooms, concluded by end of Q3.
These capital investments and efforts are expected to add to the same-store base for FY27, and provide cushion/hedge if the current crisis continues longer.

subsections.label: Segment margin performance
points: Upscale segment margin is already 42-43%.
ACIC margin moved in line to 41-42%.
Holiday Inn Express portfolio performed well.

Incremental inventory openings are predominantly upscale in strong markets (e.g., Bangalore, Hyderabad), reducing the risk of selling rooms below the INR 7,500 GST threshold versus, e.g., an upscale hotel in Ahmedabad or a mid-scale in weaker markets.

subsections.label: NCR / Hyatt Place Gurgaon recovery
points: Hyatt Place Gurgaon renovation concluded by end of Q3; fabulous growth seen from January onward.
NCR expected to return to mid-teens revenue growth in current fiscal year given a low base (impacted by both renovation and a weak market at opening).

subsections.label: FY27/FY28 revenue growth build-up by driver
points: FY27: same-store hotels (reset base) expected to grow comfortably 9-10% YoY; incremental impact of ~3-4% from FY26 renovations/additions; combined this implies ~14% total revenue growth if no crisis continuation, but guided conservatively at 10-11% due to ongoing crisis caution.
FY28: W Hyderabad opening expected to add ~6-7% growth on current revenue run-rate basis due to strong location, brand and product positioning, notwithstanding the ongoing crisis.
Beyond FY28: larger openings include Tribute Bangalore, Westin Bangalore, and Noida development.

subsections.label: GIC platform for upscale hotels
points: Formally launched a GIC platform for upscale hotels in India, committing approximately INR 750 crore for a 35% minority stake in a 1,000-room platform.
Of this, INR 600 crore has already been received, with the balance of INR 150 crore to come over the next ~2 years to fund capex for the Westin - Tribute Bangalore development.

subsections.label: New project pipeline announcements during FY26
points: Partnership with Ingka Centers (part of IKEA Group) for a 162-room upscale hotel at Sector 51 Noida, structured as a long-term variable lease, strengthening Delhi NCR presence through a capital-efficient model.
Secured a lease in a marquee under-development project in Hyderabad, One Financial District, for a 260-room hotel combining lifestyle retail, office, and hotel.

Resolved the Navi Mumbai litigation and announced development of the company's largest hotel project to date — a 700-room combination of Westin and Fairfield by Marriott, with potential revenue of ~INR 325 crore at current market RevPAR.

Board approval sought (as of yesterday) to add a 135-room Marriott hotel in Sriperumbudur, alongside the existing operating Fairfield by Marriott which has achieved an asset-level ROCE of more than 30%.

subsections.label: RARE India acquisition
points: Entered the experiential leisure segment through acquisition of a 70% stake in RARE India, a curated platform of 73 hotels and 1,000 rooms, currently under discussion for an affiliation with Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy.

subsections.label: Committed pipeline of new openings
points: Beginning with HITEC City Hyderabad at the end of FY27, followed by the Tribute portfolio at Bangalore Whitefield at the end of FY28, then Westin at Bangalore Whitefield, the upscale hotel at Ingka Noida, and the new Marriott Sriperumbudur Chennai in FY29-FY30.

subsections.label: Hyatt Regency Pune preopening status clarification
points: 22 new apartments at Hyatt Regency Pune are ready but awaiting final regulatory approvals — the hotel itself is operating fully; only these additional apartments remain classified as preopening.

subsections.label: Bangalore micro-market dynamics
points: SAMHI's Bangalore presence is in Outer Ring Road, where new hotels are opening this year; expansion/growth guidance for that asset has been moderated given the large opening over the next 12 months.

Second Bangalore investment is in Whitefield (Tribute and Westin); Whitefield has absorbed a lot of supply over the last decade and new supply growth is not material relative to the existing base there.

New Bangalore supply is concentrated in the corridor between the airport and Hebbal (~25km, including Manyata Tech Park) — where SAMHI has zero presence; more than half of future Bangalore supply is estimated to be in that corridor.
Similar micro-market dynamics apply to Hyderabad — many new-supply announcements are not in the precinct where SAMHI has current or proposed inventory.

Demand/supply must be evaluated at micro-market level, not city level; current supply base and percentage growth in Tier-1 markets is not seen as a threat, though continued caution and micro-market-level evaluation is warranted.
