subsections.label: Capital recycling philosophy
points: Asset recycling is a long-term strategic tool, not opportunistic, driven by ensuring assets deliver higher ROCE, protect ROCE, and continue to contribute earnings growth.

Evaluation considers both ROCE on depreciated book value and ROCE/opportunity cost on the underlying market value of an asset; if market value implies low ROCE on current income but redeployment can achieve mid-to-high-teens ROCE elsewhere, the asset becomes a recycling candidate.

Minority dilution (like the GIC deal) is a separate, longer-term strategic decision typically used to monetize value created in an asset (e.g., Courtyard Fairfield Bangalore, where 35% was diluted, booking a profit and securing the base for perpetuity) — management declined to speculate further on this mechanism.
Recycling target is confirmed to be more than the earlier residual INR 100 crore, now estimated at INR 200-250 crore over the next 2 years, largely via single-asset sales.

Recycling activity is restricted to non-core hotels only (e.g., Caspia Delhi, Ahmedabad, Chennai) — not core assets like Courtyard Bangalore, Sheraton Hyderabad, or Hyatt Regency Pune; the practice is described as periodic capital-discipline review, not active trading of hotels.

Example: Caspia Delhi sold for INR 63 crore against an EBITDA contribution of only ~INR 1.5-2 crore; redeployed capital (fungible) is expected to guarantee double-digit ROCE in assets like W Hyderabad, providing a large margin of safety versus the risk of new deployment underperforming.

subsections.label: No further subsidiary-level platform investment planned currently
points: No plan as of date for further capital infusions into the subsidiary (GIC) platform at a subsidiary level; near-term focus is on recycling a few small hotels valued at ~INR 200 crore in total.

subsections.label: Shareholder capital return consideration
points: Analyst raised the idea of a sustained buyback given the earnings ramp and stock discount to sector; management responded that capital allocation follows a stated waterfall: (1) deleveraging to 2.5x net debt-to-EBITDA (justified by long-tenor ~12-year debt with little principal repayment pressure for 3-5 years and financing cost down to 7.9%), (2) ensuring adequate/slightly more than adequate capex buffer for growth given cost overrun/inflation risk, (3) continuing to pursue India growth opportunities including leases, and (4) if surplus capital remains, the Board will consider a disciplined mechanism to return capital directly to shareholders — an evolving Board-level discussion (referenced on Slide 16).

subsections.label: One-time macro disruptions across FY26
points: India-Pakistan conflict (Operation Sindoor) in May.
Unusually severe monsoons and flooding in core markets in August.
Airline disruption in December.
Middle East (Gulf) conflict in March, which continues, with residual impact through April and encouraging recovery starting in May.
Combined, these compressed full-year revenue by ~INR 45-52 crore.

subsections.label: West Asia / Gulf crisis specifics
points: Impact described as inbound FIT cancellations, near land cruise, and MENA-related; impact continued through April with solid recovery signs starting in May.
Long-haul international travel resumption is occurring but flying time has increased to ~20 hours, impacting small-meeting travelers.

subsections.label: GST regulatory change — permanent margin impact
points: Move of hotel GST slab from 12% with input credit to 5% without input tax credit is viewed as a permanent reduction to margins on an absolute basis; company expects to maintain 38%+ margins despite this, given pipeline concentration in upscale assets less exposed to sub-INR 7,500 room sales.

subsections.label: Interest rate risk
points: News in the market suggests the interest rate cycle may see an upward revision due to currency weakness; company has factored in a 15-25 bps increase into FY27 interest cost guidance.

subsections.label: Construction / spillover risk
points: Analyst flagged spillover risk in terms of construction delay across the announced pipeline projects; management response emphasized separation of operating and growth teams and strong governance/guardrails on new developments (discount-to-replacement cost, mid-teens ROCE underwriting, avoiding long-lead greenfield assets).

subsections.label: Volatility / global uncertainty caveat
points: Management repeatedly cautioned that the world remains volatile ('bombs are flying around the world') and that double-digit growth, while not currently at alarming threat, requires continued vigilant monitoring.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook build
points: FY27 builds from the FY26 base with confidence in delivering 9-11% same-store revenue growth with healthy margin expansion, on top of ongoing contribution from assets opened during FY26.
GST impact will be normalized from Q3 FY27 onward as a year-ago basis resets.
Confident of contributions coming from W Hyderabad in the near term.

With GIC platform providing institutional capital firepower, the Ingka partnership adding a marquee Delhi NCR asset on variable lease, and the RARE India platform giving capital-efficient entry into the experiential leisure segment, SAMHI is positioned to compound free cash, expand the portfolio in core markets, and transform the P&L through multiple big-box assets in the pipeline without taking incremental leverage or diluting equity.

subsections.label: Long-term revenue guidance discipline
points: Since IPO, only two long-term guidances have been given: revenue growth of 9-11% (held consistently through market highs and lows) and net debt-to-EBITDA target of 2.5x.
Management emphasized that long-term guidance should remain stable and factor in disruptive events rather than being revised reactively.

subsections.label: Net debt-to-EBITDA trajectory
points: Currently at 3x net debt-to-EBITDA; absent interruptions during the year, this would have already reached the high-2x zip code (2.8-2.9x).
Company precisely reported ~3.07x; guidance maintained that leverage stabilizes at 2.5x within another 12-18 months.

subsections.label: Margin guidance context
points: 38% margin guidance for FY27/28 already factors in the permanent GST impact; excluding GST, margins would be upwards of 40% at group level.

Reported margins are expected to keep rising on a normalized basis each year since incremental inventory being added is predominantly upscale, where fewer rooms are sold below the INR 7,500 GST threshold — structurally securing 40%+ reported margins over time, subject to market-specific risk (e.g., upscale in Ahmedabad carries more risk of sub-INR 7,500 sales than mid-scale in Hyderabad/Bangalore).

subsections.label: Upside scenario framing
points: FY26 could have been a 15-16% revenue growth year absent renovation-related disruption and external crises.
If Gulf prices settle down (even if it takes another 3 months), there is a fair bit of upside potential this year beyond the 9-11% base case.

Current EBITDA growth, cash flow generation, and targeted leverage plans are all built on just the 9-11% revenue growth assumption; any upside beyond that would substantially improve EBITDA growth and margins, flowing straight to free cash with a snowball effect.
Management stated it maintains caution on guidance (downside protection) while working for upside, especially given global volatility.

guidance_ledger.statement: Overall revenue growth should be underwritten in the zip code of about 10% to 11% Y-o-Y for FY27, with caution that the current crisis may continue.
Company remains absolutely confident of maintaining a 9% to 11% total revenue growth from same-store hotels in the long term — guidance held since IPO.
Margins expected to be around 38% or so, factoring in the permanent GST impact; group level margin should be maintained at 38%-plus.
Company maintains guidance that net debt-to-EBITDA will stabilize at 2.5x; given another 12-18 months, should be in that zip code.
Cash interest expense computed at about INR 127 crore, but guiding towards INR 135-140 crore factoring in a 15-20 bps rate increase.

Allocated about INR 250 crore to INR 270 crore of capital capex for FY27, largely towards W Hyderabad (~INR 150 crore), Westin Bangalore work, maintenance, and minor renovations at Four Points Pune and Jaipur (~INR 15-20 crore).
Expect to maintain a similar zip code of capex (~INR 250-270 crore per year run rate), majority directed towards Westin Bangalore.
Commitment to fully fund the INR 2,200 crore of capex across the existing pipeline, including Navi Mumbai.

Base free cash flow held flat over 5 years produces ~INR 1,550 crore; layering same-store revenue growth (9-11% lower end) adds ~INR 1,000 crore more; with new openings, cumulative free cash post interest exceeds INR 3,000 crore over FY27-31.
Same-store hotels expected to comfortably grow 9% to 10% year-on-year for FY27 given the reset base.
W Hyderabad expected to bring, on current revenue run-rate basis, almost 6% to 7% growth for FY28.
NCR expected to come back to mid-teens revenue growth in the current fiscal year following Hyatt Place Gurgaon renovation completion.
Current pool of assets is well geared to get to the targeted 14% to 15% ROCE with very little risk.
Group ROCE profile expected to be maintained in the mid-teens zip code even with a lot of new hotel openings, aided by variable leases and land value pre-accounted for.
Asset recycling target is more than the residual INR 100 crore, estimated at about INR 200 crore to INR 250 crore, largely through sale of single non-core assets.
Balance GIC investment of INR 150 crore expected to come over the next 2-year period, in line with capex spending on Westin - Tribute Bangalore development.

As free cash flow compounds beyond committed growth requirements, the Board intends to evaluate a disciplined mechanism to return capital directly to shareholders in a manner consistent with long-term value creation.
Company expects to structurally secure its place at 40%-plus reported margins over time, given incremental investments/openings are predominantly upscale in strong markets.

New competitor announcements (e.g., a Westin in Bangalore) noted; management maintains current supply growth is concentrated in specific micro-markets (airport-Hebbal corridor in Bangalore) where SAMHI has zero presence, and that demand/supply should be evaluated at micro-market rather than city level.

Management repeatedly cautioned that 'the world is volatile' and 'bombs are flying around the world,' requiring continued vigilant monitoring even though double-digit growth is not currently seen as an alarming threat.

themes.label: Revenue growth resilience amid disruptions
themes.note: 12.3% FY26 revenue growth achieved despite a sequence of one-off disruptions (India-Pakistan conflict, monsoons, airline disruption, Middle East conflict) that compressed revenue by INR 45-52 crore.

themes.label: GST margin impact
themes.note: GST slab change from 12% (with input credit) to 5% (without) is viewed as a permanent margin drag, with impact per room sold below INR 7,500 regardless of segment; company guides 38% margin for FY27/28 despite this.

themes.label: Deleveraging and balance sheet strength
themes.note: Net debt reduced by INR 516 crore to INR 1,450 crore, net debt-to-EBITDA at ~3x with a 2.5x medium-term target, credit rating upgraded to A+ Stable.

themes.label: Free cash flow compounding / capital allocation discipline
themes.note: FY26 free cash flow of ~INR 300 crore is expected to compound to more than INR 3,000 crore cumulative over FY27-31, funding capex, deleveraging, growth and eventual shareholder returns per a structured waterfall.

themes.label: Capital-efficient growth via variable leases and GIC platform
themes.note: GIC platform (INR 750 crore for 35% stake), Ingka Noida variable lease, and Marriott Sriperumbudur land-free addition all support asset-light, high-ROCE growth without incremental leverage or equity dilution.

themes.label: Asset recycling as capital discipline
themes.note: Company has recycled ~INR 960 crore of capital over 3 years and targets a further INR 200-250 crore of non-core asset sales over the next 2 years to redeploy into higher-ROCE opportunities.

themes.label: Micro-market supply/demand dynamics in core cities
themes.note: Bangalore and Hyderabad supply growth is concentrated in specific micro-markets where SAMHI has limited or no exposure, reducing saturation risk to its existing portfolio positions.

key_takeaways: The company delivered a profit before tax of circa INR 165 crores, which was 89% growth over last year.

At the start of FY26, we set 2 specific commitments to our shareholders: A, delivered revenue growth in the range of 9% to 11% and two, bring the balance sheet to a net debt-to-EBITDA of approximately 3x. Despite revenue disruptions and active future growth, we have delivered both as revenue growth came in at 12.3% for the year, anchored to commercial demand in our core market, total income at INR 1,279 crores. And we ended the year with a net debt at INR 1,450 crores, translating to a net debt-to-EBITDA of about 3x.

These onetime events compressed our full year revenue by approximately INR 45 crores to INR 52 crores, leading to revenue growth being diluted from a potential of 16% to 17% to an actual reported number of 12.3%.

We formally launched our GIC platform for upscale hotels in India committing approximately INR 750 crores for a 35% minority stake in a 1,000-room platform. Of this INR 600 crores has already been received with the balance to come over the next 2-odd years to find capex for the Westin - Tribute Bangalore development.

We also resolved the Navi Mumbai litigation and announced the development of our largest hotel project to date, a 700-room combination of Westin and Fairfield by Marriott with a potential revenue of almost INR 325 crores on current market RevPAR.
This year, we also entered the experiential leisure segment through an acquisition of a 70% stake in RARE India, which is a curated platform of 73 hotels and 1,000 rooms.

Consolidated EBITDA for FY26 was INR 463 crores, up 8.8% on a year-on-year reported basis with an EBITDA margin at 36.2%. Adjusted for the impact on account of the GST changes, this would have been circa 13% year-on-year growth.
Adjusted for these items, FY26 EBITDA growth would have come in line of 19% to 20% with margins of 38% plus.

The combination of consistent same-store revenue growth, further levers for improved margins, decline in finance costs and fully capitalized growth pipeline gave us a free cash flow generation of approximately INR 300 crores in FY26, after both interest and Lease Minimum Guarantee payments.
So FY26 was a year that SAMHI free cash flow generation became real and FY27 onwards is the year that free cash compounds.

First, continue deleveraging towards a medium to long-term net debt-to-EBITDA target approximately 2.5x. Second, the commitment to fully fund the INR 2,200 crores of capex across the existing pipeline, including Navi Mumbai. Third, retain investable surplus for tactical mergers and acquisitions and adding long-term variable leases where returns are very accretive, And fourth, as free cash flow compounds beyond our committed growth requirements, the Board intends to evaluate disciplined mechanism to return capital directly to shareholders in a manner consistent with long-term value creation.
pressing_questions: So Karan, cumulative QTD quarter-till-date is tracking double-digit revenue growth... How is 1Q FY27 looking so in terms of booking and MICE activities?

So on the GST impact, it seems like GST is more like a permanent reduction in margin since the rules are unlikely to change. So in light of this, what margins are you expecting in FY27, 28 and how would those margins look like prior to the GST implication?
Given the kind of pipeline that you have in FY27 and beyond, is there a spillover risk in terms of construction delay in any of these project in pipeline?
I was just trying to adjust the EBITDA margin in 4Q for the crisis... Our EBITDA margin is at about 38.4%... So are we kind of facing any operational headwinds on the cost side?
The variable lease hotels that we have announced in Hyderabad and Noida, now given these are long-term leases, will the rent get capitalized on the balance sheet? Or will it be expensed into the P&L?

Sir, in the presentation, we have mentioned that due to the GST change, the number of room nights sold for less than INR 7,500 have increased quite a bit. But if I look at the occupancy of the upper mid-scale and mid-scale assets that we have given in the PPT, that figure is more or less constant. So I was just trying to think through what has happened exactly?
Where do you see in terms of your ROCE target in FY31 and your net debt-to-EBITDA? And how are you going to fund this INR 2,200 crores of capex over the next 5 years?

Isn't there a risk to invest the money that you generate from the sale of assets into a newer venture? Is there a significant delta that you can capture in terms of ROCE to take that risk...Isn't there a trade-off in terms of taking that risk?

Given your performance and ramps in earnings trading at a massive discount to sector...would it make sense for management to consider carving out a small amount of capital for buybacks on a sustained basis?

key_takeaways: Near-term profitability is being intentionally traded for scaling Hotels and building AI-native workflows/products; management explicitly rejects quarter-by-quarter margin optimization.
Buses is the current profit/growth anchor (largest CM, high CM%), with tangible differentiation via reliability programs and state-transport integrations.
Flights face real near-term volume risk from capacity cuts and fare inflation; Ixigo is still gaining share, but the 'next billion user' upgrade funnel is temporarily impaired.
Trains remain policy-constrained, but Ixigo is consolidating share and raising CM% via cost discipline and ancillary monetization (Zoop meals, metro, tour packages).
Hotels is now in an 'invest-to-scale' phase with strong captive cross-sell (90% from existing users) and a meaningful supply push (10k direct hotels, RevYStay stake, flexible inventory).

AI strategy is economics-driven (model routing, proprietary 'hardness,' intent intelligence via Tara), with management explicitly preparing investors for front-loaded tech costs before benefits appear.

quarters.summary: Management framed FY26 as a stress test in a noisy, unpredictable and turbulent environment, with the group becoming more diversified, more resilient and more balanced via multimodal mix (Flights #1 by GTV, Buses #1 by contribution margin in Q4). The company is repositioning from OTA to "Peace of Mind" business with AI-native reinvention (ixigo NEXT) to prevent "de-distribution," while near-term headwinds remain concentrated in trains (policy + supply), with buses benefiting from substitution as flights get expensive and trains remain supply constrained. FY27 Q1 base effects are expected to ease versus the Kumbh-heavy Q4 base, and management continues to prioritize absolute contribution margin/EBITDA rupees over CM% optimization, with capital allocation from the Prosus fundraise proceeding without urgency over a couple of years.

Product moat focus ('peace of mind products') includes breakdown assistance ('cab that comes and takes you to the destination'), 'Abhi Assured' service-level guarantee, and '360 bus views.'
Inventory parity: management said earlier supply gaps are largely closed — 'pretty much at parity… operators that matter… all partnered with us' with 6,000+ operators and 4,500+ transacting monthly.

subsections.label: Flights — market share gains despite weak aviation environment

International exposure: outbound was 'more than 20% of GTV' in Q3; Q4 expected 'not far off.'

subsections.label: Trains (ConfirmTkt/ixigo trains) — policy/supply headwinds; strategic feeder engine
points: Root causes are industry/policy, not company-specific: Indian Railways changes include more restrictive time periods for Tatkal access, reduced waitlist inventory, user re-verification for repeat users, Aadhaar verification norms, plus peak-period supply constraints (esp. 2S/second seater).
Despite volume pressure, ixigo claims OTA share rose to 62% vs 60% a few quarters ago.

Potential catalysts: optimism that constraints may ease with upgraded PRS rollout 'later this year' (Aug/Sep referenced) and possible revisiting of Tatkal windows; optional upside if unreserved ticketing opens to OTAs (not committed).

Strategic stance: CFO stated they can gain more share but choose not to — 'Can I gain more market share in trains… yes. Do I want to…? Answer is, no.' They view trains as a premium, convenience-led product and a high-intent user cohort to monetize via adjacencies (cross-sell).

subsections.label: Hotels — deliberate build; not yet ready to disclose as a segment
points: Management is 'excited but disciplined,' building direct supply via HELLO (AI-based hotel extranet) and a 'small on-the-ground team.'
Explicit disclosure policy: will report hotels separately only after 'product-market fit, operational maturity, and meaningful scale.'
Differentiation thesis: 'not about chasing transaction volume before trust is earned,' focusing on fulfilment reliability / post-book experience — consistent with the 'peace of mind' positioning.
No hotel-related cost capitalization (explicitly confirmed).

subsections.label: 'Peace of Mind' operating metrics (service quality as a growth lever)

subsections.label: Architecture (as described)
points: Fusion of: a proprietary small language model trained on years of voice data ('TARA' voice intelligence); deep traveller context + memory (short/long-term); real-time supply intelligence (inventory/disruptions/refunds); proprietary intelligence stack (pricing/discounting/reco/prediction/automation).
UI approach: hybrid conversational + traditional UI; 'every screen… readable by AI… navigable… actionable.'

3 layers: Layer 0 — traditional UI made AI-ready; Layer 1 — ambient intelligence across the app; Layer -1 — 'contextual and Ephemeral UX' that 'magically appears' when relevant (trip-active mode becomes a real-time OS).

subsections.label: Agentic execution (intended automation)
points: Agents intended to autonomously execute workflows: automatically checking you in, fare tracking, refund management, booking reconfirmations, trip monitoring, disruption handling.

subsections.label: Early signals and financial impact

Strategic bet: AI makes apps easier for less tech-savvy cohorts; 'democratizes apps.'

Metro ticketing launched for Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru.
Brand asset: multi-year 'ixigo New Delhi Metro station' branding at NDLS.

quarters.summary: Titan reported another quarter of strong, all-round growth across brands and businesses in Q1 FY'27 despite a not-so-favourable operating environment; management flagged one-off customs duty and MTM accounting gains inflating jewellery margins this quarter (to reverse over the next 2-3 quarters), reiterated the ~11% EBIT margin center of gravity for TMZ jewellery, reiterated commitment to double-digit healthy jewellery value growth toward FY30 Investor Day goals, and highlighted that Damas (Core business, Dubai/GCC) is loss-making currently due to regional war-related footfall/ticket-size declines while the rest of the international portfolio remains profitable at mid-single-digit EBIT margin.

subsections.label: One-off items affecting reported margins
points: Gains from customs duty rate increase (6% to 15%) will be realized as inventory gets sold over the next couple of quarters; consolidated realization this quarter was ₹407 crores (₹386 crores in Tanishq Mia Zoya, ₹21 crores in CaratLane).

Sudden and sharp customs duty change caused market volatility with divergence between international and domestic gold prices; company was advancing gold procurement to secure supply for festive demand, causing accounting MTM gain in inventory that lifted jewellery division EBIT by 75-80 bps; this MTM gain is expected to reverse in coming quarters.
Normalized EBIT margin for TMZ business, excluding both customs duty and MTM gains, was 10.9% for the quarter.

Base quarter (Q1 FY26) had its own 50 bps one-time benefit; adjusting for that, comparable base margin becomes 11.3% versus current 10.9%, implying a 40 bps GC margin erosion driven by gold price impact playing out over the last 4 quarters despite good studded growth.

MTM gains/losses arise from the difference between inventory valuation (on international benchmark, as there is no domestic spot benchmark) and hedge valuation (on domestic market); this is normally a small, manageable BAU variation each quarter, but became pronounced this quarter due to the wide gap created by the customs duty change and elevated procurement.

Reversal of the MTM/customs duty gains will happen gradually over the next 2-3 quarters as inventories are sold and gains/losses crystallize; company does not want to take credit for the gain now since the opposite situation (customs duty going down) would reverse it; will explicitly call out the impact in future quarters to allow it to be netted off.

Watches division: standard costing revaluation of inventory is run every Q1; last year (Q1 FY26) this benefit was about ₹50 crores; this quarter the benefit was far less, making reported EBIT growth look muted versus revenue growth; normalized margin was 17.8% versus 18.6% normalized in Q1 FY26.

Reclassification: color stone jewellery, previously clubbed under studded category, has been reclassified into gold jewellery so that studded now reflects only diamond jewellery (not Colorstone/Polki); reclassified numbers for previous periods have been shared for comparability.

subsections.label: International business / Damas profitability
points: Damas Core business was not loss-making at the time of acquisition, but the current regional war situation has made jewellery purchase a low priority in Dubai, Saudi and other GCC countries, causing footfall and ticket sizes to fall; a business previously operating at 20-30% margin levels can turn loss-making when volumes fall that much.

Rest of the international portfolio (excluding Damas) continues to deliver mid-single-digit (5-6%) EBIT margin; Damas' contribution to the overall international business (~₹6,000 crore run-rate) will not be very high, so overall international portfolio is still expected to deliver positive EBIT for the full year.
Damas performance is contingent on the geopolitical situation; management expects rapid improvement once the situation eases.

subsections.label: Subsidiary margin trajectories (TEAL and CaratLane)
points: TEAL remains a project-based business with lumpiness in margins; this quarter had a substantial contribution from servicing business (refitting/retrofitting of equipment), boosting margin; normalized margin is expected to gradually gravitate to 12-15/16% over the medium to long term, though full-year margin this year could be higher.

CaratLane delivered ~9.6% (approx. 9% and above) EBIT margin this quarter; trajectory should stabilize toward double-digit (10%) EBIT margin similar to Tanishq, with potential to progress to 11% or stay around that number longer term depending on gold price dynamics in the jewellery industry; quarter-to-quarter variation expected.

Both TEAL and CaratLane are still on a significant growth path with substantial opportunity to grow; management will continue to prioritize top-line growth over margin optimization in both, so margins will play out as a consequence of growth strategy rather than being actively managed to a target.

subsections.label: Jewellery demand recovery (May-June dynamics)
points: Key dates: May 10 - PM call-out on gold; May 13 - customs duty change; May 17 - Adhik Maas began; overlap of these events caused softness in consumer sentiment for about 3 weeks till end of May.

By beginning of June, demand picked up and weddings restarted post Adhik Maas; management believes what was lost in May was regained in June (deferment, not lost demand), and this normalization has already fully played out within Q1 - no expected spillover/trickle into Q2.
Studded jewellery resurgence, which began in Q4 FY26, continued into Q1 FY27; momentum from Q4 continued through Akshaya Tritiya, with a brief lull in May that recovered in June.
Buyer growth on the studded portfolio has been rising continuously since Q4 of last year - highlighted as the heartening part of the story.

Towards end of July (outside Q1 scope), some softness was observed on the plain gold side as gold prices were range-bound and consumers heard mixed news about gold direction, causing some to wait; in the last 2-3 days before the call, an upward gold price movement was observed. This softness/wait-and-see behavior was largely on plain gold jewellery, not studded.

subsections.label: Buyer growth and gold price sensitivity
points: Buyer growth of 5% reported for the quarter, with a good period in April and June and dampened sentiment in May - this is an average for the entire quarter.
Stable or marginally rising gold rates support positive sentiment and buyer conversion; volatile or persistently declining gold rates lead buyers to wait on the fence without urgency.

Management does not want to draw conclusions from a single month (June) in isolation, citing regional differences (Adhik Maas is more a North India phenomenon, not South) and it being too early to assess a durable trend between buyer growth and value growth as gold price inflation normalizes.

If Y-o-Y gold price inflation goes to zero (e.g., by Q4), a structural query was raised on whether the targeted 18-20% top-line growth band can be sustained; management's approach in such a scenario would be to go all out to acquire buyers and drive growth, but acknowledged this could affect growth rates versus the targeted band; medium to long term view of strong double-digit growth toward FY30 targets remains unchanged.

Gold coin growth (which had been running ahead of overall jewellery growth) is expected to start moderating from current levels going forward, per management expectation, though concluding gold price is now on a firm downward trajectory is seen as premature given recent upward movement in prices over the last 2-3 days.

subsections.label: Exchange schemes and cash-for-gold
points: Company rolled out 'cash for gold' (converting customer's own gold into cash, not jewellery exchange) across all stores from June; traction so far has not been significant, but it remains available as a customer solution.

The economics of gold-for-gold exchange include a deduction taken when gold is brought in for exchange, which offsets/nullifies any margin dilution, making the scheme margin-neutral versus outright sale.

Exchange (both gold bought elsewhere and gold originally bought at Tanishq) continues to be a major driver of customer acquisition, with total sale involving exchange exceeding 50% of the business - a sustaining trend.

Exchange share in procurement saw a temporary upswing (~3 weeks in May) after the PM's call-out when other jewellers also went into overdrive on exchange communication; it has since normalized. Company advised against reading a specific sequential margin trend into this.
Company has been investing significantly behind exchange communication since September of the prior year.

subsections.label: Gold savings schemes (Golden Harvest / Rivaah Golden Advantage)
points: New sign-ups for Golden Harvest and Rivaah Golden Advantage are tracking broadly in line with jewellery business growth on a value basis.

A shift in customer preference is occurring from Golden Harvest toward Rivaah Golden Advantage, as the latter helps with rupee cost averaging and was designed to address gold rate volatility; considered a positive shift for the customer.

subsections.label: Diamond jewellery and Festival of Diamonds (FOD) offer
points: Current FOD offer is a flat 20% off on diamond value, largely unchanged from the prior offer in Jan/Feb; some aged products may carry a higher discount, but the overall offer structure has not changed materially.

CaratLane responded quickly with an attractive offer following the PM's announcement and subsequent events; May second half and June were described as record performance for CaratLane, helping counter an initial negative impression; no significant structural change in overall discount levels.
Natural diamond prices (both solitaires and smaller diamonds) have shown more stability in the last 6 months, at both sourcing and retail/consumer levels.

The lab-grown vs. natural diamond narrative has stabilized in the market - the previously prominent narrative favoring lab-grown has diminished, and pricing plus sentiment/narrative for both categories has stabilized, coinciding with studded growth improving.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: No substantial increase or easing observed in competitive intensity for plain gold jewellery making charges over the last 2-3 years; intensity has generally been on an upward trend without recent easing despite gold price stabilization.

Competitive intensity varies significantly by region, with certain geographies (e.g., Gujarat) showing much higher intensity than others over the last 2-3 years; no broad national-level increase or decrease to specifically call out.

Company believes it has built a 'playbook' from having experienced multiple scenarios over the last 2-3 years (high discounting competitive intensity, stable/rising/falling gold rates), enabling it to respond to new situations, though acknowledges new scenarios could still require fresh learning.

subsections.label: Long-term growth ambition and market share headroom
points: Management reiterated a target of healthy double-digit aggressive growth for jewellery, consistent with commitments made at the Investor Day; this target/ambition is unchanged regardless of how buyer/ticket size/gold price dynamics play out in any given quarter.

Company's market share in jewellery is still single digit, implying substantial headroom for growth, driven by India's continuing love for gold and the broader India growth story - not just for the industry but specifically for the company.

Growth headroom cited as high across all businesses (jewellery, eyecare, watches, fragrances, bags, sarees) due to tailwinds of formalization, India's growth story, middle India, multiple consumption segments, portfolio play, and premiumization.

Specific jewellery growth levers reiterated: market share gains via regionalization, high-value studded, retail transformation, brand differentiation, portfolio play, and core growth in both studded and gold in the sub-₹50,000 and sub-₹1 lakh price points through buyer growth.

subsections.label: External and macro headwinds
points: Operating environment during the quarter was described as not favorable, though results still turned out well.

Sudden customs duty rate change (6% to 15%) created market volatility with international-domestic gold price divergence, requiring advanced gold procurement to secure festive demand supply, which in turn caused an accounting MTM impact.

Consumer sentiment softness for about 3 weeks (mid-May to end-May) due to overlapping events: PM's call-out on gold (May 10), customs duty change (May 13), and start of Adhik Maas (May 17), an inauspicious period for weddings/purchases.

Gold price volatility and uncertain trajectory continue to be a key swing factor for both consumer sentiment/buyer behavior and jewellery division margins; sharp intraday/day-to-day price swings ($100-200) observed.

Damas Core business (Dubai/GCC) is impacted by the ongoing regional war/geopolitical situation, causing reduced footfall and ticket sizes, turning the business loss-making versus its prior profitable state at acquisition; recovery is contingent on the geopolitical situation easing.
End-of-July softness observed in plain gold jewellery demand due to range-bound/volatile gold prices and mixed market narratives leading some buyers to wait; this is outside the Q1 reporting period.
Rising competitive intensity from increasing numbers of brands, stores and players in the jewellery category, sustained discounting behavior varying by geography and segment.

key_figures.label: TMZ jewellery EBIT margin center of gravity

subsections.label: Margin guidance reaffirmation
points: Management is not giving fresh guidance on jewellery EBIT growth or margin at this point; reiterated ~11% as the 'center of gravity' for jewellery business margin, with plus/minus variation depending on many moving parts including uncertain gold price trajectory.

Company declined to provide a full-year quantification of the customs duty benefit, noting it will come through in Q2 and Q3 as well, but wants to explicitly qualify and net off such one-offs each time rather than take credit, since a future customs duty decrease would create the opposite (negative) effect.

Levers seen as capable of helping margin move closer to the ~11% center of gravity over the full year: product mix shift toward studded, lower karatage jewellery acceptability (positive for margin), various gross-margin enhancing programs (War-on-Waste, alloy work, GC Max program, sourcing strategies) expected to bear more fruit in H2 than H1, product mix improvement as coin share potentially declines, and opportunity for a more profitable mix with higher AMCs if gold prices stay subdued.

Reiterated FY30 targets set at the Investor Day remain unchanged; medium-to-long-term double-digit growth trajectory is the basis for reaching those FY30 numbers, even though quarter-on-quarter numbers can fluctuate due to situational factors.
Overall Q1 growth momentum and July trends (described as 'not bad') give management increased positivity that FY27 growth could match or better the trajectory promised at the Investor Day.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are not giving any guidance at this point of time. In the Investor Day and prior, we have said that more of 11% being the center of gravity for jewellery business margin, we would be around that plus/minus something can happen.
We are committed to a double-digit healthy growth in value in the jewellery business. So that's the only way we'll get to our committed FY30 goals that we've said.
It will come in Q2 as well as in Q3, but I would rather refrain from giving a full year impact at this point of time.
The normalized margin would be gradually gravitating towards 12% to 15%, 16%. This year, full year basis, they can be higher.

Their normal trajectory should be towards 10%... in the long term, even depending on how the jewellery industry gold price dynamics work out, they can either progress towards 11% or stay around that number.
I would expect overall portfolio would still turn out to be positive EBIT performance for the full year.
Damas is contingent upon the current situation. As soon as that situation gets over, I'm sure they will also improve pretty rapidly.

guidance_ledger.metric: Jewellery growth rate under zero gold price inflation scenario
guidance_ledger.statement: Overall, medium to long term, we have always said that a good strong double-digit growth. And that is how you will reach to that FY30 number. So that has not changed at all in our mind.

guidance_ledger.metric: Gold coin growth (relative to jewellery growth)
guidance_ledger.statement: The kind of growth Y-o-Y coin was showing, it should start moderating from here.

We have said between 15% to 20% growth for Jewellery; that holds good and we hope to do that and maybe do a bit better; this is a general guidance for growth irrespective of gold rate over a 3-5 year horizon.

Idea is that if we are growing revenue 15% to 20%, can we grow EBIT also at least a little bit lower than revenue; sustainability of the 11-11.5% margin band depends on gold price trajectory; more informed view to be given at Investor Day in June first week.
Plan to scale up beYon to 10-12 stores in two to three cities, currently at two stores, hopefully getting a bunch of stores in place well in Q1 itself, before planning a national launch.
Damas consolidation started from January; increased disclosure expected as visibility improves; from next year onward comparisons will be available to assess growth of revenue and margin of Damas.
Work underway to bring in more buyer growth particularly in sub-₹10,000 price band category; some of that will start showing up in the next few months.

risk_register.note: Sharp intraday/day-to-day swings ($100-200) and international-domestic price divergence following customs duty change created accounting MTM impact and consumer sentiment uncertainty.

War situation reduced footfall and ticket sizes in Dubai/Saudi, turning previously profitable Damas Core business loss-making; recovery contingent on situation easing.
Range-bound/volatile gold prices and mixed market narratives caused some buyers to wait on plain gold jewellery purchases toward end of July, outside Q1 scope.

Coin growth (previously outpacing jewellery growth) expected to start moderating, though a firm downward gold price trajectory is seen as premature to conclude.
Some slowness picked up from customs viewpoint due to delay in DGFT import license renewal; company says it is well covered for Q1 with gold exchange program and back-up plans.
March month was quite disturbed in GCC where Damas and Tanishq operate, contributing to the ₹82 crore Q4 international loss; situation remains evolving/unpredictable.
Elevated and rising gold prices pressure product mix and margin sustainability in TMZ domestic business (10-20 bps margin loss noted); difficult to guarantee sustainability if gold keeps rising.
Competition, including organized players adding stores across geographies, described as 'business as usual', not seen as a growing concern.
Wedding purchase preponement due to gold price fears creates month-to-month/quarter-to-quarter noise but not viewed as a structural risk to multi-year growth guidance.
Legacy ERP to Oracle Fusion migration caused operational challenges in Jan-mid Feb impacting Valentine's fulfillment; viewed as a blip based on strong December and April performance.
EBIT margin suppressed YoY due to increased marketing spend and a one-off inventory recall of slow-moving stock, despite 16-17% revenue growth.

themes.label: Gold price volatility
themes.note: Sharp gold price swings and customs duty change caused international-domestic price divergence, MTM accounting gains, and consumer sentiment fluctuations across May-July.

themes.label: Jewellery growth guidance (15-20%)
themes.note: Management reiterated commitment to healthy double-digit jewellery value growth toward FY30 goals regardless of quarterly gold price fluctuations.

themes.label: International expansion (Damas/GCC)
themes.note: Damas Core business turned loss-making due to war-related footfall and ticket size declines in Dubai/Saudi, though rest of international portfolio remains profitable at 5-6% EBIT margin.

themes.label: Category accessibility initiatives (exchange, lightweight, low-carat)
themes.note: Cash-for-gold rolled out from June, exchange remains margin-neutral and drives over 50% of business, with continued focus on lightweight and multi-karatage jewellery for accessibility.

themes.label: Market share and industry formalization
themes.note: Company's single-digit market share in jewellery cited as substantial headroom for growth via regionalization, retail transformation, brand differentiation and portfolio play.

themes.label: Studded/diamond jewellery momentum
themes.note: Studded resurgence that began in Q4 FY26 continued into Q1 FY27 with rising buyer growth; FOD discount structure largely unchanged and natural diamond prices/narrative have stabilized.

themes.label: Subsidiary margin trajectory (TEAL/CaratLane)
themes.note: CaratLane delivered ~9.6% EBIT margin trending toward double-digit; TEAL margin lumpy due to project/servicing mix but trending toward 12-16% normalized.

key_takeaways: It's been another fantastic quarter, and I must say this quarter has been even better than the previous quarters. We've seen all-round growth across all our businesses, all our brands, subsidiaries.

We had during this quarter, gains on account of customs duty rate increase from 6% to 15%... overall at a consolidated level realization of ₹407 crores, ₹386 crores was in Tanishq Mia Zoya portfolio and ₹21 crores was in CaratLane.
The normalized margin considering both custom duty gain and MTM gain, the normalized EBIT margin for our Tanishq Mia Zoya business would be 10.9%, the number for this quarter.
We have revised the classification of our jewellery product mix... Color stone jewellery, which was earlier clubbed under the studded category, we have reclassified that into the gold jewellery.
Last Quarter 1 FY '26 watch EBIT margin was 18.6% compared to 17.8% normalized margin for this quarter.

We are not giving any guidance at this point of time. In the Investor Day and prior, we have said that more of 11% being the center of gravity for jewellery business margin, we would be around that plus/minus something can happen.

The Core business was not loss-making. But given the current situation of war... purchasing jewellery in Dubai and Saudi and other countries is the last priority for anyone there. So the footfall has fallen down. Ticket sizes have fallen down.

We are committed to -- I'm just reiterating, we are committed to a double-digit healthy growth in value in the jewellery business. So that's the only way we'll get to our committed FY30 goals that we've said.
pressing_questions: Given the sustenance of the improvement we're seeing in buyer growth, even studded growth seems to have revived quite well... Would you look to revisit the EBIT growth or margin guidance for the jewellery segment given during the Analyst Meet for the next 1, 2 years at least?

If the gold price remains where it is by Q4, the Y-o-Y inflation will become zero and a large part of it is being driven by gold price inflation. So in a scenario where gold price inflation is zero, do you think we can sort of maintain a 18% to 20% kind of top line growth in that kind of a scenario?

In context of that, do you expect sort of the headwind on your margins to sort of maybe turn into a tailwind and you could see even with a slightly lower growth being able to deliver that 18% to 20% bottom line growth?

Just to understand that as we move into H2, obviously, it may not be practically possible on that high base to deliver that kind of margin. So when we say the 11% EBIT margin, what will be the driver sort of for this to improve?

quarters.summary: Titan closed FY26 with its best-ever Q4 top-line growth, with all businesses and brands gaining visibility and equity. Management flagged near-term margin uncertainty from elevated gold prices, reiterated a 15%-20% (medium-term, 3-5 year CAGR) Jewellery growth guidance rather than FY27-specific guidance, and pointed to further detailed guidance at the Investor Day planned for the first week of June.

subsections.label: International business profitability
points: International business became profitable at operating level on a full year basis, first time after two-three years since it was started and scaled up.
Q4 loss of ₹82 crores driven by disturbance in GCC in March month, affecting both Damas and Tanishq presence there; situation in GCC remains evolving/unpredictable.
Damas consolidation started from January; company has begun increased disclosure and will provide more as visibility improves; next year onward comparisons will be available.
Damas has performed better than its internal plan despite the loss.
Of the ₹82 crores loss, a large part pertains to Titan's Middle East businesses (not majority Damas), and this shows up in the international subsidiary, not in standalone numbers.

subsections.label: Unallocated losses
points: Increase in unallocated losses from ~₹20-30 crores to ~₹140 crores in Q4 is due to a 'special reward' - a tradition of sharing superlative full-year performance with employees and connected people once results are known; this reward is largely unplanned and recognized in Q4.
The reward (₹100-120 crores) is not payment to franchisees; it went mostly to employees and other agencies connected with the company.

subsections.label: Transfer pricing / standalone vs consolidated
points: Titan formalized a transfer pricing arrangement from FY25-26 onward, treating all subsidiaries as low-risk distributors, ensuring a certain amount of basic profit for Titan as parent.

This transfer pricing adjustment shows up as ~₹80 crores impact in standalone books but nullifies at consolidated level as it is between subsidiaries and parent, making standalone profitability look lower.

The ₹102-103 crore gap between reported Jewellery EBIT (standalone) and TMZ domestic EBIT is due to this transfer pricing adjustment on India-to-international primary sales, resulting in an apparent loss this quarter versus typical profit on such primary sales.

subsections.label: Gold sourcing costs
points: No increase expected in gold metal loan costs in the short term despite some slowness from customs/DGFT license renewal delays.
Gold loan tenure increased from 180 to 270 days, which the company is successfully working with.

subsections.label: Margin sustainability commentary
points: Margin sustainability in TMZ domestic (11-11.5% band) is highly correlated with gold price movements affecting product mix; difficult to guarantee sustainability if gold continues rising.
Company has been offsetting mix pressure via 18-carat, 14-carat jewellery, mix re-engineering, lightweight jewellery, and overhead cost optimization, but margin has still lost some 10-20 bps.
Growth is stated as the number one priority; more informed guidance on margin expected at the Investor Day (June 1st week).
Margin pressure viewed as coming more from product mix (driven by gold price) than from discounting/promotional activity; exchange program investment continues but is not seen as heavily escalated.
Sustainability of margin would become easier if gold rate remains where it is; opportunity for improvement to be assessed under stable gold prices.

subsections.label: CaratLane margin
points: CaratLane margin at 8.4% this quarter was largely due to revenue softness and continued investment in campaigns to build awareness (present in 160+ towns); revenue was the single largest factor.
For the full year, CaratLane margin was almost 10%.

key_figures.label: Estimated market share gain (Jewellery, FY26 vs FY25)

subsections.label: Drivers of buyer growth resurgence
points: Resurgence in buyer growth in Q4 to 8% vs flattish prior period attributed to two buyer types: those waiting on sidelines to buy as gold rates climbed since festive season, and wedding purchase advancement as customers with Q1 weddings bought early fearing further price rises.
Resurgence also seen on studded front, aided by 'festival of diamonds' campaign - a fresh, differentiated campaign.

Continued exchange campaign launched before festive (around September) has driven buyer growth in both Q3 and Q4; exchange campaigns now run standalone and are also embedded within Tanishq new-collection campaigns, reinforcing impact with every campaign.

subsections.label: Ticket size trend
points: Ticket size increases (44% and 40% over past two quarters) linked to consistent gold rate increases through the year, with a big jump around Dussehra; comparing Q1 vs Q1 prior year will show a similar gold-rate-driven ticket-size benefit for Q1 and Q2, but H2 trend depends on gold price trajectory.

subsections.label: Consumer behavior under high gold prices
points: Consumers have started accepting gold at current elevated levels; a recent slight cool-off helped bring buyers back amid sentiment that gold will resume its upward trajectory medium-to-long term.

Company response: making jewellery both exciting and accessible via exchange program, 18-carat gold, 14-carat studded jewellery, Gramage Purchase Plan (rupee cost averaging via gram accumulation, running for 2 years), and lightweight jewellery with improved look-to-price ratio.
Interest in category seen across gold and diamond studded jewellery in Q4; new natural gemstone jewellery ('Hues'/Akshaya Tritiya launch) aims to expand the category pie.
Gold price increase seen as having created more interest in the category overall (investment and jewellery demand), across young/old, modern/traditional segments.

subsections.label: Rivaah Golden Advantage Grammage Program redemptions
points: Redemptions for the Grammage program started nationally from January 2025 (after a pilot run in Tamil Nadu prior).

subsections.label: Adhik Maas seasonality
points: Company has not given much specific thought to Adhik Maas impact for Q1 FY27; historical years showed mixed impact (2018 deceleration, 2024 no visible impact); viewed as part of normal seasonality/operating rhythm.

subsections.label: Market share and category size
points: Company estimates ~50-60 bps market share gain in Jewellery FY26 vs FY25.

Jewellery sector estimated to have added roughly ₹4 lakh crores in size over the last four-five years, a sizeable number versus other discretionary categories; growth is not purely from consumption basket but also from investment basket, making 'consumer wallet share' framing complex; company suggests discussing further at Investor Meet.

subsections.label: Watches division
points: Smart watch numbers reduced, pulling down blended growth versus analog-only growth.
Analog watch contribution within the watches business has risen to close to 90% of the division.

subsections.label: CaratLane operational disruption
points: Growth slowdown from prior quarter attributed to internal factors, not fungibility between gold and studded jewellery demand or between CaratLane and Tanishq/Mia customer bases.

CaratLane migrated from legacy ERP to Oracle Fusion, creating operational challenges especially in January and first half of February, a critical period given Valentine's Day (CaratLane's second biggest month after Diwali); some demand could not be fulfilled.
Management views this as a blip, not a structural change, citing strong December and April performance.
CaratLane present in 160+ towns; continued campaign investment despite the disruption.

subsections.label: EyeCare (Titan Eye+)
points: 32 stores closed and new ones opened for net closure of 20, as part of network revamp to enhance look and feel, an 18-month journey.
EBIT margin YoY suppressed due to increased marketing spend and a one-off inventory recall of certain slow-moving stock, despite revenue growth of 16-17%.

subsections.label: Taneira
points: Undergoing review of store operating model: merchandise mix change, price points, and consumer value proposition strengthening.
Key metrics being tracked: same-store growth/buyer growth, stock turns, and sell-throughs of merchandise.
Focus on driving buyer growth particularly in sub-₹10,000 price band; results expected to show in coming months.

subsections.label: beYon (Lab-Grown Diamonds)
points: Currently at two stores; plan to scale to 10-12 stores across two-three cities in the near term (twin-engine approach with natural diamonds) before considering a national launch.
Good traction seen during Valentine's period this year, though sample size of one store makes extrapolation unreliable; no material difference observed vs natural diamonds so far.

subsections.label: Hues (new gemstone jewellery collection)
points: Launched under Akshaya Tritiya to add natural gemstone jewellery as a new dimension/growth engine beyond coins, gold jewellery, and studded jewellery.
Targets the growing 'design seeker' segment in addition to the 'value seeker'; positioned as everyday wearable jewellery rather than locker-stored pieces.
About 200 styles, with 50% priced between ₹40,000 and ₹2.5 lakhs, extending up to ₹10 lakhs.
Approach is not driven by margin considerations but by creating category excitement; may also help address entry-level price point challenges given its wearable positioning.

subsections.label: TEAL / Justech
points: TEAL has performed 'wonderfully well' as reflected in full year results.
Justech acquisition (within TEAL) has done well.

TEAL seen as powerhouse of engineering and precision manufacturing with growth tailwinds from India manufacturing investment, aerospace, defense, infrastructure, electronic chips sectors, government-led incentives, and international clients' China Plus One strategy; automation business also has opportunities from new sectors like batteries and EVs.

subsections.label: TEAL manufacturing capability
points: TEAL positioned as a powerhouse of engineering and precision manufacturing benefiting from India manufacturing investment tailwinds across aerospace, defense, infrastructure, and electronic chips sectors.

key_figures.label: International loss (Damas/Middle East) reported in prior mention

subsections.label: Gold sourcing and inventory management
points: Some slowness observed from customs point of view related to DGFT import license renewal delays, but company is well covered for Q1.
Gold exchange program running successfully since Q3, giving another layer of flexibility to ratchet sourcing at short notice if required; other contingency plans ('Plan B') also ready.

Bullion sales increase on a full-year basis is due to inventory management via the gold exchange program - gold bought from customers' vaults is continuously liquidated and replaced rather than held long, not linked to any 1% customs duty benefit (company clarified it is not receiving sufficient quota for that benefit); no separate profit booked from this, as it is purely inventory optimization.

subsections.label: CaratLane ERP migration
points: Migration from legacy ERP to Oracle Fusion created operational challenges in January and first half of February, impacting order fulfillment during the critical Valentine's period.

subsections.label: Damas acquisition and minority stake
points: Damas consolidation began from January; company plans increased disclosure over time and comparisons will be available from next year onward.
Minority shareholder interest in Damas is fully protected; both partners jointly make decisions on brand equity upliftment and related matters for the Arab segment.

Residual stake acquisition discussion/transaction window with minority partners opens about four years after certain occasions; company stated willingness to 'overpay' if the venture proves very successful.

Retail conversions of Damas stores to Tanishq are happening in catchments where Southeast Asian customers are dominant, under a franchisee model with Damas; a lot of restructuring is underway in this integration.

subsections.label: Gold sourcing / geopolitical risk
points: Delay in renewal of import licenses by DGFT and customs-related slowness flagged as a near-term supply consideration, though company says it is well covered for Q1.
GCC region situation (where Damas and Tanishq operate) remains evolving and unpredictable, contributing to Q4 international loss.

subsections.label: Gold price volatility risk
points: High and rising gold prices create margin pressure via product mix shift and pose uncertainty for sustaining current EBIT margins in the TMZ domestic business.
Volatility in gold price and macro sentiment cited as general caveats to the 15-20% growth guidance.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Competition, including organized players expanding stores across geographies amid industry formalization, has become 'business as usual'; not flagged as a major concern but acknowledged as a persistent factor.

subsections.label: Preponement/postponement of purchases
points: Wedding purchase preponement due to rising gold price fears could represent pull-forward of demand; management views this as noise between months/quarters rather than a structural risk to multi-year growth guidance.

subsections.label: Jewellery medium-term growth guidance
points: Company reiterates 15% to 20% growth guidance for Jewellery, framed as a medium-term (3-5 year) CAGR rather than a quarterly or FY27-specific number.
Guidance to hold 'irrespective of gold rate' as it is intrinsic to the company's playbook: managing buyer growth to offset gold price impact and keep category accessible.
Underlying tailwinds cited: industry formalization favoring organized players with stronger balance sheets, trust/differentiation of brands, and the India growth story.

Caveats: volatility in gold price and macro sentiment need to be managed; not guidance for FY27 specifically - Q1/Q2 may see growth benefit from gold price inflation, Q3/Q4 impact depends on further gold price trajectory.
More detailed guidance, including margin views, expected to be shared at the Investor Day planned for the first week of June.

subsections.label: beYon scale-up plan
points: Plan to scale beYon from current 2 stores to 10-12 stores across two-three cities in the near term, expected in Q1, before considering a national launch.

guidance_ledger.statement: We have said between 15% to 20% growth for Jewellery; that holds good and we hope to do that and maybe do a bit better; this is a general guidance for growth irrespective of gold rate over a 3-5 year horizon.

Idea is that if we are growing revenue 15% to 20%, can we grow EBIT also at least a little bit lower than revenue; sustainability of the 11-11.5% margin band depends on gold price trajectory; more informed view to be given at Investor Day in June first week.
Plan to scale up beYon to 10-12 stores in two to three cities, currently at two stores, hopefully getting a bunch of stores in place well in Q1 itself, before planning a national launch.
Damas consolidation started from January; increased disclosure expected as visibility improves; from next year onward comparisons will be available to assess growth of revenue and margin of Damas.
Work underway to bring in more buyer growth particularly in sub-₹10,000 price band category; some of that will start showing up in the next few months.

key_takeaways: We have ended the year with a superlative Quarter 4 top-line growth, perhaps our best-ever in the recent past.
All our businesses have grown very well, and all our brands have enhanced their visibility and equity in the quarter and the full year that went by.
One of the positive news for international business, if you look at the full year, at operating level, they became profitable.
GCC continues to be evolving or situation which is unpredictable at this stage.
We have seen resurgence in buyer growth in Quarter 4 and what we have reported is 8% versus a flattish for the period prior to that.
This is completely, I would not say full correlation, but gold price is playing a significant role on the product mix aspect of it. And consequently, it is very difficult to tell sustainability.
In the past, we have said between 15% to 20%. So, in a sense, that holds good and we hope to do that and maybe do a bit better.
We have grown to the tune of 22%-23%, which is per se not bad. But we also had a big platform level shift. We moved from our legacy ERP to Oracle Fusion.
pressing_questions: What is the guide on FY27 Jewellery sales growth given a high base and preponement of purchases in FY26 - is 20% growth still doable?
On the Jewellery EBIT discrepancy of ₹102-103 crores between standalone reported EBIT and TMZ domestic disclosure - why a sudden loss this quarter versus typical profit on primary sales?
What kind of EBITDA margins is the India Jewellery business confident of achieving in FY27, and is the 15-20% growth guidance lowballing given current elevated gold prices?

TITAN.about: Titan Company Ltd is among India’s most respected lifestyle companies. It has established leadership positions in the Watches, Jewellery and Eyewear categories led by its trusted brands and differentiated customer experience. It was founded in 1984 as a joint-venture between TATA Group and Tamilnadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO). [1]

quarters.summary: Management reiterated full-year FY27 revenue guidance of Rs.1,500+ crores with EBITDA margin above 19%, noting Q1 dispatches of ~Rs.25 crores were pushed to Q2 due to Middle East-related export deferrals but underlying performance remains on track; order inflow guidance of at least Rs.2,000 crores for FY27 was reaffirmed (with potential upside), backed by a Rs.2,428 crore order book, strong demand across power, oil & gas and process industries domestically and overseas, ramp-up of Anjar and seamless pipe capacities, and debt reduction via the Rs.300 crore preferential issue.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margin improvement reflects three things working together: better capacity utilization across facilities, operating leverage, and initial contribution from backward integration through the seamless pipe plant.
As utilization at the seamless plant ramps up through the year, expect this to support further margin improvement.

Cost base: considerable reduction in manpower headcount already achieved; no major recruitment expected, so employee cost/other expenses trend should continue even as revenue scales, aided by operating leverage from Anjar operationalization; by year-end at >Rs.1,500 crore top line, cost as a percentage should be much lower.

Gross margin volatility explained: material cost for power sector jobs is higher compared to oil and gas/job-work scenarios (where there is no material cost), but conversion cost is much lower for power sector jobs than oil & gas jobs; overall EBITDA margin guidance of above 19% remains on track.

Fluctuation in gross margin also driven by changing mix of job-work vs material-inclusive orders; some impact also from Malwa Power, but major impact is from piping segment doing more jobs with material versus earlier job-work-only basis.

subsections.label: Working capital / cash flow strategy
points: Creditor days intentionally kept low: MSME payments must be released within 45 days; with bigger vendors, company pays on cash basis or minimum credit to get leverage on purchase prices, reflecting directly in P&L.
Focus now is to reduce debtor days via increased reliance on customer bill discounting, which should ramp up as turnover increases.
Inventory days falling considerably, expected to reach ~150-160 days by/within Q2.
Aim for total working capital cycle to hover between 180-200 days.

subsections.label: Capital structure / debt reduction
points: Rs.300 crore preferential issue approved by shareholders at AGM in June was allotted on 8 July, trading approvals from BSE/NSE received 28 July; subscribers include marquee institutional investors along with promoter participation.
Of net proceeds ~Rs.293 crores, ~Rs.225 crores earmarked for repayment/prepayment of borrowings, balance for general corporate purposes.
Expected to bring down debt levels materially, reduce financial costs on run-rate basis, and improve return ratios.
Strengthens balance sheet and leverage headroom, providing flexibility to pursue growth opportunities without stretching the balance sheet, including supporting vision for a nuclear-sector facility.
No plan for any new debt in FY27; if any requirement arises it will be small/immaterial or funded from GCP.
Focus for FY27 is on asset turns, cash generation and return ratios; improving operating cash flows expected to support gradual debt reduction through the year.

subsections.label: Order pipeline / demand drivers
points: Order pipeline described as equally distributed between oil & gas and power sector jobs; data center jobs also being targeted seriously.
Order inflow guidance of at least Rs.2,000 crores in FY27 reaffirmed; total may increase further.

BHEL moving slower than expected but placed ~Rs.200 crores order last quarter; more tenders in preparation stage expected in market this quarter, likely finalized next quarter; also getting orders for other pressure parts like headers, vessels from BHEL.
L&T has awarded all orders it had offloaded till now and is discussing more orders likely to be finalized this quarter.
Discussions ongoing with JSW, Hindustan Energy, and similar opportunities in overseas markets; no worry that order inflow will fall, though customer mix may change.
GT piping orders continuing from GE; HRSG order from GE (15-16 units agreed) yet to come, expected some delay but no impact on this year's top line due to traction from other customers.
Nooter Eriksen awarding fresh orders (yet to be declared); Thailand facility now practically 100% booked for coming three years.

Siemens: signed MOU/understanding for continuous GT piping business starting with 10 units next year, 15 units the following year, 25-30 units in the third year; each unit ~1-1.5 million euros; Siemens team visiting Anjar facility in third week of August to clear the plant; business to be considered from both Palwal and Anjar facilities, with Anjar for modular piping work.

Fertilizer sector: government announced new projects particularly in Assam being eyed seriously; one foreign customer opportunity was lost to a local player; other opportunities expected next year, nothing material this year.

Thermal power medium-term opportunity: management not solely dependent on fossil fuel boilers—focus equally large on oil & gas and power; new sectors like data centers being eyed; private players (JSW, Moser Baer, Bajaj Hindustan Group with 800MW plant) provide ample demand even if PSUs slow down; no concern on booking orders in this sector through 2030.
Domestic vs export order mix for HRSG/power: export historically >50%, this year also expected ~50% or slightly less due to more domestic power work; broadly 50% export/50% domestic.

GE relationship: even in worst case of no further GE orders, company already booked for more than one and a half years; expecting inflow of Rs.1,800-2,000 crores in remaining part of year from Siemens, Nooter Eriksen, and prospectively Mitsubishi Heavy/Mitsubishi Power; management meeting GE on 14th September to ensure commitments remain on track.

Order book vs revenue guidance: order book (Rs.2,428 crores) execution depends not just on order receipt but on release of drawings/information for material ordering; some orders (e.g., GE ~Rs.380 crores appearing in order book) have no firm inputs yet; delays in some orders are viewed as manageable/even beneficial.

Seamless pipe segment order pipeline: two big tenders due for opening expected to bring significant business; discussions ongoing with JSW, Thermax and others who would buy piping with material, using company's own pipe.
