subsections.label: Core business (piping & heavy fabrication)
points: Piping together with heavy fabrication continue to anchor execution and account for large majority of revenue and order book.
Serve marquee customers across power, oil & gas, and process industries, both in India and export markets.
Full operationalization of Anjar facility has meaningfully expanded ability to execute larger and complex projects.
With seamless pipe plant commissioned, company is capturing a greater share of value in-house.

subsections.label: Non-core segment (Malwa Power / biomass pellet)
points: Biomass pellet plant commissioned during Q1 FY27, co-located with Malwa Power Plant at Muktsar, converts paddy straw and other agri residuals into pellets supplied to thermal power plants for co-firing with coal.
Demand anchored by Renewable Bulk Purchase Obligation Framework of Government of India, giving comfort on off-take.
Since pellet plant commissioned midway through Q1 FY27, current quarter reflects only partial contribution; from Q2 onwards, near-full quarter of pellet production expected.

Working on ramping up utilization over coming quarters and securing long-term off-take tie-ups with thermal power producers; also targeting industrial furnace use as renewable substitute for LPG, LNG, furnace oil.

PPA division EBIT swung to negative (~Rs.1 crore negative) from positive (~Rs.1 crore) last quarter because pellet plant was commissioned early — fuel available could run either power plant or pellet plant, and focus was on establishing pellet business; from coming October, new fuel availability should allow running both power plant and pellet plant fully, changing the scenario.

subsections.label: Thailand facility (Nooter Eriksen / GT piping)
points: Thailand facility practically 100% booked for coming three years due to fresh orders from Nooter Eriksen.
No plans for capacity expansion in Thailand; it is considered a 'showcase unit'; expansion plans focused only on India.
Peak revenue target of Rs.170-200 crores versus Rs.130 crores achieved last year.

subsections.label: Anjar facility / seamless pipe plant
points: In-house manufacturing of P-91 and P-92 pipes at Anjar primarily meant for coal-fired boilers of 800MW, 660MW and above requiring high wall thickness; not typically used for HRSG business since HRSG doesn't require such high-thickness pipes — price competitiveness would not hold there.
Expect at least ~20% EBITDA on seamless pipe manufacturing, aiding bottom line.
Plan is 50-50 split between captive consumption and outright sale of Anjar seamless pipe capacity.
Current Anjar utilization ~50%; plan to reach 60-65% this year, 70-75% (or higher) next year, and ~100% by end of following year.
GT piping business (GE, Siemens) noted as comparatively higher margin business, though efforts required are lesser but manufacturing is very specialized/critical and takes time.
Seamless external sale margin: since it's a commodity when sold independently, margin may not be very high but still around 20%.

subsections.label: Piping/fabrication mix drivers
points: Big players (BHEL, JSW) expected to award jobs with material only going forward, per management's guesswork; L&T and Adani orders most likely on job-work basis — management stresses this is guesswork, not certain.

subsections.label: Material/technology variation across sectors
points: Piping remains the same across sectors, but material compositions vary from sector to sector; quality requirements and material mix vary from project to project.
In nuclear sector, value addition is much more than power sector; in data center segment, value addition may be less than current work.
P-91/P-92 seamless pipes are specialized, high wall thickness, large diameter products meant only for large coal-fired boilers, not for HRSG applications due to differing thickness requirements.

subsections.label: Capex cycle completion
points: FY26 was the year the company completed its major growth CAPEX cycle with full operationalization of the Anjar pipe fabrication facility and commissioning of the seamless pipe plant.
Q1 FY27 is the first quarter in which early results of that investment are visible in operating performance.

subsections.label: Facility expansion plans
points: No plans for CAPEX or capacity expansion in Thailand — it remains a 'showcase unit'; any new expansion planned only in India.
Siemens team visiting Anjar facility in third week of August to formally clear the plant for modular piping work.

key_figures.label: Export share of HRSG/power business (historical & current)

subsections.label: Domestic vs export demand
points: India's CAPEX cycle continues to build momentum as corporates set up investment in plant and equipment.
Overseas market — a meaningful part of core business — showing a clear pickup across energy, process industries and infrastructure.
Domestic and global tailwinds together create a compelling multi-year opportunity for core offerings.
Export vs domestic mix for power/HRSG expected to remain broadly ~50% export / ~50% domestic this year, similar to historical pattern.

subsections.label: Gulf reconstruction opportunity
points: With reconstruction activity beginning across the Gulf, company has not yet received direct RFQs from refineries/petrochem industries; original equipment manufacturers who supplied original plants have started receiving inquiries.

Company's business would come only through these OEMs once OEMs get work awarded; potential is huge but not yet quantifiable and not factored into projections even for next five years; any resulting business would be additional/extra.

subsections.label: Working capital management
points: Creditor days intentionally kept low due to MSME 45-day payment requirement and cash/minimum-credit terms with larger vendors to gain purchase price leverage reflected directly in P&L.
Focus on reducing debtor days via increased customer bill discounting, expected to ramp up with turnover growth.
Inventory days expected to fall further to ~150-160 days by/within Q2.
Target total working capital cycle of 180-200 days.

subsections.label: Customer relationships
points: BPCL order reinforces position as preferred supplier to marquee Indian PSU refiners.
Discussions ongoing with JSW, Hindustan Energy, Thermax and others for material-inclusive piping supply.
Mitsubishi Heavy/Mitsubishi Power likely to be added to customer roster soon.
Company positioning across power, oil & gas, and process industries in both domestic and export markets.

subsections.label: Nuclear sector entry
points: Vision to establish a facility catering to the nuclear sector, moving quickly on this; target is to have nuclear sector in the fold within next two years.
For nuclear, extensive approvals required; some approvals already in place, others being worked on; company is looking for a partner to help with pre-qualification for export jobs.

For Indian nuclear jobs, company is well qualified on its own strength but Indian nuclear jobs currently moving slowly, expected to pick up in coming years; huge potential expected from nuclear sector.
For export nuclear market, a partner is needed; discussions in advanced stage; target to close discussion and formalize agreement in Q2, though it may spill over by a month or two.
Preferential issue proceeds and resulting balance sheet strength support flexibility to pursue growth opportunities including nuclear facility vision without stretching balance sheet.

subsections.label: Restructuring of non-core segment
points: Company reshaping the non-core segment via the biomass pellet plant initiative and other restructuring initiatives across the segment.

subsections.label: Export/geopolitical risk
points: Around Rs.25 crores of dispatches scheduled for Q1 got pushed into Q2 primarily on oil & gas side, where a few export customers deferred take-offs given the situation in the Middle East; material is ready at company's end.

subsections.label: Customer order timing risk
points: HRSG order from GE (15-16 units agreed) yet to come; some delay expected, though not expected to affect top line this year due to traction from other customers.
BHEL moving slower than expected in placing thermal power piping orders relative to expectations, though tenders are in preparation.

Rajasthan cancelled a 3.2 GW thermal order in June citing adequate power generation levels aided by renewables — flagged by an analyst as a risk to thermal order visibility, though management said its focus is not solely on fossil fuel boilers.

subsections.label: Fertilizer project opportunity risk
points: One foreign customer opportunity for fertilizer-related project was lost to a local competitor in that country.

subsections.label: Order book execution dependency
points: Order book execution is not just dependent on receipt of order but also on release of drawings and information needed to order material; some orders appearing in order book (e.g., GE ~Rs.380 crores) lack firm inputs currently.

subsections.label: Margin mix risk
points: Gross margin may be slightly lower this year due to higher material cost for power sector jobs versus job-work-only oil & gas jobs, though conversion cost is lower for power sector jobs; overall EBITDA margin guidance of above 19% maintained.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Management remains fully committed to top line of Rs.1,500 crores plus and EBITDA margin of more than 19%, described as 100% without doubt.
Rs.1,500 crores considered the bare minimum number for the year; plan is to exceed guidance.
Q1 is historically the weakest quarter although the best Q1 so far this year; ramps up through Q2, Q3, with Q4 typically the best quarter.
Order inflow guidance of at least Rs.2,000 crores in FY27 reaffirmed and could increase further.
Order execution CAGR conservative target of 20%, aiming to reach Rs.2,500 crores revenue possibly by FY29 (ahead of earlier FY30 target).

Overall demand visibility across core end markets — power, oil & gas, process industries in India and overseas — remains healthy, with a strong order pipeline supporting confidence in profitable growth and long-term value creation.

guidance_ledger.statement: We remain fully committed for our top line of Rs.1,500 crores plus and EBITDA margin of more than 19%. 100% without any doubt in that.
EBITDA margin of more than 19%, 100% without any doubt in that.
We are likely to get more than 2000 crores worth of inflow in this particular year... it may increase also.
We do expect that with the introduction of this [preferential issue], the net debt by close of this FY27 should not be more than Rs.400-425 crores.
We should be doing anything between Rs.1,150 crores to Rs.1,250 crores from our piping segment, and the rest will come from our subsidiaries, including Thailand.
We are targeting that we should be reaching 2,500 crores. Although we have said FY30, but we are trying that it should happen in FY29 only.
Meeting Rs.1,500 crores this year target and growing by 20% CAGR is very easy... we are targeting that we should be reaching 2,500 crores.
Last year we did around Rs.130 crores, and the intention is that we have to keep that unit busy and target to achieve anything between Rs.170 crores to Rs.200 crores.
Our plan is around Rs.1,500 crores from Anjar facility only and by '28-29, we should be able to do it.
We should be reaching at around maybe around 60% to 65% of our available capacities [this year]... by the end of next year, we should be utilizing almost 100% of the available capacity at Anjar.
Presently we are using our Anjar facility to around 50%... next year we think that we should be touching almost 70-75% or maybe a little higher also.
Our plan is 50-50 [captive consumption vs outright sale].
We do expect that we should be earning at least around 20% EBITDA of it on this seamless pipe manufacturing also which will help us in our bottom line.
Wherever we are selling it independently, since it's a commodity, the margin may not be very high, but still, it will be around 20%.
By end of Q2 or maybe within Q2 also, it should be going somewhere around 160 days or 150 days also, it's possible.
Our aim is that these [263] days should be hovering somewhere between 180 to 200 days.
We are saying minimum will be around 1300, but it can extend to around 1800 for the remainder of the year.
We are expecting another inflow for almost Rs.1,800 crores to Rs.2,000 crores in this remaining part of the year [even without further GE orders].
Broadly speaking, you still can assume that it will be 50% export and 50% domestic.
Target is to close the discussion and formalize the agreement in Q2 under any circumstances... it may spill over for one month, two months.
We do expect that there may be some delay in that [HRSG order from GE].
Starting with 10 units in the coming year, then 15 units in the next year, and maybe around 25 or 30 units in the third year.

guidance_ledger.metric: Malwa Power/pellet plant scenario post-October fuel availability
guidance_ledger.statement: From next October, coming October, we shall be getting the new fuel and then we shall be able to run fully the power plant as well as the pellet plant.
We are not planning any CAPEX or capacity expansion in Thailand.
We may not be able to restrict to just Rs. 1,500 Cr in the coming year; this is what our commitment is for the coming year that we shall surely like to see that number on the board.
60% to 65% will be domestic and around 35% to 40% will be export orders in this financial year.
Our console level EBITDA will be above 19% in any case.
We are expecting that in this year, we should be doing almost 65 to 70 percent of our revenue from the power sector.
We are quite confident that in FY27, we should be at the optimal level as far as the fabrication facility at Anjar is concerned.
Seamless plant, we may be able to ramp up to maybe around 60% to 70%.
Debtor days are almost fixed between 95 to 100 days.
We will improve on payable days, which is as of now 42 days...definitely will have a better negotiation and it will be above 70 to 75.
Right now, in FY27, the CAPEX may be lifted to 20 to 30 Cr.
At present, the target is Rs. 2,500 [Cr] by FY2030.
Combined revenue from power and biomass pallet is expected to be around Rs. 47.71 Cr in FY27.
By third quarter...we will get a clean opinion, not a qualified opinion from the auditor.
Based upon the current level of tariffs, we are expecting both the plants shall be a little positive. They will not be negative.

risk_register.risk: Middle East situation causing export customer deferrals
risk_register.note: Around Rs.25 crores of Q1 dispatches on the oil & gas export side got pushed to Q2 as export customers deferred take-offs given the Middle East situation; material is ready at company's end.
HRSG order from GE (agreement for 15-16 units) yet to come; some delay expected, though management says top line impact this year is offset by orders from other customers like Nooter Eriksen.

risk_register.risk: BHEL order pace slower than expected
risk_register.note: BHEL moving slower than expected on thermal power piping tenders; Rs.200 crores order received last quarter, more tenders expected this quarter, finalization likely next quarter.

risk_register.risk: Thermal power order cancellations by state utilities
risk_register.note: Rajasthan cancelled a 3.2 GW thermal power order in June citing adequate power generation from renewables; flagged by an analyst as a medium-term risk to thermal order pipeline.
One foreign customer fertilizer-related opportunity was lost to a local competitor in that country; new opportunities expected only next year.

risk_register.risk: Order book execution dependency on drawings/information release
risk_register.note: Execution depends not just on order receipt but on release of drawings and information needed to order material; some orders in the order book (e.g., GE ~Rs.380 crores) lack firm inputs currently.

risk_register.risk: Gross margin volatility from material-cost mix
risk_register.note: Gross margin may be slightly lower this year due to higher material cost in power sector jobs versus job-work basis in oil & gas jobs, though conversion cost is lower for power jobs; also some impact from Malwa.
Debtor days increased from 99 (Q1 FY26) to 123 (Q1 FY27); company focusing on reducing this via customer bill discounting.

For export nuclear jobs, a large amount of pre-qualification and approvals are required; company needs a partner, in advanced discussion stage targeting formalization in Q2, may spill over by a month or two.

risk_register.risk: Malwa Power impairment / qualified audit opinion (second consecutive year)
risk_register.note: Management expects biomass pellet plant and tariff revision to mitigate impairment; targets clean audit opinion by Q3, and does not foresee financial contingency even if Appellate rules against revised tariff.

risk_register.risk: BHEL order release pacing slower than expected
risk_register.note: BHEL moving slower on order release while L&T moves faster; FY27 order inflow guidance of >Rs. 2,000 Cr is contingent on BHEL orders materializing; an L1 order of ~Rs. 210 Cr has been pending ~3 months.

risk_register.risk: Margin volatility due to project-based, non-commodity business model
risk_register.note: Management flagged that gross margin fluctuates quarter-to-quarter due to numerous factors and requested year-on-year comparison instead.
Region still assessing losses post-disruption; situation not yet normal, so no orders/enquiries materializing yet despite seen as a big future opportunity.

risk_register.risk: Raw material/alloy steel import dependence (P-91, P-92)
risk_register.note: Previously imported from China/Europe; own seamless pipeline has reduced import dependence, with a few approvals pending to reach near-full self-sufficiency for power sector jobs in India.

risk_register.risk: Capacity expansion decision uncertainty (nuclear sector, HRSG demand)
risk_register.note: Management deliberating on new capacity for nuclear sector and broader HRSG opportunity; decision still on the drawing board as capacity must be sustainable for 10-15 years.

themes.label: HRSG/Gas-turbine backlog opportunity
themes.note: GE HRSG order (15-16 units) delayed but Thailand facility 100% booked for 3 years via Nooter Eriksen; Siemens MOU for 10/15/25-30 units over three years at ~1-1.5 million euros per unit.

themes.label: Capacity ramp-up (Anjar & seamless plant)
themes.note: Anjar utilization at ~50% now, targeted 60-65% this year and ~100% by end of next year; seamless pipe plant expected to earn ~20% EBITDA and support margin improvement.

themes.label: Working capital cycle improvement
themes.note: Total working capital cycle improved from 276 to 263 days YoY; inventory days fell from 243 to 174; target of 180-200 days for FY27.

themes.label: Domestic thermal power order visibility
themes.note: BHEL moving slower than expected though placing orders; L&T and private players like JSW, Moser Baer, Bajaj Hindustan Group providing demand; Rajasthan cancelled a 3.2GW order citing renewable-driven adequate generation.

themes.label: Malwa Power tariff/impairment resolution
themes.note: PPA division EBIT swung to negative (~Rs.1 crore) from positive as fuel was diverted to establish pellet plant business; scenario expected to improve from October with new fuel availability enabling both plants to run fully.

themes.label: Capex cycle completion / new capacity evaluation
themes.note: FY26 marked completion of major growth capex cycle (Anjar + seamless plant); no further capacity expansion planned in Thailand; preferential issue proceeds to strengthen balance sheet and reduce debt.

themes.label: Core-vs-non-core restructuring
themes.note: Biomass pellet plant (72,000 MT/annum capacity) commissioned at Muktsar as part of reshaping the non-core segment, anchored by Renewable Bulk Purchase Obligation Framework.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operations for Q1 FY27 was Rs. 294.5 crores up 31.6% year-on-year, driven by continued execution momentum in the piping segment, supported by supplies to the power and oil and gas sector.
Operating EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 49.7 crores with a margin of 16.9% compared with 16% in Q1FY26 and it is up by 38.7% year-on-year.
Profit after tax for the quarter stood at Rs. 16.1 crores up Rs. 22.4% year-on-year.

Around Rs. 25 crores of dispatches scheduled for Q1 got pushed into Q2 primarily on the oil and gas side, where a few of our export customers deferred take-offs given the situation in the Middle East.
A notable highlight during the quarter was the receipt of a domestic purchase order of Rs. 386.82 crores from Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited for manufacturing and supply of piping.
The 300 crores preferential issue that was approved by shareholders at the AGM in June was allotted on 8 July, with the trading approvals from BSE and NSE received on 28 July.
Improving operating cash flows are expected to support a gradual reduction in debt levels through the year with a strong order book of Rs. 2,428 crores as of 30 June 2026.
We remain fully committed, fully committed for our top line of Rs. 1.500 crores plus and EBIDTA margin of more than 19%. 100% without any doubt in that.
pressing_questions: Sir, my question is on your order book side. Within your power segment order book, Rs. 399 crores as of September 2025, inside a total order book, that has since grown to 2,428 crores. Could you break down in rupees or in tonnage, how much is HRSG and combined cycle piping for global gas turbine OEMs?

And sir, how much is conventional coal supercritical and mundra supercritical power cycle piping for the domestic NEP build? And how much is waste heat recovery? And within your stated financial 27 inflow guidance of Rs. 2,000 crores at roughly 60% power, what share do you expect to be HRSG export work versus Indian Oil terminal work?

quarters.summary: DEE Development Engineers closed FY26 with strong core-business momentum (core EBITDA up 64.2% YoY) and a record order book (Rs. 1,940-2,040 Cr) giving multi-year revenue visibility. Management guided to conservative FY27 order inflow of over Rs. 2,000 Cr, consolidated EBITDA margin above 19%, working capital cycle of ~180 days, FY27 capex of Rs. 20-30 Cr, and a longer-term target of Rs. 2,500 Cr revenue by FY30, while continuing to pivot the non-core power segment toward biomass pellets and monitor a large HRSG/GT piping opportunity tied to global gas-turbine backlogs.

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 base effect
points: Q4 FY25 was an unusually high base as it absorbed revenue and profit spillover from Q3 FY25 last year; a cleaner read of performance is full-year FY26 PAT up 76.9% YoY.
PAT for Q4 FY26 reflects stable performance on a high Q4 FY25 base, in line with company guidance.

subsections.label: Drivers of performance
points: Revenue growth driven by healthy execution momentum in the piping segment, supported by strong supply to the oil & gas and power sectors.
Operating EBITDA growth supported by higher execution level and operating leverage in the core business, alongside the tariff revision on the non-core side.
Overall FY26 performance primarily driven by higher execution momentum and improved capacity utilization across both facilities.

subsections.label: Gross margin dip discussion
points: Management noted it is difficult to explain quarter-on-quarter margin movements as the company is project-based, not commodity-based; requested comparisons be made on a year-on-year basis.

One reason cited for the margin dip was a small portion of trading activity undertaken in Q4, where the value of the material supplied was almost 100%/95% of revenue (low value-add), which can compress margin percentage.

subsections.label: Working capital strategy
points: Inventory days expected to reduce in FY27 primarily because ~70% of jobs are towards the power sector, where cash conversion cycle and inventory holding time are much lower than in oil & gas.

Payable days reduced this year (to 42 days) because the company chose to pay in advance for material ordering to secure a better purchase discount, which improved material cost/margin at the cost of higher inventory days.
Company plans to negotiate with suppliers to push payable days back up to 70-75 days.
Strategy for FY27 includes greater use of sales bill discounting to reduce inventory days, plus expected milestone payments from export customers that will also help reduce inventory days.
Management clarified target is 180 days (not 200), with an eventual longer-term target of 150 days.

subsections.label: Equity raise / debt reduction
points: Company had earlier been planning to raise money through equity; is on the drawing board to decide strategy given the stock's strong performance, but no decision made yet — will communicate once finalized.
Improving cash flows and operating performance are expected to support gradual reduction in debt levels going forward.

subsections.label: Audit qualification (Malwa Power)
points: Second consecutive year of qualified audit opinion related to Malwa Power impairment.
Management expects both plants to turn slightly positive based on current tariff levels and does not foresee need for impairment or financial contingency.
CFO indicated the audit qualification could potentially be resolved (clean opinion) by the third quarter.

key_figures.label: Power sector orders in current order book
Order book growth vs FY30 roadmap growth assumption

subsections.label: Order book growth vs roadmap
points: Order book has increased ~50% while FY30 roadmap projects 20-25% growth; management called this a conservative estimate and said the company may need to do more work/capacity expansion, and may exceed the stated Rs. 1,500 Cr target for the coming year.
FY27 order inflow guidance of >Rs. 2,000 Cr is contingent on BHEL orders materializing, not purely additive.

subsections.label: Demand visibility
points: Demand visibility across core end markets — power, oil & gas, process industries in India and overseas — remains healthy, giving confidence in delivering profitable growth and long-term value.

Domestic thermal ordering expected to see a step-up as boiler turbine generator (BTG) orders awarded to BHEL and L&T translate into piping erection requirements peaking around FY27-28 for ~40 GW of live thermal projects; L&T is moving faster than BHEL, and the company already has orders with L&T and is discussing more.
Power sector orders in book are thermal orders from India and HRSG orders from abroad.

subsections.label: Fertilizer sector opportunity
points: A major fertilizer order by a government company in India (new plant coming up in Namrup) is being tracked; one job expected but timing of maturity within this financial year uncertain.
Company is in active discussion with one export customer for a fertilizer unit — a field expected to become a considerable part of business going forward.

subsections.label: Capacity balancing with BHEL
points: Company does not view any special 'balancing act' needed for BHEL vs other customers — orders are executed as received, with delivery timelines starting from order date (12-18 months), regardless of which OEM places the order.

subsections.label: Core vs non-core segmentation
points: Business has been separated into core (piping, heavy fabrication and others) and non-core (power) segments; core continues to generate most value and margin, evidenced in full-year operating performance.
Core business EBITDA excludes losses from the non-core power segment, which are reflected at the consolidated level.

subsections.label: Alloy mix / job work mix (approximate)
points: Job work order share estimated at approximately 30% of order book (approximate numbers, not exact); remaining orders are with-material orders.
All HRSG/thermal jobs in India are alloy jobs.
Power vs oil & gas mix for the year: 70% power, 30% oil & gas, translating to roughly 55-60% alloy steel and remainder carbon/non-alloy steel.

subsections.label: Heavy fabrication business shift
points: Heavy fabrication capacity is being ramped up.

Business model is shifting: earlier jobs were largely on a job-work basis, but over the last one year the company has been increasingly getting jobs with its own materials, which is boosting turnover in this segment.
Recent big order of Rs. 170 Cr received in heavy fabrication.

subsections.label: Piping/heavy fabrication margin outlook
points: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to be above 19%; heavy fabrication margin expected to be at a similar tune, though EBITDA margin percentage may appear to drop as more jobs are done with material (value-wise EBITDA will still increase).

subsections.label: Non-core power/biomass pivot
points: Non-core segment strategically pivoting towards biomass pellet manufacturing, focused on enhancing capital efficiency, minimizing incremental capital commitment in the power segment, and building a more sustainable, scalable business model over the medium term.
Malwa Power tariff revised from Rs. 3.5/KwH to Rs. 5.22/KwH, with retrospective recovery of almost Rs. 5.52 Cr; company also pursuing an Appellate appeal for further tariff optimization.
Biomass pellet facility recently commissioned, expected to offset current cash burn, stabilize segment profitability, and support margin improvement going forward.

subsections.label: Seamless pipe backward integration
points: Commissioned seamless pipeline during the year; this backward integration strengthens capabilities in high-spec applications, improves supply security, supports margins, and reduces lead times.
After putting up its own seamless pipeline, the company has been able to establish supply chain majorly from India for alloy steel (P-91, P-92), reducing reliance on imports from China/Europe.
Company has already received a few raw material approvals with a few more likely to come shortly, after which it will be almost 100% self-sufficient for power sector jobs in India.
Company has successfully qualified with some foreign players who may source P-91 pipe from its manufacturing unit.

subsections.label: Metallic piping for data centers
points: Company is exploring opportunities in rigid pipe / metallic piping for use inside data centers (beyond the HRSG opportunity outside data centers); has a few active inquiries but none have matured into an order yet.

key_figures.label: Thailand HRSG capacity reserved for Nooter Eriksen

subsections.label: Capex cycle completion
points: Company has completed a significant part of its growth capex cycle, particularly with full operationalization of the Anjar pipe fabrication facility and commissioning of the seamless pipe plant.
With the capex cycle now majorly complete, company expects better asset terms, stronger cash generation, and improved return ratios going forward.

Only balance/leftover capex from the previous year remains for FY27 (guided at Rs. 20-30 Cr), though management is reconsidering additional capex for new opportunities such as nuclear sector and Middle East reconstruction demand — still on the 'drawing board.'

subsections.label: Utilization ramp-up
points: Anjar fabrication facility (newly inaugurated Anjar oil & gas facility) expected to reach almost the expected/optimal utilization level in FY27.
Seamless plant utilization expected to ramp up to around 60-70% in FY27.
As seamless plant utilization ramps up, it should support further operating leverage and margin improvements.

subsections.label: Thailand HRSG capacity reservation
points: 60% of Thailand's 14,500-ton capacity has been reserved for Nooter Eriksen under a capacity-reservation agreement — the first such agreement the company has entered into; management hopes for similar agreements with other OEMs (discussions/exploration ongoing with Siemens and others, nothing finalized).
Rs. 150 Cr order value at Thailand is described as job-work value (Thailand unit functions almost purely on a job-work basis); EBITDA margin on this revenue expected to be much higher than 20%.
No significant capex required to execute the Nooter Eriksen order — only normal machinery adjustments, described as very nominal/insignificant.

subsections.label: Nuclear sector / new capacity consideration
points: Management is evaluating a potential capacity expansion to enter the nuclear sector, citing strong tailwinds, but decision is still on the drawing board; will communicate once finalized.
Management is being deliberate about new capacity decisions since any capacity built must be sustainable for 10-15 years; close to finalizing a blueprint and will update market soon.

subsections.label: Overseas market momentum
points: Overseas markets, a meaningful part of core business, show a clear pick-up in energy, process industries, and infrastructure, mirroring the domestic capex cycle.
Domestic and global tailwinds together open up a strong multi-year opportunity for core offerings in piping, heavy fabrication, and allied segments.

subsections.label: Middle East reconstruction opportunity
points: Middle East region reconstruction/rebuilding enquiries not yet materializing as everybody is still assessing losses and the situation is not yet normal; management sees it as a big future opportunity that may require some capex to grab once conditions stabilize, but currently too fluid to comment on specifics.

subsections.label: GE Vernova / HRSG relationship
points: Company has a good order book from GE Vernova and does not expect much fresh order inflow from GE this financial year as it will be executing existing orders, though there is a surge of GT piping orders expected from GE.

Apart from GE, Nooter Eriksen has fixed capacity reservations for HRSG piping (60% of Thailand capacity); company is in discussions with other players like Siemens and is confident more similar capacity-reservation agreements may follow.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: In India, the company faces practically no competition except one or two players with significantly lesser capacity; broader competition is from Korean and some Turkish players.
Suppliers/vendors for HRSG piping products are generally scarce, creating a supply-demand gap that favors the company.

subsections.label: HRSG / gas turbine backlog opportunity
points: Globally, especially in the US, data center infrastructure buildout is driving massive multi-year gas-turbine order backlogs at GE, Siemens and Mitsubishi; company supplies pipes for HRSG systems used in these gas turbine installations.
Most of the company's recent overseas orders, including the Thailand order, are related to this HRSG market opportunity.

Management's conservative estimate is to grow order inflow at a 20% CAGR, but sees potential for this to rise to 25-30% given the scale of opportunity; exact customer/order composition of this opportunity is difficult to pin down.

subsections.label: Core/non-core restructuring
points: Company separated the business into core and non-core segments during FY26, with results showing up in improved operating performance.
Non-core segment pivot towards biomass pellet manufacturing is part of a restructuring initiative aimed at minimizing incremental capital commitment in power and building a scalable model.

subsections.label: Capital raise consideration
points: Company had earlier considered raising money through equity; is now on the drawing board reassessing strategy given the stock's strong price performance, with no decision made yet.

subsections.label: Audit qualification / Malwa Power impairment
points: Second consecutive year of qualified audit opinion tied to Malwa Power plant impairment concerns.

Management believes tariff revision and the new biomass pellet plant will mitigate the impairment issue and expects no negative financial contingency even if the Appellate rules against the revised tariff, since the regulatory commission's current decision is not expected to be further reduced.
Possible resolution (clean audit opinion) targeted by the third quarter, per CFO.

subsections.label: BHEL order pacing risk
points: BHEL is releasing orders slower than expected while L&T is moving faster; FY27 order inflow guidance of >Rs. 2,000 Cr is contingent on BHEL orders materializing.
An L1 order of ~Rs. 210 Cr from BHEL has been pending for about three months without conversion to a firm order.

subsections.label: Margin volatility / project-based nature
points: Company cautioned that gross margin can vary quarter-to-quarter due to numerous factors given its project-based (not commodity-based) business model, and requested analysts compare performance on a year-on-year basis rather than quarter-on-quarter.

subsections.label: Middle East uncertainty
points: Middle East reconstruction opportunity remains highly fluid with the region still assessing damage and situation not yet normalized; timing and scale of any resulting orders cannot be estimated yet.

subsections.label: Growth roadmap vs conservatism
points: Management reiterated that FY27 order inflow and revenue targets (Rs. 1,500 Cr order commitment, Rs. 2,500 Cr revenue by FY30) are conservative estimates and could be exceeded given current traction, but company is committing to at least these numbers.
FY30 target of Rs. 2,500 Cr revenue could potentially be achieved earlier if order flow increases further.

subsections.label: Nuclear sector consideration
points: Company is evaluating whether to expand capacity to address a nuclear sector opportunity; decision still pending, to be communicated once finalized.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are expecting more than Rs. 2,000 Cr orders in this financial year. Out of that, the major contributor will be power sector (~60%), rest from oil and gas.
We may not be able to restrict to just Rs. 1,500 Cr in the coming year; this is what our commitment is for the coming year that we shall surely like to see that number on the board.
60% to 65% will be domestic and around 35% to 40% will be export orders in this financial year.
Our console level EBITDA will be above 19% in any case.
We are expecting that in this year, we should be doing almost 65 to 70 percent of our revenue from the power sector.
We are quite confident that in FY27, we should be at the optimal level as far as the fabrication facility at Anjar is concerned.
Seamless plant, we may be able to ramp up to maybe around 60% to 70%.
Our total working capital cycle would be around 200 days in FY2027 [later clarified to 180 days target].
We are targeting in FY2027 it will get reduced further by 15 to 20 days.
Debtor days are almost fixed between 95 to 100 days.
We will improve on payable days, which is as of now 42 days...definitely will have a better negotiation and it will be above 70 to 75.
Right now, in FY27, the CAPEX may be lifted to 20 to 30 Cr.
At present, the target is Rs. 2,500 [Cr] by FY2030.
Combined revenue from power and biomass pallet is expected to be around Rs. 47.71 Cr in FY27.
Our very, very conservative estimate is that we have to grow at 20% CAGR. But there is a possibility that this number from 20 may go up to 25 or 30 also.
Wherever we are selling it independently, since it's a commodity, the margin may not be very high, but still, it will be around 20%.
By third quarter...we will get a clean opinion, not a qualified opinion from the auditor.
Based upon the current level of tariffs, we are expecting both the plants shall be a little positive. They will not be negative.

themes.label: HRSG/Gas-turbine backlog opportunity
themes.note: Global data-center-driven gas turbine order backlogs at GE, Siemens, Mitsubishi are driving HRSG piping demand; Thailand capacity reservation with Nooter Eriksen and active discussions with Siemens.

themes.label: Core-vs-non-core restructuring
themes.note: Business split into core (piping, heavy fabrication) and non-core (power) segments, with core EBITDA up 64.2% YoY and non-core pivoting to biomass pellets.

themes.label: Capacity ramp-up (Anjar & seamless plant)
themes.note: Anjar fabrication facility expected near-optimal utilization and seamless plant to ramp to 60-70% in FY27, supporting operating leverage.

themes.label: Working capital cycle improvement
themes.note: Inventory days targeted down 15-20 days and payable days improving to 70-75, but total cycle target clarified at 180 days (not 150) for FY27.

themes.label: Domestic thermal power order visibility
themes.note: 40 GW of live thermal projects expected to drive piping erection demand peaking FY27-28, though BHEL order release pace is slower than L&T's, making FY27 order guidance contingent on BHEL.

themes.label: Malwa Power tariff/impairment resolution
themes.note: Tariff revised upward to Rs. 5.22/KwH with retrospective recovery; biomass pellet plant commissioned to offset cash burn and target clean audit opinion by Q3.

themes.label: Capex cycle completion / new capacity evaluation
themes.note: Major growth capex cycle largely complete (Anjar, seamless plant) with only Rs. 20-30 Cr planned for FY27, while management evaluates further expansion for nuclear sector and Middle East opportunity.

key_takeaways: Core business EBITDA (Inc. Other Income) for FY26 was Rs. 210.5 Cr, up 64.2% year-on-year, reflecting better execution, improved utilization, and operating leverage across our facilities.

Revenue from operations for Q4 was Rs. 361.6 Cr, up by 26.3% year-on-year. For the full year, FY26, it stood at Rs. 1,142 Cr, up by 38% year-on-year, driven by healthy execution momentum in the piping segment, supported by strong supply to the oil & gas and power sectors.
Operating EBITDA for Q4 was Rs. 65.9 Cr. For the full year, the operating EBITDA was Rs. 189.3 Cr, up by 52.9% year-on-year. EBITDA margin was 16.7% for FY26 versus 15.0% in FY25.
Profit after tax for Q4 FY26 stood at Rs. 27.7 Cr. For FY26, PAT increased 76.9% year-on-year to Rs. 77.2 Cr.
Our order book stands at Rs. 2,040 Cr, giving us strong revenue visibility and a healthy project pipeline across key segments.

The tariff at Malwa Power has been revised to Rs. 5.22 / KwH from Rs. 3.5 / KwH, with a retrospective recovery of almost around Rs. 5.52 Cr. Combined revenue from power and biomass pallet is expected to be around Rs. 47.71 Cr in FY27.
We are expecting more than Rs. 2,000 Cr orders in this financial year, with 60% from power and rest from oil and gas; 60-65% domestic and 35-40% export.
We are quite confident that in FY27, we should be at the optimal level as far as the fabrication facility at Anjar is concerned and also for the seamless plant, which may ramp up to 60-70%.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30, 2026): revenue grew 21% YoY (12% in constant currency) to ~INR893 crores; EBITDA at 33% (INR294 crores), which would be ~200bps higher (~35%, INR314 crores) adjusting for one-time TruBridge acquisition exceptional costs; PAT grew 28% YoY to INR193 crores (net profit for the period stated at INR194 crores or 22% margin). TruBridge acquisition closed July 10, 2026 (post quarter-end), so Q1 numbers are pre-TruBridge/standalone legacy IKS. Management reiterated its True North target of at least INR3,000 crores EBITDA by FY30 with minimal dilution (only ESOP-related) and a return to pre-TruBridge net debt levels, while resetting expectations on TruBridge's steady-state revenue base downward (to ~$300mn/year from ~$340mn anticipated pre-close) though confirming TruBridge's ~$68 million annualized operating EBITDA is intact.

subsections.label: EBITDA adjustment drivers
points: Reported 33% EBITDA would be approximately 200 bps higher if adjusted for one-time exceptional costs associated with the TruBridge acquisition.
TruBridge acquisition was accomplished at an unprecedentedly lower cost than most such transactions — just north of about 1%, of which ~INR20 crores is reflected in this quarter's costs.

Adjusting for the INR20 crores, INR294 crores becomes INR314 crores, and the 33% margin becomes north of 35% operating EBITDA, representing healthy quarter-on-quarter EBITDA growth from INR300-odd crores to INR314 crores.

subsections.label: Revenue and cost drivers (Nithya's remarks)
points: Revenue grew 12% in constant currency; forex gain was neutral this quarter compared to Q4, where there was substantial support from forex gain.
Employee benefit and other expenses were affected by a lower number of employees (cost-reducing) but offset by integration of senior technology resources from ThinkDTM and ARAI in the quarter.
One-time acquisition costs across both quarters: ~INR25 crores in Q4 and ~INR20 crores in Q1; a little more integration expense is expected in the next quarter, likely in a similar range.
Adjusting for one-time acquisition expenses and currency, adjusted EBITDA is at 35%, in line with the Q4 number.
Finance, depreciation and amortization expenses came largely in line with the previous quarter.

Tax rate was higher this quarter (22.4%), as discussed last quarter; expected to remain in the 22%-23% range for legacy IKS for the rest of the year; combined pro-forma tax rate to be discussed next quarter.

subsections.label: Return on equity decline driver
points: ROE decline quarter-on-quarter was largely due to the one-time acquisition cost and an increase in the valuation of Abridge (a strategic investment), which had to be marked-to-market at a higher valuation, increasing the equity base (denominator) without impacting the P&L — the revaluation goes to OCI/equity directly.

subsections.label: Cash flow
points: Continued strong operating and free cash flows; cash basis was affected by a one-time NEVA payment associated with a customer, which is why it's not reflecting in net debt, but underlying operating and free cash flow performance continues to reflect business strength.

subsections.label: KPI metrics
points: Adjusted EBITDA per employee continues to grow at a healthy pace given technology transformation and continuous deployment of automation.
Revenue from top 10 and top 5 customers grew healthily; contribution remained flat compared to Q4.
Top 10 customer vintage is approximately six years and top five vintage is approximately seven years, reflecting strong long-term relationships.

subsections.label: Historical journey / seventh quarter as public company
points: This is the seventh quarter of reporting as a public company; first quarter as public was quarter ending December 31, 2024.
Over a 10-year historical horizon, revenue growth of about 29% with demonstrated non-linearity between revenue and PAT.

From TTM September 2024 (pre-IPO, INR647 crores EBITDA) to TTM June 2026 (INR1,148 crores EBITDA, standalone pre-TruBridge), representing nearly a 40% CAGR annualized over 18-20 months with no dilution.

subsections.label: TruBridge financial reset drivers
points: Confirmed TruBridge's ~$68 million annualized operating EBITDA is intact as anticipated at deal close.
However, that EBITDA is coming off a lower revenue base than anticipated: revised steady-state operating revenue estimate of ~$300 million/year versus the ~$340 million/year anticipated pre-close.
Driver 1: More conservative revenue recognition for RCM deals versus TruBridge's prior more aggressive estimation-based approach — roughly $2-3 million/quarter impact.

Driver 2: Elimination of two unprofitable service lines — small IT management services for rural community hospitals and early-out type services — worth about $8 million/quarter combined; removing them does not hurt profitability and may help it slightly; TruBridge is already on its way to doing this, resetting the base over a couple of quarters.
Driver 3: Anticipated customer discounts to rapidly accelerate operating model transformation, about $2-3 million/quarter over the next few quarters.

subsections.label: Business model / recurring revenue
points: Most revenue tends to be recurring because IKS is essentially the operating infrastructure for provider systems that helps them operate day-to-day, with long tenure clients.

subsections.label: Headcount and non-linearity
points: Pre-TruBridge headcount was about 12,900-odd people (June 2026), of which ~1,900 are clinical, close to 600 are technology/engineering employees, and close to 60 are sales and marketing people.

Headcount grew only 4.2% YoY (from 12,300 in June 2025 to 12,889 in June 2026) versus 12% constant currency revenue growth, demonstrating continued non-linearity between revenue growth and people growth driven by operating efficiencies.
Operating headcount is currently a bit inflated due to anticipated TruBridge integration investments needed to elevate performance of certain TruBridge RCM customers.

subsections.label: AAW patent (predictive patient behavior model)
points: Patent approved for the AAW model, which predicts patient behavior across multiple dimensions including propensity to show/no-show, based on a composite score of patient's Awareness, Ability, and Willingness to show up.

Feeds a scheduling optimization feature within the patient engagement hub, enabling maximum fixed-cost utilization of provider time and improved access to care, via differential nudging algorithms and strategies like double-booking for high-no-show-propensity patients.

AAW algorithm also predicts patient's propensity to pay (based on awareness, ability, willingness), enabling differential nudging to collect payment before care is delivered, since post-care collection carries a high write-off ratio; patient-pay component of reimbursement is generally rising as co-pays/deductibles increase.
Already deployed in MyCareHub patient engagement technology with proven upside in patient collections and schedule optimization.

subsections.label: SLM (Small Language Model) strategy (Q&A)
points: Three SLM approaches to be deployed for different tasks: (1) classic standalone SLM — lower latency, can run on CPUs/edge devices, lower GPU/cloud cost; (2) SLM distilled from an LLM, where the LLM acts as a 'teacher' during training only; (3) hierarchical SLM+LLM model, where SLM handles intent detection, classification, simple Q&A, workflow execution and task routing, and LLM is invoked only for tasks requiring deep reasoning.

Goal is much lesser dependency on front-line LLM models over time; management could not yet quantify expected token utilization reduction (e.g., a specific % drop) but expects the metric to emerge over time.

subsections.label: Explainable/Glass Box AI mechanics (Q&A)
points: Explainability derives from knowledge graphs acquired via the ARAI acquisition and to be continually built — a knowledge graph is a set of relationships between data points that explains how the AI arrives at its inference.

subsections.label: System of action feature tracking
points: Previously tracked automation potential by feature; now tracking autonomy potential by feature, driven by the deterministic vs non-deterministic nature of each task; will continue reporting progress on this journey to autonomy, noting humans may shift from 'doers of task' to 'auditors of task' over time.

subsections.label: Client wins this quarter
points: Large, unnamed but very visible health system in California, helping them transition most regions to Epic; strengthens overall relationship and partnership with Epic in the traditional market.

Significant win with a national musculoskeletal leader — a very large national aggregator in the musculoskeletal space, starting with a significant RCM relationship and commitment to explore other platform dimensions.

Flagship relationship with Advocate Health Care expanded significantly, both in revenue cycle and coding dimensions — Advocate is one of the top five health systems in the country with north of $35 billion in annual revenue; still only scratching the surface even with this expansion.
Partnership with StrideCare, one of the largest vascular and vein surgery organizations and the leading national aggregator in that space.
Healthy mix of cross-sell wins plus new customer acquisitions in the independent single-specialty space, demonstrating continued growth momentum.

subsections.label: Cross-sell / land-and-expand strategy
points: Pivoted strategy in the health system-owned market from a full comprehensive platform go-to-market approach to a land-and-expand approach; results over the last couple of quarters show fruits of that pivot, evidenced by California health system and Advocate wins.
For independent medical groups and mid-sized health systems, seeing more appetite for platform-based deals.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape / Epic relationship
points: Concern was whether Epic would get competitive with IKS as TruBridge is integrated; instead, IKS continues to get closer to Epic in the traditional market and integrate more features, while TruBridge is independently getting closer to Epic and collaborating in the rural market.
Renewal conversations with large health systems: increasing competitive intensity is manifesting partly through pricing pressure from new platform providers pitching capabilities.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity / point solutions vs platform (Q&A - Abridge)
points: Abridge (a strategic investment held by IKS) launched a mid-June clinician intelligence platform, moving beyond AI scribe into pre-visit, during-visit, and payer-provider mediation — overlapping with IKS's platform capabilities.
Management noted there are about 30 vendors now aspiring to evolve from point solutions to platform; not all will execute successfully — there will be winners and losers.
Expanding from an AI-scribe business to a pre-peri-post-visit platform takes significant time and effort.
Competitive intensity in the space is increasing and will continue to increase given a $200-plus billion TAM growing at 8% and a $35 billion outsourced TAM growing at 12%.
IKS remains watchful of competition, including Abridge, viewing it as one of many point solutions trying to move upstream to build bigger platforms.

subsections.label: Recognition / case studies
points: Case study published with Axia Women's Health: optimized coding delivered a $12 million cash impact in a fully compliant manner with 96% coding accuracy, reducing coding denials — demonstrating the system of action's ability to deliver tangible value beyond just technology.

subsections.label: Market size and client base context
points: Total addressable market of $260 billion overall, growing at 8%, with a $35 billion outsourced TAM growing at 12%.
Serviced 600-odd large provider groups pre-TruBridge (Q1 FY27); combined clients post-TruBridge are close to 2,000, including 2,100-plus addressable rural/community hospitals.

TruBridge market share in rural EHR market

subsections.label: Five renewed strategic pillars of execution
points: Pillar 1 (most strategic): building an integrated system of action and system of record for the rural/community health system market — leveraging TruBridge's 5 million-plus patient dataset, de-identified and converted into a structured unified database to train proprietary small language models (SLMs), reducing dependence on expensive front-line LLM token costs.

Explainable/Glass Box AI: built via the ARAI acquisition, using knowledge graphs to explain how the AI arrives at inferences, not just generate answers — considered a key differentiator in healthcare.

Deterministic vs non-deterministic task framework: tasks with deterministic outcomes (e.g., medical codes) require rules-based AI/knowledge graphs plus human-in-the-loop; non-deterministic tasks (e.g., clinical documentation narratives) can achieve high autonomy via Generative AI with human-in-the-loop only for edge cases; roadmap by feature built around this stratification.

SLMs trained for the rural/community market are expected to be extensible into the traditional urban/semi-urban market (70% of care in rural/community hospital settings is outpatient, similar to IKS's traditional business).

Pillar 2: continue to empower the comprehensive system of action for the traditional (urban/large group) market via API-based EHR integration (less optimal than native workflow integration in the rural market, but still a differentiated moat versus multiple point solutions); right to win requires being #1/#2/#3 by feature per KLAS ratings (the 'Gartner of healthcare IT') and Black Book ratings.

Pillar 3: clearly stratified go-to-markets across three segments — rural/community market (comprehensive integrated system of action and record), independent medical groups and mid-sized health systems (platform-based deals with growing appetite), and large health system-owned groups (land-and-expand approach, pivoted from full comprehensive platform GTM).

Pillar 4 (financial discipline): plan to return to early-to-mid 30% EBITDA margins after the pro forma drop to 26%-27% range post-TruBridge consolidation, via (a) evolving the model from tech-enabled human-in-the-loop to appropriate autonomy leveraging generative explainable AI, (b) transforming the TruBridge operating model to leverage IKS technology plus appropriate offshore human-in-the-loop, and (c) natural operating and SG&A synergies from combining two organizations into a business just short of about $700 million in revenue.

Pillar 5 (culture): commitment to building a single institutionalized outcome-driven culture across the combined ~16,000+ employees and ~2,000 clients; consolidating leadership team, discovering complementary strengths across legacy TruBridge and legacy IKS leadership; continuing to drive value behaviors.

subsections.label: TruBridge acquisition rationale (Q&A)
points: Acquisition was the result of a deliberate, thematic Corp Dev search (not opportunistic) for an adjacent market with a large EHR vendor where deep system-of-action integration was possible without becoming overly competitive with EHR vendors in IKS's traditional market (where such vendors are already firmly installed).
Took about a year to 18 months to land TruBridge, which was in an auction process run through a banker.

Attraction to TruBridge driven by three factors: (1) the rural market is very large, (2) TruBridge holds 30%-plus market share as one of the two dominant EHRs in that market, and (3) the service mix in the rural market is very similar to the ambulatory market.

subsections.label: Acquisition philosophy / capital allocation criteria (Q&A)
points: IKS does not pursue acquisitions for the sake of acquisitions; strategic thesis must be the mainstay driver, and the deal must also make financial sense.
Two financial criteria: should not create too much leverage relative to current EBITDA, and must be accretively priced.
TruBridge example: acquired $68 million of EBITDA for about $550 million — a healthy accretive addition, with further upside expected from synergies.

subsections.label: Future M&A stance (Q&A)
points: Reaching the INR3,000 crore EBITDA True North target does not require additional acquisitions, but the door for acquisitions is not closed; an acquisition could result in doing better or worse than INR3,000 crores.
Currently focused on disciplined execution given the heavy integration workload underway.

Management views the space as having a lot of white-space opportunity going forward; circumspect about the future of point-solution vendors, including RCM-only back-office vendors, as buying behavior shifts from intellectual recognition of full-platform value to actual full-platform buying; expects to face acquisition opportunities frequently and will need to remain highly disciplined.

subsections.label: Deal close and combined scale
points: TruBridge acquisition closed July 10, 2026, subsequent to Q1 FY27.
Combined global employee base post-TruBridge is north of 16,000.

subsections.label: TruBridge revenue base reset
points: TruBridge's operating revenue base is lower than anticipated pre-close (~$300 million/year steady-state vs ~$340 million/year anticipated), driven by more conservative revenue recognition, elimination of two unprofitable service lines, and anticipated customer discounts during operating model transformation — though EBITDA of ~$68 million remains intact.

subsections.label: Integration execution risk
points: Culture integration risk flagged based on past experience with acquisitions — 'culture eats strategy and execution for breakfast'; commitment to building a single institutionalized culture across ~16,000+ employees from legacy TruBridge and legacy IKS.
Heads-down integration workload cited as a reason for near-term acquisition discipline/caution.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity risk
points: Competitive intensity in the space is increasing and expected to keep increasing given the large and growing TAM; about 30 point-solution vendors (including Abridge) are aspiring to evolve into platforms, creating potential competitive pressure, though not all will succeed.
In renewal conversations with large health systems, increasing competitive intensity manifests partly as pricing pressure from new platform providers.

subsections.label: LLM cost dependency risk
points: Reliance on front-line large language commercial models carries high and hard-to-justify token costs over time, motivating the shift to proprietary SLMs to reduce this dependency.

subsections.label: Currency (mitigating context)
points: Forex gain was neutral in Q1 versus substantial forex support in Q4, meaning underlying EBITDA performance (35% adjusted) was driven by operational improvements, not currency.

Combined EBITDA growth from IPO to FY30 (if True North achieved)

subsections.label: True North objective reiteration
points: Reiterated True North objective of at least INR3,000 crores EBITDA by FY30, to be achieved with very marginal dilution (only potentially ESOP-related), and returning to the net debt position held prior to the TruBridge acquisition.
If the True North target is hit, combined EBITDA will have grown from INR647 crores (TTM Sept 2024) to INR3,000 crores in about five and a half years from the December 2024 IPO timeline.

subsections.label: Margin recovery plan
points: Plan laid out to return to early-to-mid 30% EBITDA margins after the pro forma drop post-TruBridge consolidation to the 26%-27% range initially, via evolving to appropriate autonomy leveraging generative explainable AI, transforming TruBridge's operating model with technology plus offshore human-in-the-loop, and natural SG&A/operating synergies from combining the two organizations (~$700 million combined revenue business).

subsections.label: Growth aspiration, not formal guidance (Q&A)
points: Management does not provide formal quarter-on-quarter growth guidance; aspiration (not guidance) is to grow the legacy IKS $388 million book of business faster than the ~12% market growth rate in constant currency, implying market share gains.
Non-linearity in growth vs profitability will mostly show up in gross margin, with possible EBITDA/SG&A investments partially offsetting some of that gross margin benefit.

For the TruBridge book, management needs at least two to three quarters to understand historical growth patterns and levers before articulating a TruBridge growth aspiration; aspiration is to be the fastest-growing integrated system of action and system of record in the rural community market, but no revenue-based True North has been set yet — only an EBITDA-based True North, since revenue visibility for TruBridge is still developing.
Legacy IKS growth aspiration remains north of 12% constant currency; TruBridge growth aspiration is still being formed after 2-3 quarters of assessment.

subsections.label: Tax rate outlook
points: Legacy IKS tax rate expected to remain in the 22%-23% range for the rest of FY27; combined pro-forma tax rate (with TruBridge) to be discussed next quarter.

subsections.label: EPS accretion (Q&A)
points: Despite TruBridge revenue rationalization (base reset), FY27 is still expected to be EPS accretive, and possibly even more EPS accretive than originally imagined, because EBITDA remains unchanged despite the lower revenue base.

subsections.label: Integration expense outlook
points: A little integration expense is expected to continue into the next quarter, likely in a range similar to Q1's ~INR20 crores; further detail to be shared with Q2 results.

key_takeaways: Delivered 21% YoY revenue growth for fiscal Q1 (12% in constant currency), resulting in revenues of about INR893 crores, with 33% EBITDA at INR294 crores (approximately 200 bps higher, i.e. ~35%/INR314 crores, adjusting for one-time TruBridge acquisition exceptional costs of ~INR20 crores).
PAT grew about 28% YoY to INR193 crores, with net profit for the period at INR194 crores (22%).

TruBridge acquisition closed July 10, 2026; confirmed TruBridge's ~$68 million annualized operating EBITDA is intact, but steady-state revenue is now estimated at ~$300 million/year versus ~$340 million/year anticipated pre-close, due to conservative revenue recognition, elimination of two unprofitable service lines, and anticipated customer discounts.
Reiterated True North objective of at least INR3,000 crores EBITDA by FY30 with very marginal (ESOP-only) dilution and a return to pre-TruBridge net debt levels.
Plan laid out to return blended EBITDA margins to early-to-mid 30% range after an initial pro forma drop to 26%-27% post-TruBridge consolidation.

Significant client wins this quarter: a large California health system (Epic transition partnership), a national musculoskeletal leader (RCM relationship), expanded flagship relationship with Advocate Health Care (revenue cycle and coding), and a partnership with StrideCare, demonstrating land-and-expand cross-sell momentum in large health systems.
Patent approved for the AAW model (predicting patient no-show and pay propensity), and a case study with Axia Women's Health showing a $12 million cash impact with 96% coding accuracy.
Legacy IKS headcount grew only 4.2% YoY (12,300 to 12,889) versus 12% constant currency revenue growth, demonstrating continued non-linearity between revenue and people growth.

quarters.summary: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 18.5% YoY to INR857 crores (13% in constant currency) with EBITDA margin at ~35% and PAT margin at ~24%; FY26 revenue rose ~20% YoY to INR3,193 crores with EBITDA up 38% and PAT up 48%. Management flagged no formal guidance but reiterated a "True North" vision of tripling EBITDA from ~INR1,000 crores (LTM Dec 2025) to ~INR3,000 crores by FY30, aided by the pending TruBridge acquisition (rural healthcare EHR/RCM) and continued AI-native platform investment, while awaiting regulatory approval to close TruBridge.

subsections.label: Non-linearity between revenue and cost growth
points: Revenue grew 18.5% YoY in Q4 while headcount grew only 5.3% YoY (13,331 vs 12,661 employees), demonstrating non-linearity of the business model.
Headcount actually declined quarter-on-quarter (from Q3 FY26 to Q4 FY26) even as revenue grew 5.2% QoQ.
EBITDA growth (33% YoY) outpaced revenue growth (18.5% YoY) reflecting margin expansion; PAT growth (39% YoY) outpaced EBITDA growth due to falling interest costs from debt paydown.

subsections.label: Q4 P&L nuances (Nithya Balasubramanian)
points: Revenue came in at $95 million with some currency support; forex gain of INR35 crores was partly offset by a hedge loss of INR12 crores, net benefit INR23 crores.

Employee benefit expenses were flattish QoQ in line with headcount; other expenses increased ~INR38 crores QoQ, mostly one-time due diligence and legal fees related to the TruBridge transaction; further transaction expenses expected in Q1.
Finance costs declined sharply vs Q3 which had included a one-off write-off of debt issuance cost upon loan refinancing; interest rates and finance costs have come down.
D&A and interest income broadly in line with Q3.

Q1 calendar (Q4 FY26) is seasonally the weakest quarter for US providers due to insurance reset/deductible dynamics and an intense winter reducing patient footfalls; expected to improve in coming quarters.

subsections.label: ROE dynamics
points: ROE remains healthy at ~31%, though it declined YoY due to revaluation of the company's equity holding in a bridge system (a technology company) based on its own valuation, and revaluation of assets due to rupee depreciation against the dollar widening the base.

subsections.label: Debt and capital allocation
points: Strong FCF generation has enabled debt reduction from a peak of ~INR850 crores to INR251 crores as of March 31, 2026.
Post TruBridge close, leverage is expected to rise to ~3x EBITDA; focus will shift to deleveraging via internal accruals and combined cash flows.

subsections.label: ESOP cost
points: ESOP cost has risen sharply in recent quarters; no specific quarterly run-rate guidance given, but expected to trend in line with continued expansion of technology and leadership teams.
ESOP used as a tool to align employee incentives with shareholder value creation; additional ESOP incentives planned for TruBridge leadership post-integration.

subsections.label: Client base rationalization
points: Client count has fallen from ~900 (at AQuity acquisition) to 700+ (prior year) to 600+ now, reflecting deliberate cutting of the long tail of small clients inherited through AQuity, since the traditional model works best with large clients.
Management expects to eventually settle between 500 and 600 clients, viewing the tail-cutting process as more or less complete.

subsections.label: Top customer contribution variability
points: Quarterly top-10 revenue contribution figures (43%, 45%, 48% in Q1-Q3 FY26) look higher than the 37% annual figure; management attributes this to quarterly variances and seasonality, particularly in the revenue optimization/RCM business, and recommends viewing metrics on an annual basis.
Clients with revenue >$1 million saw a slight decline in count because some AQuity customers in that band experienced shrinkage as they were offshored and offered discounts.

subsections.label: Key customer relationships highlighted
points: Holyoke Medical Center: a mid-sized health system from the legacy AQuity customer base cross-sold the entire IKS platform; notably, not incentivized via outcomes-based pricing to adopt the full platform, demonstrating organic value of the platform.

Mission Community: an existing full-platform customer advancing to a unique AI-driven relationship to predict ICU utilization, operation theatre utilization, and nurse utilization for better resource allocation.
A top-five health system in the AQuity customer base significantly expanded its revenue cycle and value-based care relationship, evidencing the land-and-expand approach for large health systems.

subsections.label: Revenue growth composition
points: Management does not break down growth between volume and value, citing multiple drivers: number of physicians at a client, proportion of physicians actively using the product, patient footfall, and expansion in the number of features used per physician — all varying non-linearly year to year.

Management does not disclose a breakup of revenue between single-solution and multi-solution/platform customers, citing the core thesis that the bulk of revenue is expected to migrate to platform constructs over time.

subsections.label: AI-native agentic platform evolution
points: Business model evolved from human-led tech-in-the-loop (started 18-19 years ago) to tech-led human-in-the-loop (2010-2020) to AI-native agentic platform manifest starting ~2022-2023, with ambition to move as many features as possible to fully autonomous agentic execution.

Launched an interconnected agentic workflow for autonomous clinical documentation, coding, and prior authorization — tasks that cause the greatest friction in patient/provider workflows and have compounding effects when done together.

Launched 'Scribble Select', a multi-variant ambient AI scribing product allowing doctors to choose between a human-in-the-loop variant (for complex encounters) and the fully autonomous 'Scribble Now' variant (for simpler visits), addressing the observed ceiling of 50-60% doctor utilization of pure autonomous ambient scribing tools.
Continuing advances in autonomous coding with high accuracy already achieved for two specialties, with plans to expand further.
Launched MyCare Hub, a multi-agent orchestration technology spanning patient engagement features like scheduling optimization, patient onboarding, and eligibility/benefits verification.
Autonomous coding, revenue cycle engine, and MyCare Hub are now available in Epic Connection Hub, important for penetrating large health systems where Epic is the system of record.

subsections.label: Neuro-symbolic AI and 'Glass Box AI' construct
points: Generative AI (neuro models) is best suited for non-deterministic outcomes (e.g., ambient scribing narrative documentation); deterministic outcomes require combining generative AI with symbolic AI relying on knowledge graphs, ontologies, and rules/logic.
Autonomy is also constrained by the technology readiness of external counterparties (payers, clearinghouses, other providers) interacted with for tasks like referral management.

Acquihire of ARAI (founded by Dr. Roland Haas and Dr. Asoke Talukdar) brings proprietary IP including knowledge graphs and clinical decision support systems, accelerating the neuro-symbolic/'Glass Box AI' journey.

Glass Box AI concept: instead of inferring codes directly from clinical notes (traditional AI), the model maps documentation to standardized ontologies, validates relationships against known medical knowledge, and flags low-confidence outputs for human review — yielding higher accuracy, lower denials, and a clear audit trail.

ARAI has already built knowledge graphs for autonomous medical coding, denials prediction/prevention in revenue cycle, and other clinical decision support features, expected to significantly accelerate build-out versus building from scratch.
ARAI's IP becomes more valuable if the TruBridge transaction closes, given the AI training corpus opportunity it would create.

subsections.label: Certilytics partnership
points: Partnership with Certilytics (an AI-driven innovator on the payer side) aims to reduce provider-payer friction in the revenue cycle by enabling better collaboration, particularly around denials related to medical documentation or coding (excluding utilization-related claim assessment APIs, which payers are unlikely to expose).
Ambition is to elevate IKS's RCM positioning by improving outcomes through more collaborative, technology/AI-driven engagement with payers, at least in certain segments.

subsections.label: Deterministic vs non-deterministic autonomy tracking
points: Company tracks autonomy progress feature-by-feature across the 16-feature platform; even '100% autonomy' as tracked does not mean complete elimination of human-in-the-loop given healthcare's edge cases.

Two key drivers of achievable autonomy per feature: (1) whether the outcome is deterministic (requiring symbolic AI overlay) vs non-deterministic (better suited to generative AI), and (2) the technology readiness of external entities involved in the task.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape framework
points: Three genres of competition: (1) systems of record — EHR vendors, a finite/legacy category now adding generative/agentic AI; (2) point solution systems of action — the fastest-growing and easiest-to-enter category, addressing 1-3 tasks; (3) rare platform systems of action (like IKS) offering a comprehensive, accountable, interconnected feature set.
Any YoY growth above 12% (outsourced TAM growth) implies IKS is gaining market share; growth below that implies share loss.

Increasing PE capital and consolidation (e.g., Carlyle Group's recent purchase of two RCM-space companies) reflect rising competitive intensity, concentrated mainly in the point-solution category due to lower entry barriers; consolidation in that space is expected to continue as commoditization increases, pushing players to scale.

subsections.label: Differentiated go-to-market strategy
points: For mid-sized health-system-owned medical groups and independent physician groups: continue full platform-based GTM.

For large health systems: pivoted to a land-and-expand, point-solution-led entry strategy (RCM, coding, patient access features) after learning that large health-system buyers are typically point-solution focused users rather than C-suite platform decision-makers, and that large health systems currently lack appetite for full-platform adoption despite intellectual interest.
This requires IKS to rank number one, two, or three in each point solution sold to large health systems while remaining the only company with a full platform manifest for other market segments.

Recognitions: #1 in AI-driven RCM per Black Book; top performer in ambulatory RCM per KLAS, close to the #1 ambulatory RCM provider position; strong ratings in documentation and coding from both Black Book and KLAS.

subsections.label: Pricing model and productivity/deflation dynamics
points: IKS's outcome-based pricing (percentage of customer revenue) differs fundamentally from traditional IT services/BPO headcount- or transaction-based pricing, giving IKS a differentiated ability to capture AI-driven efficiency gains in margins rather than passing them fully to clients.

Minor pricing deflation on a percentage-of-revenue basis is expected over time, and has already been observed in features bought individually by large health systems (e.g., Ambient AI scribing product pricing has already seen deflation).

Deflation is expected to be greater in easily autonomizable features and lower in features that are harder to autonomize; this dynamic favors the platform system-of-action model over point solutions, since platform pricing is less prone to commoditization than individually priced point solutions.

subsections.label: CommonSpirit Health opportunity
points: CommonSpirit Health (a large healthcare provider with multiple Epic instances) terminated its deal with Tenet, creating a potential opportunity; IKS has past working history with several 'ministries' within CommonSpirit and is monitoring as CommonSpirit's own strategy becomes clearer.
IKS has increased its Epic marketplace listings to seven from a couple a few quarters back.
