quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 27% YoY, EBITDA grew 55% YoY and PAT grew 64% YoY, in line with quarter-on-quarter guidance and ahead of annual guidance. Management expects FY27 growth to be a couple of percentage points bigger than FY26's 21% YoY growth, driven by faster-than-envisaged construction industry growth, with Q2 FY27 expected to be in line with Q1 FY27, and H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1 as ag industry recovery plays out; cycle EBITDA margin guided at 20%+ with FY27 comfortably above 20%, and FY28 growth expected to continue as large ag and small ag recovery adds a second growth lever.

key_figures.label: Cash balance at time of special dividend

subsections.label: Cash flow and balance sheet
points: Net cash position rebuilt to ~INR190 crores in just 10 months since the special dividend payout of INR101 crores in October 2025, when cash balance was approximately INR210 crores, through focused operations and business growth.
Balance sheet described as in excellent health; company continues to actively evaluate acquisition opportunities to accelerate strategic agenda.

Company is debt-free with roughly INR190 crores of cash on hand, providing sufficient capacity for an acquisition; management confirmed the balance sheet is strong enough to raise debt if needed for an acquisition.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Cost of materials at 33.3% in the quarter is largely due to a product mix change (bifurcation of three-point linkage, precision machined parts and fabrication business, which have similar margins but different material consumption percentages), plus a small inventory gain of about INR1 crore.

Margin differentiation is driven mainly by delivery channel: locally made and locally sold has the lowest margin profile, direct exports carry a base margin of around 20%, and warehouse sales carry the highest margin; higher warehouse-led sales in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 positively impacted EBITDA margin percentages.

Company reiterated confidence in delivering FY27 EBITDA margin comfortably above the 20% cycle guidance, with the exact level depending on industry recovery pace, proportion of warehousing sales, and currency movements.

Gross margin differences versus the FY22 cycle stem from a changed product mix and a different mix of warehousing sales versus direct export versus locally made/locally sold; company remains confident of maintaining material cost range of 34%-37% and 20% EBITDA margin over the cycle.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Capex requirements remain roughly 2.5% to 3.5% of total revenue, covering fresh equipment, repairs and maintenance for the organic business, inclusive of all organic growth opportunities across three-point linkage, precision machined parts and fabrication, and across OEM and aftermarket.

The October 2025 special dividend was paid because at that time there was no line of sight for an inorganic investment opportunity; capital allocation decisions are constantly reviewed at the Board level.

subsections.label: New business momentum
points: Trailing 12-month new business order book remains robust at over INR225 crores with a healthy pipeline; wins span segments and geographies, reflecting continued customer confidence across the 3 product platforms.
New business momentum described as structural, with intention to build on it.

New order win book is pretty much similar across Europe and the U.S.; as the cycle follows through and new business comes through in revenue, this should be reflected in revenue contribution from both a segment and geography point of view.
New business wins are split almost equally between ag and construction industry; focus is really on large ag and construction because runways are much higher than in small ag.

key_figures.label: Construction equipment share of total revenue

subsections.label: Three product platforms
points: Company operates across 3 product platforms: three-point linkage for agricultural, PMP (precision machined parts) and fabrications.
Continuing to invest in growing construction and large agricultural equipment businesses, given that small ag is already a segment where the company holds significant global market share.

subsections.label: Construction equipment
points: Construction is today 45% of total revenue; structural drivers behind growth are new business wins, construction industry recovery and wallet expansion, all multi-quarter in nature and expected to persist.
As the ag cycle broadens, product and geographic mix is expected to rebalance — this is expected and considered healthy.

Momentum that started in second half of calendar year 2025 continued into Q1 FY27, supported by infrastructure-led spending: technology investments in the U.S. and government-led investments in Europe sustaining healthy customer schedules and order visibility.
Segment growth is supported by both market recovery and new business additions.
New order win book is similar across Europe and the U.S.; as new business flows into revenue, this should be reflected in both segment and geography revenue contribution.

subsections.label: Large agricultural equipment
points: Conditions remain subdued, widely acknowledged across the industry; leading OEMs indicate calendar year 2026 represents the cyclical bottom, with more meaningful recovery expected through calendar year 2027.

Growth in this segment is not market-driven but entirely the result of new business wins, with particular momentum in Europe; considered a natural extension of core competency and a segment being invested in with a long-term view.
Historically lower market share in large ag versus small ag because large ag is a Western-market business requiring a lengthy OEM validation and testing process before awards flow into revenue.

FY26 saw good new large ag business awards start flowing into P&L, generating more customer excitement about further large ag opportunities; company is in deep discussions with customers on multiple opportunities in this segment.

In the above-70 HP three-point linkage segment, company holds single-digit market share — described as its biggest growth runway, having won new business including with a major OEM in Europe last year.

subsections.label: Small agriculture equipment
points: India continues to perform well, supported by government subsidy programs and rising adoption across mid-to-higher horsepower categories; new business wins in India in small ag have been particularly strong.

In Western markets, small ag growth remains more measured; consumer appetite for big-ticket equipment purchases tempered by economic uncertainty and volatility, leading to continued deferral of buying decisions.

After 3 consecutive years of volume decline, some recovery in unit volumes is being seen and the direction of growth is encouraging; business growth remains strong driven by share position and continued new business additions.

India is the largest producer of tractors in the world, with 50% of tractors produced there, all of which is small ag — described as the company's home market advantage, which was expanded globally into a meaningful share of the small ag segment.

subsections.label: Aftermarket / 3PL business
points: Represents approximately 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue and was flat YoY in absolute terms.

Tariff-driven price volatility led to demand skewing as higher prices caused customers and channel partners to moderate purchasing; with tariffs having come down, normalization and return to growth are expected.

OEM business has grown strongly, naturally reducing aftermarket as a proportion of overall revenue (aftermarket fell from 20% of revenue in FY25 to 15% in FY26 to 12% now), even though absolute aftermarket revenue has remained flat.

Demand deferral in aftermarket is largely a channel problem driven by macroeconomic factors — tariffs and inflation caused by the West Asia crisis; over next 12 months this is expected to normalize as tariffs have reduced.

Aftermarket acted as an anchor when OEM business declined in FY25; now that OEM business is growing, softness in aftermarket is being absorbed — demonstrating derisking of the business model built to perform over cycles.

Company added the second largest aftermarket player as a customer back in FY25 and continues efforts to add new retail channels/distributors in the U.S. and Europe for 3PL aftermarket; will provide updates as these materialize.

subsections.label: Channel mix
points: Margins across products (three-point linkage, precision machined parts, fabrication) are fairly similar; differentiation comes from delivery channel — locally made/locally sold lowest margin, direct exports ~20% base margin, warehouse sales highest margin.
Warehousing sales share increased from 50-52% in Q1 FY26 to 56% in Q1 FY27; locally made locally sold share fell from 25% to 22% over the same period; balance is direct export.
Expected warehousing sales range of 52% to 56% over next 12-18 months, though exact stacking will depend on how each channel mix grows relative to industry and customer demand.

subsections.label: Ludhiana facility restoration
points: Restoration of the finishing shop at the Ludhiana facility is progressing well and on schedule, with customer supply remaining uninterrupted throughout.

subsections.label: Fabrication facility investment
points: 2.5 years ago, the company invested in a new facility for small and medium-sized fabrication, developed while waiting for acquisitions to materialize, allowing the company to start supplying fabrications to OEM customers in addition to PMP and 3PL.

Fabrication vertical is expected to become a meaningful vertical within the next 18 to 24 months, though its growth will not require use of cash balances beyond the stated 2.5%-3.5% of revenue capex guidance.

subsections.label: Mexico operations
points: Mexico operations are on track, with first customer deliveries from the warehouse expected in Q3 of this year — described as a meaningful milestone in the company's journey as a global supply partner.

Mexico business structured so most manufacturing happens in India, exporting from India and doing warehouse-managed sales to customers from Mexico; FY27 revenue from Mexico expected to be at a mid-single-digit million dollar level.
As customers move production to Mexico and expand Mexico facilities, Mexico revenue is expected to grow; in Phase 2, the company will also consider manufacturing in Mexico.

Mexico warehouse sales will increase warehousing sale proportion if all else remains constant, but as the industry turns, locally made/locally sold and direct export requirements are also increasing with rising customer demand.

subsections.label: Regional demand dynamics
points: U.S. ag market is the most hit, followed by Europe; India ag market is doing very well; Japan is stable and the rest of Asia is stable.
New business wins are equally spread across Europe and U.S.; a majority of new business is split between Europe and U.S., with new business also equally split between ag and construction industries.
Construction industry growth is driven by different underlying levers by region — AI and smart manufacturing investment plus government spending in the U.S., infrastructure spending in Europe.

key_figures.label: Above 70 HP three-point linkage market share

subsections.label: Acquisition pipeline
points: Company continues to actively evaluate acquisition opportunities that can accelerate its strategic agenda; has evaluated about a dozen targets since IPO across hydraulic fabrication and PTO, and on a few occasions came very close to making an acquisition but the deal fell through for different reasons — mainly because management is unwilling to proceed unless confident it will be value accretive for all stakeholders.
Currently about half a dozen acquisition opportunities are being closely evaluated; management will update investors as and when more information is available.

Acquisition criteria: must allow the company to add value for customers using current processes, product knowledge and competencies; must be ROCE and ROE accretive within an 18 to 30-month span; must add a meaningful platform in hydraulics, PTOs and fabrications; size must be manageable by the current team; company will not pursue deeply distressed assets.

If an acquisition also enables entry into other industries (e.g., aerospace, defense, automotive) while serving existing customers, the company would consider it, though core focus remains off-highway markets.

subsections.label: TAM and wallet expansion
points: Company's top customers include the top 5 global agricultural customers and the top 3 construction OEM manufacturers.

In below-70 HP three-point linkage, company has dominant global market share and continues to win new business; in above-70 HP three-point linkage, company is at single-digit market share, seen as its biggest growth runway.

For precision machined parts supplied to top 3 construction equipment manufacturers, the company still represents only a fraction of these customers' total relevant sourcing spend, indicating significant room to grow via wallet expansion.

Growth ambitions are based on wallet expansion with current customers (a fairly large existing market) plus portfolio addition via acquisitions in hydraulics, PTOs and large fabrication; company is already associated with adjacent sectors like AI/smart manufacturing and mining through its construction customers.

subsections.label: West Asia situation
points: The ongoing West Asia situation has continued to exert pressure on input costs and supply chains; teams navigated this with discipline, working closely with vendors, ensuring delivery commitments were met without disruption.

subsections.label: Tariff and macro impact on aftermarket
points: Tariff-driven price volatility caused demand skewing in aftermarket, with customers and channel partners moderating purchases; demand deferral in the aftermarket segment is a channel problem driven by macroeconomic factors — tariffs and inflation caused by the West Asia crisis.
Tariffs have since come down, and normalization of aftermarket demand is expected over the next 12 months.

subsections.label: Consumer deferral in small ag
points: In Western small ag markets, consumer appetite for big-ticket equipment purchases has been tempered by economic uncertainty and volatility, leading to continued deferral of buying decisions.

key_figures.label: FY26 revenue growth YoY (base for FY27 guidance)

subsections.label: Revenue growth outlook
points: Q1 FY27 performance is in line with quarter-on-quarter guidance shared earlier but better than the annual guidance given, reflecting quality of execution.
Overall FY27 growth expected to be a couple of percentage points bigger than FY26's 21% YoY growth, given visibility into faster-than-envisaged construction industry growth.
Q2 FY27 expected to be robust and in line with Q1 FY27.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1 FY27 given ag industry recovery is expected in the second half.
FY28 growth trajectory expected to continue as large ag and small ag recovery add a second growth lever alongside construction.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Cycle EBITDA margin (peak to trough) maintained at 20%; FY27 will be delivered comfortably above the 20%-plus margin level.
Exact margin level depends on pace of industry recovery, proportion of warehousing sales, and currency movements; company is focused on executing what is within its control.

subsections.label: Industry cycle outlook
points: Small ag industry growth expected to come through in calendar year 2027.
Large ag industry facing its trough in calendar year 2026, with mid-teens decline expected this year (specifically 15-16% degrowth versus 30% degrowth in CY25); growth expected to return in FY28.
Construction industry recovery started mid-last calendar year and is flowing through this year, expected to continue into FY27 and FY28.

India tractor industry demand stable but impact of monsoons on demand remains to be seen.

themes.label: Cyclical demand recovery
themes.note: Construction already recovering strongly (45% of revenue); small ag recovery starting but meaningful growth pushed to CY27; large ag still at CY26 trough with mid-teens decline before FY28 recovery

themes.label: 3PL-PMP derisking strategy

themes.label: Input cost inflation

key_takeaways: The first quarter of FY27 reflects the divergent dynamics currently shaping our end markets and importantly, how we are navigating them.
The restoration of the finishing shop at our Ludhiana facility is progressing well and on schedule, and customer supply has remained uninterrupted throughout.
Mexico operations are on track with first customer deliveries from the warehouse expected in Q3 of this year, a meaningful milestone in our journey as a global supply partner.

We are pleased to report revenue growth of 27% year-on-year, EBITDA growth of 55% year-on-year and a PAT growth of 64% year-on-year, in line with quarter-on-quarter guidance but better than the annual guidance we had given.
The ongoing West Asia situation has continued to exert pressure on input costs and supply chains.
Our trailing 12-month new business order book remains robust at over INR225 crores with a healthy pipeline.
On the construction equipment, the momentum that started in the second half of calendar year 2025 has continued into Q1 of FY27.

Large agricultural equipment conditions remain subdued; leading OEMs have indicated that current year 2026 represents the cyclical bottom with a more meaningful recovery expected through calendar year 2027.
Our aftermarket business represents approximately 12% of revenue in Q1 of FY27 and was flat year-on-year in absolute terms.
Our FY27 growth will be a couple of percentage points bigger than the growth that we had in FY26 on a year-on-year basis.
pressing_questions: The company has been highlighting regarding the acquisition and additional opportunities of PTOs and fabrication from 2023. When can we see it actually materializing and meaningfully contributing to revenue?

quarters.summary: Uniparts closed FY26 with revenue growth ahead of guidance (21% FY26 vs mid-teens guided; Q4 up 31% YoY/18% QoQ) as the global ag & construction cycle turns; management expects FY27 growth broadly in line with FY26, supported by improving industry cycle, new business wins (~INR225 crore trailing-12-month annualized potential), gradual recovery across geographies, with H2 FY27 expected stronger than H1, and EBITDA margin expected to sustain comfortably above the 20% steady-state level, though the exact outcome depends on volume ramp-up and delivery channel mix.

key_figures.label: Currency-driven inventory valuation gain impact on material cost

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Improving profitability driven by two factors: operating leverage now clearly visible at the full-year level as volumes increase, and conscious cost discipline through the year with expense increases limited to inflation-driven or necessary variable expenses.
Full year revenue expanded 21% while EBITDA grew north of 55%, demonstrating operating leverage playing out.

Company has consistently said 20% EBITDA margin is sustainable over the cycle; as volumes build through FY27, expects to operate comfortably above that level; exact outcome depends on pace of revenue ramp-up and delivery channel mix.

Q4 margin of 23.9%/24% driven by: (1) 18% sequential growth largely volume-led giving operating leverage more room to play, fixed costs better absorbed; (2) sequential increase in warehousing sales (highest-margin segment) from Q3 to Q4.
Material cost of 35% in Q4 has come back to the normal range of 34% to 37%.
Company reiterated it is P&L neutral as far as tariffs are concerned — no one-off tariff refund impact in margins.

Freight and raw material cost components are a direct pass-through to customers; volume increases and currency depreciation help mitigate inflationary elements; employee cost (variable) increases are being absorbed via operating leverage.
Two years ago warehousing sales were at 46-47% of sales; company had guided to reach 50% level in two years, which has now been achieved.
FY26 turnover of ~INR1,200 crores (last reached in earlier cycle) now delivered with better EBITDA margins than at that earlier time.

subsections.label: Working capital
points: Net working capital improved from 155 to 136 days, driven by both inventory and receivable improvement.

Business model involves nearshoring — manufacturing in India, shipping to overseas warehouses, then supplying to customers just-in-time — keeping inventory levels structurally high; conscious effort reduced inventory from 146 days (FY25) to 134 days (FY26).
Receivable days and payable days have been brought almost at par in FY26.
Company believes these working capital levels are sustainable with continuing efforts.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Special dividend of INR101 crores declared in Q3 FY26 was partly a result of evaluating an acquisition opportunity carefully and then deciding not to proceed.
Total dividend distributed for FY26 was INR170 crores, underscoring commitment to disciplined capital allocation and shareholder returns.

An analyst suggested share buybacks could be more tax-efficient than dividends under recent tax policy changes (buyback tax for shareholders ranges 12.5%-20% vs 36% dividend taxation; for promoters buyback tax is ~30% vs higher dividend tax) — management did not respond to this specific suggestion in the transcript.

key_figures.label: Proportion of new business wins from Large Ag and PMP

subsections.label: Order book dynamics
points: Order books strengthened sequentially in Q4 FY26 compared to Q3 FY26, though pace of recovery varied across geographies and industry segments.

New business momentum has gained meaningful traction with trailing-12-month wins exceeding INR225 crores, growing over 12.5% quarter-on-quarter; wins are distributed across segments and geographies, providing visibility into future growth.

Company's largest runway for growth remains in large ag and PMP; new business wins in these two segments are broad-based, with 70% of new business win proportion coming from these segments; continues to win new business in small ag as well.

New order wins figure (~INR225 crores) represents annualized potential of new projects won in the trailing 12 months on a rolling window basis — old projects fall off as they generate revenue, new ones are added; this figure has held at INR200 crore-plus for several quarters, indicating consistent win rate and conversion of older wins into actual revenue as the cycle improves.

During the down cycle of the last 2 years (one of the deepest troughs in ag/construction equipment industry in 30-40 years), OEM customer demand fell, impacting Uniparts sales and causing order books to decline; consequently, previously won new business either got delayed or was executed in smaller amounts.
FY27 growth visibility is based on the order book itself — expected growth in range of ~20% (in line with FY26).

subsections.label: Pricing / cost pass-through
points: Currency depreciation is linked to inflation; FX pass-throughs to customers are netted off against inflation increases as per customer contract design and negotiations.
Freight and raw material cost components are a direct pass-through to customers.

subsections.label: 3PL and PMP derisking strategy
points: 3PL revenue has come down almost 30% over the last 3-4 years due to the tractor market downturn, but the company has not lost market share; revenue from 3PL and PMP is now almost a 50-50 split as company has grown with construction segment customers as a derisking strategy.
Company maintains its SOBs (share of business) and continues to grow with both ag customers and PMP business.
Strategy is to maintain derisking growth across both segments (3PL and PMP) and both industries (ag and construction) as it grows with different customers and product lines going forward.

subsections.label: PMP growth potential
points: PMP business supplies pins and bushings that go into articulated joints, critical for operations/functions of equipment manufactured by Agri and construction equipment customers.

Company is 100% supplier or has a large share of business with top 3 construction equipment manufacturers globally for the products it supplies, but remains only a fraction of their total relevant category spend — this represents the structural growth opportunity for PMP.
Over a 2-year period, 3-point linkage business share moved from >50% and PMP from ~45% to now roughly 50-50.

subsections.label: New product wins by segment
points: New wins in trailing 12 months (~INR225 crores) are broad-based across construction and agriculture industries, with emphasis on large ag and PMP segments where majority of new business has come.

New products being supplied include 3-point linkage products in large ag and precision machine parts (PMP) in the PMP segment; products remain technically similar to current manufacturing but features/specifications differ order to order.

Margins are driven by delivery channel (direct exports = base/steady-state 20% margin; local manufacture/local delivery = lower margin; warehousing sales = somewhat higher margin) rather than by end segment (large ag vs PMP).

subsections.label: Aftermarket
points: Aftermarket (U.S. and Europe) continues to be a stable contributor to revenues across North America and Europe for FY26.
Q4 FY26 aftermarket performance was better than Q3 FY26; sequentially Q1 FY27 aftermarket expected to be in line with Q4 FY26.
Aftermarket tariff-related dynamics are specific to the U.S.; growth as % of revenue has not yet returned to earlier historical levels despite sequential improvement post-tariff normalization.

subsections.label: R&D and engineering collaboration
points: Company invests in R&D; given it works with world's largest ag and construction equipment customers, it maintains engineering teams that collaborate with customer engineering teams to assess feasibility of products and co-design specific solutions.

This engineering collaboration is credited as a key reason for winning new business, especially in large ag, where significant new wins occurred over the last year, growing strongly to reach 20% of FY26 revenue.

Company continues to work on new products with customers across all segments; no specific single new product was disclosed beyond the 3-point linkage (large ag) and PMP (precision machine parts) categories.
Oilfield/oil-and-gas products (highlighted at IPO) continue to be manufactured and supplied to current customers, with efforts continuing to expand that product line.

key_figures.label: Number of acquisition targets evaluated since IPO

subsections.label: Capacity strategy
points: Capacity, including maintenance capex, is maintained in the range of 2.5% to 3.5% of revenue; when investing in capacity, company evaluates whether incremental investment can yield better capability or higher capacity.
When new business is won, typically only balancing capex is required (not large new capex), keeping capex within the 2.5%-3.5% of revenue range.

Steady-state EBITDA margin of 20% over a cycle allows continued investment in the business for customers even during downturns; over the last 2 years the company continued to invest in capabilities across the group, including in-sourcing in the U.S. factory and building out warehousing/nearshoring model with investment in Mexico.
Company states it is not capacity-constrained to any particular peak revenue level and can continue to accept growth as it comes.

Company is a batch and discrete manufacturing company; capacity is defined by bottleneck processes; capacity investments are planned to ensure only balancing capex is needed when new business arrives.

Capacity is largely fungible between the two main business lines (3PL and PMP) for many processes, though certain processes may not be fungible; capacity allocation/planning aims to ensure adequate room for growth.

subsections.label: Fire incident at Ludhiana facility
points: Towards the end of Q3 FY26, a fire incident occurred in the finishing shop of one of the Ludhiana facilities; company swiftly implemented interim arrangements, primarily leveraging subsidiary operations and, to a limited extent, select external partners, enabling uninterrupted customer support with minimal disruption.
Rebuilding effort is underway; incident is fully covered under insurance policy and claim was filed during the quarter; normal operations expected to return on schedule (by end of the year).

Insurance policy covers fixed assets and inventory losses as well as loss of profits (LOP), including any increased costs incurred due to the fire; management stated no expected impact on margins because of comprehensive insurance coverage.

subsections.label: Mexico expansion
points: Company continues to build out its warehousing/nearshoring model with investment in Mexico; currently in discussions with 3 customers in Mexico, 2 of which are in ramp-up phase; as these businesses fructify, expected to provide another impetus to profitability.

subsections.label: Regional industry outlook
points: North America construction equipment: customer commentary and industry data point to continued growth in FY27, demand expected to gradually strengthen through the year with H2 better than H1; market supported by data center investment, advanced manufacturing and broader digital infrastructure spending in the U.S.

Europe construction equipment: market appears to have passed its cyclical low, with early signs of recovery becoming more visible in Q4 FY26; demand for compact equipment has been a bright spot; infrastructure-led spending supported by fiscal stimulus, defense investment and energy transition projects expected to provide a more stable demand environment; recovery is gradual, with modest growth anticipated for the full year.

Small agriculture North America: on path of recovery, led by livestock and dairy production demand, with higher end of smaller ag sector range also showing resilience as farmers cycle through equipment replacement; segment poised for ~5% growth in FY27 in line with industry estimates.

Small agriculture Europe: showing early signs of stabilization after prolonged softening; recovery gradual with momentum expected to build through H2; FY27 outlook positive with modest growth anticipated; growth in small ag Europe expected to be stronger in H2 than H1.

India tractor industry: demand remains stable, though monsoon impact remains to be seen; inventory replenishment gaining traction and order book strengthening; company well positioned given strong market share and diversified presence, with confidence in delivering healthy growth through FY27.

Large agricultural machinery: continues to work through current down cycle; leading OEMs affirm Q4 FY26 represents a cyclical trough; in North America, industry volumes for large tractors continue to track down in mid-to-high teens YoY; in Europe, sentiment is gradually improving and is ahead of North America in recovery.
South America outlook is showing some weakness per an analyst question; management did not quantify Uniparts' exposure to South America directly in response.

subsections.label: Geopolitical supply chain disruption
points: In March, a fresh escalation in West Asia introduced supply chain uncertainty requiring swift action; teams put alternate arrangements in place rapidly to ensure uninterrupted customer supplies.
Evolving geopolitical situation has resulted in increasing input prices, partly mitigated by favourable exchange rates.
Foremost priority remains business continuity and customer service; company continues to closely monitor developments and will respond proactively as situation evolves.

subsections.label: Customer inventory behavior
points: Regardless of tariffs, customers aim to maintain sufficient inventory to serve their end customers on time; in aftermarket, customers build inventory ahead of high season sales; in OEM channel, as the industry cycle picks up and OEMs work through backlog orders, they are ordering more from Uniparts.
Company's inventories in its warehouses are rising in absolute terms as OEM ordering increases, though days of inventory remain under control.

subsections.label: Customer concentration and market share
points: Company is a 100% supplier, or holds a large share of business, to the top 3 construction equipment manufacturers globally for the specific product categories it supplies, but remains a small fraction of their total relevant category spend.

No market share has been lost in the 3PL segment despite a ~30% revenue decline over the last 3-4 years, as SOBs (share of business) with ag customers have been maintained while growth has also occurred with PMP/construction customers.

key_figures.label: Number of acquisition targets close to completion

subsections.label: Acquisition pipeline
points: Company has evaluated about a dozen acquisition targets since IPO across platforms it wants to grow in; has been close to completing acquisitions on 2 occasions, both of which fell apart for varied reasons.

Internal acquisition framework requires: target must add a meaningful third platform, be manageable in size, and be ROE/ROCE accretive; company does not want to acquire merely to claim it has made an acquisition.

The special dividend paid in Q3 FY26 was partly a consequence of having carefully evaluated an acquisition opportunity and then deciding not to proceed; company will update investors when something concrete is on the table.

subsections.label: Strategic priorities
points: Management remains focused on executing strategy with discipline, including deepening customer partnerships, broadening presence across segments and geographies, and building a business that is stronger and more adaptable than before.
New business momentum is described as a direct reflection of this strategic effort.

subsections.label: Fire incident
points: Fire incident in finishing shop of a Ludhiana facility toward end of Q3 FY26; interim arrangements (subsidiary operations, limited external partners) used to maintain supply continuity; rebuilding underway, covered under insurance including loss of profit (LOP); normal operations expected back on schedule by end of the year.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / West Asia escalation
points: Fresh escalation in West Asia in March introduced supply chain uncertainty; alternate arrangements were rapidly implemented; situation has led to increasing input prices, partially offset by favourable exchange rates; company continues to monitor and respond proactively.

subsections.label: Tariffs
points: FY26 tested the team with tariff headwinds among other disruptions; company states it is P&L neutral as far as tariffs are concerned.
Aftermarket in the U.S. affected by tariff dynamics; sequential improvement seen but has not yet returned to prior historical percentage-of-revenue levels.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Employee costs in North India reportedly up ~20-25%, a large variable cost component (~20% of total revenue per an analyst's estimate); raw material prices (e.g., steel) near all-time highs; sea freight costs higher.

Currency depreciation is linked to inflation, and some of this inflation is mitigated by favourable exchange rates; freight and raw material costs are largely a direct pass-through to customers; volume growth and currency depreciation help absorb fixed cost inflation via operating leverage.

subsections.label: Cyclical downturn
points: Ag and construction equipment industries experienced one of the deepest cyclical troughs in 30-40 years over the last 2 years, which reduced OEM customer demand, impacted Uniparts sales, caused order books to decline, and delayed or reduced execution of previously won new business.

subsections.label: Large ag North America volume decline
points: Industry volumes for large tractors in North America continue to track down in the mid-to-high teens YoY, though European sentiment is gradually improving.

subsections.label: South America weakness
points: An analyst flagged weakness in the South America market outlook; company's exposure/impact was raised as a question but not directly quantified in the response.

subsections.label: Currency volatility
points: Company is cognizant that currency depreciation can create inventory valuation gains (favorable) while currency appreciation would work in the opposite direction, impacting material costs by roughly 2% either way.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Overall growth in FY27 expected to be in line with FY26, supported by an improving industry cycle, execution of recent business awards/wins, and gradual recovery across end markets.
Q1 FY27 expected to be in line with Q4 FY26; second half of FY27 expected to be stronger than first half of FY27.
Construction segment continues to offer strong visibility across regions, combined with new business awards and improving industry environment supporting growth momentum.
Small ag Europe growth expected to be stronger in H2 than H1; small ag North America poised for ~5% growth in FY27 in line with industry estimates.

India tractor demand remains stable with inventory replenishment gaining traction and order book strengthening, though monsoon impact remains uncertain; company expects healthy growth in this segment through FY27.

Large ag machinery: Q4 FY26 seen by OEMs as cyclical trough; recovery expected to build as production volumes normalize through the year, aided by new program wins in Europe and diversified presence across tractor platforms.
Aftermarket expected to remain a stable contributor to revenue.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Company has consistently guided that 20% EBITDA margin is sustainable over the cycle; as volumes build through FY27, expects to operate comfortably above that level; exact outcome depends on pace of revenue ramp-up and delivery channel mix.
Mexico ramp-up (2 of 3 customers in ramp-up phase) expected to provide additional impetus to profitability as these businesses fructify.

key_takeaways: The final quarter of FY26 provided further evidence that the global agriculture and construction equipment cycle is turning.
Order books strengthened sequentially compared to quarter 3 FY26, although the pace of recovery varied across geographies and industry segments.

In quarter 4 FY26, delivered approximately 31% year-on-year revenue growth and about 18% sequential growth over quarter 3; for the full year FY26, revenue grew by 21% over FY25, higher against the guidance of mid-teens growth given earlier.

One of the Ludhiana facilities experienced a fire incident in the finishing shop toward the end of quarter 3; interim arrangements enabled uninterrupted customer support; the incident is fully covered under insurance and the claim was filed during the quarter.

In March, a fresh escalation in West Asia introduced supply chain uncertainty; alternate arrangements were put in place rapidly; input price inflation from this is being partly mitigated by favourable exchange rates.
New business momentum has gained meaningful traction with trailing 12-month business wins exceeding INR225 crores, growing over 12.5% quarter-on-quarter, distributed across segments and geographies.

Uniparts delivered an EBITDA margin of 24% in quarter 4 FY26 and 22% EBITDA margin for the full year FY26; company continues to be net debt free with a net cash position of INR160 crores as on March 2026.
Trailing 12-month EPS post the quarter 4 results is INR35.07, 80% higher than that at the end of FY25.
Total dividend distributed for FY26 was INR170 crores, including a special dividend of INR101 crores declared during Q3 FY26.

Overall, growth in FY27 is expected to be in line with what it was in FY26, supported by an improving industry cycle, execution of recent business awards and wins, and a gradual recovery across end markets.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 19.2% YoY to ₹370 Cr; standalone sales grew 14.7% YoY with EBITDA up 21.7% YoY, which management framed as proof that the diversification strategy is working. Forward outlook centers on six growth vectors (aerospace, automotive adjacencies, electrification, mobility beyond vehicles, heavy-duty off-highway, mission-critical friction solutions), an FY31 aerospace platform target of ₹300 Cr revenue/₹90 Cr profit, a company-wide ~₹270 Cr capex program, a new Unitech JV for cylindrical roller bearings commissioning by April 2027, and a guidance-conservative but trending-up FY31 total revenue ambition of ₹2,500-3,000 Cr.

subsections.label: Robotics/humanoids and customized precision components
points: Management positioned NRB as a customized solution provider beyond bearings: “we make bearings, but we also make precision components.”

points: Management stated no concrete plan to merge the smaller bearing entity into NRB.
Rationale: preserve niche proprietary tech and entrepreneurial agility—“much more strength in having smaller sized subsidiaries…”
Also described portfolio strategy: different brand/price point helps address price-sensitive replacement demand without ceding share to competitors.

subsections.label: Deliberate strategic pivot built on core engineering/R&D
points: Management emphasized the pivot is adjacent-market expansion, not a leap: “This is a fresh start, it’s not any speculative leap into unknown territory.”
Core differentiators cited: advanced manufacturing + proprietary/copyrighted computational analysis software and simulation.
Integrated engineering stack: dynamic motion studies, lightweighting, noise reduction, materials science, sealing, lubrication, and “breakthrough friction solutions.”
R&D positioned as the “backbone,” with intent to convert engineering capability into new vertical growth.

subsections.label: Six growth vectors management is scaling into
points: Aerospace (small today, strategically critical): acquisition rationale—“We bought access, not capacity… buying speed, not scale.”
Automotive adjacencies beyond legacy: tapered/ball bearing wheel hubs, spherical roller bearings, plus expansion beyond transmission/chassis into steering systems, one-way clutch, wheel bearings.

Electrification beyond EV: merged electric mobility + engineering into a broader “electrification” vertical; focus areas include high-frequency drives, e-2W, off-highway e-mobility, industrial electrification, and issues like electrical erosion mitigation and ultra-low friction torque. Management indicated: “many more new announcements… in the next three to six months.”
Mobility beyond vehicles: robotics, AGVs, “open air mobility,” drones, advanced transit—requiring “micro precision friction management.”
Heavy duty off-highway: highlighted capability in extreme loads/harsh conditions; new customer win: “acquisition of JCB UK as a customer.”

Mission-critical friction solutions (stationary + mobile industrial): industrial gearboxes, data center cooling architecture, renewable/energy drives, precision gearboxes—areas where “downtime carries massive penalties.”

quarters.summary: Management guided FY27 international business growth of ~10-14% (possibly up to 15%) vs FY26's ~4%, reiterated a medium-term aspiration of ~INR2,500 cr revenue in ~5 years supported by potential strategic JVs for import-substitution bearings, and expects margin expansion from the current operational improvement plan and brownfield capex program to be structural rather than one-off, with capex benefits phasing in from FY27 through Q1 2028.

subsections.label: Margin expansion drivers
points: Management emphasized margin expansion is structural, not a 'one-off,' attributing it to a 'comprehensive operational improvement plan,' including: higher solar energy usage leading to lower power & fuel costs; higher automation reducing labor dependence; continuous yield improvements; renegotiated vendor costing across 'material components, logistics, insurance across all elements of material related costs.'

subsections.label: Quality of growth
points: Management explicitly stated, 'we are satisfied with the quality of growth,' citing volume-led growth, market share gains, capacity sweating, mix improvement, and repeatable internal efficiencies.

subsections.label: Q4 gross margin anomaly explained
points: A key investor concern was Q4 gross margin dropping below historical ~60%.

Management attributed it to forex: 'Fundamentally only one reason, foreign exchange,' compounded by product mix and translation effects (including an 'aberration' from exchange rate differential on the last day of the year impacting how overseas entity expenses/COGS were booked).
Management message: not structural; should normalize, and investors should focus on YTD rather than quarter anomalies.

subsections.label: Mahant order book momentum
points: Order book grew from INR25 cr (at acquisition announcement) to ~INR50 cr, which management called a sign HAL has 'heartily endorsed' the NRB ownership change.
Pace of execution is variable in aerospace and depends on platform rollout.

subsections.label: Diversification into industrial friction solutions
points: Strategy is explicitly not commodity industrial bearings; it is 'niche and profitable… specialized application-specific industrial friction solutions' where NRB's engineering can differentiate.
Target segments named: construction equipment, off-highway, industrial gearboxes, switchgears, power generation, and the electric grid transmission ecosystem.

Industrial profitability framework: NRB's hurdle is 18-20% EBITDA for focus areas; management acknowledged dispersion ('some… 30%… some… 14%') but expects the portfolio to align with the goal of 'maintaining profitability consistently between 18% and 21%' over time.

Current scale: industrial business already ~14-15% of revenue, and management's aim is 20-25% (timing uncertain because automotive growth can change the denominator). A rough 'ballpark' offered: ~3 years to reach ~20%, with a caveat that auto cycles may shift the mix.
Capacity fungibility: management stated industrial/automotive capacity is flexible/fungible; even referenced JV flexibility where '20%… may be used for automotive if automotive suddenly requires it.'

subsections.label: Application footprint (automotive)
points: NRB is primarily in transmission, driveline, chassis, steering; less in engine (except 2/3 wheelers) and less in wheel applications (which management called an opportunity).

subsections.label: Illustrative customer/platform penetration
points: Management claimed broad premium OEM fitment in transmissions (e.g., Mercedes platform coverage, BMW 'i' models) and highlighted a patented combined cylindrical thrust bearing used in heavy trailer 'kingpin' applications across global truck brands.

subsections.label: Mahant Tool acquisition: aerospace/defense entry and certification acceleration
points: Rationale: NRB framed Mahant as a shortcut to aerospace manufacturing readiness—'trust me, we saved three years'—primarily by acquiring people, design capability, and certification pathway rather than buying scale.

What Mahant makes (value-chain positioning): 'mission critical areas' for Indian defense aircraft platforms, including landing gear components, fuel injection system parts, doors, and other safety-critical components.
Customer concentration: order book is 100% HAL, but spread across 'multiple divisions… each division is like a company of its own.'

Certifications: Mahant is already 'in the process of certification'; management indicated ~6 months to receive certification, and said NRB-developed products will also be included in that certification scope.

subsections.label: Customer/program positioning and 'mass customization' as a moat
points: Management positioned NRB as structurally advantaged in an environment shifting toward variant-rich platforms: NRB has a 'mass customization mindset,' able to start at small volumes and scale rapidly amid shifting technology winners.

The company emphasized deep co-design integration: bearings are 'co-designed at the platform level,' and NRB is 'deeply embedded… difficult to replace,' citing work on future steering systems (example: Magna's new e-steering platform for BMW stable).

subsections.label: EV/technology stance and pricing discipline
points: NRB positioned itself as technology-agnostic: 'Whether it's ICE… Hybrid… EV,' with bearing content 'largely value neutral.'

EV-specific bearing pricing: management said EV applications are priced 'to maintain our existing margin profile,' and asserted NRB is 'one of the most risk-mitigated companies… when it comes to… pricing and future profitability.'

key_figures.label: Commissioning start timeline for brownfield capex

subsections.label: Utilization reality
points: Reported utilization ~85%, but management argued effective utilization is 'much closer to full' after adjusting for maintenance, shift patterns, changeovers, and demand variability.
Bottlenecks identified at specific plants; brownfield capex initiated with machinery orders placed and 'machines have started to arrive.'

subsections.label: Commissioning timeline
points: Commissioning 'starting from June–July' (near-term) and continuing through FY27 and beyond 'up to the first quarter of 2028.'

Benefit phasing: 'partial benefits initially from the current quarter and more during the rest of the year,' alongside ongoing quality and efficiency gains that should support a higher growth trajectory.

subsections.label: Capex quantum and composition
points: FY27 capex expected: management guided ~INR120 cr (vs analyst's INR80 cr assumption), explicitly noting this includes land.

They also referenced prior public disclosure: ~INR200 cr capex over the next 18 months and up to INR40 cr for land (management framed this as a total announcement of INR240 cr, with INR120 cr being 'just for this year').
Spend mix: '90% for machines and 10% for infrastructure and building and plant.'
Maintenance/normal capex: stated policy-like framework—spend about '10% of our turnover on a combination of maintenance, quality, new product development, and small-small capex improvements.'

subsections.label: International business performance
points: Despite export softness, international business grew 'a little over 4%' YoY (management uses a consolidated 'international customers supplied' lens to avoid intercompany distortions).
Growth was 'not necessarily very satisfying,' but positive given conditions.

subsections.label: Inventory strategy: deliberate buffering as a competitive lever
points: Management proactively defended inventory levels as strategic, with inventory 'positioned across India and key global locations such as Germany and the United States' to absorb logistics volatility and protect customer production schedules—particularly important where NRB is a near-sole supplier.
Importantly, inventory ended >INR20 cr lower YoY despite higher sales, and management said the position is 'close to optimal at this point' given disruptions.
Inventory is linked to pricing power and partnership status: reliability plus engineering capability 'reinforced pricing discipline across cycles.'

subsections.label: Service-level priority
points: Management underlined delivery reliability: 'At no point did we fail to meet key customer commitments… non-negotiable.'
This is positioned as a core moat given high customer share-of-business (often 60-70%, and in some cases ~100%).

subsections.label: Mahant Tool acquisition strategic rationale
points: NRB framed Mahant as a shortcut to aerospace manufacturing readiness—'trust me, we saved three years'—primarily by acquiring people, design capability, and certification pathway rather than buying scale.

subsections.label: Potential strategic JVs
points: Potential strategic JVs for import-substitution bearings not currently made in India.
Government/BIS-driven opportunity; MNCs often sell such products as traded imports due to excess capacity elsewhere, whereas NRB claims it can profitably make smaller volumes.

subsections.label: Operating environment
points: FY26 described as globally difficult (geopolitics, logistics disruptions, energy availability, overseas uncertainty), but domestic business saw no 'material impact.'

subsections.label: Geopolitical shock in Q4
points: The company cited 'sudden challenges… due to the Middle East situation,' and noted India was 'particularly affected by the gas shortage.'
This drove customer-side product-mix changes and some quarter plan shortfall: 'to some extent, the situation did reduce our original business plan for the quarter.'

points: International business growth plan (FY27): management guided ~10-14%, possibly 'even 15%,' vs FY26's ~4%.

Medium-term ambition: reiterated an aspirational (increasingly 'concretized') goal of ~INR2,500 cr revenue in ~5 years, supported by potential strategic JVs for import-substitution bearings not currently made in India, and government/BIS-driven opportunity where NRB claims it can profitably make smaller volumes vs MNCs selling traded imports.

NRBBEARING.about: NRB Bearings have pioneered in the manufacturing of needle roller bearings in India since 1965. More than 90% of the vehicles running on Indian roads are running on bearings manufactured by NRB. The Company is engaged in the business of manufacturing ball and roller bearings having its applications in automotive sector as well as across all mobility applications.

quarters.summary: Greaves Cotton delivered consolidated revenue growth of 31% YoY (core business +16% YoY) in Q1 FY27, but margins came under pressure (2-2.5%) from commodity inflation and purposeful Greaves.Next investments. Management expects Q2 to be marginally better than Q1, with H2 better than H1, and remains committed to full-year FY27 margin targets under Greaves.Next despite near-term pressure. GEML delivered record 101% volume growth, more than doubling revenue, and continues on its path toward EBITDA breakeven in 4-6 quarters, backed by a fully subscribed INR530 crore rights issue.

subsections.label: Margin pressure drivers
points: Margins were lower due to purposeful Greaves.Next investments in people, leadership, SG&A, technology and organizational capabilities to support the next phase of growth.
Commodity prices increased during the quarter, particularly following geopolitical developments in West Asia, resulting in higher input costs (platinum, aluminum, steel, fuel) across most businesses.

Mitigation actions: deferring selective nonessential costs while protecting long-term growth investments, a structured cost control program, and pricing actions where cost increases could not be absorbed.
Cost avoidance and price increase measures expected to begin showing effect from Q2, with full benefits evident in H2 FY27.

subsections.label: Margin outlook commentary
points: Price increase lag versus inflation expected to catch up in Q2 and Q3.
Operating leverage expected to improve as Q1 is historically the smallest quarter.
Full impact of cost savings initiatives to be seen in coming quarters.
Company balancing deferral of some expenses against upfront investments (exports, technological upgrades) that cannot wait, prioritizing long-term growth.
Q2 expected to be marginally better than Q1; H2 expected to be better than H1.
Management remains confident of meeting full-year FY27 margin targets set under Greaves.Next despite near-term pressures.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Board subscribed to GEML's rights issue investing INR331 crores, reflecting confidence in GEML's progress in India's EV landscape.
Board approved additional investment of approximately INR50 crores in Greaves Finance Limited to support its continued growth.
Core business capex on track per strategy; core business continues to generate healthy cash flows with line of sight into future cash flows.
Company is rated AA- with nil debt; financial leverage headroom seen as vital to enable higher ROE and be EPS accretive.

Sufficient liquidity was available in the standalone balance sheet as of March 2026 to fund INR50 crores into GFL and INR331 crores into GEML plus capex and dividend requirements for Q1 and Q2, leaving reasonable cash for FY27 requirements.

subsections.label: Disclosure enhancements
points: Segments recast to align with core & investee businesses.
Core P&L shared separately in the annexure.
Revenue bridge for last 3 years shared to enable shift from earlier segments to new segments.
Conventional 3-wheeler diesel engine business share in overall business carved out separately.

Unallocable/other expense of INR25.82 crores includes corporate costs like CSR expenses, director sitting fees, corporate legal and corporate payroll expenses; in core business financial snapshot (slide 27) these have been tucked into the core business itself for clarity.

subsections.label: Energy Solutions
points: Demand remained strong, supported by continuing investments across infrastructure, manufacturing, commercial and industrial applications.
Medium horsepower genset business (focus area) outperformed, supported by strong demand in industrial and commercial applications.

Successfully executed a large institutional order covering supply, installation, commissioning and aftersales services, strengthening order pipeline and reinforcing customer confidence in integrated solutions capabilities.
Continued digitization agenda through AI-led predictive maintenance initiatives and CRM programs to improve customer engagement and service responsiveness.
Commissioned a pilot Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) facility as an important step in developing capabilities in the emerging energy solutions area.

subsections.label: Mobility Solutions
points: Segment includes automotive engines, aftermarket retail and spares, engineered components (Excel), Greaves Technologies and e-Powertrain initiatives.
Automotive industry maintained healthy momentum, particularly in domestic 3-wheeler segment.
Retail aftermarket portfolio pruning exercise completed; business is now more focused and on track to perform per strategy.
Excel returned to growth path; both domestic and export business performed well and maintained healthy margins (in excess of 25% EBITDA).
Excel added new customers including international customers, strengthening quality and diversity of customer portfolio.
e-Powertrain program progressing through customer validation activities and engagement with multiple OEMs in L3 and L5 segments.

subsections.label: Industrial Solutions
points: Broadly stable performance; reported revenue largely flat YoY but grew 9% when accounting for portfolio rationalization.
Commenced exports of FM-UL compliant firefighting engines during the quarter.
Successfully completed a large defence order (engines for large defence trucks); such business expected to repeat in coming years.
Further growth opportunities seen through new products, exports and adjacent applications.

subsections.label: GEML 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler performance
points: 2-wheeler portfolio grew ~120% YoY; 3-wheeler portfolio grew ~80% YoY.
Magnus G-Max named Family Scooter of the Year at Times Drive Auto Summit 2026 — third Scooter of the Year recognition for Ampere brand.
All-new Magnus Neo launched this quarter with new look/design engineered for better rider ergonomics.

Market share growth attributed to new product portfolio/strategy, 'build for Bharat' mass-segment focus, network expansion (dealer count from ~300 to 600), e-commerce growth (selling in a month what used to sell in a year), and brand search/website traffic growth of 50-100%.
Growth in markets outside the core 4 states (25% of industry) is coming in well, indicating balanced delivery.
3-wheeler financing ecosystem expanded via partnerships with AU Small Finance Bank, VPay Finance and Koch Finance to improve affordability/accessibility.
Network expansion focused on markets with high 3-wheeler industry volumes.

subsections.label: Excel Controlinkage detail
points: Domestic business has grown double digit steadily over the last 2 years.
Setback in a large export market last year due to the Russia-Ukraine war, which had represented a big chunk of business.
Company took action last year to find other global growth opportunities; this quarter saw business start from Europe, with hopes for the U.S. soon.
Operations transformed using Greaves' manufacturing expertise; invested in automation to improve quality and prepare for volume ramp-up.
Debottlenecked operations, improving output by 10-15% over the last few months.
Utilization varies by product line: pushpull cables at 70-75% utilization; rubber components just starting with very low utilization and significant growth opportunity.

subsections.label: Greaves Technologies
points: Placed under mobility customer segment; focus has been to stabilize the business, which was heavily dependent on 2-3 large auto customers with unexciting margins.
Team has worked to stabilize and improve margin levels before pursuing growth opportunities.
International business team engaging with global customers, large Indian manufacturers and large automotive companies, primarily in Europe.
Received a pilot order from a global engine manufacturer to do design work for them.

subsections.label: GFL (Greaves Finance Limited)
points: AUM stands at INR560 crores and growing well.
Forms part of the EV ecosystem needed alongside GEML's manufacturing/supply chain.
Contribution to GEML's financing portfolio has grown to a top 3-4 level, nearing double-digit percentage of total financing requirements.
Provides automated, tech-led solutioning allowing approvals in minutes, plus innovative dealer and customer financing solutions.
Brand-agnostic financing approach seen as standard industry practice; objective is to be a preferred partner through innovative solutions, not exclusivity.

subsections.label: Genset engine range expansion
points: Gradually expanding range of own-produced engines for gensets; 650 kVA own engine launched last quarter, bringing a more reliable and tested quality product and improving margins since fully manufactured in-house.
For larger sizes, strategic supply agreement in place with one of the largest engine producers in the world, continuing to strengthen that relationship.

AI data center demand for higher kVA gensets showing very strong demand globally and in India; company engaged with strategic partners for higher-kVA offerings, but details not disclosed as discussions are still evolving.

subsections.label: Leadership/technology capability
points: Appointed a new Group Chief Technology Officer to advance future-ready technology and innovation agenda and strengthen connection between engineering, product development and growth.

subsections.label: 5C components / North America OEM business
points: New components business supplying 5C components to a large global OEM in North America; described as robust and recent, supported by a dedicated business development team finding such opportunities globally.

subsections.label: Motorcycle (2-wheeler bikes) opportunity
points: Motorcycles seen as an opportunity to be looked at; prototypes already underway.
Prioritization under review by leadership team versus large scooter opportunity; timing not yet decided.

subsections.label: CSN facility investment
points: Commissioned a state-of-the-art robotic gantry cell at the CSN facility during the quarter.
Main benefit expected from quality improvement and strengthening advanced manufacturing capability, alongside productivity gains.

subsections.label: GEML capacity
points: 2-wheeler production capacity is about 480,000 units, providing coverage for some time ahead.

subsections.label: Excel capacity
points: No capacity limitation seen for growth over the next couple of years given debottlenecking and planned capital allocation for automation, capex and capacity improvement under Greaves.Next.
Different plant sections have varying utilization: rubber components just starting with low utilization and high growth headroom; pushpull cables (main area) at 70-75% utilization.

subsections.label: International expansion
points: International business accounted for approximately 13% of core business revenue during the quarter.

Incorporated Greaves International Trading FZE in Dubai as a regional hub for Middle East and Africa, to strengthen distribution capabilities, build closer customer relationships and pursue regional opportunities.
FM-UL qualified firefighting pumps business now in active discussions for partnerships in the Middle East and Europe.
Excel export business resumed from Europe this quarter, with hopes to start business from the U.S. soon, following the Russia-Ukraine war setback.
Greaves Technologies international business team engaging with global customers primarily in Europe.

subsections.label: GEML network expansion
points: Dealership network expanded from ~300 to 600, previously confined mainly to south India and a couple of other states.
Expansion strategically targeted at geographies and town categories with high opportunity and synergistic portfolio/market share build potential, applicable to both 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler segments.
Growth in markets outside the core 4 states (Bihar, Orissa, Bengal, Tamil Nadu — 25% of industry volumes) coming in well, indicating balanced pan-India delivery.

subsections.label: Greaves.Next strategy
points: Strategy built around three business segments: Energy Solutions, Mobility Solutions and Industrial Solutions.
Segments recast in disclosures to align with core & investee businesses, moving away from the earlier engineering/retail/Excel split.
Growth ambition of 16-20% CAGR for core businesses over the next few years reiterated.

subsections.label: Portfolio pruning / rationalization
points: Retail aftermarket: exited product lines such as 2-wheeler spares, lead acid batteries, and multi-brand retail for electric 2-wheelers; wind-down took a few months, with Q1 FY27 the first quarter with a clean, focused portfolio.
Farm equipment business vacated due to increasing Chinese competition making the business less attractive over time.
Aftermarket business margins already showing improvement post-pruning, with sharper team focus on strategic product lines.

subsections.label: GEML rights issue
points: INR530 crore rights issue fully subscribed by existing shareholders GCL and Abdul Latif Jameel in proportion to shareholding.

Strengthens engineering, manufacturing and customer experience capabilities; accelerates investment in next-generation products, powertrains, battery management systems and new-age technology across 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler portfolios.
Rights issue described as sufficient for approximately the next 2 years including capital investments, given falling burn rates (now single-digit) and improving volume/realization/margin trajectory.
Because it was a rights issue for existing shareholders, there was no change in shareholding or need to disclose a valuation.

subsections.label: BESS pilot
points: BESS pilot is in early stages; goal is to ensure the product is not only technologically viable (capability already exists) but also commercially attractive, capturing value via energy savings.
Plan to go to market in subsequent quarters once pilot validates commercial value.

subsections.label: Commodity and geopolitical pressure
points: Commodity prices (platinum, aluminum, steel, fuel-related inputs) increased during the quarter, particularly following geopolitical developments in West Asia, raising input costs across the industry and for most businesses.

Mitigation ability differs by customer segment: OEM contracts typically have raw material price indexing mechanisms that kick in with a lag; aftermarket/retail channel (distributors, retailers, mechanics) allows more direct ability to pass on price increases.
There is a time lag between cost inflation impact and price increase realization; full pass-through has not yet been fully recovered.

subsections.label: Excel export market disruption
points: Russia-Ukraine war caused a setback in a large export market for Excel last year, representing a big chunk of lost business.

subsections.label: Farm equipment competitive pressure
points: Farm equipment business became less attractive over time due to Chinese competition in the market, leading to exit.

subsections.label: GEML financing NPAs (analyst-raised)
points: EV financing business (GFL) noted by an analyst to have higher yields but also higher NPAs as part of the broader ecosystem discussion.

subsections.label: Margin and growth outlook
points: Q2 FY27 expected to be marginally better than Q1; H2 FY27 expected to be better than H1.
Company remains committed to full-year FY27 margin targets set under Greaves.Next despite the year's headwinds.
Core business growth ambition maintained at 16-20% CAGR over the next few years.
Demand across segments holding strong despite geopolitical differences; company remains on track to deliver revenue growth targets set out in Greaves.Next.

subsections.label: GEML outlook
points: GEML expects to maintain, if not build on, its current 100%+ growth momentum.

Loss per unit has fallen substantially versus a year ago; company optimistic of maintaining this run rate and possibly moving into positive EBITDA territory in the next 4-6 quarters, though exact timing/quantum not committed.
Ambition to reach double-digit national market share, expected in the near future (4-8 quarters), based on historical trend of ~1-1.5% share gain every 3-4 quarters.
Current capital infusion expected to be sufficient for approximately the next 2 years including capital investments, with hope to reach positive territory by then.

key_takeaways: Greaves Cotton has begun FY27 with another quarter of disciplined execution.
We delivered a strong revenue growth across the consolidated and the core businesses.
We continue to advance Greaves.Next through investments in our businesses, capabilities and international presence.
We have taken clear actions to address the near-term pressure on margins.
At a consolidated level, we recorded a revenue of INR975 crores, which represents a year-on-year growth of 31%. Within that, our core businesses grew 16% year-on-year with a revenue of INR710 crores.
Margins were lower due to 2 factors: purposeful investments under Greaves.Next strategy, and commodity price increases particularly following geopolitical developments in West Asia.
We expect both these measures, the cost avoidance as well as the price increases, to begin showing an effect from Q2 with the full benefits becoming evident in the second half of FY27.

The successful completion of the INR530 crores rights issue, which is fully subscribed by our existing shareholders, GCL and Abdul Latif Jameel in proportion to the shareholding, is critical to the confidence that they are placing in us.
We have delivered record volume growth of 101% in quarter 1 over quarter 1 last year, compared with the 75% growth that the industry brought in.
pressing_questions: On the drop in margins that we saw this quarter, you cited higher commodity costs and deliberate investments. Could you help us quantify the impact of these investments versus the cost pressures that we could split it for us?

You've got a very good increment in volumes and also similarly in revenue. Just wanted to know at what run rate on revenue do we see a positive EBITDA levels for GEML specifically?
Now Magnus Neo, do we with the launch of the Magnus Neo and Reo, do we see a double-digit market share on a national level by the end of FY27?
So my first question is we saw Vahan 40% Q-o-Q growth, but we can see only 20% growth in revenue Q-o-Q. And what was the reason for that?

But what is the reason to be brand agnostic given that they are helping the Greaves Electric Mobility. A brand-agnostic approach basically on the other side also means you are exposing the brand to other competitive brands as well.
How far are we in terms of readiness for this particular project and partnerships from a ground launch [higher kVA/data center gensets]?

Could you please provide stand-alone revenue and operating margin for Excel in this quarter? For the last 3 years, somehow we have not been able to scale this subsidiary. Could you please throw some light on what issues are we exactly facing in this segment?

quarters.summary: Greaves Cotton delivered 22% consolidated YoY revenue growth in Q4 FY'26 with improved profitability, and recorded its highest-ever annual consolidated and standalone revenue in 10 years; management reiterated medium-term core business growth guidance of 16%-18% with 13%-15% EBITDA margins and INR 500-700 crore CAPEX over the next 4-5 years, while flagging near-term margin pressure from commodity/input cost inflation and continuing to evaluate the GEML IPO timeline (DRHP extended to Sept 30, 2026 by SEBI).

subsections.label: Q4 & FY26 core P&L
points: Consolidated revenues increased by 22% YoY in Q4 and EBITDA increased 49% during the same period.
Full year consolidated revenue growth of 18% YoY was driven by broad-based growth across businesses and consistent execution across segments.
Profitability metrics improved significantly for FY26, with EBITDA and PBT before exceptional items growing at 76% and 118% YoY respectively.
Standalone revenue grew 22% YoY in Q4 while EBITDA increased only 4% YoY in Q4.
FY26 standalone EBITDA margin expansion of 40 basis points was supported by strong demand and cost optimization initiatives.

subsections.label: Impairment
points: During the quarter, management made an impairment for the value of certain tangible and intangible assets under development relating to investment in ePowertrain technology, which has not scaled up or realized expectations due to underlying changes in project execution and customer demand.
This resulted in a conservative provision of almost INR 16 crores during the quarter.

subsections.label: Gross margin pressure
points: Standalone gross margin dropped both sequentially and YoY, primarily reflected in Q4 numbers where RMC was on the higher side vis-à-vis Q3, impacting FY26 vs FY25.
Commodity cycle pressures emerged since March, specifically in aluminum, copper and platinum.
A pass-through mechanism has already been activated in Q1 to recover pricing.
Volumes supporting operating leverage and cost-consciousness-led decisions are expected to help offset margin pressure, though management stays cautious on how the commodity cycle evolves.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Balance sheet continues to remain strong with a healthy cash balance.
Planned investments are aligned with strategic priorities, focusing on R&D and technological upgrades, capacity expansion and digital tools.
A big portion of net worth (INR 1,619 crores) is tied up in investee businesses (GEML and GFL) which have different growth trajectories requiring future capital contribution in short/medium term.
Additional INR 500+ crores of cash at group level is earmarked for future growth.
Excluding investee businesses and reserved cash (~INR 900 crores), core business capital employed is ~INR 700 crores, generating healthy returns to date.
Leadership KPIs are linked to growth, disciplined capital allocation, and business results via long-term incentive plans aligned with GREAVES.NEXT strategy and capital market conditions.

subsections.label: Employment cost
points: Different level of maturity curve between GCL (mature, regular cash generator) versus GEML/GFL (evolving, investing ahead of business) makes direct comparison unfair.

Secured single largest institutional order worth INR 35 crores covering end-to-end delivery including supply, installation, commissioning and long-term maintenance, demonstrating integrated solutions capability.
Launched a new 650 kVA genset product, based on an engine developed fully in-house by R&D team, strengthening portfolio to address wider customer requirements.
Growth driven by integrating sales and service teams, increasing ground presence of service technicians, and launching a retail annual maintenance contract program.
Service business has been growing faster than overall business.
Increased sales/distributor presence in under-leveraged regions where the company had strong market share in medium-cost power nodes (residential/commercial), which drove business growth.
Company describes itself as keeping pace with industry growth and expects to maintain/accelerate; not explicitly claiming market share gains.

subsections.label: Mobility Solutions
points: Segment includes automotive engines, aftermarket retail, Engineered Components (Excel) and associated services.

Strategy is to build diversified, fuel-agnostic portfolio via strong OEM partnerships, continued investment in advanced powertrain technologies, expanding aftermarket footprint, and scaling Excel Controlinkage's products.
Auto industry growth of 9% in FY26 supported by structural tailwinds such as GST 2.0 and stable monetary conditions.
EV adoption accelerating but multi-fuel-based technologies expected to coexist for extended period.
Q4 automotive growth of 48% driven by strong domestic demand for 3-wheeler diesel engines and continued momentum in exports of Euro V+ engines.
Aftermarket business: portfolio focus sharpened; core business remained resilient; retailer engagement accelerated with ~350 retailers onboarded with roadmap to scale to 3,000 by FY27.

Exited non-core, low-return segments such as two-wheeler parts, construction equipment, and select battery and digital platform businesses as a deliberate GREAVES.NEXT step to improve business quality and margins.
Company remains positive on aftermarket given its asset-light nature and strong margin profile.
Excel expanded product range into small commercial vehicle segment and added new geographies/customers, improving diversification and growth visibility.
ePowertrain: supplied first pilot batch of rare-earth-free motors to a 3-wheeler L5 OEM customer; in advanced discussions for a firm order within the year.

Non-3-wheeler diesel engine business (63% of mobility solution) is a focus for future growth as diesel engine growth trajectory may not sustain aggressive rates; new business development efforts are directed to this area, positioning it as a cash-generating engine to fund new growth activities.
L5 3-wheeler auto segment in India: company dominant in diesel variety; industry split 40% electric/40% CNG/20% diesel, with 63% share within diesel segment (increased during the year).

Export side: new business started during the year supplying Euro V+ compliant engines to micro car application via strategic partnership with Ligier, one of largest micro car manufacturers in Europe; business scaled up and continuing trajectory.

Network expansion drove scale and productivity: active dealer count grew 13%, showroom revamps contributed to 30% improvement in per dealer productivity.
