subsections.label: Power Generation Business
points: Continued strengthening of position in the domestic power generation market.

Over the last year, fundamentally redesigned approach to the sub-30 kVA market — created a comprehensive portfolio architecture covering multiple customer segments, technologies and price points rather than competing with individual products.
This strategy has significantly strengthened competitive position in India's largest genset segment and contributed meaningfully to domestic market share gains.
Optiprime modular power platform continues to gain momentum as customers evaluate resilient and scalable power architectures for data centers and mission-critical infrastructure.
Secured an important order in the data center segment during the quarter, validating both market need and differentiated capabilities of the modular architecture.

subsections.label: Industrial Business
points: Industrial business grew 19% domestically.
Construction segment saw double-digit growth despite muted growth in overall construction industry.

Marine segment more than doubled (grew 125%); on Marine, growth was described as a matter of execution timing — 'one of those quarters which was heavy on execution and it just how the billing happens' — management cautioned not to read into it more than that.

Railways grew 62%; railway had a strong Q1 with revenue growing materially year-on-year, supported by new engine application and repowering opportunities; qualification creates a relatively long product life cycle, but program timing can make quarterly revenue uneven; focus is on converting qualification and orders into repeatable execution rather than extrapolating one strong quarter.
Both marine and railway are businesses with durable platform relationships and strong spares/service annuity behind the first sale.

Growth no longer confined to selling engines into applications always served — received a landmark order from the oil and gas segment for natural gas gensets across ratings up to 500 kVA (this falls under Industrial segment), reinforcing presence as a credible gas power solutions partner.

Order presents capabilities: company has probably the largest range of gas engine gensets that are CPCB IV compliant; executed across biogas, wellhead gas, piped natural gas, and smaller ranges of LPG; deploys Optiprime solutions up to 2 megawatts in gas.

Established dedicated subsidiary for defense business called Kirloskar Advanced Systems Limited last quarter; India's defense opportunity expanding rapidly; R&D and IP entirely indigenous, allowing global standard solutions reinforcing national capability; being built deliberately for the long term.
NPCIL order execution is milestone-based and at execution stage; some revenue will start flowing this financial year, remaining in coming quarters/years; no NPCIL contribution in Q1 specifically.
No specific individual growth numbers given for HHP vs mid/smaller nodes, but largest chunk of growth is coming from HHP (off a lower base); growth is seen right across.

subsections.label: Distribution & Aftermarket Business
points: Considered the truest measure of the franchise — grows only where installed base is large, service network reaches, and customer returns.
Grew across every channel this quarter, led by service, which brings resilience and healthy cash generation.
Completed first end-to-end turnkey repowering high horsepower project — a 1,010 kVA installation won in direct competition, signaling extended capability.
Business has consistently grown double digit every quarter for the last 12 quarters.
Initiatives: upskilling of service engineers; restructured service channel; new product launches; technical capability driven for replacement and repowering with engines.
Result of initiatives: increasing number of service contracts — a larger asset base is now under service contract than before.
In several cases, company offers 2-hour service response guarantees for mission-critical applications; management is fairly satisfied with progress but says there is a long way to go.

There may have been a shortage of spare parts noted from channel feedback per an analyst; management did not directly quantify sustainability of the 20% growth but reiterated aspiration towards the $2 billion vision, with all businesses including distribution & aftermarket playing an important role.

subsections.label: KOEL Fluid Dynamics
points: Business broadly flat year-on-year with domestic sales up and exports down.
Underneath flat headline, business strengthened materially: Channel pump business more than doubled, and company delivered highest ever V8 submersible output.
Balance sheet improved: total borrowings reduced from INR167 crores to INR77 crores, working capital improved by 11 days, and credit rating upgraded to AA.
Business is being made structurally healthier while it waits for export markets to recover.

subsections.label: Arka Financial Services
points: Arka reported revenue growth of 9% to INR210 crores, with assets under management standing at INR7,651 crores at end of quarter.
Team has crossed 1,800 employees across approximately 136 branches, giving a considerably stronger platform for growth ahead.

On long-term plans, company pivoted into a secure/different strategic direction last year (comment cut off due to audio issue); long-term plan for Arka includes a potential hive-off of the business, but this takes time and will be done in a stepwise manner; updates will be communicated when available.

subsections.label: Consolidated Segment Summary
points: Power and Energy businesses continue to perform well.
KOEL Fluid Dynamics maintained stable domestic performance despite export headwinds.
Arka Financial Services continued its growth trajectory with higher revenue, expanding assets under management and a broader national footprint.

Strong domestic execution and expansion into high-value mission-critical applications continue to drive top-line performance while mitigating geopolitical volatility through disciplined cost optimization and operational excellence.

subsections.label: Engineering and Technology Strategy
points: Continuing to build the next generation of growth platforms that will define KOEL's future.

Investments in modular Optiprime power systems for AI data centers, gas-based distributed power, defense, high horsepower engines and advanced industrial applications are steadily expanding addressable market and creating new avenues for long-term growth.

Optiprime hybrid power systems, although developed with AI data centers in mind, the architecture is also relevant to microgrids, industrial prime power, utilities and other applications where fast-changing loads and resilient operations are essential.

Under the new energy vertical, a whole bunch of product development initiatives are being driven, including gas units; new energy vertical functions more as a program management office focusing on development of different fuel power systems including ethanol, methanol, isobutanol, natural gas, and hydrogen.
Microgrids being pursued via deployment across customers in coordination with sister company Kirloskar Solar within the group, though power systems and gensets continue to be the mainstream business.

subsections.label: International Business Weakness
points: International business remained affected by geopolitical developments and delayed customer investment decisions across several regions.
The Middle East region is an important export market and continued to operate below normal levels, impacting both business mix and operating leverage during the quarter.

A lot of business today comes from the Middle East region; due to the conflict in West Asia, logistics queues were choked, and as a result, even where orders existed, some fulfillments could not happen.

Company remains committed to EBITDA delivery for the full year despite these conditions, and remains confident in the long-term opportunity, continuing to engage closely with customers while preparing for demand normalization.

Queues are seen opening up; it is more a question of ensuring supply chain and fulfillment happens properly; demand and opportunities for execution do exist but are being carefully watched; 3 to 6 months considered a fairly reasonable assumption for normalization.

subsections.label: Data Center / Hyperscaler Opportunity
points: Data centers represent an important structural opportunity because they require high reliability, rapid response, robust control and strong life cycle support — all areas aligned with KOEL's power system capabilities.
Q1 was strategically significant as the company secured its first hyperscale data center order of approximately 192 megawatts; viewed as a reference point rather than an endpoint.
Immediate objective is to execute this order extremely well and establish KOEL as a credible HHP ultra-high horsepower alternate for hyperscalers, co-location players and EPC partners.

Company is strengthening product capability, testing, supply chain readiness, controls and service support around this opportunity, and will be disciplined about distinguishing pipeline from actual orders and actual revenue.

On customer profile for the order: company continues to work with multiple customers; in this case, one has materialized with purchase orders; company does checks and balances; further order details are internal and proprietary; many customers are entering the data center segment and company receives queries all the time — not unusual.

A lot of effort put into the data center segment including internally driven upskilling programs; engaged with most data centers today; already executed a whole bunch of orders across edge or enterprise data centers; this particular order is with a larger data center.

Conversations continue to progress with many customers; looking at a whole bunch of different solutions ranging from behind-the-meter solutions to hybrid solutions, as well as Optiprime; company has a fairly strong suite of products and is fairly confident of continuing to gain traction.

This is a composite contract including supply of gensets plus an O&M contract for a longer period; genset supply revenue recognition will happen in this financial year; the O&M contract will continue for at least 5 to 6 years.
Below 750 kVA nodes: domestic franchise is strong and market presence is being gained overwhelmingly; above 750 kVA, market share has also been gained but off a smaller base, so not yet significant.

subsections.label: Pricing Strategy
points: Price increases can be readily passed on when the product is more distribution led; otherwise, it is contract and tender specific.

Company has been proactive in having conversations with customers on price increases; believes it was amongst the first to start the conversation while realization has lagged for most players — described as being prudent and fair to the business.
Not all realization comes in a single quarter; realization is staged; effort is to pass on inflation to the extent possible and protect margins.
Management declined to quantify the split between pricing-led and volume-led growth within the 18% Power Generation revenue growth, citing varied realization across the quarter.

subsections.label: $2 Billion FY30 Aspiration
points: Company has laid down its 5-year strategic plan with an aspiration to be a $2 billion revenue enterprise by FY30, translating to close to INR16,600 crores.
Not providing a year-wise breakup of the path to this target.
On margin front, company would like to earn a higher double-digit EBITDA margin by FY30, though no specific range was given.
Industrial and aftermarket, along with all businesses, have an important role to play as the company moves toward the $2 billion vision/ambition.

subsections.label: Kirloskar Advanced Systems Limited (Defense Subsidiary)
points: Established last quarter as a dedicated subsidiary for the defense business.

India's defense opportunity is expanding rapidly; research, development and intellectual property are entirely indigenous, allowing global standard solutions that directly reinforce national capability.
Being built deliberately for the long term.

subsections.label: Arka Financial Services Long-Term Plan
points: Long-term plan includes a potential hive-off of the Financial Services business, but this takes time and will be pursued in a stepwise, stage-wise manner.
Company pivoted strategically last year (detail on this pivot cut off due to audio issue during the call).
Updates on the hive-off plan will be communicated as they become available.

subsections.label: Geopolitical & Export Headwinds
points: Significant geopolitical uncertainty and unusually weak export markets affected the quarter.
Middle East region, an important export market, continued to operate below normal levels, impacting business mix and operating leverage.
Conflict in West Asia caused logistics queues to be choked, preventing fulfillment even where orders existed.

subsections.label: Commodity Cost Inflation
points: Elevated commodity costs and a timing difference between cost inflation and price realization impacted EBITDA.
Margin contracted predominantly due to a massive increase in global commodity prices; price increases taken to counter this, but there is a lag between price increase and price realization.

subsections.label: Employee Cost Escalation
points: Employee-related expense increased materially year-on-year (~40%) due to annual increments, ESOP-related expense, and capability additions/investments supporting future growth programs.

Some of these costs are structural, some timing related; better fixed cost absorption and productivity is an explicit management priority as revenue scales, particularly in international HHP and aftermarket business.

subsections.label: Full-Year & Forward Outlook
points: Company remains committed to EBITDA delivery for the full year despite challenging export markets.
Expects profitability to improve as pricing actions progressively flow through over coming quarters, supported by cost optimization and operational excellence initiatives.
Reiterated $2 billion / ~INR16,600 crore revenue aspiration by FY30 without giving a year-wise breakup.
Would like to earn a higher double-digit EBITDA margin by FY30 but declined to give a specific range.

Margin trajectory: over last 3 years margin improved by more than 400 basis points; endeavor is to continue improving margin going forward; management 'hopes' margins will be better than the last couple of years.
Middle East export normalization: 3 to 6 months considered a fairly reasonable assumption, contingent on logistics queues opening up and supply chain/fulfillment being restored.

guidance_ledger.statement: Aspiration to be a $2 billion revenue enterprise by FY30; by FY30, should be close to INR16,600 crores company; not giving a year-wise breakup.
On the margin front, definitely would like to earn a higher double-digit EBITDA margin; declined to give a specific range where it will land at FY30.
Remain committed to our EBITDA delivery for the full year despite export headwinds.
As pricing actions progressively flow through over the coming quarters, supported by ongoing cost optimization and operational excellence initiatives, we expect profitability to improve.

Our endeavor is to improve the margin from here on; we have improved margin by more than 400 bps in last 3 years and will continue to work on margin improvement; hope margins will be better than last couple of years.
3 to 6 months is a fairly reasonable assumption for greater normalization of export/RM pass-through metrics.

guidance_ledger.statement: For genset supply, revenue recognition will happen in this financial year.
The O&M contract will continue for at least 5 to 6 years.
NPCIL order execution is milestone-based; some revenue will start flowing this financial year, remaining in coming quarters or years.

Will continue to aspire towards the $2 billion vision/ambition; all businesses have an important role to play including distribution and aftermarket (no explicit quantified growth guidance for next quarter given).
Prior quarter guidance: will certainly try for LHP business to grow in line with or a little better than industry growth in FY27 (no update provided this quarter).

Prior quarter guidance: investing close to INR1,400 crores on HHP capacity expansion at Kagal over next 2 years (no update provided this quarter).
Prior quarter guidance: asset turn will be in the range of 4% to 5% depending upon the nodes (no update provided this quarter).

guidance_ledger.metric: Peak revenue potential from new capex

Continuing effort to pass on inflation to the extent possible and protect margins; realization is staged across quarters.
Progressing well against the goal to be a USD2 billion company by Fiscal Year '30.

key_takeaways: Standalone revenue grew 16% year-on-year to INR1,461 crores, led by robust domestic demand across power generation, industrial and distribution and aftermarket businesses.
Power generation grew by 18%, industrial by 19% and distribution and aftermarket business delivered another strong quarter with 20% growth.
In the power generation business, one of the highlights of the quarter has been the continued strengthening of our position in the domestic power generation market.
We received a landmark order from the oil and gas segment for natural gas gensets across ratings up to 500 kVA.
Last quarter, we also established a dedicated subsidiary for our defense business called Kirloskar Advanced Systems Limited.
On the international business, as expected, our international business remained affected by geopolitical developments and delayed customer investment decisions across several regions.
While these conditions affected our international performance, we remain committed to our EBITDA delivery for the full year.
EBITDA for the quarter reflected 3 primary factors: lower export volumes, elevated commodity costs and the timing difference between cost inflation and price realization.
Q1 was strategically significant because as you mentioned, we secured our first hyperscale data center order of approximately 192 megawatts.
pressing_questions: Congrats on reasonable strength in domestic business... this trend in Marine and Railways, of course, on a quarterly basis, these seem pretty strong, right? So is there some quarter-related thing or what exactly is happening here? Is it sustainable?

In this particular quarter, I see that, on the standalone numbers specifically, I see that there is a sharp increase in the employee cost... roughly around, if I may say, like 22% quarter-on-quarter and let's say, close to 40% Y-o-Y. So is this the run rate that we should look at? Or is there some one-off element within that, if you can clarify?

Just wanted to revisit our view of the future... Should we say in 3 years' time, there should be kind of doubling given all the opportunity in the product portfolio that now we are rapidly developing? And if that is the case, will the margin and the profitability likely to inch up from where it has been till now?
So my question is related to the distribution and the aftermarkets... how are we in terms of service levels currently versus our peers?
On the Financial Services business, Arka, what are our long-term plans? And are we planning to hive-off the business going ahead or what's our strategy for the Financial Services business?

subsections.label: Growth drivers
points: Achieved highest-ever quarterly standalone sales of INR1,522 crores in Q4 FY26, a 24% YoY growth, resulting in full-year net sales of INR5,604 crores (25% YoY growth).
Strong performance was broad-based with double-digit growth across all business units.
Numbers reported are for continuing operations only and exclude exceptional items.

subsections.label: Working capital
points: Working capital position continues to remain healthy with payables at approximately 60 days and receivables at around 41 days.
Inventory levels stood at approximately 48 days, improved from 66 days last quarter, supported by disciplined working capital management led by improved inventory and receivables efficiency.
Overall cash conversion cycle continued to be maintained within a disciplined range, supporting overall liquidity and operating flexibility.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Each kVA node has its own associated margin profile; overall margin is a composite number with no margin deterioration and operating leverage kicking in for certain nodes.
Larger operating leverage expected to kick in soon as capacity investments and international traction mature, potentially from FY27 onwards per management's directional response.
Raw material cost inflation is expected to be partly passed on to the market as it is hard for players to absorb all of it themselves.

key_figures.label: Combined NPCIL and marine order value

subsections.label: NPCIL / marine order execution
points: NPCIL order execution timeline is by 2029; all teams are actively working on it as execution is critical, tracked on regular cadence and project managed; company is on track to deliver by committed timelines.
Revenue will be recognized as billing happens on the NPCIL order; billing/revenue recognition had not yet started as of the call.

subsections.label: Demand environment
points: Demand drivers across industries are seen as remaining strong, and management does not expect the raw material inflation situation to be experienced in isolation versus peers.
Response to data center segment has been encouraging with successes seen in the last year; company remains committed to the segment and believes it has a unique proposition.

Company is present in Edge and Colo data center segments and is making inroads into hyperscalers; management expects double-digit contribution from data centers but declined to disclose exact figures.
Nothing meaningful yet on inquiries for alternate-fuel power generators (gas/ethanol/methanol/hydrogen blends), though company is hopeful.

subsections.label: Powergen
points: Q4 is traditionally a strong quarter, making the 30% YoY Powergen growth a significant achievement.
Market share improved significantly across all nodes; in high horsepower (HHP) segment, market share was negligible a couple of years ago and is now approaching double digits.

HHP focus and Optiprime have shown significant strides over the last year; units sold up to 3,000 kVA; management believes entering a node/market first (domestic) creates an opportunity to succeed there.
LHP (low horsepower) remains the core 'bread and butter' business and will remain a big focus area even as new avenues in projects and HHP are pursued.

Company declined to disclose HHP volume/price breakup or HHP contribution to Powergen revenue, and declined to disclose data center revenue contribution (though management aims for double-digit contribution).

subsections.label: Industrial
points: Construction, mining and railways have been the primary growth drivers for the Industrial segment.

Construction segment growth reflects the mandatory emission standard shift from CEV BS-IV to CEV BS-V (effective January 2025), representing both an opportunity to acquire customers and a risk of losing them.

Customer acquisition in construction is a long-drawn process involving technical alignment, product-fit assessment, engineering tweaks, site approvals and proto testing — a joint effort typically taking 18 months or more.
Growth validates the strength of products under the new emission standard and the capability of the engineering team.
Growth outlook for industrial and distribution is broad-based across multiple sub-segments, with a game plan per segment, though which sub-segment leads will vary by year/cycle.

subsections.label: Aftermarket / Distribution
points: Journey over the last 4 years has been to transition from a parts provider to a complete ecosystem manager, improving share of annual maintenance contract (AMC) customers and leveraging service channels to offer allied products and hold goods.

subsections.label: Kirloskar Fluid Dynamics (pumps)
points: This is the first full quarter for the consolidated entity; exports outperformed domestic growth.

subsections.label: Financial services (Arka)
points: 5-year strategy centers on a deliberate pivot towards realizing the loan book; scaled from 34 to 137 branches in FY26.
Strategy focuses on local market depth, operating only in regions with established infrastructure for direct, high-touch customer service.
Even with significant investments in the secured retail business, FY26 PAT remained stable at INR69 crores, similar to FY25 PAT before extraordinary items.
Asset quality remains robust with prudent leverage and capital ratios; GNPA and NNPA remained flat sequentially versus Q3, and GNPA has come down in absolute terms.

subsections.label: HHP / Optiprime engineering
points: HHP engines are totally localized — developed by the company's own engineering teams and completely manufactured in-house.
Company has capability to address nodes even beyond 3,000 kVA (e.g., NPCIL order of 10 units, each 6.3 MW/~8,000 kVA genset), though it has actively sold routine products only up to 3,000 kVA.
For data centers the company currently goes up to 1,650 kVA in single engine and is on track to increase that.

subsections.label: R&D / patents / technology roadmap
points: R&D expense is rising in absolute terms as sales grow, given the steady 2%-2.5% rate applied to a larger revenue base.

Company declined to disclose details on new product launches/engineering development, citing confidentiality, but stated it is deeply focused on key customer segments and equipped to develop products the market requires.

Company has developed engines running on different fuels (gas, ethanol, methanol, hydrogen blends) as part of its technology roadmap defined about 3 years ago and disclosed in investor materials; ready to address demand for alternative fuels if it picks up.

New Netherlands subsidiary's disclosed scope includes heat/ICE engines, gas turbines, transformers and energy storage solutions (including batteries) as potential technologies for the power systems space over time — management clarified this reflects the broad scope disclosed at incorporation, not necessarily what will actually be pursued; 'it may happen and not happen.'

A recent patent (on hybrid generators) was cited by an analyst, referencing CEO's name on the filing, though management did not elaborate further on it specifically beyond the general R&D percentage answer.

subsections.label: Kagal capacity expansion
points: The earlier INR700 crores capex for 50,000 engines is about enhancing existing lines and adding new lines within the existing Kagal plant, and is expected to come online by April of next year.

The new INR1,400 crores investment (over the next two years, for 20,000 engines) is higher per-engine because it includes construction of a new building at the same Kagal site (no new land acquisition) plus completely new lines and equipment, and is targeted at higher/HHP category engines.
The INR1,400 crores capex is confirmed as fully new capex, with no replacement component.

Capacity being built is for use across the whole of KOEL (not geography-specific), though it is focused on HHP markets in Powergen as the key theme of capital deployment; specific target geographies not disclosed.
Capitalization of the new capex is targeted to complete within the next 2 years, after which associated revenue will start kicking into the P&L.

subsections.label: International vs export strategy
points: Management distinguishes 'exports' (manufacturing locally and shipping to a country via an agent) from being 'international' (building a genuine business in-geography, hiring locally, setting up comprehensive offices, and evaluating local manufacturing/assembly where viable).
Company committed to the Middle East market a few years ago and is present there; sees potential tailwinds from infrastructure rebuilding in the region if geopolitical situations necessitate it.
In the last quarter, no impact has been seen from the Middle East crisis on the ~40-50% of export revenue derived from that region; harder to comment on subsequent quarters.
Kirloskar Americas has seen a lot of effort/investment in the past year, but nothing meaningful or significant to discuss yet.
No specific commentary given on inquiries tied to Vizag data center capacity buildout; company is engaged with customers across all locations without a specific Vizag differentiation noted.
New Netherlands subsidiary incorporated in line with the importance of international business to the company's 5-year goal, aimed at structuring efficiently for growth and stakeholder value creation.

subsections.label: Raw material cost management
points: Copper prices have risen through the year and pig iron prices rose ~15% recently; management declined to quantify price hikes taken in FY26 or bifurcate impact between copper and pig iron.
Company continues to evaluate its pricing policy and takes price increases at regular periods, but declined to quantify FY26 price hikes.

subsections.label: New subsidiaries
points: Incorporated a new subsidiary, Kirloskar Advanced Systems Private Limited, to pursue advanced technology and systems integration opportunities, particularly to serve key accounts in sectors like defense, leveraging engineering capability beyond the traditional engine business.

Incorporated a Netherlands subsidiary given the importance of international business to the 5-year goal, to structure the group efficiently as it grows; disclosed scope includes heat/ICE engines plus energy transition products such as gas turbines, transformers and energy storage/batteries, though management clarified this reflects a broad potential scope rather than confirmed business lines.

subsections.label: Long-term goal
points: Company reiterated it is progressing well against its goal to be a USD2 billion company by FY30, citing FY26 numbers as evidence of progress.
Industrial and aftermarket segments are expected to play an important role in reaching the USD2 billion milestone.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / macro risk
points: Current geopolitical situation (e.g., war) may cause short-to-medium-term structural changes; management is keenly watching the macro environment, noting any impact would not be unique to the company and could bring both headwinds and tailwinds (e.g., infrastructure rebuilding demand in affected regions).
No short-term disruptions were faced during the quarter despite Middle East crisis/gas crisis concerns.
~40-50% of export revenue is derived from the Middle East; no impact seen in the last quarter from the regional crisis, though future quarters are harder to predict.

subsections.label: Raw material cost inflation
points: Business is entering what may be a turbulent period on raw material costs (e.g., copper, pig iron); management intends to focus on long-term growth and maintaining sustainable margins.
Some raw material cost inflation is expected to be passed on to the market as it will be hard for industry players to fully absorb the increases themselves.
Company declined to quantify price hikes taken or to bifurcate copper vs. pig iron cost impact for FY26.

subsections.label: Emission standard transition risk/opportunity
points: The mandatory shift from CEV BS-IV to CEV BS-V emission standards (effective January 2025) represents both an opportunity to acquire customers and a risk of losing them in the construction segment.

key_takeaways: At a consolidated level, we achieved 22% growth in revenue. We are now amongst the top 10 manufacturers in the world by volume in the industrial and Powergen space.
We sold over 1 million pumps last year and our international business crossed INR1,000 crores in gross sales.

At a standalone level, the company achieved its highest-ever quarterly sales in Q4, reaching INR1,522 crores, a 24% year-on-year growth. This resulted in full year net sales of INR5,604 crores, representing a 25% year-on-year increase.
While the overall annual diesel generator market grew 18% to approximately 179,000 units, including telecom, KOEL grew by 41%, selling upwards of 50,000 units in FY26.
Our Industrial segment grew 22% annually generating revenues of INR1,444 crores. Construction, mining and railways have been our primary growth driver.
We have incorporated a new subsidiary called Kirloskar Advanced Systems Private Limited... to serve key accounts in sectors like defense.
We are investing close to INR1,400 crores on [Kagal capacity expansion]... that will be our capital allocation for this next two years.
In summary, we are progressing well against our goal to be a USD2 billion company by Fiscal Year '30 and our numbers indicate that progress.

With the war and potential fuel price hikes and all the other stuff, what challenges do you expect in the environment for the business over the next 6-9 months?
Are there any more products that we are working on over the next one to three years which can drive growth further up or maybe variants of existing ones which can see a ramp up?
What is your growth outlook across industrial as well as distribution revenue going ahead?

What is the asset turn that we can expect on this gross block [post the ~INR2,100 crore total capex]?
What was the impact on this quarter and next quarter from the Middle East market (40-50% of export revenue)? Can you give us the proportion or contribution of HHP to our Power Gen segment?

The INR1,400 crore capex — what is the peak revenue potential and how many years to eventually reach it?

KIRLOSENG.about: KOEL, one of the flagship companies of the Kirloskar group, manufactures and services diesel engines and diesel generator sets. The company also makes diesel, petrol and kerosene-based pump sets. It has manufacturing units in Pune, Kagal, and Nashik. The company caters to the agriculture, power generation, and industrial sectors.[1]

quarters.summary: GTBL reported strong Q1 FY27 growth (revenue +22.1% YoY, EBITDA +49.4% YoY, PAT +22.1% YoY) driven by robust sales volumes, and is undertaking a major transformation into a fermentation-based, innovation-led CDMO platform via the MicroBiopharm Japan acquisition and Sanofi France brand portfolio acquisition, alongside doubled fermentation capacity (full steam by end of August 2026) and new API block coming online through FY27, with expected asset turns of 1.4x-1.5x on ~INR200 crores of new fermentation/API capex and a base-case high-teen top-line growth aspiration over the next 3-5 years.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 performance drivers
points: Revenue growth came from a robust increase in sales volumes, reflecting a healthy demand outlook for products.
Balance sheet remains healthy and provides flexibility to continue investing in long-term growth initiatives.

subsections.label: Historical flatness explanation (FY23-FY26)
points: Numbers have been pretty flat in terms of revenue and margins over the last 4-5 years because the company has been sold out in capacity.
First few years were spent upgrading the old facility; next 3 years spent creating new infrastructure.
FY26 was pretty stable and steady versus previous years; one year saw slight reduction due to production issues from excessive rains and power fluctuations.
Company was pretty much sold out in terms of capacity throughout, producing at usual efficiency.

subsections.label: Gross block movement bridge
points: Gross block was around INR62 crores in FY23 and grew to around INR435 crores (including CWIP) in FY26 balance sheet — an incremental addition of about INR370 crores over 3 years.
The INR370 crores comprises new fermentation facility, API facility, new R&D infrastructure, and the hybrid power project.
Of the INR370 crores, around INR200 crores (new fermentation facility + API facility) is considered for asset turn calculation, implying an asset turn of around 1.4x to 1.5x.

subsections.label: Funding strategy for acquisitions
points: Company keeping multiple funding avenues ready — optimal mix of debt and equity — to be finalized by month-end closing.
Equity raise decided at up to INR1,000 crores; exact debt quantum not yet finalized, kept flexible.

Interest cost concern raised by an analyst (implying ~INR200 crores annual interest burden on INR2,000 crores debt at 10% cost) was countered — management stated actual interest cost in the two acquisition geographies is significantly lower than 10%, and the acquired business is expected to be cash flow positive from the outset.
An additional debt flexibility option of INR450 crores exists, and a guarantee of INR1,000 crores has been taken from a group company.

subsections.label: Promoter pledge reduction plan
points: Promoter share pledge/encumbrance stood at around 48-48.5% as of June 2026, with about 1.5-2% released in July 2026.
Management expects the promoter pledge/encumbrance to go down significantly within a year to 15 months.

subsections.label: Base business capex outlook
points: Most of the company's capex program is now completed; only about INR10-15 crores of last-mile spend remains for FY27.
Some maintenance capex will also be incurred, historically a few crores; total base business capex for FY27 expected around INR20 crores including everything.

subsections.label: Demand and capacity utilization
points: Company has historically been sold out in capacity across recent years, constraining revenue growth despite steady demand.
Target customer base for expanded fermentation capacity is everyone using the intermediate, in and outside the country.
Company aims to dilute customer concentration further by selling intermediate to any manufacturer in the country and outside who is making these APIs.

subsections.label: API block commercialization
points: The API block is currently booking all three molecules: Rifapentine, Rifaximin, and other (implied third molecule) — 'All 3, all 3' per management.

API block was delayed roughly 2 years versus the FY25 guidance given in November 2023, because the company lacked sufficient fermentation intermediate capacity — existing intermediate output was already contracted to long-term customers, so capacity could not be diverted to API production without cannibalizing existing sales.
Additional fermentation capacity now being built is intended to be used to feed the API block.

subsections.label: MicroBiopharm platform commercialization status
points: Apart from ADCs (a relatively new, patented technology at MBJ with no CDMO project bagged yet), all other platforms — peptides, plasmids, oncology, precision fermentation, immunosuppressants, anti-infectives — are already commercialized, each with at least one project developed and commercialized, with respective GMP accreditations.
Revenue split by individual technology vertical was not disclosed ('not in a position to divulge at this stage').
MicroBiopharm is 100% API CDMO with very little formulation (about 4-5%); APIs are predominantly made by fermentation; 60% of MBJ's business is currently CDMO.
Most of MBJ's commercialized projects are off-patent; new development pipeline projects are under patent but not yet commercialized.
MBJ clientele/revenue: 60% from Japan, 40% from outside Japan.

subsections.label: Sanofi brand portfolio
points: 13 established brands in anti-TB and anti-infective segments, giving access to 55 countries across Europe, Middle East and Africa.
All Sanofi brands are branded generics; Sanofi is currently not marketing them aggressively.
Brand names will remain unchanged; only the manufacturer will change from Sanofi to Themis Biosyn.
Distribution approach varies by country: in some markets distributors/field force market the products, in others no one currently promotes them — a 'mixed bag' country to country.
Margin expansion opportunity seen via integrating GTBL's own API into the Sanofi supply chain in place of API Sanofi currently uses, in addition to distribution-led growth.

subsections.label: Rifamycin market shift
points: Global product market is shifting from Rifampicin toward Rifapentine, though not as rapidly as some expect, partly because manufacturing 1 kilo of Rifapentine requires more Rifa-S than manufacturing Rifampicin.
Management stated the shift doesn't matter either way for GTBL since the company is ready with both APIs (Rifampicin-linked Rifa-S and Rifapentine).

subsections.label: MicroBiopharm technology capabilities
points: MBJ brings capabilities including peptides, plasmids (base for DNA, RNA, gene therapy, CAR-T), precision fermentation, enzyme engineering, and ADCs (under development, patented, not yet commercialized).
Therapy areas added: immunosuppressants, oncology, anti-infectives.

Building these capabilities in-house would have taken GTBL 7 to 8 years; MBJ acquisition gives an immediate jump-start including existing projects, supplies, and relationships with big pharma in Japan and globally.
P450 enzyme library and other proprietary MBJ technology expected to be absorbed and commercialized with meaningful synergy work achievable within the first year.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape in fermentation CDMO
points: Few global companies operate as fermentation-based CDMOs covering this breadth of capability; large players cited include Lonza and WuXi (China), and in India, Anthem Biosciences.

subsections.label: Fermentation capacity expansion
points: Company has practically doubled fermentation capacity (added 540 KL); not all of the expansion is solely for Rifampicin — some capacity added for R&D and cGMP pilot facilities.
New manufacturing site expected to start full steam by end of August 2026.
Fermentation capacity utilization is binary ('0 or 100') — expanded capacity will run at full scale once operational, producing continuously.
Output from expanded capacity expected to begin appearing this quarter (Q2 FY27) and more fully in the second half of the year, covering both fermentation block and API block.

subsections.label: Hybrid power project
points: Hybrid power plant has not yet gone live; Phase 1 expected to go live in September 2026, with Phase 2 starting about 2 months later.
Expected to improve EBITDA margins by providing power at a significantly lower price.

subsections.label: Sanofi geographic footprint
points: Sanofi brand acquisition gives access to 55 countries across Europe, Middle East and Africa markets, expanding GTBL's downstream commercial presence and international marketing access.

subsections.label: MicroBiopharm geographic revenue split
points: 60% of MBJ revenue from Japan, 40% from outside Japan.

subsections.label: Optimus Drugs dispute
points: A recent dispute with Optimus Drugs over their initial decision not to buy GTBL's product has been resolved; both companies worked constructively to resolve the dispute and are restarting business.
Management declined to detail the reason for the dispute due to confidentiality.
During the roughly 6-9 months of non-supply to Optimus, GTBL was still able to easily sell out its capacity to other buyers, as there are more than enough buyers for the same product in the country.

subsections.label: Sanofi manufacturing transition
points: Post-closing, a transition service agreement between GTBL and Sanofi will run for 3 years, transferring marketing authorizations country-by-country from Sanofi's name to GTBL's name, eventually moving manufacturing control (not sites or people) to GTBL.

GTBL will use CMOs — some already used by Sanofi and some GTBL will newly create — to manufacture the Sanofi portfolio; management hopes to complete this much earlier than the 3-year maximum, with tech transfers expected complete within the first year.

GTBL's own API is expected to eventually be integrated into the Sanofi supply chain; GTBL is targeting API approvals in the coming years and expects to be ready well before Sanofi integration occurs, without requiring prior Sanofi inspection/audit for this readiness.

subsections.label: Sanofi brand commercialization strategy
points: Company plans a more aggressive marketing stance on Sanofi's branded generic products, since Sanofi was not aggressively promoting them.
GTBL has the opportunity to use Sanofi's existing distributors (some quite strong) and has already tied up with strong distributors in certain markets where more can be done.
Marketing approach varies by market — some via distributors, some via field force, some markets currently unpromoted.

subsections.label: Customer concentration strategy
points: Endeavor is to sell intermediate to any manufacturer in the country and outside who is manufacturing these APIs, to dilute customer concentration.

subsections.label: MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) acquisition
points: GTBL announced plans to acquire MicroBiopharm Japan, specializing in precision fermentation and various other technologies and therapy areas.
Provides access to advanced fermentation technologies, specialized scientific talent, proprietary know-how, manufacturing capacity, and an established R&D platform.
Adds therapy areas across immunosuppressants, oncology and anti-infectives, and technical capabilities including peptides, plasmids, ADCs and enzyme engineering.
One of the two acquisitions is expected to close soon (around end of August 2026); funding for this deal is largely secured, with some last-minute approvals required.

MBJ had been under a private equity firm for the past 5-6 years; as the fund's life closed, MBJ became available for sale — GTBL had approached MBJ about a potential sale roughly 2.5 years ago, indicating the initiation was well thought out from GTBL's end.

Although MBJ's top line may not have improved significantly under PE ownership, there has been a significant improvement in the bottom line via creation of value-added businesses and technologies that improved the EBITDA line.
Management expects some synergy projects between GTBL and MBJ to start within the first year.
Management does not intend to manage the MBJ business directly from Japan — strong existing MBJ management team continues; the focus is bringing synergies through integration and common projects.

subsections.label: Sanofi France brand acquisition
points: GTBL is acquiring 13 established brands from Sanofi France in the anti-TB and anti-infective segments, giving access to 55 countries across Europe, Middle East and Africa.
This is an asset-light acquisition — no manufacturing assets are being acquired from Sanofi.

The second acquisition (Sanofi) is expected to take longer to close — about 6-9 months or longer, with a long-stop date of June next year (2027), due to significant regulatory approvals required from over 50 countries.
Creates opportunities for forward integration from intermediates to APIs and finished formulations.

Complements MicroBiopharm: MBJ strengthens upstream scientific/manufacturing capabilities while Sanofi portfolio expands downstream commercial presence via established brands and international marketing access.

subsections.label: Themis Medicare merger - withdrawn
points: A merger with group company Themis Medicare was announced around November 2024, aimed at creating a fully integrated pharmaceutical company with API fermentation and domestic market brands.
After about 6 months, the decision was made to withdraw the merger scheme.
Around the same time, GTBL appointed an external firm for strategic options review, which clarified the concept of becoming a fermentation-based CDMO.

Management decided that pursuing other (predominantly domestic) businesses would dilute GTBL's focus, so it chose to grow strictly as a fermentation-based CDMO rather than diversify into other businesses.

subsections.label: Post-merger production allocation (Themis vs GTBL)
points: Contracted CMO production for the Sanofi business may or may not include Themis Medicare as a CMO; as plans currently stand, it will not be Themis because Themis already has other projects/product categories underway.
GTBL will move some Sanofi production to other CMO sites, potentially outside India.

subsections.label: Long-term strategic vision
points: Over the last 18-24 months, strategic initiatives have all been connected by one objective: transforming GTBL into an integrated fermentation-led pharmaceutical platform.

Ongoing multiphase capex program is expanding fermentation infrastructure, strengthening R&D capabilities, and creating downstream API manufacturing capacity to diversify the product portfolio, deepen technology capabilities, and enable greater value addition.
Company aims to progressively move downstream from fermentation-based intermediates into APIs and other high-value products, capturing a larger share of the pharmaceutical value chain.

Vision is to become a fermentation-based CDMO, grow on that platform, and improve financial performance — combining organic growth (selling more of existing/new products) with inorganic growth (MBJ and Sanofi).

On a base-case basis, management targets high-teen revenue growth over the next 3-5 years (management declined to specify an absolute revenue target, e.g., did not confirm a specific INR500 crore figure suggested by an analyst).

Both acquisitions target already-steady, historically stable businesses (no major upside or downside over the past 5 years) rather than turnaround situations, to manage integration risk given leveraged funding and management bandwidth constraints.
Expected margin profile post-integration/stabilization for both new businesses is expected to be close to GTBL's current margin levels, i.e., not expected to be significantly margin dilutive.

Company's forward priorities: executing expansion projects, integrating recent acquisitions, commercializing new capabilities, broadening product portfolio, and maintaining strong financial performance.

subsections.label: Historical delays and communication gap
points: No earnings conference call was held for almost 3 years prior to this one; management attributed the gap to a flat business phase during which the company was sold out in capacity and focused on capex/infrastructure building, with projects running about a year behind schedule.
API block revenue guided in November 2023 to start from FY25 was delayed roughly 2 years due to fermentation capacity constraints.

subsections.label: Regulatory approval risk on Sanofi deal
points: Sanofi acquisition closing requires significant regulatory approvals from over 50 countries, expected to take 6-9 months or longer, with a long-stop date of June 2027.

subsections.label: Leverage and integration risk
points: An analyst raised concern about interest burden from an estimated ~INR2,000 crores debt component (implying ~INR200 crores annual interest at 10% cost) potentially consuming a large share of profit from new business generating an estimated INR1,000-1,200 crores initial-year revenue; management countered that actual borrowing cost in the two acquisition geographies is materially below 10% and that the acquired business is expected to be cash flow positive from inception.

An analyst flagged the historical difficulty Indian companies face in digesting large overseas acquisitions, and the risk of thin management bandwidth given two back-to-back major acquisitions plus a group company with inherent challenges; management responded that both acquired businesses are steady, well-run (strong existing MBJ management team) and that GTBL's role is to bring synergies rather than turn around distressed businesses.

subsections.label: Historical production disruption
points: One prior year saw a slight revenue/profitability reduction due to production-related issues caused by excessive rains and power fluctuations.

subsections.label: Customer dispute (resolved)
points: A recent dispute with Optimus Drugs led to a period of non-supply, though this is now resolved and business is restarting.

subsections.label: Promoter share pledge
points: Promoter encumbrance/pledge stood at around 48-48.5% as of June 2026, with about 1.5-2% released in July; management expects it to reduce significantly within 12-15 months.

subsections.label: Near-term output ramp
points: Output from expanded fermentation and API capacity expected to begin appearing from Q2 FY27 (current quarter) and more fully in the second half of FY27.
New fermentation manufacturing site expected to run full steam by end of August 2026.
Hybrid power plant Phase 1 expected live September 2026, Phase 2 about 2 months later, expected to aid EBITDA margins.

subsections.label: Funding and closing timeline
points: MicroBiopharm Japan deal expected to close around end of August 2026, funding largely secured pending some last-minute approvals.
Sanofi acquisition expected to close in 6-9 months or longer, with long-stop date June 2027.
Equity raise of up to INR1,000 crores planned; final debt/equity mix to be decided closer to the MBJ closing date.

subsections.label: Longer-term growth outlook
points: Management expects growth on a quarter-on-quarter basis from new capacity, with additional revenue/earnings uplift expected from MBJ synergies and Sanofi portfolio integration.
On a base-case basis, company targets high-teen revenue growth over the next 3-5 years without committing to a specific absolute revenue figure.
Expect some MBJ-GTBL synergy projects to start within the first year of integration.
Promoter pledge expected to reduce significantly within 12-15 months.

key_takeaways: Revenue from operations for Q1 FY27 stood at INR43.8 crores compared with INR35.9 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, an increase of 22.1% year-on-year.
EBITDA for the quarter grew by 49.4% year-on-year to INR20.8 crores with an EBITDA margin of 47.5%, up by 867 basis points.
Profit after tax stood at INR11.1 crores compared with INR9.1 crores in Q1 FY26, reflecting a growth of 22.1% year-on-year.

GTBL recently announced plans to acquire MicroBiopharm Japan, which specializes in precision fermentation and various other technologies and therapy areas, adding immunosuppressants, oncology, anti-infectives and technical capabilities such as peptides, plasmids, ADCs and enzyme engineering.
GTBL is acquiring 13 established brands from Sanofi France in the anti-TB and anti-infective segments, giving access to 55 countries across Europe, Middle East and Africa markets.
Company has practically doubled fermentation capacity (additional 540 KL), with the manufacturing site starting full steam by the end of this month.

Gross block grew from around INR62 crores in FY23 to around INR435 crores in FY26 (including CWIP), an incremental addition of around INR370 crores, of which around INR200 crores is expected to deliver asset turns of 1.4x to 1.5x.
On a base case basis, management wants to grow on a high-teen basis over the next 3-5 years.

The MicroBiopharm Japan deal is expected to close by end of August 2026; the Sanofi acquisition is expected to take 6-9 months or longer, with a long-stop date of June 2027 due to regulatory approvals required from over 50 countries.

quarters.summary: FY26 was a strong growth year with revenue up 57% to INR 1,098 crores, service EBITDA up 70% to INR 142 crores, and Q4 marking the company's first-ever adjusted EBITDA breakeven quarter on a consolidated basis. Management expects FY27 to be profitable for the full year on a consolidated basis, continued 40%+ historical CAGR-like growth, corporate overheads to remain largely flat in absolute terms (shrinking as % of revenue), and a 5-year target of service EBITDA expanding to ~24-25% with corporate overheads shrinking to sub 5-6%, translating to an adjusted EBITDA/PBT-PAT margin of 18-20% of revenues by around FY30.

subsections.label: Pro forma basis note
points: FY25 financial numbers and financial KPIs are presented on a pro forma basis, consistent with RHP disclosures.

Reason: the listed entity TFS acquired a material subsidiary, Turtlemint Insurance Broking (TIB), on May 8, 2024, so audited financials consolidated TIB for only 328 days, not 365; comparative financials therefore compare whole year with whole year on pro forma basis.

subsections.label: Service EBITDA definition
points: Service EBITDA is profitability after accounting for all variable costs: commissions paid to PoSP partners, campaigns run with them, selling and distribution costs (frontline team costs engaging with partners), and direct-tech API costs incurred in producing policies.
Metric reflects the unique economics of Turtlemint's aggregated producer network including commission cost and cost of operating infrastructure supporting the producer base.
Service EBITDA has historically grown faster than revenue growth rate.
Service EBITDA grew from FY23 loss of INR 65 crores to FY26 of INR 142 crores, a margin of 13% of revenue in FY26, up 70% YoY.

subsections.label: Corporate overheads
points: Corporate overheads include people's costs (technology and brand teams), marketing and other expenses, and corporate/compliance teams.
These costs do not expand with number of transactions on the platform, driving strong operating leverage; overheads have been shrinking as % of revenue over the last three years.

Costs maintained largely flat over the last four years while the company scaled materially (kept within an INR 230-260 crore band across FY23-FY25); improvement driven by continuous deployment of automation in internal processes and business.
Corporate overheads were INR 247 crores in FY26 (23% of revenue) versus INR 270 crores in FY25 (38% of revenue); Q4 FY26 corporate overheads were 16% of revenue.

subsections.label: Levers of service EBITDA expansion
points: Growth of renewal revenues (grew ~50% over prior year, reaching INR 225-230 crores, ~20% of overall revenue) is one key lever.

Improving productivity of relationship managers (whose cost is included within service EBITDA) is the second lever; premium productivity for frontline employees grew over 20% in the last year, enabled by tech platform investments allowing frontline staff to service more PoSP partners monthly given end-to-end digital policy issuance.

subsections.label: Profitability progression
points: FY26 adjusted EBITDA was -INR 105 crores (-10% of revenue), improved from -INR 186 crores (-27% of revenue) in FY25.
PAT before exceptional items was INR 129 crores (12% of revenue) in FY26 versus -INR 203 crores (-30% of revenue) in FY25.

Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 357 crores, up 42% YoY; Q4 service EBITDA was INR 60 crores, up 60% YoY; Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA and PAT both turned positive, marking the first profitable quarter, with adjusted EBITDA reaching breakeven.
ESOP cost was INR 25 crores in FY26 (2.3% of revenue) versus 1.7% of revenue in FY25.

subsections.label: Exceptional items
points: FY26 exceptional item charge of INR 55 crores was a non-cash adjustment resulting from arrangements related to conversion of preference share capital to equity capital, as documented in shareholders' agreements.
Charge was recorded in the nine-month period up to December 31, 2025, disclosed in the prospectus.
No exceptional items in quarter ended March 31, 2026, and none expected in FY27.

subsections.label: Cash conversion and working capital
points: Balance sheet has few fixed assets beyond IT equipment; no cost capitalization, all costs expensed; net working capital and cash/bank balances represent net worth.

Accounts receivable is the key working capital metric tracked; supported by insurance partners with 15-day or monthly billing/collection cycles, keeping receivables at 40-50 days of quarterly revenue, with closing consolidated accounts receivable of INR 150-160 crores in FY26.
Commissions to PoSP partners are, to the maximum extent possible, paid only after collections from insurance companies, maintaining a positive cash cycle.
Movement in receivables and payables in FY26 cash flow was small relative to company scale, supporting ~99% PAT-to-cash-from-operations conversion.

subsections.label: Dividend/distribution policy
points: Management has historically been conservative on cash; as sustained profitability is demonstrated over the next one or two years, the company looks forward to having an appropriate dividend/distribution policy for shareholders.
No buyback or major cash-deployment decision currently indicated; company noted it is well set up as a high operating-leverage business.

subsections.label: Historical KPI CAGRs (FY20-FY26)
points: Quarterly active DPs grew from 7,000 to approximately 84,000 at a CAGR of 64%.
Verified DPs grew from 1.2 lakh to 6.5 lakh at a CAGR of 41%.

Revenue grew from INR 163 crores in FY20 to close to INR 1,100 crores (INR 1,098 crores) at a CAGR of 46%, with platform premium growing to INR 3,868 crores in FY26 (up 31% YoY from INR 2,946 crores in FY25) and overall revenue up 57% YoY (from INR 700 crores).

points: GI businesses are more than 90% of platform premium/revenue versus life insurance businesses (life <10%); company does not want to disclose further splits within GI.
Within GI, health has been growing extremely strong, up more than 60% in the last year, partly aided by affordability tailwinds (GST cuts) leading to >75% growth.
As health business and renewal book size grow over time, profitability is expected to improve; renewal book was ~20% of revenues, about INR 230-odd crores for FY26.
Renewal rates are higher than industry average across all product categories sold, given high granularity of PoSP base and high contactability of end customers.
New vs renewal service EBITDA margins differ by 2.5-3x, underscoring the profitability uplift as the renewal book scales.

subsections.label: Enterprise business (Turtlefin)
points: Turtlefin premiums come from enterprise customers — large banks, FinTechs, NBFCs using Turtlemint's tech platform to drive digitization in their own ecosystems; enterprise premium is ~20% of total platform premium in FY26 (up from an implied ~INR 66 crores/6.6 billion in FY25, with total platform premium moving from INR 29.5 billion in FY25 to INR 38.6 billion in FY26, per analyst reference).
Enterprise premium growth is driven by growth of partner businesses and amount of digitization/change management they can drive.
A good number of new accounts were added in FY26 that will go live in the coming year, expected to drive faster enterprise premium growth than seen last year.

Turtlefin is a high-margin business because the tech is already built and is being licensed; take rate is low (technology fee, not full broking commission) but transaction/volume-based and high margin.

subsections.label: Non-insurance / adjacency businesses
points: Insurance broking (TIB) revenue is 97% of total revenue, with non-insurance business at 3%.

Company also distributes mutual funds (~INR 1,400 crores AUM distributed in FY26) and loans (annualized disbursement run-rate of ~INR 300 crores in recent quarters) as adjacencies, leveraging the large customer base and wide DP network.
Loans is a very recent addition.
These businesses enjoy stronger profitability; incremental revenue mostly drops directly into service EBITDA/EBITDA.
It is early in the journey for these adjacencies but management sees good optionality as they learn and build.
In Turtlefin, no direct variable cost is associated with tech service fees since existing teams/tech platforms deliver the revenue, offering higher margin accretion potential in outer years.

subsections.label: Motor and product category migration
points: Most PoSPs without insurance background start their journey distributing awareness content around two-wheeler/motor insurance.
Depending on interest, PoSPs migrate to higher-end products like health insurance; supply for higher-end products comes from existing activated DP base.

Company declined to give exact breakup of motor sub-categories (ODTP, CV/fleet vs two-wheeler/local consumer), citing desire to establish more credibility on the street before sharing further granularity.

subsections.label: Insurer concentration
points: Low concentration with any single insurance company; works with 45+ insurer partners; top 3 partners account for about 22% of business; difference in share between partners ranked one to five is not very high.
Insurance companies get higher share based on quality of tech integration, mapping accuracy, and frequency of quotes shown.

subsections.label: Claims support role
points: Company has an in-house expert claims desk and claims engine supporting policyholders, especially for delayed or rejected claims (usually due to communication gaps, pending documentation, or policy understanding issues).
For health insurance, an in-house doctor is available; for other products, ex-surveyors are part of the claims team.
Status updates provided via consumer app to track claim documentation and process.
In Q4, settled about INR 85 crores+ of claims that were either delayed or rejected, working closely with insurance companies.

subsections.label: Digital ecosystem for advisors
points: Turtlemint Academy provides mobile-based training across products, claims handling, and selling skills, with 52,000+ monthly active users consuming 6,500+ training hours monthly and certifying/activating 5,000+ new sellers per month.

Customer engagement tools enable advisors to share personalized posters, videos, and content (1.25 million content pieces shared monthly, across 8 regional languages) via WhatsApp and Facebook, generating leads at scale.
Digital transaction infrastructure enables a 100% paperless journey with policies issued across 40 insurers, generating about 8 lakh quotes daily.
Turtlemint Pro app is the number one highest downloaded app among insurance seller apps, with 5 million+ downloads on Google Play in the last year and a 4.5-star rating.

subsections.label: Internal tools
points: Proprietary Ninja Sales Pro app is an internal sales and ops CRM application equipping relationship managers and frontline staff with AI-powered dashboards, tools, and training modules to support, recruit, and activate digital partners.
These initiatives have consistently improved frontline staff productivity by 20%+ each year, contributing to improved service EBITDA margins.
Insurance Hub streamlines policy issuance and integrations across 40+ insurer partners in a fully paperless manner.
Turtlefin enterprise distribution platform enables banks, NBFCs, FinTechs and other enterprises to digitize insurance in their ecosystems via plug-and-play modules and a one-API solution.
A consumer app helps customers simplify insurance management.

subsections.label: Agentic AI initiatives
points: Company is actively working on building agentic AI-enabled services to drive key KPIs: increasing agent activation and productivity, higher cross-sells and renewals, superior customer service, and better claims support.

AI investments already made in support tickets (majority now AI-first handled with fallback to humans if required) and renewal calling (nudging customers for renewals, especially for smaller ticket-size products, showing good results on renewal rates).

Insurance is a complex, underwritten product with many human-to-human interaction points (claims, endorsements, underwriting follow-ups, nudging due to buying inertia) that lend themselves well to automation via agentic AI/LLM-based models, seen as a huge enabler for the business.
Policy recommendation engine on the platform recommends products/options based on customer demographic.

subsections.label: Distribution network reach
points: Platform connects 6.5+ lakh advisors (digital partners), 46 insurance companies, and policyholders spanning 19,000+ PIN codes across India.
Network is granular such that top 100 DPs contribute less than 5% of the business (4.62% of platform premium as of March 31, 2026).
DPs present in remote parts of the country including Ladakh, Arunachal, Lakshadweep Islands, covering 98-99% of PIN codes.
76% of premium comes from beyond the top 30 cities, reflecting focus on Tier 3/Tier 4/B30 markets.

P3M active digital partners reached 93,000+ as of March 31, 2026, with the P3M active base growing at a 51% CAGR over the last 7 years; average quarterly active DPs across FY26 (average of Q1-Q4 P3M) were approximately 84,000.

subsections.label: Recruitment and onboarding
points: About 80% of onboarded digital partners do not come from an insurance background and are freshers to insurance; most are under 35 years of age.
About 60-65 different profiles encountered when DPs come onto the platform (college students, financial advisers, retired bank employees, etc.).
Recruitment is done digitally through the app as well as offline through pan-India branch network.

subsections.label: Cohort earnings growth
points: Digital partners onboarded in FY20 are earning up to 3.8x their initial earnings on the platform, facilitated by growing platform familiarity, ability to sell across multiple insurers/categories, and securing renewals.

key_figures.label: Assisted distribution share of retail insurance sales in India

subsections.label: Business model & vision
points: Mission: make insurance simple, accessible, and trusted for every Indian household; vision of 'Insurance for All by 2047' (a Government mission meaning by 2047 everyone in the country should be insured for one asset, one health, and one life policy).
Thesis: customers need advisory and guidance support in selecting insurance products; data shows assisted distribution accounts for over 95% of all retail insurance sales in India.

Insurance is significantly underpenetrated in India (3-4% penetration), providing immense growth opportunity; a tech-enabled adviser-led model is seen as best suited for reaching underserved segments.

Triadic ecosystem (policyholders, digital partners, insurers) creates value for every stakeholder: policyholders get choice, expert guidance, claim support (especially Tier 3/Tier 4/B30); digital partners get multi-insurer products, digital tools, training, income opportunity, long-term career path; insurers get reach, granular underwriting, and cost-efficient scale.

subsections.label: Growth strategy (RAP model)
points: Growth strategy anchored in ability to recruit individuals at scale, onboard them onto Turtlemint Pro platform, handhold via training, equip with skills/tools to activate, help them start producing, and improve productivity YoY — described as 'Recruit, Activate, and Produce' (RAP).
This is now executed at scale, creating a repeatable growth engine.

Two cohort dynamics drive growth: existing cohorts grow via productivity improvement YoY, and new cohorts add incremental growth; this creates a compounding 'book-building' effect via renewal book contribution.

subsections.label: Competitive differentiation vs other distributors (e.g., Policybazaar)
points: Historically insurance distribution had significant overhead; digitization, financial awareness, and macro changes are now driving penetration into Tier 3/Tier 4 markets.

Turtlemint's belief: insurance is an advisory-led product that doesn't come naturally to people and needs to be explained; addressing this via a network of individuals within the potential policyholder's social community, with an economic model built around it, is the company's differentiator and has led to significant scale and high operating leverage.

subsections.label: Insurer partnership value proposition
points: Turtlemint provides insurers Tier 3/Tier 4 access where insurers may not have presence.
Enables granular underwriting for insurers via digital policy issuance in specific PIN code pockets and product categories.
Provides large-scale, low-OpEx distribution.

Delivers quality of book: better renewal rates, improving renewal rates and persistency, using tech to identify leakage/fraud, and demonstrated lower loss ratios versus insurers' own product for specific categories in some cases.
These are long-term relationships built over several years with negotiations over longer periods.

subsections.label: Employee attrition and compensation
points: Company reports better attrition versus industry for both frontline and non-frontline teams, credited to compensation structures: fixed pay, performance-tied variable pay, long-term guaranteed bonus paid over four years to retain top employees, and a generous ESOP scheme covering more than 500 employees.
Latest quarter attrition figure not immediately available; extensive data was given in the DRHP.

subsections.label: Regulatory uncertainty on commissions
points: Ongoing discussion/regulation on commission cuts for insurance distribution; actual discussion paper not yet known, creating uncertainty on impact.
Uncertainty on how PoSPs will be classified under commission regulations — whether bucketed as agents or brokers, and whether treatment could differ across channels.

Management believes Turtlemint's asset-light, performance-driven model (costs incurred only after a transaction) gives ability to absorb any commission/regulatory volatility and pass down cost structure changes, citing past experience during GST cuts (OND period) when health insurers reduced distributor commissions and Turtlemint was able to absorb and pass down the cuts while still growing 70-75%+.

subsections.label: Base effect on growth sustainability
points: H1 FY26 growth was elevated due to a base effect from the previous year (FY25); Q4 growth is seen as closer to steady-state growth.
Second half of FY27 will face a high base effect from strong H2 FY26 growth, per analyst query.

subsections.label: Seasonality
points: Q4 is seasonally the biggest quarter of the year (high season), which contributed to the first EBITDA-positive quarter; seasonality will continue to play out across FY27 quarters.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Board decided not to give formal future guidance, but management offered directional commentary since this was the first earnings call.
Q4 FY26 was the first profitable quarter, demonstrating operating leverage with scale and expanding service EBITDA leading to significantly higher profitability potential ahead.

For FY27, expect to reduce losses/improve profitability by more than 40%, consistent with historical pattern; every quarter in a financial year is bigger than the previous quarter, with Q4 being the big season.
Expect the entire FY27 year to achieve profitability on a consolidated basis.

Growth expected to continue as historically: P3M active will grow, driving productivity of existing and new cohorts, and improving renewal rates (renewal rates in the quarter were significantly higher than same period previous year) will further benefit profitability.
No exceptional items expected in FY27.

subsections.label: Long-term (5-year / FY30) targets
points: Over the next five years, service EBITDA is expected to expand and corporate overheads to shrink as % of revenue (though overheads will grow in absolute inflation-adjusted terms).

Adjusted EBITDA (PBT/PAT level) expected to be in the range of 17-18% to 20% of revenues in about five years, largely driven by improvement in service EBITDA from today's levels of 13-14% to about 24-25%, while holding corporate overheads relatively flat, shrinking to sub 5-6% of revenue.

Growth in renewal book contribution (annuity income that drops directly into EBITDA) is expected to continue contributing to service EBITDA expansion; quality of book (e.g., low TP-only policy share, near-100% contactability) is a focus area.

subsections.label: Dividend policy outlook
points: As sustained profitability is demonstrated over the next one or two years, company looks forward to establishing an appropriate dividend/distribution policy for shareholders.

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect our EBITDA to be in the range of 18-20% of revenue in the next five years period (PBT/PAT level between 17-18% to 20% of revenues)
Service EBITDA expansion from today's 13-14% to about 24-25% in the next few years
Corporate overheads will be in the range of sub 5-6% as they are not scaling with revenue

We will reduce our losses or improve our profitability by more than 40% how we have done in the past
Historically, we have grown at a CAGR of about 40% plus, and we will ensure that we keep performing as per how we have done in the history of the company
We don't expect any exceptional items in FY27 either

As we demonstrate maybe one or two years of sustained profitability and strengthening profitability, we do look forward to having the appropriate dividend distribution policies for all the shareholders

We should start to see growth in our enterprise premiums also at a faster pace than what we saw in the last year, aided by new accounts going live
