themes.label: Operating leverage / margin expansion
themes.note: Corporate overheads shrank from 38% to 23% of revenue YoY in FY26 (16% in Q4), driving first-ever adjusted EBITDA breakeven quarter and a 5-year target of 18-20% EBITDA margin.

themes.label: Renewal book / annuity income growth
themes.note: Renewal revenue grew 51% to INR 225 crores (20% of revenues), with renewal rates higher than industry average and expected to keep expanding service EBITDA via book-building.

themes.label: Regulatory uncertainty on commissions
themes.note: Ongoing discussion on commission regulations and PoSP classification (agent vs broker) creates uncertainty, though management cites past GST-cut experience as evidence of resilience.

themes.label: AI/tech-led productivity
themes.note: Agentic AI investments in support tickets and renewal calling, plus Ninja Sales Pro CRM, have driven 20%+ annual frontline productivity gains and are seen as a growth enabler.

themes.label: B30/Tier 3-4 penetration and granular distribution
themes.note: 76% of premium comes from beyond top-30 cities; network spans 19,000+ PIN codes with top 100 DPs contributing only 4.62% of premium, underpinning the 'Insurance for All by 2047' strategy.

themes.label: Diversification into adjacent financial products
themes.note: Mutual fund AUM of ~INR 1,400 crores and loan disbursement run-rate of ~INR 300 crores annualized are early-stage adjacencies leveraging the existing DP network and customer base.

themes.label: First profitability milestone
themes.note: Q4 FY26 marked the company's first-ever adjusted EBITDA breakeven quarter on a consolidated basis, with full-year FY27 consolidated profitability guided.

key_takeaways: FY26, for us, was a strong year of performance. Our platform premium grew from INR 2,946 crores to INR 3,868 crores. Our revenue grew from INR 700 crores to INR 1,098 crores, just INR 2 crores short of 1,100, and growth was 57%. Our renewal revenue grew by 51% to INR 225 crores. Service EBITDA grew 70% to INR 142 crores.

In Q4, revenue grew 42% to reach INR 357 crores, and service EBITDA grew by about 60% to reach INR 60 crores. We are also happy to announce, in Q4, that this was our first breakeven quarter ever at an adjusted EBITDA level on a consolidated basis.

Since FY20, our quarterly active DPs have grown from 7,000 to approximately 84,000 at a CAGR of 64%. Our verified DPs grew from 1.2 lakh to 6.5 lakh at a CAGR of 41%. Revenue has grown from INR 163 crores in FY20 to now close to INR 1,100 crores at a CAGR of 46%.

In FY26, our corporate overheads were INR 247 crores for the whole year, down from nearly INR 270 crores in FY25. This has resulted in corporate overheads as a percentage of revenues, reducing from 38% of revenues in FY25 to 23% for the whole year FY26.
Adjusted EBITDA for the whole year was INR 105 crores loss, or about roughly minus 10% of revenues. This is significantly lower than INR 186 crores of loss in the prior year at minus 27%.

For the year ended FY26, PAT before exceptional items was INR 129 crores, or about 12% of revenues. This has improved for about INR 203 crores for the prior year, which was nearly minus 30% of revenues.
For the year ended March 31, 2026, our cash conversion is at 99% of profit after tax and before exceptional items.

On a long-term basis, in the next five years period, we expect our service EBITDA to expand and our corporate overheads to shrink as a percentage of revenue... we expect our EBITDA to be in the range of 18-20%.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Improvement in margins attributed to scale/higher volumes rather than price hikes, as only a minimal price correction was effective from 1st April.
Major raw material cost pass-through will be effective from 1st July, which management expects to further support margins.
Operating leverage expected to kick in further as volumes increase, supporting additional 1-2% margin upside making 28.5-29% a distinct possibility.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Company is debt-free and intends to remain so.
Cash accruals generated over the coming 2 years will be used to fund the INR120 crores capex for the new Greenfield Foundry, rather than raising external capital.
Management declined shareholder suggestion of a rights issue, citing sufficient internal reserves (INR120 crores as of March '26) and potential EPS dilution.
Management said it would take shareholder's bonus issue suggestion to the Board for consideration.

subsections.label: Order booking cadence
points: Company generally books orders for a forward period of about 3-4 months, with orders replenished every month.
Order book value of INR140 crores represents firm business of about 3-4 months at a time; exact YoY growth number not available on call but management indicated an increase versus last year.

Demand visibility driven by indications from domestic and export customers of increased volumes, elevated commodity prices, rising infrastructure spending in India and abroad, and increased investment in sectors like railways.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Demand growth is a composite effect of new parts moving into serial supply and an overall increase in demand from customers across all 9 sectors served.
All 9 sectors served have been requesting improvement in supplies and increase in orders.
Automobile industry cited as a comparison, growing at 10-15%, indicating broader engineering industry strength.
Despite geopolitical issues, India seen as relatively insulated due to large domestic consumption.

key_figures.label: GET revenue contribution target (alt figure cited)

subsections.label: Sector diversification / derisking
points: Over the last several years, company has added new industry sectors to derisk from concentration in mining, which has dropped from 84% ten years back to about 54% now.
Earthmoving grew from near zero to about 36% currently; Construction grew from 15-16% to about 20-21% currently.
Company caters to 9 different sectors in total (6 existing plus 3 newer ones).

Current sector revenue split for FY27: Mining ~27%, Earthmoving ~43%, Construction ~15%, Defense ~1%; Mining+Earthmoving+Construction combined represent ~70% of revenue, with the other 6 sectors making up the remaining ~30%.

subsections.label: Ground engaging tools (GET)
points: Company is in the process of developing new GET parts; once approved, these will move into serial supplies.
GET currently contributes less than 1% of revenue (1% in FY26); targeted to rise to 3.5% in FY27 and to about 6% by FY29 (also referenced as 4.5-5% in response to another question).

subsections.label: Defense
points: Defense has been given a lower priority over the past year as opportunities and pricing in other sectors are seen as better; defense currently contributes only about 1% of revenue.
Management views defense as a risky business given dependence on a single customer, despite market fanfare around the sector in India.
Israel defense component trials are ongoing; company expects updates in the coming few months.
No firm plan exists to significantly scale overseas defense revenue beyond 1-2% over the next 3 years.

subsections.label: New parts development
points: More than 100 new parts have been developed in the last 18-24 months, which will now move into serial supply.
Increase in volumes will come from a composite effect of new parts entering serial supply plus rising demand from existing customers.
New parts expected to contribute about 20% of business over the next 2-3 years, with existing parts contributing the remaining 80%.

subsections.label: New product / part development
points: Continuous drive for new parts development; more than 100 parts developed in last 18-24 months, moving into serial supply.
Israel defense component currently in trials; results expected in coming months.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion rationale
points: Board has approved establishment of Greenfield Foundry with 8,500 tons capacity, capex of INR120 crores over the next 2 years, targeted commissioning by 31st March FY28, and casting weight range of 5 kg to 1,000 kg, to cater to growing market demand and enhance manufacturing capabilities; peak revenue potential from the new facility estimated at INR300 crores.
Land for the new facility (100,000 sq meters) was already available, given by the Government of Gujarat some months back.
New facility is 12 km from existing facility; raw material procurement strategy will remain the same as for the existing facility.

Existing capacity stands at 29,000 tons, with utilization at 48% in FY26 and 63-66% in Q1 FY27 (Q1 FY27 production volume ~4,700 tons, alternately cited as ~4,000 tons by a participant); full-year FY27 utilization guided at 63%, implying about 18,000 tons of incremental volume.

90% utilization target for FY29 is on existing capacities only; the new facility will only start contributing revenues later, and additional capacity is being created because existing utilization is reaching 90%, beyond which bottlenecks arise.
Increasing capex viewed as a signal of how the demand scenario is playing out and how existing clients are looking to increase sourcing from the company.

subsections.label: Renewable energy / energy transition
points: Two renewable power projects under implementation: a 2.4 MW hybrid (wind+solar) plant and a 1.4 MW solar plant, both expected to be commissioned before 31st December '26, as part of strengthening renewable energy footprint and reducing carbon emissions in line with increasing production requirements.
Company is considering transitioning some manufacturing processes from natural gas to electricity-based systems over the next 2-3 years, given shortage/price volatility of natural gas, LPG etc.

At current gas prices, there would be savings from using electricity instead of natural gas, but long-term natural gas pricing trends are unpredictable, making the switch's economics uncertain over the longer term.

subsections.label: Workforce readiness
points: Number of employees increased by only 32 (3%) per the annual report; management stated the company is adequately staffed at all levels for current year's budgeted production.
Recruitment and training for additional headcount is planned for mid-year to prepare for FY28, with further recruitment as needed in FY28 or FY29.

subsections.label: Inventory / production ramp
points: Rise in inventory (WIP not yet converted to sales) attributed to the nature of the industry — when production increases, inventory piles up initially, and with a time lag of 1-2 months, inventory levels normalize; company then operates at elevated inventory levels.

subsections.label: Export mix strategy
points: Historically exports have ranged 45-50% of revenue over several years, sometimes reaching as high as 60-62%.
For FY27, exports expected at about 49-50% on value basis; next year domestic expected to be slightly better at ~53% with exports at ~47%.

On tonnage basis, export share was about 60-62% in Q1 FY27 (an initial figure of 51% was also cited before correction); export/domestic mix going forward assumed on a roughly 50-50 basis on volume terms.

Company is Tier 1 supplier for more than 98-99% of sales, giving directly to OEMs; some OEMs in India may further export the supplied components, meaning true (direct+indirect) export exposure could be slightly higher than reported, though the company does not track this precisely.
US railroad opportunity has been deprioritized in favor of pursuing better markets, products and pricing in other industrial sectors; will be revisited later.

Company has broadened export geographies from 2 countries (US and Germany, which represented 100% of exports) 10 years back to about 16 countries currently, with intent to keep reducing dependence on US and Germany (currently ~70% combined, with the other 14 countries making up ~30%) over time.

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing
points: Steelcast does not use raw material from ship breaking directly, as its high-strength low-alloy and carbon steel products require cleaner scrap with very low sulfur, phosphorus and carbon.
Company sources from downstream industries (e.g., rolling mills) that are themselves downstream of ship breaking, for locational advantage — not directly from Alang ship breaking yard.
Raw material sourcing strategy for the new Greenfield Foundry (12 km from existing facility) will remain the same as for the existing facility.

subsections.label: Fuel/energy availability
points: Energy costs have remained elevated due to global geopolitical developments and sustained pressure on fuel prices; company has ensured adequate fuel availability to support uninterrupted production.
Natural gas prices are currently about 50-55% more expensive compared to February-end levels.

subsections.label: Macro environment
points: Global economy remained resilient despite geopolitical tensions, trade policy shifts and supply chain realignments; global GDP growth estimated at 3.3% for CY2026.

India continues to be the fastest-growing major economy (GDP growth estimated 6.5-7% for CY2026), supported by robust domestic consumption, sustained government-led infrastructure spending, and strong policy focus on manufacturing and localization.
Industrial activity remains strong across manufacturing, infrastructure and mining, creating a favorable demand environment for key industrial sectors.
Government initiatives such as Make in India, PLI schemes and infrastructure investments continue to support India's long-term manufacturing and industrial growth story.

subsections.label: Industry trends
points: Casting and forging industry continues to benefit from strong demand across mining, earthmoving, construction, railways, defense and other industrial sectors.

Demand fundamentals driven by strong equipment utilization in mining and construction, continued infrastructure expansion, and growing requirements for ground engaging tools, wear parts and high-performance steel castings used in excavators, loaders and heavy earthmoving machinery.

Indian foundry industry projected to grow at a healthy pace supported by investments in transportation, energy, mining, industrial development; forging industry benefits from opportunities in automotive, defense, railways and heavy engineering sectors.
Automobile industry cited as growing at 10-15%, seen as a positive read-through for the broader engineering/casting industry.

subsections.label: Capital structure considerations
points: Shareholder suggested funding the INR120 crores capex via a rights issue at a premium (e.g., ~INR200-300, illustratively reducing an example INR100 crores project cost to INR10 crores of cash outlay, financing ~60% of project cost) to reduce cash burden; management responded that the company already has sufficient reserves (INR120 crores as of March '26) and does not need additional shareholder capital, and that increased equity would dilute EPS.
Shareholder suggested a bonus issue to improve visibility, brand equity and shareholding count; management said it would take this suggestion to the Board.

Shareholder suggested focusing on specific defense components to improve long-term sales productivity; management reiterated its view that defense is a risky, single-customer-dependent business and that better opportunities exist elsewhere, but said it would consider defense opportunities if they arise.

subsections.label: Cost/input pressures
points: Input costs of various raw materials and natural gas have increased, necessitating an upward price correction effective 1st July '27 (referenced elsewhere as 1st July, aligned with the sales price variation formula with customers).
Cost pass-through to customers occurs with roughly a 1-quarter lag, both for increases and decreases in input costs.
Natural gas prices are about 50-55% higher than February-end levels, adding cost pressure, though this is expected to be compensated via the pass-through formula.
Currency fluctuation (rupee depreciation/appreciation) is shared with customers rather than fully hedged or retained by the company.

subsections.label: Customer concentration / segment risk
points: Defense business viewed as high risk due to dependence on a single customer, despite favorable market sentiment toward the defense sector in India.
Company has historically been concentrated in mining, earthmoving, US and Germany export markets; ongoing diversification efforts aim to reduce this concentration risk over time.

subsections.label: Geopolitical/macro risk
points: Geopolitical tensions, trade policy shifts and supply chain realignments continue to pose risks to the global economy, though India is seen as relatively insulated due to large domestic consumption.

For FY27, initially guided to 25% growth versus last financial year, later revised upward on the call to 30% given strong indications from most customers, with the 25% figure characterized as conservative.

There will be sequential improvement in top line for several quarters going forward; margins will remain in guided range with focus on driving top line; operating leverage benefit should kick in as scale increases.
Increasing capex viewed as a signal of the demand scenario and increasing sourcing intent from existing clients.
FY27 growth of 25-30% guided in volume terms, with export/domestic mix assumed on a roughly 50-50 basis on a volume basis.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: EBITDA margin could rise 150-200 bps to around 28.5-29% for FY27 versus 27% in FY26, theoretically achievable and something management will strive for, aided by cost pass-through (effective 1st July) and operating leverage.

guidance_ledger.statement: Targeting a growth of 25% compared to last financial year; later in the call revised to 30% volume growth given strong customer indications, calling 25% conservative.
Targeting a growth trajectory of approximately 20% CAGR over the coming years.

EBITDA margin could see 150-200 bps improvement to around 28.5%-29% for FY27, aided by cost pass-through and operating leverage; management called this a distinct possibility they will strive to achieve.

quarters.summary: Steelcast delivered strong FY26 revenue/EBITDA/PAT growth with export-led demand, but Q4FY26 saw margin pressure from higher fuel, power and manufacturing costs; management expects cost pass-through via price adjustments and rupee depreciation in coming quarters. Management guided to ~20% CAGR volume/revenue growth over the next three years (esp. FY27), an aspiration of >₹100 crore PAT in FY27, doubling of sales by FY29 (to ~₹860 crore) on present capacity, sustainable EBITDA margins of 25-26% going forward, and a capacity expansion decision by end-July 2026.

subsections.label: Cost discipline & margin pressure
points: Material costs effectively managed despite commodity volatility through agile procurement strategies such as just-in-time sourcing, ensuring stable consumption levels.
Manufacturing expenses increased due to higher maintenance activities, machinery repairs, and provisions related to export-related obligations.
Higher fuel prices coupled with increased production activity led to a rise in power and energy costs.
Other operating expenses remained largely stable, and consumption of stores and spares was managed efficiently with only marginal movement.
Despite short-term margin pressure, annual performance remains strong, underpinned by healthy growth in volumes, revenues and profitability versus prior year.

subsections.label: Cost pass-through / price adjustments
points: Company expects to receive price adjustments from customers in subsequent quarters to compensate for elevated fuel and freight costs, especially given the Middle East situation, wherever applicable.
These adjustments and rupee depreciation are expected to help offset the cost impact observed during the current period.
Raw material costs have risen ~10% across the board since around March 1; impact on sales prices expected to be ~4-5%.
Partial compensation already received effective April 1, with remaining adjustment expected from July 1; company believes it will be largely covered for this cost increase.
Rupee depreciation expected to provide additional support, with exports contributing over 60% of revenue.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital allocation
points: Company maintains a debt-free balance sheet with healthy cash reserves of around ₹114 crore, providing flexibility to navigate uncertainties and capitalize on opportunities.

On bonus issue: management stated there is nothing on the horizon currently, though several options are being considered; any action will be in the larger interest of the company's 16,000 shareholders.
Paid-up capital stands at ₹10.1 crore.

subsections.label: YoY vs QoQ comparison caveat
points: Management noted Q4FY26 was ~12% lower than Q4FY25 on PAT and topline, but recommended comparing annual numbers rather than quarterly, calling such quarterly movements 'aberrations'; also recommended looking at preceding quarter numbers.

subsections.label: Demand trends
points: Overall volumes improved compared to the immediate past period, though there was some moderation versus the corresponding period of the previous year.
Revenue trends followed a similar trajectory, with sequential growth supported by strong contributions from both export and domestic segments.
Demand continued to improve in recent months despite ongoing global uncertainties, particularly in regions affected by prolonged geopolitical tensions.

New part development orders have been unaffected by near-term uncertainties, geopolitical tensions, the Middle East war and the earlier Russia-Ukraine war; pace has in fact significantly increased in the last 4-6 weeks.

subsections.label: Pricing / realizations
points: Realizations remain steady despite geopolitical tensions and near-term uncertainties, supported by a sales price variation formula with all customers that allows cost increases to be passed through (and cost reductions to be passed back).
No significant effect on realizations from mix shift as utilization/growth increases.

subsections.label: Overseas defense repeat orders
points: Repeat orders from overseas defense relate to parts for compact vehicles generally used in ground wars.
Prototypes and the prototype batch have been approved; company is now awaiting serial supply orders.
If serial supplies materialize, sales potential estimated in the region of INR15-18 crore.
Business model for defense parts will follow the same cost-plus/automatic price-adjustment formula as existing customers; working capital cycle expected to be similar (75-110 days range).

points: Ground engaging tools contribution to total sales was 1.1% in FY26 and is planned to rise to 3.8% in FY27.
Growth comes from existing customers; customer names not disclosed.

subsections.label: Railroad segment challenges
points: Company faced challenges in railroad developments being worked on and has not yet fully resolved them.

Competitive intensity in mining, earthmoving, construction and locomotives is relatively more favorable compared to railroad, so company continues to work on railroad issues while capitalizing on opportunities in these other industries.

subsections.label: Sector diversification request
points: An analyst requested a more detailed revenue breakup in upcoming presentations — sector-wise split (auto, non-auto, earthmoving, ground engaging tools, etc.) and a more granular export breakdown (e.g., North America vs other regions), ideally as a multi-year trend, to show diversification progress.
Management said the suggestion is well taken and will try to implement it from Q1 of FY27.

subsections.label: New part development
points: New part development is a constant exercise; close to more than 50 parts are under different stages of development.
As parts are ready, they are sent to customers for approvals, which then convert into serial supplies.
Major end-user industries for new parts: mining, earthmoving, construction, locomotives, railroad.
Parts vary based on customer requirements within existing capability range of 5 kg to 2,500 kg, with no restriction to a specific weight segment; depends entirely on customer needs.
Due to confidentiality, detailed application-level disclosure was not possible.

subsections.label: Data center demand assessment
points: Management stated there is practically no requirement of steel castings in data centers, so no significant increase in demand is expected from data center capex trends, unlike what some large clients in other industries have indicated.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion decision timeline
points: Company was initially contemplating a capacity expansion decision by December 2026 but has now decided to bring the decision forward to end-July 2026, driven by increasing demand and new parts getting converted to serial supplies.

Management does not want to wait until reaching 75% utilization levels to decide on capex; with current utilization at 63-64% and strong customer indications, company is in an advanced stage of finalizing the capex for capacity expansion.
Exact capex numbers (including project cost and expected timeline) to be shared by end-July 2026; company is currently halfway through the exercise.

subsections.label: Hybrid power project
points: 2.4 MW hybrid power project is under commissioning by June 2026, expected to improve sustainability while generating annual savings of approximately ₹3.6 crore.

subsections.label: Export vs domestic performance

Exports contributed over 60% of revenues during the year, reaffirming strong global positioning.
Steady traction witnessed from North America and other developed markets, alongside increased engagement with global OEMs driven by ongoing supply chain diversification.
'China + 1' strategies being adopted by companies are benefiting countries like India amid geopolitical tensions and supply chain realignments.

Diversified customer base and presence across multiple sectors and geographies help mitigate concentration risks and enhance business resilience.

subsections.label: Governance

Effects include impact on crude oil prices, inflation, trade and balance of payments, remittances and employment, financial markets and investor sentiment, and energy security — underscoring the need for India to develop strategies to mitigate economic vulnerabilities.
Company has so far successfully managed these disruptions and is confident of navigating future disturbances.

Company actively manages key risks arising from cyclicality of end-user industries, foreign exchange fluctuations, volatility in raw material and energy costs, and geopolitical/supply chain disruptions.
Orders for a previously supplied overseas defense export product are getting delayed due to the Iran-U.S. war, though expected to materialize in the next 1-2 quarters.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY'27 was MPS's strongest opening quarter on record, with revenue up 20.4% YoY and EBITDA up 53.0% YoY, margins expanding across all three segments without material headcount growth. Management reaffirmed FY'27 guidance to comfortably cross INR 300 crores EBITDA, framing it as a floor rather than a ceiling, with conviction anchored in operating leverage, an AI-driven shift toward outcomes-based revenue, and early validation of the Unbound Medicine acquisition.

key_figures.label: Comfortable debt capacity (vs PAT of INR 200 crores)

subsections.label: Operating leverage
points: Revenue grew 20% while EBITDA grew 53% and headcount rose less than 3%, described as operating leverage converting growth into margin rather than consuming it.
Strip out AJE (resetting by design), and underlying business grew faster: revenue up 28.4%, EBITDA up 50.5%, margin expanding close to five points to 32.4%.

subsections.label: Balance sheet / housekeeping
points: Cash and cash equivalents of INR 138.02 crores as of 30 June against borrowings of INR 37.63 crores relating to the facility drawn for the Unbound Medicine acquisition.
Collections stayed tight, with DSO improving to 45 days from 51 days at end of March.
No exceptional items in the quarter, so results read clean.

subsections.label: Rule of 50 framing
points: Rule of 50 test: revenue growth rate plus EBITDA margin should clear 50 to indicate compounding rather than growth bought with margin.
Q1's 20% revenue growth and 34% EBITDA margin put the Company comfortably past 50; management hopeful of clearing 50 for the full year, but cautions phasing may not be neat every quarter.

subsections.label: Capital allocation for M&A
points: First area of attack for funding acquisitions is cash accruals (~INR 138 crores on hand, generating INR 15-18 crores/month).
Second area is debt: assuming PAT of ~INR 200 crores with similar cash flow, a corresponding debt level of INR 200 crores is considered comfortable.
Acquisitions in the INR 300-500 crores range seen as doable via internal cash accruals plus debt; no equity issuance planned barring exceptional circumstances ("never say never").

subsections.label: Headcount detail by segment
points: Research headcount grew from 2,262 to 2,452 over last year.
Education headcount went down from 799 to 765.
Nominal overall headcount increase because increments and Unbound additions were nullified by AJE's US roles being entirely offshored to India by end of Q4 FY26.
Net Promoter Scores rose during this transition, attributed to increased operational control post-offshoring.

key_figures.label: Research Solutions share of total revenue
Corporate Learning steady-state EBITDA margin target
MPS Research organic growth vs market

subsections.label: Research Solutions
points: Segment described now as an AI-first knowledge solutions company serving the research economy, built on a stack of product layers, not a services book.
EBITDA grew well ahead of revenue and margin widened to 45.1%, reflecting scale and margin moving together as the reset of the last two years becomes the norm.

AJE (author solutions) is deliberately resetting: consumer base finding new level, revenue smaller but far more profitable and higher quality than the inflated base carried two years ago; core now premium editorial/language editing and AI-assisted author workflows.
AJE launched Pre-Submission Peer Review in April, its first new service in over two years, with demand running ahead of plan.

Pre-acceptance peer review and journal editorial office business (enabled by AJE acquisition) is one of the fastest-growing lines; MPS is now the second largest peer-review provider by volume, aiming to be first by year-end.
Growth anchored by largest global publishers entrusting more submission workflow, including sensitive portfolios.

Author Solutions increasingly paid for outcomes (acceptance, integrity decisions, submissions processed) rather than hours/pages; controlled work shows ~52% manuscript acceptance rate vs ~32% industry baseline.

Growth avenues: premium tiers where authors pay for quality/turnaround, AI-driven productivity gains shared with clients and retained as margin, and expansion into fast-growing markets such as China with partnerships already signed.

subsections.label: Education Solutions
points: Education is MPS's second growth pillar; step-up driven in good part by Unbound Medicine now in base for first full quarter, reflected in client count rising to 841 from 404.

Underlying content and learning business (excluding acquisition effect) grew strongly on three drivers: (1) AI-enabled content/production deepening with largest US knowledge organizations across K-12 and higher education, moving from pilots to multi-year, multi-product programs; (2) accessibility line producing accessible learning media at scale with AI, building toward large journals rollout later this year, high-margin/high-growth; (3) new lanes such as clients paying MPS to review and quality-check AI-generated instructional content, a service that didn't exist a year ago.
Healthy pipeline across largest relationships with focus on extending into international knowledge organizations, plus first full year of Unbound to build on.

subsections.label: Corporate Learning (Liberate Global)
points: Second consecutive quarter of growth; margin story more notable than revenue, with EBITDA growth of 60.7% and margin expansion to 25.3% from under 17% a year ago, achieved on headcount roughly a third lighter than last year (last year's restructuring flowing through).

Repositioning from learning creation to enterprise capability enablement: AI-enabled and immersive solutions embedding learning/performance into flow of work, enhancing existing LMS, LXP, SharePoint and enterprise platforms with AI, simulations and immersive experiences for scalable, reusable solutions across business units/geographies.
Growth broadening with new client additions across geographies and AI-led wins acting as strategic anchors into larger enterprise transformation programs.

Headcount reduction breaks into three parts: (1) largest — structural redundancy from last year's restructuring consolidating duplicated roles and delayering delivery model (one-time reset); (2) shift from fixed to variable capacity via gig/associate model to flex cost with project demand; (3) smallest but growing — productivity gains from AI-enabled authoring/content/quality workflows letting smaller core teams deliver same or more.

Senior instructional design and client-facing bench were not touched; reductions concentrated in redundant/non-billable layers; delivery quality and client retention held through transition, with no rise in rework or client escalations despite margin expansion.
Improvement attributed to mix and operating leverage, with cost base rebuilt rather than chasing volume.

Two further engines going forward: shift toward AI-enabled, immersive, performance-focused solutions raising engagement value/margins; and deeper account penetration via cross-selling, managed learning services, AI platform enablement and enterprise-wide rollouts, with multiple enterprise engagements approaching $1 million and a healthy new-logo pipeline.
North America is less significant for Corporate Learning than for Research/Education, so less forex/dollar tailwind benefit versus the rest of the business.
Segment focus for rest of FY27: hold exit margin as run rate, make AI-led delivery the dominant part of the mix, and complete integration of legacy entities into one unified Liberate Global brand.

subsections.label: Client count / rationalization
points: Company-wide client count fell QoQ from 906 to 841; management clarified the only pruning in the business is within AJE, as previously described (no broader client rationalization).

subsections.label: Research Solutions technology stack
points: DigiCore, an AI-enabled production ecosystem, is now live in client delivery across top-tier knowledge organizations, with Research Integrity Check layered on top to detect paper mills, identity fraud, and image manipulation — positioning MPS at the 'verification' bottleneck rather than content generation.

AI-enabled composition and quality workflows are live in customer delivery, moving clients onto a modern, higher-productivity platform; on largest programs this shows up as one-touch workflows, automated alt-text for accessibility, and AI-driven quality checks catching errors before proof stage.

Platform stack (HighWire, DigiCore Pro, THINK365, now in production) forms the hosting/publishing backbone for largest clients on multi-year, mission-critical, hard-to-replace contracts — described as the stickiest revenue.
MPS Labs is the AI and engineering engine whose work compounds across every segment at very little marginal cost — described as a structural moat.

Priorities for rest of FY27: sustain operating leverage as new work reaches steady state, scale DigiCore and integrity adoption across renewal base, and keep converting the platform pipeline into revenue.
A stack of homegrown AI tools enables MPS's peer-review team to handle high submission volumes at scale.

subsections.label: Unbound Intelligence (AI use case)
points: Unbound Intelligence uses LLM-type models scraping a 'walled garden' of paywalled publisher content and MPS's own peer-reviewed science assets (not the open web) to answer real-time questions in the flow of work (e.g., a nurse asking a clinical question via a mobile app chat interface).
Differentiator versus generic models like ChatGPT: answers are grounded in peer-reviewed, sound-science, paywalled content rather than unpredictable open-web scraping, reducing hallucination risk.

subsections.label: Corporate Learning AI applications
points: AI applied across the entire learning value chain, not just content creation: modernizing/repurposing thousands of legacy learning assets on clients' LMS/LXP/SharePoint into role-based, performance-enabling learning.
Chatbots support immediate operational queries, problem-solving, and reduce downtime for clients.
BridgeAI provides multilingual translation experiences at enterprise scale, reusing rather than rebuilding content.

AI embedded in instructional design process, assessment/evaluation rubrics, translation/localization, QA, and media production, aiming for better results and reduced delivery timelines while maintaining quality.

AI is becoming a growth engine via enterprise engagements to build AI-enabled learning platforms, copilots, and simulation-based experiences that address broader workforce performance challenges, increasing customer lifetime value and margin profile.

subsections.label: Unbound Medicine integration
points: First full quarter inside MPS proved the thesis: recurring, high-renewal subscription business anchored in medicine and nursing, sold to a broad institutional base of medical/nursing schools, hospitals, and academic libraries.

Lowers customer concentration and gives more predictable forward revenue than MPS's traditional project book; no anchor relationships billing less — a long tail of high-quality recurring accounts has simply been added.
Brings 'Unbound Intelligence,' a knowledge-engineering layer turning trusted medical content into AI products designed not to hallucinate.
Integration being done deliberately, learning the renewal cycle before committing to synergy timelines; early cross-sell conversations started with publisher customers.

New learning this quarter: synergy potential between Liberate (Corporate Learning) and Unbound around experiential 'learning by doing,' identified via a US roadshow where Soma and the Unbound sales team met Unbound customers.
Strong ownership culture at Unbound cited as a factor enabling a 35-person team to deliver $9 million of revenue and keep growing.
Unbound holds pricing power: every renewal (whether a 10-year-old or 3-year-old customer) carries a price increase each year within a contract term, despite competing against much larger companies.

Cross-sell opportunity identified: Liberate's AI-enabled immersive/enterprise platform solutions can build on Unbound's existing content platform, which is currently more static/content-heavy and lacks 'learning by doing' elements critical in medical/nursing continuity.

Engagement with senior leaders/chairs of institutes/universities suggests an open-minded, largely untapped opportunity to combine instructional value with tech/AI enablement for continuous education, layered onto Unbound's renewal/recurring model.

subsections.label: M&A strategy / pipeline
points: Active acquisition pipeline exists; company avoids assets below $15 million revenue as a rule, though this was modified for Unbound due to its strong strategic fit.
Preferred acquisition domain is Education, which has been the fastest-growing area for MPS.
Domain filter: Science remains MPS's core; targets should support outcome-based (25% of revenue) and recurring (45% of revenue) revenue themes.

Filter for high-stakes subject matter where AI is a tailwind not a subtractor — e.g., nursing/medical or cybersecurity domains where errors carry severe consequences and full AI automation is unlikely, making AI a multiplier rather than a threat.
A motivated seller is described as an 'invisible' but necessary variable determining deal closure and competitive pricing.

Financial filters: target must show at least 10% revenue CAGR over trailing 3 years and pre-acquisition EBITDA margin of 5-15%; MPS aims to lift EBITDA margin to 30% and unlock 'Rule of 40' economics for each acquired asset.

Strategy shifted from acquiring distressed assets historically (when MPS lacked scale/cash, starting from INR 125 crores revenue with a loss in 2012) to acquiring assets with inherent strength; distressed-asset ROCE was often north of 30%, sometimes north of 50%, but distracted management from organic growth by requiring constant turnaround work.

Continuity practices: during diligence, identify teams to retain and extend via financial (stock options) and operational (larger roles on MPS platform) incentives; deals have been walked away from during due diligence due to cultural misalignment, including a recent education-sector target where MPS disagreed with shortcuts taken with customers despite attractive economics.

Vision 2027/2032 long-term planning framework referenced; talent machine (internal and external) is expanding as part of this build, with internal promotions up versus prior years and external hiring success rates benchmarked favorably against the market.

subsections.label: AI and outcomes-based revenue shift (strategic framing)
points: MPS runs on the principle that AI should show up in revenue, not on slides; DigiCore and Research Integrity Check deployed at scale, AI author workflows have processed over a million manuscripts, BridgeAI translating at enterprise scale inside Corporate Learning.

Common thread across segments: MPS sits at the layer where AI cannot afford to be wrong — every fact sourceable, every output trusted; as models strengthen, constraint shifts from generating content to verifying it, domain context, and the last mile inside real workflows — a tailwind, not a threat, for MPS.

Revenue mix is steadily shifting from being paid for effort (pages/hours) to being paid for outcomes (manuscript acceptance, paper mill detection, accessible assets delivered at scale, subscription renewals, performance-changing learning programs); outcomes carry better economics and are harder to commoditize.
This outcomes shift is cited as a large part of why revenue grew 20% while EBITDA grew 53% this quarter.

subsections.label: Culture and organizational integration
points: Culture maintained via core values EEE (excellence, efficiency, empathy) executed through a singular cultural principle of ownership mindset, applied to all global acquisitions.

subsections.label: AJE reset
points: AJE (author solutions) revenue is deliberately smaller as the consumer base finds its new level after being resized from an inflated base carried two years ago; described as a reset by design rather than a risk to be managed, but flagged as reducing headline blended growth figures.

subsections.label: Management/talent transitions
points: Analyst raised concern about management-level exits/replacements over the past year; management response framed as a natural byproduct of a rapidly scaling talent machine, with more successful outcomes than mistakes, benchmarking favorably against market on external hiring success and increased internal promotions.

subsections.label: Headcount reduction / quality risk
points: Corporate Learning headcount down ~33% YoY, raising a question on whether productivity/outsourcing gains could dilute service quality; management states senior instructional design and client-facing bench were untouched, and quality/client retention held with no rise in rework or escalations.

subsections.label: AI disruption risk vs tailwind
points: Market worry that stronger AI models could commoditize the business is explicitly addressed; management's view is the opposite — as models strengthen, the constraint shifts to verification, domain context and last-mile trust, which is a tailwind, not a threat, for MPS's positioning.

subsections.label: Capital allocation discipline
points: Analyst urged management to maintain a balance between cash and debt for future acquisitions and avoid raising equity, which is costly to shareholders; management agreed equity issuance is not the preferred route, favoring cash accruals plus debt ("never say never" caveat).

subsections.label: FY27 EBITDA guidance reaffirmation
points: Guidance to comfortably cross INR 300 crores EBITDA in FY27 is unchanged and, if anything, firmer; built bottom-up from each segment's operating plan at an unchanged planning rate.
Management explicitly frames the number as a floor rather than a ceiling.
Q1 has landed ahead of a straight-line path to the FY27 target, and second half has historically outrun first half, positioning the Company to clear the line comfortably.

Conviction cited: strongest opening quarter in Company history, margins expanded in all three segments, delivered without leaning on headcount; the work to deliver the year is already in flight, not merely planned.

subsections.label: FY28 targets
points: FY28 targets clarified as approximately INR 1,500 crores in revenue (Vision 2027/topline target referenced by an analyst) and around INR 450 crores in EBITDA.

subsections.label: Rule of 50 aspiration
points: Rule of 50 (revenue growth + EBITDA margin > 50) is a mark management is hopeful of clearing for the full year, though not promised every quarter given business phasing.

Same Rule of 40/50 framework will be applied to Unbound: expectation is Unbound first climbs to Rule of 40 (EBITDA margin in mid-to-late 20s with balance from revenue growth), and eventually crosses Rule of 50 as it settles into MPS.

subsections.label: Organic growth aspiration
points: Management acknowledges organic growth (ex-Unbound) is in the early teens currently but says aspirations are higher; expects MPS to outperform market growth rates in all three segments — Research market grows at 8-9% vs MPS ~15%; Education market grows ~15% vs MPS growing much higher; Corporate market grows 12-13% vs MPS at 6-7%, described as the area needing the most catch-up.

Management states it is 'not settling for achieved organic growth' and reiterated aspiration to drive organic growth toward the late teens, per closing remarks acknowledging analyst challenge on this point.

subsections.label: Segment-level outlook commentary
points: Research Solutions priorities: sustain operating leverage, scale DigiCore/integrity adoption across renewal base, convert platform pipeline into revenue.
Education: healthy pipeline across largest relationships, focus on extending into international knowledge organizations, plus benefit of first full year of Unbound.
Corporate Learning: hold exit margin as run rate, make AI-led delivery dominant in mix, complete integration into unified Liberate Global brand.

guidance_ledger.statement: We continue to expect the Company to comfortably cross INR 300 crores in EBITDA in FY'27... built bottom-up from each segment's operating plan, at an unchanged planning rate, and it implies a three-year EBITDA CAGR of roughly 21 percent from FY'24 to FY'27. Please read the guidance as a floor we intend to clear, not a target we hope to reach.

The INR 1,500 crores is for FY'28 next year, and that probably will translate to more like INR 450 crores EBITDA. So, to summarize: for FY'28, the targets are approximately INR 1,500 crores in revenue and around INR 450 crores in EBITDA.
For FY'28, the targets are approximately INR 1,500 crores in revenue and around INR 450 crores in EBITDA.

Rule of 50 is a mark we are hopeful of clearing for the full year, and opening FY'27 on the right side of it tells you the operating model is doing exactly what we built it to do. I am not going to promise you that we clear 50 in every quarter of this year, because the phasing of our business does not work that neatly.

guidance_ledger.metric: Unbound Medicine EBITDA margin / Rule of 40-50 trajectory
guidance_ledger.statement: The expectation is, first, Unbound climbs to Rule of 40, which is hopefully an EBITDA margin in the mid-20s to late 20s, and the balance of it flows through revenue growth. And ultimately, as the business settles into MPS, it crosses the Rule of 50 as well.

We expect that in all the 3 markets, MPS outperforms those markets on organic growth... Given the type of business and platform that MPS is, we should be growing at a premium to the market rates and industry rates, and that is the goal here. We're not settling for where we are today.
Doing an acquisition in the INR 300 crores to INR 500 crores range seems fairly doable between internal cash accruals as well as debt.

We have a healthy pipeline across our largest relationships and a focus on extending into international knowledge organizations. That, together with the first full year of Unbound to build on, gives us real conviction under the guidance Prarthana reaffirmed.
Our focus is to hold this exit margin as the run rate, make AI-led delivery the dominant part of the mix, and complete the integration of our legacy entities into one unified Liberate Global brand.
In a steady state, the business should operate at a 30% EBITDA margin, and organic growth should be closer to 12%.

Heading into the rest of FY'27, my priorities are simple: sustain this operating leverage as new work reaches steady state, scale DigiCore and integrity adoption across the renewal base, and keep converting the platform pipeline into revenue.
We are now the second largest peer-review provider in the industry by volume, and we aim to be the first by the end of this year.
No mention this quarter of the previously indicated timing for a tighter FY'28 guidance (previously flagged for end of Q3 or Q4 FY'27).
No mention this quarter of dividend resumption timing (previously tied to closure of the deployment cycle).
Combined EBITDA margin for FY'27 expected to be in the 30% to 35% range, with margins typically expanding as revenue grows.

guidance_ledger.metric: Segment revenue mix contribution to FY27 delta
guidance_ledger.statement: Ballpark split of the FY27 EBITDA delta: Research ~55%, Education ~35%, Corporate Learning ~10%.
A tighter guidance for FY'28 will be shared either at the end of Q3 FY'27 or end of Q4 FY'27.

guidance_ledger.metric: Unbound Medicine monthly revenue run rate
guidance_ledger.statement: Expecting Unbound to run at USD750,000 to USD950,000 per month in FY'27, depending on seasonality.

Unbound expected to start FY'27 at around 15% EBITDA margin (first couple of quarters similar or slightly lower than historical 18-19%) and exit at an EBITDA margin of 25% to 30%, timing uncertain (Q2 or Q3).
Strong pipeline across largest customer relationships with particular focus on extending into international knowledge organizations and continuing to scale the accessibility business.
Pre-acceptance B2B services saw more than 90% growth and demand is expected to scale even further.

risk_register.note: AJE revenue deliberately smaller as consumer base finds its new level post-reset, though now more profitable and higher quality; pruning behind it, expected to grow on value not volume going forward.
Attributed to a rapidly expanding talent machine; management says more decisions are right than wrong, benchmarking favorably on external hiring success and rising internal promotions.

risk_register.risk: Headcount reduction impact on service quality (esp. Corporate Learning)
risk_register.note: ~33% YoY headcount reduction in Corporate Learning; management states senior/client-facing roles untouched, quality and client retention held with no rise in rework or escalations.
Management argues stronger AI models shift constraint toward verification and last-mile trust, which is a tailwind rather than a threat for MPS's positioning.

risk_register.risk: Equity dilution risk in funding acquisitions
risk_register.note: Management commits to funding acquisitions via cash accruals plus debt, not equity, barring exceptional circumstances.

Deals have been walked away from during due diligence due to cultural misalignment, e.g., an education-sector target where MPS disagreed with shortcuts taken with customers despite favorable economics.

AI is expected to super-compress pricing of commoditized production work (basic copy editing, page-based content, generic instruction), which will be placed with very few scaled AI-enabled suppliers; businesses hyper-concentrated there without automation/AI capability will feel severe pricing pressure and loss of relevance.

Viewed as a tailwind rather than headwind for MPS since the gating constraint shifts from model capability to trust, verification, domain context and workflow integration — the 'last mile' where MPS operates.
Broader geopolitical/macro risks exist similar to pandemic-era shocks; no unique risk specific to MPS; Company says it would adapt if a major event occurs.
Reports and internal memos regarding work-from-home policies and government-related guidance noted; WFH is normal for MPS and has improved margins, so any tightening is a watch item.

risk_register.risk: Ex-AJE Q4 margin sluggishness / headcount timing
risk_register.note: Research headcount increased in anticipation of growth causing some ex-AJE Q4 margin sluggishness, described as a timing issue ahead of expected FY'27 growth.

risk_register.risk: Execution risk in translating AI into revenue
risk_register.note: The risk for MPS is not AI displacement per se but failing to execute seamlessly and convert AI capability into revenue while the market splits into commoditized vs. trusted layers.

risk_register.risk: FX / constant currency growth concern raised by analyst
risk_register.note: An analyst suggested FY'26 growth was largely flat in constant currency terms due to forex gains; management disputed the constant-currency characterization as not correct.

themes.label: Margin expansion / operating leverage
themes.note: Revenue grew 20.4% while EBITDA grew 53.0% and headcount rose less than 3%, with EBITDA margin expanding to 34.3% from 27.0%.

themes.label: AI-first repositioning
themes.note: Research, Education and Corporate Learning all described as AI-first businesses with AI embedded live in delivery, positioning MPS at the layer where AI cannot afford to be wrong.

themes.label: Unbound Medicine integration
themes.note: First full quarter proved the thesis: recurring subscription base, pricing power, and emerging Liberate-Unbound cross-sell synergy around experiential learning.

themes.label: Corporate Learning turnaround
themes.note: Second consecutive quarter of growth; margin expanded to 25.3% from under 17% on a ~33% lighter headcount, driven by mix and operating leverage.

themes.label: M&A pipeline / inorganic growth
themes.note: Active pipeline with a $15 million minimum revenue filter, focus on Education and high-stakes AI-tailwind domains, financed via cash plus debt (INR 300-500 crores range).

themes.label: Capital allocation / dividend pause
themes.note: Cash accruals (INR 138 crores, INR 15-18 crores/month) plus debt capacity of ~INR 200 crores preferred over equity for funding acquisitions; no dividend discussion this quarter.

themes.label: AI disruption risk vs tailwind
themes.note: Management argues stronger AI models shift the constraint to verification and last-mile trust, framing AI as a tailwind rather than a commoditization threat.

key_takeaways: Q1 has opened FY'27 as the strongest first quarter in the Company's history, on every line that matters. Reported revenue for the quarter was INR 224.24 crores, up 20.4 percent over the same quarter last year.
EBITDA was INR 76.96 crores, up 53.0 percent, with the EBITDA margin expanding to 34.3 percent from 27.0 percent a year ago.
Profit after tax grew 43.0 percent to INR 50.39 crores, and basic EPS came in at INR 29.70, an all-time Q1 high, up from INR 20.78.

Revenue grew 20 percent. EBITDA grew 53 percent. Headcount rose less than 3 percent. That is operating leverage doing exactly what it is meant to do, with growth converting into margin rather than consuming it.
We continue to expect the Company to comfortably cross INR 300 crores in EBITDA in FY'27... Please read the guidance as a floor we intend to clear, not a target we hope to reach.
Our revenue is steadily shifting from being paid for effort to being paid for outcomes... That shift is a large part of why revenue grew 20 percent this quarter while EBITDA grew 53 percent.
This was its first full quarter inside MPS, and the headline for me is that it proved the thesis rather than the pitch [on Unbound Medicine].
Corporate Learning was the segment that carried the most stress last year, and it is now the segment most clearly turning a corner. This was our second consecutive quarter of growth.
pressing_questions: If you strip off the Unbound revenue, growth is in the early teens. And AI will enable more reliable solutions. So why can't we think about a much higher organic growth than we have reported now?

How does our acquisition strategy change now that we need to plan for larger deals to move the needle, while maintaining culture and ensuring smoother integration compared to the earlier strategy of smaller acquisitions?

quarters.summary: FY'26 closed as MPS's most profitable year with record EBITDA (INR236cr) and EPS (INR102.11); FY'27 guidance is to comfortably cross INR300cr EBITDA (~3-yr EBITDA CAGR of ~21% FY24-FY27), built bottom-up from segment operating plans, with Research ~55%, Education ~35% and Corporate Learning ~10% contribution to the incremental delta. Vision 2027 (~INR1,500cr topline by FY'28) remains intact and in line of sight, with tighter FY'28 guidance to be shared at end of Q3 or Q4 FY'27.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: FY'26 closed as the most profitable year in the Company's history, with EBITDA and EPS both records.
Q4 was the strongest quarter for FY'26 with revenue growth converting to margin expansion, indicating operating leverage at work.
Both records were delivered while the Company acquired Unbound Medicine, consolidated three legacy entities into Liberate Global, and absorbed a one-time regulatory charge through the P&L.

subsections.label: Exceptional items
points: FY'26 saw a positive contribution of INR7.64 crores from exceptional items; details are included in the financial results released on Friday, and the items do not impact the underlying earnings trajectory.

subsections.label: Balance sheet
points: Borrowings of INR40.25 crores relate to the facility drawn for the acquisition of Unbound Medicine.
ROCE for FY'26 was broadly in line with the historical capital efficiency profile, even after taking the full balance sheet impact of Unbound.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Capital allocation principle for the last 7 years: capital earns its keep within 12 months or gets returned to shareholders.
That principle has produced more than INR650 crores of cumulative cash return to shareholders between FY'19 and FY'25 and a payout ratio among the highest in the industry.

Over FY'26, the Board has chosen not to recommend a final dividend because capital was deployed into the Unbound Medicine acquisition in February, the Company is carrying a hyperactive M&A pipeline, and the deployment opportunity in front of it exceeds the cash in hand.
The principle has not changed; the cycle has — distribution resumes when the deployment cycle closes.
The 7-year record stands as evidence that the Company does return capital when it can put it to work.

subsections.label: Research Solutions — four product layers
points: Reframed as an AI-first knowledge solutions company serving the research economy, not a services business.

Layer 1 - Trust and integrity: DigiCore (AI-enabled production ecosystem) deployed at scale across top-tier knowledge clients; Research Integrity Check (RIC) named top innovator at STM AI Innovation Day 2025; RIC delivers AI-led detection of paper mills, identity fraud, image manipulation, integrated with leading third-party integrity tools; bottleneck in research is no longer generation but verification.

Layer 2 - AI author services: AJE Digital and Rubriq have cumulatively processed over a million manuscripts; controlled trial shows 52% manuscript acceptance lift vs ~32% industry baseline, representing a measurable AI-attached revenue line.

Layer 3 - Pre-acceptance JEO office: standout margin business inside Research, with FY'26 revenue growing meaningfully on three large knowledge organization engagements; EBITDA margin well above segment average; Scholar Finder and Manuscript Expert AI tools scale volume without proportional headcount growth.

Layer 4 - Platform stack and MPS Labs: HighWire and DigiCore Pro form hosting/production backbone for largest knowledge clients; Think365 (2 years in building) now in live production and gaining commercial traction; MPS Labs (200 engineers) creates reusable capabilities compounding across all four layers at zero marginal cost.

FY'27 priorities: sustain Q4 operating leverage as new transitions reach steady state, scale DigiCore Pro and RIC adoption across the renewal cohort, continue JEO office trajectory through a comprehensive retention plan.

subsections.label: Education Solutions — growth drivers
points: Education was the segment that delivered scale in FY'26; growth driven by three forces.

First: AI-enabled content and production work — expanded engagements with several large U.S.-based knowledge organizations across K-12 and higher education, converting earlier programs into multiyear multiproduct engagements; manpower efficiency improved as AI system production moved from pilot to core delivery.

Second: accessibility and learning services line — AI-assisted accessibility production at scale (30M+ auto-generated accessible media assets annually) became a meaningful, high-margin business; FY'26 revenue roughly tripled, anchored by two large new accessibility engagements with leading global knowledge organizations.

Third: Unbound Medicine acquisition closed Feb 9, 2026; headcount transitioned cleanly into consolidated entity; integration thesis intact; Unbound gives an institutional foothold in medicine and nursing, a recurring revenue platform with strong renewal economics, and a natural cross-sell counterparty; brings 'Unbound Intelligence' knowledge engineering layer turning trusted medical IP into AI products that do not hallucinate.
FY'27 outlook: strong pipeline across largest customer relationships, particular focus on extending into international knowledge organizations and continuing to scale the accessibility business.

subsections.label: Corporate Learning — reset and turnaround
points: Corporate learning was the segment that absorbed the most stress in FY'26 and is the segment most clearly turning a corner; Q4 was the first positive revenue print of the year.

Three structural levers executed through the year: (1) portfolio rationalization — walked away from low-margin compliance work diluting mix and brand, average price point and gross margin improved as legacy book tapered down; (2) core-plus-flex talent model scaling cost with revenue rather than ahead of it, with headcount down ~32% YoY on a sharper cost base; (3) deliberate shift towards higher value AI/AR/VR/simulation-led builds — Bridge AI (multilingual translation engine) in active deployment with enterprise customers, AI-enabled chatbots, roleplays and simulation-led experiences scaling rapidly as core learning enablers.

Q4 closed with the strongest order book of FY'26; added new entrants across top customer relationships; AI-led wins continue to anchor the new pipeline; integration into unified global structure on plan.
FY'27 focus: sustain Q4 exit margin into the run rate, scale AI-led delivery as dominant mix, complete integration of three legacy entities into one unified Liberate Global brand.

Deliverables shifted from simple learning outputs/courses to higher-order learning experiences embedded into enterprise workflow ('performance enabler'); AR/VR programs live for technical and field training; consequence is higher value engagements, longer program cycles, stickier customer relationships and improved margin profile versus what the legacy book could support; Q4 improvement and FY'27 plan built on this new work profile, not a recovery of the old book.

subsections.label: Customer base mix shift (post-Unbound)
points: Traditional Research/Education customer base was relatively concentrated among large knowledge organizations, associated with higher revenue per account and deep account-director relationships.

Unbound brings a broader institutional base of medical schools, nursing schools, hospitals and academic libraries — many more, smaller accounts, with high renewal economics and low concentration risk.
Averaging across the combined base causes per-customer revenue to decline arithmetically, not due to degradation; none of the anchor clients is billing less.
Customer concentration is materially lower than 12 months ago, viewed as an improvement in quality of revenue, and the renewal-driven model gives more predictable forward revenue.

subsections.label: AJE / pre-acceptance growth levers for FY'27
points: Pruning of the AJE/B2C base is essentially behind the Company; set up for growth in FY'27.
B2B side: pre-acceptance services grew more than 90%, with demand expected to scale further; delivery model built with technology at the center of service delivery and workflow management.

B2C side: leaner, more agile delivery model now focused on growth via higher value services and more competitive benefits through portfolio expansion, market diversification, and deeper publisher/institutional partnerships.
Remaining core after pruning is high-value: premium editorial, language editing, AI-assisted workflows — base is now margin accretive rather than a drag.

Growth from here comes from three places: premium tiers in Author Services where authors pay for quality/turnaround; AI-driven productivity embedded in workflow (benefit partly passed to client, partly retained as margin); cross-selling to corporate publisher relationships opening new revenue lines and supporting expansion into under-penetrated ecosystems such as China.

subsections.label: APAC / China expansion
points: Growth push into China, a high-growth research ecosystem; MOUs already signed and operations initiated with some publishers in China.

Strategy combines strong relationships with growth publishers and local partnerships across new territories like China, strengthening reach within China and helping global publishers strengthen their outreach in China.
Not just a China play but an APAC play; Japan is another market receiving personal attention from the CEO (based in Singapore); more updates expected as the Company progresses.

points: Closed 9 February 2026; whatever was acquired has mostly been completely paid for except small insignificant closing amounts; now in closed-and-integration phase.

subsections.label: M&A pipeline and strategy
points: Overall pipeline continues to expand; out of 35 companies, 5 are fairly advanced, 5 are live, 2 are at an advanced stage fitting well within existing segments.
Most advanced opportunity: a Higher Ed and Online Learning carve-out in the Western world, strategically meaningful, expanding into adjacencies.
Another opportunity: a cross-border asset in the same business, rationale being capability expansion within existing workflows.
Also evaluating a transformational play in the broader ecosystem that could help enter an adjacent market; details withheld as price-sensitive information.

Applying the same discipline as Unbound: same return threshold, same integration economics, same strategy lens; focus on growth assets with a defensible moat, sensible valuations, and clear capability/platform/customer-fit alignment.

subsections.label: Corporate structure
points: Three legacy entities consolidated into Liberate Global (Corporate Learning) during FY'26; deliberate integration into unified global structure on plan; FY'27 focus includes completing integration into one unified Liberate Global brand.

subsections.label: Right to win / competitive positioning
points: Company holds ~0.5% market share of total serviceable market, presenting huge headroom; framed via 'right to win': (1) AI-first knowledge solutions positioning at a layer where AI cannot afford to be wrong — a defensible position with a smaller competitive set than the commodity generic AI layer; (2) integrated platform stack (HighWire, THINK365, RICs, BridgeAI, Unbound's platform, DigiCore) with very few competitors able to match it, built over years; (3) MPS Labs' 200 engineers building AI/infrastructure that compounds across Research, Education and Corporate at low marginal cost, described as a structural moat; (4) deep, decades-long customer relationships with top-tier global knowledge organizations, expanded via the Unbound acquisition, with growth via expanding within large accounts rather than cold-calling.
Path framed as incremental: moving from 0.5% to 1%, then 1% to 2% share over several years, via being true partners working from customers' business problems backwards.

subsections.label: Vision 2027 / longer-term target
points: ~INR1,500 crores topline target by FY'28 remains intact and in absolute line of sight.
FY'27 INR300cr+ EBITDA focus is meant to make FY'28 reachable rather than a big unreachable leap; internal plans go through FY'30 but current focus is FY'27 and FY'28.

The INR300cr+ EBITDA mark for FY'27 is an organic, bottom-up operating commitment that does not include any new acquisitions beyond what has already been done — additional M&A would be incremental to this number.

Vision 2027 was always designed as a combination of organic momentum plus selective, disciplined inorganic activity; Unbound cited as a proof point of disciplined execution (high recurring revenue, stable customer base, high renewal rate, not overpaid).
Building blocks for Vision 2027/FY'28: Research business compounding, Education trajectory continuing, Corporate Learning turning a corner — all three segments firing and on track.
Tighter FY'28 guidance to be shared at the end of Q3 FY'27 or end of Q4 FY'27, similar to the process used for FY'27 guidance this year.

subsections.label: AI disruption risk framing
points: Market is bifurcating: on one side, AI will super-compress the price of commoditized production work (basic copy editing, page-based content, generic instruction) placed with very few scaled suppliers; businesses hyper-concentrated there without automation/AI capability (as MPS has built via MPS Labs) will feel severe pricing pressure and loss of business relevance.
On the other side, demand for trusted AI deployment inside high-stakes knowledge workflows (medicine, nursing, scholarly publishing, regulated learning accessibility) is expected to expand sharply.

Agentic AI deployment announcements from foundation model providers are viewed as tailwinds, not headwinds, for MPS's kind of work — as models improve, the gating constraint shifts from model capability to trust, verification, domain context and integration into existing workflows, where foundational models struggle in the 'last mile' that MPS occupies.

By segment over the next 3 years: Research (~55% of revenue in FY27) sees rising demand for integrity/verification as fake papers and AI-generated submissions multiply; Education (~35% of revenue) sees demand for trusted medical/instructional AI products grow as institutions cannot rely on general-purpose chatbots in clinical/learning contexts; Corporate Learning sees AI-led simulation, multilingual translation and role-play becoming default.

Net view: AI expected to be materially net additive on the demand side; the risk for MPS is not AI displacement but failing to execute seamlessly and translate AI into revenue while the market splits.

subsections.label: Macro / geopolitical risk
points: No unique risks pertain to MPS alone; exists in a shifting geopolitical environment with the same news everyone else sees.
Broader geopolitical and macroeconomic risks cited, similar to those seen during the pandemic.
Reports/internal memos regarding work-from-home policies and government-related guidance noted; working from home is normal for MPS and has in fact improved margins.
If a major macroeconomic or geopolitical event shakes up the entire industry/economy, the Company would adapt, citing a track record of adapting better than most historically.

Guidance reflects work already in flight, not a step change being asked to be believed on faith.
Guidance is organic and does not include any new acquisitions beyond Unbound; additional M&A would be incremental to the INR300cr+ number.

key_takeaways: FY'26 closed as the most profitable year in the Company's history: Group revenue was INR768 crores, up 5.7% over FY'25; EBITDA was INR236 crores, up 11.8%, with EBITDA margin expanding to 30.7%; PAT grew 16.3% to INR173 crores; basic EPS was INR102.11, a Company record up 16.3% YoY.
Excluding AJE, FY'26 revenue grew 15.4% to INR646 crores; Research segment EBITDA margin expanded 330 basis points to 39.9% for the year; Education delivered EBITDA growth of 42.6% YoY.

Q4 was the strongest quarter for FY'26: revenue grew 12.7% YoY to INR205 crores; EBITDA grew 20.5% to INR67.5 crores with margins expanding to 32.9%, indicating operating leverage at work; PAT was INR47 crores, sequentially up 32.5%.

Based on current run rate and operating plan, the Company expects to comfortably cross INR300 crores in EBITDA in FY'27, implying a 3-year EBITDA CAGR of approximately 21% from FY'24 to FY'27, built bottom-up from the operating plans of each business segment.

Over FY'26, the Board has chosen not to recommend a final dividend, as capital was deployed into the Unbound Medicine acquisition, the Company is carrying a hyperactive M&A pipeline, and the deployment opportunity exceeds cash in hand.

Corporate learning was the segment that absorbed the most stress in FY'26 and is the segment most clearly turning a corner; Q4 revenue grew 2.4% YoY to INR25.5 crores, the first positive print of the year; FY'26 revenue closed at INR96 crores, down 16.5% versus FY'25.
Vision 2027 target of approximately INR1,500 crores of topline by FY'28 remains intact and in absolute line of sight.
pressing_questions: The first question was on the slide that you presented in the presentation, saying that we just have a 0.5% market share of the total serviceable market share that we have? So the headroom that is presently shows huge room to grow. So, I just wanted to understand how MPS is being positioned from a “right to win” perspective within this market opportunity. And also, what are the capabilities that are either in the working progress mode or lacking mode that will help us reach there?

So INR 300 crores EBITDA for FY'27 is great. But what I wanted to understand is the larger picture. Earlier, we had spoken about reaching approximately INR 1,500 crores of top line by, let's say, FY'28. So I just wanted to have your thoughts on whether that number is still in the line of sight? Or is there any change in the way we see it?
Sir, are there any more acquisitions immediately on the cards, and whatever we acquired and have already paid for?
Sir, FY '27, what EBITDA combined margin should we think for INR 300 crores?

Sir, firstly, I wanted to know if you can share what the financial numbers were for FY 2026 for Unbound, like what the revenue and EBITDA were, just headline numbers? And how do you expect it to move in FY 2027?

In the last 3 or 4 months, every other week, we've been seeing updates coming out from AI companies... My question is there any way to know that there will not be an update in the future that strikes at the heart of how we make money?

Can you just let me understand the reason for dipping EBITDA margin and the spike in ex-AJE headcount? The second question is with regard to AJE: has a rundown in the AJE model been completed? Or is there any tailing effect in FY'27? And what would be the growth drivers for FY'27, and the third question would be regarding the FY'28 target of around INR 1,500 crores. Since FY'26, we have reported a below average run rate revenue growth rate at around 6%. So, what would be the growth drivers to achieve the target, given a higher growth rate?

Sir, my question relates to the growth guidance of INR 300 crores EBITDA. So, INR 300 crores EBITDA organically would mean about INR 900 crores to INR 1,000 crores top line. But historically, we have seen that most of our growth has come from inorganic acquisitions... about INR 65 crores EBITDA delta. So, which is the area where the lion's share of the delta will come from? And what are, what is the one major risk in achieving our target of INR 300 crores in your assessment?

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 marks the first quarter under IHC/IFC ownership, with management framing it as the start of a "compounding journey" after FY26-Q4's "kitchen-sink" adjustments. AUM grew to ₹56,239cr in line with guidance; liability-side ratings upgrades and cost-of-funds reduction are positioned as the primary long-term earnings pillar, alongside a strategic shift from portfolio management to growth and product diversification, branch/digital scale-up, and continued outsized recoveries from the legacy book. FY27 disbursement plan of ₹30,000cr and cost-to-income guidance of ~50% (declining to 30-35% by FY29) frame the near-term outlook, with inorganic growth optionality flagged from next financial year.

Cost of funds (CoF) guidance and cadence: Started at 10.5%, reached 10% during the quarter ("stock cost of funds"). Target 9.6% by September, 9.3% by FY27-end.
FY27 disbursement plan: ₹30,000cr (explicit), split ₹10,000cr in 1H and ₹20,000cr in 2H; management said Q2 is tracking: "disbursals are bang on to achieve… first half."

quarters.summary: Sammaan Capital's Q4/FY26 call marks its first earnings release since IHC's acquisition of a strategic stake. Management outlined a multi-year transformation plan: rating upgrades from all 3 domestic agencies within 50 days of IHC's investment, a target to reach AUM of ~INR2 lakh crores with ROE reaching high-teens and ROA around 4%+ by FY30, cost-to-income falling from ~50% to ~26%, and disbursements of ~INR30,000 crores targeted for FY27, growing to ~INR72,000 crores by FY29-30, with growth initially led by existing mortgage/business-loan products before diversifying into gold loans, unsecured loans and other products from FY28 onward.
