subsections.label: Balance sheet fortification
points: Balance sheet fortified for growth with new IHC capital, reflected in rating upgrades that have started unlocking lower borrowing costs.
Company will maintain a well-diversified and matched borrowing program; lenders comforted by promoter backstop.
Historically maintained capital adequacy north of 20%; despite ample capital, gearing capped at 3.5x-4x learning from past cycles.
Liquidity principles maintained at higher of 6 months of repayments or 10-15% of borrowings.

subsections.label: Credit cost and write-offs
points: Provision buffers on opening AUM capture terminal credit costs; no incremental net provisions required on this AUM going forward.
Management pushed back on the term 'write-off', characterizing the provisioning as credit costs enabling management bandwidth for growth.
Recoveries of ~INR7,000 crores from provided-for assets are baked into projections; historical experience of recovering 70-80% via sales to asset reconstruction companies cited as comfort.

subsections.label: Dividend policy
points: Company will resume dividend payments with a policy of at least 25% of profits, targeting up to 40% payout.

subsections.label: NIM drivers clarification
points: Cost of funds figures cited relate only to cost of debt funds on balance sheet borrowings, not blended with equity, which has no added P&L cost.

NIM expansion driven partly by spread earned on the sold-on book (difference between AUM and on-book loan book), e.g., this gap widens from ~INR30,000 crores to ~INR45,000 crores in FY28, boosting NIM.
Equity infusion provides both liquidity and a capital buffer; capital buffer has been partly consumed but liquidity benefit continues.

subsections.label: Product suite and yield strategy
points: Focus on residential housing finance, business owner loans, commercial real estate/project loans, plot loans, and a little unsecured lending (business and personal).
Prime mass market home loans (8.5-10% yield) sourced with intent to sell to banks; affordable housing loans (10-13% yield) held on balance sheet.

Secured business loans to individuals, SMEs, corporates, and micro-LAP segment split similarly: prime mass market (9.5-11%) sourced to sell to banks, affordable semi-urban/micro-LAP (11-13.5%) sourced to hold.
CRE project loans done strictly on co-originate model with credit funds in pari-passu structure without credit guarantee; balance sheet stake roughly 10-15% of overall disbursements.
New products to be added gradually, including some unsecured and other secured products.

subsections.label: Guardrails and portfolio construction
points: Target portfolio: 60% secured lending, 20% unsecured/semi-secured lending, ensuring 80% of book remains retail.
Balance ~20% of AUM held with minor balance sheet stake, majority with variety of credit funds.
Growth to be pursued responsibly within guardrails to sustain multi-decade compounding and steady best-in-class ROA/ROE.

subsections.label: Asset-light model execution
points: Asset-light model proven scalable over last 4-5 years; playbook fully operational, integrated with large number of banks.
Asset-light share varies by product, from as high as 60% for prime home loans to near 0% for some unsecured products.
On average, ~30% of incremental disbursals targeted under co-lending or direct assignment arrangements.

subsections.label: Productivity and scale ramp-up
points: Productivity has already improved 2x between March and April 2026.
Q1 disbursals (seasonally slower quarter) expected to be 50-60% higher than Q4, then increasing 30-40% per quarter thereafter.
Current scale targets (this year, next year) are comparable to disbursal levels already achieved by the company 8-10 years back, giving confidence in ability to handle scale.
Productivity gains (0.6 to 2+ loans per person per month) and amortization of centralized/senior management cost over a larger book are key drivers of cost-to-income reduction.

subsections.label: AI/digital transformation priorities
points: IHC and senior management across investee companies emphasize digital and AI transformation; working with relevant teams to create AI adoption model, AI policy and AI integration.

Priorities include enhancing customer experience/service responsiveness with human-led relationship-driven experience important for self-employed/small business/SME/micro company borrowers requiring handholding.
AI-driven automation targeted to drive operational efficiency at scale and create greater operating leverage, essential to bring cost-income ratio below ~30% while pursuing strong growth.
Analytical models being implemented for early warning signals and proactive risk management/portfolio visibility.
Bots and other tools being implemented to personalize collections/recovery programs and improve efficiency/productivity in collections.
Continuous focus on fraud prevention and cybersecurity/digital resilience as an integral part of financial services.
AI tools being used for governance oversight — reading Board meeting minutes to flag action points/red flags for continuous governance.

subsections.label: Tech investment already made
points: CRM/Salesforce upgrade invested 6 months ago in anticipation of growth; cost already taken and built into P&L.
Investment in LMS (loan management system) capacity being assessed relative to loan volume growth needs.

key_figures.label: Existing branches sized for other products

subsections.label: Network expansion phasing
points: Company not in a rush to hyper grow; will continue to play on strengths of existing 3-4 products with a track record of INR3.6 lakh crores disbursed and terminal cost understanding.
Will build next via loans against securities and gold loans (both secured), requiring a different type of branch network, assurance and oversight function.
From fiscal '28, will widen product suite to include additional opportunities identified in the marketplace.
Large products to be introduced/expanded in FY27 and FY28 are already existing categories; additional opportunities identified for later phases.
Book intended to have a lot of granularity, well diversified across many loan programs.

subsections.label: Loan turnaround time target
points: Current secured mortgage loan turnaround time of 5-7 days targeted to reduce to 2-3 days through operational efficiency/AI initiatives.

subsections.label: IHC transaction details
points: Transaction stands closed with share allotment to IHC completed on 31 March 2026.
IHC is the promoter and strategic shareholder; Mr. Alwyn Crasta, Group CFO, appointed as Nominee Director on the Board on 15 May.

IHC has direct operating oversight through nominee directors and Board subcommittees; Sammaan's operating teams already engaging with IHC Group experts across IT, AI, risk management, credit development and finance.
This is IHC's first promoter-level investment in India, reflecting confidence in the company and the broader Indian financial services sector.

Indian PM's UAE visit and press statements from Ministry of External Affairs and UAE Minister of Foreign Trade highlighted the Sammaan investment, signalling long-term commitment to India's financial sector.

subsections.label: IHC/Avalora strategic rationale
points: Avalora Holdings is the consolidator of non-banking FI and FI platforms within Judan Financial Holding (a subsidiary of IHC), unifying group financial services investments across Asia, Middle East, Africa, Central Eastern Europe and Latin America.
Sammaan Capital positioned as a core part of IHC's Asia investment strategy and as a strategic NBFC platform for Avalora's non-banking FI business.
Investment framed as long-term, not short-term positioning; described as the beginning of a long-term relationship with the Indian market.
IHC's approach centered on capital, operational discipline and long-term alignment to support transformation and scale.

IHC bringing institutional framework, superior risk management/governance practices, technology oversight, and focus on continuity/succession planning given financial services is a people-based business.

subsections.label: Non-mortgage / new product build strategy
points: Management team has prior experience managing secured and unsecured loans, personal loans, commercial vehicle loans, and loans against securities at scale (tens of thousands of crores).
Tech enables continuous monitoring/control of decisions, especially for unsecured lending conducted via app.
Distinct teams/branch networks required per product: mortgage team won't do personal loans; gold loans require unique branch network and oversight function.
Cross-sell (e.g., insurance sold to over 90% of borrowers) seen as key profitability driver.
Existing profitable INR53,000 crore book frees management bandwidth to focus fully on new growth.

Company philosophy: business is fundamentally about liability management, not asset management; diversified liability portfolio (lenders and instruments) and lowest cost of funds seen as biggest competitive advantage.

Growth for FY27 and FY28 will largely be via mortgages (higher ticket loans) while capacity, cost of funds and enabling factors are built; by FY30 mortgage-backed products expected to be ~50% of disbursals vs ~50% via other products.
For FY27-28, 80% of disbursals dedicated to existing products, proportion declining as other products scale.
Mortgage products expected to provide book size; other products expected to expand customer franchise, enabling subsequent cross-sell opportunity.

subsections.label: Investment requirements for new products
points: Gold loan branch setup costs about INR20 lakh per branch and takes ~3 years to become fully productive/profitable.
240 existing branches already sized up to handle other products; physical distribution investment required but not running into hundreds of crores.
Bigger investment area is workforce expansion at a steady clip, requiring more assurance function hiring and product-level hiring.

Tech investments already made ahead of need, e.g., CRM/Salesforce upgrade made 6 months ago in anticipation of growth; these costs already taken and will run through the P&L, driving projected profits.

subsections.label: Rating and cost-of-funds risk
points: International/offshore credit rating agencies have not yet upgraded Sammaan, though management is optimistic on replication of domestic upgrades following ongoing engagement; ~90% of borrowings happen onshore.
Cost of funds decline will lag due to existing stock of long-term (3-4 year maturity) fixed borrowings that cannot be renegotiated (bonds), unlike bank loans which may be negotiable.

West Asia conflict and hardening yields flagged by an analyst as a potential headwind to the previously guided 270 bps FY27 cost-of-funds decline; management maintained it stands by the 270 bps figure but clarified this is tied to the AA-to-AAA ratings journey, not a single-year event.

subsections.label: Competitive intensity
points: Market now has a larger number of AAA-rated, strong, well-capitalized NBFCs compared to 8-10 years ago when the company (as Indiabulls) was one of few AAA names, raising competitive intensity questions for achieving projected profitability improvement.

subsections.label: Execution/credibility risk
points: Analyst flagged a potential error in FY30 ROA projection (appeared as ~8%); management confirmed an error and corrected the figure to 4.4% for FY30, matching FY29, and committed to updating the presentation and stock exchange filings.

subsections.label: Legacy book/credit cost risk
points: Legacy book required significant provisioning; management pushed back on the framing of this as a 'write-off', asserting these are credit costs providing buffers, with recoveries of ~INR7,000 crores expected and built into projections.
Historical experience shows 70-80% recovery achieved when selling to asset reconstruction companies, cited as risk-mitigating comfort.

subsections.label: Overall growth trajectory
points: Management targets AUM of ~INR2 lakh crores with a mix of mortgage and non-mortgage products, high-teen ROE, and best-in-class ROA/ROE over a multi-year horizon.

Growth for FY27 and FY28 will largely be via mortgages while capacity, cost of funds and other enabling factors are built; by FY30 expect ~50/50 split between mortgage-backed and other products in disbursals.
Company reiterated confidence that with continued steady compounding, it will reach 18% ROE in due course, acknowledging India will go through cycles.

subsections.label: Rating trajectory
points: AA+ achieved across all three domestic agencies (CRISIL, CARE, ICRA) within first 50 days of IHC investment, versus internal expectation of a Q3 event.

AAA is described as the ultimate destination; management expects to reach it faster than what is captured in current projections given strong operational readiness, financial position and promoter backing.
International rating agency upgrades expected to follow given multiple engagement meetings by both Sammaan and IHC management teams.

themes.note: IHC completed USD 1 billion strategic investment, now holding 28.5% (rising to 43.5% post warrant conversion), positioned as first promoter-level India investment for IHC.

themes.label: Credit rating upgrade cycle
themes.note: All three domestic rating agencies (CRISIL, CARE, ICRA) upgraded Sammaan to AA+ within first 50 days of IHC investment; international agency upgrades expected to follow.

themes.label: Cost of funds reduction
themes.note: Domestic bonds appreciated ~100 bps and international bonds ~250 bps since Sep 2025 announcement; further 60-70 bps domestic improvement and 270 bps total decline expected on AA-to-AAA journey.

themes.label: AUM and disbursement growth targets
themes.note: Company targets disbursals of ~INR30,000 crores in FY27 rising to ~INR72,000 crores by FY29, with AUM target of ~INR2 lakh crores over multi-year horizon.

themes.label: Profitability improvement (ROA/ROE/cost-income)
themes.note: Cost-to-income targeted to nearly halve from ~50% to 26% by FY30; ROA targeted to reach ~4.4% and ROE to high-teens, though an FY30 ROA figure required correction from ~8% to 4.4%.

themes.label: AI/digital transformation
themes.note: 37 AI use cases built covering customer experience, operational efficiency, risk management, collections, fraud prevention, cybersecurity and governance oversight.

themes.label: Legacy book resolution and provisioning
themes.note: Opening AUM of INR53,160 crores carries 0 gross/net NPA with no incremental provisions needed, but management defended sizable prior provisioning (not termed write-off) with ~INR7,000 crores of expected recoveries baked into projections.

key_takeaways: This call marks a significant milestone taking you through our first earnings release since IHC's acquisition of a strategic stake in Sammaan Capital and the beginning of what would truly be a transformative chapter for this institution.

Our USD 1 billion investment in Sammaan represents an important milestone for IHC. It is our first promoter level investment in India and reflects our confidence in both the company and the broader Indian financial services sector.
We start with an opening AUM, which has a 0 gross and a 0 net NPA. No incremental net provisions are required in future with respect to this opening AUM of roughly INR53,160 crores.

As Dalia mentioned, IHC has been working with us with all the credit rating agencies. CRISIL upgraded us on 9th of April, CARE on 12th of May and ICRA earlier today... within the first 50 days of the IHC investment, all 3 domestic rating agencies have upgraded us.
We intend to, through this year, disburse approximately INR30,000 crores. We are targeting a profit after tax this year of INR1,400 crores.

The cost-to-income ratio should half from here. We are currently at about 50%. We are targeting to go down to 26%. The ROA will double year-on-year and thereon also increase 50%. We intend to target high-teen ROEs and be best-in-class in both ROA and ROE.

Yes, there is an error, and that number is 4.4% in financial year '30... So the ROA... fiscal year '27, we expect that to improve to 1.8%, fiscal '28 to 3.7%, fiscal '29 to 4.4% and in fiscal '30 also be at 4.4%.
We would recover close to about INR7,000 crores from what we have provided. And that has been baked into all of these projections in due course of time.
pressing_questions: Given the ambitious AUM growth targets outlined through FY '30, could you help elaborate on the execution road map as well? Specifically what proportion of growth is expected to come through the existing core segments versus the new product lines?

In this kind of a market competitive scenario, how do you see this competitive scenario playing out? Because your projections are not just growth, it is a massive increase or improvement in profitability... what gives you sort of a confidence about these projections that, okay, this time you are going to achieve these numbers? And on that front, I mean, I guess there is some kind of error, I guess, in your FY '30 ROA projection because that's suddenly going to 8-odd percent.

My question was largely around the NIM expansion that we are seeing in FY '27 to FY '28. It's projected to go from 3.5% to 5.8%, whereas the cost of funds is not declining to that measure. And the leverage also on the book is increasing... what are the levers which are actually leading to this such a significant yield expansion?

In the previous conference call, it was mentioned that over FY '27, around 270 bps decline in cost of funds is expected. So in the current backdrop of the West Asia conflict and yields hardening currently, do you think this 270 bps reduction in cost of funds is still achievable for FY '27?

I'm shocked with your write-offs. What is the total outstanding write-off as of 31st March road map for writing? What will be the percentage of recovery from write-offs as the projections include all these writings or not?

quarters.summary: YES Bank delivered a strong Q1FY27 with Net Profit up 33.7% YoY to INR 1,071 crores, driven increasingly by core recurring earnings even as non-core income (SR gains, Treasury Income) moderated. Management reiterated near-term aspiration of NIM moving towards 3%+ over the next 2 years, full year ROA aspiration around 1% for FY27, core ROA expansion of 15-20 bps for FY27, SR portfolio gains guidance of INR 800-1,000 crores for FY27, and Advances/Deposits growth guidance of 15-17%, while flagging margin expansion will be a steady structural climb rather than straight-line, and capital raise enabling resolution kept as optionality with no immediate need seen for next 3-4 quarters.

subsections.label: Profitability Quality
points: Net Profit growth achieved even after moderation of non-core income streams such as SR portfolio gains and Treasury Income.

This is the outcome management had spoken about last quarter regarding core business gradually taking over from one-off gains, with recurring, sustainable earnings engine increasingly driving performance.

subsections.label: NIM Drivers
points: Bank continues to benefit from lower Cost of Deposits even as yields are impacted by interest rate cut transmission and change in mix.
NIM held steady sequentially.
Continued rundown of low-yielding RIDF and Priority Sector Deposits, disciplined deposit repricing, and improving CASA mix are the underlying levers for margin expansion.
Margin expansion will be a steady structural climb rather than a straight-line quarter-to-quarter, given rate cut cycle now on par and intense deposit competition.

Since April of previous financial year, Cost of Deposits has come down substantially without resulting in Deposit attrition, giving better pricing power and leverage on asset selection, plus focus on higher-yield products.

subsections.label: Cost Discipline
points: Cost-to-Income Ratio improvement reflects genuine operating leverage — income growing well ahead of costs.

subsections.label: Asset Quality
points: Further improvement in asset quality despite Q1 seasonality.
Normalized for an intra-quarter account movement in Q4, slippages are at broadly similar levels quarter-on-quarter.
Retail segment slippages improvement continued, at the lowest in the past 10 quarters.

Commercial Banking/MSME portfolio continues to be of high quality with controlled slippages in Q1; limited impact seen from the West Asia war/Max situation on the portfolio, with clients managing the crisis well.

subsections.label: SR Recovery Dynamics
points: SR redemptions were lower this quarter versus prior comparatives; face value of SRs outstanding is declining, making recoveries more unpredictable quarter to quarter.
Stored value still sits in the SR book — NAVs are upwards of INR 2,000 crores against face value of INR 1,500 crores, suggesting gross recovery could be higher.
Resolution pace depends on J.C. Flower's execution, over which the Bank has no control on timing.
Management no longer ascribes much value to corporate resolutions as that story is behind them; focus now is on J.C. Flower ARC recoveries and on core ROA.

subsections.label: Capital Position and Raise
points: Board enabling resolution for capital raise is a readiness measure, not linked to any specific trigger or the pending AT1 court case; same enabling approval was in place for FY26 and continues effectively through FY27 till AGM date.
Bank has sufficient cushion to grow for next 3-4 quarters at current 14% CET-1.
Confidence stems from availability of Deferred Tax Asset (DTA), which allows growth of 12-13% RWA without consuming capital; even at 15-16% growth, capital consumption is lower.

Bank is comparing capital buffers with peers and rating agencies' expectations; more buffers seen as beneficial, and last capital raise was done when CET-1 was at 11-11.5%; this time bank does not want to drop to those levels, aiming to raise around the 13% handle to keep adding to buffers.
No adjustment made to financial statements on account of the pending AT1 court case at this point in time.
Enabling resolution only gives Bank optionality to trigger a raise if beneficial for growth and shareholder value creation; was also approved by shareholders last year and is being refreshed.

subsections.label: ECL Transition
points: ECL transition numbers not yet publicly disclosed as the bank is still finalizing them.

ECL has an offset component from Security Receipts — if allowed the SR benefit, there is no impact on ECL; however, the SR-related ECL adjustment will not be allowed on the Balance Sheet, requiring the impact to be taken through the P&L for the year.
At the gross level, some ECL impact is likely but not expected to be material.

New circular on credit Risk-Weighted Assets is also coming in from 1st April; combined impact of ECL transition and new capital adequacy credit risk weights is expected to not be material on core equity.
Bank will provide better visibility on these numbers during the course of the year as they firm up.

subsections.label: Advances Growth Composition
points: Growth was broad-based across businesses; Corporate and Institutional Banking grew strongly.
Part of the Corporate growth is transitional and shorter tenure in nature.
On an average balance basis, underlying loan growth is in the 15-16% handle, which management finds comfortable and consistent with its commitment to grow in line with or slightly ahead of industry.

subsections.label: Deposits Franchise
points: CASA growth on an average balance basis (15%) is a creditable outcome given the sharp rate actions taken during FY26 and Q1FY27.

Retail and Branch-led Deposits reflect growing granularity of the franchise; in a system where deposits are the binding constraint, the Bank is choosing to compete via its granular Branch-led liability franchise.

subsections.label: Advances vs Deposits Growth Balance
points: Advances growth appears higher than Deposits on end-of-period balances, but daily average balances for both Advances and Deposits show CD ratio has remained the same versus March quarter — no worsening of CD ratio; growth rates for both are in line.
Bank will continue to focus on liability-led Balance Sheet expansion, never aggressively pursuing Assets in the absence of a Deposit construct.
Over the last 3 years, the Bank has delivered among the best outcomes on Cost of Deposits versus the industry, reflected via improving CASA ratio and higher share from Branch Banking/Retail Deposits.

subsections.label: Retail Growth Strategy
points: Retail book growth (7% range) reflects that portfolio takes time to reflect improved underlying momentum; incremental/fresh business is growing 25-30% depending on segment.
Momentum on fresh Retail business is strong even though portfolio book growth remains modest for now; this will start reflecting in book growth in subsequent quarters.

Retail disbursement growth on Q-o-Q basis attributed to seasonality (March typically very high) plus element of co-lending/partnership-led disbursements; organic levels are similar quarter-on-quarter.

Run-off factors (from prior deliberate slowdown of loan book during FY23-25) are still affecting Retail book growth; as run-off tapers over next 3-4 quarters, disbursements should translate into double-digit book growth.

Retail product strategy is multi-product/diversified: Personal Loans slowed over last 2 years but are now growing again; Loan Against Property (LAP) continues to perform well; 'franchise products' like Home Loan/Auto Loan offered as needed; co-lending structures also in place.
Guardrail maintained: approximately 75% secured versus 25% unsecured mix within Retail, ensuring unsecured does not dominate.

subsections.label: Commercial Banking / MSME
points: Commercial Banking portfolio continues to be of high quality with controlled slippages; management continues to assess portfolio for impacts of the West Asia war but reports very limited impact and clients managing the crisis well.

subsections.label: FCNR Deposit Demand
points: Strong demand seen in FCNR deposits from two aspects: pure deposits and leverage.
Leverage limits already filled; leverage currently capped at 9x, with possibility of revisiting if market expectation warrants a higher level.
Bank believes it is ahead of the market/other banks on FCNR positioning, though no specific number was given.
Straight/pureplay FCNR(B) deposit gathering via Branch Banking franchise faces no constraint and is getting good traction; leveraging part depends on limits granted by partner/foreign banks.
Interest coming from various geographies, including notably from the East.

subsections.label: Indo-Japan Corridor
points: Indo-Japanese trade and investment corridor strengthening year after year, especially after recent inter-government and Prime Ministerial meetings and trade team engagement.
Japan taking a lead in India infrastructure financing (bullet train, shipbuilding) and other sectors like defense.
Growing interest from Japanese corporates to establish operations in India via wholly owned subsidiaries, joint ventures, or distribution channels.

subsections.label: External Validation / Ratings
points: Moody's upgraded issuer rating to Ba1.
CARE upgraded Basel III Tier 2 and Infrastructure bonds to AA+.
ICRA upgraded the same instruments to AA.
S&P Global assigned the Bank its inaugural international rating of BB+.

These rating actions are seen as independent affirmation of strengthening fundamentals — improving profitability, better liability profile, enhanced asset quality, robust capitalization, and confidence from strong institutional sponsorship.
Upgrades carry tangible benefits for funding costs, Wholesale and Financial Institutions relationships, and brand.

subsections.label: Awards and Recognition
points: Awarded 'Most Sustainable Bank' at Business Today's India's Most Sustainable Companies 2026.
Included in the FTSE4Good Index for the fourth consecutive year.
Recognized among the top 25 India's Best Workplaces in BFSI for 2026.
NRI homecoming campaigns earned several awards for being most disruptive in the use of AI.

subsections.label: Competitive Positioning on CASA
points: An individual investor raised concern that the Bank is not growing CASA Deposits ratio as well as peers like IDFC First Bank, and suggested extending IPO subscription cut-off times (currently 3:30 PM vs IDFC's 4:30 PM and SBI's 5:00 PM) and more aggressive Retail customer acquisition ahead of large IPOs (NSE, Jio, etc.); management acknowledged the suggestion and said they will work on it.

subsections.label: SMBC Collaboration
points: Collaboration with SMBC referenced as part of the Bank's PPPT structure and governance framework.
Bank is working with many international banks, including SMBC, on limits to make the FCNR leverage facility available.

Leveraging partnership with SMBC for the Indo-Japanese trade/investment corridor is already underway, including Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) in place; specifics not disclosed due to confidentiality.

Endeavor is to capture the maximum business happening in the India-Japan corridor — trade, investments, infrastructure — through the Bank, alongside opportunities from Japanese corporates setting up wholly owned subsidiaries, joint ventures or distribution channels in India.

subsections.label: Capital Raise Enabling Resolution
points: Board passed an enabling resolution for capital raise (referenced quantum of INR 16,000 crores with 10% equity dilution per an investor question) to keep readiness/optionality; not a trigger of any specific event.
Enabling approval has been carried forward from last year's shareholder approval and continues effectively through FY27 till the AGM date.
Decision to raise capital will depend on market opportunity and conduciveness to shareholder value; management is monitoring peer capitalization levels as one consideration.

subsections.label: Macro Environment
points: Q1 quarter characterized by resilient domestic demand, strong tax buoyancy and steady manufacturing momentum set against rising cost pressures and a more uncertain global backdrop.

Direct tax collections grew a healthy 16.4%; GST collections stayed strong at nearly INR 1.95 lakh crores in June; manufacturing has been in expansion mode for 37 straight months; industrial production hit a 5-month high led by capital goods; system-level loan growth showing uptick.
Inflation rose to a 17-month high of 4.4% on food and fuel costs, prompting RBI to lift its inflation projection to 5.1%, though monsoon recovered well after a dry start, easing some concern.
GDP growth forecasts have not been impaired despite inflation pressure.

subsections.label: FCNR/Leverage Constraints
points: Global borrowing spreads for overseas financial institutions taking a 5-year view on India have inched up.

Global liquidity availability is uneven across geographies; some overseas geography or set of geographies must fund India for the size the Bank is looking at, requiring risk limits to rise commensurately.
Process of risk review and limit-setting across institutions for 3-5 year periods, in a commercially viable manner, is underway but has been slower than expected partly due to geopolitical issues.
Bank has capped leverage at 9x currently on FCNR product; could revisit if market expects a higher level, but no specific number given for growth in this leverage.

subsections.label: AT1 Court Case
points: A court case is pending regarding AT1 bonds; there is no adjustment to the Bank's financial statements on account of this court case at this point in time; capital raise enabling resolution is not linked to this court case.

subsections.label: ECL Transition Risk
points: ECL transition to new framework next year could have some gross-level impact not expected to be material, combined with new capital adequacy credit risk weight circular effective 1st April; overall impact on core equity not expected to be material, but numbers not finalized yet.

subsections.label: Overall Compass for the Year
points: Compass for the year ahead unchanged: aspiration of delivering full year ROA around 1%, focus on improving core profitability, growing Advances and Deposits in a profitable and calibrated way, deepening Deposit and CASA franchise, moving margins structurally higher over the medium term, holding the line on Asset Quality with conservative provisioning — anchored in the People-Product-Processes-Technology (PPPT) structure and collaboration with SMBC, within a strong governance framework.

subsections.label: Reported vs Core ROA
points: Fully reported 1% ROA for FY27 is contingent on external factors like bond gains and trading also playing out, in addition to core ROA improvement of 15-20 bps.

guidance_ledger.statement: Near-term aspiration is to move the NIM towards the 3% plus handle over the next 2 years.
North of 3% is something we would be able to achieve.
Maintain our guidance of INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores of gains from this portfolio for this financial year '27, despite tepid gains from the SR portfolio in Q1.
Endeavor to grow at a little above what the industry would be growing at, in the range of maybe 15% to 17%.
Aspiration would be delivering a full year ROA around 1%; if resolutions and external factors like bond gains and trading play out, should be able to deliver the fully reported 1% ROA for fiscal '27.
Our expectation is fiscal '27, we should see a 15 to 20 basis points expansion in the core ROA.
Can we reach like mid-teens number by FY27 as disbursement translates to loan growth - Yes, sure. Absolutely. We are working towards that as well.
As run-off starts tapering, we should be able to deliver a double-digit growth as well on Retail in about 3 to 4 quarters from now.
14% is reasonable for the next 4 quarters of growth; may raise capital to keep it around the 13% handle level to add buffers depending on market opportunity.
Keeping leverage at 9x at this point in time; may change leverage if market expects it to be raised.
Impact of ECL transition combined with new capital adequacy credit risk weights is not expected to be material on core equity; will provide better visibility during the course of the year.

risk_register.risk: Inflation rising to 17-month high of 4.4% on food and fuel costs, prompting RBI to lift inflation projection to 5.1%
risk_register.note: Monsoon recovered well after a dry start, easing some of the concern; GDP growth forecasts have not been impaired.

risk_register.risk: Margin expansion pace constrained by rate cut cycle being on par and intense deposit competition
risk_register.note: Management cautions margin expansion will be a steady structural climb rather than a straight-line quarter-to-quarter.

risk_register.risk: Global borrowing spreads and uneven global liquidity constraining FCNR leverage growth
risk_register.note: Risk review and limit-setting process across institutions for 3-5 year periods is slower than expected, partly due to geopolitical issues.
No adjustment made to financial statements on account of this court case at this point in time; capital raise enabling resolution not linked to this case.

risk_register.risk: ECL transition and new capital adequacy credit risk weight circular impact
risk_register.note: Gross-level ECL impact likely but not expected to be material; combined impact with new credit risk weight circular (effective 1st April) also not expected to be material on core equity; numbers still being finalized.

risk_register.risk: West Asia war impact on Commercial Banking/MSME portfolio
risk_register.note: Management continues to monitor closely but reports very limited impact; clients have managed the crisis well.

risk_register.risk: SR recovery unpredictability due to declining face value and dependence on J.C. Flower's execution pace
risk_register.note: Face value outstanding declining to INR 1,500 crores; resolution timing outside Bank's control.

risk_register.risk: CASA growth lagging peers like IDFC First Bank
risk_register.note: Raised by an individual investor as a concern; management acknowledged the suggestion to work on it, no explicit risk status given by management.

themes.label: Margin expansion trajectory
themes.note: NIM improved 20 bps YoY to 2.7%, held steady sequentially; aspiration to move towards 3%+ over next 2 years, though expansion will be a steady structural climb, not straight-line.

themes.label: Core earnings vs one-off income
themes.note: Net Profit growth achieved despite moderation of non-core income (SR gains, Treasury Income), reflecting core recurring business increasingly driving performance.

themes.label: Asset quality improvement
themes.note: Gross Slippage improved to 1.4% from 1.6% QoQ and 2.4% YoY; Retail slippages at lowest in 10 quarters; GNPA/NNPA at 1.3%/0.2% with 81.7% provision coverage.

themes.label: Liability-led balance sheet growth
themes.note: Deposits grew 14.3% YoY with CASA at 15% on average balance basis; Bank continues to prioritize liability-led growth over aggressive asset growth without deposit backing.

themes.label: Capital raise optionality
themes.note: Board enabling resolution for capital raise (INR 16,000 crores/10% dilution referenced) kept as readiness measure; management sees 14% CET-1 as sufficient for next 3-4 quarters but wants to build buffers opportunistically.

themes.label: Rating upgrades / external validation
themes.note: Moody's, CARE, ICRA upgrades and inaugural S&P Global rating (BB+) seen as affirmation of strengthening fundamentals, aiding funding costs and institutional relationships.

themes.label: FCNR and Indo-Japan corridor opportunity
themes.note: Strong FCNR demand with leverage capped at 9x; SMBC partnership and MOUs being leveraged to capture growing Indo-Japanese trade/investment corridor business.

themes.label: Retail growth momentum vs book growth lag
themes.note: Retail disbursements growing 27.5-30% YoY and fresh business growing 25-30%, but book growth still modest (6.9%) due to run-off effects; double-digit book growth expected in 3-4 quarters.

key_takeaways: Our Net Profit grew 33.7% that is year-on-year to INR 1,071 crores.

Our Operating Profit grew 25.5% year-on-year to INR 1,704 crores. Net Interest Income was up 17.5% year-on-year at INR 2,786 crores, and our Net Interest Margin improved 20 basis points year-on-year to 2.7%, also holding steady sequentially.
Our near-term aspiration is to move the NIM towards the 3% plus handle over the next 2 years and the underlying levers are well understood.
Our Core Fees registered a strong 18.7% growth year-on-year with broad-based traction across cards, third-party products, forex as well as transaction banking.
Our Cost-to-Income Ratio improved further to 62.8% from 67.1% a year ago, reflecting genuine operating leverage - income growing well ahead of costs.
On a reported basis, Gross Slippage was lower at 1.4% of Advances against 1.6% in the previous quarter and 2.4% in quarter 1 FY26.
Despite tepid gains from the SR portfolio in Q1, we maintain our guidance of INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores of gains from this portfolio for this financial year '27.
Total Advances grew 18.3% year-on-year to INR 2.85 lakh crores.
On Deposits, the Total Deposits grew 14.3% year-on-year to INR 3.15 lakh crores.

Moody's upgraded our issuer rating to Ba1. CARE upgraded our Basel III Tier 2 and Infrastructure bonds to AA+. ICRA upgraded the same instruments to AA and S&P Global has assigned the Bank its inaugural international rating of BB+.

quarters.summary: Embassy Developments started FY27 with strong presales (up 338% YoY) and collections (up 54% YoY), driven by continued absorption of FY26 launches; management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crores presales from owned projects, INR2,000 crores from DM projects, and ~INR3,000 crores of collections, with 11 launches (INR19,400 crores GDV) planned across the year, 4 in Q2 and the rest in Q3/Q4. Reported P&L remains depressed (net loss) due to completion-based revenue recognition even as operating metrics (presales, collections, sold inventory) stay healthy; balance sheet strengthening continues via a promoter preferential warrant allotment to repay Embassy Group's shareholder debt, with management targeting a gradual reduction first in cost of debt and later in overall institutional debt from FY27-end into FY28.

subsections.label: Accounting characteristics
points: Revenue from residential projects is recognized only upon project completion and handover under applicable accounting standards, creating a timing difference between operating performance (presales/collections) and reported financials.
Reported P&L should be viewed alongside underlying operating metrics which provide visibility into future revenue recognition and cash flow generation.
While reported earnings continue to be influenced by timing of project completions, underlying operating performance remained healthy during the quarter.

subsections.label: Collections and cash flow
points: Collections increased 54% YoY, supported by steady customer inflows across ongoing projects.
As launch pipeline gathers pace and execution advances, milestone-linked collections are expected to accelerate over the balance of FY27.

Company started FY27 with negative operating cash flow in Q1 because no projects were launched in the quarter; most projects launched in Q3/Q4 of last fiscal, and collections for those kick in about 6 months later (Q2/Q3/Q4 of FY27).
Very good collection in Q1 (~INR500 crores) against INR1,680-odd crores collected in the entire last financial year.
Management expects an inflection point around mid-calendar-2027 (April/May) when Greenshore, Verde, Citadel and other projects come out of ground and slab cycle collections accelerate significantly.
Company is early in its capex cycle with excavation ongoing on most projects; significant collections typically start once slab cycle begins.
Presales grew 338% YoY in Q1 FY27.
Construction spend of INR276 crores in Q1 FY27 equated to 56% of collections.

Collection-to-presales ratio was 35% in FY26 versus an industry average benchmark of 70%; company targets improving this to 50% in FY27 (based on guidance of INR3,000 crores collections against INR6,000 crores presales).

subsections.label: Balance sheet and capital structure
points: Board approved a preferential allotment of convertible warrants to promoter Embassy Group, subject to shareholder approval, proceeds earmarked to repay Embassy Group's outstanding shareholder debt, reducing it to nil.
Preferential allotment priced at INR111.51/share, consistent with the previous preferential issue price done a couple of years back before the merger; pricing was deliberate.

Promoters voluntarily committed to convert all warrants into equity within 6 months versus the maximum permitted tenor of 18 months, reflecting confidence in short- and long-term business fundamentals.
This preferential allotment does not bring additional liquidity into the system; it converts accruing (>15%) shareholder debt into equity as a confidence signal.
Outstanding shareholder debt totals INR1,063 crores, comprising INR700 crores owed to Blackstone and INR363 crores owed to Embassy Group.
Company remains focused on optimizing capital structure via refinancing existing borrowings and reducing overall cost of debt, expected to improve profitability and operating cash flows over time.
As collections accelerate and cash flows strengthen, this is expected to naturally support gradual reduction in institutional debt over time.

Capital allocation philosophy: prioritize project execution, maintain adequate liquidity for ongoing construction, selectively pursue high-quality business opportunities, preserve financial flexibility.
In talks with Blackstone to convert their portion of debt to equity; awaiting response.

Roadmap for debt reduction: sequence is first reduce cost of debt (via refinancing as collections build), then reduce overall debt quantum as projects throw off surplus cash beyond construction spend; full portfolio refinancing targeted around March/April next year.

Gross institutional debt of ~INR4,500 crores was taken predominantly to fund launch of ~INR16,000 crores of inventory launched last year and ~INR19,000 crores planned this year (~INR35,000 crores total), against which net debt is only ~INR3,300 crores; current net debt-to-equity of 0.35x considered comfortable, with a future target range of 0.3x-0.35x.
Cash and cash equivalents stood at ~INR1,200 crores as of June 30, 2026.
Average cost of debt is ~14% currently; Blackstone debt specifically carries an 18% rate, accrued but not paid out.

Management exploring possibility of adopting percentage-of-completion accounting method instead of completion method, to review over next couple of quarters and implement if feasible without adverse taxation implications.

Goodwill on balance sheet (~INR2,500 crores) arose from reverse merger accounting done in January last year, representing the difference between prevailing Indiabulls Real Estate share price and value of projects at that time; tested for impairment every 6 months; management views it as retaining value given rising Indian land prices, calling it 'priced in a little ahead of schedule' rather than impaired.
Typical project value breakup: land cost ~30-35%, construction spend ~30-35%, and profit margin ~30-35% of project value; own land bank projects targeted to generate >50% cash surplus.
Total GDV stands at ~INR57,000 crores against a cash surplus of ~INR30,000 crores per the investor deck.

FY27 guidance: presales of INR6,000 crores from owned developments plus INR2,000 crores from development management projects; collections guidance of INR3,000 crores; launch pipeline GDV of INR19,400 crores (INR13,300 crores from owned projects, INR6,000+ crores from development management projects).

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Demand across core markets continues to be healthy across both premium and luxury residential segments.

Customers increasingly favor developers with a proven track record and reputation for trust; India seen in the midst of a multi-decade housing cycle with industry consolidating toward strongest, most reliable developers.
Nearly 60% of inventory launched in FY26 already sold; Bangalore performing especially well with ~72% of launch inventory sold within 6 months.
Citadel (large ~INR8,000-9,000 crores stock project) skews the pan-India 60% first-6-month sales ratio; Bangalore ratio seen as better gauge of on-ground demand robustness.
OC-received product portfolio ~98% cumulative sold; ongoing development portfolio of 11 assets ~70% sold based on saleable area.

Ongoing inventory available for sale at start of FY27 was INR10,500 crores, plus INR400 crores of completed OC-received inventory, against cumulative unsold inventory across the launched/under-construction portfolio of INR13,630 crores.
Fresh launches pipeline for FY27 carries a GDV of INR19,400 crores.

subsections.label: Project execution milestones
points: Embassy One 09 in Gurgaon (One 09 Phase 1) and 5 towers in Golf City Savroli received occupancy certificate (OC) during the quarter, moving closer to customer handovers.

Embassy Citadel in Mumbai has approval for all 81 floors of development upfront, unlike the market norm of stage-wise approvals, providing greater execution certainty; Leighton appointed as civil contractor for Embassy Citadel.
Embassy Paradiso at Embassy Springs and balance towers of Golf City Savroli nearing completion, slated for OC in FY27.
Embassy Edge and Embassy East Avenue progressing well towards completion in FY28, both already substantially sold.
Newer launches Embassy Verde Phase 2, Embassy Greenshore and Embassy Eden recording healthy sales with construction advancing as per plan.
Embassy Citadel combined with prime Worli location positions it as one of the most compelling luxury residential developments in the portfolio with strong long-term value and surplus.

Portfolio reflects a healthy mix of projects nearing delivery and new developments progressing on construction, providing visibility into future completions, revenue recognition and cash flow generation.

subsections.label: Brand and legacy project management
points: Embassy is refocusing back into residential development after a period focused on commercial, replicating Bangalore luxury leadership into the premium segment (e.g., Embassy Springs) and into Mumbai (Citadel, Juhu).

Legacy Indiabulls projects taken on as liabilities to fix: Panvel was a ghost site with only 40 laborers when taken over, now has 1,500 laborers, project fully revamped, banks funding customers, sales happening.

Some legacy projects (e.g., Savroli, 109 Gurgaon Phase 1) intentionally not branded with Embassy name as they were too close to completion; company still honored obligations, unlocked back-ended collections from earlier 20:80 payment schemes, and closed those books.

In Gurgaon/NCR, some landlords initially confused by the 'merger' terminology (technically a merger, in substance a takeover) into thinking Embassy and Indiabulls are working together; management clarifying they are entirely separate; expects this perception issue to fade as more projects are launched under the Embassy name.

Company believes it commands a pricing premium over other developers when launching projects in Bangalore; in Mumbai, deliberately pricing Worli's first inventory tranche to let early customers benefit before raising prices closer to competitor levels; considers itself already on par with Mumbai competitors for the Juhu project.

Embassy Hub plot A GDV of INR2,100 crores with company share of 91%; other project GDVs include Embassy One North tower (INR1,400 crores), Embassy Knowledge Park (INR4,450 crores), Embassy Springs (INR1,900 crores), and 109 Commercial Phase 2 (INR800 crores).

subsections.label: Core markets and pipeline diversification
points: FY27 launch pipeline is well diversified across the 3 core markets: Bengaluru, Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), and NCR, with continued focus on premium apartments, luxury residences and villa developments.
Company has strengthened senior leadership in NCR and business development team in Mumbai, and is actively looking for new projects in NCR and MMR regions.
Bangalore is described as the company's home market where it understands the regulatory system well and is most comfortable, versus growing comfort in Mumbai.

In NCR, actively trying to grow presence in Gurgaon; hired a regional head; some landlords initially confused Embassy with Indiabulls due to the merger, but this is expected to fade with time and further launches.

subsections.label: Brand positioning strategy
points: Embassy positions itself as top luxury residential developer in Bangalore historically; now expanding play across segments — luxury and premium (e.g., Embassy Springs) — with significant sales coming through the premium segment.
Strategy to replicate the successful Bangalore brand playbook in Mumbai via marquee, irreplaceable locations like Citadel (Worli) and Juhu (2.5-acre sea-touching site).
Management frames the honoring of legacy Indiabulls project obligations (fixing failed sites, unlocking back-ended collections) as part of building customer trust that most developers would avoid.

subsections.label: Land bank monetization
points: Land bank monetization is a priority but not the most immediate one; management understands the composition of the land bank and sees potential in the Raigad region where land compounding/growth is expected.
Total land bank exceeds 3,000+ acres, of which Nashik accounts for 1,400+ acres and other scattered parcels (ex-Nashik) account for 1,600-1,800 acres.

Other lands (besides Nashik) are scattered and require significant capital for aggregation — buying out cheese-hole parcels and purchasing access — to be addressed once the company has sufficient surplus to deploy.

First priority is to launch launchable lands, generate surplus, collect money, and pursue business development (BD) opportunities that can move from greenfield to launch quickly — e.g., Whitefield land acquired last September (1.7 million sq ft project area, 68.5% company share, ~INR2,000 crores GDV) is already being launched in Q3 this year (~12 months greenfield-to-launch, described as fast for the industry).

Nashik (1,400+ acres): company working with MIDC, met them a couple of times seeking an amicable solution; simultaneously pursuing a debonding exercise requiring clearance from 5 different government agencies, estimated to take another 6-9 months to complete from today; a sublessee of ~80-plus acres has intervened in the application, slowing the legal process; solution likely to be a mix of amicable resolution with MIDC and continuing the debonding exercise.

Of the ~1,800 acres ex-Nashik scattered land, Sohna Road (500 acres, of which 75 acres developable) is the identified stretch being readied for development; balance is scattered land aggregation which will take considerable time; management does not want to commit to timelines or include it in the pipeline until ready, given how land aggregation works in India.
Beyond-FY27 development pipeline totals 20.3 million sq ft with an approximate GDV of INR23,470 crores.

subsections.label: Commercial land optionality
points: Company holds 2 large commercial land parcels: Embassy East Business Park and Embassy Knowledge Park (commercial portion).

Embassy East Business Park Phase 1 launched last year, excavation ongoing; company intends to build out the asset, potentially hold as an annuity asset or seek a REIT exit closer to completion; views REIT as an exciting group strategy.

Embassy Knowledge Park commercial portion intentionally excluded from GDV/surplus in all investor decks; product is still being finalized — envisioned as a low-rise R&D-type center rather than a typical office asset like Embassy Manyata or other REIT assets; company expects to provide clear timelines, GDV and surplus by end of the fiscal year.

subsections.label: Branded residence repositioning
points: Embassy One North tower project was earlier branded as a Four Seasons-affiliated hotel/residence (Four Seasons owned by Embassy REIT); Embassy REIT has since terminated Four Seasons, and correspondingly Embassy Developments terminated the Four Seasons branding for the residences.
Project will now launch as Embassy One North tower under the Embassy banner only, which management believes is more profitable for the company; launch intentionally pushed to Q2.

subsections.label: Regulatory/approval delays
points: Bangalore has been 'a little problematic' since change of Chief Minister — the GBA (planning authority) has not been able to convene meetings, though management does not attribute Q1 non-launches to this specifically.

Peer developer (Prestige) reported 4 Bangalore projects shifting from Q1 to Q2 due to RERA and building plan delays; management does not attribute its own timing issue to the same cause, citing deliberate strategic choice instead (Four Seasons de-branding) plus a resolved TDR FSI issue.
Other Bangalore projects among the remaining 5 owned projects targeted for Q3, with possibility some spill into Q4.

subsections.label: Nashik land/legal risk
points: Debonding process (SEZ to non-SEZ conversion) requires clearance across 5 government agencies and is expected to take another 6-9 months from today.
A sublessee holding ~80-plus acres has intervened in the MIDC application, which is expected to slow the legal process further.
Resolution path envisioned as a mix of amicable settlement with MIDC alongside continuing the debonding exercise.

subsections.label: Brand/perception risk from Indiabulls legacy
points: In Gurgaon/NCR, some landlords have questioned whether Embassy and Indiabulls (erstwhile company, now separate and still active in NCR) are working together, due to confusion from the 'merger' terminology, even though technically it was a takeover; management says this will fade with time and market education but hasn't been raised recently.

Legacy Indiabulls project execution/collection issues (e.g., Panvel, back-ended 20:80 payment schemes) required rectification, described by management as a 'painful' but necessary obligation to honor.

subsections.label: Accounting/earnings optics
points: Completion-based revenue recognition accounting causes reported P&L (losses) to diverge from healthy underlying operating performance; management expects continued reported losses for several more quarters due to this timing mismatch.
Goodwill of ~INR2,500 crores on balance sheet stems from reverse merger accounting; tested for impairment every 6 months, though a shareholder questioned its usefulness.

subsections.label: High cost of debt
points: Average cost of institutional debt is ~14%; Blackstone debt specifically accrues at 18%, added to gross debt rather than paid out, a headwind to profitability until refinanced.

INR2,000 crores from the developed managed projects
Approximately INR3,000 crores of collections; we remain on track to deliver our FY27 collections guidance of approximately INR3,000 crores

We expect to launch 4 of these 11 projects in the current quarter, which is Q2
Other projects between Gurgaon and Bangalore, we feel comfortable that Q3 is what we're targeting, but Q3, Q4 is where I can see the rest of the projects landing

key_takeaways: We have started FY27 with good momentum. The first quarter reflects the progress we have made over the past year, especially as the launches from the second half of FY26 continue to translate into healthy sales and collections.

Nearly 60% of our inventory launched in FY26 has already been sold, and Bangalore continues to perform especially well with approximately 72% of launch inventory sold within 6 months.

We remain comfortable with our FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crores in presales from the owned developments, INR2,000 crores from the developed managed projects and approximately INR3,000 crores of collections.

The Board has just approved a preferential allotment of convertible warrants to the promoter Embassy Group, subject to shareholder approval. The proceeds will be used to repay outstanding shareholder debt of Embassy Group, further strengthening our balance sheet and reducing our cost of capital over time.

During Q1 FY27, revenue from operations stood at INR217 crores compared to INR681 crores in Q1 FY26... the company reported a net loss of INR234 crores compared with a net loss of INR166 crores in the corresponding quarter last year.

As of June 30, 2026, our gross institutional debt stood at approximately INR4,500 crores, while cash and cash equivalents were approximately INR1,200 crores, resulting in net institutional debt of approximately INR3,300 crores and a net debt to equity of 0.35x.
Embassy Citadel in Mumbai has approval for all 81 floors of development upfront... we have appointed Leighton as our civil contractor for Embassy Citadel.

subsections.label: Revenue recognition mismatch
points: Real estate revenue for RERA registered projects under Ind AS 115 is recognized on completed contract basis, only on receipt of OC and handover to customers, not at presale.
Over 80% of FY26 presales were concentrated in H2, predominantly from Embassy Citadel, Embassy Greenshore, Embassy Eden and Embassy Verde Phase 2, whose target OC dates range FY28 through FY32.
Revenue from these projects will be recognized from FY28 onwards in respective years when OC is received; FY26 P&L reflects a fixed cost structure incurred ahead of the revenue recognition curve.
As OC is received for launched projects, revenue recognition profile is expected to progressively normalize and accounting profit margins to improve over the years.

subsections.label: Reverse merger accounting impact
points: Under Ind AS 103 reverse merger accounting treatment, existing NAM shareholders became the largest shareholders, so NAM was treated as accounting acquirer and EDL as accounting acquiree.

As fair-valued inventory is sold over time, consolidated P&L accounting profit margin is reduced to the extent of the differential between historical cost and fair value step-up; this does not impact underlying cash flows on these assets.

subsections.label: Collections vs presales lag
points: FY26 collections (INR1,673 crores) were marginally lower than FY25 (INR1,852 crores) even as presales grew 128% YoY, because milestone-linked collections from H2 FY26 presales will largely flow through FY27 and FY28.
Presales-to-collection conversion is described as a structural lag, not an operational issue.

subsections.label: Debt and capital structure
points: Upcoming launches and strategic projects expected to generate meaningful cash flow surpluses, supporting structured reduction in institutional debt while funding future growth.

FY27 plan is to deploy most of ~INR3,000 crores collections toward ~INR2,500 crores construction spend, so a large debt reduction is not expected this year; company expects to be in a much stronger position by year-end to pay down debt over the next ~24 months.
Cost of debt (14.8%) expected to gradually decline toward 10% over 12-18 months as projects mature and cash flow improves.

subsections.label: Interest capitalization
points: Whatever interest could be capitalized to projects has been capitalized; ~INR550 crores was expensed to P&L because it was deployed on OC-received (legacy) projects and corporate expenses, which cannot be capitalized.
Company's first 6-8 months priority was completing legacy projects, so capital/debt was deployed there and expensed rather than capitalized.
Borrowing against OC projects sometimes funds general corporate purposes (e.g., premium approval charges for Blu project), making a simple apples-to-apples debt-to-project comparison inaccurate.

subsections.label: Promoter pledge
points: Promoter pledge was ~47% before the NCLAT matter; it was increased to 68% only because the share price fell (no additional debt was taken by promoters).
As share price recovers, pledge is expected to revert to ~48% and promoters plan to pay off pledge-related debt over the next 2-3 years, eventually fully unpledging shares.

subsections.label: Equity/debt conversion stance
points: Shareholder debt of ~INR1,100 crores held along with Blackstone will be converted to equity over time, but management is waiting for the share price to reach appropriate fair valuation levels before converting, to avoid dilutive conversion at low prices.
Management believes the current share price is undervalued following resolution of two legal overhangs, and expects the stock to recover over the coming months.

subsections.label: Sequential sales ramp-up
points: Quarterly presales increased steadily from INR198 crores (Q1) to INR409 crores (Q2) to INR1,392 crores (Q3) before closing at INR2,632 crores in Q4, reflecting accelerated launches through the year.
Quarterly collections increased steadily from INR322 crores in Q1 to INR577 crores in Q4.
Area sold increased from 206,000 sq ft in Q1 to 1.78 million sq ft in Q4.

subsections.label: Key Q4 launch drivers
points: Embassy Citadel, entry into South Mumbai luxury segment, is a 1 million sq ft development with estimated GDV of over INR8,800 crores; prelaunch achieved INR797 crores (~8% of inventory) in just 45 days from mid-February launch, validating product positioning and pricing strategy in a competitive luxury market.
Embassy Verde Phase 2 at Embassy Springs delivered 87% absorption within the quarter generating INR588 crores in Q4 presales.
Together Citadel and Verde Phase 2 contributed INR1,385 crores or ~53% of Q4 presales.

Embassy Eden (Bangalore luxury villa) established a clear category leadership position; Bangalore luxury (INR10 crores+ ticket) launches accounted for over 65% of all FY26 Bangalore sales in that segment (~INR2,000 crores), showcasing Embassy's strength in Bangalore luxury.

subsections.label: Demand momentum / market view
points: Management does not see real estate demand slowing yet despite market noise about a slowdown; Verde sold 80%+ and Embassy Eden (INR20 crores+ ticket, high end of Bangalore market) sold 48% in 6 months.

Top developers are seen consolidating market share as the market potentially slows; Embassy believes it will be an outlier gaining market share, leveraging its strong Bangalore brand to build similar strength in Mumbai.
FY27 pipeline balances luxury/ultra-luxury (Juhu, Sky Terraces, Embassy One) with fast-moving mid-segment product, seen as a hedge for this stage of the cycle.
Management believes real estate is a hedge on inflation and pricing will eventually catch up to cost increases from energy shocks.

subsections.label: Embassy Citadel demand color
points: Citadel positioned as a value proposition in Worli given smaller ticket size and lower pricing vs top developers; management is intentionally not shying away from discounts while building brand/luxury moat in Mumbai.
Contractor La Tim (described as best contractor in the country) has been engaged for Citadel; excavation is underway; management feels comfortable with timelines.
RERA completion date shown as 2035 (moved from 2032) is a filing buffer only; actual target OC is FY31/32, consistent with market norms for large 300-meter towers.

subsections.label: FY27 launch pipeline detail
points: 9 owned projects with cumulative GDV of INR13,300 crores, supplemented by 2 DM projects, taking total launch GDV to ~INR19,400 crores.

Key headline launches: Embassy One North Tower in Bengaluru (adjacent to Four Seasons Hotel), Embassy Knowledge Park Villas and Apartments in North Bangalore (adjacent to Embassy Riding School), Front Parcel Villas & Apartments at Embassy Springs, newly acquired Whitefield JDA project, Plot A at Embassy Hub in Hebbal, and 109 Commercial in Gurgaon.
Two DM projects: Juhu (super exclusive/ultra-luxury, expecting IOD shortly) and Sky Terraces in Bangalore (expected robust demand at launch), combined GDV ~INR6,000-6,100 crores.

Pipeline is geographically balanced across the 3 core markets (Bangalore, MMR, NCR) and weighted toward categories with demonstrated strong absorption: luxury residences and villas, premium apartments and lifestyle second homes.

Launch timing color (from Q&A): Embassy One North Tower launching this quarter (building plan already obtained); Embassy Knowledge Park towards end of this quarter or spilling into Q2; Juhu in Q2; Sky Terraces end of Q1 or Q2; Embassy Springs Front Parcel probably Q2 or Q3 — bulk of launches concentrated in H1/early H2.

subsections.label: Long-term pipeline & land bank
points: Planned project pipeline beyond FY27 carries a further 20.4 million sq ft with estimated GDV of ~INR23,500 crores.
Combined with the 3,250-acre fully paid land bank, this provides multiyear revenue visibility and flexibility to phase launches according to market conditions.

subsections.label: Steady-state margin framework
points: Management is shifting focus from EBITDA (a P&L item dependent on revenue recognition timing) to net surplus margin from launched projects, expected to be close to 50% over the next several years as projects are delivered.
This net surplus cash is intended to fund more projects/business development and service debt, rather than being reflected in near-term reported EBITDA.

subsections.label: Brand evolution
points: Company undertook a brand evolution, shifting from a legacy-led identity to a more forward-looking brand with renewed philosophies, values and visual identity.

subsections.label: Platform integration
points: FY26 marked the first full year of the merged platform following integration of NAM Estates and the erstwhile Indiabulls Real Estate Limited under the unified Embassy Developments brand.
FY26 characterized as a year of solidifying operations, integrating and building teams, and executing in a disciplined manner while managing cash flows effectively.

subsections.label: Non-core land monetization
points: Company evaluates monetizing non-core/non-strategic land parcels when good offers arise, particularly parcels not mutated or scattered/not aggregated by erstwhile Indiabulls.

500+ acres in North on Sohna Road (Aravalli area); ~75 acres potentially developable (rest is forest land); no current market value estimate; land conversion process has started but is not a near-term priority given the exciting FY27 launch pipeline; company is also evaluating disposing of this land given limited FSI/value potential, suited mainly to resort/farmhouse/bungalow development; three seasons of cultivation required before farmhouse development is possible on the 75 acres.

subsections.label: Nashik SEZ monetization plan
points: Company is pursuing a debonding exercise to convert the Nashik SEZ land from SEZ to non-SEZ status, expected to take several months but targeted for completion within the fiscal year.

Post-debonding, plan is to develop industrial plotted land for small and mid-sized manufacturing companies seeking light industrial use, rather than SEZ or warehousing use, based on perceived belt demand.
Monetization depends first on a positive legal outcome with MIDC/government.

subsections.label: Lam Research sublease clarification
points: Company clarified it did not sell land to Lam Research but subleased a 25-acre portion; lease-cum-sale agreement with KIADB ends June 6, 2029; company will mutually seek an extension if Lam Research's >$1 billion R&D fab project is not completed by then, consistent with prior extension practice.

subsections.label: Blackstone shareholder debt conversion
points: Shareholder debt of ~INR1,100 crores held jointly with Blackstone is planned to be converted to equity over time, timed for when share price reaches an appropriate fair valuation to minimize dilution.

subsections.label: Legal/regulatory overhangs (resolved)
points: NCLAT, by order dated 4th May 2026, set aside the earlier NCLT admission order in the Section 7 application filed by Canara Bank, squashing CIRP proceedings entirely; NCLAT held that no deed of guarantee existed and the application was barred under Section 10A of the IBC; company exited the ASM framework and resumed normal trading on BSE and NSE effective 6th May 2026.

Karnataka High Court set aside the KIADB resumption order relating to 78 acres at Kadugodi, Bangalore (Embassy East Business Park), based on the company's undertaking to comply with lease terms and obtain KIADB's NOC prior to any third-party interest creation.
Management stated it is not aware of any other legacy legal/regulatory agreements that could similarly harm the company; the NCLAT matter caught the company by surprise but has been overcome.

subsections.label: Nashik SEZ legal issue (ongoing)
points: Legal issue with MIDC over Nashik SEZ land is ongoing; company has received a stay, with next hearing date June 12; company is also pursuing an amicable settlement with authorities to enable land development.

subsections.label: Cost inflation
points: Construction and finance costs have risen somewhat; management expects them to moderate and has a procurement strategy that delays non-crucial items without stopping construction.

Company believes it is relatively insulated versus peers because it has fully paid-up land and high gross margins with almost no JVs, unlike developers who share cost increases via JV/land-cost arrangements; real estate viewed as an inflation hedge with pricing expected to eventually catch up to cost increases from energy shocks.

subsections.label: Promoter pledge risk
points: Promoter pledge rose from ~47% to 68% purely due to share price decline (no new debt taken); expected to revert toward ~48% as share price recovers, with promoters planning to pay down pledge-related debt over 2-3 years.

subsections.label: KIADB lease/Lam Research sublease risk
points: Lease-cum-sale agreement for KIADB land (including 25 acres subleased to Lam Research) ends June 6, 2029; risk of non-extension is mitigated by mutual extension practice historically used.

points: Deliver on the launch pipeline, accelerate construction progress to drive collections, and reduce financing costs through refinancing.
Management declined to provide explicit revenue guidance for FY27/FY28, choosing to stick to presales and collections guidance only.

points: Top 3 milestones flagged by management for investors over next 12-18 months: presales, collections, and reduction in cost of debt/overall debt as receivables grow and financing shifts from the initial higher-rate 'one-and-done' raise to cheaper financing.

key_takeaways: Q4 FY '26 was the strongest quarter in our company's history. Q4 presales stood at INR2,632 crores, up 89% quarter-on-quarter. FY '26 presales increased to INR4,631 crores, up 128% year-on-year.

During FY '26, we launched projects with a cumulative GDV of approximately INR16,300 crores across 6 different launches. We achieved approximately 93% of our FY '26 presales guidance of INR5,000 crores.

On the legal and regulatory front, the company secured favourable outcomes in two significant legal and regulatory matters. The honourable NCLAT set aside the earlier NCLT admission order in the Section 7 application filed by Canara Bank, thereby squashing the CIRP proceedings in entirety... Following this, the company exited the ASM framework and resumed normal trading on both BSE and NSE effective 6th May 2026.

Our reported P&L for FY '26 reflects an accounting loss of INR872 crores at the PAT level... This is largely a function of real estate revenue recognition accounting policy, under which income is recognized only on project completion and handover.

On the FY '27 outlook... we are providing the following FY '27 guidance. A presales of INR6,000 crores from our own projects, representing a 30% year-on-year growth, along with an additional INR2,000 crores from the DM projects totalling INR8,000 crores. Collections of approximately INR3,000 crores, reflecting around 75% year-on-year growth.

New launch GDV of approximately INR19,400 crores across 11 owned projects and along 2 DM projects, Juhu and Sky Terraces in Bangalore, with the combined GDV of DM projects is approximately INR6,100 crores.

As of March FY '26, our gross institutional debt stood at approximately INR4,100 crores with cash and cash equivalents of around INR1,100 crores, resulting in net institutional debt of approximately INR3,000 crores. Our net debt to equity ratio stood at 0.3x while gross debt equity was at 0.4x.
Our priority for FY '27 are clear, deliver on the launch pipeline, accelerate construction progress to drive collections and reduce financing costs through refinancing.

quarters.summary: LT Foods delivered record Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of INR3,161 crores (up 26% YoY, 19% normalized), with EBITDA of INR363 crores and PAT of INR183 crores; management stated results are in line with annual estimates and the company is on track for the full year across all financial parameters. Key forward areas include continued India growth, US tariff normalization, Europe/UK investment phase turning profitable over coming quarters, organic business restructuring targeting double-digit growth/margin in ~1.5 years, and RTH/RTC capacity doubling over 3 years.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margins moderated from 12.1% to 11.5% primarily due to ongoing restructuring within the organic foods segment.

Gross margin fall on subsidiary basis driven by two factors: change in shipment/payment terms from CIF to C&I basis (with a related party US subsidiary), and drop in organic segment margins from 35% to 33%.
Otherwise overall gross margins improved and this is reflecting in EBITDA margins as well, with EBITDA margins improving QoQ.
US tariff reduction from 50% (last quarter) to 10% was the main reason for the QoQ improvement in GP margins, since company cannot earn margins on the tariff itself.
Last quarter had one-off exceptional events including a damage retention charge that has phased out this quarter; logistics cost as % of revenue normalized to 4.7%.

subsections.label: Other income and expense normalization
points: Other income was low this quarter versus prior quarters due to a one-off income from revaluation of investments in the previous quarter; income has now normalized.

Other expenses increased YoY from INR419 crores to INR486 crores mainly because Golden Star subsidiary is now consolidated (was not consolidated in the prior year), increasing both revenue and expense side.

subsections.label: Working capital and balance sheet
points: Meaningful improvement across key operating metrics: inventory days reduced from 221 to 187 days YoY; receivable days improved from 30 to 26 days YoY; overall working capital reduced from 195 to 170 days YoY.

Supplier financing has increased interest cost but reduced working capital via lower inventory and debtor days; management believes they are near optimum level with only 4-5 days of further legroom, not a major further reduction.
ROCE remains robust at 21.1%, demonstrating ability to generate healthy returns while continuing to invest behind future growth.
Net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 0.48x and net debt-to-equity remained comfortable at 0.15x, providing flexibility for future expansion.
