subsections.label: India franchise
points: India growing profitably for the last 3 straight years with a CAGR of 12%, with profit growing faster than revenue at a CAGR of more than 30%.
Basmati remains majority unbranded in India; every year more households shift to branded and trusted basmati, supporting long growth runway.

Growth supported by continued marketing share gain and deeper household penetration (64.4 lakh households in Q1FY27, up from an increase of 20 lakh households last year); Daawat franchise strengthening.
Leadership maintained across e-commerce and quick commerce platforms, key drivers of premiumization and consumer acquisition.

Market share reported as improved this quarter; management attributes the appearance of declining market share over recent years partly to a Nielsen methodology reset 2-3 years back, not real share loss; company remains number 1 in strong markets like Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP and commands 40-plus share on e-commerce platforms.

Focus on market creation — increasing overall basmati category size as basmati remains underpenetrated, and shifting loose basmati consumers to branded products, rather than just competing for existing branded share.
Company has gained market share in the last quarter, both in channel mix and overall growth rate.

subsections.label: International — North America
points: International business contributed 71% of consolidated revenue, with North America maintaining leadership position with 49% growth (27% normalized).
Royal and Golden Star continue to pull ahead as clear segment leaders behind consistent brand investments, innovation and execution across channels.
US basmati import share now more than 60%; growing faster than the category.
Tariff shifts created pricing volatility this year; focus is on converting dollar growth into real unit growth as pricing normalizes, while broadening reach across every price point and format.
Golden Star (100% owned, not a JV) got consolidated this year, whereas last year it was not consolidated — this affected YoY comparability of revenue and other expenses.
Jasmine rice market is 3x bigger than basmati in the US; different consumer bases for basmati vs Jasmine with no cannibalization; Jasmine growing slightly faster than basmati, both in 5-10% range.
Basmati has higher EBITDA margin due to bigger working capital cycle and higher gross margins; Jasmine has higher ROIC given shorter 120-day working capital cycle; both businesses have healthy ROCE.

subsections.label: Organic Food and Ingredients
points: Revenue declined temporarily due to remodelling of the organic business — shift from wholesale to direct-to-retailer CPG model, plus European capacity expansion, drove cost pressure in FY26.
Underlying demand fundamentals remain healthy; gradual normalization expected over coming quarters as business mix improves; long-term belief in global organic food market opportunity persists.

Restructuring involved moving from selling to wholesalers to direct sales to retailers (CPG), requiring new infrastructure, organization and capex — full ramp expected to take about 1.5 years (by FY27-28).
Two main markets for organic are Europe (biggest) followed by America; launched 'I'm Organic' under Daawat brand in e-commerce as start of organic product range expansion.
Company charges a premium in basmati and Sona Masoori organic products versus other players in the market.

subsections.label: Ready-to-Heat / Ready-to-Cook (RTH/RTC)
points: RTH/RTC portfolio delivered 13% YoY revenue growth, with 42% growth in Biryani kits; represents an important strategic growth avenue.
US RTH facility expected to become operational this quarter, which will accelerate growth in this segment in upcoming quarters.
Breakeven for RTH expected at revenue size of INR400 crores, targeted to be achieved in 2-3 years; currently on track though US RTH facility timing has somewhat affected the pace.
Aim to double RTH/RTC revenue in 3 years' time as new capacity comes online; achieved growth of 13% currently, with aspiration to reach 20-25% growth.

subsections.label: Geography commentary
points: Europe and UK are currently in investment phase; continuously investing in capacity, cost structure and right channel mix, expecting translation into profitability over coming quarters in the medium term.

Middle East is a tough and saturated market as a relatively new entrant (15 years present); despite regional disruption to shipping this year, demand held firm and e-commerce business took the number 1 category position; approaching market across multiple price points to build inroads.

Rest of world is a small market in basmati consumption terms but company enjoys leadership position in most countries, solidifying position via continuous brand investments and distribution expansion.

Middle East strategy: no plans to exit despite 15 years without major scale — remains core business; will focus on premium and mid-segment where gross margins are good, not the lower/commoditized end; mix of distributor-led and direct distribution route-to-market depending on the country; expected growth of ~15% given small base.

Geopolitical disruption impacted Middle East and Europe/UK logistics/freight costs significantly, turning geography-level margins negative this quarter; company hopes to partly pass on costs to consumers in coming quarters. Middle East freight rate spiked from $200 to $4,000, and competitive landscape did not allow full pass-through in that market.

Saudi/Middle East described as a very mature market with tough entry barriers and mostly a commoditized market segment; company pursuing a slow-and-steady approach over 15 years, choosing channels/products with better right to win.

subsections.label: Australia entry
points: Company has just opened an entity in Australia with only very small equity infused; no capex plan currently, will see how it evolves.

subsections.label: Competitive dynamics — India basmati
points: Analyst noted the rise of a 'number 3' player (Fortune plus Kohinoor) in India basmati; management focus remains on market creation — growing overall category size and converting loose basmati consumers to branded products, which is expected to support market share gains regardless of competitor moves.

Management states it has gained market share in the last quarter both in channel mix and growth rate terms, and does not have visibility into whether other players' shares moved but reiterates strength in core markets.

subsections.label: US category dynamics
points: Jasmine rice category is growing in the US with no impact from duty; basmati category also growing; company's US business growing faster than the category overall for both segments.

subsections.label: FY30 ambition
points: FY30 ambition is a step change of more than doubling revenue with expanding margins, driven by reaching consumers at every price point, building distinctive brands, expanding availability and scaling organizational backbone digitally.
Also plans to expand portfolio into adjacent categories by leveraging brand equity and distribution network.
Three broad growth areas identified: core specialty rice (across globe), organic, and RTH/RTC (bigger in USA); RTH capacity doubled with an aim to double the ready-to-eat business in 3 years.

subsections.label: Organic business remodeling
points: Organic business model changed from wholesale to CPG (direct to retailer) route to market, with associated organizational and capex investment already set up in Europe.

subsections.label: El Nino / weather and crop risk
points: Sowing season underway with El Nino risk; some areas in deficit, some in excess; majority of basmati-grown area has alternative irrigation (canal or groundwater), so historically limited impact expected, but a little impact is likely — exact crop size projection to be clearer by mid-August.
80-85% of basmati crop is supplied via alternative sources (canal and groundwater); 14-15% depends on rainfall.

No red alert currently on groundwater impacting crop; some districts (about 20% of growing area) have issues, but majority districts are not a challenge; management does not expect crop size to exceed last year's, given farmers received good prices last year, so prices expected to remain firm.

If crop is lower, inflation could follow; company plans to pass on inflation to consumers as it has historically been able to do, and does not expect impact on demand given basmati's premium/specialty positioning.
Basmati EBITDA margin historically around 13-14%, with possible plus/minus 1% swing if crop/inflation issues occur.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and freight disruption
points: Geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and freight volatility cited as challenging operating environment factors for the quarter.

Middle East and Europe/UK logistics costs surged due to regional disruption to shipping, driving negative geography-level margins this quarter; Middle East freight rate rose from $200 to $4,000; competitive landscape prevented full cost pass-through in that market.
Company hopes to partly pass on elevated logistics costs to consumers in coming quarters.

subsections.label: US tariff uncertainty
points: Standing 10% US tariff rate expired on 24th July but has continued at the same 10% rate post-expiry.
Company had a 50% tariff impact in the prior quarter, since reduced to 10%; this was the main driver of gross margin recovery in the current quarter (cannot earn margin on tariff itself).

Organic exports to US (rice and oilseeds) also carry a 10% duty; company is not currently exporting soya to USA, avoiding the separate high soya CVD case (previously reduced from over 300% to 75%), and is pursuing further reduction of remaining balance through court, hopeful of a win.
Company is eligible for refund of duties from the US court ruling; partial refund received in Q1 but no income has been booked yet as discussions with customers are ongoing.

subsections.label: Organic segment margin pressure
points: FY26 organic business saw cost pressure from the shift in business model from wholesale to CPG and from European capacity expansion, pressuring margins temporarily.

key_figures.label: Organic business full recovery target year

subsections.label: Full-year outlook
points: Q1FY27 results are in line with annual estimates; company is on track for the full year across all financial parameters.
Organic business expected to return to double-digit growth and double-digit margin in coming quarters, fully back by FY27-28 (about 1.5 years from now).
RTH breakeven expected at INR400 crores revenue scale, to be achieved in 2-3 years; RTH/RTC revenue aimed to double in 3 years given new capacity coming online.
India FY30 ambition: more than double revenue with expanding margins.
Europe/UK investments expected to translate into profitability over coming quarters in the medium term.
Basmati margin expected to remain around historical 13-14% EBITDA range, with plus/minus 1% variability depending on crop/inflation outcomes.
Medium-term segment growth guidance: basmati segment 10-12%, RTH segment 15-20%, organic segment 10-12%, with organic business targeting INR70-80 crores EBITDA and 7-8% EBITDA margin by end of FY27.
Middle East expected to grow ~15% going forward given small base.

guidance_ledger.statement: Q1FY27 results are in line with our annual estimates, and we are on track for the full year across all financial parameters.
We are expecting that end of the year, for example, this organic business will be around INR70 crores to INR80 crores of EBITDA.
Right now [organic EBITDA margin] is 4% will be in the range of 7% to 8% [by end of year], and going forward, it will come back to the double-digit EBITDA.
We are confident that the organic business, both in terms of growth and margin will be double digit in the coming quarters... we are saying 1.5 year by year '27-'28, it will be fully back.
Breakeven [for RTH] will be coming at a revenue size of INR400 crores... It will take 2 to 3 years' time for achieving that number. We are on track.
In 3 years' time, we are aiming to make our ready-to-eat business double... in 3 years' time, we wanted to double the revenue of RTH.
The basmati will grow in 10%, 12%.
The RTH because it's a small base, that will grow in 15%, 20%.
Organic will be in the range of 10%, 12%. That's the guidance.
The margin can be historically what we have seen is that basmati is around 13%, 14% EBITDA margin. So there can be a plus/minus 1% if things happen.
The growth will be in the range of 15% as the base is small, but we will keep growing in the Middle East.
Our FY'30 ambition is a step change of more than doubling the revenue with expanding margins.
We expect these investments to translate into the profitability over the coming quarters in the medium term.
Can we achieve 20%-25% growth? Yes. That's what we said that the new capacity is going to start in the coming time.
We hope we are at the optimum level of the supplier funding of these kinds. So yes, some legroom of 4-5 days might be there, but not a major one from this current level.

risk_register.risk: El Nino / weather impact on basmati crop and yield
risk_register.note: Majority of basmati-growing area has alternative irrigation (canal/groundwater), limiting historical impact; some impact expected but exact crop size unclear until mid-August; ~20% of growing districts have issues; if crop is lower, inflation could follow, though company expects to pass this on to consumers.

Impacted Middle East and Europe/UK logistics costs heavily, turning geography margins negative this quarter; Middle East freight rate rose from $200 to $4,000; competitive landscape prevented full pass-through.
Tariff reduced from 50% to 10% versus prior quarter, aiding margin recovery; standing 10% rate continued post its July 24 expiry; company confident of passing tariffs to consumers.
FY26 cost pressure from shift from wholesale to CPG model and European capacity expansion; margins temporarily lower (EBITDA margin at 4% in Q1FY27) but expected to normalize over ~1.5 years.

risk_register.risk: Middle East market saturation and competitive intensity
risk_register.note: Tough, saturated, mature and commoditized market with high entry barriers; slow-and-steady approach after 15 years of presence; no plan to exit.

risk_register.risk: India basmati competitive intensity (new entrant, e.g., Fortune/Kohinoor)
risk_register.note: Management focus is on market creation/converting unbranded to branded consumers rather than direct share battles; states share gained this quarter.
Prior duty reduced from over 300% to 75%; balance still contested in court, company hopeful of a win; company no longer exports soya to USA.

themes.label: Branded basmati premiumization/market creation
themes.note: India growth driven by shifting loose basmati consumers to branded, trusted basmati amid still-majority-unbranded market.

themes.label: US tariff headwind normalization
themes.note: US tariff reduced from 50% to 10% aiding margin recovery, though tariff volatility and litigation on organic/soya duties continue.

themes.label: Organic business restructuring
themes.note: Shift from wholesale to CPG model and European capacity expansion pressured organic margins to 4% EBITDA, with double-digit recovery targeted in ~1.5 years.

themes.label: Geopolitical/freight disruption
themes.note: Middle East and Europe/UK logistics costs spiked (Middle East freight from $200 to $4,000), pressuring geography-level margins.

themes.label: RTH/RTC capacity expansion
themes.note: US RTH facility going operational this quarter to accelerate growth; targeting revenue doubling in 3 years and breakeven at INR400 crores revenue.

themes.label: El Nino / monsoon crop risk
themes.note: Majority of basmati area has alternative irrigation limiting impact, but some districts affected; clarity expected by mid-August, with potential inflation pass-through if crop is short.

themes.label: Working capital efficiency
themes.note: Inventory, receivable and overall working capital days all improved YoY, supporting ROCE of 21.1% and comfortable leverage.

key_takeaways: LT Foods has delivered another strong quarter, achieving 26.4% year-on-year growth despite a challenging operating environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and freight volatility.

India is a proven growth engine still in its early innings as there is a huge potential lies in front of us. The U.S. is genuinely category leader working through near-term tariff headwinds. Europe and the U.K. are in the investment phase with strong long-term potential.

The Middle East is a tough market wherein we are building inroads. Organic is a long-term bet where we have reset course and all the geographies and business segments are moving forward with full rigor.

During Q1FY27, the consolidated revenue on a year-on-year basis grew by 26%. On a normalized basis, it grew by 19%, and the revenue stood at INR3,161 crores, driven by strong demand across our key geographies and sustained momentum in our branded portfolio.
Profitability remained healthy. However, the EBITDA margins moderated from 11.5% to 12.1% primarily due to ongoing restructuring within the organic foods segment.

Our core basmati and specialty rice business continued to perform exceptionally well, delivering revenue growth of 34% year-on-year basis to INR2,845 crores... this segment EBITDA margin stood at stable 13%.
In India, the revenue grew by 23% on a year-on-year basis... Our market share reached to 23.1%, while our household penetration increased to 64.4 lakh households.
International business also continued its growth momentum and contributed 71% of our consolidated revenue, with North America maintaining the leadership position with 49% growth.
In Organic Food and Ingredient business witnessed a temporary decline in the revenue due to remodelling of the organic business. The revenue stood at INR254 crores with EBITDA margin at 4%.
Importantly, these results are in line with our annual estimates, and we are on track for the full year across all financial parameters.
pressing_questions: I've been looking at your market share since the last 2 years in India, and it has consistently gone down from 30% to 10% to now 33%. In fact, FY26 was 23.7%, and it's now 23.1%. So any reason why this is going down? Is it because of the competitive intensity rising because of that third player coming in as someone had mentioned before on the call? Or is it something else?

We would probably have scratched just about 2% to 3% of this market. So what is our strategy in the next maybe 5 to 10 years to further make inroads here? ... Or at some point, is there a thought to maybe exiting or abandoning because we have not made further inroads even after 15 years?

So on a Q-on-Q basis, our gross and EBITDA margins have improved. So despite the elevated freight cost, we are showing an improvement in the gross margins. So what has been the major driver? And can you just quantify that what as a percentage of sales, the freight cost got elevated?
Even though there is revenue growth [in RTH/RTC], why EBITDA margin is declining? Is there any change in the target to reach for the breakeven to happen?

quarters.summary: Management indicated margins should be viewed on a full-year basis rather than quarter-to-quarter, with cost-of-funds benefits (borrowing mix, CASA, deposit repricing) expected to play out gradually over the medium term; loan growth is expected to stay healthy across corporate/wholesale (~18%), MSME/business banking (22.3%), and retail (wheels, unsecured, mortgages), aided by the FCNR window and ECLGS 5.0, while profit growth is expected to be at or above balance sheet growth over the longer term and CASA/retail deposit mix improvement is targeted over a 2-3 year horizon.

subsections.label: Margin drivers - cost of funds
points: Cost of funds is the biggest margin lever; potential 40-50 bps change versus historical norms/industry, but change is gradual, not sudden.

System liquidity needs to stabilize (average 2.08 trillion vs peak 5.5 trillion and trough -0.43 trillion in recent quarter) for rates to stabilize; policy measures like FCNR/swap window aim to reduce this volatility.
Retail deposit costs across the industry (including HDFC Bank) have been steady/circumspect, but non-retail deposit costs remain elevated.
Borrowing mix at 11% is not expected to settle quickly at 8-9%; industry benchmark is ~5-6%; expected to reduce via natural maturity and balance sheet growth reducing reliance on borrowings.
CASA mix has been actively pursued; despite FY26 CASA-linked deposit growth of 9.5-10%, market share was still gained; this remains a longer-term journey, not a quarter-to-quarter shift.

subsections.label: Margin drivers - asset mix
points: Asset yield/margins should be assessed on a full-year basis, not quarter-to-quarter, due to timing differences in loan booking through the year.
Retail mix at 52% is targeted to move back toward historical ~60% level, mirroring India's consumption share of GDP, as a long-term margin contributor.
This quarter saw some mix change toward more non-retail shorter-term assets; cost of funds moderation elements are being tactically managed.

subsections.label: Profit growth vs balance sheet growth
points: Reported PAT growth of 5% YoY reflects high base from one-timers last year (HDB gains, floating provision/counter-cyclical buffer, contingent provision); adjusted growth was 9.8%.
9.8% adjusted profit growth still trails balance sheet growth (13-14%); management reiterated long-term goal for profit growth to be at or above balance sheet growth, assessed on a full-year basis.

subsections.label: CASA and deposit mix
points: CASA ratio decline attributed to industry-wide slowdown in household deposit growth (one of lowest across deposit categories per RBI data) and bank's faster time deposit growth needed to fund higher balance sheet growth appetite.

Wholesale/non-retail deposit mix rose to 20% this quarter from 17%, reflecting change in composition; management expects this to normalize to more stable long-term levels (as seen over past decade) rather than be a sustained trend.
Endeavor is to move CASA back toward pre-merger/near-merger levels (~38% post-merger, 40% pre-merger).
Approach to grow CASA is via increasing unit customer count (distribution reach, customer additions) rather than counting on household deposit growth acceleration from single digits to ~15%.
Time deposit penetration is low (only 14% of customers have TDs with the bank), representing a large deepening opportunity alongside CASA growth - 'it's not this or that, it's both.'

subsections.label: Provision coverage / ECL transition
points: Headline PCR has declined from 71% (2019) to 66% currently; largely explained by higher proportion of agriculture book (secured) in the mix - ex-agri PCR is comparable (71% then vs 70% now).

Shorter-term PCR differences are driven by secured-unsecured mix: unsecured PCR is mid-70s or higher, secured is lower; unsecured/retail book growth (cards, personal loans) has been modest over past two years even as disbursements grow in healthy double digits.
PCR is formulaic based on composition of book, not discretionary.
Existing reserving process/methodology assessed as adequate for ECL transition (effective April 1, 2027); Stage 3 (NPA-equivalent) coverage adequate.

ECL floors will increase required provisioning versus current standard asset provision of ~40 bps (unsecured stage 1 floor of 1%, stage 2 floor of 5%), but these enhancements are seen as adequately covered by existing contingent provisions and others.
Post-transition, ongoing credit cost impact expected to be some increase but 'nothing material.'

subsections.label: Borrowings/bonds maturity profile
points: Annual report shows maturity profile of borrowings; INR 40,000-50,000 crores maturing over next couple of years.

Rate differential exists: maturing borrowings cost a little more than 7%, versus retail TD at ~6%, offering 100-125 bps benefit if borrowings are replaced with time deposits (or a mix of time and CASA).

subsections.label: Credit card metrics
points: Credit cards book grew 2.3% this year while credit card spends grew 13%, indicating spending growth outpacing receivables growth.
Total customer relationships stand at 101-102 million, with cost-to-assets ratio referenced at 1.9%.

key_figures.label: Borrowing mix expected settling range (industry benchmark)

subsections.label: Growth across segments
points: Corporate/wholesale segment growth of 18% continues the trajectory seen in the previous quarter.
MSME segment showing robust growth; business banking (largest MSME component) grew 22.3% this year, topping even March quarter performance despite June typically being a softer quarter.
Participation in ECLGS 5.0 scheme drove INR 14,000 crores in disbursements as of June 30, described as amongst the highest among participating banks due to spread of customers and portfolio quality.
Core retail segment saw strong YoY growth in wheels business disbursements, unsecured business (personal loans/business loans) at ~20% YoY, and mortgages disbursement growth of ~14% YoY.
New retail product lines - gold loans and micro loans (dukandar lending) - are smaller parts of the retail basket currently but growing well and contributing to diversification within retail.

Retail loan growth has been range-bound at 7-8% and not yet showing pickup, per analyst observation; management expects wheels, unsecured, and mortgage disbursement traction to translate into growth pickup over several quarters.

subsections.label: Branch productivity and vintage
points: About 40% of branches (of a 9,700 branch network) are less than 5 years old, reflecting the significant branch addition undertaken in FY22-23.

Per-branch productivity has risen to INR 330 crores currently from INR 266 crores in FY23 and less than INR 200 crores further back, indicating early-vintage branches are progressing similarly to legacy vintages as they mature (0-5, 5-10, 10-15 year vintage curve).
Aggregate per-branch productivity of INR 330 crores considered extremely productive and best-in-class in the industry.
Branches are a key channel for deposits as well as retail assets and SME loans; wholesale/top corporate/mid-corporate loans are centrally managed through relationships rather than branch-level.

subsections.label: Savings account (SA) market share and quality acquisition
points: Incremental SA market share gains have flatlined despite branch additions; management attributes this partly to industrywide slowdown in household deposit growth (lowest among deposit categories per RBI data).
Approach to SA growth centers on increasing unit customer count via distribution and customer addition rather than relying on household deposit growth acceleration.

Bank tightened acquisition quality over FY24-26 using algorithms/rule engines to counter a rise in mule accounts/fraudulent activity industry-wide, which slowed new account acquisition during this period as a deliberate correction.
Management expects a step-up in acquisition volumes (unit economics) going forward with quality guardrails in place, anticipating reasonably healthy SA growth over a 1-3 year period.

subsections.label: AI and digital initiatives
points: Bank is reimagining digital journeys and analytics to drive new levels of adoption, expected to bring efficiencies in coming quarters.
Bank described itself as 'on the cusp of harnessing GenAI technologies' across processes, with lighthouse programs expected to go into production during the course of the year.
Security highlighted as a critical strategic focus, with AI being leveraged to augment defence/security mechanisms.
Technology investment (including security and AI) will continue even as distribution investment is somewhat muted, reflecting front-loaded investment in prior years.

key_figures.label: FCNR mobilization in 2014 - pace pickup timing

subsections.label: Leadership transition
points: New part-time Chairman Rajiv Kumar has been appointed, following interim chairmanship by Keki Mistry; management indicated this brings stability and minimizes uncertainties.
Board (GNRC) is actively working on appointing an additional Whole-Time Director (ED); conclusion and announcement expected in a short time period, no specific date given.

CEO reappointment process is described as 'work in progress' with the GNRC and Board fully seized of the matter; necessary announcements to follow once concluded - no confirmation of RBI application status was given.

subsections.label: Strategic focus areas
points: Management outlined four key strategic pillars: (1) customer focus to the level of obsession, leveraging AI in journeys; (2) reducing turnaround time for product/service delivery through daily operating rhythm; (3) releasing capacity at customer-facing end to increase engagement and business momentum; (4) driving cost-to-earnings efficiencies through reduced turnaround times.
Strategy aims to balance growth and efficiency, with potential CASA/margin benefits as a byproduct ('a bonus') rather than the primary driver.

Focus is also on cross-sell/wallet-share gains within existing customer base via best-in-class experience, alongside new-to-bank acquisition, across retail, MSME, and eventually wholesale/capital markets segments.

Investment phase (distribution, technology) over the past five years is now shifting to a 'harnessing' phase; distribution investment to be slightly muted going forward while technology (security, AI) investment continues.
Returns/efficiencies from past investments (branch distribution, technology) expected to play out over the next two to three years, supporting growth-efficiency balance.

subsections.label: External/macro risks
points: Weather-related disruptions such as El Nino flagged as a risk; full impact expected to play out in Q3 of the financial year.
Geopolitical situation in West Asia flagged as a risk factor, though the country/economy is seen as having weathered it reasonably well thus far.

Competition intensity described as very high, particularly on the corporate side where spreads remain thin; bank stated it is being selective and pursuing holistic primary relationship engagement instead of purely price-based competition.
Non-retail deposit rates remain elevated, unlike granular retail deposit rates which have been reasonably stable.

subsections.label: Operational/franchise risks (past period)
points: Company navigated 'certain challenges over the last four months,' described as a 'very tough period' for the institution (context: governance/leadership transition period).
Industry-wide rise in fraudulent/mule accounts over FY24-26 required tightened acquisition guardrails, which had a near-term dampening effect on new customer acquisition.

subsections.label: Forward outlook themes
points: Margins to be assessed on full-year basis; cost of funds benefits expected to play out in annual and strategic review plans but not in a hurry.
Borrowing mix expected to decline toward industry levels (~5-6%) over time via natural maturity and balance sheet growth, not expected to settle quickly at 8-9%.
Retail asset mix targeted to move back toward ~60% over time from current 52%, mirroring India's consumption share of GDP.

CASA ratio endeavor is to move back toward pre-merger/near-merger levels (~38-40%), via increasing customer units rather than relying on household deposit growth acceleration; expected over medium to long term (next 2-3 years), current quarter's 20% wholesale mix expected to normalize.
Profit growth targeted to be at or above balance sheet growth in the longer term (assessed on full-year, not quarterly basis).

FCNR mobilization: bank aims for 'a very handsome' and 'significant market share' in FCNR deposits, benchmarked to its historically strong share during the 2014 FCNR(B) window, though no specific number was committed; milestones expected in July-September.

Loan growth: management sees resilience and credit demand holding across wholesale, MSME, and retail segments; corporate/mid-market and retail expected to continue driving growth in coming quarters, though full El Nino impact yet to play out (expected Q3).
ECL transition (effective April 1, 2027) expected to be adequately reserved for; post-transition ongoing credit cost impact expected to be some increase but 'nothing material.'
Technology/security investment to continue; distribution investment to be comparatively muted; returns/efficiencies from past investment expected to play out over next 2-3 years.

guidance_ledger.statement: We see credit demand holding and resilience in the economy across wholesale, MSME and retail segments; well positioned across most business segments, though full El Nino impact yet to play out in Q3

key_takeaways: Deposit growth continues to be relatively better than historical Q1 trends; the bank continues to gain market share both on an incremental and stock basis.
Advances have done very well over the last three-four quarters and that trajectory continues; the bank is 'on the verge of pressing the pedal' on advances growth.
Corporate and wholesale segment grew at about 18%, MSME/business banking grew at 22.3%, and ECLGS 5.0 disbursements reached close to INR 14,000 crores as of June 30.

PAT growth was reported at 5% YoY but adjusted for one-timers (HDB gains, floating/contingent provisions) was 9.8%; management expects profit growth to be at or above balance sheet growth over the longer term.

CASA ratio has declined, with wholesale deposit mix rising to 20% from 17%; management attributes this to industry-wide household deposit growth slowdown and the bank's need to fund higher balance sheet growth via time deposits; endeavor is to move back toward pre-merger CASA levels of ~38-40% over the medium to long term.

FCNR mobilization is a key opportunity; bank spent much of June on documentation/approvals and expects milestones in July-September, aiming for a significant market share as it achieved in 2014-15, though no specific number was committed.

New Chairman Rajiv Kumar has been appointed, following interim chairmanship by Keki Mistry, bringing a sense of stability; additional Whole-Time Director appointment and CEO reappointment process remain work in progress with the Board.

Provision coverage ratio (66% headline, down from 71% in 2019) is explained largely by a higher proportion of agriculture (secured) book; ex-agri PCR is comparable (70% vs 71%); ECL transition effective April 2027 is expected to be adequately reserved with no material ongoing credit cost impact.

quarters.summary: Management expects loan growth momentum to continue into FY27, supported by corporate demand (electronics, food processing, auto/auto ancillaries, renewables, semiconductors, acquisition/project finance) and stepped-up retail growth (wheels, personal loans, business loans, mortgages), though tempered by geopolitical uncertainty expected to last a couple of months. NIM is expected to remain range-bound near-term with focus shifting to ROA as the key metric, supported by residual TD repricing, cost efficiencies and technology-led operating leverage; deposit growth is expected to continue with increasing granularity and core retail share.

subsections.label: NIM and returns
points: Yield on assets had faster transmission than deposits on a full year basis, leading to a NIM drop.
Despite NIM drop, ROA remained stable at 1.9% due to cost efficiencies and lower credit costs from quality growth.

Rate cycle: policy rate cuts of 125 bps not anticipated a year ago; ~70% of loans are floating rate with immediate transmission, while deposit repricing (via time deposits) has only captured 40-50 bps of the asset repricing so far, hence pressure on NIM.

Time deposit growth (15.5% YoY) outpaced total deposit growth (14.4%), reflecting higher propensity toward relatively higher-priced time deposits versus CASA, which along with borrowings mix shift explains part of NIM stickiness.
Geopolitical uncertainty has paused the rate cycle; securities market indications suggest rates may be rising again, adding uncertainty to NIM trajectory going forward.

Management stated that if borrowings decline structurally (e.g., to 6-7% of liabilities) with all else equal, NIM would improve significantly, and that borrowings mix change is a favorable lever not yet fully unlocked.

Management now internally prioritizes ROA over NIM as the key performance metric, since ROA also captures cost and credit efficiencies and culminates in EPS growth; PPOP considered an intermediate metric that doesn't fully capture returns since higher risk can boost PPOP but get given away in credit costs below it.
NIM is expected to remain range-bound; management will lean on efficiency levers (operating and credit side) to keep returns stable when NIM is in a small range.

subsections.label: Cost efficiency and operating leverage
points: Full year cost growth of ~6.5-7% is lower than top-line growth, driving cost-to-income improvement.
Cost-to-assets ratio of ~1.9% considered best-in-class, but management sees further opportunity from technology implementations.
Sizable multi-year technology investments (nearly $1bn) are expected to translate into operating leverage and enhanced ROA over the next 1-3 years as they are implemented across the organization.

subsections.label: Deposit granularity and mix
points: Focus on garnering more granular time deposits; less than INR 3 crore deposit bucket rose from 31% to 47% of net incremental deposit accretion YoY, reflecting a push toward sustainable, less volatile deposits.

~15% of total deposits (linked to corporate and capital markets relationships) remain volatile/high-frequency in nature, moving out and returning around month/quarter ends, though full-year net incremental mobilization in this segment is being managed upward.
Retail deposits remain steady at 80-85% of total bank deposits historically.
Deposit gathering was concentrated in the last month of the quarter (Feb-March) versus January, which remained tight; market liquidity turned easier later in the quarter, aiding accretion.

Quarter's deposit accretion driven by system liquidity, expanded customer base/distribution, and stronger corporate relationships (13% corporate loan growth) generating a higher share of wallet from corporate clients.

subsections.label: Investment yield and treasury
points: Investment yields have declined for the last two quarters due to maturing book being replaced by new book, and duration positioning changes by treasury across rate cycles; new securities added at current higher yields are a small fraction of the overall book and take time to move overall book yield.

No material negative treasury/FX impact this quarter despite yield movements; treasury/FX income growth was modest due to lower FX trading volumes and lower spreads amid geopolitical risk, along with some impact from unwinding.

subsections.label: Cost of funds and repricing outlook
points: Cost of funds at ~4.4%, down ~50 bps YoY; further residual repricing benefit expected as time deposits (which take 5-6 quarters to fully reprice) continue to mature, all else being equal.

Time deposit rates in the market have not changed for at least 4 months; bank is priced in line with competition; geopolitical developments in March have hardened rates again, adding uncertainty to further repricing benefit.

subsections.label: Third-party distribution fee income
points: Third-party product fee revenue growth of only ~3.5% for the full year, lagging retail asset and liability fee growth.

Slowdown attributed to modest volume growth (following a spike entering Q4 FY25) and an unfavorable shift in product mix affecting realized commission/spreads (e.g., lower life insurance sales), rather than a structural change; RM engagement level cited as a factor, though management said there is nothing specific to read into it.
Penetration of third-party products in the customer base remains only mid-single-digit, implying a large opportunity space.

subsections.label: Corporate growth drivers
points: Corporate growth seen sustaining, driven by demand across sectors: electronics, food processing, auto, auto ancillaries, renewable sector, and semiconductors.
New opportunities opening up in acquisition financing, in addition to existing project finance and supply chain financing.
Growth may be tempered by geopolitical fallout, expected to last no more than a couple of months into the financial year.

subsections.label: Retail growth drivers
points: Retail growth has stepped up from last year, with improvement visible over the last 3 quarters across wheels business, personal loans, and business loans.
Mortgage book demand has held consistent and performed well.

Levers for retail acceleration include expanded physical distribution (mortgages now from ~7,800-8,000 locations vs 6,800 earlier), improved digital channel utilization (10-second loans in auto and personal loans), higher customer acquisition, and salary account foray creating a pre-approved base for cross-sell without compromising asset quality.
Disbursals have increased quarter-on-quarter across retail products; bank believes it is among top two in mortgage disbursements with hardly a gap versus market leader.
Auto loan business continues to lead the market with the largest OEM and dealer engagement, acting as feeder for retail loans.
New gold loan business launched over the last year has built a good quality book and is expected to continue contributing.
MSME/business banking growth expected to continue in the 18-20/21% range depending on economic developments; bank ranks #1 nationally in MSME, #1 in 15 of 28 states, and top-2 in 25 of 28 states.

subsections.label: Mortgage merger synergies (HDFC Ltd merger)
points: Liability penetration among inherited e-HDFC home loan customers rose from 36% at merger to ~50% of stock within 2.5 years, net of attritions and acquisitions.
98% of all home loans disbursed now come with a liability account opened with the bank.
60-65% of the liability-linked home loan stock pays EMI through their own account with the bank, reflecting value accretion and risk benefits of the combined relationship.
CASA balances from the inherited book grew from INR 50,000 crores at merger to INR 86,000 crores currently.
Average balances of customers who keep liability relationship along with home loan are 2x to 2.25x higher than standard average balances otherwise seen.

Cross-sell 'thali' includes credit cards, home insurance, wealth accounts (SmartWealth), and digital properties (PayZapp wallet/gateway); 23% of home loan customers on stock now have active credit cards.
Bank has the lowest NPA percentage in the industry on a home loan book of comparable size, as per management's understanding.

subsections.label: Digital front-end investment
points: Major investment directed toward improving digital front-end customer experience: upgraded interfaces, simplified acquisition and service journeys, modernized digital platforms.
Launched new net-banking and mobile-banking platforms during the year, plus a payment platform launched about two years ago, all operating at population scale.

Mobile app security features include OTP-less authentication, an enhanced-security 'lock' feature, and a full-stack UPI-enabled wallet called the Zapp account, positioned as one of the most secure offerings in the country.

subsections.label: Intelligence layer and AI platform
points: Building an AI-ready 'intelligence layer' bringing automation and analytics to core operations, via decoupled front-end/back-end architecture through a modern API gateway and orchestration layer, supporting agent-driven AI models.

Built a robust data foundation with a customer-level, enterprise-level single source of truth; went live with Lakehouse Architecture — a centralized, scalable data lake with reusable, enriched data marts.

Built an in-house unified AI platform spanning the organization, enabling rapid deployment of AI agents without custom interfaces between systems; brings together enterprise search, document extraction, voice-based agents, and a full AI development lifecycle.

Platform supports multi-foundational and open models, includes a unified evaluation model for governance, compliance, and security, with an independent risk team unit providing a second-line safeguard.
Key AI platform components: Model Context Protocol, Agentic Studio, and Agentic Mesh — positioning the bank among a small group of Indian and global banks with such advanced in-house capabilities.
5 AI use cases already in production and 14 more in development, aimed at improving turnaround times, first-time-right outcomes, and freeing mid/back-office capacity for customer-facing roles.
Technology leadership expected to be a key driver enhancing return on assets over the next 1-3 years.

An NCDRC order dated March 23 highlighted that the complainants (in the Dubai branch matter) are not retail in nature and are not uninformed investors, and had clear intent to pursue high-yield, high-risk investment products; management stated there is nothing incremental beyond this.

Lower FX trading volumes and spreads this quarter attributed to various risks in foreign exchange trade amid geopolitical uncertainty, along with impact of some unwinding.

System credit growth running ahead of nominal GDP-based expectations (13.5-13.9% actual vs 10.5-11.5% planning assumption) flagged as a factor requiring calibrated, responsible growth to avoid future risk.

key_takeaways: We had estimated the system credit growth to be around 10.5% to 11.5%. We did 12%, up from 5.5% last year.
Deposit growth rate at 14.4% continues to grow faster than the credit growth, which is what we've always been doing. The growth rate is better than the system growth rate yet again.
Net income growth clocked at 11%, similar to the last financial year, whilst EPS growth of 10% versus 3% last year.

The yield on assets had a faster transmission as against deposits on a full year basis, leading to a NIM drop. Despite the drop in NIMs, the return on assets continue to be stable at 1.9% due to cost efficiencies with cost-to-income declining from 40.5% to 39.5% on a core basis and focus on quality growth reflecting in lower credit costs.
The distribution nearly doubled to 9,700 branches. The number of customers nearly doubled to 100 million customers. Our tech investments more than quadrupled to around $1 billion.

We have a strong capital position at 19.7%. Our asset quality is extremely healthy at 1.15% gross NPAs. The bank has created a large provisioning buffer of almost 125 basis points to absorb any shocks in the future.

The loan deposit ratio is not a constraint. We have demonstrated our ability to gain market share on deposits every year, almost around 30 to 50 basis points over the last 5 years. Hence, it's no longer a binding constraint.
In the less than 3 crores retail liabilities, we have moved up from 31% of the net total accretion to about 47% of the total net deposit accretion for the year.
We already have 5 use cases in production and 14 more in development, improving turnaround times, first-time right outcomes, and freeing mid-office and back-office capacity for customer-facing roles.
pressing_questions: Firstly, on the deposits. So how do you look at the deposit market share? We have done very well in this quarter but if I look at it in context of how the system itself has done, we have seen a very sharp pickup in the deposit accretion for the system overall. So how do you kind of look at the market share that HDFC Bank has been able to garner this quarter in context of system number? And any color if you can also share on what has driven this huge surge in the business numbers over the last fortnight?

So firstly, again, touching upon on the growth side. So, we indicated like we will try to grow in line with the industry average, but we are seeing industry average being upwards of 15%, we are still at 12%. So we have been below it. And next year, would we retain the guidance of growing above the industry average or would we say like we will still grow in line with the industry average because industry average itself has picked up to a very large extent? And on the deposits, how much of this is transitory in nature? And how much of this it can sustain?

My first question, Srini, is more on the guidance. I think if I heard you right, you said LDR is no longer kind of relevant or a constraint. And I also heard you saying that loan growth, you would rather focus on improving momentum rather than benchmarking the system? So is there one metric that you use internally to assess performance, which kind of captures some of these pushes and pulls you have on the different metrics that would also be helpful, I guess, for investors to track performance?

The borrowings have come off almost 11% year-on-year, but the NIM trajectory is broadly similar with what some of your peers have reported. So is that something you expected a year back, meaning borrowings come off, but NIM doesn't really get impacted or has something changed in that front? And more importantly, will a reduction in borrowings have a meaningful impact on NIM going forward?
So this number [yield on investments] is down about 60 basis points in the last two quarters and the overall yields have gone up. So why is the interest income on investment yields going down?

So I had a question on the third-party distribution fee. Actually, if I look at it on a full year basis, the growth has been hardly 3.5%. And this is lagging the overall customer growth... What is really leading to this? Is it just a slowdown or cross-sell has become more difficult or refocusing on some products?

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was a strong quarter for Gujarat Energy Limited (post-merger integrated entity) with revenue growth of 63% YoY, EBITDA growth of 65% YoY and PAT growth of 78% YoY. Management guided for continued gas trading profitability of INR1,100 crores (conservative, unchanged from prior guidance), CGD EBITDA margin guidance of Rs5.5-6.5/scm reiterated, CGD capex guidance of ~INR1,000 crores reiterated, and long-term Morbi gas demand expected to settle at a floor of 1.8-2 mmscmd amid propane price competition. Management flagged continuing geopolitical/Middle East volatility as a headwind to sourcing and pricing, while highlighting new long-term LNG contracts (Total, Uniper, Qatar) targeted to start from 2028, and plans for a company-owned propane import/storage facility near Morbi.

subsections.label: Cash utilization plan
points: Company has cash of around INR7,200 crores; capex plan of ~INR1,000 crores is for the CGD business.
Rest of the cash is planned for strengthening the present business (CNG and pipelines) and for diversification strategy in the energy business.
A concrete deployment plan for the surplus cash is expected to be presented to investors by Q3.

subsections.label: Dividend policy
points: Company follows Government of Gujarat's guidelines with respect to dividends; a dividend of close to INR835 crores was given last quarter.
Plans for better-return investments are being worked on; details expected to be shared with investors by Q3.

subsections.label: Tax refund process
points: Company is in the process of filing revised tax returns for merger-related unabsorbed losses/tax adjustments for FY24-25 and FY25-26.
Refunds expected to take at least a year to materialize; expected quantum confirmed at approximately INR900 crores.

subsections.label: Intersegment transfer pricing
points: Post-merger, internal transfer pricing between Gas Trading and CGD segments now has flexibility since the arm's length concept required for two separate companies no longer applies internally.
Sourcing and pricing between segments can now differ; there is still a markup on CGD transfers from the trading segment.
The reported Gas Trading segment EBIT reflects the entire volume (12.22 mmscmd), including the 8.9 mmscmd transferred internally to CGD, not just the 3.32 mmscmd external sales.

subsections.label: CGD margin drivers
points: CGD EBITDA margin of 5.18 Rs/scm in Q1 FY27 reflects margin being spread over a bigger volume base.
Management does not break down margin performance by individual segment/region (e.g., Morbi vs non-Morbi) within CGD; margin is assessed at the portfolio level.

subsections.label: Gas Trading business
points: During the quarter, global energy markets witnessed significant disruption due to geopolitical developments and supply-side constraints.
Company leveraged robust sourcing capabilities, extensive supplier network and deep market expertise to secure critical LNG volumes for customers despite unprecedented circumstances.

Strong Gas Trading EBT growth reflects favorable timing of gas sourcing relative to margins and long-term agreements linked to dated Brent pricing on an aging basis, giving a slight advantage on product offered to market.
Term contracts (e.g., fertilizer) are structured on Brent, three-months pricing basis; most power consumers are on spot; sourcing mix is a blend of Brent and Henry Hub, plus APM gas for CGD.

Domestic gas (HPHT) margins are fixed; fertilizer marketing margin is fixed at close to 20 (units not specified); in other segments (industrial etc.), marketing margin depends on market conditions at the time.
Company does not expect any negative/reversal of gains in subsequent quarters despite a strong Q1.

New long-term LNG contracts signed with Total, Uniper and Qatar; company is in the market for two more contracts; long-term sourcing timeline shifted due to geopolitical shocks (originally targeted 2026/27, now targeting 2028 start).
Long-term contracts are generally sold on a back-to-back basis (including some Henry Hub volumes back-to-back); not all volumes kept exposed to spot.

subsections.label: CNG segment
points: CNG infrastructure expanded to 844 stations; 6 new stations added and 9 upgraded during the quarter.
Plan to add more than 75 new CNG stations and upgrade approximately 70 CNG stations during the current financial year.
CNG remains an attractive fuel option, approximately 46% cheaper than petrol and 25% cheaper than diesel based on current pricing.
Company confident of sustaining 12-13% CNG growth for the next couple of years, supported by continued station additions.
CNG volume of 3.76 mmscmd reflects new benchmark for the company.

subsections.label: PNG Domestic segment
points: Healthy customer additions continue; PNG penetration drive gained momentum due to government policy measures to boost PNG connections amid constrained LPG supplies caused by Middle East conflict.

GEL undertook aggressive marketing campaigns across digital and print media, mobilized additional contractors for new connections, and prioritized outreach to essential category customers (hospitals, community kitchens, etc.).
Additions in both domestic and commercial categories expected to remain robust as newer geographical areas (Punjab, Haryana, MP, Rajasthan, Maharashtra) mature and deepen customer penetration.

subsections.label: PNG Industrial segment - Morbi
points: Morbi Ceramic cluster remains the largest partner in the PNG industrial segment; company's supply strategy provided significant support to Morbi ceramic industry during the crisis period.

Availability of alternate fuels such as propane remained adversely impacted during the quarter, and the company's ability to source and supply gas even against increased demand from Morbi is cited as a testament to its gas trading capabilities.

Post-July, propane availability has gradually improved as suppliers began sourcing from non-Middle East countries (USA, Venezuela, others), causing Morbi gas offtake to reduce to the current ~3 mmscmd run-rate.

Gas price (Rs78/scm) is at a premium to propane (Rs65/scm) currently due to elevated spot LNG prices (~$20) and propane availability improving; expectation is Morbi will continue at ~3 mmscmd at least this quarter.

A floor of ~1.8-2 mmscmd of Morbi demand is expected to remain with gas because certain smaller companies lack propane infrastructure or space to install propane facilities; these contracts are on a one-month basis.

subsections.label: PNG Industrial segment - Non-Morbi
points: Non-Morbi industrial volumes (~2-2.2 mmscmd currently) have stayed in a fairly narrow range for the past 2-3 years; management indicated this is not only due to pricing but also due to ongoing infrastructure development.

Promising regions include DNH, Ahmedabad rural, Dahej, Kutch and Thane, where pipeline network is in advanced stages and reaching industrial areas; 86 new industries added April-June 2026 in non-Morbi section.
Volumes in these regions are expected to reach at least 3 mmscmd within 1.5 to 2 years as LNG prices are expected to stabilize in about a year.
Key alternate industrial fuels being competed against include steam (in Ankleshwar/South Gujarat), briquettes and other solid fuels in other regions.
No mandatory regulatory push exists for industrial gas usage (unlike domestic/commercial segments), so industrial remains an open-competition market versus alternate fuels like propane.

subsections.label: Power business
points: Gas-based power plants (GSEG 51 MW and Pipavav) have been operating at low PLFs — GSEG around 6% and Pipavav around 1% in the last quarter.
Utilization mainly occurs during peak summer electricity demand/shortage periods; otherwise limited utilization.
Management is working on a strategy to revive the power business and will update investors in a few months.
Company is exploring multiple options including back-of-the-meter deals to supply power to data centers, similar to other power companies.

subsections.label: Propane import facility plans
points: Company has plans to set up its own propane import and storage facility near the Morbi market.
A few sites in Gujarat have been shortlisted; studies are ongoing; details to be shared with investors shortly.
This propane facility capex is not included in the INR1,000 crore CGD capex guidance; it is in early DRHP stage, with a detailed project report needed before capex proceeds over the next two years.

subsections.label: Post-merger integration
points: Company completed listing and trading of additional equity shares allotted pursuant to the merger scheme during the quarter.
Post-merger performance reflects the strength of the integrated business model, combining scale, sourcing strength, operational synergies and broader capabilities across the energy value chain.
Company positioned as one of India's leading integrated energy companies with presence across gas trading, city gas distribution, exploration and production, and renewable energy.

subsections.label: GSPL Transmission Limited (GTL) listing
points: GTL is now a separate company; its financial results are available on its own website and are being disclosed quarter-on-quarter.

Listing of GSPL Transmission Limited, originally expected by end of July/mid-August, is now expected towards early September due to coordination with BSE, NSE and SEBI on exemption requirements for listing without a public issue route.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and supply disruption
points: Global energy markets witnessed significant disruption during the quarter due to geopolitical developments and supply-side constraints (Middle East conflict).

Availability of alternate fuels such as propane was adversely impacted during the quarter due to the Middle East crisis, though it has since improved as suppliers diversified sourcing to USA and Venezuela.

Timeline for reasonable-priced long-term LNG supply has repeatedly shifted due to successive geopolitical shocks — Russia-Ukraine conflict followed by Middle East/Iran developments — pushing the anticipated new wave of LNG supply from originally 2026/27 to now 2028.
Looking ahead, global energy markets are likely to remain uncertain due to continuing geopolitical developments.

subsections.label: Propane competitive pricing risk
points: With propane sourcing diversifying to non-Middle East countries, price gap between gas and propane is expected to remain elevated, making it difficult to regain lost Morbi volume back to prior peak levels.
Gas price at Rs78/scm remains at a premium to propane at Rs65/scm currently amid elevated spot LNG prices (~$20).

subsections.label: Third-party trading volume decline
points: Third-party gas trading volume dropped to 3.3 mmscmd from around 5 mmscmd previously due to volume cut-off from the Middle East and high prices; power volumes were also absent this time, further impacting the segment.

subsections.label: Power segment underutilization
points: Gas-based power plants continue to operate at very low PLFs, utilized mainly during peak summer demand periods.

subsections.label: Revenue/margin projection for FY27
points: For gas trading business, projecting around INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores of margins for FY27.

For CGD business, guidance will remain with the same numbers as earlier, except by Q2 the company will be in a better position to give firmer numbers due to continuing Middle East crisis-related volatility.

subsections.label: Cash deployment / capital allocation timeline
points: A concrete plan for cash deployment (diversification strategy in energy business, strengthening of CNG/pipeline business) is expected to be presented to investors by Q3.

guidance_ledger.statement: We stick to our guidance last time we gave around INR1,100 crores of profit from the gas trading business; despite strong Q1, we stick to the earlier guidance on a conservative basis
We make a margin of close to 4% to 5% in the gas trading business; there will be exceptional quarters but we stick to that guidance
We have given a guidance of 5.5 to 6.5 Rs/scm; we'll still stick to that guidance
There will be capex on the CGD segment, which we are giving a guidance of close to INR1,000 crores; we still stick with that
There is no capex on the gas trading segment
As of today, around 28% (~2 million ton LNG equivalent) is on term contract basis; we expect to do close to at least 4 million tons in 2030
In the long term, we do expect good third-party volumes especially in FY28-29 where we expect pricing to be much more reasonable; long-term volume should be in the range of 4.5 million to 5 million
We expect to continue to do close to 3 mmscmd of gas at least in this quarter [in Morbi]
1.8 million to 2 million mmscmd would be a fair number to assume [as sustainable Morbi floor volume] because in the past it had reduced to around that number
As we expect LNG prices to become stable maybe in a year from now, we expect these volumes to be at least 3 mmscmd by 1.5 years to 2 years from now
We have been growing at close to 12%, this quarter growing at 13%; we'll be able to sustain that growth for the next couple of years
Planning to add more than 75 new CNG stations and upgrade approximately 70 CNG stations during the current financial year
For the gas trading business, we are projecting around INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores of margins

With respect to the CGD business also, we'll be going with the same numbers which were there earlier, except by Q2 we'll be in a better position to tell you the numbers because of Middle East crisis volatility

We are effectively closely coordinating with BSE, NSE and SEBI on this since it will require exemption for listing without going for public issue route, it is likely to take slightly longer time. We expect this towards early September

With respect to the rest of the cash to be utilized, we are working on certain programs...on a concrete plan, we will be coming in maybe in Q3 -- by Q3 we'll be having a concrete plan of how that deployment of the cash will happen
It will take time in the sense at least a year to get the refunds because we need to refile the accounts returns
We are working on the strategy on how to revive it or how to do certain things. We'll be coming back to the investors maybe in a few months down the line
We have plans to have our own propane import facility; we have shortlisted a few sites in Gujarat; those studies are going on; we will be coming to you with some details shortly
We will be maintaining INR1,000 crores to INR1,100 crores of profitability annually in gas trading (excluding one-offs)
With respect to the E&P business, we will be close to INR100 crores capex; we will be drilling a few wells
There is no capex in respect to trading segment
We expect the entire process for listing and trading of GTL shares to be completed by end of July '26

risk_register.note: Availability of alternate fuels like propane was adversely impacted during the quarter but has since improved post-July as suppliers diversified sourcing to USA, Venezuela and other non-Middle East countries, reducing Morbi gas offtake from ~8 mmscmd to ~3 mmscmd.

risk_register.note: Gas priced at Rs78/scm remains at a premium to propane at Rs65/scm; expected to stay elevated given current spot LNG prices (~$20), making it tough to regain volume, though ~1.8-2 mmscmd floor expected to remain with gas due to lack of propane infrastructure among smaller customers.

themes.label: Corporate restructuring / merger execution
themes.note: Company completed listing and trading of additional equity shares allotted pursuant to the merger scheme; post-merger integrated model now spans gas trading, CGD, E&P and renewables.

themes.label: Morbi industrial demand surge
themes.note: Morbi volumes surged to ~8 mmscmd in May-June amid propane shortage but have since receded to ~3 mmscmd as propane availability improved from non-Middle East sources; a floor of 1.8-2 mmscmd is expected to persist.

themes.label: Gas trading resilience amid volume decline
themes.note: Gas Trading EBT grew 206% YoY on favorable sourcing timing and Brent-linked contracts, even as third-party trading volume declined to 3.3 mmscmd from ~5 mmscmd due to Middle East disruptions and high prices.

themes.label: Geopolitical/Middle East conflict impact
themes.note: Global energy markets remained disrupted by geopolitical developments; long-term LNG supply timeline pushed from 2026/27 to 2028 due to successive shocks (Russia-Ukraine, then Middle East/Iran).

themes.label: Power segment underperformance and turnaround optionality
themes.note: GSEG and Pipavav gas-based power plants operated at very low PLFs (~6% and ~1%); management exploring revival strategy and back-of-the-meter deals such as data center supply.

themes.label: Capital allocation review
themes.note: Company holds ~INR7,200 crores cash; concrete deployment plan for diversification and business strengthening expected by Q3; dividend continues per Government of Gujarat guidelines.

themes.label: CGD network expansion (CNG/PNG)
themes.note: CNG stations expanded to 844 with plans for 75+ new stations and 70 upgrades in FY27; domestic PNG customer base crossed 24.77 lakh households aided by government PNG drive amid LPG supply constraints.

key_takeaways: The Gas Trading segment delivered strong profitability with earnings before tax increasing to INR726 crores in this quarter as against INR237 crores in the previous year same quarter, reflecting a growth of 206%.
In the CNG segment, we achieved a new benchmark with CNG volume of 3.76 mmscmd during this quarter compared to 3.33 mmscmd in the previous year same quarter, registering a growth of 13%.
During the current quarter, the company added approximately 59,000 new domestic PNG customers, taking our cumulative domestic PNG customer base to more than 24.77 lakh households.
The PNG Industrial segment delivered a strong performance during the quarter. Industrial sales volumes increased to 7.17 mmscmd in Q1 FY27 from 4.71 mmscmd in Q1 FY26, registering a growth of 64%.

For Q1 FY27, we reported revenue from operations of INR9,670 crores compared to INR5,924 crores in Q1 FY26, representing a year-on-year growth of 63%. EBITDA stood at INR1,482 crores compared to INR896 crores in Q1 FY26, reflecting a growth of 65%. Profit after tax stood at INR998 crores compared to INR561 crores in Q1 FY26, registering a growth of 78%.
The company's total pipeline network spans approximately 45,900 kilometers across six states and one union territory. During the quarter, the company invested INR127 crores in CGD infrastructure.

This quarter is significant for the company as apart from delivering excellent performance across our key business segments, We also completed the listing and trading of our additional equity shares allotted pursuant to the scheme.
Looking ahead, global energy markets are likely to remain uncertain due to continuing geopolitical developments. However, we remain confident in our strategy.

So what really the gross margin you're making here? — Management declined to detail beyond segment-level results in the investor presentation.

Amit Murarka: In this quarter, the CGD EBITDA margin has come down. Is it largely because of Morbi or is there any reason in that number? — Management did not attribute it to a specific segment, stating they look at the portfolio level rather than each segment.
Somaiah: Q4 non-Morbi industrial pricing number — Management could not provide immediately and asked the analyst to send a mail for details.

quarters.summary: Gujarat Energy Limited (erstwhile Gujarat Gas Limited) reported Q4/FY26 results post the scheme of arrangement merging GSPC, GSPL and GSPC Energy into Gujarat Gas (renamed Gujarat Energy Limited) and demerging the gas transmission undertaking into GSPL Transmission Limited (GTL). Management expects listing of additional shares and GTL shares to complete by end-July 2026, guided margin ranges for CGD (INR5-6.5/scm) and gas trading (4-6%) to be maintained, expects 25-30% growth in gas trading volumes by 2030-31, and flagged continued volatility from Middle East conflict, propane unavailability, and forex/impairment losses in the power segment.

subsections.label: Financial reporting comparability
points: FY25-26 financials and restated FY24-25 financials are not like-to-like due to inclusion of the demerged Gas Transmission business (GSPL) in the restated FY24-25 base but not in FY25-26.

subsections.label: Dividend & capital return
points: Board recommended dividend of INR8.90/share (445% of face value), total outgo ~INR835 crores, reaffirming commitment to shareholder value.

subsections.label: Tax position
points: INR7,200 crore of tax losses arose at time of merger (1 April 2024); INR2,800 crore absorbed in FY25 and INR2,500 crore absorbed in FY26, leaving ~INR1,900 crore of carry-forward losses against which no tax will be payable on future profits up to that amount.

Tax losses must be utilized within 8 years; ~INR5,000 crore already used across FY25 and FY26; advance tax paid in those years is expected to generate a refund of ~INR900 crores, though the refund timeline depends on income tax department assessment.
A deferred tax asset has been created on the balance sheet for these tax losses; detailed schedule to be provided in financial statements.

subsections.label: Balance sheet - cash & investments
points: Presentation shows ~INR5,000 crore cash, but consolidated balance sheet shows ~INR1,300 crore cash and cash equivalents plus ~INR5,500 crore of 'other financial assets' (largely fixed deposits >1 year and GSFS fund placements), reclassified over the last 2 years; combined this totals ~INR6,800 crore.
Management to share a detailed breakup of other financial assets on request; full detail will be available in account schedules.

subsections.label: Capex guidance
points: No capex is planned for the Trading segment.
CGD capex guided at ~INR1,000 crores; E&P capex guided at ~INR100 crores for drilling a few wells.
Normal historical capex run-rate is ~INR800-900 crores/year while operating cash flows are significantly higher, prompting the ongoing capital allocation review with McKinsey.

subsections.label: Power segment exceptional items
points: Segment losses attributed to exceptional items, including forex loss on BHEL/APC contracts (denominated in USD) and impairment: GSEG forex loss of INR15 crore and GPPC forex loss of INR23 crore, described as notional losses linked to dollar-denominated contract values.

subsections.label: E&P segment profitability
points: E&P is profitable at the operating level (~INR29 crore operating profit in FY26) but reports a loss after depreciation.
A 'tail leg' of ~10% of one asset (a KG basin asset) is held despite an operational loss on that specific asset, while other E&P assets are profitable.

subsections.label: Gas Trading segment
points: Gas Trading is described as the most value-accretive aspect of the GSPC merger, with pre-merger 5-year cumulative revenues exceeding INR1 lakh crores and EBITDA exceeding INR9,000 crores.

FY26 trading volume fell ~19% YoY (10.2 vs 12.6 mmscmd) but EBT still rose to INR1,334.61 crores from INR1,222 crores due to a diversified sourcing portfolio, demonstrating resilience despite challenging conditions.

Company maintains long-term contracts on both sourcing (Qatar, Shell, Total, Uniper) and sales side (fertilizer companies till 2028, CGD companies - Sabarmati Gas, Indian Oil, Adani, Charotar Gas, IRM, IGL, Megha - and industrial customers JSW, Deepak Fertiliser, PGP Glass, Indo Baijin, Nirma), with a back-to-back contract structure limiting exposure.

Sourcing contract details: Qatar Energy new contract 1 million ton ramping to 1 MMTPA by 2030, valid ~17 years from 2026; existing Qatar contract expires 2028; Shell contract - 15 cargoes/year, expires 2030; TotalEnergies - 6 cargoes/year, 2026-2035; Uniper - 6 cargoes/year, 2028-2037.

Trading margin guided at 4-6%, expected to be maintained despite volatility; management expects gas trading volume growth of 25-30% by 2030-31 as prices normalize post-conflict resolution starting 2028-29.
Two cargoes scheduled in May/June already lost this year due to the Middle East conflict impacting the new 1 MMTPA Qatar contract ramp-up.

FY26 trading EBT of INR1,334 crore vs a stated recurring run-rate of INR1,000-1,100 crore; the gap explained by one-offs: ~INR200 crore related to a back-to-back liability with Petronet LNG/GSPC LNG for diverted cargoes, and a customs duty refund (~INR50 crore).

subsections.label: CGD segment - CNG
points: Highest-ever CNG volume of 3.6 mmscmd in Q4 FY26, with growth stronger outside Gujarat (18%) than within Gujarat (11%), reflecting success in deepening presence across new geographies.
CNG remains economically attractive vs petrol and diesel, supporting vehicle base growth to ~17.68 lakh vehicles.

subsections.label: CGD segment - PNG Domestic
points: Growth driven by a Government of India PNG penetration drive launched to replace LPG amid constrained LPG supplies caused by the Middle East conflict.

Initiatives include aggressive marketing campaigns (print, media, digital), appointment of direct marketing agents, mobilizing additional contractors, and prioritizing outreach to essential category customers (hospitals, hotels, community kitchens).

Newer geographical areas (Punjab, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra) expected to continue maturing and enhancing customer penetration, supporting robust domestic and commercial customer additions.

subsections.label: CGD segment - PNG Industrial / Morbi
points: Morbi ceramic cluster is the largest PNG Industrial partner; the company's supply strategy provided significant support to Morbi during the March-May 2026 crisis period caused by propane supply constraints.

Overall PNG Industrial volume declined YoY (Q4 FY26 vs Q4 FY25) but rose sequentially QoQ, driven mainly by the sharp ramp-up in Morbi off-take (units rose from 83 to 710) even as non-Morbi volumes declined marginally.

Propane suppliers expected to remain impacted over the short-to-medium term, potentially encouraging further industrial reliance on natural gas; company monitoring spot RLNG prices, alternate fuel availability and demand trends.
Focus stated as maintaining balance between volume growth and sustainable margins.
Morbi demand ceiling estimated by customers at 8.8-8.9 mmscmd, against current ~8 mmscmd, leaving a further ~10% growth potential room in the near term.
Morbi contracts are signed on a monthly rolling basis, started mid-April post voluntary shutdown; good volumes expected to continue in the near term.

On sustainability of Morbi volumes if propane normalizes: management does not expect propane to return to normal levels in the short-to-medium term, and expects gas pricing to remain competitive with propane even if it returns, given propane prices track oil prices similarly to Brent-linked gas contracts.
