subsections.label: Scheme mechanics
points: On 1 May 2026, GSPC, GSPL and GSPC Energy Limited merged into Gujarat Gas Limited; consequently GSPC, GSPL and GSPC Energy ceased to exist.
Concurrently with the GSPL merger, the gas transmission business undertaking was demerged into GSPL Transmission Limited (GTL).
Name of Gujarat Gas Limited altered to Gujarat Energy Limited effective 14 May 2026, reflecting positioning as an integrated energy company.

FY25-26 financials and restated FY24-25 financials are not like-to-like because restated FY24-25 includes the Gas Transmission business of GSPL, which is not part of FY25-26 financials due to the demerger effective 1 April 2025.

An application has been made to BSE and NSE for listing permission of additional shares allotted to GSPC/GSPL shareholders; once received, corporate actions will follow for crediting shares to Demat accounts and subsequent listing/trading.
GTL will separately declare a record date for issuance of GTL shares to Gujarat Energy shareholders, followed by listing and trading permission on BSE/NSE.

Anyone holding Gujarat Energy shares on the record date to be fixed for GTL will be eligible to receive GTL shares; buying Gujarat Energy shares today does not guarantee GTL shares unless held on that record date.

subsections.label: Business development strategy / capital allocation review
points: McKinsey engaged as strategic consultant to evaluate growth opportunities in existing businesses and advise on organic and inorganic expansion initiatives.

Objective is to set up GEL for steady growth over the next decade: accelerate core business growth, define expansion opportunities in adjacencies/emerging energy segments, create a future-ready portfolio, strengthen organizational capabilities post-merger, and build a structured implementation plan.
Company has ~INR6,000+ crores cash on books; management indicated a definitive capital allocation plan (use of cash) will be shared with investors in the next quarter or subsequent quarter.

subsections.label: GSPC LNG Mundra stake increase
points: Outstanding liability/back-to-back agreement receivable from GSPC LNG with respect to diverted cargoes at Petronet LNG Dahej was converted into equity, increasing Gujarat Energy's stake in GSPC LNG from 14% (at merger announcement) to 36.8%.
Beyond 25% stake, GSPC LNG becomes a subsidiary requiring consolidation.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / gas market volatility
points: Middle East conflict caused gas market instability during Q4 FY26, contributing to LPG supply constraints and impacting scheduled LNG cargo deliveries (2 cargoes under the new Qatar 1 MMTPA contract already lost in May/June 2026).

Global energy markets continue to face uncertainty due to ongoing geopolitical developments; company relies on diversified sourcing, strong infrastructure, disciplined capital allocation, and customer-centric approach to navigate challenges.

subsections.label: Propane supply disruption / dependency risk
points: Propane suppliers expected to remain impacted over the short-to-medium term; while this currently benefits gas demand in Morbi, it also creates uncertainty about long-term sustainable Morbi gas volumes once propane supply normalizes.

Increasing near-term reliance on short-term LNG to meet ramped-up Morbi/CGD demand creates exposure to spot price volatility; management addressing this via new long-term Brent-linked contracts (Qatar, Uniper) and by seeking additional Henry Hub-linked long-term volumes for more stable pricing.

subsections.label: Power segment exceptional/forex losses
points: GSEG and GPPC reported forex losses (INR15 crore and INR23 crore respectively) linked to USD-denominated BHEL/APC contract obligations, plus impairment, contributing to segment losses despite low PLF.

subsections.label: Tax refund timing uncertainty
points: The ~INR900 crore advance tax refund is subject to income tax department assessment timelines, which management could not commit a date for.

subsections.label: Forward outlook
points: Management expects reasonable gas prices to return starting FY28-29 once the Middle East conflict is resolved.
Company currently doing 10-12 mmscmd in gas trading but expects 25-30% growth in the business by 2030-31.
Capital allocation plan for surplus cash to be shared with investors in the next quarter or subsequent quarter, based on the ongoing McKinsey-led strategic review.
Next scheduled interaction with investors is early August 2026 with Q1 results.

key_takeaways: On 17th April 2026, we received the final order from Hon’ble Ministry of Corporate Affairs, approving the scheme of arrangement. The scheme of arrangement has become effective from 1st May 2026.

Gujarat State Petroleum Corporation Limited, Gujarat State Petronet Limited and GSPC Energy Limited have been merged into Gujarat Gas Limited; the gas transmission business undertaking has been demerged into GSPL Transmission Limited (GTL); the name of Gujarat Gas Limited has been altered to Gujarat Energy Limited with effect from 14th May 2026.

For Q4 FY '26, EBITDA stood at INR943 crores compared to INR790 crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. For the full year, EBITDA stands at INR3,772 crores as compared to INR3,241 crores in previous year. PAT for the full year stands at INR2,299 crores as compared to INR2,308 crores in the previous year.
Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share, equivalent to 445% of face value with a total dividend outgo of approximately INR835 crores.
We achieved our highest ever CNG volume of 3.6 mmscmd during Q4 FY '26, representing a 12% year-on-year growth.
Gas Trading segment earnings before tax increased to INR1,334.61 crores in FY '26 from INR1,222 crores in FY '25, despite trading volumes falling by about 19% due to the Middle East conflict.

The number of units off-taking gas in Morbi increased from 83 units with gas consumption of 1.66 mmscmd in March '26 to 710 units with gas consumption reaching approximately 8 mmscmd by the last week of May '26.
We have engaged McKinsey as a strategic consultant to evaluate growth opportunities within our existing businesses as well as to advise on both organic and inorganic expansion initiatives.
pressing_questions: On the power business (PLF in single digits, losses in the segment) - what is the outlook and turnaround plan? (Management response was preliminary, indicating they would 'come back gradually on this')
On sustainable Morbi volumes once propane normalizes - management stated confidence but exact quantification not fully provided beyond qualitative assurance.

On EBITDA margin per SCM for Morbi volumes specifically - management deferred, saying 'I can make a talk on the quarter 1 numbers, then we can talk on those numbers', not answering directly in this call.

On whether intersegment transfer pricing between Gas Trading and CGD would shift more profit into CGD in future years - management declined to confirm directly ('I'm not saying that, but you can always interpret what I'm saying').

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~17% YoY to ₹156 crore, with PBT turning positive and consolidated improvement "at all stages" of the income statement. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹875 crore as "easily achievable" given order book plus Q1 execution, and reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of ~₹100-105 crore (13-14% PAT margin), alongside the long-term ₹1,500 crore revenue by 2031 aspiration — all framed as capacity-planning guides subject to geopolitical volatility, execution constraints and talent. Capacity expansion in India was commissioned in Q1 (foundry and gate & wall manufacturing, +up to 30% capacity), while US and Saudi Arabia greenfield plants are progressing toward operations by March FY28, with capex of ~$12m (US) and ~$4m (Saudi). Operational disruptions persist from Middle East logistics (vessel unavailability, Gulf War, Houthi attacks) and a Singapore client payment risk, and US tariff policy uncertainty is constraining commercial aggressiveness even as the company shifts more manufacturing to the US.

key_takeaways: Revenue: Management reported ₹156 crore in Q1, up ~17% YoY.
Profitability inflection: PBT turned positive vs last year; management also highlighted consolidated improvement "at all stages" of the income statement.
India capacity expansion commissioned: In Q1 the company commissioned foundry expansion and gate & wall manufacturing expansion, increasing capacity "by up to 30%".
Consolidated order book: ₹932 crore, split India ₹293 crore / ex-India ₹639 crore.

Revenue target de-risking (management's framing): Management said if you add revenue recognized in Q1 + current order book, it exceeds ₹1,080 crore, implying the FY27 revenue target of ₹875-900 crore is "easy" to meet (subject to disruptions).

Middle East dispatch constraints: Material produced and stocked because the company is "not getting any vessels from India" to ship due to the regional conflict; Qatar consignments stuck due to "Gulf War."
Jash Process Equipment (ex-Vestech): Material commercial miss: management stated they lost ~₹150-200 crore of orders in the last 3-4 months, prompting an "intense review."
New product/market vector: data center pressure vessels — won first order for 4 units; negotiating 32 units; received inquiry for more than 600 pressure vessels, enough to make a new plant.
FY27 revenue outlook reiterated: ₹875 crore (India ₹320 cr, ex-India ₹555 cr), described as "easily achievable" given order book + Q1 execution visibility (subject to disruptions).

FY27 profitability outlook: Management closed with confidence in meeting projections including "around 100 to 105 crore… profit after tax" and suggested 13-14% PAT margin is achievable but contingent on geopolitical stability.

quarters.summary: Jash Engineering closed FY26 with muted consolidated revenue growth (INR757cr vs INR746cr) due to US tariff volatility and Middle East war disruptions, but management guides to INR875cr revenue and 12-13% PAT margin for FY27 on an order book of INR899cr as of 1st May, with a five-year ambition of INR1500cr+ revenue backed by capacity expansion in Houston and Saudi Arabia.

subsections.label: Revenue & Margin Drivers
points: Consolidated income grew marginally from INR746cr to INR757cr, described by management as disappointing.

Growth was affected by US tariff hikes (25% in January, 50% in June) causing slowdown in US production, and by the Middle East war disrupting Middle East deliveries and Far East/Southeast Asia dispatches due to ship/container unavailability.
Domestic business grew 18% YoY at relatively good profitability, offsetting the INR50-60cr export shortfall.
Standalone PAT fell only 1 percentage point (14.38% to 13.38%) despite export weakness, reflecting strength of the domestic business.
EBITDA level saw no growth and came down because overheads grow 7-10% annually while revenue growth was below that threshold.
Gross profit margin grew marginally mainly due to rupee depreciation.
Q4FY26 was outstanding partly due to high foreign currency gain versus rates estimated at quoting stage.
Standalone revenue fell due to export decline; domestic revenue rose 18% with good margins.
Rodney Hunt revenue fell due to initial uncertainty on tariffs, but order-taking resumed from Oct-Dec and healthy order book now exists.
Waterfront had minor revenue increase and reduction in losses; expected to double revenue this year.
Q4 gross margin improvement attributed to forex gains — orders taken at lower estimated USD/INR rate realized at higher invoice rate, e.g., INR82 estimated vs INR92 realized.
Gross margins considered sustainable as long as the dollar does not weaken; Q4 margin also aided by higher revenue absorbing fixed overheads.
Other expenses spike in the quarter was a one-off US bank charge (~INR10cr).
Other income rose mostly due to foreign exchange gains.

Standalone PAT margin trend shown across FY23-FY26 (14.52%, 14.21%, 14.39% [restated FY25 vs earlier 14.38%], 13.38%) with no big differential reflecting a standard margin policy; big acquisitions or turmoil can affect it.
Consolidated PAT margin around 12%.
Management's standard strategy is moderate growth with focus on margins; growth of 13-17% welcomed with margin of minimum 12% up to 14-15%.

Rodney Hunt pending orders of USD28-29mn placed before February tariff revision: over 80% already estimated at 50% tariff; some orders quoted between February-June may carry 25% tariff and remain unexecuted; raw material escalation (steel prices up ~20% in India, also in America) affects achievable margins on these orders, though they should still yield higher margin than the base 50%-tariff-assumed calculation.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation / Capex
points: FY26 capex was INR37cr in plant & machinery plus INR30cr for acquisitions, totaling INR67cr.
FY27 capex planned at INR15-16cr for the five Indian plants; capex for America (Houston) and Saudi Arabia expansion not yet quantified as progress is still uncertain.

Promoter shareholding variation quarter-to-quarter attributed to sales by the erstwhile promoter Amin family (no longer promoters); Patel family promoters have only purchased, never sold; last quarter a warrant due in February was exercised, marginally increasing promoter holding.

subsections.label: Order Book Composition & Growth Outlook
points: Order book of INR899cr as of 1 May, combined with ~INR40-45cr already achieved, supports the INR875cr FY27 revenue projection as conservative but achievable.
Growth balanced between export and domestic; management chooses higher-profitability domestic jobs and would take more domestic business if export slows during execution.
April revenue booking was very low (Q1 typically lowest quarter); INR36cr of March dispatches was not recognized as revenue and will flow into April/May.
Pipeline includes INR28cr already negotiated and a further INR80cr under negotiation expected to close within a few weeks.
Rodney Hunt healthy order book will more than make up prior year's shortfall; orders resumed from Oct-Dec after initial post-tariff hesitation.

Jash conservative FY27 revenue projection of INR530cr considered easily achievable; Waterfront projected at INR60cr (75-85% of last year's achievement); Rodney Hunt projected more than 25% above what was achieved last year.

Mahr (screens) order booking remains sub-INR20cr; management notes screens manufactured broadly, not only reflected via Mahr's own revenue — screens built by Jash or via new UK orders won't reflect in Mahr's revenue since only design work is done by Mahr.
Southeast Asia/Far East mix declined from 16% to 10% due to project-based lumpiness, not a structural demand issue; Vietnam order dispatch delay has since been resolved.

Rising sea level opportunities (2100-year horizon) are being tendered progressively: Hong Kong Yuen Long Barrage is the first major project (~INR40cr total); Singapore projects (USD800-900mn offers submitted) will start tendering from 2028 with awards likely staggered over 20-25 years, first orders potentially from 2029; Jash's market share in these could range 20-40%.
War had no direct effect on order intake; lower orders were due to US tariff uncertainty. Southeast Asia, Middle East, Far East and Europe orders continued; Middle East dispatch remains a problem.

subsections.label: Product Mix
points: Water control gates remains the biggest and dominant product, with Screens and Valves as number two and three respectively; balance equipment including hydro power and pumping is ~8%, giving a fairly balanced mix that avoids over-dependence on gates.
Valves mix improved from 11% to 13%, while screens mix has remained largely flat.
Market share worldwide: 44.5% of business is in India and ~55% is outside India; mix varies but the larger share consistently comes from outside India.

subsections.label: Company/Subsidiary Performance
points: Rodney Hunt (US): revenue fell in FY26 due to tariff-driven uncertainty in the first few months but order-taking resumed Oct-Dec; healthy order book now supports expectation to more than make up last year's shortfall with enhanced growth and outstanding PAT this year.

Waterfront (UK): minor revenue increase and reduction in losses in FY26; expected to double revenue this year; UK water industry operates under Ofwat's 5-year AMP cycle where the first 1.5 years are planning-heavy and slow, followed by three years of execution and a final slow year — currently mid-cycle, with huge growth expected from H2 of this year; grew from GBP2-2.2mn at acquisition to a projected GBP5.5-6mn this year, with a further doubling to GBP12mn targeted over the next two years; original 4-year target of INR200cr revenue may now take 5 years, revised to INR125-135cr including Penstocks.
Jash (India, standalone): all three major group companies (Rodney Hunt, Jash, Waterfront) are expected to show enhanced growth and outstanding PAT this year.

Shivpad: merged into Jash Engineering Limited; is process equipment for the municipal business (vs WesTech's industrial focus); had quality issues (not labour issues) — labour lacked required skill, a team was brought to Indore for training and sent back, issues nearly resolved; no incremental capacity addition planned there.

WesTech (renamed Jash Process Equipment Private Limited, acquired mid-January): contributes a small percentage of revenue this year since acquisition was recent; serves industrial paper & pulp, metal and minerals, alumina sectors (distinct design/sturdiness vs Shivpad's municipal equipment); outsources all manufacturing currently, leading to lower profitability — will progressively use Jash's own manufacturing infrastructure to reduce costs, a process expected to take 1-2 years.

Mahr Maschinenbau: order book strong; screens are manufactured broadly (not exclusively reflected in Mahr's revenue) — equipment built by Jash or via new UK orders will not show up in Mahr's revenue since Mahr does design only in some cases.

subsections.label: Capacity Expansion
points: Penstocks UK acquisition completed in early April 2026; will be merged with Waterfront Fluid Controls, with a target for combined revenue to reach INR125-135cr in 3-4 years' time.

With current manufacturing capacities run on a 2-3 shift basis, the company can achieve INR1200cr; once Houston (US) and Saudi Arabia plants are online and functioning well, capacity would exceed INR1500cr within about five years — marketing must then scale up correspondingly to capture that revenue.

Rodney Hunt's new Houston plant cost has risen sharply — original quote of USD4.2mn has roughly doubled to USD7-8.5mn in current quotes; various offers were called and revised, and management must decide when to proceed; target commissioning for both Houston and Saudi Arabia plants pushed to before December 2027.

Rationale for Houston plant: inability to get production staff in Orange, Massachusetts (a small town young workers are leaving for cities), causing execution delays; management has land and approved drawings but the contracted builder's owner passed away leading the company to close down, delaying the project; reaching historical INR600-700cr Rodney Hunt revenue levels at Orange alone is possible only with adequate staffing and modernization, which management is not pursuing given staffing constraints.

Saudi Arabia plant: company has been set up as a first step; land acquisition still pending; site visit planned for end of June/July 2026, after which land will be acquired and work will start, targeting commissioning by December 2027 (delayed from earlier December 2026 target due to the regional war disrupting travel/visit plans).

Rodney Hunt targeting growth from current USD30mn revenue to USD75mn over the next five years; FY27 target of USD38mn is viewed as conservative since order book and execution combined already exceed USD40mn; management explicitly not targeting USD100mn due to factors outside its control (e.g., unpredictable US tariff policy, including a recent shift of certain products to Section 232 national security tariff classification).

Employee cost at Rodney Hunt has grown due to prior hiring, but employees have not been reduced despite turbulence, as the same workforce is expected to deliver the USD38-39mn revenue target; management describes its approach as conservative rather than aggressively scaling ahead of demand, citing high uncertainty in the US project-manufacturing environment.

subsections.label: Geographic Diversification Strategy
points: Management previously flagged intent to reduce dependence on the US (historically ~45% of revenue); is diversifying via UK (Penstocks acquisition) and Saudi Arabia (new plant setup), plus WesTech acquisition to strengthen India process-equipment offering in the industrial sector.
Middle East war affected not only Middle East deliveries but also dispatches to Far East and Southeast Asia due to sudden unavailability of ships and containers.
Southeast Asia, Middle East, Far East and Europe continued to generate orders through the turbulence; only dispatch to the Middle East remains a problem.

India wastewater/water infrastructure opportunity: new Rs.4 lakh crore Jal Jeevan Mission budget targeting completion of India-wide water supply by 2028-29, after which ~80% of delivered water will need wastewater treatment; most Indian metropolitan cities currently have no more than 70% treatment capacity; further downstream opportunities in reuse, storm water, desalination and rising sea level mitigation are expected to unlock huge potential after 2028-29.

Rising sea level projects: Hong Kong (Yuen Long Barrage, ~INR40cr, first project of its kind, with 14-person delegation including 6 video crew visiting the plant in June for inspection/testing) leads the pack; Singapore is at design/consultant stage for USD800-900mn worth of quoted projects with tendering to start from 2028, spread over 20-25 years, first order flow potentially from 2029.

subsections.label: Input Costs & Working Capital
points: Raw material (steel) prices have risen roughly 20% in India, and similarly in America, affecting margin outcomes on new and pending orders depending on material of construction and timing of price rise.

In the US, a 50% steel tariff caused domestic steel mills to raise prices by more than 50% to capture margin, which management notes was the intended purpose of the tariff, but this makes American-made steel purchases (e.g., for Rodney Hunt) more expensive even though competitiveness versus imports is not impacted since US steel is already >50% costlier than in India.

Management agreed to share standalone and consolidated working capital details separately with an analyst upon request (via email); considering whether this should become a regular part of the investor presentation, subject to discussion with EY (IR advisor) on whether it is industry standard practice; goods-in-transit cycle (e.g., dispatch to US) is lengthy, prompting the analyst's interest in working capital visibility by domestic vs. overseas operations.

subsections.label: Market Positioning
points: Company market share is described as good worldwide, with 44.5% of business in India and ~55% outside India, varying by year but consistently weighted toward international business.

Rising sea level mitigation is a long-horizon (2100-year projection) opportunity across geographies including Hong Kong, Singapore and Indonesia, with each government planning and executing per its own fiscal capacity.

India's wastewater treatment market remains underpenetrated relative to the country's size, described as historically politically motivated with government focus first on drinking water supply (Jal Jeevan Mission) before wastewater treatment; big future potential expected to unlock post-2028-29 in treatment, reuse, storm water and desalination as water scarcity (e.g., in Indore) intensifies.

subsections.label: M&A / Corporate Structure
points: Acquisition of Penstocks UK completed in early April 2026; will be merged with Waterfront Fluid Controls, targeting combined revenue of INR125-135cr in 3-4 years.

WesTech acquisition (renamed Jash Process Equipment Private Limited) completed around mid-January 2026; distinct from Shivpad (municipal process equipment) as WesTech serves industrial paper & pulp, metal and minerals, alumina sectors with sturdier equipment design; strategy, costing, manufacturing and vendoring standardization underway before margin visibility improves.
Shivpad has been merged into Jash Engineering Limited (standalone entity).

Management open to further acquisitions over the next 2-3 years if good opportunities arise and can be scaled, noting recent acquisitions have not been financially stressful as they were not large companies.

Strategy is to reduce the number of subsidiaries by merging companies with similar businesses (e.g., merging two UK entities into one) to avoid replicating top management teams; India-acquired companies (e.g., WesTech) already came with complete management teams in place, reducing leadership/staffing stress from the acquisition spree.

Management views the first two years post-acquisition as inherently challenging (establishing systems, strategy, policy, evaluating manpower), after which a growth phase follows; does not see current multi-country execution (UK, Middle East, India, US) as a constraint given the relatively small size of acquired companies.

subsections.label: Key Risks Flagged
points: US tariff volatility: increases from 25% (January) to 50% (June) caused mis-estimation on orders taken in between, leading to margin/losses when actual tariff exceeded what was quoted; management states it is not worried about the tariff level itself but about variation/instability in the tariff rate.

Recent shift of certain Jash products (valves/gates) to Section 232 national security tariff classification in the US, which the Supreme Court cannot override (unlike country-wise tariffs which the Supreme Court ruled against in February) — an unpredictable, uncontrollable development.

Middle East war disrupted project deliveries in the Middle East and indirectly affected Far East/Southeast Asia dispatches due to ship and container unavailability; dispatch to the Middle East remains a problem even though order intake continues.
Raw material (steel) price escalation of ~20% in India and similarly in the US pressures margins on new and pending orders.
Rising cost of Houston plant construction (quotes nearly doubled from USD4.2mn to USD7-8.5mn) reflects broader US cost inflation and instability, delaying capacity expansion decisions.
Staffing constraints at the Orange, Massachusetts plant (young workers moving to cities) causing execution delays, necessitating the Houston relocation/expansion.

General uncertainty in US policy-making (tariff instability, national security reclassification) creates risk in a project-manufacturing (vs mass-production) environment where outcomes are hard to predict.

War-related instability in the Middle East (Saudi Arabia) delaying land acquisition and site visits for the new plant, and creating broader hesitancy for infrastructure investment until stability returns.

Inflation/cost escalation affecting EPC contractors and employees (fixed salaries against rising costs) creating market unrest, though management does not see this translating into reduced order flow for water infrastructure given underlying water-security need.

subsections.label: Outlook Commentary
points: Management describes the FY27 revenue guidance of INR875cr as conservative given order book of INR899cr plus INR40-45cr already billed (total ~INR940-950cr), citing raw material price increases as a reason for caution on profit guidance despite this being 'easily possible'.

Five-year plan is to double revenue from INR757cr to upwards of INR1500cr; capacity to support this level would come online once Houston and Saudi Arabia plants are operational; marketing effort would then need to scale to capture that potential.

Management reiterated it prefers to remain conservative and achieve stated targets rather than being overly optimistic and failing, citing the prior year's inability to foresee US and Middle East disruptions.
CAGR from FY17 to FY26 has been ~18%; going forward to FY31, CAGR is expected to be somewhat lower (management referenced ~16%) simply because the revenue base has increased.

Rodney Hunt targeted at 38 USD million for FY27 (conservative, as order book + execution already exceeds USD40 million) building toward a five-year target of USD75 million, with USD100 million not being explicitly planned due to external uncertainty.
Waterfront targeted to reach GBP5.5-6mn (~INR65-70cr) this year, doubling to GBP12mn within a further two years; Penstocks-Waterfront combined entity targeted at INR125-135cr in 3-4 years.

US tariff situation is viewed as 'quite stable now'; management states it is comfortable with any tariff level provided it stays stable, and is optimistic about FY income if tariff stability holds and the Middle East war concludes.
Standalone PAT margin guidance context: FY23 14.52%, FY24 14.21%, FY25 14.39%(reported also earlier as 14.38%), FY26 13.38%, reflecting a broadly standard margin policy of the company.

quarters.summary: Hitachi Energy India started FY27 with strong order intake, revenue and profitability growth, backed by a record order backlog and healthy bidding pipeline. Management remains confident in multi-year growth from transmission, renewables, data centers and BESS, while continuing capacity investments (new Karjan facility) though it does not provide explicit forward numeric guidance on orders/revenue.

subsections.label: Financial statement analysis
points: Other income of approximately INR 57 crs primarily comprised interest income on deposits.
Material costs as a percentage of revenue were maintained within the historical range during Q1 FY27 despite the evolving geopolitical environment.
Exchange and commodity losses increased as a percentage of revenue during the quarter due to an unrealized loss of INR 36.37 crs.
Despite the forex loss impact, total expenses as a percentage of revenue were broadly maintained in line with the previous quarter, reflecting disciplined cost management.
Depreciation increased compared to the previous quarter, reflecting ongoing capital expenditure towards capacity expansion.
Finance cost remained broadly stable.
Gross margin improved on a QoQ basis compared to the previous quarter.
On a YoY basis, gross margin saw a slight contraction, which management attributed to the different product mix executed during the quarter (not commodity cost pass-through issues).
Q1 is characterized by management as a 'soft quarter' from various standpoints.

Full revenue contribution from the two HVDC projects (Khavda, Bhadla) has not yet materialized; historically the first year of HVDC execution sees lower revenue recognition, picking up in year 2 and 3. Khavda project is picking up; Bhadla project is starting. There was some contribution from HVDC to Q1 FY27 revenue but not the majority of revenue (attributed largely to base orders).

Notable wins: first BESS project, a 2 GW wind power evacuation project in Europe, and GIS/GIB solutions for a 100 GW solar park in western India.
Secured multiple data center orders from hyperscalers during the quarter, including a large Hyderabad project (40 x 2500 kVA) awarded by a leading Indian multinational conglomerate.
Order backlog represents strong double-digit growth compared with Q1 FY26, providing good revenue visibility for coming quarters.

subsections.label: Key order wins detail (Slide 7)
points: Europe grid expansion order: collaboration on three key transmission links (TenneT-related, ~INR 1,700 crs combined) delivering 6 GW of clean electricity, strengthening energy security and grid reliability and supporting Europe's clean energy transition.
BESS project (165 MW/330 MWh) in Andhra Pradesh reflects validation of capabilities in grid integration, power quality, and advanced energy solutions - described as a major milestone.

Data center-related order for a Load Pooling Station and Main Pooling Station comprising 56 bays of 400 kV GIS and 12.8 km of 400 kV GIB infrastructure, supporting a 100 GW solar park in western India.

subsections.label: Order mix and channels (Slide 10)
points: Domestic order growth driven by strong momentum across industry, data center, and renewables segments.
From a business segment perspective, Product orders emerged as the largest contributor in Q1 FY27.
From an end-market perspective, order book remained well diversified with contributions broadly distributed across sectors.
Strong contributions from EPC contractors and OEM customers during the quarter.

Transmission and railway/metro segments showed a temporary downturn in order mix YoY; transmission characterized as a timing issue; railway projects progressing slower than anticipated, expected to pick up from H2 of the year based on discussions with rail and metro authorities.

points: TenneT/Europe-related order combination (~INR 1,700 crs, comprising 3 orders) is more focused on services and support.

Excluding the ~INR 1,700 crs order and HVDC, remaining order intake of ~INR 3,300-3,400 crs was mostly base orders; no other major large single orders this quarter apart from strong data center orders.
Multiple data center orders were received, not a single large order.
Management declined to disclose HVDC proportion of the INR 32,222.1 crs backlog specifically, stating enough indications were given for analysts to calculate themselves.

Data center order visibility going forward described as strong; gestation period for data center projects is short, so if ~15 GW is targeted by 2030, project pipeline will be sustainable going forward, contingent on government support.
Analyst calculation cited order growth in Q2FY26 vs Q1FY26 (ex-HVDC) of 28%, implying Q2FY26 order value of ~INR 2,200 crores.

subsections.label: HVDC pipeline
points: A full greenfield HVDC project is already under bidding and is expected to be awarded in approximately 6 months.

subsections.label: Kinet Railway Solutions opportunity
points: Program related to Kinet Railway Solutions to manufacture Vande Bharat sleeper trains for Indian Railways.

Scope of work depends on whether it involves engines or cross-country electrification; all four business unit portfolios could be involved; if for locomotives, only traction transformers would be involved.
Management declined to share quantum/value opportunity for this segment-wise.

subsections.label: Business segment mix
points: Product orders emerged as the largest contributor to order intake in Q1 FY27 from a business segment perspective.

subsections.label: BESS offering
points: First Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) order received; solution is modular and scalable, unveiled during Investor Day in May 2026.
Company does everything except the batteries; designs specification requirements for batteries customers would need.

Margin profile for BESS difficult to specify at this stage as technology needs to mature; significant localization required in this segment; margins expected to gradually reach desired levels over time.
Solution includes digital layers enabling monitoring and digital services going forward.
It is an end-to-end project order excluding batteries, but integrating the battery into the software of battery management is part of the solution.

Two approaches to BESS: (1) supply of PCS solutions (not yet localized) to battery energy storage developers; (2) complete end-to-end battery energy storage solutions via grid integration business, excluding civil work — containerized and scalable solutions including design, automation, PCS, and grid connection, with software to connect to batteries also part of the package.
BESS order is for a C&I (commercial & industrial) customer, but company will also pursue utility-scale customers; not limiting focus only to C&I.

subsections.label: Data center product launch
points: Company has just launched a 'Grid to rack solution for data centres,' showcased at investor meet in Mumbai.
Portfolio for data center customers includes entire grid integration: GIS, dry transformers, power transformers, and services.
Currently evaluating how best to position and deploy the 'Grid to rack' offering for customers.
Data center customers are currently securing long lead items such as dry transformers and GIS.

subsections.label: Talent development and industry collaboration (Slide 9)
points: Hitachi Energy TEC trained 10 executives from Bhutan's Druk Green Power Corporation (DGPC) through a five-day GIS program combining technical expertise with hands-on factory exposure in commissioning, troubleshooting, and protection systems.
In partnership with NIT Warangal, hosted INNOTHON 3.0 with 127 participants across 28 teams developing AI/ML-powered digital twin solutions.
Participated in ELECRAMA's Flag off ceremony discussing India's growing global influence and opportunities from energy transition, smart grid expansion, and manufacturing growth.

subsections.label: Karjan transformer factory (Slide 11)
points: Construction began in June 2026 on Hitachi Energy India's 20th manufacturing facility in Karjan, Vadodara.
Investment reinforces commitment to India's energy transition, energy security, and 'Make in India' initiative.
New facility designed as a fully digital and smart manufacturing unit, leveraging advanced technologies to enhance quality, productivity and operational performance.

Targeted commissioning date of December 2028; facility will expand manufacturing footprint, strengthen local capabilities, and support growing demand for sustainable energy infrastructure in India and global markets.

subsections.label: Safety practices
points: Safety remains fundamental to license to operate; best-in-class safety practices embedded across factories and project site offices.
450+ life-saving rules inspections conducted and 800+ safety observation tools used during Q1 FY27, targeting a recordable injury frequency rate of 0.09.
All high-risk hazards identified during the period were closed following the inspections and observations conducted.
Continued implementation of health and safety programs and training initiatives across facilities to strengthen safety culture.

subsections.label: Backward integration / localization strategy
points: Capex aimed at increasing capacity and localizing components to remain competitive with global players (Korean, Mexican manufacturers), provided there is a level playing field.

Localization of more components intended to create an end-to-end manufacturing scenario in India over time; volume and other factors expected to provide cost leverage (management did not quantify a specific % cost reduction figure).

subsections.label: Export market
points: Export contribution on revenues is around 25%, described as the current run rate.
Company trending at 25%-26% exports on the order side.

BESS and data center focus is currently primarily domestic; domestic BESS requirements are strong given the mandate that every renewable energy project needs energy storage; company plans to validate technology first before scaling; order pipeline for exports remains robust.

subsections.label: Commodity price exposure
points: Presently no material commodity impact on the business; even if there is a small impact, it can be managed.
60%-65% of orders have pass-through commodity pricing terms; no commodity impact in this quarter per se.

points: Government allowing entry of 4 Chinese players into the market, catering more to GIS and transformer side, with a 60%-65% local content requirement.

Management view: more competition is welcome to meet demand-supply challenges, as long as there is a level playing field; company does not see any issue competing while ensuring margin ambitions are met.
Transformer and GIS competitors (including entities like TBEA) were already competing in some form; management does not foresee any material impact or major threat from this development.

subsections.label: Market drivers (Slide 5)
points: India's electricity demand expected to grow strongly over the coming decade; grid becoming increasingly complex with higher load densities, rising reliability requirements, and emerging demand drivers such as AI-enabled workloads.
Addressable market opportunities span renewable energy, transmission investments to integrate non-fossil fuel capacity, industrial capex cycle, data center investments, and electric vehicle adoption.
Improving DISCOM fundamentals supporting higher investments in distribution infrastructure.
These trends reinforce confidence in a multi-year growth opportunity.

subsections.label: FY27 priorities (Slide 14)
points: Focus on strengthening core businesses in Utilities and HVDC while ensuring continuity and resilience of installed base through Services business unit.
Committed to efficiently executing strong backlog, enhancing productivity, and maintaining highest standards of quality and customer satisfaction.
Well positioned to capitalize on emerging growth opportunities in BESS, renewable integration, data centers, and grid modernization.
Continued investment in people, technology, manufacturing capacity, and operational capabilities to support long-term sustainable growth.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Geopolitical challenges continue to affect the country, though underlying business fundamentals remain exceptionally strong.
Unrealized foreign exchange loss of INR 36.37 crs recorded during the quarter impacted EBITDA and increased exchange/commodity losses as a percentage of revenue.
Railway projects progressing slower than originally anticipated; expected to pick up from H2 of the year.
Transmission order mix showed a temporary downturn, characterized as a timing issue, not a major concern.
Entry of 4 Chinese players into GIS/transformer market with 60-65% local content requirement flagged as a competitive development, though management does not see material impact.
Macroeconomic uncertainties and project execution challenges noted as ongoing considerations in a dynamic environment.

subsections.label: ESG targets and action plan (Slide 4)
points: Company believes it is well positioned to achieve 2030 sustainability targets.
16% reduction in freshwater usage compared with 2019 baseline achieved through recycling initiatives and deployment of water-efficient fixtures; confident 2030 water target remains within reach.
Halol facility earned the Water Positive Index Certificate last quarter.
Gender diversity increased from 5.8% to over 10%, with a further target improvement of 3-4 percentage points by 2030.
Zero integrity incidents recorded during the year, reflecting uncompromising commitment to integrity.
Sustainability progress closely aligned with broader energy transition and India's commitment at COP26.

subsections.label: General outlook
points: Order inflows may vary quarter to quarter, but overall opportunity landscape continues to expand, giving confidence in future growth trajectory.
Strong order backlog combined with healthy bidding pipeline provides good visibility for future revenue growth.
Company remains focused on execution discipline, profitable growth, and delivering stakeholder value.
Record order backlog and healthy bidding pipeline provide strong visibility for growth going forward.

Management remains confident in ability to create long-term value while contributing to a resilient, secure, and sustainable energy future, backed by strong market fundamentals, robust order pipeline, and differentiated technology portfolio.
Company does not provide explicit forward-looking numeric guidance on orders/revenue.
Full greenfield HVDC project under bidding, expected to be awarded in approximately 6 months.
Data center project pipeline expected to be sustainable if ~15 GW target by 2030 materializes, contingent on government support.
Closing remarks: business executing well, market demand robust, pipeline stronger than ever, while remaining mindful of macroeconomic uncertainties and project execution challenges.

key_takeaways: We have started the FY27 on a strong note, delivering robust growth in both orders and revenues.
We began construction of Hitachi Energy India's 20th manufacturing facility in Karjan, Vadodara in June 2026.
On a comparable basis, order intake in Q1 FY27 increased by 26.1% YoY and 39.7% QoQ.
We closed the quarter with an order backlog of INR 32,222.1 crs, representing strong double-digit growth compared with Q1 FY26.
We delivered strong revenue growth of 68.6% YoY, driven by robust execution of our order backlog.
Disciplined execution and operating leverage resulted in a 120.2% YoY increase in Profit Before Tax (PBT), while operational EBITDA grew 135.0% YoY to INR 399.9 crs.
This EBITDA performance includes an unrealized foreign exchange loss of INR 36.37 crs recorded during the quarter.

Our record order backlog and healthy bidding pipeline provide strong visibility for growth, and we remain focused on translating these opportunities into disciplined execution and sustainable value creation.

quarters.summary: Hitachi Energy India closed FY26 with record order backlog (Rs 29,555.3 Crores, up 53.6% YoY) providing strong multi-quarter revenue visibility; management highlighted a temporary industry slowdown/geopolitical supply-chain pressure but reiterated a robust multi-year demand outlook driven by energy transition, grid expansion, electrification, data centers, renewables and energy storage. The Board approved an additional Rs 2,000 Crores capex (greenfield large power transformer facility at Karjan, Vadodara, Gujarat, plus two additional lines at Bangalore for power quality products), taking cumulative capex to ~Rs 4,000 Crores, with the new transformer facility targeted for commissioning by Q4 CY2028.

subsections.label: Order intake dynamics
points: Order intake for FY26 grew across sectors: industry, data centers, railways and renewables.
Small dip in transmission order intake was due to a mismatch in the value of large orders booked in FY26 compared to FY25 (large lumpy orders), not due to demand weakness.
On the order mix chart, the product segment took the lead, while utilities and direct end customers emerged as clear winners across their respective sectors and channels.
Management stated base orders (ex-services, ex-exports) had strong growth for the whole financial year, pushing back on analyst suggestion of a weak base order year.
Management noted that even excluding non-HVDC orders, there has been growth in the domestic order book.

Capacity that could have gone to some orders may instead be filled by the HVDC portfolio, which is one possible explanation for perceived softness in non-HVDC domestic order inflow, though management does not see this as an underlying weakness.

Transmission project delays flagged earlier in the year are viewed as behind the company now; transmission and renewable investment pipeline strong, along with some fossil power plants, data centers, semiconductor industry, battery-related industries, and automobile industry expansions.

subsections.label: HVDC pipeline
points: HVDC pipeline seen as very robust; one project already up for TBCB bidding, with at least 3-4 more projects expected in the pipeline over the next 2 years.
Pipeline is a mix of both LCC and VSC technology; company holds leadership position globally in both.

Company states no capacity limitation currently to take on more HVDC projects in the near term; capacity being built proactively since 2022 when HVDC/control production factory in Chennai was set up ahead of visible pipeline.

subsections.label: Exports strategy (3-pronged)
points: Allocated markets: long-term development of specific markets (Indian subcontinent — Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan — and Southeast Asian countries) together with local sales/marketing organizations; no two Hitachi Energy companies compete in the same market; sales made directly to third-party customers (e.g. GIS sold in Southeast Asia and to some European customers).

Global feeder factories: certain products manufactured only in India within the Hitachi Energy ecosystem (e.g. 66kV high circuit breakers, COMBIFLEX relays) and sold worldwide, directly to customers or via Hitachi Energy offices (related party).

Component feeder factories: India manufactures components that are part of a full product, sold to other Hitachi Energy factories globally (US, Germany, Sweden, Switzerland) — this is contract manufacturing, low risk with stable margin, and is a pass-through arrangement to the parent companies.

subsections.label: Data center and energy storage opportunity
points: Data centers coming up in India from a small base but growing at a much higher rate/percentage than other segments.
For every data center, ~15% of data center capex is addressable by Hitachi Energy.
Battery energy storage market seen at ~80 GW over next 5-6 years per CEA report, requiring significant new technology focus.

subsections.label: Segment leadership and growth areas
points: Company remains leader in core segments: utilities, HVDC, industries, data centers.
Actively expanding into high-growth areas such as energy storage, where strong and sustainable demand trends are seen.

Sharpening strategy to capture opportunities across services, exports and digital innovation; strengthening the service business in India is a key pillar for ensuring continuity/resilience of energy systems.
In the order book, transmission is the largest segment by far, followed by renewable, then industry, service and exports.

subsections.label: HVDC margin profile
points: HVDC described as margin-accretive but was not a very substantial share of revenue in the quarter or the year (~15% of FY26 revenue, ~Rs 1,100 Crores).
Company's focus remains on base business, service business, and export business in addition to HVDC as one of several levers.

subsections.label: Royalty and R&D structure
points: Company pays royalty to parent for continued access to new technologies/products even while manufacturing locally, to ensure availability of technologies consistent with global standards.

R&D spend is managed centrally by the parent, not locally by the India entity; new products for data centers, energy storage and other new segments are being sourced from parent and will be showcased at investor meet.

New capex/capacity investment is not related to local content requirements — company already exceeds recent government local content circular requirements; new capacity is driven purely by demand from renewable, transmission and data center segments.

subsections.label: Greenfield large power transformer facility - Karjan, Vadodara, Gujarat
points: Board approved additional Rs 2,000 Crores investment including establishment of greenfield large power transformer facility in Karjan, Vadodara, Gujarat.
This is an accelerated execution program targeting completion/manufacturing start by last quarter of calendar year 2028.
New facility will manufacture large power transformers and HVDC converter transformers for both VSC and LCC technology, plus large power transformers required for data centers.
This investment is over and above the capex program previously announced in October 2024; groundbreaking ceremony scheduled for June 12.
Projects from the Oct 2024 capex program (Rs 2,000 Crores) are on the ground and taking 3-4 years to complete.
New capacity addition is approximately 30 GVA baseline, potentially up to 40 GVA depending on product mix — this is additional capacity, roughly doubling existing capacity.
Capex driven purely by demand outlook (renewable, transmission, data centers), not by minimum local content regulatory requirements — company already exceeds local content norms.

subsections.label: Bangalore factory expansion (power quality)
points: Two additional lines being added at Bangalore factory for power quality products (7th and 8th lines, up from existing 6), due to strong demand growth for power quality products.
Rs 2,000 Crores capex is largely directed at expanding existing product capacity (large power transformers, power quality), not addressing any portfolio gaps.

subsections.label: HVDC and control production facility - Chennai
points: HVDC and control production factory set up in Chennai starting 2022, ahead of visible pipeline, in anticipation of future demand.
Additional transformer factory being set up to manufacture converter transformers in anticipation of HVDC and other demand.

subsections.label: Safety, sustainability and ESG
points: Zero fatalities during FY26, reflecting proactive safety culture and risk management.
Over 1,700 life-saving rule inspections conducted during the year.
Annual health checkups and ongoing safety awareness sessions form core part of employee/subcontractor wellbeing approach.
Company received several customer/partner awards during the quarter for enhancing safety culture at project sites.
Achieved 100% renewable energy in operations via rooftop solar and long-term power purchase agreements with solar developers.
Surpassed water reduction targets with 11% reduction from 2019 baseline through recycling initiatives and efficient fixtures.
Halol facility (Gujarat) earned a Water Positive Index certificate.
Halol and Mysore facilities certified platinum for zero waste to landfill.
Increased gender diversity substantially, reinforcing inclusive workplace commitment.
Zero integrity incidents recorded during the year.
ESG rating from Crisil improved to 61 (Strong); NSE rating increased to 62 (Adequate).

subsections.label: Export market allocation
points: Allocated export markets include the Indian subcontinent (Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan) and Southeast Asian countries, catered to exclusively by Hitachi Energy India (no competition among Hitachi Energy entities in these markets).
In Southeast Asian countries, the entire product portfolio is included as part of the allocated market.

Exports also go to Europe and other regions through global feeder factory arrangements and via Hitachi Energy offices worldwide (US, Germany, Sweden, Switzerland referenced as component/component feeder factory destinations).

subsections.label: Structural demand drivers
points: India's electricity demand poised for strong sustained growth over the coming decade, supported by industrial expansion, renewable integration, EV adoption and rapid scale-up of new-age load centers such as data centers.

Grid becoming more complex with higher load density, increasing reliability requirements, and new demand drivers such as AI-led workloads, driving significant investment across transmission, distribution and grid infrastructure.

Compelling opportunity across segments: strong momentum in renewables, transmission investment to integrate non-fossil capacity, visible industrial capex cycle, rising data center investment, and early-stage but accelerating EV penetration.
Improving DISCOM health enabling higher spending in distribution.

subsections.label: Customer engagement and industry positioning
points: Participated in India Energy Week 2026, engaging stakeholders and fostering global partnerships shaping the energy transition.
Hosted a pre-event as part of India's AI Impact Summit exploring the changing role of energy in the age of AI, with participation from Ministry of Power and Ministry of IT leadership.

Showcased product/solutions portfolio at Bharat Electricity Summit, one of the largest transmission energy events in the country; booth visited by Ministers of Power and Renewable Energy and other industry leaders.

subsections.label: Price escalation / commodity pass-through
points: Most of the portfolio has commodity price pass-through via price variation clauses built into contracts, applied openly and transparently to manage elevated metal prices and geopolitical-driven inflation.

Elevated freight/transport charges (partly due to Strait of Hormuz-related disruption) are harder to pass through; company is actively managing and looking at mitigation initiatives for this cost element.

subsections.label: AI acceleration and productivity
points: Kick-started 'AI Nexus' program, harnessing data analytics and AI to drive smarter, faster decisions and better outcomes.
Continued focus on productivity, operational excellence, quality and scalability.
Two clear stated priorities: sustaining growth momentum and improving efficiency across all areas of operations.

subsections.label: Notable project execution / commissioning
points: Successfully commissioned India's first city infeed project — Mumbai City infeed project (Adani), 1,000 MW on VSC-based HVDC technology, including design, engineering, supply, erection and commissioning of HVDC converter stations at Aarey and Kudus, supporting 1,000 MW into the Mumbai grid.
Other commissioned projects during the year: renewable substation at Barmer, transformer supply to leading utilities, and AIA substation in Rajasthan.
Comprehensive scope of work spans full value chain: design, engineering, manufacturing, supply, erection, testing and end-to-end commissioning.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and supply chain risk
points: Current geopolitical situation in the Middle East (including Strait of Hormuz-related disruption) has triggered pressure on supply chains, an industry-wide (not company-specific) temporary challenge; several mitigation measures have been put in place.
India remains exposed to global energy price volatility, though this strengthens the structural investment case for transmission and grid infrastructure.
Company navigated a temporary industry slowdown in the quarter while continuing to invest in long-term growth and margin resilience.

Elevated inflation and elevated metal/commodity prices are being managed via price variation clauses in most contracts; elevated freight/transport charges are harder to pass through and are being actively managed.

subsections.label: Forward outlook (qualitative)
points: Management does not provide specific forward-looking numeric guidance on order inflow, but describes pipeline as very strong in renewables, data centers, transmission and other projects, with industry showing some intermittency but improving.
Confident in a multi-year growth opportunity across segments, underpinned by strong order backlog, technology leadership, execution track record and customer intimacy.
Company will continue to invest in capabilities — people, technology and capacity expansion — to support sustainable growth.
HVDC pipeline over next 2 years expected to include 3-4 more projects; company states no capacity constraint to pursue these.
Data center capacity in India projected to grow 6-9x over the next 5 years from current <2 GW base to a projected 13-18 GW.

guidance_ledger.metric: New greenfield large power transformer facility commissioning
guidance_ledger.statement: We would like to complete this state-of-the-art Greenfield transformer factory to produce our large power transformers and HVDC converter transformer by last quarter of 2028 calendar year.
We are going to create anywhere between 30 GVA to 40 GVA... additional capacity, doubling the capacity.
With this, our total cumulative capex stands close to Rs. 4,000 Crores.
We are doing the groundbreaking ceremony on 12th of June.
At least in the next 2 years, we are talking about anywhere between 3 projects, if not, 4.
We don't give any forward-looking numbers going forward... but our pipeline is very strong in renewable, data center... transmission and other projects.
Projections are anywhere between 13 to 18 gigawatts depending upon which data... 6 to 9x of the capacities from here.
Almost 80 gigawatts of battery storage for the next 5, 6 years, as you can see from the CEA report.
Our average exports are around 25% to 30% (excluding large HVDC lump orders).

guidance_ledger.metric: Explicit numeric order/revenue guidance for FY27
guidance_ledger.statement: As you know we don't give any forward-looking numbers going forward.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical situation in the Middle East pressuring supply chains
risk_register.note: Industry-wide temporary challenge; company has put mitigation measures in place.
India remains exposed, though it strengthens the structural case for transmission/grid investment.

risk_register.risk: Temporary industry slowdown in the quarter
risk_register.note: Company navigated this while continuing to invest in long-term growth and margin resilience; management views this as behind them now.
Managed via price variation clauses/commodity pass-through built into most contracts.

risk_register.risk: Elevated freight/transport charges (Strait of Hormuz related)
risk_register.note: Cannot always be passed through; company is actively looking at mitigation initiatives.

risk_register.risk: Transmission project delays earlier in the year
risk_register.note: Contributed to a small dip in transmission order growth in FY26; management views this as behind them now.

risk_register.risk: Sequential gross margin contraction due to product mix
risk_register.note: Attributed to product mix change quarter-to-quarter, not a structural issue; full-year gross margin still improved ~200 bps.

themes.label: Order backlog strength
themes.note: Record order backlog of Rs 29,555.3 Crores, up 53.6% YoY, providing multi-quarter revenue visibility.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: Additional Rs 2,000 Crores capex for greenfield large power transformer facility (Karjan, Vadodara) and Bangalore power quality lines, taking cumulative capex to ~Rs 4,000 Crores, targeting 30-40 GVA additional capacity by Q4 CY2028.

themes.label: HVDC growth lever
themes.note: HVDC pipeline robust (3-4 projects over next 2 years), margin-accretive but only ~15% of FY26 revenue; company sees no capacity constraint.

themes.label: Export strategy
themes.note: 3-pronged export strategy (allocated markets, global feeder factories, component feeder factories) with exports at ~25-30% of revenue/orders ex large HVDC lumps.

themes.label: Margin improvement
themes.note: FY26 PBT margin 16.9% vs 8.1% in FY25; PAT margin 12.1% vs 6%; gross margin improved ~200 bps to 40%.

themes.label: Data center and energy storage opportunity
themes.note: India data center capacity projected to grow 6-9x over 5 years from <2GW; ~80GW battery storage opportunity per CEA report over next 5-6 years.

themes.label: Geopolitical and supply chain pressure
themes.note: Middle East geopolitical situation and Strait of Hormuz disruption pressuring supply chains and freight costs, an industry-wide temporary challenge being mitigated.

key_takeaways: Record order backlog of Rs 29,555 crores as of March 31, 2026, which provides a strong revenue visibility for several quarters going forward.

The successful commissioning of India's first city infeed project in Mumbai further demonstrates our execution capabilities and reinforces our position as a trusted partner in critical grid infrastructure.
We have navigated a temporary industry slowdown while continuing to invest in long-term growth opportunities and margin resilience.

During our Q4FY26 Board Meeting, the Board approved an additional investment of Rs. 2,000 Crores... establishment of greenfield large power transformer facility in Karjan, Vadodara in Gujarat... to produce our large power transformers and HVDC converter transformer by last quarter of 2028 calendar year.
With this, our total cumulative capex stands close to Rs. 4,000 Crores.

For the full year period, we reported... order... growth of 1.6% in FY26 to Rs. 18,456.5 Crores. And the revenue on a complete year Rs. 8,147.7 Crores, a growth of 27.6% and PBT Rs. 1,375.2 Crores, a growth of 166.3% and PAT is Rs. 987.8 Crores, a growth of 157.3% and EBITDA margin on an annualized basis is 15.4%.
We are proud to report zero fatalities during the financial year just concluded, reflecting the effectiveness of our proactive safety culture and risk management measures.
HVDC is margin-accretive, and it was not very substantial in this quarter or in this year... our HVDC revenues out of Rs. 8,000 Crores is around Rs. 1,100 Crores.
pressing_questions: The base orders look very weak for this year. I mean, if I remove services and the export, the base ordering looks to be very weak for FY26. In fact, there could be maybe a decline Y-o-Y. So, what is your commentary on the base ordering?
The gross margins contracted on a sequential quarter-on-quarter basis by a significant amount. What was the mix change or factors that drove this outcome?

Overall, your order inflows for the fiscal grew by 1.6%, but excluding HVDC orders from the base for both the years, the non HVDC order inflow, at least the domestic non-HVDC order inflow was falling in FY26 over FY25. What led to this outcome and what is the outlook going forward?
In the current inflationary commodity price environment, how effective has the price escalation process been in protecting the margins of your HVDC and transformer contracts?

quarters.summary: Management flagged continued net decline in paying suppliers due to moderation in gross adds and elevated Silver-tier churn, while Platinum/Gold cohorts kept upselling well; the company is investing in AI, trust/verification and a new NBFC subsidiary (IndiaMART Finance Limited) for short-term transaction financing to support marketplace effectiveness, with BUSY Infotech guided to sustain ~27-30% CAGR over the next couple of years and an aspirational 35-40% CAGR over five years.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margins continued to be elevated on account of savings arising from lower customer acquisition and operating leverage.
Increase in Other income was primarily due to mark-to-market gains on the treasury portfolio.

subsections.label: New subsidiary
points: Board of Directors has approved the creation of new subsidiary, IndiaMART Finance Limited, which will serve MSMEs for their short-term credit requirement.

subsections.label: Supplier base decline drivers
points: Decrease in paying supplier base primarily attributed to moderation in gross addition as well as elevated churn at the Silver subscription tier.
Platinum and Gold subscribers continue to have good upsell and retention rate.

subsections.label: Buyer enquiry trend
points: Buyer enquiries have typically been flattish, plus/minus 1%, at unique business enquiries of 26-27 million.

Advertising spend of Rs. 7-8 crore per quarter over the last 3 quarters has shifted the buyer base from organic decline towards higher-ARPU, more monetisable buyer categories (top 10% categories), rather than growing overall buyer numbers.
Overall buyer number stagnation is a function of advertising being targeted only at monetisable categories/geographies, not spread broadly.

Primary buyer acquisition source (Google) shows cannibalisation due to non-organic-link blocks (popular products, Q&A, sponsored links) pushing organic results below the first fold on mobile; company is experimenting with expanding advertising to Facebook/Meta, Instagram, YouTube to source additional buyers.

Decline in unique business enquiries (11% YoY) is difficult to fully attribute: ~4-5% linked to OTP verification; remainder uncertain, possibly related to internal changes, traffic migrating to LLMs, or macro factors like war/US tension.

subsections.label: Churn cohort analysis
points: Silver monthly churn unchanged at 7%, contributing to continued flattish-to-negative total customer numbers.
First 12 months is the biggest churn/retention issue even within Silver tier; renewal and retention rate roughly doubles from the second year onwards.
Segmented verification and targeting initiatives are underway but not expected to yield quick churn containment - effects likely visible after about a year.

subsections.label: Net growth philosophy
points: Management indicated it will not accept structurally higher churn and simply push gross adds, citing CAC/LTV risk: acquiring similar/low-end customers with greater intensity would raise CAC and lower LTV.
Company must fix product-market fit (renewal behavior) before pressing on growth pedal.

There are areas of category-based/tiered pricing (three-tier pricing system) where money is being left on the table, particularly within Platinum, based on ROI/value of product or number of buyers per product.

subsections.label: Buyer verification depth
points: Paid customer base: ~99% email ID verified, ~99% phone verified, ~99% GST verified.
Free customer base: 100% email and phone verified; GST verified at about 50%, moving toward 80-90%.
Bank account verification just started; expected to cross 50% within next year and 80% within two years.
On buyer side, only ~10 million of ~40 million total active buyers have GST/verified business buyer status; increasing this is still a pending initiative.

subsections.label: BUSY billing growth optics
points: Q1 FY26 (prior year) had about Rs. 10 crores of one-time winbacks, and that growth rate was also significantly higher than normal; excluding that one-time advantage, normalised growth in the current quarter would be about 30%.
Deferred revenues and recognised revenues growth is at a more normalised level of 30% to 40%.

subsections.label: Product launch
points: Launched a new version of BUSY called BUSY Magic, which has a completely revamped UI/UX.
Investments in improving product and overall user experience are seen as creating a foundation for the next phase of growth for BUSY.

subsections.label: Drivers of revenue-per-license growth (28% CAGR breakup)
points: Growth is led by sale of new licenses.
Increase in prices of products.
Improvement in the overall ratio of customers renewing year-on-year.
Increasing proportion of customers taking add-on products like the mobile app within BUSY.

subsections.label: Forward trajectory for licenses/ARPU
points: Company is migrating from licensing to a subscription model.
Aim to accelerate new license sales growth to about 15-20% in the immediate year or two (vs historical 10%).
Substantial value still left on the table in realisation from existing customers relative to value derived by them, expected to be captured gradually as customers accept higher payments over time.
New product under preparation to be accessible on desktop, cloud, and mobile phone (single product across platforms) to support better ARPU.
Combination of price increases and value-added service adoption expected to drive ARPU improvements continuously over next 3 to 5 years.

subsections.label: AI evolution initiatives
points: Streamlined discovery process via standardised cataloguing, intelligent matchmaking, and content moderation.
Operating one of the largest agentic call handling systems in the country, autonomously handling over 1 lakh calls per day.

AI voice generation quality has crossed a threshold enabling natural, human-like interaction; buyer call centre upgraded from manual (~80,000 calls/day) to AI voice call centre; initial cost gains were modest but voice quality now supports buyer verification and buyer intent understanding.

AI provides 10x better and 10x faster content aggregation and audit versus prior human BPO/parsing methods; value creation in this area is still in early stages, with most value expected to accrue toward end of next year.
Potential AI application in security/trust building via social trust built from content aggregation, beyond current user-declared ID-based trust.

More complex use cases like CRM ticket resolution or complex procurement solutions expected to take years to build out given rapid technological change in voice, text, and video over the last 2-3 years.

subsections.label: Trust and safety features
points: Multi-layer KYC process, TrustSEAL verification, transparent supplier ratings and reviews already in place.
New seller verification feature helps buyers verify sellers before making payments.
Buyer Payment Protection Program introduced for eligible purchases with TrustSEAL verified suppliers, offering payment assurance of up to Rs. 5 lakh.
Moving toward 100% OTP verification for buyers (previously only phone-number based) to reduce unnecessary AI-based agent parsing from bot/agent traffic.
Deploying further identity verification beyond phone number and GST, including APIs and self-declared buyer information.

Launched a 'know your seller'/seller verification page where buyers can input a number, GST number, or email ID to view a seller trust profile - addressing cases where IndiaMART introduces buyers to additional suppliers beyond their initial selection.

Introducing bank account verification for TrustSEAL/paid sellers so buyers can make verified transfers rather than relying on QR codes or NEFT/RTGS instructions sent via WhatsApp that could be spoofed.

subsections.label: LLM/search traffic dynamics
points: Considerable traffic is shifting from search engines to LLMs; unclear whether LLMs will become the dominant search paradigm or fully absorb search/internet traffic.

Tension exists: withholding content from LLMs risks omission from LLM responses; fully exposing content risks LLMs retaining most value and returning little traffic (unlike Google's more 'give and take' link economy).
Management expects a hybrid model (like Google/Gemini) to emerge over time but cannot predict the outcome.

LLM traffic attribution analytics are still nascent; expected to take about a year for a clear winner or 2-3 dominant players to emerge in traffic analytics/webmaster tools distinguishing agent, bot, and LLM traffic - this was the reason company stopped reporting traffic data about a year ago.
No official company position on regulatory guardrails around LLM data practices in India.
