subsections.label: Semaglutide launch performance
points: Company launched first generic semaglutide vial on day 1 in India; could not launch pen on day 1 due to logistical reasons, launched pen about a month later (announced March, launched April).
Vial pricing sells for less than INR1,000/month vs pen normalized at INR3,000-4,000/month, capturing price-sensitive market segment unwilling to pay for pen.
Vial is the only generic in the market currently; pen faces more competition and company is getting 'some share' there but doing better with vial.
Market remains super competitive but company achieved a 'reasonably good start' and disrupted the market, though pen still dominates overall market sales value.
Product sold partly through digital pharma platforms though management doesn't have full visibility into specific channel partners; products require prescription.

subsections.label: Pomalidomide
points: No substantial pomalidomide revenue bump seen this quarter; launch was fairly competitive with multiple generics (4-5 players) securing exclusivity in the first wave, contrary to expectations of a clean 6-month exclusivity bump.

subsections.label: Crop Health Sciences (Agrichem) business detail
points: Business is being demerged, partly because end customers for pharma vs agrichem are quite different, allowing more focused approach.
Strategy mirrors pharma approach: seeking differentiated, patent-controlled molecules with limited competition rather than commodity products.
Only 3-4 years of commercial presence in this segment; past 2 years spent mostly learning how the market works.

Growth from INR60 crores (last year) to INR140 crores this year, with aspirations to grow significantly further, driven by new product launches, channel partner penetration (currently fewer channel partners than peers), and people additions.

Input raw material costs for agrichem have risen 25-30% due to West Asia war-related inflation; ~half of kharif season procurement was already completed allowing near-term price management, but pricing outlook beyond that is uncertain and being closely monitored versus competitive behavior.
Agrichem business has high exposure to domestic sales (limited exports), so it is more impacted by input cost inflation than export-oriented businesses.

subsections.label: South Africa / Adcock contribution
points: Adcock currently represents about 22% of NATCO's normalized base earnings this quarter.
NATCO holds ~35% stake in Adcock via associate accounting (see-through only on 35%); hopes to increase shareholding over time if major shareholder provides opportunity.
Adcock positions NATCO as the #2 pharma company in South Africa, achieved via acquisition rather than slow organic build (contrasted with Brazil's ~10-year organic build).

subsections.label: Diversification of earnings base
points: Earnings now come from 5 key markets: India, U.S., Brazil, Canada, and South Africa (via Adcock associate) — versus historical over-reliance on the U.S.

Management goal is to shift earnings mix so base business contributes ~70% of profit and first-to-file/special products contribute 25-30% of profit, reversing the historical ratio, to reduce earnings volatility over the next 5 years.

subsections.label: NRC-2694 (internal innovative pipeline)
points: Only active internal innovative pipeline asset currently running; too early stage to report commercialization timeline.

subsections.label: eGenesis investment (external innovative pipeline)
points: USD 8 million investment in eGenesis, described as the most exciting innovative pipeline bet.
eGenesis is the first company globally to transplant a genetically modified pig kidney into a human; 2 patients treated so far, both did well for about 6 months before complications.
Key open question is determining the right immunosuppression dose to make the therapy work longer-term; company is recruiting more patients and expects more transplants in the next 12-18 months.
eGenesis is also exploring liver (in addition to kidney) applications.
Management characterizes this as a 'moonshot'/binary bet — cannot predict timeline or quantum of any topline contribution; will provide patient updates as available.

subsections.label: R&D filing strategy
points: FY26 filings (7-8 in US) did not include any major first-to-file wins; competition (7-8 or even 15-20 competing filers) has increased for commodity-type filings.
Strategy is to target either products where competition is limited or identify novel first-to-file opportunities — described as 'winner takes all' in the US market, especially for NCE-1 filings.

Company references past FTF successes: ibrutinib (30-month exclusivity, already approved), olaparib (hoping for 30-month exclusivity subject to FDA clearance), carfilzomib (FTF), and semaglutide filings in pipeline.
Aim is to secure 2-3 more FTF/complex opportunities over the next 3-4 years to sustain the pipeline for the next 7-8 years.

subsections.label: Plant inspection status
points: Kothur (formulation facility), Chennai (API facility), and Mekaguda (API facility) were all inspected in 2025/last financial year, all cleared and received EIRs.
Vizag facility has not been inspected in a long time; an inspection is expected sometime this year.

subsections.label: Regional performance and outlook
points: Brazil doing well, with multiple first-time oncology portfolio launches; positioned as a major growth trigger for FY27.
Canada business described as stable and comfortable; expected to grow 10-15% in FY27, with bigger launches expected in FY28 rather than FY27.
Semaglutide not yet filed in Canada; company has other oncology products coming through in both Brazil and Canada that will drive earnings.
New products (oncology pipeline) in Brazil and Canada expected to receive approval in H2 FY27, with earnings impact expected in FY28.
Agrichem/crop health business exports are minimal — predominantly a domestic (India) business.
Export-oriented pharma businesses have been relatively less impacted by input cost inflation/exchange rate versus domestic-focused businesses, partly offset by currency depreciation.

subsections.label: South Africa/Adcock strategic rationale
points: World pharma market requires presence in ~10-15 key markets to be successful; Adcock acquisition allows NATCO to build scale in South Africa that would not have been achievable organically.
Growing organically in a competitive generic environment is difficult; inorganic/bold acquisitions are necessary to acquire share, size, and scale.

Expected return on South Africa investment is currently only slightly better than bank interest, but expected to improve to 15-20% return on capital (or more) over 2-3 years as new initiatives (oncology pipeline, GLP) bear fruit.

subsections.label: Gestation periods across markets
points: Brazil returns being seen now after a ~10-year journey; building from scratch takes 5-7 years.
Canada business is stable.
US front-end (bought a few years ago) still losing money; expected to break even this year.
South Africa investment expected to take 3-4 years to show full value.
Indonesia business still losing money.
Acquired businesses generally take 2-3 years to show outcomes versus 5-7 years if built from scratch, partly due to 2-3 year regulatory approval timelines.

subsections.label: Logistics impact from West Asia war
points: Company had to reroute shipments from traditional carriers due to the Middle East conflict, leading to increased freight expenses, though product supply was maintained.
Pharma business currently has a reasonable amount of inventory buffer, so summer input cost increases are not expected to impact the June/August quarter; impact may be seen later in the year.
Agrichem business had already completed about half of kharif season procurement, allowing near-term price management despite 25-30% raw material cost increases.

subsections.label: Semaglutide competitive positioning
points: Vial-only-generic positioning allows capture of a price-sensitive market segment unwilling to pay pen pricing (INR3,000-4,000) but willing to pay ~INR1,000 for vial.
Pen market remains highly competitive and dominates overall category sales value despite vial's price advantage.

subsections.label: US filing competitive landscape
points: For most generic filings, there are typically 7-8, or even 15-20, competing filers, making such filings largely commodity-type with limited earnings upside.
Real value creation requires filing where competition is limited or being genuinely first-to-file, which is rare (a handful of successes over a 3-4 year period is considered a great outcome).

subsections.label: Ongoing M&A pursuit
points: Company is actively running a couple of acquisition transactions/negotiations but nothing has reached announceable stage.
Hopeful of closing at least one acquisition in FY27, though management stresses 'until it's done, it's not done'.
Management is bullish on acquisitions outside India (citing more reasonable valuations abroad) versus within India.
Rationale: any transaction should strategically strengthen the core business and build geographical distribution.
INR2,400 crores net cash provides comfort to pursue one or two large acquisitions.

subsections.label: Crop Health Sciences demerger
points: Company is in the process of demerging the Crop Health Sciences (agrichem) business, partly to allow a more focused approach given differing end customers versus the pharma business.

subsections.label: Capital allocation philosophy vs. buyback
points: Management explicitly declined to pursue buybacks currently, preferring to deploy cash toward acquisitions that build a more diversified, long-term global company with more stable earnings; buyback described as something that 'can also be considered at the right time'.

subsections.label: Long-term company vision
points: Aspiration to build NATCO into a company with more geographical diversification and less earnings volatility, akin to larger global generics companies (referenced aspirationally to Dr. Reddy's/Sun Pharma scale).
Combined NATCO + Adcock turnover is approaching $1 billion in revenue, described by management as having 'built a global company' with modest capital.
Vision over next 5 years is to shift earnings mix so base business contributes ~70% of profit vs. 25-30% from first-to-file/special products (reversing historical ratio) to reduce volatility.

subsections.label: West Asia (Middle East) war impact
points: Caused rerouting of shipments away from traditional carriers, increasing freight expenses, though supply continuity was maintained.

Driving input raw material cost inflation, with 25-30% increase seen in agrichem raw materials; pharma inputs also rising but company holds sufficient inventory buffer to defer impact to later quarters.
Domestic-focused businesses (like agrichem, which is predominantly domestic) are more exposed to this cost inflation than export-oriented businesses, which see some offset from currency depreciation.

subsections.label: Loss of lenalidomide (Revlimid) exclusivity
points: Primary driver of YoY revenue and profit decline in FY26; earnings this year are being generated with 'practically no lenalidomide or very competitive lenalidomide' contribution.

subsections.label: Cyclical/roller-coaster business nature
points: Business inherently has boom years (driven by exclusivities/jackpots) followed by dip years when those exclusivities lapse or become competitive; FY27 characterized as one such dip/base year.
No major exclusivities expected in FY27; some expected to trigger in FY27-28 timeframe and beyond.

subsections.label: Increased competition in filings
points: US generic filings increasingly commodity-type due to 7-8 or up to 15-20 competing filers, reducing the frequency of true first-to-file wins.
Pomalidomide launch was far more competitive than expected, with 4-5 players securing exclusivity in the first wave.

subsections.label: eGenesis investment risk
points: Described by management as a 'moonshot' — binary outcome risk; correct immunosuppression dosing remains unresolved and timeline to any commercial/topline impact is unknown.

key_figures.label: Earnings CAGR expectation from FY28 onwards

subsections.label: FY27 outlook framing
points: FY27 is framed as a 'base year' settling around INR700-750 crores PAT, with South African associate profit assumed within this projection.
Guidance built with 'some buffer' given uncertainty from war-related factors; management cannot predict everything that will happen during the year.
No major new exclusivities expected in FY27; growth triggers are semaglutide vial, Brazil oncology launches, and incremental South Africa/Adcock consolidation.

subsections.label: Post-FY27 growth trajectory
points: Management expects some exclusivities to trigger in FY27-28, with earnings growth becoming visible from FY28 onwards.

Expects earnings to compound 15-25% annually starting FY28, driven by level of exclusivity achieved and market share, positioning FY27 as a stable base from which more predictable compounding growth follows versus historical one-off-driven earnings.
US, Brazil, and Canada are all expected to drive earnings growth from FY27-28 onward.
New oncology pipeline products for Brazil/Canada expected to receive approval in H2 FY27 (H2 of financial year 2026-27), with earnings impact expected in FY28.

guidance_ledger.statement: Our expectation is that we should do about INR3,400 crores to INR3,500 crores of revenue.
Our PAT expectation is between INR700 crores to INR750 crores.
Our South African associate firm should do, depending on the exchange rate, about $580 million to $600 million of revenue.
The PAT expectation of that is about $47 million to $48 million, again, subject to how the exchange rate moves and other war-related factors.
Including the surcharge, it would be around 25%.

We see that our earnings should compound around 15% to 25% every year starting from '28... From there onwards, we will be compounded growing around 15% to 25% depending on the level of exclusivity and how much market share we have.
We are thinking that we should be able to do about INR75 crores to INR100 crores annualized over the year.
We are expecting that business should go to INR55 million to INR60 million this year.
Canada, we are expecting will grow around 10% to 15%.
In terms of like R&D expenditure next year, I think we expect to spend about 7% to 9%.
Hopefully, this year, we are trying another 8, 9. So trying to target a couple of complex and first to files. Hopefully, we'll have 1 or 2 this year.
U.S., we just bought a front end about a few years ago. Still is losing money. So hopefully, this year, we'll be able to break even.

guidance_ledger.metric: South Africa investment return on capital
guidance_ledger.statement: Over a period of time, you will see the benefit where we'll be able to see about 15% to 20% return on capital or even more.
H2 of financial year '26, '27, we're expecting approval. Based on that, we expect the earnings impact will be in '27, '28.
Hopefully, we'll be able to close something in financial year '27... hopefully, we'll be able to achieve something in this financial year as well.

guidance_ledger.metric: Base business vs special product profit mix
guidance_ledger.statement: In an ideal world, I would want our base revenue to contribute 70% of our profit and the first to file or special product to contribute 25% to 30%. Earlier, the ratio was the other way around.

risk_register.note: Required rerouting shipments from traditional carriers, increasing freight expenses, though supply was maintained.

risk_register.risk: Input raw material cost inflation from war-related factors
risk_register.note: Agrichem raw materials up 25-30%; pharma inputs also rising but buffered by existing inventory until later in the year.
Primary driver of YoY revenue/profit decline; earnings now generated with practically no lenalidomide contribution.

risk_register.risk: Cyclical/roller-coaster earnings nature of the generics business
risk_register.note: Management describes recurring pattern of boom years from exclusivities followed by dip years; FY27 flagged as a dip/base year with no major exclusivities.

risk_register.risk: Increased competition in first-to-file/complex generic filings
risk_register.note: 7-8 or up to 15-20 competing filers common; pomalidomide launch was far more competitive than expected with 4-5 players securing exclusivity.
Correct immunosuppression dosing remains unresolved; outcome described as binary with unknown timeline to any commercial impact.
US front end still losing money since acquisition a few years ago; hoped to break even this year.
Indonesia business still losing money, company wants to catch up.

risk_register.risk: Exchange rate volatility affecting South Africa/Adcock guidance
risk_register.note: Revenue and PAT guidance for South African associate explicitly 'depending on the exchange rate' and 'subject to how the exchange rate moves and other war-related factors'.

themes.label: Exclusivity cliff / one-off earnings volatility
themes.note: Loss of lenalidomide exclusivity drove FY26 decline and FY27 is guided as a subdued base year with no major exclusivities.

themes.label: Geographic earnings diversification
themes.note: Earnings now come from 5 markets (India, US, Brazil, Canada, South Africa via Adcock) versus historical US concentration, aimed at reducing volatility.

themes.label: M&A / inorganic growth strategy
themes.note: Company is running ongoing acquisition negotiations, prefers deploying INR2,400 crores net cash toward acquisitions over buybacks, targeting deals outside India.

themes.label: GLP-1/semaglutide launch traction
themes.note: First-generic vial launch doing well due to price-sensitive segment capture, but pen launch delayed and highly competitive; annualized sales guided at INR75-100 crores.

themes.label: West Asia war cost/logistics impact
themes.note: Conflict drove freight cost increases via rerouting and 25-30% raw material inflation, with domestic-facing agrichem business more exposed than export-oriented pharma.

themes.label: First-to-file pipeline competitiveness
themes.note: Increasing competition (7-20 filers) has reduced FTF win rate; pomalidomide launch was more competitive than expected with 4-5 exclusivity holders.

themes.label: Innovative/breakthrough pipeline optionality (eGenesis)
themes.note: USD 8 million eGenesis investment in genetically modified pig kidney transplants described as exciting but binary 'moonshot' with unresolved dosing questions.

key_takeaways: NATCO recorded consolidated total revenue of INR4,375.9 crores for the year ended March 31, 2026, as against INR4,784 crores for the last year.
The net profit for the period on a consolidated basis was INR1,418.5 crores as against INR1,883.4 crores last year.
For the fourth quarter, which ended March 31, 2026, the company recorded a net revenue of INR816.9 crores on a consolidated basis as against INR1,287.3 crores during fourth quarter of last year.
The profit for the fourth quarter on a consolidated basis was INR269 crores, including the share of profit of associates, as against INR406 crores same period last year.

Net profit for the quarter and financial year includes a onetime benefit of INR115 crores as the company has elected to move to the new tax regime from FY '26-'27 and has remeasured its deferred tax assets on MAT credit and other deferred tax assets/liabilities.

For the quarter, revenue from the associate company, Adcock Ingram Holdings Limited, South Africa was at INR1,208.2 crores and profit after tax was at INR102.5 crores. NATCO's share of profit based on the current holding stood at INR35.7 crores.
Our expectation is, Rahul, that we should do about INR3,400 crores to INR3,500 crores of revenue. Our PAT expectation is between INR700 crores to INR750 crores.

In addition to that, our South African associate firm should do, depending on the exchange rate, about $580 million to $600 million of revenue. And the PAT expectation of that is about $47 million to $48 million.
I think we see that our earnings should compound around 15% to 25% every year starting from '28.
pressing_questions: Over the last several quarters, shareholders have been waiting for the meaningful value creation. Can you please explain what are the key triggers that will improve the investor confidence and will drive growth in the coming year?
FY '26 was a challenging year compared to FY '25. What is giving the management confidence that FY '27 will be a better year for share?
Sir, is there any chance the company will get a sustainable and stable profits in the future because we cannot endure this roller coaster like revenues and profit dips?
Sir, so we are 100% control of what we do... So we have a lot of cash. So are we not at all open to buybacks at a certain price point?

KISSHT.about: Incorporated in 2016, OnEMI Technology Solutions Limited is a technology-enabled lender in India, primarily offering digital loans through its mobile application for various consumption and business needs.[1]

quarters.summary: Management reiterated it remains firmly on track to deliver/over-deliver the FY27 guidance set last quarter across AUM growth (>40%, expected to be over-delivered), Gross NPA, credit cost (15% YoY reduction), ROA and ROE, aided by operating leverage, cost-of-borrowing reduction and continued shift toward high-quality customers; cost of borrowing is guided to fall by a minimum of 100bps in H2 FY27, with further gains possible on a ratings upgrade in FY28.

key_figures.label: Total income as % of average AUM change
Incremental borrowing cost reduction vs FY26 average

subsections.label: Revenue margin drivers
points: Total income as a share of average AUM fell 249 bps over the quarter, described as deliberate and part of a conscious strategy to acquire a higher proportion of high-quality, lower-risk customers who are priced lower.

Rising share of off-book lending (from 49.7% to 53.6%) also contributed to the reduction in revenue margin, since off-book lending carries lower revenue margin (service fee over cost of funds) though PPOP has continued to improve despite this.
Management stated that despite margin compression, the benefit of better risk and lower cost from higher-quality customers has been unilaterally positive.

subsections.label: Balance sheet strength
points: Balance sheet strengthened considerably in the quarter on the back of the IPO completed in May 2026, raising approximately INR 850 crores.
Net worth grew to INR 2,245 crores, nearly four times its level in March 2023, built on retained earnings, organic profitability and the IPO proceeds.
Funding remains balanced, supported by more than 45 lending partners.
Capital adequacy at the NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% in Q1 FY27 from 25.3% in Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Cost of funds trajectory
points: Given the equity raise, hardly any incremental debt was raised in Q1 as the company was capital surplus, hence limited difference in cost of borrowing between Q4 and Q1.
Only one incremental debt raise occurred in Q1 FY27, at a fully loaded cost of ~12.9%.
Incremental borrowing cost was ~150 bps lower than the average FY26 borrowing cost; some Q3/Q4 borrowing (post Fitch A- rating in November) had already come in at rates ~100 bps lower.
Guidance is for cost of borrowing to drop by 100 bps in H2 FY27 as old higher-cost debt (18-24 month tenure) runs off the book.

Reported cost of borrowing increase versus last quarter was clarified as an accounting anomaly from switching from monthly average debt AUM to daily average debt AUM (interest is paid on daily balance); on a daily-average basis there was actually a ~10 bps improvement.

Active engagement ongoing with India Ratings and CRISIL; management is cautiously optimistic about a ratings upgrade given risk performance improvement, higher capitalization, and profitability; any upgrade would not meaningfully impact FY27 cost of borrowing but would meaningfully impact FY28.

subsections.label: NIM/yield disclosure
points: Company will consider disclosing product-wise (LAP vs PL) NIM and yield starting next quarter; currently only on-balance sheet NIM/yield disclosed (32% average yield, 18% spread).
Off-balance sheet economics are booked as servicing/fee income rather than interest income/cost, so NIM is not directly comparable/disclosed for that book.

key_figures.label: LAP share of total AUM prior quarter
LAP customers sourced from existing PL base

subsections.label: LAP business build-out
points: LAP business, started two years back, comprises model-based underwriting, branch-led fulfilment, smart document processing, and AI-validated property valuation — described as the first of its kind in India, not a plain-vanilla LAP offering.
LAP AUM reached INR 617 crores across 101 branches in 8 states, rising to 7.7% of total AUM from 7.3% the prior quarter.
LAP yield ranges 16-23/24%, averaging 21.8%.
Management is confident the risk quality in LAP will hold up well over time based on how risk curves and DPD-5/15/30 payout patterns are shaping up.
LAP cannot grow as fast as personal loans but is growing well as a proportion of the business.
LAP is expected to achieve breakeven around Q3 of this year (FY27); until then it creates an expected drag on overall profitability as part of the plan.

Branch profitability for LAP is achieved faster (7-8 months) than typical industry benchmark (16-18 months) because more than 40% of LAP customers are sourced from the existing personal loan customer base, reducing sourcing costs.
Early bucket LAP loans (originated 1.5-2 years back) are performing well, arguably reflecting extra prudence in underwriting.
LAP ROE target is also 20%+, same as personal loan business — the business is not ROE dilutive and helps spread fixed/indirect expenses.

subsections.label: Personal loan strategy
points: Personal loan business viewed as massive opportunity; company has grown more than 60% every year over the last five to six years, with the personal loan book growing 73% YoY in FY26.
Personal loan yield is 29-30% base rate, or 36-37% all-in including fees.
Repeat, high-quality customers are moving to longer tenures, which will make disbursement growth slower than AUM growth going forward.

subsections.label: Mutual fund distribution (new fee income line)
points: Company has begun building capabilities in mutual fund distribution, since a large proportion of customers have invested in SIPs and mutual funds over time.
Subsidiary has already secured AMFI registration.

Fee income potential outside lending comes primarily from insurance/protection products (already generating fee income via credible partners) and savings/investment products (mutual funds, newly added); these add incremental revenue lines without altering the core business model.

key_figures.label: AUC (Area Under the Curve) of underwriting model
Model separation improvement vs bureau score alone
Voice agent efficiency vs human (early bucket tele-collection)
Own code written with AI assistance

subsections.label: Technology-first philosophy
points: Management describes the company as a technology company that lends, not a lender with bolted-on technology; underwriting and collections are built and run entirely in-house.
Underwriting models have evolved from simple decision trees to gradient boosting to today's transformer-based systems (the 'T' referenced is akin to GPT-style transformer architecture).
AUC (Area Under the Curve) of the underwriting model improved to 74% from 66% in 2023, with model separation now 2.5x better than bureau score alone.
Objective of models is to identify behavioural deterioration before it becomes delinquency.

subsections.label: AI in collections and fraud
points: AI is most visibly at work in collections and fraud detection; more than 95% of collections are handled in-house via 7,000+ field agents and 1,000+ tele-callers.
Voice agent efficiency in early-bucket tele-collection has improved to more than 80% of human efficiency, up from 70% previously.
Feature store watches 7,200+ signals for drift; multi-agent fraud system runs 50+ separate checks including deep fakes, forged documents, anomaly detection, and network fraud.
Many of these metrics have held steady since FY26, which management interprets as evidence that infrastructure is comfortably keeping pace with growth.

subsections.label: AI in support and engineering
points: AI-assisted support covers 100% of calls for quality review and has cut response time to under 90 seconds.
More than 80% of the company's own code is now written with AI assistance.
Management view: technology investment has made good judgment more scalable, not made lending less about judgment.

key_figures.label: Organic channel share of customer sourcing
Organic channel share expected stabilization range

subsections.label: Organic brand growth
points: Registered users reached 74.6 million, up 33% YoY, with cumulative customers served at 12.25 million, up 26% YoY.
Organic channel share has risen consistently over the last three years, from ~8% in 2022-23, to 23-24% average in FY26, to 27% in Q4 FY26, and 31% in Q1 FY27.
Management's own assessment is that as a high-quality credible brand is built, organic share will stabilize between 40% and 50%.

subsections.label: Product pecking order for future expansion (10-year horizon)
points: Pecking order for future lending products evaluated: gold loan, business loan, education loan, then auto loan and others, in that order, over a 10-year horizon.
Also evaluated loan against mutual fund given large customer overlap with mutual fund holders, since the process is more digital.
Management cannot speculate on which specific new product will be added next, but is confident more products will be added over a decade.
Immediate focus remains on personal loan and LAP, both viewed as huge opportunities.

subsections.label: Customer engagement & cross-sell
points: Given the large customer base of 12.25 million who frequently return to the app for repayments and other services, the company sees an opportunity to leverage this engagement for cross-sell of adjacent products.

key_figures.label: Incremental cost of funds last quarter
Incremental debt raise in Q1 FY27
Incremental borrowing cost reduction vs FY26 average

subsections.label: Gross NPA vs credit cost reconciliation
points: Credit cost improved to 6.80% of average AUM in Q1 FY27 from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26, a 22 bps QoQ reduction.
Gross NPA stood at 2.25% and Net NPA at 0.36% in Q1 FY27, with Stage-3 ECL coverage at 84.1% and Stage-2 coverage at 80.4%; collection efficiency was 96.82%.
Stage 2 assets improved to 3.15% from 3.9% a year earlier.

Gross NPA reflects loans between 90-DPD and 150-DPD (write-off occurs at 150-DPD for personal loan book) and applies only to on-book, since off-book already carries FLDG cover; credit cost reflects the combination of 100% write-offs plus provisions across Stage-1, Stage-2, and Stage-3.

FLDG: unutilized FLDG (5% given upfront on off-book disbursement) is not included in credit cost but blocks capital available for lending; only the utilized portion of FLDG (~1% impact on opex) is included in credit cost.

subsections.label: Pin code-level risk actions
points: Company serves 17,000 pin codes total, with 11,000 contributing 98% of business.
Last quarter the company paused lending across roughly 450 pin codes based on early warning system signals.
Since then, signals have turned modestly positive and approximately 40% (180 of 450) of these pin codes have been reopened; management frames this as cautious optimism, not a change of stance.
Remaining 270 pin codes continue to be paused, with ongoing evaluation and monitoring before any further reopening.
Company reiterated it would rather carry prudence slightly early than discover optimism slightly late.

subsections.label: AI-related salaried profile stress
points: Early signs indicate AI is reshaping certain salaried profiles; underwriting has been adjusted to weight durability/sustainability of income more than quantum.

Specific tightening applied to salaried applicants showing no EPFO credit in the last one or two months (possible job loss signal), with additional checks via EPFO and account aggregator data requiring salary credit as recent as the prior day (not stale data).

Tightening also applied to self-employed/small-business segments showing volatility in banking credit over the last six months (Jan-June pattern not seen a year earlier), viewed as more cyclically impacted by global/India macro factors; disbursement to this segment has been reduced.

In specific segments, approval bands were tightened last quarter from approving up to band 4 to approving up to band 3.7; this is being re-evaluated this quarter to assess whether the extra caution was warranted, with a possible reversion to normal band-4 approval.

subsections.label: Industry-level stress signals
points: Bureau data for the industry shows a divergence: headline asset quality looks benign, but stress is building beneath the surface, concentrated in small-ticket loans and borrowers carrying debt across multiple lenders, including households taking new lines to service old ones.
For the industry, quality of new customers has softened even as headline personal-loan delinquencies have improved — both are described as true simultaneously.
Company's own recent vintages are performing materially better than a year ago; early loan behavior is considered a dependable guide to eventual loss.

subsections.label: Bounce rate and collection efficiency reconciliation
points: Bounce rate is a function of multiple factors including proportion of customers who have already paid down many EMIs (naturally lower bounce) and Q1-specific seasonal/technical bounce factors; it has remained range-bound and does not signal deteriorating risk.
New sourcing since December 2025 (past 7-8 months) shows materially improved bounce rate and better early-loss indicators (30+, 90+), supporting confidence to reopen paused pin codes.

July trends (post Q1) show improvement in bounce/collection efficiency versus June-ending numbers, partly due to the usual Q1 seasonal phenomenon reversing and partly due to genuine risk improvement across specific segments where caution had been applied.

subsections.label: Macro watch-items
points: RBI has held a neutral stance and left rates unchanged; management values predictability in cost of funds over cheap money availability.
West Asia geopolitical risk is being watched for transmission via higher oil prices, shipping costs, and customer confidence, though it does not touch the book directly.

RBI's push on FCNR(B) deposits has drawn in foreign currency and eased system liquidity, which tends to lower cost of funds for lenders; neither West Asia nor FCNR(B) changes strategy but both warrant attention as lending books are often affected by second-order impacts.

key_figures.label: Cumulative margin reduction absorbable while maintaining ROA (3-year view)

subsections.label: Overall guidance reiteration
points: Management remains firmly on track for the FY27 guidance set out on different parameters — AUM, Gross NPA, credit cost, and profitability including ROE (20%+) and ROA (5%+).
On AUM growth, having already delivered 13% QoQ growth in Q1, management is confident of over-delivering on the >40% FY27 guidance given last quarter.
Credit cost guidance of 15% YoY reduction is being tracked well, evidenced by the drop from 8.85% (Q1 FY26) to 6.80% (Q1 FY27).

subsections.label: Cost of funds outlook
points: Cost of borrowing is guided to decline by a minimum of 100 bps over the next three quarters (H2 FY27 primarily), as older higher-cost debt (18-24 month tenure) runs off the book; some current incremental borrowing is already coming in at 12%-12.4%, versus 14.45% last quarter.
Over a 3-year view, management's own expectation is for cost of borrowing reduction to be upwards of 200-300 bps.
Rating upgrade discussions with India Ratings and CRISIL are ongoing; any upgrade would not meaningfully affect FY27 cost of borrowing but would meaningfully impact FY28.

subsections.label: Margin/ROA trajectory (3-year DuPont view)
points: Three unambiguous benefits expected in the P&L/DuPont over the next 3 years: (1) operating leverage — opex currently at 18% of AUM (down from 19.9%), with >50-55% being fixed cost expected to grow only at inflationary rates (partly offset by AI/headcount efficiencies), yielding an estimated 4-5% benefit; (2) cost of funds reduction of an estimated 2-3% (200-300 bps); (3) risk/credit cost reduction, estimated at a broad ~40% relative reduction.

Cumulative effect of these three benefits is estimated at 8-9% over three years, which management believes can fully absorb an equivalent reduction in revenue margin while still delivering ROA of 5%+.

Company follows a 'feedback loop' approach: benefits are first realized and confirmed in the book, then passed on to customers with a lag (approximately one quarter), to protect P&L and balance sheet stability; if a benefit is not realized in a given quarter, the pass-through is withheld until it is.

subsections.label: LAP-specific outlook
points: LAP business expected to achieve breakeven around Q3 of FY27, after which it will deliver its own targeted ROE (20%+) without diluting overall company ROE.
LAP branches being added every quarter (currently 101); management remains committed to scaling.

subsections.label: Product portfolio outlook (10-year horizon)
points: Company aspires to build a large, credible, profitable business over a much longer (decade-long) horizon; more lending products will be added over time.
Any future products will be added while maintaining commitment to 5% ROA and 20% ROE, consistently, quarter on quarter, even while absorbing initial 'burn' from new product build-out.

guidance_ledger.statement: We remain firmly confident of over-delivering on the number that we had given last quarter of 40%.
We remain firmly on track for the FY27 guidance we set out on different parameters, be it AUM, Gross NPA, credit cost, and profitability including ROE and ROA.
We firmly hold to our guidance which we gave last quarter, which is 15% reduction in credit cost, and we are tracking well on that.
We remain firmly, firmly committed to delivering an ROE guidance that we had given... we'll continue to deliver a healthy ROE, healthy defined as 20% plus in next few quarters.
We'll continue to deliver a healthy ROE, healthy defined as 20% plus in next few quarters.
Our guidance for particularly H2 of FY27, that you will see the cost of borrowing dropping by 100 basis points and it will only increase as the old debt basically runs off the book.
If I take a three-year view, our own view would be it can be upwards of 200 to 300 basis point reduction that we will see there.

We are cautiously optimistic that... either one of them or both of them will look favorably from a rating perspective, but that's an active discussion happening. Any upgrade will not potentially impact cost of borrowing for FY27 but will meaningfully impact it in FY28.
If I take a next three years view, the benefit coming only on account of operating leverage is around 4% to 5%.
The risk benefit is again going to be somewhere around almost 40% lower if I take a very broad number.

guidance_ledger.metric: Cumulative revenue margin reduction absorbable while maintaining ROA
guidance_ledger.statement: Now if I take a cumulative of all these numbers, we are talking about a benefit of around 8% to 9% over three years... I can still deliver my ROA of upwards of 5% while reducing my revenue margin by 8% to 9%.
Till now last year this quarter and around Q3 or so LAP will achieve breakeven.
The ROE for this business is also 20% plus for us. So it is not ROE dilutive, in fact it is just augmenting and building the scale.

It is only natural that we will add more lending products... the pecking order has been gold loan, business loan, education loan, and then auto loan and then so on and so forth... but which one is something very difficult for us to say.

Even as we think about the next set of products... we will continue to do it in a way that we are able to absorb the burn and still deliver profitability which is a 5% ROA and a 20% ROE consistently quarter on quarter.
Our own assessment is, if we are able to create a high-quality credible brand, the number will stabilize at somewhere between 40% to 45% or 40% to 50%.
We will consider starting to disclose that from next quarter.
Year-on-year reduction in impairment costs of 10%-15%.
Continued improvement in Stage-1 mix.
Over time, we believe secured business will deliver almost the same 19% to 21% ROE for us as well.

There is basically... headroom for further reduction in yield over the next four quarters... the trend you saw from Q3 to Q4 is a trend... very symbolic of the kind of trend you may see going forward.

Our average spread would be in the ballpark of 14 to 16% in the longer term... yield minus the cost of borrowing will basically be closer to about 18 to 19% in the near term and in the longer term, it will reduce.
We plan to have at least 80 more branches by end of this financial year.
We do not want to provide a guidance on disbursement for FY27.

guidance_ledger.metric: Capital requirement / need for fresh capital
guidance_ledger.statement: Given our current capital position, we are comfortably capitalized to achieve the 40% AUM growth guidance for FY27.

We see the steady state leverage as being 2.5 to 3 on debt-to-equity... over a period of time, if the secured book becomes more meaningful, there is potential for further improving the leverage but that probably is a two-year journey.

risk_register.note: Bureau data shows headline asset quality benign but stress building beneath surface, concentrated in small-ticket loans and borrowers with debt across multiple lenders; company's own recent vintages performing materially better than a year ago.

themes.label: Asset quality improvement
themes.note: Credit cost fell to 6.80% from 8.85% YoY and 7.02% QoQ; Stage 2 improved to 3.15% from 3.9% YoY; collection efficiency at 96.82%; company reiterated 15% YoY credit cost reduction guidance.

themes.label: Yield/margin moderation
themes.note: Total income/average AUM fell 249bps due to deliberate shift to high-quality lower-priced customers and rising off-book share (49.7%→53.6%), yet PPOP and ROA/ROE continued to improve.

themes.label: Secured book (LAP) scale-up
themes.note: LAP AUM at INR 617 crores (7.7% of total) across 101 branches in 8 states; expected to hit breakeven around Q3 FY27 with 20%+ ROE target, faster branch profitability (7-8 months) due to 40%+ cross-sell from PL base.

themes.label: AI/ML-led underwriting and collections
themes.note: Underwriting AUC improved to 74% from 66% (2023); voice agents now at >80% of human efficiency in collections (up from 70%); >80% of code AI-written; feature store monitors 7,200+ signals.

themes.label: Credit rating upgrade and cost of borrowing
themes.note: Active engagement with India Ratings and CRISIL for possible upgrade; incremental borrowing cost ~150bps lower than FY26 average; guided 100bps reduction in cost of borrowing in H2 FY27.

themes.label: IPO capital deployment
themes.note: IPO completed in May 2026 boosted NBFC subsidiary capital adequacy to 40.2% from 25.3% and net worth to INR 2,245 crores, nearly 4x March 2023 levels.

themes.label: Prudent risk management amid macro uncertainty
themes.note: Company paused lending in 450 pin codes last quarter, reopened 180 (40%) on improved signals while keeping 270 paused; tightened underwriting for salaried profiles showing AI-linked employment loss signals and self-employed segments with volatile banking credit.

key_takeaways: The registered users grew 33% year-on-year to 74.6 million. We have now served 12.25 million customers, an increase of 26% year-on-year. AUM stood at INR 8,001 crores, up 61% year-on-year and 13% quarter-on-quarter. Profit after tax grew to INR 95 crores, higher by 59% year-on-year and 16% quarter-on-quarter. Return on average AUM held steady at 5.05%, a reflection not only of growth, but of its quality.
Credit cost was 6.80% of average AUM, down from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26. This is, we believe, this is a significant improvement.
We firmly hold to our guidance which we gave last quarter, which is 15% reduction in credit cost, and we are tracking well on that.

Capital adequacy in our NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% from 25.3% last quarter. Net worth grew to INR 2,245 crores, nearly four times its level in March 2023, built on retained earnings, organic profitability, and the IPO completed in May 2026.
On the guidance for future, we remain firmly on track for the FY27 guidance we set out on different parameters, be it AUM, Gross NPA, credit cost, and profitability including ROE and ROA.

Last quarter, out of caution, we paused lending across roughly 450 pin codes based on what our early warning system had flagged. We have re-examined those pin codes since. The signals have turned modestly positive, and we have reopened approximately 40% of these pin codes already.
Also, a rising share of off-book lending, which has gone up from 49.7% to 53.6%, adds to the reduction in revenue margin.

We are also watching the early signs that AI is reshaping certain salaried profiles. We have already, adequately altered our underwriting, to give more weight to the durability and sustainability of income, and not merely the quantum.
pressing_questions: Between last quarter and this quarter how many pin codes are now touched where you have paused? On an overall basis how has that moved Q-o-Q, and how does this reconcile with slightly lower collection efficiency and slightly higher bounce rates?

In terms of your incremental yield on the product, is it coming down, stable? What is the yield on personal loan versus LAP now? What is the incremental cost of funds versus last quarter's reported 14.45, and what is the margin outlook from here?
What is the ROA/ROE target for the LAP business, and how much time does a branch take to achieve breakeven? How are the early buckets (started two years back) behaving versus recent buckets?
The FLDG portion of the credit cost - what portion is this for the quarter, and does the credit cost reduction from 8% to 6% odd include the FLDG portion?
Credit cost is lower, however gross NPA has increased - do we consider gross NPA on a combined on-book and off-book basis?
Can we disclose the NIM and yield product-wise (LAP vs PL) in the quarterly presentations, and what is the NIM for this quarter?

quarters.summary: Kissht's FY26 performance reflected strong AUM and PAT growth alongside improving asset quality, with management guiding FY27 AUM growth of over 40%, GNPA below 2.25%, 10-15% YoY reduction in impairment costs, and ROA of 4.5-5% (ROE 19-21%), while continuing a deliberate strategy of yield moderation toward higher-quality customer segments, scale-up of the secured LAP business, and deployment of IPO proceeds toward on-book capital and technology/AI infrastructure.

subsections.label: Revenue vs AUM growth differential (Q3 to Q4)
points: Revenue is up around 4-5% while portfolio yield from Q3 to Q4 is up by around 1% per the KPI handbook (per moderator/analyst framing).
Management clarified the difference between AUM growth and revenue growth QoQ is coming from two reasons: a small margin compression, and a reduction in other income.

subsections.label: OPEX increase in Q4
points: Two key drivers of increased OPEX in Q4: (1) LAP business, which has not reached breakeven and is still probably a year or two away from steady state ROA, plus increased branch count adding load on OPEX; (2) a reasonably large one-time investment in the collections team (more on the field side than tele-calling) made with specific intent to build recovery/NPA-recovery capability for FY27, ahead of anticipated 40%+ AUM growth.

subsections.label: Margin/yield trajectory
points: Total income yield as % of AUM has moderated deliberately as the company pursues higher-quality borrower segments and passes on benefits of operating leverage and lower funding costs to customers.
Near-term yield compression is expected, offset by falling impairment costs (9.7% FY25 to 8.2% FY26, 7% in Q4 alone).

Two immediate unit-economics benefits expected going forward: operating leverage and cost-of-funds improvement, expected to give healthy headroom for further yield reduction over next four quarters, with a trend similar to Q3-to-Q4 expected to continue.
Benefits are passed to customers only after ensuring ROA is not jeopardized — there is a lag in passing on benefits.

subsections.label: Capital adequacy and net worth
points: Net worth growth of 2.4x over 3 years achieved almost entirely through retained earnings and organic profitability.
Net worth to be further bolstered by ₹850 crore IPO proceeds, split 75% on-book capital and 25% technology/AI infrastructure.

subsections.label: IPO proceeds deployment update
points: Approximately ₹630 crore (75% of primary issue) already infused as fresh equity into NBFC subsidiary Si Creva Capital, in line with prospectus objects; onward lending deployment has commenced and is progressing as planned.
Balance 25% earmarked for general corporate purposes, being deployed in a calibrated manner toward technology, AI infrastructure, brand building, customer acquisition, and strategic objectives.
Company is comfortably capitalized to achieve the 40% AUM growth guidance for FY27 without needing near-term additional capital.

subsections.label: Leverage strategy
points: On-book (predominantly personal loan) steady-state leverage seen at 2.5-3x debt-to-equity.
Potential for further leverage improvement as secured book becomes more meaningful — described as a two-year journey.
Off-balance-sheet leverage is not a real constraint since only capital blocked is the 5% FLDG; growth will continue as long as off-balance-sheet partners remain interested in retail/MSME opportunity.

points: 19% QoQ AUM growth driven by relentless focus on targeting high-quality customers, which involves reducing rates offered to such customers (contributing to slight QoQ margin reduction).
Large base of 11.76 million unique customers with 3.5 million active at any point provides flexibility to target repeat customers, supporting stable growth trajectory.
Same growth momentum stated to be visible in April-May run rate.

subsections.label: LAP business rationale and scale-up
points: Started LAP around 2 years back not purely for diversification but to serve customers wholesomely — over 40% of LAP customers come from existing Kissht customer base, an organic demand that also helps branch economics.
LAP is fully technology-enabled: model-based underwriting, branch-led fulfillment, smart document processing, AI-validated property valuation — described as not standard plain vanilla LAP.

LAP LTV of 48% is a deliberate conservative stance and expected to remain range-bound; proposition is built around superior turnaround time and offer for tier-1 city customers, not higher risk-taking via LTV.

LAP contributes 7.3% of total AUM and may remain a small portion in FY27 as well since personal loan is growing at a decent rate; LAP branch expansion (80 more planned) will be calibrated, deepening into existing geographies — Karnataka, AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, UP and Maharashtra — while ensuring branch profitability and early risk-signal outcomes.
LAP continues to be a business that has not reached breakeven and is probably a year or two away from steady-state ROA — a drag on OPEX.

subsections.label: Personal loan customer profile / cross-borrowing behavior
points: Around 45% of active customers already hold another personal loan outside of Kissht; specific split by number of loans (one/two/three) not available.
The other personal loan is typically taken from a larger institution and is typically of a larger ticket size than what Kissht offers.

subsections.label: Product roadmap - non-lending and future products
points: A new fully-owned subsidiary has been created for distribution of mutual funds and other wealth products, driven by customer demand; this is treated as a cross-sell/adjunct to the core lending business.

Future lending product considerations (not immediate, to be pursued over several years) include gold loan, business loan, education loan, alongside continued focus on personal loan and LAP as priority products; fee-based cross-sell products (insurance, mutual fund distribution) are also planned as adjuncts.

subsections.label: Underwriting model evolution
points: Underwriting stack has evolved from a simple decision-tree model to a gradient-boosting model (machine learning technique) to transformer-based AI models, with AUC reaching 74% on the latest model, up from 66% in 2023.
AUC (area under the curve) measures how well a model separates good borrowers from bad ones; higher number means sharper separation.
Investor presentation pages 23 and 24 elaborate this with detailed evidence.
Objective is to detect behavioral deterioration before it surfaces in delinquency numbers, not merely identify stress after the fact.

subsections.label: AI in fraud management
points: Multi-agent fraud intelligence system covers deep fakes, document forgery, text analysis, multivariate anomaly detection, and network fraud, orchestrating over 50 fraud triggers.

Architectural shift moved past static rules to a multi-agent setup covering vision, text, tabular and graph data; agents surface new fraud hypotheses on their own when spotting anomalies, relevant given weekly-mutating fraud patterns.

subsections.label: AI productivity and operations impact
points: AI-assisted customer support delivers 100% call-quality coverage and reduced average response time from 200 seconds to under 90 seconds.
More than 80% of internal code is now written with AI assistance.
In LAP business, AI-powered smart document processing improved First Time Right (FTR) rates by over 30% while credit queries fell by 50%.

subsections.label: Early warning / surveillance system
points: GenAI-augmented feature store monitors over 7,000 features for causal drift.
Early warning system runs across 7,000 features; AI's heavy lifting there is attribution — identifying which features are driving shifts in portfolio metrics when they change.

subsections.label: Company positioning on technology
points: Management states Kissht is "a technology company that does lending — not the other way around"; all core systems are built in-house with AI embedded across underwriting, fraud detection, collections, servicing, portfolio surveillance, and software development.

subsections.label: Collections infrastructure
points: Collections covered by 7,000+ field agents and 1,000+ tele-callers, with more than 95% of collections in-house, covering 17,000+ pin codes with swift field intervention from as early as 5 DPD.
Proprietary Automated Collection System enables scale of operations.
Institutionalized collections approach: defined processes, swift actions, measurable outcomes, zero dependence on individual judgment.
Stage-2 book reduced from 3.5% to 2.4%; Stage-3 from 2.9% to 2.1% — attributed to better borrower selection, tighter geography management, and disciplined collections.
Bounce rate remains strong at 13.1% and stable across the year, with April and May also steady.

A large one-time investment was made in the collections team in Q4 (more on field side), specifically to build recovery/NPA-recovery capability ahead of anticipated FY27 AUM growth of 40%+; a dedicated team was created specifically for NPA recovery.

subsections.label: GNPA historical spike explanation
points: GNPA rose from 0.79% to 2.89% over two years primarily due to a technicality: the write-off period was extended from 120 days to 150 days after discussions with auditors, based on recovery patterns observed; this caused the apparent spike, not a change in underlying credit quality.
Write-off period has been at 150 days for two years now, and current GNPA reflects consistent behavior since that change.

subsections.label: NACH and repeat-loan tracking
points: 100% of customers are NACH covered; active base of 3.5 million generates about 3.5 million NACH presentations per month.
Around 45% of active customers already hold another personal loan outside Kissht, typically from a larger institution and of larger ticket size; specific breakdown by number of loans not available.

subsections.label: Customer profile
points: Company operates PAN India, with 81% of borrowers from the top 100 cities.
Nearly half the portfolio is salaried customers, mostly young people with average age of 32 years, average CIBIL score of 746.
Loan purposes: ~45% business, 30% consumption, 15% emergency, 10% other.

subsections.label: Customer acquisition channels
points: Despite being a fintech, reliance on digital marketing remains limited, contributing less than 50% of overall customer acquisition.
Other channels contribute almost 55% of acquisition, including partnerships with merchants, e-commerce platforms, aggregators, and a growing organic channel.
Organic share of acquisition is as high as 30% and growing steadily.
Association with Sachin Tendulkar has accelerated brand trust, particularly in mass-market and mass-affluent segments where his trust equity runs deepest.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Competitors include Bajaj, Chola, and other players with varying levels of focus on personal loans; company differentiates via (1) demonstrated credit performance backed by AI/ML models and collections focus, and (2) large customer base enabling scalability via repeat customers and further selection of high-quality customers.
Additional differentiators include diversified acquisition channels (digital lending plus merchant/e-commerce/aggregator partnerships) and growing organic/zero-CAC acquisition.

subsections.label: Long-term product strategy (3-5 year view)
points: Company favors doing few things well rather than spreading thin across many products; heavily focused on personal loan currently, with LAP as the only near-horizon addition launched after multiple pilots roughly two years ago.

Future product consideration list (not immediate, to be pursued over several years) includes gold loan, business loan, education loan, alongside a natural cross-sell of fee-based products such as insurance and mutual fund distribution.

subsections.label: New wealth management subsidiary
points: A new fully-owned subsidiary has been created for distribution of mutual funds and other wealth products, as customers are demanding these offerings and there is a large opportunity; best executed via a separate entity, consistent with the RSP-stated strategy of expanding lending and non-lending offerings.

subsections.label: Listing milestone
points: FY26 marked the company's first year as a listed company; listed on NSE & BSE on 8th May (2026), oversubscribed across all categories.
Listing viewed as an inflection point that demands the highest standards of transparency, consistency, and governance.

subsections.label: Liability structure / funding partnerships
points: Balanced and diversified funding structure of almost 50% on-book and 50% off-book.
On-book AUM of ₹3,556 crore supported by 45+ lending partners, with cost of borrowing between 11.5% and 14.25%.
Off-book AUM of ₹3,510 crore, with FLDG (First Loss Default Guarantee) provided up to 5%; almost 100% of off-book AUM is covered by FLDG.

subsections.label: Macro environment
points: Global environment factors flagged: higher oil prices, elevated rates, geopolitical disruptions, currency volatility — all weighing on India too.

Management view: in such an environment, discipline, adaptability, and risk adjustment matter more than speed of growth; prudence is framed as a competitive advantage rather than a conservative instinct.

Economic cycles reveal themselves quietly through small distortions — changing repayment behavior, pockets of stress, subtle shifts that initially appear isolated — requiring sharper underwriting and faster recalibration rather than merely slowing down.

subsections.label: Credit risk / heterogeneity of Indian borrowers
points: Indian credit behavior is extraordinarily heterogeneous; repayment patterns shift across geographies, occupations, local economies, employment cycles, and even neighborhood-level stress signals, requiring disproportionate emphasis on model recalibration, early warning indicators, and granular data intelligence.

subsections.label: Prudence measures taken
points: As a measure of prudence, disbursements were reduced by approximately 7% and lending was paused across approximately 450 pin codes where early-warning systems flagged elevated risk, while continuing to grow in high-quality segments — framed as a regular, systematic exercise, not a reactive one-off measure.

subsections.label: FLDG/counterparty risk on off-book book
points: Off-book AUM risk exposure is contractually capped at FLDG of up to 5%; lenders may negotiate on hurdle-rate expectations depending on their conviction on FLDG coverage, but structural/contractual risk exposure is capped at 5%.
Leverage on off-balance-sheet book is not viewed as a constraint since only the 5% FLDG capital is blocked.

subsections.label: Growth and asset quality guidance for FY27
points: Company expects to grow AUM at north of 40%, with disciplined asset quality and calibrated risk selection; secured business scale-up also expected to be strong.
On asset quality: targeting gross NPA below 2.25%, year-on-year reduction in impairment costs of 10%-15%, and continued improvement in Stage-1 mix.
On profitability: targeting return on average AUM of 4.5%-5%, entailing return on average equity of 19-21%.
Guidance reiterated as applicable for FY27 specifically.

subsections.label: AUM mix and secured business ROA/ROE flow-through
points: Overall growth (secured + unsecured combined) expected at ~40%; despite secured business carrying a lower ROA, the 4.5% ROA guidance is for the overall book.
Over time, secured (LAP) business is expected to deliver almost the same 19-21% ROE as the overall book.

subsections.label: Rating trajectory and cost of borrowing outlook
points: Crisil rated the company A- in February 2026; India Ratings rated it A- in November of the prior year; constant engagement ongoing with both agencies covering continual risk improvement and improved balance sheet strength post-IPO.
Company is cautiously optimistic about a further ratings upgrade from both agencies at some point in FY27, an active discussion over the next 6-8 months.
Since the Crisil upgrade in February, a 200 bps improvement in marginal cost of borrowing has already been seen, expected to sustain into the following year.
A further ratings upgrade could yield an additional 100-150 bps reduction in cost of borrowing, more likely visible in FY28 (potentially later part of FY27).

subsections.label: Yield/spread trajectory guidance
points: Portfolio yield of ~30-31% in Q4 expected to continue trending lower, following a pattern similar to the Q3-to-Q4 move, over the next 4-6 quarters.
Spread guidance (yield minus cost of borrowing): ~18-19% in the near term, expected to reduce in the longer term.

No disbursement guidance provided for FY27, as management's guidance framework is centered on AUM growth rather than disbursement, since disbursement is an outcome of tenure changes among repeat and higher-quality customers.

subsections.label: Capital sufficiency for growth
points: Company stated it is comfortably capitalized to achieve the 40% AUM growth guidance for FY27 without an imminent need for a new capital raise.

themes.label: Asset quality improvement
themes.note: GNPA improved from 2.89% to 2.12%, Net NPA at 0.29%, Stage-2 and Stage-3 book both declined, collection efficiency above 97%.

themes.label: Yield/margin moderation
themes.note: Deliberate shift to higher-quality, lower-yield customers causing near-term yield compression, offset by falling impairment costs and expected operating leverage/cost-of-funds benefits.

themes.label: Secured book (LAP) scale-up
themes.note: LAP AUM at ₹518 crore (7.3% of total AUM) across 98 branches in 8 states, with 80 more branches planned by FY27 end, though still pre-breakeven.

themes.label: AI/ML-led underwriting and collections
themes.note: AUC improved from 66% to 74%, underwriting stack uses 7,000+ variables, AI embedded across underwriting, fraud, collections and customer support.

themes.label: Credit rating upgrade and cost of borrowing
themes.note: A- rating from Crisil (Feb 2026) and India Ratings drove a 200 bps marginal cost of borrowing improvement, with further upgrade potential expected in FY27/FY28.

themes.label: IPO capital deployment
themes.note: ₹850 crore IPO proceeds being deployed 75% into on-book capital (₹630 crore already infused into Si Creva Capital) and 25% into technology/AI and corporate purposes.

themes.label: Prudent risk management amid macro uncertainty
themes.note: Global macro headwinds (oil prices, rates, geopolitics, currency volatility) prompted a 7% disbursement reduction and lending pause across ~450 pin codes as a systematic prudence measure.

key_takeaways: AUM grew 73% year-on-year and 19% quarter-on-quarter to ₹7,066 crore.
For FY26, total income reached ₹2,209 crore, up 63% year-on-year. Pre-provisioning operating profit grew 54% to ₹836 crore, and PAT grew 75% year-on-year to ₹281 crore.
We delivered a return on average assets of 5% and return on average equity of 24%.
GNPA reduced from 2.89% to 2.12%, a year-on-year improvement of 77 basis points. Collection efficiency remained above 97%. Net NPA was contained at 0.29%.

As a measure of prudence, we reduced disbursements by approximately 7% and paused lending across approximately 450 pin codes, where early-warning systems flagged elevated risks - while continuing to grow in high-quality segments.
The first EMI T90, has improved significantly from 1.5% to 0.7% in FY26.
LAP AUM stands at nearly ₹518 crore, across 98 branches in 8 states, contributing 7.3% of total AUM.
FY26 marked our first year as a listing company - we listed on NSE & BSE on 8th May this year, oversubscribed across all categories.

We expect to grow at north of 40% in AUM, with disciplined asset quality and calibrated risk selection, while secured business scale-up is also expected to be strong. On asset quality, we are targeting gross NPA below 2.25%, year-on-year reduction in impairment costs of 10%-15%, and continued improvement in Stage-1 mix. On profitability, we are targeting a return on average AUM in the range of 4.5%-5%, which entails a return on average equity in the range of 19-21%.
pressing_questions: What's your engagement with rating agencies on a potential upgrade and how much could a one-notch upgrade reduce your cost of borrowings?
Why is there such a reason for such high GNPA shoot-up in two years (from 0.79 to 2.89)?

Regarding the quarterly movement between the AUM and the revenue - revenue is up around 4-5% while portfolio yield from Q3 to Q4 is up by around 1% per the KPI handbook - is this differential more because of compression in yields or did we lend more during the end of the quarter, and will this continue going ahead?

KPIGREEN.about: Incorporated in 2008, KPI Green Energy Ltd is part of KP Group. They develop, build, own, manage, and maintain renewable power facilities (solar and wind solar hybrid power project) as an Independent Power Producer (IPP) and as a service provider to Captive Power Producers (CPPs) under the ‘Solarism’ brand. [1] Group Companies: [2] KP Energy Limited KP Green Engineering Private Limited KPF Green Hydrogen & Ammonia Technology Private Limited KP Human Development Foundation

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw 16% YoY total income growth and 21% YoY EBITDA growth with margin expansion to 37%, but PAT declined YoY due to higher depreciation and finance costs on the rapidly growing IPP asset base; management expects full earnings contribution of newly commissioned IPP assets to build through FY27, with stabilization largely by FY28. Management flagged geopolitical-driven input cost pressure (steel, cables, logistics) impacting EPC/CPP margins more than IPP, guided revenue growth to be maintained around 30-40% (conservative vs. earlier 40-50% CAGR commitment), and reiterated IPP capacity build-out, Botswana/UAE international expansion, and Sundrops IPO plans.
