subsections.label: PAT vs cash profit divergence
points: YoY movement in PAT reflects higher depreciation and finance costs on rapidly growing asset base.
As new IPP capacity is commissioned, associated depreciation and interest are recognized upfront, while full revenue and earning contribution of these assets materialize progressively over the year.
Cash profit is described as a better measure of underlying cash generation and grew 6% YoY versus a PAT decline.
Full earning contribution of newly commissioned assets expected to build through the remainder of FY27.

subsections.label: Debt and leverage trajectory
points: Company currently at comfortable leverage (~2.x long-term debt to net worth).
Debt for larger upcoming projects (250MW and 370MW) has already been expensed/drawn.
Going forward, debt-to-equity (long-term debt to net worth) guided to reach a maximum comfortable level of 3:1.
Interest cost calculation is real-time/phase-wise as disbursements occur in tranches tied to project commissioning (COD); exact annual interest/depreciation figures difficult to project mid-year.
Balance sheet is prepared only on a half-yearly basis, so detailed amortization schedule of the INR5,200 crore March 2026 borrowing base cannot be disclosed.

subsections.label: Interest & depreciation dynamics
points: Interest during construction (IDC) for completed portions of projects has been fully utilized/capitalized; going forward the entire interest will be booked as an expense rather than capitalized.
Depreciation follows Companies Act (10-15%) but income tax allows 40% depreciation benefit, which supports cash profits.
Management later clarified/revised depreciation rate for the 25-year IPP plant to ~5% (correcting an initial 15% estimate) since plant & machinery depreciation for long-tenor plants is lower.
Depreciation is charged only once assets are put to use (post-COD), and is booked in a phase-wise manner as portions of plants are capitalized.

subsections.label: CPP/EPC margin pressure (KP Energy vs KPI Green)
points: Gross margins for CPP segment across KP Energy and KPI Green have fallen substantially due to geopolitical-driven cost increases in steel, cables, logistics, ROW.
KPI Green's margin impact is limited to ~300 bps because costs are shared/bifurcated with the IPP business, which contributes ~17-18% of KPI's top line.

KP Energy, being purely an EPC business (with negligible IPP contribution), saw a much sharper EBITDA margin decline from 22% to 12% as it bears the full cost impact without IPP cost-sharing benefits or economies of scale (e.g., shared crane usage).

Management expects margins to recover toward historical levels once geopolitical cost pressures ease, though timing is uncertain as the issue has resurfaced despite earlier expectations of resolution.

subsections.label: Financing profile
points: Company continues to build on the successful listing of India's first externally credit-enhanced green bond (INR670 crore, 8.50% coupon, 5-year tenor, 65% partial guarantee from GuarantCo, AA+ rating), reinforcing market confidence in KPI Green's business model, governance standards, and renewable growth platform.

subsections.label: Governance changes
points: Management changed auditors to BDO (a top-5 firm) to bring best practices and better processes, and added experts to the Board, framed as a positive action to build stakeholder/lender confidence — not a response to any governance issue.
Promoter has been increasing stake (via warrants and promoter group company Quyosh purchasing shares), with promoter holding now above 51%.
Institutional investors including Vanguard, Abu Dhabi Investment Fund, Okoworld, a pension fund, and Blackrock remain invested in the stock, per management.

subsections.label: Order book visibility
points: IPP segment has energized a substantial portion of existing projects in hand.
CPP order book of approximately INR5,000-plus crore provides enough order book in hand for the CPP side.

IPP revenue expected to show a stronger upward trajectory going forward since expenses have already been expensed out and revenue is now flowing in, built in a phase-wise manner that will strengthen progressively.

Data center demand is described as the latest entrant and an opportunistic horizon in the RE sector; KPI is in touch with data center players with ongoing inquiries, but no material/finalized order book contribution disclosed yet.

key_figures.label: KPI IPP revenue share of top line
Sun Drops expected FY27 top line (IPP+CPP)

subsections.label: IPP vs CPP mix strategy
points: Company aims to maintain IPP at ~20% of total revenue mix because it is long-term, sustainable revenue with 85-90% EBITDA margins and 25-year visibility, removing ongoing profitability/top-line concerns once commissioned.
EPS decline this quarter attributed to temporary PAT-level impact from depreciation/interest on new IPP assets, not to underlying EBITDA weakness (EBITDA was strong versus prior quarter).

Management frames IPP investment as driving future PE re-rating and market cap appreciation (citing ACME as a comparable pure-IPP player), positioning share price appreciation as the primary investor return driver rather than near-term ROE/dividend.

subsections.label: KPI Green vs KP Energy margin divergence
points: KPI Green's overall EBITDA has grown; margin drag is limited because costs are shared between IPP and CPP within KPI, and IPP contributes 17-18% of top line.

KP Energy is purely an EPC business with negligible IPP contribution (~1-2% of top line), so it bears the full brunt of geopolitical cost inflation without cost-sharing benefits, causing a much sharper margin decline (22% to 12%); KP Energy's EPC revenue share is ~83% of its total revenue.
Economies of scale (e.g., shared equipment like cranes across businesses) benefit KPI Green but not KP Energy to the same extent.

subsections.label: Sun Drops Energia performance and plans
points: Sun Drops posted strong quarterly profitability (revenue INR150-155 crore, EBITDA INR42 crore, PAT INR26 crore at ~17% PAT margin, cash profit ~INR30 crore) since it does not carry the large IPP depreciation/interest burden that KPI Green does.
Sun Drops is adding battery energy storage system capability and battery energy manufacturing.
Company is proceeding with Sun Drops IPO plans.
Sun Drops expected to cross INR1,500 crore of top line this year across IPP and CPP.

key_figures.label: Expected annual IPP generation at full run rate
Expected IPP top line at 1GW run rate
IPP revenue at full scale (revised estimate)

subsections.label: Portfolio scale-up
points: KPI Green continues to scale its renewable portfolio across IPP and CPP segments.

Portfolio expanded from 4.06 GW to 6.94 GW in a single year (71% growth), reflecting both execution strength and continued strong demand for the double-engine IPP plus CPP business model; installed capacity stood at 1.87 GW with 5.07 GW work-in-progress as of June 30, 2026 (IPP 2.57 GW, CPP 4.37 GW).
0.85 GW commissioned and 2.88 GW of fresh orders booked over the trailing 12 months.
Expanding IPP portfolio expected to generate more than 390 crore units annually at full run rate, strengthening recurring revenue base and improving long-term earnings visibility.
Long tenure 25-year PPAs, strong execution capabilities, and integrated project development expertise underpin a platform combining growth with predictable cash flows.

subsections.label: Execution enablers
points: Strategic land bank (8,657 acres) and power evacuation capacity (5.10 GW) have both grown, securing the project pipeline and supporting faster, lower-risk conversion of orders into operating capacity.
During the quarter, geographical footprint expanded into Rajasthan, taking total site count to 133.

subsections.label: Generation ramp-up
points: Q1 FY27 unit generation under the IPP portfolio grew nearly 4x YoY.
Generation achieved in this single quarter already exceeds 65% of the entire FY26 generation, reflecting the scale of the annuity base and growing recurring revenue engine.
Despite a lender-mandated 1-year stabilization period, achieving 65% of last year's full generation in a single quarter shows plants are nearing full-fledged running.

subsections.label: Peak IPP economics (analyst Q&A clarification)
points: Management initially estimated an IPP annual interest cost of ~INR450 crore (at 8.5% rate on ~INR5,000 crore debt) and EBITDA of 85-90% on ~INR1,000-1,500 crore revenue at full 1GW+ capacity.

In response to analyst push-back on the implied profit-before-tax gap, management revised the depreciation assumption from ~15% (standard plant & machinery) down to ~5%, reflecting the 25-year plant life, to reconcile the EBITDA-interest-depreciation math.
Management expects the business to generate a minimum of INR1,500-1,600 crore of revenue once IPP portfolio is fully stabilized/energized.
Peak capacity utilization for current IPP build is expected in Q3 or Q4 of FY27, as Q2 is impacted by monsoon/rainy season.

subsections.label: International expansion
points: KPI is expanding international footprint to strengthen global market presence.
In Botswana, an MOU has been signed with the government for 5 GW of renewable energy, with planning for the first 500 MW phase underway.

Botswana project will be an IPP model; KPI has a subsidiary in GIFT City, under which the Botswana company will sit; 500 hectares of land has already been acquired and the company is at an advanced stage of signing PPAs.
No revenue expected from Botswana this fiscal year; revenue contribution is expected in upcoming years.

In the UAE, through a global alliance with Fabtech Group and F Plus Healthcare Technologies, execution is underway for a solar power project integrated with BESS awarded to subsidiary Sun Drops Energia Limited, to power a containerized data centre facility.

subsections.label: Inventory buildup and normalization
points: Inventory buildup seen towards the end of the last financial year (as of March) has come down to some extent in this quarter and is expected to decline further going forward.
Inventory was built up due to worsening geopolitical conditions; material was piled up while available to avoid delays in execution capability.
As projects are completed, inventory is expected to normalize downward over time.

subsections.label: Geopolitical-driven input cost impact
points: Major impact from geopolitical conditions relates to fuel and component costs feeding into solar plants — cables, steel (MMS structures, evacuation towers), ROW issues, and logistics.
Company has absorbed some portion of the cost impact and passed on some portion to customers.
Impact has been more severe for EPC-only businesses (KP Energy) than for KPI Green, which shares costs with its IPP business.
Issue was expected to resolve roughly 6 months prior but has resurfaced repeatedly, making the timeline for margin recovery uncertain.

subsections.label: Billing delays with large customers
points: Slower-than-expected revenue growth (16% actual vs. 20-30% expected) attributed partly to utility-scale project billing delays with institutional customers such as Coal India Limited, Adani Group, and Aditya Birla Group, pushing billing to the next quarter.

subsections.label: Data center opportunity
points: Data centers represent a new, opportunistic demand segment requiring round-the-clock power operations; KPI is in touch with data center players with ongoing inquiries, to be disclosed to stakeholders as and when materialized.

subsections.label: Share price and investor perception
points: Management noted a disconnect between business growth (revenue/profit doubling) and market cap (down ~60%), with stock trading at roughly half the sector PE, per an investor question.

Management stated share price is not directly controlled by management but cited actions such as hiring BDO as auditor and promoter stake increases (via warrants and promoter group company Quyosh share purchases) as confidence-building measures.
Promoter holding is now above 51%.
Institutional investors cited as still holding the stock include Vanguard, Abu Dhabi Investment Fund, Okoworld, a pension fund, and Blackrock (referred to as 'Blackstone' during the call in error).

key_figures.label: Floating solar EPC order (Kadana Dam, Gujarat)

subsections.label: New growth platform projects
points: In battery energy storage, the 565 MW / 1,130 MWh BESPA has been executed, with financial closure under process.
In floating solar, the company is actively executing a 142 MW EPC order at Kadana Dam, Gujarat.
For the 150 MW wind project for GUVNL, the PPA has been signed and financial closure achieved.
PPA signing of the 300 MW SJVN-backed wind project is under process.

Company has secured both an intrastate trading license from GERC and an interstate trading license from CERC; energy trading is being undertaken on a pilot basis, creating wider market access and better realization opportunities.

subsections.label: Future growth segments
points: Focus remains on strengthening the IPP portfolio, expanding the CPP business, and building capabilities in future growth segments such as BESS, green hydrogen, floating solar, offshore wind, pump storage, and energy trading.
Strategy is to build an integrated renewable energy platform with strong execution capabilities, predictable annuity revenue, and long-term value creation for stakeholders.

subsections.label: Leadership changes
points: Company welcomed Professor Sunil Maheshwari as Vice Chairman and Mr. Rajesh Shrivastava as Whole-Time Director during the quarter, strengthening Board depth in strategy, governance, business transformation, renewable energy, infrastructure, and organizational leadership.
Mr. Kapil Kriplani has been welcomed as incoming Group CFO, bringing experience in finance, capital markets, and strategic growth initiatives.
CFO Mr. Salim Yahoo is stepping away due to personal family commitments; management and investors on the call thanked him for his contributions and service.
Auditor changed to BDO (a top-5 firm) as part of a push toward better governance practices and processes.

subsections.label: Geopolitical cost pressure
points: Geopolitical conditions are impacting input costs — cables, steel/MMS structures, evacuation towers, ROW, logistics, and equipment hire (e.g., cranes, diesel) — rather than sales/demand.
This is the first earnings call where 'geopolitical' has been used this extensively, per an analyst observation.
Impact is more severe for pure EPC businesses (KP Energy) than for KPI Green, which shares costs with its IPP business.
Company is uncertain when the issue will resolve, as it was expected to ease roughly 6 months ago but has resurfaced repeatedly.

subsections.label: Seasonality
points: Renewable generation (solar and wind) is inherently seasonal; Q2 is typically impacted by monsoon/rainy season, affecting generation, revenue, and margins.
Two quarters (current and upcoming) are expected to be impacted by seasonality, creating a dip in PAT margin versus prior guidance.

subsections.label: Execution timing risk
points: Utility-scale project billing delays with large institutional customers (Coal India, Adani Group, Aditya Birla Group) pushed some billing into the next quarter, moderating revenue growth below expectations.

subsections.label: Investor confidence / market cap disconnect
points: Management acknowledged a disconnect between business growth and share price/market cap performance, with the stock trading at roughly half the sector PE despite doubling growth, as raised by an investor.

key_figures.label: Revenue estimate on conservative 30% growth basis

subsections.label: Growth guidance moderation
points: Management is being conservative on the 40-50% growth guidance given earlier (including by the Chairman/CMD in a separate interview) due to geopolitical conditions creating execution hurdles; targeting 30-40% YoY growth for now, with upside to 50-60% if conditions settle.
CPP segment: management reiterated they are keen on increasing growth back to the 40-50%/50-60% levels previously guided, contingent on geopolitical conditions.
On a conservative 30% growth basis, revenue estimated at ~INR3,500 crore for FY27, with expected net profit margin of ~15%, implying PAT of ~INR520 crore.

subsections.label: PAT margin guidance walk-back
points: Previously guided 16-18% PAT margin for FY27 will not be met at that level this year; margin will be lower than earlier guidance due to lost seasonality-impacted quarters (Q1 and Q2), though H2 (Q3-Q4) will cover a portion of the gap.
Full-fledged benefit of plant stabilization, and margins closer to historical levels, expected in FY28 once plants are fully stabilized.
In absolute terms, PAT is still expected to grow compared to last year, even if the percentage margin is uncertain and dependent on seasonality (wind, sun, rain).

subsections.label: IPP capacity utilization ramp
points: Peak capacity utilization for current IPP build expected in Q3 or Q4 of FY27, with Q2 impacted by monsoon.
At full 1GW+ IPP run rate, top line from IPP segment expected to be a minimum of INR1,000+ crore, with EBITDA margin of 85-90%.
Next financial year (FY28), IPP segment revenue expected to exceed INR1,000 crore (management calls this a conservative number).

subsections.label: Interest and depreciation outlook
points: Full interest cost (previously partly capitalized as IDC) will now be booked as expense as construction completes, while depreciation will be recognized in a phase-wise manner as portions of plants are capitalized post-COD.
Exact interest/depreciation figures for FY27 are difficult to specify given phase-wise disbursement and capitalization timing tied to real-time project commissioning.

guidance_ledger.statement: The growth we have committed for 30% to 40% year-on-year, that is something that which we will be able to maintain.
40%, 50% growth we have said earlier also... if we get an opportunity if this condition settles down, we'll surely jump towards 50%, 60%.
PAT margin guidance of 16% to 18% will be less compared to what was shown/guided earlier due to lost quarters from seasonality; full benefit expected in FY28.

guidance_ledger.metric: Debt to equity (long-term debt to net worth)
guidance_ledger.statement: Debt to equity will be in the comfortable position of 3:1 max to max, which will be long-term debt to net worth.

guidance_ledger.metric: IPP top line at full 1GW run rate
guidance_ledger.statement: I am expecting at least my top line coming from my IPP segment going forward, minimum it will be upwards of INR1,000 crores.
Altogether, you can see that the business will be able to generate INR1,500-1,600 crore plus of revenue minimum.
I can expect it in the third or the fourth quarter [to be at peak capacity]. Second quarter is a little bit rainy...so it will offset.
My annual interest cost for the full year with the entire capacity, like I say that '27,'28 would be around INR450-odd crores.
My IPP business gives me an EBITDA of 85% to 90%.
As soon as the things improve, we will be able to jump back to our margins; we are keen on getting back to our old levels (20%).
The total investment might go upwards of INR5,000-6,000 crore in the asset side as we go forward in '27, '28... in a phase-wise manner.
Sun Drops, I think this year on the IPP and the CPP side, if I look at, we will cross INR1,500-odd crore of top line in this year.
By execution point of view, I think this year, we will not see any revenue. Upcoming years, you'll start seeing revenues in the Botswana project also.
In absolute terms, it will surely grow. The PAT will grow compared to the absolute [prior year].
We will try to maintain IPP at a level of 20-odd percent of the total revenue mix.
Total capacity on IPP side expected to add approximately 1.6-1.7 gigawatt, majority of which will be this financial year.
We are on track to achieve our 10-gigawatt target by 2030, and we are confident that we will reach this milestone ahead of schedule.
First commitment of 500 megawatts by end of FY - by end of December '27.
The peak interest cost approximately would be at around INR300-odd crores.
We will curtail the drop this year itself, and next year we'll see ROE coming back to the earlier levels.
250 megawatt we have October '26.
Another 370 megawatts we have again October '26.
New 150 megawatt, we have November 27.

We will be able to contribute 40% to 50% growth year-on-year with the existing order book and with the new order book; even post FY27 on a higher base can continue to grow at 30%, 40% on the CPP side.
Sundrops will be coming up shortly with filing of DRHP for the IPO... this year, this financial year, we'll be doing the listing for Sundrops.

guidance_ledger.metric: BESS revenue contribution to top line
guidance_ledger.statement: Next year, '27, '28, we'll find the revenue getting clocked into our top line of Sundrop.
Within 3 months after COD completion, I think by March '27, all the pledge will be released by the bank.
As the share of IPP increases, EBITDA margin is expected to keep rising; we don't want it to go down, we want margins maintained or improved while CPP business also grows.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical conditions impacting input costs (steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics, ROW, crane/diesel costs)
risk_register.note: First call where 'geopolitical' terminology used extensively; impacts cost side, not sales, and hits EPC-heavy KP Energy harder than IPP-diversified KPI Green.
Q2 monsoon season typically dampens generation; two consecutive quarters flagged as impacted, causing PAT margin dip versus prior guidance.

risk_register.risk: Utility-scale billing delays with large institutional customers
risk_register.note: Billing with Coal India, Adani Group, Aditya Birla Group got postponed to next quarter, moderating revenue growth below expected 20-30%.

risk_register.risk: Rising leverage/depreciation-interest drag on PAT and EPS from rapid IPP scale-up
risk_register.note: EPS turned negative YoY for the first time; management calls this temporary/life-cycle related, expected to normalize by FY28.

risk_register.risk: Market cap / share price disconnect from business growth
risk_register.note: Market cap fallen ~60% despite growth doubling; stock trading at roughly half sector PE, per investor question.

risk_register.risk: Uncertain timeline for geopolitical cost resolution
risk_register.note: Issue expected to resolve ~6 months ago but has resurfaced repeatedly, making margin recovery timing unpredictable.

risk_register.risk: Grid stabilization charges newly introduced in Maharashtra under base-compatibility policy
risk_register.note: Impact on CPP segment feasibility still being evaluated; not present in Gujarat or other states currently.

risk_register.risk: Renewable energy curtailment during peak hours (solar and wind)
risk_register.note: Largely a transmission bottleneck being discussed at CERC/transco level; no concrete deadline for resolution; most CTU augmentation projects slated for 2028-2030.

risk_register.risk: Sector-wide growth deceleration / geopolitical and economic slowdown
risk_register.note: Cited as reason for moderating growth guidance from 50-60%/60-70% CAGR down to 40-50% CAGR through FY30.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation (solar modules, steel, copper)
risk_register.note: Mitigated via advances to manufacturers and inventory stocking to protect EPC margins.

risk_register.risk: Rising interest and depreciation costs from IPP capex ramp-up compressing ROCE/ROE
risk_register.note: ROCE fell from 18-19% to 13-14%; expected to stabilize this year and recover next year.

risk_register.risk: Delay in project revenue recognition due to third-party (GSECL) substation completion
risk_register.note: Khavda project billing delayed 6-7 months; PPA tenure extended and partial billing accepted; remaining substation work expected to complete this quarter.
~50% of promoter shares pledged pre-IPO; SBI has sanctioned release upon COD completion of 250MW/370MW projects, expected by March 2027.

themes.label: IPP ramp-up drag on returns
themes.note: PAT declined YoY and EPS turned negative for the first time due to upfront depreciation and interest recognition on newly commissioned IPP capacity, even as EBITDA and cash profit grew.

themes.label: Growth guidance moderation
themes.note: Management moderated FY27 revenue growth guidance to 30-40% YoY (from earlier 40-50% CAGR commitment) citing geopolitical conditions, while reiterating upside potential if conditions ease.

themes.label: IPP/CPP portfolio mix and margin management
themes.note: Company aims to hold IPP at ~20% of revenue mix for its 85-90% EBITDA margin and 25-year annuity visibility, while CPP/EPC margins (especially at KP Energy) have been squeezed more sharply by input cost inflation.

themes.label: BESS and new-segment diversification
themes.note: Company progressing on BESPA (565MW/1,130MWh), floating solar (142MW Kadana Dam), wind (150MW GUVNL, 300MW SJVN), and energy trading licenses (GERC/CERC), alongside future focus on green hydrogen, offshore wind and pump storage.

themes.label: International expansion (Botswana)
themes.note: 5GW MOU signed with Botswana government, 500 hectares of land acquired, PPA signing at advanced stage, but no revenue expected this fiscal year; UAE BESS-integrated data centre project also underway via Sun Drops.

themes.label: Input cost and supply chain hedging
themes.note: Geopolitical conditions have driven up costs of steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics and equipment hire, impacting EPC-heavy KP Energy far more sharply (EBITDA margin 22% to 12%) than IPP-diversified KPI Green (~300bps impact).

themes.label: Sustainable financing and market access
themes.note: Company continues to build on its India-first externally credit-enhanced INR670 crore green bond (8.50% coupon, AA+ rated, 65% GuarantCo guarantee), reinforcing lender/market confidence.

pressing_questions: Given the expansion of our IPP segment, could you give us some color on how you see the debt and cash position evolving going forward?

While we have maintained our margins on a broader basis, our execution was very slow as compared to our guidance in this quarter — what is the reason, and how should we look at revenue and margin for full year FY27?
When you are saying 30%, 40% growth, this is different from what your Chairman and Mr. Farukbhai yesterday mentioned in the interview about 40%, 50% CAGR — just wanted clarity.
Are you thinking about any changes in the proportion between IPP and CPP given the strain on the balance sheet, continuous equity infusion, and EPS turning negative for the first time?
The gross margins for the CPP segment for KP Energy and KPI have fallen substantially — is this a onetime issue or the new normal?
You had guided 16% to 18% PAT margin for FY27, and Q1 is quite low — do you expect to cover it in H2, or do you want to revise that guidance?

Despite the company's growth doubling, market cap has fallen by nearly 60% and the stock trades at roughly half the sector PE — where does management believe this weakness is coming from, and what concrete actions have been taken to attract institutional investors?

quarters.summary: FY26 was a strong year with revenue up 56% YoY, EBITDA up 73% and PAT up 57%; management guides to 40-50% YoY growth in revenue/PAT going forward (down from earlier 50-60% commentary), while IPP capacity ramp-up (COD Oct'26/Nov'27) and associated interest/depreciation costs are expected to weigh on ROE/ROCE near-term before turning EPS/cash-flow accretive from FY27-28 onward. Company continues to build out IPP, CPP, BESS (via Sundrops), floating solar, green hydrogen, wind, power trading and international (Botswana) growth avenues, targeting 10GW by 2030.

subsections.label: Growth Drivers & Momentum
points: Journey over the past 5 years reflects strength and scalability of the business model with 92% CAGR in sales and 104% CAGR in profit.
Total assets have more than doubled every year over the last three years, driven by disciplined investment in renewable assets, land, evacuation infrastructure and execution capabilities.
Q4 FY26 numbers reflect strong momentum in closing quarter and demonstrate ability to execute at scale while maintaining profitability.

subsections.label: Interest Cost Drivers
points: Interest cost increased sharply YoY because last year a QIP was used to repay long-term and short-term loans, keeping FY25 interest cost artificially low; this year more capacity was added (250MW, 370MW, 240MW) which is capex-heavy for the IPP segment, raising interest costs.
Peak interest cost is expected to be around INR300-odd crores; IPP segment breakeven for any project is typically 6-7 years but strong cash flow from the IPP segment is expected from FY27-28.
Because PPAs (e.g., with GUVNL) allow phase-wise commissioning in batches of 25MW/50MW, revenue starts flowing even during construction, partially offsetting interest cost burden.

subsections.label: ROE/ROCE Trajectory
points: ROCE has dropped from 18-19% to 13-14%; management expects to curtail the drop this year and expects ROE to recover to earlier levels next year.
Full financial impact (positive) from IPP capacity addition expected only in FY27-28 when entire plants are operational and revenue fully flows in.

subsections.label: Other Income / Depreciation / Finance Cost movements
points: Other income rose from ~INR20 crores to ~INR45 crores due to interest income on fixed deposits accumulated through the year.
Depreciation more than doubled due to asset additions; consolidated asset base rose from ~INR2,500 crores to over INR5,000 crores.

Finance costs rose substantially because last year's QIP proceeds temporarily reduced borrowings/interest; this year working capital limits were increased in line with higher top line, raising interest cost.

subsections.label: Working Capital & Debtor/Inventory Days
points: Working capital requirement is higher due to the EPC business; working capital increase has also raised interest cost, but operating cash flow generation remains healthy.

Debtor days have declined despite top-line growth, as debtors have remained at similar absolute levels; inventory days have risen due to deliberate stock build-up (30-40% of order book value) to hedge against input cost inflation and supply-chain/geopolitical risk, ensuring timely execution.

subsections.label: Cash Flow Outlook
points: Operating cash flow more than doubled YoY, crossing INR400 crores from ~INR200 crores previously.

IPP segment does not require working capital, unlike CPP/EPC; hence increasing IPP share is expected to have a positive impact on operating cash flows going forward, since it adds strong EBITDA without absorbing working capital.

subsections.label: Project Wins During the Year
points: Secured several strategic project wins across solar, wind, hybrid, floating solar, green hydrogen and BESS.

Wins include: 150 MW wind project with GUVNL; 445/890 MWh standalone BESS project; 120/240 MWh standalone BESS project; 142 MW floating solar project; 250 MW solar project from SJVN; 1.13 GW solar balance-of-plant project from Adani Group; 300 MW wind project from SJVN.

subsections.label: Bid Pipeline & Win Ratio Strategy
points: Overall bid pipeline stands at 4-5 GW; historical win ratio has been around 75%, but going forward the company plans to be more selective, focusing on high-margin tenders and those enabling faster execution.

Industry-wide, more than 20-30 GW of projects are scheduled to be commissioned over the next two years, and KPI is positioning as an execution partner for other IPP customers in addition to bidding directly.

key_figures.label: Expected annual generation from IPP portfolio
CPP order book executed to date

subsections.label: IPP Strategy & Portfolio Mix
points: Focus remains on strengthening IPP portfolio, expanding CPP business and building capabilities in future growth segments: BESS, green hydrogen, floating solar, offshore wind, pump storage and energy trading.
IPP segment gives very strong EBITDA (~85-90%); increasing IPP share in overall revenue mix is expected to improve profitability as EPC/CPP growth alone would strain margins.
Company aims to maintain or improve margins by balancing IPP growth against continued EPC/CPP segment growth (EPC order book of ~INR5,000 crores).

subsections.label: Khavda IPP Project Delay
points: Khavda project billing was delayed by 6-7 months (not a full year) because the government substation under GSECL's scope was not completed on time, even though the plant itself was ready.

GSECL has agreed to extend the PPA tenure to compensate for the delay, and is accepting partial power infusion/billing for completed portions (e.g., 120 MW of a 240 MW project) even before the substation is fully complete.
Some portion of the GSECL substation capacity is still pending and expected to be completed by this quarter end, after which full revenue recognition will begin.

subsections.label: CPP / EPC Order Book Composition
points: CPP order book of INR5,246 crores includes both new orders and pending balance from previous order book; includes major orders such as Aditya Birla, Adani Green, and multiple orders in Sundrop not fully factored into the headline number due to being small orders.

CPP capacity additions are recognized in the presentation only upon full project completion (milestone billing basis), so YoY capacity-addition comparisons are not like-for-like; a quarter may show a large addition simply because a long-running project completed.

Exact conversion of order book value to capacity/megawatt is not precise since some orders include material (panels/turbines) and some do not; company declined to disclose the split between with-material and without-material order value citing competitive sensitivity.

subsections.label: BESS (Battery Energy Storage) Outlook
points: BESS addresses the intermittency/FDRE (Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy) issue in solar/wind generation; DISCOMs and government institutions want dispatchable renewable power.
Margins in BESS are not as lucrative as IPP; profitability depends heavily on tender-win pricing and evolving VGF (Viability Gap Funding) support; most projects likely rental-model based.
Market is nascent; various states (Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat) have declared gigawatt-scale BESS targets/policies; tariff structures will depend on time-of-day demand curves.
Two major BESS orders currently held: 445/890 MWh and 120/240 MWh, both with end-customer GUVNL.

Sundrops Energia (KPI subsidiary) has been dedicated to the BESS and battery manufacturing segment; DRHP filing and IPO listing targeted this financial year, with revenue expected to be clocked into Sundrop's top line from FY27-28.
VGF alone is not seen as a long-term solution; as volumes scale toward India's 250 GWh 2030 target, in-house facility/manufacturing scale-up is expected to bring cost reductions.

subsections.label: IPP Capacity Ramp-up Timeline
points: IPP capacity as on March 31, 2026 was 965 MW; as of the call date, capacity has already crossed the 1 GW mark following CEIG approvals.

Total IPP capacity (DC level) is targeted to reach approximately 1.6-1.7 GW mostly within this financial year (FY27), with COD for 250MW and 370MW projects set for October 2026 and 150MW wind project for November 2027.
A further 300MW SJVN wind project's COD cannot yet be given as the PPA is yet to be signed; PPA signing typically allows 18-24 months for project completion thereafter.

key_figures.label: 1 gigawatt IPP capacity in hand referenced for phased breakeven discussion
Plant portion generating revenue before COD

subsections.label: Land Bank Composition
points: Out of total 7,210 acres, approximately 800-1,000 acres is owned by the company; the remainder is held under 26-27 year lease agreements with farmers or private partners.
Land bank and power evacuation are cited as the two key enablers of the company's growth, and evacuation is not considered a bottleneck for growth despite slower headline evacuation growth this year.

subsections.label: Evacuation Capacity Growth
points: Evacuation capacity growth slowed this year (3.26 GW to 3.59 GW, ~10% increase) versus a 100% increase from FY24 (1.6 GW) to FY25 (3.26 GW).

Management attributes the slower headline growth to the evacuation approval process requiring applications across multiple group companies, with plans to transfer evacuation rights to KPI later; multiple evacuation applications are pending and expected to reflect in future growth.

subsections.label: Geographic Expansion
points: Beyond core Gujarat operations, the company has entered Rajasthan (recent order win), and has taken initial project resources in Karnataka; also participating in Odisha's floating solar bidding process.
Company is now planning entry into Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

In Maharashtra, traction has been limited historically; the state has recently declared BESS-compatible project policies mandating base-load compatibility for projects above 100 kW, creating renewed interest particularly for round-the-clock users like data centers; KPI is in advanced stages of resource search (land, grid connectivity) in Maharashtra.

subsections.label: International Expansion — Botswana
points: A company has been set up in Botswana as a step-down subsidiary of KPI (via a GIFT City entity), enabling fund infusion under FEMA's Overseas Direct Investment (ODI) rules, which permit investment up to 4x the parent company's net worth into international/step-down subsidiaries.
All groundwork, approvals, teams and offices in Botswana have been established; PPAs are expected to be signed shortly in Botswana or neighboring countries.

First commitment target is 500 MW by end of December 2027; equity funding will leverage KPI's growing net worth, with additional options like InvIT under consideration; in-principle approvals already secured from various international funds for investment into Botswana.

key_figures.label: Input cost as % of project cost (panels/turbines)

subsections.label: Input Cost & Inventory Hedge Strategy
points: Major input costs are panels and turbines, comprising 60-70% of total project cost under 'with material' contracts.

Company has given advances to turbine and panel manufacturers and built up stock/inventory on its books to hedge against rising input prices amid geopolitical conditions, helping safeguard and maintain profitability margins.
Inventory build-up (~30-40% of order book value) is deliberate to enable timely execution of the large order book and avoid delays from supply-chain/geopolitical disruptions.

key_figures.label: Solar balance of plant project from Adani Group

subsections.label: Sustainable Financing Milestone
points: Successfully listed India's first externally credit-enhanced green bond — INR670 crores, 5-year instrument, 8.50% coupon, quarterly amortization, backed by a 65% partial guarantee from GuarantCo (an international private infrastructure development group), rated AA+(CE) by CRISIL and ICRA.

This innovative structure broadened the investor base among long-tenured domestic institutions and set a new benchmark for sustainable finance in India, reinforcing market confidence in KPI Green's business model and governance.

subsections.label: Power Trading License
points: KPI Green received both an interstate trading license from CERC and an intrastate trading license from GERC, enabling participation in pan-India power market exchange and bilateral contracts, creating wider market access, better realization opportunities and enhanced portfolio flexibility.

subsections.label: Sundrops Energia IPO
points: Sundrops Energia (subsidiary dedicated to BESS and battery manufacturing) plans to shortly file its DRHP for an IPO; listing targeted within this financial year.
Substantial growth targeted for Sundrops next year as well, building on FY26 performance.

subsections.label: Promoter Pledge Reduction Plan
points: Approximately 50% of promoter shares are pledged, originally pledged pre-IPO as collateral security for upcoming projects.

State Bank of India has sanctioned release of pledge (as part of the current INR3,000 crores sanction for 250MW/370MW projects) upon COD completion of these projects; full pledge release expected within 3 months of COD, by around March 2027.

subsections.label: Long-term Vision
points: Company is on track to achieve its 10 GW target by 2030 and is confident of reaching this milestone ahead of schedule.
Vision extends beyond India to develop renewable energy projects in international markets, leveraging proven execution capabilities and industry expertise.
Strategic focus remains on increasing the share of the IPP business to build a stable annuity income stream for the next 25 years.

subsections.label: Grid Stabilization Charges (Maharashtra)
points: Maharashtra has newly introduced grid stabilization charges under a policy requiring base compatibility of 50% mandatory; KPI is evaluating project feasibility and impact of these charges on CPP segment economics.
As of now, the exact impact is uncertain and requires detailed evaluation; management noted Maharashtra has high captive charges that could offset impact elsewhere.
Such grid stabilization charges are not present in Gujarat or other states currently.

subsections.label: Renewable Energy Curtailment
points: Curtailment of renewable energy during peak hours (both solar and wind) is a widely discussed industry issue, largely a transmission-related constraint, being examined by CERC and various transcos/discoms/state ERCs.

Solutions being discussed include creating green corridors for proper power evacuation and load flow studies; most CTU (Central Transmission Utility) projects addressing this are slated for 2028-2030, with no concrete deadline or verdict yet from CERC.

subsections.label: Sector Growth Deceleration / Guidance Moderation
points: Management acknowledged that overall renewable sector growth acceleration has moderated compared to earlier periods (when CAGR guidance of 50-60%, 60-70%, even 70-80% was given), attributing this to geopolitical conditions and economic slowdown; growth guidance has moderated to 40-50% CAGR through FY30.
Despite the moderation, management emphasized that few or no other companies in the renewable sector are achieving 40-50% YoY growth, and reiterated commitment to this growth trajectory.

subsections.label: Input Cost Inflation
points: Rising prices of key inputs — solar modules, steel and copper — pose a risk to EPC margins; company mitigates this through advances to manufacturers and inventory stocking.

subsections.label: IPP Ramp-up Drag on Returns
points: Rising interest costs (up 130% YoY) and depreciation (more than doubled) tied to IPP capex have compressed ROCE from 18-19% to 13-14%, with recovery expected only from FY27-28 as capacity becomes fully operational.

subsections.label: Project Execution Delay (Khavda)
points: Revenue billing on the Khavda IPP project was delayed 6-7 months due to incomplete government (GSECL) substation infrastructure, outside KPI's direct control, though compensated via PPA tenure extension and partial billing.

subsections.label: Growth Guidance Evolution
points: Management reiterated a binding commitment (per CMD Dr. Faruk Patel) to grow at 40-50% YoY, moderated from previously communicated ranges of 50-60% and, historically, 60-70%/70-80% CAGR through FY30.

Management maintains that despite geopolitical conditions and economic slowdown reducing sector-wide acceleration, KPI continues to outperform peers, with few other renewable companies achieving similar growth rates.
CPP segment growth of 30-40% is expected to be sustainable even on a higher base into FY28-29, supported by a large addressable market and pipeline of tenders.

subsections.label: ROE/Margin Outlook
points: Management expects to curtail the ROE/ROCE decline this year and for ROE to recover to earlier levels next year.
EBITDA margin is expected to keep rising as the IPP share increases in the overall mix, while CPP/EPC growth is maintained in parallel to sustain top-line growth.

subsections.label: Capacity & Expansion Targets
points: IPP capacity guided to reach ~1.6-1.7 GW largely within FY27; specific COD dates given for 250MW/370MW (Oct 2026) and 150MW wind (Nov 2027) projects.
Company reaffirmed its 10 GW target by 2030, with confidence of achieving it ahead of schedule.
Botswana operations targeted to reach a first commitment of 500 MW by December 2027.
Sundrops Energia (BESS subsidiary) IPO/DRHP filing targeted within this financial year; BESS revenue expected to start contributing to top line from FY27-28.

guidance_ledger.statement: We are binded to grow at a rate of 40% to 50% year-on-year; this year also we are committing to that growth on the top line and profitability.
Total capacity on IPP side expected to add approximately 1.6-1.7 gigawatt, majority of which will be this financial year.
We are on track to achieve our 10-gigawatt target by 2030, and we are confident that we will reach this milestone ahead of schedule.
First commitment of 500 megawatts by end of FY - by end of December '27.
The peak interest cost approximately would be at around INR300-odd crores.
We will curtail the drop this year itself, and next year we'll see ROE coming back to the earlier levels.
250 megawatt we have October '26.
Another 370 megawatts we have again October '26.
New 150 megawatt, we have November 27.

We will be able to contribute 40% to 50% growth year-on-year with the existing order book and with the new order book; even post FY27 on a higher base can continue to grow at 30%, 40% on the CPP side.
Sundrops will be coming up shortly with filing of DRHP for the IPO... this year, this financial year, we'll be doing the listing for Sundrops.

guidance_ledger.metric: BESS revenue contribution to top line
guidance_ledger.statement: Next year, '27, '28, we'll find the revenue getting clocked into our top line of Sundrop.
Within 3 months after COD completion, I think by March '27, all the pledge will be released by the bank.
As the share of IPP increases, EBITDA margin is expected to keep rising; we don't want it to go down, we want margins maintained or improved while CPP business also grows.

themes.label: IPP ramp-up drag on returns
themes.note: Rising interest and depreciation from IPP capex have compressed ROCE from 18-19% to 13-14%, with recovery expected only from FY27-28 as capacity turns cash-flow positive.

themes.label: Growth guidance moderation
themes.note: CAGR guidance moderated from 50-60%/60-70% to 40-50% through FY30, attributed to geopolitical and macro slowdown rather than company-specific weakness.

themes.label: IPP/CPP portfolio mix and margin management
themes.note: IPP EBITDA margin (85-90%) far exceeds EPC/CPP (16-18%); management balancing growth of both to sustain top line while protecting margins.

themes.label: BESS and new-segment diversification
themes.note: Sundrops Energia dedicated to BESS/battery manufacturing, targeting IPO/DRHP this year; BESS market nascent with margins dependent on VGF and tender pricing.

themes.label: International expansion (Botswana)
themes.note: Step-down subsidiary set up in Botswana under FEMA ODI rules; targeting first 500MW commitment by December 2027.

themes.label: Input cost and supply chain hedging
themes.note: Rising panel/turbine/steel/copper costs mitigated via manufacturer advances and inventory build-up (30-40% of order book).

themes.label: Sustainable financing and market access
themes.note: India's first externally credit-enhanced green bond (INR670 crores, AA+(CE)) and new CERC/GERC power trading licenses broaden funding and revenue realization options.

key_takeaways: FY '25-26 has been another landmark year for KPI Green Energy Limited with strong growth across all key financial and operational parameters.
Compounded growth over the past 5 years has been remarkable with 92% CAGR in sales and 104% CAGR in profit.
Total income stood at INR2,742 crores for FY26 vs INR1,755 crores in FY25, growth of 56% YoY; EBITDA increased to INR1,006 crores (73% growth); PAT stood at INR509 crores (57% growth).
Installed capacity stood at over 1.62 gigawatt with work-in-progress capacity of over 4.64 gigawatts; installed plus upcoming portfolio reached approximately 6.26 gigawatts.
Successfully listed India's first externally credit-enhanced green bond of INR670 crores, rated AA+(CE), backed by a 65% partial guarantee from GuarantCo.
Received both interstate trading license from CERC and intrastate trading license from GERC, enabling participation in pan-India power market exchange.
Company reaffirmed 10-gigawatt target by 2030 and confidence of reaching it ahead of schedule; strategic focus is to increase IPP share for a stable annuity income stream for the next 25 years.

Growth guidance has moderated to 40-50% YoY through FY30, down from previously communicated 50-60% and historically 60-70%/70-80% CAGR ranges, attributed to geopolitical conditions and sector-wide deceleration.
pressing_questions: When is the breakeven going to happen for the IPP segment, and what is the peak interest burden the P&L will absorb, and at what point does IPP transition become EPS accretive rather than dilutive?
Can ROE/ROCE be expected to continue declining until FY28 given the phased IPP ramp-up?
Why has evacuation capacity growth slowed to only ~10% YoY versus 100% growth the prior year?
What is the current status and equity funding structure of the Botswana project?
Why has the growth guidance moved from 50-60% to 40-50%, and is there a structural slowdown?
What is the equity IRR of a BESS project compared to a regular IPP project? (unanswered due to call audio issues)
What is the current CPP order book, and how does INR5,246 crores reconcile with the previously mentioned INR6,000 crores?
Why has inventory increased ~4x with a 2x increase in inventory days despite declining debtor days?

MANORAMA.about: Manorama Industries is engaged in manufacturing specialty fats and butter made from exotic seeds and nuts. [1]

quarters.summary: Manorama delivered 39.5% YoY revenue growth in Q1 FY27, crossing INR 4,000 million quarterly revenue and EBITDA for the first time, with PAT up 67.6% YoY. Management guided to full-year fractionation capacity utilization of ~80-85% on the enlarged 52,000 tons capacity, a capex spend of ~INR 225-250 crores in FY27 (part of a larger ~INR 460 crore program), commissioning of the new solvent fractionation/refinery (India) and backward-integration plant (Burkina Faso) tentatively by Q3 FY28 with full revenue visibility from FY29, and continued healthy top-line growth in FY27 supported by capacity ramp-up and product mix improvement; margins are expected to remain broadly stable/sustainable going forward.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: 39.5% YoY revenue growth driven by richer product mix of value-added offerings and higher traction of expanded fractionation capacity.
EBITDA and PAT growth reflects sustained demand across end-use industries, deeper customer relationships and increasing contribution of value-added specialty fats and butters portfolio.
PAT margin improvement reflects continued focus on optimizing product mix, enhancing capacity utilization and driving efficiencies across operations.
Gross margin moves in the 45-50% range depending on freight cost timing and by-product (de-oiled cake) realization; best tracked with EBITDA margin rather than in isolation.
Raw material cost runs at approximately 50% of sales annually.

subsections.label: Cost items
points: Employee cost decline QoQ (~20%) attributed to a one-time performance incentive provision in the prior quarter; going forward run rate expected around INR 14-15 crores per quarter.
Other expenses increase (16%) primarily due to higher freight and container costs.
Other income of INR 16 crores (INR 13 crores forex gain, INR 3 crores FDR/other) primarily from FDR income and forex gains, not related to QIP proceeds received this quarter; expected to normalize.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / balance sheet
points: Successful completion of INR 500 crore QIP strengthens balance sheet and provides financial flexibility to accelerate growth across manufacturing, sourcing and high value-added segments.
FDR balance excluding QIP stands at INR 150 crores.
Company aligned with existing bankers (State Bank of India as lead banker) with sanctioned bank limits for working capital requirements.
No further equity dilution planned in near term after the recent QIP; additional working capital needs expected to be met via debt/existing facilities.
Requirement of around 50% in terms of raw material funding for the business.
Hedging ratio of net forex exposure maintained at 50-60% under ongoing policy.
Asset turn currently around 7x.
Company has delivered 20-25 consistent quarters of good performance over the last 3-4 years.

subsections.label: Subsidiary financials
points: Consolidated vs standalone revenue difference is minimal (INR 4-5 lakhs) this quarter.
Subsidiary PAT losses declined from INR 8 crores in Q4 FY26 to INR 3 crores in Q1 FY27 as prior one-time costs did not recur; current costs are normal operational costs for subsidiaries.
West African entities are mostly cost/procurement vehicles with no standalone revenue, so consolidation carries operating costs without corresponding top line.

Brazil (Dekel) entity is in a build-out phase establishing commercial volumes; these are deliberate funded investments in long-term capability expected to reduce drag on consolidated margins over time and eventually become contributors.

key_figures.label: CBE and stearin contribution to revenue
Volume-led growth contribution to overall growth

subsections.label: Product mix
points: CBE and stearin together contribute 71.4% of revenue, with CBE forming 30% within that combined figure; both are described as technically similar products.

Pricing for value-added, formulated products (based on customer specifications/recipes for confectionery, chocolate, cosmetics) has remained largely stable in line with the costing model, despite macro volatility.
Realization per ton for CBE and stearin not disclosed as products are not single SKUs but multiple formulations/specifications for different customers.
Revenue contribution from imported seeds/butters is 50-60%, versus ~50% from domestic seeds/butters.

subsections.label: Growth composition
points: 39% YoY growth is largely volume-led, with approximately 85% of the Y-o-Y growth attributable to volume.

subsections.label: Contract structure
points: Customer contracts run on a 9-12 month cycle; renewals are an ongoing process not concentrated in a specific quarter, so renewal percentage by quarter cannot be quantified.

subsections.label: CBA / ECBE technology
points: New CBA (cocoa butter alternative) product technology under development at an ESOS plant in India, converting oil liquid fractions into hard fractions using enzymes, producing a solid fraction termed ECBE (enzymatic cocoa butter equivalent).
ECBE applications mirror cocoa butter alternative uses in food segment — chocolate, confectionery, HoReCa market and other food applications.
Technology represents a forward integration model enabling use of existing raw materials as well as additional raw materials beyond currently imported/locally bought nuts.
Company also uses an interesterification process to create value-added products from co-products/by-products like olein and other specialty fats and butters.
R&D team continuously working to create more value-added products from the existing product portfolio.

key_figures.label: Already operationalized portion of debottlenecking (of 7,500 tons planned)
Payback period for Burkina Faso plant

subsections.label: Capacity and utilization
points: Current fractionation capacity stands at 47,500 tons; incremental debottlenecking of 4,500 tons planned for FY27 to take total capacity to 52,000 tons.
Of a 7,500-ton debottlenecking plan, that full portion has already been operationalized to date.
Capacity utilization stood at 80% in Q1 FY27, in line with full-year guidance of 80-85%.
Balance debottlenecking capacity intended to be implemented during FY27 around Q3, subject to operational timelines.
Second plant debottlenecking also planned around Q3, supporting full-year utilization guidance of 80-85%.
Management internal execution target is 80-85%, but guides stakeholders to take 80% as the base utilization figure; any improvement (85-90%) will be communicated as achieved.

subsections.label: New capex program
points: Total proposed new capex plan is INR 460 crores; FY27 capex guidance is INR 225-250 crores, with ~INR 20 crores spent in Q1 FY27 and ~INR 70 crores cumulatively spent to date, leaving ~INR 220 crores planned for the remainder of FY27.
Debottlenecking cost is INR 5-6 crores.
Solvent fractionation 3 and refinery expansion targeted for commissioning around Q3 FY28 in India.

Burkina Faso facility (extraction and expelling capacity) also tentatively targeted for commissioning around Q3 FY28; regulatory approvals awaited; project capex is INR 120-130 crores with an expected payback period of ~3 years post-operational.
New capex will start contributing to revenue gradually from commissioning, but full impact expected to be more visible in FY29 as these are technical plants requiring gradual utilization ramp-up.
Of the total INR 460 crore proposed capex, Burkina Faso portion is ~INR 120-130 crores, with the balance allocated to Indian projects (solvent fractionation, refinery, extraction/expelling).
Management unwilling to disclose specific land purchase cost for the 24-acre Burkina Faso plot beyond the overall ~INR 120 crore project figure.

subsections.label: Asset turn outlook
points: Current asset turn is approximately 7x; management could not commit to a specific future asset turn (7x/8x/9x) for the new facilities but aims to perform in line with historical direction; positive on new investments providing steady, healthy growth over a 3-5 year horizon (FY30-31).

Shea-nut growing countries in Africa presence footprint

subsections.label: Export/domestic mix
points: Export to domestic revenue mix stood at 60:40, reflecting continued strength of global customer base alongside healthy domestic demand.
In Q1 FY26 (comparable prior year quarter), export share was in the range of 55-60% (also referenced as 50-60%).

subsections.label: Sourcing diversification / route risk
points: Company supplies to more than 30 countries and sources raw materials from Africa, Malaysia, Indonesia and other countries via different routes, providing high diversification in both exports and raw material sourcing, mitigating dependency on any single shipping route despite geopolitical disruption.
Company has 10 wholly owned subsidiaries across Africa regions and a presence footprint spanning 22 shea-nut growing countries in Africa.

subsections.label: Africa sourcing expansion
points: Incorporated Manorama Savannah Agro Chad Sarl in Chad, a wholly owned subsidiary, expanding sourcing footprint in West Africa.
Chad subsidiary is a vehicle for sourcing shea nut and butter raw materials from the Africa region, enhancing sourcing security, traceability and supply chain resilience.
Acquired approximately 10 hectares (24 acres) of land in Burkina Faso for a shea nut and mango nut processing facility, with regulatory approvals currently in progress.

subsections.label: Brazil / LatAm (Dekel) partnership
points: Trial production started last quarter with samples sent to the Brazilian entity (Dekel Corporation) for processing; production currently originates from the Indian plant and will be dispatched gradually to Brazil.
Ramp-up expected to occur gradually over the next 2-4 quarters as production scales quarter-on-quarter; company sees good demand scenario for products in that market.

Dekel facility is a processing facility only; revenue will be visible from the Indian plant rather than attributed separately to Dekel, and no specific revenue/margin numbers for Dekel are available yet.
Management could not quantify maximum potential revenue from the Brazil unit but is directionally confident of a good opportunity in that market.

subsections.label: R&D and integration strategy
points: MILCOA Research and Development Center, recognized by DSIR (Government of India), continues to drive product innovation and strengthen competitive advantage.
R&D capabilities play a pivotal role in shaping backward and forward integration initiatives.

Upcoming seed processing and extraction facilities in Raipur and Burkina Faso, along with exploration of downstream value-added opportunities, are expected to enhance value capture, improve margins and drive sustainable growth across the value chain.

subsections.label: Capital raise
points: Successful completion of QIP marks an important milestone, strengthening balance sheet and providing financial flexibility to accelerate growth across manufacturing, sourcing and high value-added segments.
No further equity dilution planned in the near term following the recent INR 500 crore QIP.

subsections.label: Export ban risk (Nigeria)
points: Nigeria, one of 22 shea-nut growing countries in Africa, has put a temporary export ban on shea nuts; company states this does not materially impact its sourcing strategy given its vast, substantial presence across the wider Africa region (10 wholly owned subsidiaries).
Raw material cost as % of sales expected to run at 75-80% in H1 FY27, declining below that range in H2 FY27.

subsections.label: Supplier dispute / debit note
points: Company has raised a debit note and is claiming the full amount from a manufacturer/supplier following a recent development (disclosed via exchange notification); company is diversified across multiple suppliers/countries and is not solely dependent on the supplier in question.
Company is confident of recovery within a certain time and will update per SEBI regulation as progress occurs.

subsections.label: Shipping route / geopolitical risk
points: Company supplies to more than 30 countries with diversified shipping routes for raw material sourcing (Africa, Malaysia, Indonesia, others) and exports, reducing material impact from geopolitical disruption on any single route.

Macroeconomic and geopolitical tensions (including export bans) have been ongoing for a couple of quarters; company acknowledges indirect impact possible via freight, logistics or other macro factors, but manages this through sourcing, export and production flexibility.

subsections.label: General business risk
points: Management reiterates that 'business is business, business has risk,' but states the company has built a robust model to navigate such risks.

key_figures.label: Raw material cost as % of sales

subsections.label: Growth and margin outlook
points: Management guides that FY27 has started on a very healthy note, with Q1 providing a good base and establishing a good run rate for the year; further scope of improvement expected as the year progresses, supported by capacity ramp-up and debottlenecking.
Company is confident on delivering healthy top-line growth in FY27.

Margins may see modest quarter-to-quarter movement depending on mix and one-off items, but the underlying range (gross margin 45-50%, raw material cost ~50% of sales) is expected to hold broadly stable; management guides toward 'more sustainable margin' without committing to a specific improvement trajectory at this time.
Operating leverage expected to come into play as capacities expand and product mix improves, though specific 2-3 year margin trajectory not quantified.
Employee cost run rate expected to settle at INR 14-15 crores per quarter going forward.
Full-year capacity utilization guided at 80-85%; FY27 capex guidance of INR 225-250 crores.

subsections.label: Capacity and capex timeline
points: Balance debottlenecking (part of 4,500 tons) expected to be completed around Q3 FY27, subject to operational timelines.

New capex (solvent fractionation, refinery in India; extraction/expelling in Burkina Faso) tentatively targeted for commissioning around Q3 FY28; contribution to revenue expected to start gradually from commissioning with full impact more visible in FY29.

subsections.label: Prior guidance clarification
points: In response to a question referencing a prior INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance cited from a November conference, management clarified that guidance was given on a utilization basis (around 80% utilization on 52,000 tons capacity) rather than as an absolute revenue number, and stakeholders should model revenue from that utilization guidance.

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect our [utilization] to be around 80%, 85% for full year for this year.
The balance is intended to be implemented in a manner during FY27 around Quarter 3 of this financial year, subject to operational time lines.
Ballpark capex guidance for this year should be around INR225 crores to INR 250-odd crores of investment in financial year approximately in FY27.
Total proposed capex plan of INR460 crores, with Burkina Faso portion around INR120-130 crores and balance for Indian projects.

guidance_ledger.metric: New facility commissioning (solvent fractionation, refinery, Burkina Faso)
guidance_ledger.statement: Solvent fractionation 3 and refinery are being targeted for commissioning around FY28, around Q3 of that financial year; Burkina Faso facility tentatively expected around the same period.
It should start contributing gradually from that period [Q3 FY28]. But that full impact will be more visible in the FY29 as we ramp up.
We also see further scope of improvement as the year progresses... we are very confident on delivering healthy top line growth in FY27 as well.
Margins can see modest quarter-to-quarter movement depending on mix and one-off items. But the underlying range is expected to hold broadly stable... it should hold the current range in broad terms.
We would direct you for a more sustainable margin. At this moment, we can guide you this only for that... multiple levers... should take company in an improving trajectory only.
We are very much positive that our new investments... should give us a good, steady, healthy growth for our near term vision for our 3 to 5 years for FY30, 31, we should be there.
The run rate, which we can take should be around INR14 crores to INR15 crores per quarter going forward.
Other income... should get normalized probably.
Any additional working capital over the next 2 years will be made by debt and not necessarily by equity dilution... that is not there in the plan, of course not.
Currently, executing target for the company is [85%-90%]. But for our stakeholders, we can take 80% and whatever improvement is there will be shown and will be shared to our stakeholders.

No new specific number reiterated this quarter for the previously stated FY30 revenue target of more than INR3,500 crores; management clarified prior guidance was based on utilization, not absolute revenue.
Anything between the 45%-50% level of gross margin is normal in the parlance of the business model.

The outlook for FY 27 remains strongly positive on the top-line front, driven by structural growth levers; growth primarily volume-led with some price realization benefit; overall FY27 expected to be a very good growth year.
We are very confident on the business balance to achieve that kind of a growth (25%-30%) given our coming capacities which will be there.
There is a clear output which is visible of a 30% volume accretive growth and 5%-10% could be our price realization benefit also.
All our projects are targeted to be commissioned by the financial year '28, in that particular way. It is like a two-three year window.
We are expecting that also to be streamlined in this financial year only. We will update you once that also has been done.

guidance_ledger.metric: Asset turn on forward integration project
guidance_ledger.statement: We are expecting more than 6x of asset turn on our forward integration project, which is around INR 330-340 Crores of the total capex amount.
We have just started with our Dekel operations currently... a better number guidance maybe we can give you going forward.
In relation, it could be a potential fundraise, maybe through a permissible modes and instruments and we are currently evaluating various options; will make appropriate disclosure once finalized.
We are confident to maintain going forward all subsidiary companies also healthy financials as well.

key_takeaways: We have entered financial year '27 with strong conviction and momentum delivering a 39.5% year-on-year revenue growth in quarter 1 financial year 27 and crossing the INR4,000 million quarterly revenue and EBITDA milestone for the first time.

Our profitability grew by 67.6% year-on-year, reflecting sustained demand across the end use industries, deeper customer relationships and the increasing contribution of our value-added specialty fats and butters portfolio.
We expanded our sourcing footprint in West Africa through the incorporation of Manorama Savannah Agro Chad Sarl in Chad, our wholly owned subsidiary in Chad.
We acquired approximately 10 hectares, 24 acres of land in Burkina Faso for a shea nut and mango nut processing facility with regulatory approvals currently in the progress.

The successful completion of our qualified institutional placement, QIP, marks another important milestone, strengthening our balance sheet and providing the financial flexibility to accelerate growth across manufacturing, sourcing and high value-added segments.
Revenue increased by 39.5% year-on-year to INR404 crores, driven by a richer product mix of value-added offerings and higher traction of our expanded fractionation capacity.
EBITDA grew by 42.2% year-on-year to INR106 crores, while EBITDA margin expanded by 49 basis points to 26.3%.
Profit after tax increased by 67.6% year-on-year, that is INR79 crores with profit after tax margin expanding by 326 basis points to 19.5%.

So can we expect the same 7x asset turn going forward in FY29, FY30 when this new facility will be fully ramped up?
So my question is regarding how much amount or how much percentage are we confident that we will be able to recover the amount from the supplier?
With the additional capacities coming on... how do you see operating leverage kicking in, in the next 2, 3 years for the company?

quarters.summary: Manorama Industries delivered a strong FY26 with 76.1% standalone revenue growth, EBITDA margin of 27.1% and PAT margin of 17.2%, driven by volume growth and value-added product mix improvement (CBE rising from 10% to 30% of revenue). Management guided FY27 to be a strong growth year (volume-led ~20-30% growth plus 5-10% price realization), reiterated a sustainable EBITDA margin band of 25-27% and gross margin band of 45-50% on a yearly basis, and outlined a phased ~INR 460 crore capex program (including a Burkina Faso backward-integration project and forward-integration CBA/fractionation/refinery project) targeted for commissioning by FY28, funded so far through internal accruals with an enabling QIP resolution of up to INR 500 crore kept as an optionality.

key_figures.label: Capex spent so far on INR460cr program

subsections.label: FY26 Financial Highlights
points: Manorama Industries delivered excellent financial performance in FY '25-26 with all key metrics reflecting operational execution and business momentum.
Standalone revenue growth was driven by volume growth and improved product mix.
EBITDA margin reflects focused product mix optimization and disciplined cost management.

subsections.label: Foreign exchange position and mark-to-market
points: During the quarter, due to adverse currency fluctuation, the company recognized a mark-to-market provision on forward contracts entered into in accordance with the foreign exchange hedging policy.
The company also recorded foreign exchange income during the quarter, resulting in a net foreign exchange loss for the quarter on a standalone basis.

subsections.label: Balance sheet and return ratios
points: The company's standalone balance sheet continues to reflect financial strength and discipline.
Working capital days reduced reflecting continued focus on working capital efficiency.

Whatever inventory is reported towards the end of the balance sheet year is the base to generate revenue for the coming year; inventory is well aligned with scale of operations and supports the integrated global supply chain.

subsections.label: Capital allocation and strategic outlook
points: Ongoing capacity, debottlenecking and expansion, along with strategic capex investment across India and Africa, aligns with long-term ambition to expand global footprint and strengthen position in specialty fats and butter market.
Company will continue to allocate capital with discipline, prioritizing investments that generate high return and strengthen competitive moat globally.

subsections.label: Consolidated vs standalone margin gap
points: The 5% gross margin gap on a consolidated basis versus standalone is due to newly incorporated subsidiary companies (9 subsidiaries across countries) being in their first year of operation, with initial setup-related costs including employee cost, establishment expenses and other operating overheads.

These costs are primarily influenced by freight cost and other related production costs for the newly started subsidiary operations, and chemical input costs; they are largely one-time/transitional and expected to normalize as operations scale up.
Consolidated EBITDA margin was around 26% versus 27% standalone; management does not consider this a significant margin dip and expects normalization.

subsections.label: Subsidiary losses
points: Seven audited African subsidiaries posted INR 13.5 crores losses for FY26, of which almost INR 6 crores came in Q4.

Losses attributed to first year of operation across nine subsidiary geographies (not restricted to West Africa; includes LATAM and other geographies), driving initial setup-related costs, operational costs, employee costs, and establishment expenses.
Management characterizes these as one-time and transitional in nature, expected to stabilize going forward.
Consolidated EPS grew only ~6% versus more than 150% growth seen in the previous three quarters, attributed to subsidiary costs of setting up new companies.

subsections.label: Financial correction/reporting
points: The company posted revised results because a revised financial statement file was uploaded inadvertently due to a technical issue where the wrong file was uploaded earlier; the revision is purely corrective in nature to ensure accuracy and completeness.
Shareholders were asked to consider the revised financials for further questions.

subsections.label: Reporting practice - standalone vs consolidated in press release
points: Newspaper releases report both standalone and consolidated figures per regulatory requirement; the press release/presentation reports only standalone numbers as there is no regulatory requirement to disclose consolidated figures in press releases.

Management indicated that going forward, given subsidiaries were only recently formed and this was their first year of operation, the company may start including consolidated numbers in the press release as well.

subsections.label: Funding of capex
points: From a financial strength perspective, company has a free cash Fixed Deposit of around INR 130 crores.
Company has already spent INR 52 crores on the capex project and is providing internal funding support for the planned expansion program at this stage.
Any external financing requirement will be updated to shareholders accordingly; as of now, funding is through internal accruals.

subsections.label: Product mix upgrade
points: CBE contribution to top line rose from 10% two years ago to 30% today, reflecting remarkable improvement in product mix for specialty fats and butters.
Value-added product mix (CBE plus stearin) now accounts for 70-75% of the business.

230 bps margin expansion in FY26 attributed to a mix of improved value-added product mix (CBE share rising) and higher plant utilization/manufacturing efficiency — a combination of both factors, not a single driver.

subsections.label: Fractionation output
points: Full-year fractionation utilization was around 85% (this excludes the debottlenecking facility).
