subsections.label: Capacity upgrades in FY26
points: Solvent fractionation plant 2 increased installed capacity by 30% (25,000 to 32,500 tpa) as part of an overall debottlenecking initiative.
A similar debottlenecking initiative for solvent fractionation plant 1 (15,000 metric tons) will be taken in this fiscal year.

subsections.label: Strategic capex program (~INR 460 crore)
points: Investment program spans setting up a new solvent fractionation manufacturing facility for Sal, Shea, Palm, Mango and other exotic seeds and ESOS.
Establishment of a new facility for cocoa butter alternatives (CBA).
Expansion of refining capabilities with an additional 200 tons per day refinery.
Commissioning of raw material processing units in Burkina Faso, West Africa.
These initiatives reflect focus on the long-term global opportunity, deepening competitiveness, securing reliable long-term supply, and reinforcing the foundation for sustained growth.

Projects are at different stages of implementation and ramp-up; company maintains disciplined capital allocation with an expectation of more than 6x asset turn on the forward integration project (~INR 330-340 crores of the total capex).
Forward integration project includes the CBA plant, solvent fractionation 3 plant (converting soft fraction olein into hard fractions) and a refinery plant.
All projects targeted to be commissioned by FY28, in a phased two-to-three year window.
Management expects the forward integration project to have similar or potentially better margins than current business once ramped up and optimized for product mix.

subsections.label: Burkina Faso project rationale
points: The Burkina Faso project is a backward integration initiative, envisaged capex of around INR 120 crores, aimed at eliminating logistics costs currently incurred on seed imports (seeds represent ~45-60% of raw material).
Going forward the sourcing will shift to a butter perspective rather than seed perspective, saving logistic/freight cost on seed imports from West African countries.
Expected to improve efficiency and yield on butter content, contributing to sustainable margin improvement.

It is a government-backed project, with an MoU signed with the government of Burkina Faso; management does not expect political uncertainty to affect the project, and it will also support livelihoods of forest dwellers of West Africa.
Processing seeds immediately (rather than after 60 days as currently done before bringing to India) should yield a better fat output.
Butters (not oil) will be brought to India for further value addition (fractionation etc.); the seed-processing part will be done in Burkina Faso only.

The existing 90,000-ton Indian solvent extraction facility can be better optimized for Indian exotic seeds like Sal and Mango kernels once Burkina Faso plant takes over shea nut processing — described as a dual benefit.

subsections.label: Debottlenecking progress and utilization
points: Existing capacity is at 85% utilization on 40,000 tons; debottlenecking will take capacity to 52,000 tons per annum (input capacity).
7,500 tons of debottlenecking capacity added by end of FY26; balance 4,500 tons expected to be streamlined this financial year, with an update once implemented.
Company is targeting utilization of around 85-90% on the 52,000-ton full capacity for this fiscal year, and will update quarter-to-quarter on progress.
New debottlenecking addition (52,000 tons) does not carry much cost, estimated under INR 8-10 crores for both plants.
Company plans to optimize existing Indian facility for other Indian exotic seeds (Sal, Mango) as Burkina Faso plant absorbs shea nut processing.

subsections.label: Fractionation output detail
points: Fractionation utilization for the full year was around 85%, excluding the debottlenecked facility.

subsections.label: Global footprint and subsidiaries
points: Company has expanded its global footprint with established nine subsidiaries across different countries, marking an important strategic step towards building a diversified international presence.
Operations are diversified, not restricted to West African countries; company has operations in the LATAM region as well as other geographies.

subsections.label: Middle East and geopolitical exposure
points: Middle East exposure is only 2-3% of total revenue.
Company has minimal revenue exposure to geographies affected by ongoing geopolitical tensions (Iran, U.S., Russia-Ukraine).

subsections.label: Dekel (Brazil) tolling arrangement
points: The Dekel arrangement in Brazil is a cost/processing-fee model — the company pays a processing cost per ton of goods processed; there is no profit-sharing or royalty/revenue-share agreement.
Payment is made as goods are processed (per metric ton, post-processing), not upfront for the entire year.
This is the first year/first quarter of operation through the company's own processing facility in LATAM; volumes are still minimal and ramping up, with better guidance expected going forward.

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing
points: Around 20-25% of raw material was purchased from Manorama Africa Limited (promoter entity) in FY26, versus 60% referenced for the prior year; FY27 procurement is expected to continue along the same line.

subsections.label: Foreign exchange risk management
points: Company follows a prudent and structured foreign exchange risk management policy to minimize the impact of currency volatility on earnings and cash flow.
Around 60% of net foreign exchange exposure is currently hedged through forward contracts, providing earnings visibility and protection against adverse currency movements.
The remaining ~40% unhedged exposure retains flexibility to benefit from favorable currency movements; company also has a natural hedge via import and export.

subsections.label: QIP resolution
points: The QIP resolution is an approved enabling resolution separate from the capex funding plan; it could be a potential fundraise through permissible modes and instruments.

Company is currently evaluating various options and will make appropriate disclosure in accordance with applicable law once specific transaction parameters (structure, size, timing, other terms) are finalized.

subsections.label: Long-term target
points: Company reiterated confidence in prior long-term guidance of more than INR 3,500 crores of revenue by FY30, supported by upcoming capacity additions including the 75,000-ton solvent fractionation capacity and backward integration process, aimed at building a very integrated value chain that scales both revenue and operational efficiency.

subsections.label: Closing strategic priorities
points: Expansion of manufacturing capacity to address growing demand for specialty fat products, value-added, scientifically made, and jointly collaborated with customers.
Investment in research and development to expand specialty fat formulations and application-specific products.
Centering sourcing capabilities in key raw material regions with robust supply chains.
Expanding global market presence through international subsidiaries and strategic partnerships.
Optimization of operational efficiency across the whole integrated value chain.
Target is to make every human on this earth somewhere a customer; remains committed to becoming the partner of choice for both international and domestic customers.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro risks
points: Ongoing geopolitical tensions including Iran, U.S., Russia-Ukraine, or tariffs are expected to have a near-term indirect impact, not only on the company's industry but on the broader industry environment as a whole, primarily through higher energy prices, elevated freight costs and currency volatility.

From a business fundamental perspective, the company remains largely insulated from any direct substantial impact since key raw materials (Sal, Mango, Shea) are not sourced from affected regions and revenue exposure to these geographies is minimal.
There could be some short-term macro pressure such as input cost inflation on freight, but this does not materially impact the company's core business model or long-term growth trajectory.
Despite headwinds from geopolitical tension (Russia-Ukraine war, U.S.-Iran conflict), company has reported a sustainable margin and aims to maintain and sustain this level.

subsections.label: Africa political/currency risk (Burkina Faso)
points: There are certain political, currency risks involved in operating in Africa.

The Burkina Faso project is government-backed via a signed MoU with the Government of Burkina Faso; management believes political uncertainty or insecurity will not really affect operations given the government-backed nature of the project.

subsections.label: Subsidiary start-up costs / consolidated margin dilution
points: Nine newly incorporated subsidiaries in their first year of operation have incurred initial setup-related costs (employee cost, establishment expenses, operating overheads) that have temporarily impacted consolidated margins; these are expected to be largely one-time/transitional in nature.

Seven audited African subsidiaries posted INR 13.5 crores losses for FY26 (of which ~INR 6 crores in Q4), attributed to first-year setup costs across a diversified set of nine subsidiary geographies (including LATAM).

subsections.label: Currency/forex volatility
points: Adverse currency fluctuation during the quarter resulted in a mark-to-market provision on forward contracts; cumulative mark-to-market provision for the year stood at INR 23.3 crores.
Company acknowledges this is a scenario that occurs for a time and cannot be assumed to be sustained for a lifetime, but follows a prudent, structured FX risk management policy.

subsections.label: FY27 growth outlook
points: Outlook for FY27 remains strongly positive on the top-line front, driven by structural growth levers already in motion: capacity expansion via debottlenecking (one plant already done, output increased 30% on the 25,000 metric ton plant) and continuously increasing value-added product mix.

FY27 growth is expected to be primarily volume-led with some price realization benefit, structurally driven by capacity expansion, plus global diversification into international markets with increasing value-added product mix.
Management is confident of a very good, strong growth year for FY27 as well.
Company aims to achieve growth in the 25-30% range (referenced against ~60% CAGR over the last 3 years and a now-higher base), and is confident given coming capacities.

subsections.label: Margin guidance
points: Maintained margin guidance of 25%-27% EBITDA margin; cash conversion cycle achieved in FY26 broadly expected to be in line for the next one-two years.
Guidance is to be viewed on a yearly basis rather than quarter-to-quarter, though the company tries to maintain consistency quarter-to-quarter as well.

Anything between 45%-50% gross margin and 25%-27% EBITDA margin is considered normal for the business model, per past management guidance; no significant margin dip reported at either consolidated or standalone level.

subsections.label: FY28 growth visibility (beyond capex commissioning)
points: Existing capacity is at 85% utilization on 40,000 tons; debottlenecking will raise capacity to 52,000 tons (input capacity), and value-added product mix continues to be upgraded — both current and coming fiscal years are expected to be good for growth given utilization is not yet optimized.

Expected price realization growth of 5-10% combined with ~30% volume-accretive growth, plus still-unutilized 15% of existing plant capacity, provide visibility into turnover growth over the next two years alongside further capex plans.

subsections.label: Long-term target reaffirmation
points: Management reaffirmed confidence in the previously communicated long-term goal of more than INR 3,500 crores of revenue by FY30, supported by capacity additions (75,000 tons additional solvent fractionation capacity) and backward integration aimed at an integrated value chain improving both scale and operational efficiency.
Annual cash profit (PAT + depreciation) of INR 258.77 crores already exceeds the gross block of INR 250 crores, indicating capital efficiency to support planned capex.

risk_register.risk: Subsidiary start-up costs diluting consolidated margins
risk_register.note: Nine newly incorporated subsidiaries (first year of operation) incurred setup-related costs (employee cost, establishment expenses, overheads) temporarily impacting consolidated margins; seven audited African subsidiaries posted INR 13.5 crores losses in FY26, INR 6 crores in Q4; expected to be one-time/transitional and normalize as operations scale.
Consolidated EPS grew only ~6% versus more than 150% growth in previous three quarters, due to expenses/costs of setting up new subsidiary companies.

themes.label: Value-added product mix shift
themes.note: CBE contribution to revenue rose from 10% two years ago to 30% today, with stearin+CBE now 70-75% of business, driving margin expansion.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / debottlenecking
themes.note: Plant 2 capacity increased 30% to 32,500 tpa; further debottlenecking and a ~INR 460 crore multi-year capex program (backward and forward integration) targeted for FY28 commissioning.

themes.label: Margin guidance discipline
themes.note: Management reiterated sustainable EBITDA margin band of 25-27% and gross margin band of 45-50%, to be viewed on a yearly rather than quarterly basis.

themes.label: Working capital efficiency
themes.note: Working capital days improved to 125 in FY26 from 151 in FY25, with strong operating cash flow of ~INR 259-260 crores.

themes.label: Subsidiary start-up drag on consolidated numbers
themes.note: Nine newly formed international subsidiaries incurred first-year setup costs, contributing to African subsidiary losses of INR 13.5 crores in FY26 and only 6% consolidated EPS growth versus 150%+ in prior quarters; management calls this one-time/transitional.

themes.label: Backward/forward integration (Burkina Faso & CBA/refinery)
themes.note: Burkina Faso backward integration (~INR 120 crore) aims to cut logistics costs and improve yield; forward integration project (~INR 330-340 crore) targeted for >6x asset turn.

themes.label: Geopolitical/currency risk insulation
themes.note: Company reports minimal direct revenue exposure to conflict-affected geographies (Middle East only 2-3%) but recorded INR 23.3 crore cumulative FX mark-to-market provision in FY26.

key_takeaways: Manorama Industries has delivered an exceptional performance in FY 2026, reporting a strong year-on-year revenue growth of 76.1% with stand-alone revenues reaching INR 1,358 crores.
Our solvent fractionation plant 2 increased installed capacity by 30% from 25,000 tons per annum to 32,500 tons per annum as part of an overall debottlenecking initiative.

Through strategic capital expenditure commitment of approximately INR 460 crores over the next two to three years, this investment program spans setting up of a new solvent fractionation manufacturing facility, establishment of a new facility for cocoa butter alternatives, expansion of refining capabilities, and commissioning of raw material processing units in Burkina Faso, West Africa.
Working capital cycle improved to approximately 125 days in FY 26 compared to 151 days in FY '25.
Net cash flow from operating activities stood at INR 259 crores, ROCE of 33.6% and ROE of 40.3%.

EBITDA INR 367.7 crores with an EBITDA margin of 27.1%, reflecting focused product mix optimization and disciplined cost management. Profit after tax INR 233.2 crores, translating to a PAT margin of 17.2%.
We maintained a margin guidance of 25%-27%.
In the end, the consolidated EPS has grown by only 6% compared to almost more than 150% growth that we saw in the previous three quarters.
pressing_questions: Second, on the growth guidance, like, how should one look at it, top-line growth for next couple of years, given that the capacity additions which we are doing and margins you have already highlighted, if on top-line growth, if you can share some color?
What about, ma'am, FY '28? As I can understand, this entire capex will be commissioned together. From where we can expect the growth to come for FY '28?

Our gross margins have fallen from 48% to 43% on a consol basis quarter-on-quarter. Whereas, on a standalone basis, they have remained the same on a QOQ basis. Can you highlight why this difference is arising?

Sir, in the seven audited African subsidiaries, we posted INR 13.5 crores losses for FY 26, out of which almost INR 6 crores came in Q4 itself. Is this implying a loss run rate that has doubled in the final quarter? Is it the startup cost? Is it the Forex translation loss? Is it the operating losses in the trading P&L on these entities?
In the end, the consolidated EPS has grown by only 6% compared to almost more than 150% growth that we saw in the previous three quarters.

The other question that I had was about the INR 23.3 crores cumulative month-to-month hit on the forwards in FY '26. You have a 57% export revenue. What is the hedge ratio policy, and has it been recalibrated after this year's experience?

METROBRAND.about: The company is one of the largest Indian footwear & accessories specialty retailers and are among the aspirational Indian brands in the footwear category.Its a one-stop shop for of branded products for the entire family, including men, women, unisex, and children, and for every occasion, including casual and formal events.[1]

quarters.summary: Metro Brands guided to continued full-year FY'27 revenue growth of ~15% (give or take a couple of points), EBITDA margin around 30%, PAT margin in the 13%-15% range, and gross margins maintained in the 55%-57% guided band (actuals running near 60%); management flagged a Q2 slowdown from a later Diwali shifting sales into Q3, expects e-commerce to grow in a healthy 20%-30% range going forward, and expects FILA to see acceleration towards the end of FY'27 while Clarks EBO rollout begins Q3 FY'27 with a runway of 100-150 stores.

key_figures.label: Marketing spend impact on PAT delta
Walkway stores among last year's new stores

subsections.label: PAT margin drivers
points: PAT margins were impacted by 4 items: increase in investment in brand-building marketing; a modest increase in occupancy costs, primarily driven by new format additions and the number of new stores opened; lower treasury income against a high-performing number last year; and investment in talent and tech in the organization as the company continues to invest for the future.

Of the ~200 bps PAT delta, a significant portion (~100+ bps) came from increased marketing spend for brand-building at the top of the funnel, which takes time to filter down to the bottom of the funnel.
Lower treasury income also impacted PAT — treasury returns were in the teens last year and are not in the teens this year, consistent with market conditions.

New stores are dilutive to PAT — of 140 new stores opened last year (net 120 after 20 closures), all run at similar gross margins but not the same EBITDA/PAT margins; ~40 of the 140 were Walkway stores which carry a significantly lower PAT.

Management is confident of returning to 15%+ PAT growth once treasury normalizes, marketing spend normalizes (having overinvested last year), talent investments start to pay off, and new stores mature/perform better.

subsections.label: Margin guidance reaffirmed
points: Gross margins guided in the 55%-57% range; company is running above that and confident of maintaining the range.
EBITDA margin guided at ~30%, which management stated is what has always been guided to.
PAT guided at 13%-15% for the full year; company feels confident of being in that range by year end.

subsections.label: Minimum wage / cost inputs
points: Minimum wage hikes get implemented as soon as notification is out; increases are being heard of in a few states.

Currently, salary paid to front-end staff is generally above prevailing minimum wages in those states, providing some cushion, though the company wants compensation to remain in the top-notch retailer bracket over time.

Input cost inflation seen at normal inflationary levels of 3%-5%, with nothing yet coming from oil price fluctuations; mitigated via forward buying (buying 4-5 months out) and locking in production costs as costs started rising.
No unusual price hikes taken in the last quarter beyond normal inflationary price hikes on certain products from time to time.

subsections.label: Realization / ASP drivers
points: 6% YoY realization increase primarily driven by mix — newer, slightly premium format contribution to sales has improved, lifting ASP.
Q1 is a reasonably large quarter for Crocs, so ASP growth in Q1 tends to run higher than the full-year average; full-year ASP growth expected to be closer to 3%-4%.

key_figures.label: Sports vertical contribution target via Metro Mochi stores

subsections.label: April-May softness, June recovery
points: April and May were soft due to the overhang of the U.S.-Iran conflict and a shift in marriage dates linked to the Adhik Maas.
June recovered extremely well, delivering a mid-teen double-digit gain for the quarter overall.

Last year in June there were significant monsoons nationwide which helped the Crocs business tremendously; this year that boost was absent pre-monsoon, so Crocs underperformed pre-monsoon, but the rest of the business offset that to land within the normal ~15% net growth range.
As monsoons arrived later, the Crocs business has performed to plan; the shift was described as quarter-to-quarter timing, not an underlying issue with Crocs.

subsections.label: Wedding season and Diwali timing
points: Last year, wedding dates in April/May were significantly lower (recalled as effectively zero), causing a hit to that period, with demand rebounding in June this year.
Wedding season goods peaked in June as anticipated.

Diwali is shifting later this year versus last year; Diwali shopping season begins a few weeks before the festival, which previously spilled into Q2 last year but will not fall in Q2 this year — expected to shift some growth into Q3, though management does not expect a Q2 demand dampening.

Dispersion of wedding dates within a month matters: more dispersed dates allow more weddings and more spend; no significant concern seen for the current year's wedding date count, though clustering effects are watched.

subsections.label: Demand breadth and drivers
points: Demand was seen across multiple price points, multiple geographies (not concentrated in metro or Tier 3 cities specifically) and across all banners, not just one or two.

Conversion numbers are rising, indicating higher total bill values and traffic; new-customer counts entering stores are also tracked as a gauge of marketing efficacy, and both are trending positively.

Same-store-growth (SSG) drivers include: improving traffic via marketing initiatives; improving conversion rate via staff quality, service, store displays and product assortment; and increasing basket size via product adjacencies and ASP increases.
Three consecutive quarters of steady double-digit growth mark a stabilization versus the lumpy post-COVID growth pattern seen in the prior 6-8 quarters.
Estimated June growth came in at over 20% YoY.

subsections.label: Growth aspiration vs. discipline
points: Management does not view 20% growth as impossible but prefers measured growth over chasing an aggressive number and falling short, citing inventory and brand-share risk from over-forecasting.
Over the last 4 quarters, the company believes it has outperformed peers in growth.
2-year CAGR trend cited across recent quarters: 8%, 13%, 15%, and 12% this quarter.

key_figures.label: Healthy e-commerce growth range going forward
Premium mix a few years ago
Clarks women's MBO doors target by year end

subsections.label: E-commerce channel deconstruction
points: Digital business has 3 pillars: D2C website, marketplace/omni, and SOR (sale-or-return) 3P business.
D2C website grew almost 60% YoY and marketplace/omni business also grew 60% YoY; it was the SOR 3P business that pulled down the total e-commerce growth to 9%.
SOR business lumpiness stems from seasonal order cycles — a quarter may see products shipped out while a later quarter sees returns without corresponding new shipments, dampening reported growth.
A conscious decision was taken to reduce lower price points and discounts on the 3P business, which was a contributing (but not singular) factor pulling down SOR growth.

Management does not anticipate the SOR effect to be significant going forward and expects the e-commerce business to grow well into double digits on an ongoing basis, with a healthy range considered 20%-30% (much more or much less would signal something is off).
Company wants to continue lowering discounts on e-commerce but will manage this carefully so as not to lose new customers that e-commerce brings into the fold.
5-year CAGR for e-commerce has been 45%.

subsections.label: Clarks brand performance
points: Clarks women's line, launched late last calendar year, performed extremely well; expanded from 200 MBO doors at launch to 350 doors this spring, with a target of 700 doors by year-end.

Clarks is not cannibalistic — consumer data shows new consumers coming into the fold buying products they hadn't bought from Metro before; it does not cannibalize Metro, Da Vinchi, Mochi or J.Fontini brands.
Clarks men's collection launched early this year in under 100 doors and has surprisingly done well, also non-cannibalistic.
Clarks EBOs to begin opening from Q3 FY27; expected to scale faster than any brand except possibly Crocs 5 years ago.

Estimated runway for Clarks EBOs is 100-150 stores in the near-to-foreseeable future, growing further as Tier 2 cities develop into Tier 1 and aspirations rise; similar brands have roughly 200 stores in market today, of which management estimates only ~150 would be profitable.
Clarks' production has moved entirely to India catering specifically to Metro's markets, giving the supply chain nimbleness and boosting confidence in future investment.

subsections.label: MetroActiv and Walkway performance
points: MetroActiv: 3 stores opened; a couple performed well, one did not, partly impacted by BIS-related issues faced at Foot Locker; management plans to test a different expansion strategy before scaling further.

Walkway: grew from a base of ~70 stores by opening over 30 new stores (50% growth rate); many stores are performing well, some are not, but management understands the reasons and continues to iterate the format.
Walkway caters to a lower price point in the pyramid and is viewed as a long-term growth driver despite lower per-store productivity.

Walkway's reported margin will be structurally lower than Metro Mochi/Crocs, but success will be judged by achieving ROCEs of 25%-30% on a consistent basis over the medium-to-long term, versus current treasury yields of ~7%-8%.

subsections.label: FILA brand repositioning
points: 3 new brand-new FILA EBOs opened, geographically spread to read performance across different markets; 1 older EBO from the original acquisition was closed.
The new stores are performing well but need further stabilization; reviving a brand that had been on discount for 18-24 months is not easy.

Management sees itself on track to return FILA to a growth path, though slightly behind original schedule; a good pilot needs to run through a full season, with acceleration expected towards the end of FY27.

EOSS discounting on FILA inventory reflects a mix of leftover inventory acquired from the prior owner and normal in-season sports discounting; sports products have a 3-4 month lifecycle versus Metro Mochi's longer cycle, and brands must buy ~9 months ahead of lead times, resulting in routine EOSS discounting that is considered normal for the category.

subsections.label: Business vertical structure
points: Company operates 4 verticals: core business (Metro and Mochi); value vertical (Walkway and Shoe Depot); strategic brands (Crocs, Clarks, FitFlop); and the sports division.

New leadership appointments include a Chief Business Officer for the sports vertical and a President for the Metro Mochi business; the COO oversees value brands and strategic brands, aimed at giving dedicated focus and resourcing to each vertical's growth runway.

Sports business growth path is twofold: via the FILA brand and via the retail brands Foot Locker and MetroActiv; if the ~700 Metro Mochi stores can contribute 10%-15% of sales from sports, that would be a significant driver.
Estimated runway for FILA EBO, Foot Locker and MetroActiv combined is 300-500 stores over a 5-7 year horizon, described as a directional North Star rather than a forward-looking prediction.

subsections.label: Premiumization trend
points: The 3,000+ price segment now contributes ~57% of sales, up from the 40s a few years ago, with continued premiumization expected especially in Metro Mochi, Foot Locker, FILA, Clarks and FitFlop banners.
Walkway is the only banner that does not run in the higher price range; even Crocs tends to skew premium.
Company tracks volume growth closely to ensure price increases are not causing customer attrition or market share loss.
Premium mix typically normalizes in Q2 and Q4 after end-of-season sales, with Q1 and Q3 typically showing higher premium mix due to seasonal sale cycles.

subsections.label: Store network trajectory
points: Net 9 new store openings in the quarter (13 opened, 4 closed) is lower than most other quarters, but management does not view this as reflective of a change in the growth goal — market economics vary how stores open from quarter to quarter, and the pattern of ebb and flow (as seen with larger openings in some prior quarters) is expected to continue.

Company still expects to reach the usual triple-digit range of store openings for the full year; the challenge is not availability but ensuring the right stores are opened from a financial-discipline perspective, avoiding profit-losing stores.
Demand for retail space in India is described as far outstripping supply.

subsections.label: Distribution center
points: The new ~250,000 sq ft distribution center, launched in March, is now fully operational with all integrations complete.

subsections.label: Forward buying strategy
points: Company mitigates input cost spikes via forward buying and locking in production costs — buying is done 4-5 months out, giving runway to ease into price changes rather than facing overnight cost shocks.

Sports brands, including FILA, require placing orders ~9 months ahead of lead times, which is standard across all sports brands and results in inventory hedging that leads to routine seasonal discounting.

subsections.label: Capital allocation framework for brand investment
points: Key evaluation criteria for allocating capital to a brand: whether it is additive or dilutive/cannibalistic to the existing portfolio; how much capital allocation it merits versus other options, given all 9 banners have significant growth runways; and identifying unmet consumer needs/demand.
At a granular level, every deal/opportunity is evaluated for fit with the specific banner and the company overall.

Management believes it currently has the right banners, capital and leadership to drive growth, covering almost every footwear need for Indian consumers, and intends to grow with financial discipline rather than expand banners for its own sake.

subsections.label: Marketing spend strategy
points: Increased marketing investment (~100+ bps impact on PAT) reflects top-of-funnel brand-building spend, which takes time to filter to the bottom of the funnel.
Launching new brands (Clarks, Foot Locker, FILA) requires significantly higher front-end marketing spend, similar to D2C start-ups; spend intensity reduces once a brand gains velocity.

Marketing as % of sales is not expected to keep rising above last year's elevated level, since spend was already stepped up starting last year and will also be diluted as sales grow; historical marketing spend range was 2.5%-3% of sales.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth stance
points: Highlighting new brands/adjacent categories as an inorganic opportunity was part of an original IPO-era deck and has not been actively pursued recently.

Management feels it currently has an adequate number of banners to serve various consumer occasions in India but remains open to exploring new brands if consumer demand emerges for something not currently served.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical overhang
points: U.S.-Iran conflict created a consumer sentiment distraction (not described as a direct business impact) during April-May, contributing to softness in that period.
Shift in marriage dates linked to Adhik Maas contributed to April-May softness.

subsections.label: BIS regulatory disruption
points: There is erraticness in whether footwear import factories get BIS approval or renewal, with very little advance notice, creating operational uncertainty ('duck and weave') especially for high-end athletic product.
Renewals for ASEAN country factories are reportedly not coming through, which management said has more impact than the general QC order changes allowing imports.
A recent BIS QC order change allowing import of goods was said to have no significant plus or minus impact on the company.
MetroActiv and Foot Locker stores were impacted to a degree by BIS-related issues, though these issues are being mitigated slowly.

Footwear imports into India, which had been declining for the last 3 years, have started to show growth this year, alongside improvement in approved BIS licenses over the last year — noted as an external observation, though management maintains they are not yet fully out of the woods on high-end athletic product.

subsections.label: Input cost / wage inflation
points: Potential input cost spikes were identified but mitigated through forward buying and cost locking.
Normal inflationary pricing observed at 3%-5%, with no impact yet from oil price fluctuations.
Minimum wage hikes in certain states could affect costs if implemented, though current pay levels are generally above prevailing minimums, providing cushion for now.

subsections.label: Treasury income normalization
points: Treasury income was lower this year versus a high-performing base last year (returns in the teens last year, now around 7%-8%), impacting PAT margin.

subsections.label: Full-year outlook
points: Company continues to guide to a 15% PAT-linked growth for the full year, alongside gross margin of 55%-57%, EBITDA margin of ~30%, and PAT margin of 13%-15%.
Q2 may see some growth impact from the later Diwali shifting shopping season demand into Q3, but no Q2 demand dampening is expected overall; growth is expected to be made up in Q3 and beyond.
Management reiterated that despite a good case for higher growth (e.g., 20%), it prefers measured targets given inventory and brand-share risk of over-forecasting.

Expect PAT growth to return to a mid-teen to high-teen percentage range as treasury income normalizes, marketing spend normalizes (having been elevated in the prior year), talent investments start to pay off, and new stores mature.
Clarks EBOs expected to open starting Q3 FY27, scaling faster than any brand except possibly Crocs, with a store runway estimated at 100-150 in the near-to-foreseeable future.
FILA expected to see acceleration toward the end of FY27 as the pilot stores complete a full season and repositioning progresses.
E-commerce expected to continue growing well into double digits, with a healthy sustainable range considered 20%-30%.
Full-year store openings expected to reach the usual triple-digit range despite a low net addition in Q1.
Full-year revenue growth guidance is ~15% (+/- a couple of points).

guidance_ledger.statement: We guide to 15% for the year, give or take a couple of points left or right of that
We have guided gross margins in that range of around 55% to 57%; we are above that and confident of maintaining that range
EBITDA in that 30-ish range
We have guided for somewhere close to 13% to 15%; we feel confident that by the end of the year, we should be around that range
Expect PAT growth to return to mid-teen to high-teen percentage range once treasury normalizes, marketing normalizes, talent investment pays off and new stores mature
A very good 20% to 30% growth in e-commerce would be considered healthy for our business

I don't see any reason why we shouldn't be able to get to the usual triple digit of store openings

Expect FILA to become meaningful to overall numbers in the next 18 months as repositioning progresses

Company will be doing an SAP upgrade later on this year

risk_register.risk: Gulf crisis impact on raw material and input costs
risk_register.note: Company is closely monitoring the Gulf crisis for potential impact on raw materials and other input costs, though it believes it can mitigate most of it for the near term.
Management remains aware that geopolitical issues could cause disruptions and plans to stay agile to maximize sales and profitability.

risk_register.risk: BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) import compliance issues
risk_register.note: BIS challenges remain unresolved for Foot Locker and MetroActiv (heavily import-dependent); licensing renewal outcomes are erratic across brands, creating unpredictable timeline for normalization; Clarks less affected due to local production.
Footwear remains a discretionary purchase that can be deferred, though management believes premium customer base is less elastic to inflation than middle-class consumers.
Rental market competition has stabilized somewhat compared to the previous hyper-competitive acceleration phase, though it has not returned to earlier favorable levels.

risk_register.risk: Leadership/talent gaps from growth and attrition
risk_register.note: Management expects ongoing gaps in leadership team to emerge due to growth and attrition, even though current team is considered strong.

themes.label: Demand recovery
themes.note: April-May softness from geopolitical distraction and wedding date shift gave way to strong June rebound and steady double-digit growth

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Normal inflationary pricing of 3%-5% seen, mitigated via forward buying; no oil-driven impact yet, gross margin maintained near 60%

themes.label: BIS import compliance
themes.note: Erratic factory approvals/renewals, especially for ASEAN sourcing, continue to disrupt MetroActiv and Foot Locker operations

themes.label: Store network expansion
themes.note: Only net 9 stores added in Q1 versus prior quarters' pace, but full-year triple-digit openings still guided; Walkway grew 50% and FILA/Clarks/MetroActiv formats continue rollout

themes.label: Digital commerce growth
themes.note: D2C and marketplace/omni grew ~60% each, but SOR 3P lumpiness and discount reduction pulled total e-commerce growth down to 9%; healthy range guided at 20%-30% going forward

themes.label: Premium customer insulation from inflation
themes.note: 3,000+ price segment now ~57% of sales, up from 40s a few years ago, with premiumization continuing across Metro Mochi, Foot Locker, FILA, Clarks and FitFlop

themes.label: Leadership and technology investment
themes.note: New CBO for sports and President for Metro Mochi appointed to drive vertical focus; investment in talent, tech and marketing weighed on PAT margin this quarter but expected to normalize

key_takeaways: In Q1 FY '27, we posted a 14% growth in our stand-alone business, along with a 9% growth in EBITDA, leading to a 13% PAT.

April and May were soft due to the overhang of the U.S.-Iran conflict and also a shift in marriage dates linked to the Adhik Maas. However, we were very pleased to see June recover extremely well for us to post a mid-teen double-digit gain for the quarter.
Our D2C website grew at almost 60% compared to last year. Our marketplace omni business also grew by 60%. It was the SOR 3P business that pulled down the numbers to a 9% growth.
We opened 13 new stores and closed 4 stores for a net of 9 stores... it is in no way reflective of our goal of continuing our growth.
Our gross margins... continue to match our highest gross margin for the past 5 quarters, coming in at almost 60%.
EBITDA margins continue to remain at 30%, which is what we've always guided to.

PAT margins were impacted by 4 items: our increase in investment in brand-building marketing; a modest increase in occupancy costs, primarily driven by new format additions and the number of new stores we opened; lower treasury income against a high-performing number last year; and last, but most importantly, our investment in talent and tech in the organization as we continue to invest for the future.
Our new distribution center of roughly 250,000 square feet, which launched in March, is now fully operational with all integrations complete.
We continue to guide to a 15% PAT for the full year.
pressing_questions: So then in this sports category, how are you looking at in totality where we should be in the next 3 to 5 years versus today in terms of maybe number of stores or revenue, or some color on growth that you could share with us in this category as you've been trying to build up this category?

Just one point, if I can ask more. Let's say, in terms of footfalls versus conversion, this metric, let's say, 2 quarters back versus now, if you can, let's say, probably maybe qualitatively give us some idea on these 2 variables, how are they now versus, let's say, 2 quarters, 4 quarters back?
Given the entire context of how demand is going across, how is the outlook looking like for FY '27?... shouldn't like 20% growth be like the baseline?
Any time line for this pilot and strategy going forward, like second half of FY '27 should see meaningful acceleration here on FILA?

quarters.summary: Metro Brands closed Q4 FY26 with 20% standalone revenue growth, 20% EBITDA growth and 18% PAT growth, with digital commerce growing 53% and holding a 12% share of quarterly revenue; management expects to sustain ~15%+ annual growth over the long term while monitoring Gulf-crisis-led input cost inflation (~10%) and BIS-related import issues affecting Foot Locker/MetroActiv expansion, with FILA expected to turn meaningful to numbers in the next ~18 months.

key_figures.label: Eastern India revenue share (per store, YoY)
Digital commerce business share of total revenues

subsections.label: Q4 FY26 performance drivers
points: 20% growth in standalone business along with 20% growth in EBITDA leading to a PAT growth of 18%.
Digital commerce business grew 53% and holds a 12% share of total revenues for the quarter.
Metrics delivered within guidance range for the year: PAT in the mid-teen percentage range, EBITDA in the high 20s to low 30s, and sales growth of 15%, despite a slow start to the fiscal year.

subsections.label: Pre-IndAS metrics
points: Pre-IndAS EBITDA margin for the full year was around 21%.
Pre-IndAS PAT margin for the full year was 15.5%.

subsections.label: Eastern India rounding clarification
points: Apparent 10% YoY decline in Eastern India per-store revenue is attributed largely to number of stores and rounding effects (e.g., 14.51% rounds to 15% while 14.49% rounds to 14%), not an actual decline.
Eastern part of the business has historically been in the 13% to 15% range; last quarter and full year it was 14%.

subsections.label: Footfall and SSG trends
points: Footfall growth is being seen in Metro Mochi stores, along with growth in basket size of goods purchased.

Square footage per store maintained at 4,500 compared to last quarter, indicating growth is not solely coming from new stores (new stores are typically less productive than existing stores initially).
A portion of revenue increases comes from new stores and from annualization of stores opened in previous years, but same-store growth (SSG) is stated to be the primary driver.
Company believes it is gaining market share based on comparison with market performance in previous quarters.

In-store footfalls are growing, measured partly via number of bills; CRM database shows new customers entering stores in the back half of the year, with steady improvement in business tracked from Q1 through Q4, driven by ability to acquire new customers and win back/repurchase existing customers.

subsections.label: Demand outlook and elasticity
points: Management is confident of continuing to grow the business in the (+15%) range year-on-year over the long term, while acknowledging hiccups and quarter-to-quarter variability (e.g., wedding dates) will occur.

Footwear purchase is viewed as discretionary but not a frequent or big-ticket purchase, and the premium customer base is seen as less elastic to inflation than middle-class consumers, whose spending is affected more directly by inflation.

Value-segment (Walkway) customers are under-penetrated relative to the unorganized footwear market (overall unorganized footwear share ~70%), giving significant growth opportunity from unorganized-to-organized shift.
No single significant driver (e.g., wedding dates) was identified for the sequential demand improvement; marketing initiatives cited as driving new footfall.

subsections.label: Men's vs Unisex mix
points: Increase in men's category contribution is offset by an equivalent decrease in unisex category, driven by reclassification from certain third-party brands (e.g., Walkway and Clarks related movements); no substantive underlying trend to read into it.

subsections.label: Growth strategy across banners
points: Each banner (Foot Locker, Clarks, Metro Mochi, etc.) has significant opportunity to grow in absolute store/numerical quantum over the next few years, though percentage growth rates will differ significantly given differing base sizes (e.g., Clarks starts from zero stores so percentage growth is 'infinite' on a math basis, while Metro Mochi's percentage growth appears smaller due to a larger existing base).
Company is well capitalized with tools and willingness to open stores across brands; the constraint is finding the right locations in the right markets for the right banner, not capital.

subsections.label: Walkway format
points: Walkway has strong penetration potential given more Tier-3/Tier-4 towns than Tier-1 towns in India, and unorganized sector dominance (potentially ~85% of business in these tiers vs overall market average of ~70% unorganized) provides significant headroom for organized growth.

Company has yet to fully crack the format mechanics across Tier-2 town streets, Tier-4 street stores, small shopping centers, high streets, and high-density markets — considered an evolving formula, not a completed pilot.
Profitability and model of Walkway are starting to make a lot more sense, especially in terms of ROCE.

subsections.label: Distribution center expansion
points: A new DC opened in March 2026 increases storage capacity by 200,000 square feet, ensuring capacity to cater to growth.

subsections.label: FILA local manufacturing
points: FILA repositioning is underway with local manufacturing; company has spent significant time and money cleaning up old inventory and is building the brand for the long term rather than seeking a quick sale.

key_figures.label: Aggregated store opening opportunity (Fila, Foot Locker, Clarks, MetroActiv)

subsections.label: Store network milestones
points: Crossed the 1,000-store mark last quarter by opening a net of 42 stores, ending the quarter with a total of 1,032 stores.
Opened the first two FILA stores since the acquisition.

Opportunity exists to open an aggregated ~50 stores across Fila, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv, subject to finding the right locations, rentals, timing, and mitigating BIS-related import issues (especially for Foot Locker and MetroActiv, which are heavily dependent on imported products).

subsections.label: Rental/real estate market
points: Real estate rental competition has stabilized somewhat compared to the previous hyper-competitive acceleration phase, though the market has not returned to previously favorable conditions; a strong BD team is working to find the right locations.

subsections.label: Input cost mitigation strategy
points: Company is forward-buying raw materials in bulk to avoid significant price hikes.
Overall input cost inflation observed is around 10%, with certain categories spiking more than others.

Company holds more than six months' worth of inventory and has additional order space beyond that period which is price-protected, allowing a more gradual absorption of cost increases rather than sharp spikes.
Slightly higher inventory levels reflect some front-loading done in anticipation of price rises expected to gradually come through.
No immediate/knee-jerk pricing action planned in the near term; inflation impact expected to be 'nothing more than normal inflation' (~10%).

subsections.label: BIS import compliance
points: BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) issues affect brands to varying degrees depending on import dependency; Foot Locker and MetroActiv are heavily impacted due to reliance on imported products, whereas Clarks is less affected as production has moved to India.
BIS licensing situation is described as erratic — sometimes licenses are renewed, sometimes not — making it difficult to predict when supply chain challenges will normalize.
The import-dependent portion of a brand's portfolio (estimated ~15% in an illustrative example) can be highly profit-accretive, so missing that portion could disproportionately impact profit.

key_figures.label: Unorganized share in value segment (illustrative, Tier-2 to Tier-4)

subsections.label: E-commerce and omnichannel growth
points: E-commerce should be viewed as a percentage of total business rather than as a standalone growth number, since both are growing together.

E-commerce is expected to represent somewhere between 12% to 15% of business in the near term, potentially growing further; e-commerce growth can be lumpy depending on festive season timing and online brand sales activity.

subsections.label: Consumer sentiment and premium positioning
points: Strong quarterly performance attributed to a combination of company-specific initiatives (product launches, marketing, technology/CRM investment) and market share gains from unorganized players, alongside relative insulation of the premium customer base from inflation given footwear is not a frequent or big-ticket purchase.
Premium customers experience a delayed effect from inflation compared to middle-class consumers, whose basic basket of goods is hit harder and faster.

Value-segment (Walkway) customer base offers large headroom given the segment's severe under-penetration relative to the unorganized value footwear market and the aspiration of customers for better organized shopping environments.

subsections.label: Leadership and organizational investment
points: Three significant senior hires in the last 12 months: a new Chief Technology Officer, a new Chief Marketing Officer, and, most recently, a new Chief Product Officer — all bringing deep domain, scale, and complexity experience.

Chief Product Officer role in its current form is new; Chief Marketing Officer role is new (position vacant for a couple of years); Chief Technology Officer is a replacement with a slightly differentiated remit.
A Chief Digital Insights Officer was hired in the previous fiscal year, enabling the company to take advantage of AI initiatives.
Management expects ongoing leadership gaps to emerge due to growth and attrition, but currently feels the senior leadership team is strong ('terrific team in place').

subsections.label: Technology upgrades
points: Company completed an evaluation of store POS systems and is moving to a more robust POS system, with the tech upgrade starting in June and expected to be rolled out by the end of the year.
In-house development of AI agents to manage agentic workflows within the organization at high efficiency.
Continued investment in giving employees access to different AI tools/sites suited to varying functional needs.
An SAP upgrade is planned later in the year.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and input cost risk
points: Company is closely monitoring the Gulf crisis for its potential impact on raw materials and other input costs, though it believes it can mitigate most of it for the near term.
General awareness that geopolitical issues could cause disruptions; company plans to stay agile to maximize sales and profitability under such conditions.

subsections.label: BIS/import compliance risk
points: BIS-related import compliance issues remain unresolved and unpredictable, impacting expansion plans particularly for Foot Locker and MetroActiv, which are heavily dependent on imported products.
Licensing renewal outcomes are erratic across brands, creating uncertainty on timeline for normalization.

subsections.label: Real estate/rental competition
points: Rental market competition for retail space remains elevated versus historical norms, though the sharp acceleration seen previously has stabilized somewhat.

subsections.label: FY26 delivery vs guidance
points: Despite a slow start to the fiscal year, the company delivered metrics within its guidance range: PAT in the mid-teen percentage range, EBITDA in the high 20s to low 30s, and sales growth of 15%.

subsections.label: Forward growth outlook
points: Management reiterated medium-term guidance towards 15% to 18% growth, with capital and willingness available to expand across banners (Foot Locker, Clarks, Metro Mochi, FILA, MetroActiv) as opportunities arise.
Long-term confidence in sustaining (+15%) year-on-year growth, while acknowledging quarter-to-quarter variability from factors like wedding dates and other one-off effects.

Store expansion guidance described qualitatively as opening 'as many good ones as we can find,' with an aggregated opportunity of ~50 stores across Fila, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv, subject to location, rental, timing and BIS-related conditions.
FILA expected to become meaningful to overall numbers in the next ~18 months as repositioning and local manufacturing build-out progress.

themes.label: Demand recovery
themes.note: Steady improvement in SSG and footfalls tracked from Q1 through Q4, driven by new customer acquisition and repurchase, with confidence in sustaining (+15%) long-term growth.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Input costs up ~10% amid Gulf crisis, mitigated via forward buying and six-plus months of price-protected inventory; no immediate price hikes planned.

themes.label: BIS import compliance
themes.note: Unresolved and unpredictable BIS licensing issues continue to constrain expansion of import-dependent brands like Foot Locker and MetroActiv.

themes.label: Store network expansion
themes.note: Crossed 1,000-store mark with net 42 store additions in Q4 FY26; ~50-store aggregated opportunity across Fila, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv for FY27.

themes.label: Digital commerce growth
themes.note: E-commerce grew 53% in Q4 FY26 and is expected to hold a 12%-15% share of total business in the near term.

themes.label: Premium customer insulation from inflation
themes.note: Premium customer base viewed as less elastic to inflation than middle-class consumers, though footwear remains a discretionary and deferrable purchase.

themes.label: Leadership and technology investment
themes.note: New CTO, CMO and CPO hires plus POS system upgrade, in-house AI agent development, and planned SAP upgrade underpin growth capability.

key_takeaways: In Q4 FY26, we posted a 20% growth in our standalone business along with a 20% growth in EBITDA leading to a PAT of 18%.
We continue to see consistent growth from our multiple E-Com channels in our digital commerce business as it grew 53% and holds a 12% share of our total revenues for that quarter.

We crossed the 1,000-store mark last quarter by opening a net of 42 stores and ended the quarter with a total of 1,032 stores. In those openings, we also had our first two FILA stores that we opened since the acquisition.

As we look to the future, we are closely monitoring the Gulf crisis to see the impact that it could potentially have on our raw materials and other input costs, though we believe we can mitigate most of it for the near term.
In March of 2026, we also opened a new DC that increases our storage capacity by 200,000 square feet, ensuring that we have the capacity to cater for our growth.

I am very pleased to see and proud of the team that, at the end, delivered metrics in our guidance range, which has been PAT in the mid-teen percentage range, EBITDA in the high 20s to low 30s, and of course, a sales growth of 15%.

Overall, if it does impact us, in those items that it impacts us, I think we have seen overall input costs of 10%, maybe, so it's not significant in spike, though there are certain categories that spike a little bit more than the others.
When we look to the future, we are pretty confident that on a long-term basis we can continue to grow our business in that (+15%) range year on year, as we have done and shown over periods of time.
pressing_questions: How much input cost inflation is the company facing, and is it looking at price hikes given six months of inventory and forward procurement locking in higher prices?
How has demand historically panned out during high inflation periods, given footwear is a discretionary purchase that can be deferred?
In-store sales have shown single-digit growth over the last three years — how much of top-line growth is from new store additions versus SSG, specifically for Metro Mochi/core network?
Given the medium-term 15%-18% growth guidance and multiple brands, how is growth segregated between core brands versus new-age brands, and what quantum of growth is expected from each cohort?
What is the current pipeline for Fila, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv store additions in FY27?
Is the BIS issue present in Clarks as well as Foot Locker/MetroActiv?
Can you highlight the pre-IndAS EBITDA and PAT margins for the full year?

How should e-commerce and omnichannel sales be viewed for the upcoming year, and when will Foot Locker's BIS-related supply chain challenges normalize, and when will FILA's repositioning meaningfully contribute to growth and profitability?

Is the strong performance driven by the company's own efforts (expansion, branding, servicing) or a genuine uptick in consumer sentiment, especially given white-collar job stress in the customer's demographic?
Are we out of the hyper-competitive rental market cycle, and what is the guidance on store expansion run-rate going forward?

CENTUM.about: Founded in 1993, Centum Electronics Limited is one of the largest Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) companies in India. It offers entire spectrum of design services and manufacturing of systems, subsystems for mission critical products in Defence, Space, Aerospace, Industrial, Transportation and Medical sectors.[1]

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was described as muted relative to full-year expectations for both growth and margins, driven by quarterly variation in project execution and revenue phasing, particularly in BTS. Management reiterated confidence in stronger execution in subsequent quarters enabling full-year growth objectives, and urged evaluation on a full-year basis given the lumpy, milestone-driven nature of defense/space execution. The quarter also saw completion of the overseas restructuring/exit, a large one-time deconsolidation gain, a strong order book (~INR 1,800 cr, +31% YoY) and order inflow inflection (+70% YoY; BTS +150% YoY), continued EMS scaling (especially semiconductor equipment, expected to double/triple over two years), and reiterated FY27 growth (~25%) and margin (aiming above 13%) guidance.

key_figures.label: One-time profit on deconsolidation of overseas subsidiaries

subsections.label: Performance framing
points: Management characterized Q1 as 'somewhat muted compared with our expectations for the full year, both in terms of growth and margins,' attributing this to quarterly variation in project execution and revenue phasing, particularly in the BTS business.
Despite the softer quarter, the company reiterated confidence that stronger execution expected in subsequent quarters will enable delivery against full-year growth objectives.
Management again urged investors to view performance on a full-year basis given the lumpy, milestone-driven nature of defense/space execution.

subsections.label: Margin driver (standalone)
points: Margins during the quarter were impacted by relatively lower contribution from the BTS business.
Mix improvement expected as execution on key BTS programs accelerates over the coming quarters.

subsections.label: Consolidated PAT composition
points: Reported PAT of INR 106 cr was inflated by a one-time profit on deconsolidation of overseas subsidiaries of INR 94 cr, versus continuing-ops PAT of INR 11 cr.

subsections.label: Order book and visibility
points: Standalone order book of ~INR 1,800 cr (+31% YoY) described by management as strong visibility for future growth.
BTS order inflow of INR 130 cr (+150% YoY) highlighted as the key driver of the overall inflow acceleration.

Management response to revenue conversion concerns: to the question on whether the larger order book should drive BTS revenue recognition, management said 'the simple answer is yes,' while reiterating quarterly lumpiness.

subsections.label: Working capital signal
points: Advances of ~INR 210 cr, with CFO stating two-thirds is coming from BTS, consistent with milestone/advance-heavy contracting.

key_figures.label: Complex test system order (non-recurring engineering/test systems)

subsections.label: BTS (defense/space/radar/EW/nav) — execution phasing, acceleration expected
points: Q1 revenue softness tied to BTS execution schedules, but management expects continued strong order intake through the year particularly in Space, Radar, Electronic warfare, and Air navigation.

subsections.label: Space opportunity & SBS program
points: Management described space as 'quite an exciting' multi-year domain, noting Centrum's ~25-year heritage and progression from doing niche components to modules to subsystems to now building complete payloads, with intent to go further into satellite integration.
On space-based surveillance (SBS): 'moving well,' with the company having started to book some good orders and expecting a very strong order intake from SBS within FY27.
Also referenced executing a major program for payloads or electronic warfare-based payloads aligned with SBS, expected to have repeat requirements after delivery.

subsections.label: BTS program updates (development stage → prototype → production optionality)
points: Virupaksha and UHM both framed as development programs.
UHM: completed the first phase of design reviews, now in realization of the first prototypes, with prototypes expected in the next year, then awaiting HAL for serial production quantities.
Virupaksha: in design; expects development order completion around Q4 or Q1 (next year boundary).

GRSE / 'Takan system' (technology partnership + localization engineering): first deliveries expected beginning of next year, and the company is awaiting further orders in the coming one or two quarters.
Competitive positioning proof-point: on UHM, management cited more than 10 bidders, only three shortlisted, and Centrum was L1 (but refused to name others).

subsections.label: EMS growth and demand lanes
points: Vertical demand visibility across Semiconductor equipment (major ramp), Industrial automation, and Electrification & grid automation.

subsections.label: Semiconductor equipment: customer status, growth trajectory, margins
points: Definition: manufacturing box builds and PCBAs that go into equipment used in semiconductor fabrication processes like photolithography or etching.
Customer profile: a global OEM, one of these key global OEMs (not named), with Centrum ramping new part numbers and products.
Outlook: expected to double or triple in the next two years; also described as reaching '25 to 30' (unit unclear in transcript) over 1-2 years, directionally communicated as strong, steep growth.
Qualification/production maturity: products are in production, qualification behind them, now in serial production, while additional part numbers continue through qualification gates.
Competitive landscape: Centrum is the first major supplier in India, with primary competition located in Southeast Asia (Malaysia), not domestic.

Commercial/margin model: EMS margin benchmark 10-11%, typically a cost plus model; management clarified it did not claim higher semiconductor margins — the margin upside discussion relates to design-led manufacturing, not EMS build-to-print.

subsections.label: Electrification/grid automation: localization + NPI pipeline
points: Received a strategic partner award from a leading global industrial and energy conglomerate, presented as validation of execution and relationship strength.

Strategy: serve global customers implementing localization strategies in India while meeting global demand for advanced electronics; Centrum aims to leverage engineering capabilities, manufacturing scale, and high reliability expertise.
Multiple products in NPI (new product introduction) for electrification/grid automation; expected to contribute meaningfully over the next two years.

subsections.label: Non-recurring engineering/test systems
points: Certain engineering/test systems (e.g., 'complex test system' order ~INR 55 cr) are described as non-recurring/volatile — not always a recurring type of revenue, coming up from time to time; management downplayed long-term materiality.

key_figures.label: Bangalore aerospace park facility capex estimate

subsections.label: Capex / capacity expansion: Bangalore aerospace park facility
points: Facility at KIADB Aerospace Park, Bangalore: design stage complete; construction to start soon.
Land owned by another group company; 'we don't have to invest anything... this year.'
Capex likely begins end of next fiscal when shell is ready and spending starts on MEP/HVAC, clean rooms, plant & machinery.
High-level estimate: INR 50-70 cr, subject to next-year budgeting.

key_figures.label: Historical BTS vs EMS revenue mix
UHM development phase completion - prototypes expected timeline

subsections.label: Overseas exit essentially completed (capital allocation reset)
points: The quarter marked successful completion of the restructuring and exit from overseas subsidiaries, explicitly to sharpen focus on the India platform and enable more disciplined capital allocation.
French court approved the transfer of substantially all operating business and employees of Centrum TNS Group SA and certain subsidiaries to bidders MBDA and SII.
Entities ceased operating and were deconsolidated effective 4 June 2026.
Process converted to liquidation judiciaire with a judicial liquidator appointed 2 July 2026 for wind-down.
Management stated that with operating assets transferred and restructuring substantially completed, no further liabilities are expected in relation to these subsidiaries.
Strategic implication: frees bandwidth and resources towards the standalone business and enables greater transparency into continuing operations.

subsections.label: Design-led manufacturing (DLM) as margin lever
points: With overseas engineering-services purpose now obsolete, management is repurposing and integrating engineering with EMS to offer end-to-end solutions or design-led manufacturing solutions.
Stated benefit: should support improved margin profiles.
Management expects first DLM program wins in the coming quarters.
Strategic pivot to design-led manufacturing is being called out as the primary margin-expansion pathway.

subsections.label: Direct engagement with armed forces (channel broadening)
points: While many contracts route via PSUs (HAL/GRSE) and agencies (DRDO/ISRO), management stated they are increasing end-user linkage and are answering RFIs with the armed forces directly for 'full system kind of opportunities,' but will update only once mature.

key_figures.label: French court approved transfer effective date - entities ceased operating/deconsolidated

subsections.label: Quarterly lumpiness and margin volatility
points: Quarterly lumpiness and margin volatility driven by BTS execution phasing was the central near-term issue; Q1 is positioned as a timing/mix quarter rather than demand deterioration.

subsections.label: Non-recurring revenue items
points: Certain engineering/test systems (e.g., complex test system order ~INR 55 cr) are non-recurring/volatile and not always a recurring type of revenue.

subsections.label: Overseas restructuring risk de-risked
points: With operating assets transferred and restructuring substantially completed, management does not expect any further liabilities in relation to the overseas subsidiaries.

key_figures.label: GRSE Takan system - awaiting further orders timeline

subsections.label: Growth and margin guidance
points: Growth guidance: maintained ~25% revenue growth for FY27 and visibility for next year also at similar trajectory.
Margin guidance: last year about 12.5%; aiming to move it up and above about 13%, with next-year margin stable or slightly improve (but 'too early').

subsections.label: Mix outlook and KPIs to watch
points: Export mix expected to remain around 50 to 55% or even maybe higher, influenced by EMS growth; no major mix shift otherwise expected.
BTS vs EMS revenue split: management expects both to grow; BTS could be marginally favorable versus the historical ~70/30 mix, but not hugely drastically different.
Working capital signal: advances (~INR 210 cr) largely BTS-linked (two-thirds), indicating continued milestone/advance contracting.

subsections.label: Newsworthy takeaways (investor-relevant)
points: Overseas exit de-risked with explicit statement of no further liabilities expected, plus INR 94 cr one-time deconsolidation profit.
Order inflow inflection (Q1 inflow +70% YoY; BTS inflow +150% YoY) with large INR 1,800 cr order book.

Semiconductor equipment EMS has moved from qualification to serial production, with management calling it highly recurring (subject to broader capex cycles) and guiding for doubling/tripling over two years.
Strategic pivot to design-led manufacturing as the primary margin-expansion pathway, with first DLM program wins anticipated in coming quarters.
SBS and EW payload pipelines called out for FY27 order intake strength and potential repeat demand.

themes.label: Design-led manufacturing shift
themes.note: Repurposed overseas engineering capability now integrated with EMS to pursue design-led manufacturing as primary margin lever, with first program wins expected in coming quarters.

key_takeaways: Overseas exit de-risked with explicit statement of no further liabilities expected, plus INR 94 cr one-time deconsolidation profit.
Order inflow inflection (Q1 inflow +70% YoY; BTS inflow +150% YoY) with large INR 1,800 cr order book.

Semiconductor equipment EMS has moved from qualification to serial production, with management calling it highly recurring (subject to broader capex cycles) and guiding for doubling/tripling over two years.
Strategic pivot to design-led manufacturing as the primary margin-expansion pathway, with 'first DLM program wins' anticipated in coming quarters.
SBS and EW payload pipelines called out for FY27 order intake strength and potential repeat demand.
pressing_questions: Whether the larger order book should drive BTS revenue recognition — management said 'the simple answer is yes,' while reiterating quarterly lumpiness.
On UHM competitive positioning, management was asked to name the other bidders but refused, only confirming more than 10 bidders, three shortlisted, and Centrum as L1.

quarters.summary: Centum Electronics closed FY26 with strong standalone growth (~25% YoY revenue) across BTS and EMS, a healthy standalone order book (~INR 1,645 crores, +23% YoY), and improved balance sheet metrics, even as consolidated margins came in slightly below the guided 13-15% range due to EMS product mix. Management is completing decisive restructuring of underperforming overseas subsidiaries (Canada wind-up; French subsidiary in court-supervised sale expected to conclude by July 2026) and expects the core standalone/ESDM business to sustain 25-30% medium-term revenue growth and 13-15% EBITDA margin over the next 1-2 years.

subsections.label: Margin shortfall vs guidance
points: Full-year standalone EBITDA margin of ~12.5% came in below the guided 14-15% range because of the product mix in the EMS business; management had anticipated a slightly better product mix last year, and this will be executed in the current financial year, which should yield better EMS margins going forward.

subsections.label: Discontinued operations accounting treatment
points: Net losses of overseas subsidiaries in Canada and Europe have been reported under discontinued operations; Canada results were moved under discontinued operations in Q3 FY26 itself, and European subsidiary results are now reported under discontinued operations in Q4 following commencement of court-supervised restructuring in France.
Previously reported period numbers have been restated to reflect this classification.
Balance sheet items relating to the subsidiaries have been classified as 'assets held for sale' and 'liabilities directly associated with assets held for sale.'

Goodwill and intangible assets (including capitalized R&D) that were impaired and reported under exceptional items in Q3 FY26 in the consolidated statements have been reclassified under discontinued operations.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital efficiency
points: Debt to equity maintained at a comfortable level.
Adjusted net working capital days improved, driven by better working capital management.
Adjusted ROCE improved significantly, reflecting stronger profitability and improved capital efficiency.

subsections.label: Tax implications of losses
points: Losses incurred in the subsidiaries with associated tax credits would only accrue benefit if someone acquires the loss-holding entity, which management does not expect to happen.

Of the standalone exceptional items (~INR 200 crores), the investment-related impairment of INR 153 crores is a capital loss available for future capital gains set-off; other items have been used to offset profits made during the current year.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 discontinued-operations outlook
points: Management does not have a precise forecast for Q1 FY27 losses from discontinued operations since it is uncertain which business segment/court outcome will occur in June, and whether control will be lost triggering deconsolidation.
There is a high possibility of losing control due to the court process, which could mean not consolidating the European subsidiary in Q1 if the triggering event occurs in June.
No cash has flowed from the standalone/parent entity to the subsidiaries for several quarters; the subsidiary is expected to be fully deconsolidated by Q1, or worst case Q2 FY27.

Management stated the loss should not be in the same range as Q4 (which included several one-time items from Canada and other items); consolidated numbers going forward 'don't really mean much from a P&L standpoint' and focus should be on standalone performance.
On the balance sheet, liabilities held for disposal are significantly higher than assets held for disposal for the subsidiaries being divested.
