subsections.label: ROW (Right of Way) challenges
points: Two types of ROW issues: (1) permissions such as forest clearance or wildlife sanctuary clearance, for which the company has structured a clear process and knows expected timelines; (2) ROW from general public/landowners (farmers, individuals), where despite compensation orders as per government policy, some individuals or groups still create obstruction.
State and central governments are increasingly serious about resolving ROW issues, including use of police protection for ROW access.

DLVC (District Level Valuation Committee) mechanism assesses prevailing market rate in an area and decides compensation accordingly, providing flexibility where the official ready reckoner/Jantri rate is lower than actual market price — this mechanism already existed (not new) and helps resolve ROW issues.
Fatehpur-Bhadla project has not faced any significant ROW challenge to date.

Any government-driven revision to compensation policy would be treated as a 'change in law' pass-through, so the company is neutral to such revisions, though management does not expect significant revision anytime soon.

subsections.label: Policy debate on transmission cost vs. batteries (BESS)
points: A policy-level debate is ongoing regarding how much transmission capacity the country should add, given cost implications, especially for renewable projects, and whether more co-located BESS should be pushed to optimize transmission costs.

Management believes interstate transmission lines will continue to be built and bid out, but expects greater future activity from states, since power still needs to be distributed to the last-mile consumer via state-level transmission corridors connecting renewable evacuation to load centers.
States such as Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka have already started bidding multiple intrastate projects.

Management clarified that interstate transmission build-out is not fully complete; if the country scales up battery storage massively, the required transmission quantum might reduce to some extent, but not entirely.

key_figures.label: 12-month transmission tendering pipeline expected to finalize
key_figures.value: 80,000 to 1,00,000 (INR80,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores)

subsections.label: Transmission pipeline outlook
points: 12-month pipeline of INR80,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores is expected to get finalized via bidding, depending on how the bidding process proceeds.
This 12-month pipeline number has remained almost the same versus the same time last year.
Total identified projects for bidding stand at about INR150,000 crores.

Intrastate opportunity estimated at INR30,000-40,000 crores annually across all states combined, driven by states needing to build corridors connecting renewable evacuation points to load centers and then to end consumers.

subsections.label: Long-term EBITDA trajectory (verbal guidance, not formal EBITDA guidance)
points: Management does not formally guide on EBITDA but indicated that with INR72,000 crores of under-construction pipeline getting completed, this would translate to additional tariff of about INR10,000-odd crores.
Distribution business EBITDA (currently INR2,500 crores) expected to translate to close to INR3,000-3,200 crores.
Smart meter business EBITDA expected to reach an INR2,400-3,000-odd crores trajectory once the entire smart meter portfolio is fully realized.

Transmission EBITDA is expected to be roughly 2-3x the current numbers once all existing under-construction transmission projects (with locked-in tariffs) are completed and commissioned over the next 36-40 months.

Growth beyond the current 3-4 year corridor is expected to continue via C&I, potential distribution business expansion, and district cooling (an incubating business), while maintaining financial and execution discipline.

guidance_ledger.statement: We will have about INR22,000 crores of capex next year (transmission ~15,500, distribution ~2,350, smart metering ~3,900), so between 21,000 to 22,000.
FY28 capex will be around 23,000, of which transmission ~20,000, distribution ~2,000, smart metering ~1,500 (order book only, excludes additional orders); overall between 22,000 to 25,000.
Capitalization number in FY27 would be about 21,000-22,000 crores.
In FY28, capitalization could be about 13,000 crores; thereafter capitalization will improve in transmission as HVDC projects start getting commissioned from FY29.
We plan to do transmission capex of about INR15,000-16,000 crores with INR8,000 crores of WIP, and plan to capitalize about INR14,500-15,000 crores out of this block.
We will continue to maintain that leverage in the ratio of around 4.5x to 4.7x.
Next year probably we'll be doing about minimum about 1 crore meters.
We will continue to maintain that market share between 25 percentage to 30 percentage.

guidance_ledger.metric: New transmission opportunity value from market share
guidance_ledger.statement: Maintaining 25-30% market share converts to INR40,000-50,000-odd crores of new opportunity in transmission itself.
12-month pipeline would be about INR80,000 crores to INR1 lakh crores, depending on how bidding process proceeds; we expect bids of that magnitude will get finalized.

guidance_ledger.metric: EBITDA (revenue run-rate add from FY26 commissioning)
guidance_ledger.statement: This year's capitalization for transmission will add another INR1,600 crores of EBITDA (revenue) on a fully run-rate basis from projects commissioned this financial year.
Given the capitalization plan, we expect consolidated EBITDA (operating profit) could be around INR11,500 crores next year.
Once all existing under-construction transmission projects get completed with locked-in tariffs, transmission EBITDA will be 3x from existing transmission EBITDA trajectory.
Distribution business currently has INR2,500 crores EBITDA, which will translate to close to INR3,000-3,200 crores.
Smart meter business will start generating INR2,400 crores to INR3,000-odd crores of EBITDA trajectory once the entire smart meter portfolio is realized.
Currently the number is INR1,300-odd crores which is the full year tariff from the Mumbai HVDC project, which we will start accruing from next financial year.
Evaluation at MERC and STU level is ongoing; management cannot commit currently whether it will start working from this fiscal.

Management stated it will separately walk through the entire borrowing program for next 4-5 years; two things certain: leverage will not reach 4.5x-4.6x ceiling, and INR77,000 crores of capex is locked in over 4 years.
We will have a detailed presentation on C&I once we complete next financial year and have this call again somewhere in May next year.

risk_register.risk: ROW (Right of Way) challenges from landowners/general public despite compensation orders
risk_register.note: Despite collector compensation orders as per government policy, some individuals/groups still create obstruction; police protection increasingly used; governments are systematically working to resolve this.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory/policy debate on transmission cost vs. battery storage (BESS)
risk_register.note: Ongoing policy-level debate on whether to push co-located BESS to optimize transmission cost; could affect quantum of future transmission capacity needed, though not expected to eliminate the need.

risk_register.risk: Compensation policy revision (change in law) risk
risk_register.note: Any government revision to compensation could be treated as change in law pass-through; company neutral to it but doesn't expect significant near-term revision.

risk_register.risk: China equipment sourcing restriction under TBCB
risk_register.note: Per TBCB bid conditions cannot use Chinese-manufactured equipment; no import from China envisaged, so not seen as a constraint.

risk_register.risk: Sector-wide equipment supply constraints (GIS, transformers, reactors, HVDC components)
risk_register.note: New domestic capacity being added by OEMs (e.g., GE, Hitachi) investing in India; supply-related issues easing out; no AESL project delayed due to equipment delivery delay owing to strategic procurement.
Evaluation still ongoing at MERC and STU level; management cannot commit on commissioning timing.

risk_register.risk: Land possession delay for Khavda-Olpad HVDC (Olpad)
risk_register.note: Olpad land possession from Power Grid expected in about a month; construction cannot start at Olpad until possession secured.

themes.label: Capex ramp-up
themes.note: Consolidated capex nearing INR15,000 crores in FY26, guided to rise to ~INR20,000-22,000 crores in FY27 and ~22,000-25,000 crores in FY28.

themes.label: Credit rating & cost of capital improvement
themes.note: Most assets now AAA+/AAA rated with falling interest cost even as capex scales up, plus $500 million bond refinanced via Apollo.

themes.label: HVDC project execution
themes.note: Mumbai HVDC fully commissioned in FY26; Fatehpur-Bhadla and Khavda-Olpad HVDC projects progressing with land possession and construction ramping up.

themes.label: Smart metering scale-up
themes.note: 83 lakh meters installed in FY26 versus 70 lakh target, guided to add minimum 1 crore meters in FY27, with 9-10 crore meter market opportunity remaining.

themes.label: C&I business emergence
themes.note: ~5,000 MW renewable capacity contracted with ~1,400 MW tied to customers; seen as a major future growth driver including data center demand.

themes.label: Leverage & capital discipline
themes.note: Net leverage guided to remain in 4.5x-4.7x range despite rising capex and EBITDA growth ambitions.

themes.label: ROW & land acquisition challenges
themes.note: ROW issues persist from landowners despite compensation policy mechanisms (DLVC); governments increasingly proactive including police protection use.

key_takeaways: Commissioned the Mumbai HVDC project, a RAB-based project important for Mumbai transmission capacity augmentation and integrating more renewable power for AEML.
Surpassed the FY26 smart meter deployment target of 70 lakh meters, installing about 83 lakh meters on the ground — the highest by any operator, not only in India but globally.

AEML consolidated capex (transmission, distribution, smart metering) has reached close to INR15,000 crores, with plans to reach about INR20,000 crores capex this year, alongside significant improvement in credit ratings (most assets now AAA+ or AAA) and reduced interest cost.
AEML RAB has grown from INR5,400 crores to over INR10,500-plus crores; transmission RAB-based asset grew by INR7,000 crores from HVDC addition to a prior base of INR10,000 crores.
Refinanced a $500 million bond via Apollo, a U.S. insurance investor, demonstrating financial and operational strength amid challenging geopolitical conditions.
Improved transmission market share to almost 29% of projects that went into bidding this year, with about INR150,000 crores of projects already identified for bidding.
O&M availability at 99.7%, and distribution losses reduced to 4.2% (from a starting point of 8.5%).

C&I identified as a major growth driver for next year, with close to 5,000 MW of renewable capacity contracted and about 1,400 MW already tied to third-party consumers; detailed C&I presentation planned for next year's call.
pressing_questions: Is it possible to share the percentage completion for Fatehpur-Bhadla? How much percentage completed till date? (Management: 'I don't have that number ready, Mohit, but we will send you that.')

Bharat Shah's question on whether operating profit of about INR8,000 crores and EBITDA of INR8,700-odd crores should be in the corridor of INR25,000-27,000 crores in 3-4 years' time was not directly confirmed by management, who declined to provide a specific EBITDA number.

Shirom Kapur's query on the discrepancy between smart meter operational EBITDA (non-Ind AS) reported in the 9-month FY26 presentation (INR466 crores) versus full-year FY26 (INR452 crores) despite a positive Q4 was not resolved on the call; CFO said he would have to check where the 9-month number came from.
